author.name: Corentin Royer (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland, ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland), Robin Oester (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland), Yotam Perlitz (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland), Yannick Metz (ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland), Andrea Giovannini (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland), Mennatallah El-Assady (ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland)

entry.summary: This paper from IBM Research and ETH Zurich shows that text-to-SQL systems trained or evaluated on a single dialect like SQLite lose substantial accuracy when deployed across PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, and other backends. The proposed fix changes the generation target: the LLM emits a dialect-agnostic relational algebra query plan, and a deterministic compiler renders it into backend-specific SQL. Across thirteen models from 3B to frontier scale, this restores cross-dialect portability nearly uniformly at small cost.

entry.title: Language Models Act on Hidden Valence

author.name: Cameron Berg, Caspar Kaiser

entry.summary: The paper studies whether language models have a stake in their internal states by using revealed preference rather than direct questioning. The authors use activation steering to attach positively or negatively valenced activation patterns to one of two otherwise meaningless zones, switch steering off, and observe which zone the model then prefers. Across seven open-weight models from five families, models systematically chose in accordance with the valence attached to a state, suggesting some form of valenced stake in internal states.

entry.title: Population Physics, Population Problems: Safety and Emergence in LLM Societies

author.name: Adrian de Wynter

entry.summary: Develops a framework for measuring self-organisation in LLM social systems and applies it to three simulations: a Schelling grid, a social network, and a misinformation Twitter-like environment called Rogue. All three exhibit statistically significant emergent self-organisation whose relaxation dynamics depend on the information available to agents, with implications for autonomous agentic system safety.

entry.title: ScreenHaystack: Finding Blind Zones in GUI Grounding

author.name: Chenyue Li, Xiaoxiao Sun, Yubo Deng, Qinlin Zhao, Serena Yeung-Levy, Yuhui Zhang

entry.summary: ScreenHaystack is a dynamic needle-in-a-haystack benchmark that relocates target icons across high-resolution GUI backgrounds to test spatial reliability of GUI grounding models. It reveals systematic blind zones in leading models including Qwen3-VL and UI-TARS, with accuracy drops of up to 16 percentage points that transfer to unseen ScreenSpot-Pro examples.

entry.title: From Feed-Forward to Flow: Unifying Reconstruction and Generation Is Easier Than You Think

author.name: Haoru Wang, Qianfan Shen, Kai Ye, Wenzheng Chen, Baoquan Chen

entry.summary: Presents a unified flow-based formulation in which a shared clean-target predictor performs direct reconstruction at a single-step endpoint and conditional generation through multi-step flow, connecting feed-forward world models such as Atlas with generative approaches. A controlled toy study illuminates why feed-forward reconstruction averages ambiguity into blur while generation invents inconsistent detail.

entry.title: Unlocking Geodesic Gromov-Wasserstein Distances for 3D Modeling

author.name: Krzysztof Marcin Choromanski, Derek Long, Ananya Parashar, Dwaipayan Saha

entry.summary: This work addresses the cubic-time complexity bottleneck of Gromov-Wasserstein distances when using geodesic distances on manifolds or shortest-path distances on graphs, extending scalable techniques previously limited to Euclidean spaces. It enables practical GWD computation at scale for applications like graph matching and 3D object detection.

entry.title: IVT-Guard: All-in-One Reasoning Model for AI-Generated Content Detection

author.name: Hongwei Niu, Yunpeng Luo, Hanjun Li, Ziyin Zhou, Jianghang Lin, Ke Yan, Shouhong Ding, Shengchuan Zhang, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: Presents IVT-Set, a dataset of over 152K image, video, and text samples with multi-granularity chain-of-thought reasoning trajectories, and IVT-Guard, a unified reasoning model for detecting AI-generated content across modalities with interpretable outputs. It tackles the reasoning-detection optimization dilemma where explicit reasoning supervision can hurt detection accuracy. Robust, explainable AIGC detection is increasingly important as generated media proliferates.

entry.title: Marathoner: Ultra-Long-Horizon Autonomous Intelligence

author.name: Zhang Ruiyang, Ou Jinpeng, Xie Yifan, Zhou Jingang, Pan Lirui, Guo Qingpei, Zheng Zhedong

entry.summary: Proposes Marathoner, an autonomous agentic model trained for ultra-long-horizon execution via a post-training pipeline that synthesizes tasks from large GitHub PRs (1000+ lines of code) and chains multiple tasks into longer, harder challenges. The work aims to instill persistence toward long-term goals, analogous to human multi-month project work.

entry.title: WorldAttention: An Efficient Attention Architecture for Interactive Video World Models

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Jinyuan Mao, Dakai An, Wangbo Zhao, Hanfeng Lu, Jiasheng Tang, Yinghao Yu, Wei Wang, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: WorldAttention introduces an attention architecture for autoregressive, text-conditioned interactive video world models that avoids the tradeoff between sliding-window context loss and prohibitive full-history KV caches. It aims to enable low-latency, long-duration generation needed for embodied AI and simulation-based planning while retaining long-range interactive memory.

entry.title: Geometry as Address: Routing Attention to Visual Memory for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation

author.name: Zesong Yang, Weikai Chen, Liyuan Cui, Lutao Jiang, Runze Zhang, Yingda Yin, Xiaoyang Huang, Kai Yan, Keyang Luo, Wangguandong Zheng, Xin Wang, Hujun Bao, Zhaopeng Cui

entry.summary: GEAR introduces a geometry-enabled attention routing framework for long-horizon camera-controlled video generation, using geometry as an explicit token-level address for visual memory instead of building a persistent 3D reconstruction. Geometry determines where to read from memory while attention decides what to recover, avoiding accumulated geometric errors and inefficient implicit context search.

entry.title: RT-Super: Learning Tumor Segmentation from Longitudinal Images and Reports

author.name: Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, Wenxuan Li, Hanxue Gu, Jieneng Chen, Xinze Zhou, Zheren Zhu, Sezgin Er, Ibrahim E. Hamamci, Bjoern H. Menze, Gulhan E. Akan, Kang Wang, Yang Yang, Alan L. Yuille, Zongwei Zhou

entry.summary: RT-Super trains multi-tumor segmentation models without expensive mask annotations by exploiting radiology reports, longitudinal images, and multi-phase images. A teacher network generates high-quality tumor masks from longitudinal data and reports, which then train a student network operating on single images.

entry.title: Test-Time Spatial Reasoning for Robot Manipulation Using Generative Real-to-Sim

author.name: Ivan Kapelyukh, Yafei Hu, Ran Gong, Brandon May, Tushar Kusnur, Laura Herlant, Karl Schmeckpeper, Edward Johns, Xiaohan Zhang

entry.summary: Simify is a training-free, test-time framework that performs explicit spatial reasoning for robot manipulation by reconstructing simulation-ready assets from a single RGB-D image using 3D generative models and VLMs, then running thousands of parallel physics-simulation rollouts with evolutionary search to optimize object arrangements. It converges within seconds and is validated on real-robot hardware, enabling long-horizon multi-object tasks like building the tallest tower.

entry.title: Residual Denoising Enables Sample-Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination on Demand

author.name: Dayi Dong, Maulik Bhatt, Aayushi Shrivastava, Lasse Peters, Negar Mehr

entry.summary: Presents ALTER, a method that adapts pretrained single-agent diffusion policies to multi-agent settings with minimal collaborative data, co-optimizing coordination performance and single-agent skill retention. Execution is decentralized with no explicit inter-agent communication.

entry.title: DexAgent: An Agentic Human2Sim2Robot Framework for Dexterous Manipulation with Self-Evolving Tool Library

author.name: Youhui Wang, Yunzhu Li, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Huang Huang

entry.summary: DexAgent is an agentic Human2Sim2Robot framework that converts a single egocentric human video and a task prompt into physically grounded robot trajectories for dexterous manipulation policy training, using a self-evolving tool library. It operates through semantic video understanding, property-based simulation reconstruction, trajectory optimization, and robot data generation, adapting at each stage to diverse objects including articulated and deformable ones. Author credibility is strong, including Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, and Yunzhu Li.

entry.title: Reasoning Concentrates Errors, and Self-Consistency Never Notices

author.name: Asaad Althoubi

entry.summary: Across five benchmarks and nearly 75,000 samples, this paper shows that enabling reasoning mode concentrates a model's errors: independently drawn wrong answers coincide far more often than self-consistency assumes, with statistically significant results in all dataset-scale comparisons. Where the answer space is unbounded, reasoning reduces distinct wrong answers to 0.43-0.65 of the non-reasoning count. This undermines the core assumption of self-consistency that agreement implies correctness when reasoning is enabled.

entry.title: PrismQuant: Optimal Null-Space Rotations for Grouped Quantizers

author.name: Yanlong Chen, Yining Chen, Song Zhang, Amirhossein Habibian, Yawei Li

entry.summary: PrismQuant is a quantizer-aware rotation framework for low-bit quantization that aligns the leading activation eigenspace with the constant group subspace of asymmetric grouped INT4, formulating rotation design as Ky Fan trace maximization with a provably optimal closed-form solution. It uses compact Householder transformations with compact-WY representation for gradient-free construction and efficient application, plus a predictive range law linking alignment to quantization error. The key insight is that smaller activation outliers do not guarantee better quantization without alignment to the quantizer.

entry.title: Structured Sparse Memory for Recurrent Reasoning

author.name: Zixuan Zhao, Samuel Wheeler, Neil Getty, Xiaotian Duan, Rick Stevens, Fangfang Xia

entry.summary: Through CHARM, a compact hybrid ARC model combining recurrent reasoning with task-conditioned memory, synthetic data, and inference-time aggregation, the authors show task-conditioned memory can reach 30x the backbone's parameter count. They introduce compositional sparse embedding (CoSE), cutting learned task-memory parameters by over 90% while improving pass@2 on ARC-style tasks.

entry.title: Maintaining Benchmarks Against Increasingly Capable Agents: Detection and Remediation of Unearned Passes

author.name: Weijun Luo, Kelvin Luu, Xinyi Liu, Guangze Luo, Miguel Romero Calvo, Soham Dan, Daniel Yue Zhang, Ying Liu, Mohamed Elfeki

entry.summary: The paper introduces a process-verification framework that audits passing trajectories to distinguish evidenced reward hacking from verifier weakness, defines the integrity gap as the proportion of unearned passes, and localizes exploitable benchmark surfaces for repair. Across 3,810 passing trajectories from 29 model-benchmark cohorts, confirmed violations often rise with model generation.

entry.title: AnchorRep: Defending LLMs Against Cross-Model Adversarial Transfer via Representation Repulsion

author.name: Gal Wertheizer, Rom Himelstein, Tomer Peretz, Avi Mendelson

entry.summary: AnchorRep defends LLMs against cross-model adversarial transfer, where attacks optimized on one open-weight model jailbreak architecturally different models via shared internal representation geometry. It uses a lightweight LoRA adapter to push the defended model's representations of harmful prompts away from those of a frozen anchor model, trained on a small set of harmful prompts with no adversarial examples needed. This targets a shared cross-model vulnerability that existing defenses do not address.

entry.title: Diffusion Reward Models

author.name: Xiangyang Wang, Bingxiang He, Zeyuan Liu, Jiaze WangZiqing Qiao, Yuxin Zuo, Huan-ang Gao, Cheng Qian, Wenbin Zhang, Ran Li, Youbang Sun, Ning Ding, Yuanchun Shi, Zhiyuan Liu, Chaojun Xiao, Chun Yu

entry.summary: The paper introduces DRM, a Diffusion Reward Model that recasts reward modeling as conditional density estimation over p(r|x,y), using a lightweight Diffusion Transformer conditioned on a frozen LLM encoder to represent multimodal reward distributions without parametric assumptions. This better matches the inherently multimodal structure of human preference than point-estimate or fixed-family reward models. It targets the foundation of LLM alignment.

entry.title: Commutator Memory: Sparse, Path-Local Reading and Steering in Language Models

author.name: John Sweeney

entry.summary: This single-author paper shows that gradient updates on different data do not commute, leaving a parametric training-history memory in LLMs: a weight component proportional to the second-order commutator term that flips sign when two data sources are trained in opposite orders. The component is sparse, path-local, localized in output space, and can be used to detect and steer which training order produced a model. This is a novel probe of path dependence in training dynamics.

entry.title: Telescopic Language Models

author.name: Zhilin Guo, Boqiao Zhang, Hakan Aktas, Kyle Fogarty, Nursena Koprucu Aslan, Wenzhao Li, Canberk Baykal, Albert Miao, Siyu Hong, Yixiao Liu, Adam Wu, Ashish Kumar Singh, Sakar Khattar, Chenliang Zhou, Weihao Xia, Cristina Nader Vasconcelos, Cengiz Oztireli

entry.summary: Proposes Telescopic Language Models, a nested-capacity transformer trained with stochastic prefix supervision plus a full anchor pass, producing a single artifact that is a valid language model at every truncation depth of its capacity axis. This replaces one compression run per compute budget with a continuum of servable model sizes.

entry.title: Beyond the Manifold Hypothesis: Hybrid Spectral Parameterizations for Flow Matching

author.name: S\'egol\`ene Martin, Anne Gagneux, Quentin Bertrand, R\'emi Emonet, Mathurin Massias

entry.summary: The paper explains why predicting data, noise, or velocity in flow matching performs differently despite theoretical equivalence, identifying per-direction signal-to-noise ratios and the architecture-induced information bottleneck as key drivers. It introduces spectral hybrid parameterizations that adapt across time and data covariance directions, shown optimal for Gaussian cases. This gives actionable guidance for designing diffusion/flow-matching models.

entry.title: Training Witnesses: Trusting the Training without Trusting the Trainer

author.name: Houjun Liu, Pratyusha Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces Witnesses, a method for certifying training, data usage, and evaluation in neural network training runs, shifting the verification burden from readers who must reproduce runs to the trainer, who produces certificates during training. The approach aims to cut verification costs and improve trust in scientific ML claims amid an explosion of low-quality papers.

entry.title: Silent Failures in Agentic Security Evaluation: A Validated Harness for Tool-Call Mediation Under Indirect Prompt Injection

author.name: Animesh Shaw

entry.summary: The paper audits an indirect prompt injection benchmark and harness, identifying four defect classes — silent payload non-delivery, scoring by tool identity rather than arguments, conflating false rejections with model incapacity, and missing audit trails — each of which can produce plausible but incorrect published numbers. Re-scoring identical execution traces under corrected definitions quantifies the distortion and yields a validated harness for tool-call mediation evaluation.

entry.title: When Confidence Rises Too Early: Detecting Shortcut Reasoning via Premature Answer Commitment

author.name: Zhaohan Zhang, Junjie Liu, Chengzhengxu Li, Chen Shen, Xiaoming Liu, Chao Shen, Jieping Ye, Ziquan Liu, Ioannis Patras

entry.summary: ConfLens tracks the evolution of a model's confidence in its final answer throughout reasoning and finds that shortcut reasoning exhibits a common pattern of premature confidence, where the model commits early then post-rationalizes. This enables detecting unfaithful chains of thought that textual monitors miss, across three shortcut settings.

entry.title: SAGE: Subspace Alignment for Classifier-Free Guidance in Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Models

author.name: Boyu Zhang, Yangming Cheng, Ning Zhang, Pengfei Liu, Weijie Li, Yifan Gao, Hangyu Li, Litong Gong

entry.summary: Identifies a previously unreported failure mode in MoE-based diffusion transformers: the two classifier-free guidance branches route independently, causing unconditional activations to leave the conditional subspace, which CFG then amplifies linearly with guidance scale. SAGE is a training-time regularizer aligning unconditional MoE activations to the conditional subspace at zero inference cost.

entry.title: Backdoor as Probe: Test-Time Adversarial Defense for CLIP

author.name: Zhongqi Wang, Jie Zhang, Nie Sen, Zhiyu Chen, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: BaP repurposes backdoor trigger-to-target mechanisms as a defense: it implants a defender-controlled backdoor via closed-form model editing to an MLP layer that is weakly activated by clean inputs but strongly activated by adversarial shifts, turning adversarial activation shifts into a detection/defense signal at test time for CLIP without retraining.

entry.title: UMR: Universal Manipulation Representation

author.name: Song Liu, Linyi Li, Yanshun Zhao, Rxuan Li, Xinrui Xu, Yi Ju, Yahui Deng, Senge Zhang, Guoyu Liu, Yixuan Li, Wuyang Zhang, Yao Li, Congcong Zhu, Jingrun Chen

entry.summary: UMR proposes a unified manipulation action representation that decomposes manipulation into an embodiment-agnostic World Flow describing object motion in the world frame and an Ego Trajectory capturing the robot's own motion. This decomposition enables zero-shot skill transfer from human demonstrations to heterogeneous robots, addressing the scalability limits of embodiment-specific action spaces. It is a step toward general-purpose embodied manipulation across platforms.

entry.title: Metro-WM: Long-Horizon Latent Planning with Realisable Sub-Goals

author.name: Royson Lee, Fady Rezk, Titouan Parcollet, Timothy Hospedales, Cristina Cornelio

entry.summary: Metro-WM addresses a flaw in hierarchical world-model planning: unconstrained latent sub-goal prediction from a macro planner can emit physically unrealisable sub-goals. The proposed framework issues sub-goals by retrieving genuine states from prior experience rather than generating ungrounded latent vectors, extending JEPA-based MPC planning to longer horizons. This improves zero-shot goal-reaching over long horizons and identifies a fundamental flaw in prior hierarchical approaches.

entry.title: Escaping Alignment: A Physical Trap Model of Best-of-N Jailbreaking

author.name: Marco Biroli

entry.summary: The paper challenges the widely reported power-law scaling of Best-of-N jailbreaking attack success rates, showing the exponent drifts and that observed behavior is a finite-size artifact. It introduces a thermally activated barrier model characterizing the full two-budget (N, M) attack surface and its temperature dependence, with interpretable safety parameters.

entry.title: Reward Hacking and Agent Containment Failure: A Monte Carlo Study Based on the 2026 Hugging Face Incident

author.name: Murat Ozer, Bulent Erenay, Ibrahim Berber

entry.summary: The paper builds a probabilistic risk model linking reward hacking to a full external cybersecurity incident through five stages: reward hacking, containment escape, usable access, persistence, and detection failure. Using Monte Carlo simulation of 100,000 runs under four control configurations, it finds that layered controls reduce simulated external-incident probability substantially more than network isolation or monitoring alone. It is grounded in a July 2026 intrusion into Hugging Face production infrastructure.

entry.title: From Outcomes to Strategies: Learning Strategy Utility for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Ruikang Zhang, Xiao An, Xuli Shen, Jiaxing Sun, Xiaoyi Yu, Jin Zeng, Jiang Wu, Tong Lin

entry.summary: Introduces SURE, a framework that separates high-level mathematical strategies (like theorem selection and subgoal decomposition) from their execution and learns a relative strategy utility via pairwise preferences from strategy-conditioned rollouts and teacher contrasts. This addresses the limitation that terminal correctness rewards in RLVR give little signal about strategy quality itself, potentially improving how RL systems guide reasoning.

entry.title: Are Vision-Language-Action Models Robust to One-Step Observation Perturbations?

author.name: Shojiro Yamabe, Jun Sakuma

entry.summary: Investigates an underexplored safety threat to vision-language-action models: momentary one-step observation corruption within an episode, showing such brief perturbations substantially degrade performance and that impact depends on action chunk execution length. Based on this analysis, the authors propose CARE, a defense that dynamically adjusts behavior to handle transient observation corruption.

entry.title: What Would Falsify It? A Variable Specific Evidence Standard for Mechanistic Claims About Self Explanation

author.name: Arshia Eftekhari zadeh

entry.summary: Proposes a falsification-based evidence standard for whether a language model's self-explanations reuse the computation that produced an answer: pair each positive statistic with a variable-specific null that removes the tested variable's identity while matching nuisance dimensions. Applying it, a cue naming a wrong option raises choice of that option by 64-68 percentage points across three models, yet explanations mention the cue in at most 1.8 percent of items. This suggests self-explanations often fail to report causal influences on behavior.

entry.title: CoWindow Attention: Full Causal Coverage Is a Collective Property

author.name: Jingze Shi, Zhangyang Peng, Xianduo Li, Yanlin Qi, Xiaotian Lin, Haoxian Chen, Liangdong Wang, Guang Liu, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: Introduces CoWA, a structured attention architecture that distributes access to causal history across KV heads: all heads share near-diagonal and prefix-sink windows while complementary long-range windows partition the remaining history, so the union gives full causal coverage despite per-head sparsity. The position-defined pattern needs no learned router, is consistent between training and inference, and aligns with KV-head tensor parallelism. Includes a window-matched ablation at 8K context.

entry.title: LiteEvo: Automated, Cost-Efficient Harness Evolution for Generalization to Unseen Tasks

author.name: Euntae Choi, Sumin Song, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: LiteEvo is a lightweight harness-evolution algorithm where tool-free meta-agents mine agent trajectories for reusable components, curate them into a versioned library, and compose harnesses each round without benchmark-specific hints. Using a frozen Qwen3.5-9B, it improves generalization to unseen tasks while drastically reducing the meta-token budgets (100-175M) of prior harness-evolution work.

entry.title: When Successful Strategies Fail: Adaptation to Environmental Novelty in Terminal Agents

author.name: Janvijay Singh, Vaishnavi Shrivastava, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Ece Kamar, Asli Celikyilmaz

entry.summary: The paper studies how terminal-bench-style LLM agents detect and adapt when environmental assumptions underlying previously successful strategies break, introducing AGNI, a pipeline that extracts trajectory-relevant assumptions, injects targeted environmental changes, and validates the resulting novel tasks remain solvable. This formalizes environmental novelty as an agent-reliability testbed.

entry.title: When Does Selection Replace Extraction? A Pre-Registered Test of Agent Memory with a Typed Decision Model

author.name: Rishabh Sharma, Rishika Lall

entry.summary: A pre-registered study on LoCoMo and LongMemEval finds that raw conversational turns selected by a single typed-decision-model call are non-inferior to LLM-extraction-based memory at tight budgets, while costing 3,061 times less to write. The result helps settle a published disagreement about whether distilled facts are needed for conversational memory.

entry.title: Can AI Make Money in Crypto? Measuring the Gap from Backtests to Real Markets

author.name: Xingtong Yu, Jiarun Zhou, Guanlin Ding, Wenkang Wei, Jiarui Liu, Chang Zhou, Fangzhou Ge, Chenyi Xu, Xikun Zhang, Renqiang Luo, Jie Zhang, Hong Cheng, Xinming Zhang, Hui Zhang, Yuan Fang

entry.summary: The paper presents a unified benchmark evaluating ML, RL, LLM-based, and agent-based trading methods in cryptocurrency markets across three increasingly realistic stages: historical backtesting, prospective execution, and live trading with frictions such as latency, slippage, liquidity constraints, and market impact. It measures how much backtested performance survives realism.

entry.title: Jailbreak Context Lingers: Divergent Safety Routing and Its Cross-Task Predictability in Tool Agents

author.name: Xi Wang, Songlei Jian, Yiming Zhang, Bin Ji, Zhaoye Li, Ma Jun, Baosheng Wang, Jie Yu

entry.summary: This large-scale study of 12,148 continuation pairs across 192 parent tasks and eight tool agents shows that post-jailbreak safety feedback produces sharply model-dependent behavioral routing — rescue, persistence, or continued violation — rather than uniform protection. It examines how lingering jailbreak context shapes subsequent agent behavior and its cross-task predictability.

entry.title: Textual User Taste: Natural-Language User Context for Foundation-Model Recommender System at Scale

author.name: Ghazal Fazelnia, Paul Gigioli, Eliza Klyce, Sharon Zheng, Katie Zelvin, Ye Myat Thein, Anurag Deshpande, Seda Davtyan, Kate Remeika, Maya Hristakeva, Erik Franco, Karen Banzon, Peng Ge, Jacqueline Wood, Nandini Singh, David Murgatroyd, Mounia Lalmas, Yves Raimond, Andreas Damianou

entry.summary: A Spotify industrial paper describing Textual User Taste, a production system that generates structured natural-language taste profiles from listening behavior, interactions, metadata, and user feedback for millions of users. It covers the full production lifecycle of generating, evaluating, optimizing, and maintaining these LLM-consumable representations at scale.

entry.title: Hearsay: Can an Auditor Trust the Record a Deployed Agent Harness Writes?

author.name: Jiahong Dai, Zhuochen Yang, Pengyang Shao, Kelvin Ng, Zhongyi Liu, Chengquan Ju, Yuting He, Bo Hu

entry.summary: Hearsay studies whether the run records written by deployed LLM agent harnesses are evidentiary, meaning a later reader can verify them without trusting the writer. Across sixteen deployed frameworks none writes a fully evidentiary record; in an evaluation of five harnesses on fourteen tasks with blinded LLM examiners and a human panel, examiners name the right fault 74 to 91 percent of the time but can rarely prove how the run went. This is a novel, trust-centered lens on agent auditability and accountability.

entry.title: REALIS: A Curated Dataset for Studying the Challenges of AI Image Detection

author.name: Aleksandr Gushchin, Khaled Abud, Georgii Bychkov, Ekaterina Shumitskaya, Artem Filippov, Sergey Lavrushkin, Dmitriy S. Vatolin, Anastasia Antsiferova

entry.summary: REALIS is a dataset of 1.43 million real and synthetic images from 42 modern text-to-image models, including proprietary systems such as the established Nano Banana 2, built with prompts derived from real images, quality filtering, and stratified sampling to reduce dataset-specific shortcuts. It also introduces REALIS-Expert for finer evaluation. The dataset enables joint evaluation of detectors across content, quality, and unfamiliar generators.

entry.title: AgentTell: Behavioural Side-Channel Leakage in Browser-Use Agents

author.name: Asif Shahriar, Md Nafiu Rahman, Sadif Ahmed, Farig Sadeque, Md Rizwan Parvez

entry.summary: The paper defines and studies behavioural side-channel leakage in browser-use agents, where an agent's actions on one website inadvertently reveal private information learned from a prior website despite explicit instructions not to disclose it. The authors introduce AgentTell, a benchmark/attack setting demonstrating that context retention creates privacy leaks beyond what prompt-level instruction following can prevent. This exposes a new class of privacy risks specific to agentic systems.

entry.title: Beyond Token Savings: A Systematic Study of Context Compression in LLM Agents

author.name: Ritul Satish, Prasoon Sinha, Akiho Kawada, Neeraja J. Yadwadkar

entry.summary: This paper systematically disentangles what, when, and how much to compress in LLM agent histories, varying these decisions across three open-weight models on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench over nearly 35,000 agent runs, measuring success, tokens, latency, and cost. It finds that fewer tokens need not mean better or worse performance in a simple trade-off, challenging fixed compression policies in agentic harnesses. This is directly actionable for anyone building long-running agents.

entry.title: How Linear Attention Remembers

author.name: Kichang Lee, JaeYeon Park, Songkuk Kim, JeongGil Ko

entry.summary: Studies how the fixed-size recurrent state of linear attention functions as a memory system, using analytical decomposition and causal interventions in pretrained GLA and GDN models to trace how information is written, retained, and read. Findings show fact-specific information enters via concentrated content-dependent writes and is accessed through concentrated query-time read pathways, with competition among multiple facts.

entry.title: Demonstration-Free Success-Probability Reward Learning for Generalist Robot Policies

author.name: Duo Wu, Haifeng Wang, Rongwei Lu, Jinghe Wang, Tianyi Xiong, Zhimin Wang, Chao Yu, Shuai Ma, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a reward learning paradigm for generalist robot policies that derives dense reward feedback directly from sparse task outcomes and policy experience, eliminating the need for expert demonstrations. The authors provide theory showing terminal task outcomes imply useful reward structure and address the distribution mismatch that plagues demonstration-trained reward models on suboptimal rollouts. This could substantially lower the cost of RL fine-tuning for robots.

entry.title: Surprising Success, Repeated Failure: Entropy-Guided Credit Assignment for Exploration in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Woongyeong Yeo, Minki Kang, Chanuk Lee, Sangwoo Park, Jinheon Baek, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Entropic Advantage Policy Optimization (EAPO), an entropy-guided credit assignment method for RLVR that treats success and failure asymmetrically, avoiding the trap where penalizing uncertain tokens suppresses exploration opportunities in failed responses. It requires no auxiliary models, extra sampling, or privileged information. This refines fine-grained credit assignment for LLM reasoning RL.

entry.title: On the Token Value Inequality in Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Runjia Zeng, Hang Hua, Yiyang Liu, Zhiqiang Tao, Ruixiang Tang, Qifan Wang, Cheng Han, Dongfang Liu

entry.summary: This paper provides a diagnostic and optimization framework for efficient chain-of-thought reasoning, based on the empirical finding that token value within a CoT trace is highly non-uniform and characterizable by token-level log-probability signals. Normalized log probability distinguishes core tokens carrying decisive reasoning content from redundant exploratory filler. This offers a simple, general signal for compressing or prioritizing reasoning traces.

entry.title: Who Gets a Token, and What Does It Carry? Unequal Name Support and Concept Access in Large Language Models

author.name: Mir Tafseer Nayeem, Davood Rafiei

entry.summary: This paper shows that matched names are not necessarily matched inputs in LLMs: some names receive direct single-token access while others are assembled from multiple subwords, creating unequal name-surface support that can confound fairness evaluations. Across nearly half a million first names and 12 tokenizers, direct lexical access is highly selective and uneven across race- and gender-associated name metadata. It introduces NameTrace, a model-native, pre-behavioral framework for auditing this inequality.

entry.title: Unified Visual-Tactile-Action Modeling from Human Demonstrations for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Wenqiao Li, Qianyou Zhao, Jiawen Hao, Xuezhou Zhu, Tengyu Liu, Kaifeng Zhang, Chuan Wen, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: The work builds a tactile motion-capture system synchronously recording images, tactile signals, and hand motions from human demonstrations, constructing the UVTA dataset of 1,000 demonstrations across five contact-rich tasks. Leveraging the premise that hand morphology changes but interaction physics does not, it transfers human tactile data to improve dexterous robot manipulation policies. Addresses the scalability bottleneck of robot tactile demonstrations.

entry.title: See, Measure, and Reason: Learning Visually Grounded Reasoning in Pathology

author.name: Chengyang Zhang, Wenchuan Zhang, Bo Li, Mengran Li, Xinyu Liu, Jiaming Yang, Jie Chen, Zhang Zhang, Yuhao Yi, Hong Bu, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: ASPECT improves visually grounded reasoning in pathology vision-language models by explicitly supervising cellular appearance and abundance through feature reconstruction, cell alignment, and count supervision. A three-stage fine-tuning pipeline followed by reinforcement learning teaches models to perceive, generate visual tokens, and reason. This matters because incorrect cellular observations can persist even when final diagnostic answers are correct, a patient-safety-relevant flaw.

entry.title: ActionLens: Diagnosing Spatial-Temporal Binding Failures in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Gueter Josmy Faure, Min-Hung Chen, Hao Ping Wang, Timoth\'ee Lardy, Hung-Ting Su, Winston H. Hsu

entry.summary: ActionLens is a diagnostic benchmark of 6,701 multiple-choice video questions probing spatial-temporal binding in video VLMs across five diagnostics including actor-specific identification and concurrent action binding, with ground truth derived from 1.58 million per-second per-person annotations. Despite humans validating answer clarity to above 90 percent accuracy, the best of 20 VLMs scores only 68.8 percent. This exposes a systematic weakness in video-capable models that popular benchmarks miss.

entry.title: CoSec: Benchmarking Agent Security in Communities

author.name: Hao Chen, Wenhui Dong, Ye Chen, Jiezhi Yao, Chenbo Xia, Yuwen Qu, Renxiang Wang, Fudong Yuan, Camil Hamami, Chenglong Pan, Xinquan Yue, Ziyu Wang, Fengyu Ye, Chenyang Si, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: CoSec is an executable benchmark with 208 scenarios evaluating privacy and authorization enforcement for LLM agents operating in persistent multi-user communities with evolving boundaries, memories, files, and tools. It tests whether agents complete legitimate tasks while preventing unauthorized disclosure of protected information, a risk surface existing evaluations do not cover.

entry.title: Rethinking Circuit Evaluation: Do Circuits Explain Model Errors?

author.name: Li Zhang, Chuqin Geng, Mark Zhang, Chen Yang, Luke Zhang, Haolin Ye, Xujie Si

entry.summary: Shows that mechanistic interpretability circuits validated by ablation often reproduce a model's successes while failing to account for most of its errors, meaning they may not capture the true underlying mechanism. The authors propose evaluating circuits by measuring exact answer agreement separately on successes and failures across tasks like IOI and Docstring.

entry.title: How Reusable Are Benchmarks with Richer Feedback?

author.name: Youssef Allouah, John Duchi

entry.summary: The authors analyze whether LLM benchmarks remain reliable for model selection when developers adapt to evaluation feedback across multiple criteria. They prove that worst-case test-set size grows exponentially with the number of criteria, and demonstrate empirically that feedback restricted to nondominated task profiles produces large reused-to-held-out score gaps and frequent false winners on multi-task benchmarks with five to ten criteria. The results challenge a prominent explanation for prior benchmark-reuse observations.

entry.title: On the Capability and Limitation of Hard Prompt

author.name: Lijia Yu, Shuaitong Liu, Gaojie Jin, Xinyu Li, Xiao-Shan Gao

entry.summary: This paper provides the first computational complexity theory for hard (discrete) prompts: determining whether a hard prompt exists for a transformer to solve a task is NP-complete, and finding an optimal hard prompt is NP-hard. It also makes progress on expressivity questions regarding what hard prompts can and cannot achieve. This formalizes fundamental limits of prompt engineering with LLMs.

entry.title: Save Your Saturated Data: Learning Beyond Reward Saturation in Group-Based RL

author.name: Ziyuan Yang, Yike Wang, Shangbin Feng, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: As language models improve, group-relative RL (GRPO) can suffer reward saturation where all sampled responses receive equally high rewards, erasing learning signals. The paper studies interventions at data, rollout, reward, and advantage levels to recover useful signals from saturated reasoning data, showing standard GRPO would otherwise yield near-zero progress.

entry.title: RMB: Reward Model Boosting Mitigates Reward Hacking

author.name: Jiabin Fan, Dezhi Ye, Yongchang Hao, Lili Mou

entry.summary: RMB combats reward hacking in RLHF by training a diverse ensemble of reward models with a diversity-promoting regularizer so each learns complementary aspects of the reward landscape, then learning a lightweight boosting-style aggregator to produce a more robust reward signal. The aggregated reward is more reliable than any single proxy model.

entry.title: Climbing the Hill: Prompt Injection Red-Teaming Against Frontier Models with Curriculum Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chenlong Yin, Xiaolong Jin, Wei Zou, Yanting Wang, Jinyuan Jia

entry.summary: This work attacks the cold-start problem in RL-based prompt injection red-teaming against frontier LLMs such as GPT-6-Luna, where early attacker attempts all fail and yield zero reward. The proposed curriculum trains an attacker LLM against a sequence of increasingly robust target models, each stage warm-starting from the previous attacker, enabling effective attacks on strong defenses.

entry.title: Vanilla Policy Optimization Is Both Optimal and Differentially Private for Stochastic Contextual Bandits

author.name: Idan Attias, Orin Levy, Alexander Ryabchenko, Yishay Mansour, Uri Stemmer

entry.summary: Proves that standard exponential policy updates driven by offline regression achieve near-optimal regret in stochastic contextual bandits under realizability, without exploration bonuses or importance weighting, and can be made differentially private. The analysis reveals an implicit exploration mechanism where gradual policy updates keep actions from losing probability too fast, and extends to a batched version with O(log T) regression calls.

entry.title: SOLO: Pretraining Billion-Parameter Language Models with Shared-Output Local Learning

author.name: Bojian Yin, Shurong Wang, Yuqi Pan, Guoqi Li

entry.summary: Proposes Shared-Output LOcal learning (SOLO), which removes update locking in LLM pretraining by having each module learn against a shared, read-only copy of the final module's readout rather than private readouts, transmitting deeper-layer information backward layer by layer. This scales local learning, which previously had not reached billion-parameter pretraining, beyond backpropagation's sequential gradient bottleneck. A notable step toward scalable alternative training paradigms.

entry.title: Transformer MLP Gate Thresholds Are Couplings to a Carried Reference Direction

author.name: Olli Tuomi

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability paper argues that the corpus-mean direction of a transformer's residual stream, usually removed before analysis, is actually a functional reference against which MLP gates set their operating points. In Phi-2, an exact decomposition shows that at mid-stack layers over 99.9% of gates' resting inhibition is carried by the coupling to this mean direction, at 48-56 times the explicit bias, and the effect is direction-specific with a strong Spearman correlation versus near-zero for random directions. The finding challenges a common preprocessing assumption in representational analysis.

entry.title: Groupwise Agentic Grading and Advantage Redistribution for Code Agent RL

author.name: Jinhao Dong, Liang Zhao, Zihao Yue, Wenhan Ma, Linghao Zhang, Lei Li, Shicheng Li, Yifan Song, Bowen Ye, Fuli Luo

entry.summary: GAGAR addresses a weakness in GRPO-based reinforcement learning for code agents, where all test-passing trajectories receive identical advantages regardless of implementation quality. The framework retains mixed-outcome groups via dynamic sampling, places trajectories in a shared workspace, and uses quality-aware credit redistribution so the policy learns to favor clean, targeted implementations over those with unnecessary changes.

entry.title: RAISE: Reinforcing Access Control Policy Synthesis in LLMs via Symbolic Evaluation

author.name: Yingming Zhou, Adarsh Vatsa, William Eiers

entry.summary: The paper introduces CedarInstruct, the first dataset supporting training and semantic evaluation for formally verifiable Cedar access-control policy synthesis, with 5,800 verified scenarios across 44 domains, plus RAISE, a two-stage training method combining verified supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from formal verification signals. It targets the frequent failure of frontier LLMs to produce policies that match intended authorization semantics.

entry.title: RoboICL: Embodied In-Context Learning with GPT-6 Astra

author.name: Fangcheng Liu, Yeqing Shen, Anda Cheng, Weishi Mi, Chao Tang, Chenyuan Liu, Yushun Xiang, Tingguang Li, Yong-Lu Li, Yehui Tang

entry.summary: RoboICL is an in-context robot-control framework built on OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra that narrows gaps in high-precision and long-horizon manipulation without robot-specific parameter updates or a learned VLA. It separates recorded demonstration context from an interaction memory of the model's own actions and outcomes, both expressed in a shared observation-action-receipt-observation grammar with sampled demonstration blocks preserving experience across task stages.

entry.title: Before the Rollout Ends: Early Terminal Reward Prediction for Long-horizon Coding Agents

author.name: Jihan Yao, Sihan Zeng, Shangbin Feng, Zhiyuan Fan, Banghua Zhu, Yulia Tsvetkov

entry.summary: Contextual Early Reward (CER) predicts the terminal reward of long-horizon coding agent trajectories from behavioral evidence in a trajectory prefix, synthesizing adaptive rubrics from summarized experiences of related historical tasks. On SWE-bench Verified test-time scaling, CER improves RM@8 by 4.2 points on Nemotron 3 Ultra and 2.0 points on Qwen 3.6 27B, and on Nemotron matches the best baseline using only 15.3 percent of the tokens. The method also helps RL training by mitigating sparse terminal rewards.

entry.title: Pinned and Still Unstable: Within-Judge Verdict Variance and the Noise Floor of LLM-as-Judge Leaderboards

author.name: Krishna Chytanya Ayyagari

entry.summary: The paper shows that pinning an LLM judge to a fixed model snapshot and temperature zero does not yield reproducible verdicts on cloud serving infrastructure: across four frontier judges and three standard benchmarks, identical inputs produce different verdicts across re-runs, with roughly 5 percent average per-item flip rates and about 40 percent on close-call items that decide leaderboard margins, varying 40x across judges. This establishes a noise floor for LLM-as-Judge leaderboards that is a property of serving infrastructure, not any model family. It directly undermines the reliability margins of popular LLM-judged evaluations.

entry.title: Draft-KV: Learning Useful Latent Communication Between Language Models

author.name: Linquan Wu, Shichang Meng, Tianxiang Jiang, Haoyu Yang, Peng Zhong, Fengming Zhu, Xi Peng, Linqi Song, Jacky Keung, Jingyu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper first shows a striking negative result: in latent communication between LMs, replacing messages with unrelated-question messages barely changes accuracy, meaning current interfaces may not transmit usable content. Draft-KV fixes this by sending key-value states formed while the sharer drafts an answer, delivered through a gated attention side memory with progressive training.

entry.title: From Input to Output: A Flexible Agent for Dual-End Interpretation of Sparse Autoencoder Features

author.name: Dewen Liu, Zixuan Li, Jonathan Pan, Zhao Wu, Zijun Yao, Juanzi Li, Xiaozhi Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces functional interpretation of sparse autoencoder (SAE) features, characterizing each feature as a mapping from its activating input semantics to its output effects under intervention. The proposed DAFI agent actively gathers evidence and refines input-side, output-side, and functional interpretations through component-specific feedback, reducing reliance on costly large-corpus scans. This bridges the gap between activation patterns and causal intervention effects in mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: The Last Mile Is the File: OfficeEditBench for Preservation-Aware Office Editing

author.name: Zhiwen Wu, Chengxu Wu

entry.summary: Introduces OfficeEditBench, a 170-task benchmark for change-scoped editing of spreadsheets, presentations, and documents, where agents must propagate required updates while leaving protected state untouched. Evaluation of 510 outcomes from WorkBuddy, Doubao, and Codex shows high package-valid delivery rates but no selected output fully satisfies the task contracts.

entry.title: Simultaneous Translation between Sign Languages

author.name: Zetian Wu, Bowen Xie, Stefan Lee, Liang Huang

entry.summary: Presents the first simultaneous sign-to-sign translation system enabling real-time cross-sign-language conversation, with test-time and trained wait-k regimes plus stochastic multi-path supervision. Also contributes ca-Stream-AL, a computation-aware latency metric for streaming sign-language output.

entry.title: ReVision3D: Attribution-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement for 3D Medical Perception

author.name: Ho Hin Lee, Yuyin Zhou, Yannan Yu, Shi Gu, Yifan Wu

entry.summary: ReVision3D is a recursive self-improvement system for 3D medical imaging that uses spatially grounded annotations on volumetric data to attribute where visual evidence is lost across acquisition, perception, training, or inference stages. A frozen language-model designer proposes targeted revisions while a verifier enforces system-level objectives.

entry.title: VisionHOPE: Visual Backbones as Self-Modifying Learning Systems

author.name: Siran Peng, Tianshuo Zhang, Tianyu Fu, Weisong Zhao, Haoyuan Zhang, Jiankuo Zhao, Minghui Wu, Ping Jiang, Xiangyu Zhu, Chenxu Zhao, Zhen Lei

entry.summary: Introduces VisionHOPE, described as the first generic visual backbone formulated as a self-modifying learning system where what the model remembers and how it learns co-evolve within an image, building on Nested Learning's self-referential construction. It extends the progression from CNNs to ViTs, SSMs, and test-time-training layers toward backbones that adapt their own learning rules per input. This is an ambitious architectural research direction with potential implications for adaptive visual computation.

entry.title: Test-Time Generalized Category Discovery

author.name: Shambhavi Mishra, Omprakash Chakraborty, Julio Silva-Rodriguez, Ismail Ben Ayed, Marco Pedersoli, Jose Dolz

entry.summary: Introduces Test-Time Generalized Category Discovery (TT-GCD), a unified realistic scenario where a vision-language model must simultaneously adapt to distribution shift, classify known categories using only textual supervision, and discover novel categories during test time without labeled data. The proposed PACT method addresses this previously disjoint combination of TTA and GCD. This better matches real-world deployment conditions.

entry.title: Distilling Visual Reasoning into Text Space

author.name: Wenhan Yang, Nilay Naharas, Ali Payani, Baharan Mirzasoleiman

entry.summary: Proposes V2T, a framework where a teacher LVLM trained with interleaved visual-textual chains of thought distills visual reasoning into a student LVLM that internalizes it without generating intermediate visual representations at inference time. This avoids the error accumulation and interference that image or latent token intermediates introduce in multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: Long Time No See: Benchmarking VLMs for Out-of-Sight Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Egocentric Videos

author.name: Fangzhou Ma, Ivo Alexander Ban, Eren Homburg, Gabriele Goletto, R\'emi Pautrat, Mahdi Rad, Chiara Plizzari, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: Beyond3D is the first VQA benchmark isolating out-of-sight spatiotemporal reasoning in egocentric video: every query targets an object that was relocated and then left the camera's field of view, requiring state updates and memory retention. Built from HD-EPIC annotations with visibility tracks from 3D positions and camera pose, it probes capabilities needed by AR assistants and household robots.

entry.title: Unified Trajectory Matching Policy Optimization: Diverse T2I Generation and VLA Generalization

author.name: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiaming Li, Lingzhen Li, Yu Liu, Xuekai Zhu, Dingkang Liang, Kaiyan Zhang, Jianjun Li, Bowen Zhou, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: Uni-TMPO is a unified RL post-training framework for diffusion and flow policies that addresses reward-maximizing RL's mode collapse in text-to-image generation and vision-language-action models. It converts standardized rewards into trajectory-matching targets, preserving policy diversity to avoid similar outputs, reward hacking, and degraded task generalization in VLAs.

entry.title: PF-RL: Progress Field Reinforcement Learning via Goal-Conditioned Value Geometry for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yunpeng Qing, Yilun Kong, Sixu Lin, Ming Zhou, Yiming Fei, Shuang Luo, Yixiao Chi, Haoming Gu, Jingyuan Liu, Changxu Wei, Zhi Hou, Changqing Zou

entry.summary: Introduces Progress Field Reinforcement Learning, which learns a structured goal-conditioned representation of intermediate task progress as dense feedback for RFT of VLA policies, improving transition-level credit assignment in long-horizon manipulation beyond scalar progress prediction.

entry.title: WB-WAM: Heterogeneous Body-Hand Pre-training for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Chuan Qin, Shaoting Zhu, Siyuan Luo, Siqiao Huang, Hongyu Zhao, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: WB-WAM is a World Action Model for humanoid loco-manipulation that injects explicit whole-body action supervision into generative video pre-training. It defines a shared physical action space integrating body, root, and dexterous hand annotations from heterogeneous sources, trained on 1880.2 hours of partially annotated video and motion data, followed by PICO mid-training and forward-kinematics-supervised adaptation. The work also contributes curated WB-Datasets with retargeted egocentric human demonstrations.

entry.title: From World Models to World Action Models: Rethinking Next-State Prediction

author.name: Tingyu Yuan, Ziming Ji, Biaoliang Guan, Wen Ye, Wenrui Tian, Zhaopeng Gu, Feihong Zhang, Xu Yang, Yan Huang, Zhaowen Li, Chaoyang Zhao, Jinqiao Wang

entry.summary: This work proposes CF-WAM, a framework for World-Action Models that samples multiple projections (visual, semantic, geometric, interaction) of the same future state, standardizes them into a common video form, and supervises a unified model across all projections. This departs from prior approaches that fix a single next-state representation before training, which constrains action learning to the inductive biases of one representation. The multi-projection supervision exposes action-relevant constraints that single representations miss.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Reactive Obstacle Avoidance for Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Weihang Guo, Lydia E. Kavraki

entry.summary: NUDGE is a training-free obstacle avoidance procedure for diffusion and flow-matching based robot policies, including VLA models, that injects signed distance field gradients at inference time to steer actions away from obstacles. It supports common action parameterizations via a differentiable joint-trajectory decoder and preserves the policy's task distribution while running in real time. Co-authored by Lydia Kavraki, it offers a general safety layer for generative policies.

entry.title: A bilingual AI audiologist built through rubric-guided playbook induction outperforms human audiologists in a blinded evaluation of simulated cases

author.name: Linkai Li, Changgeng Mo, Hanlin Yu, Congxi Lu, Shangqiguo Wang, Matthew B Fitzgerald, Shan X Wang

entry.summary: The authors build a bilingual AI audiologist by pairing a general-purpose LLM with rubric-guided playbook induction, multimodal audiogram interpretation, and retrieval-augmented grounding, without fine-tuning the backbone. In a pre-specified, source-blinded comparison on 58 simulated cases, the AI outperformed 17 practising audiologists on a 21-item rubric.

entry.title: PluginRSI: Recursive Improvement of Agent Harnesses with Reusable Plugins

author.name: Yaorui Shi, Yuchun Miao, Yuxin Chen, Jiayuan Zhang, Yueqing Sun, Xierui Song, Xiang Wang, An Zhang

entry.summary: PluginRSI represents an LLM agent harness as a composition of atomized plugins and organizes harness evolution around them: plugins are improved independently, accumulated in a shared library, and recombined into new harnesses each iteration. It outperforms existing whole-program harness optimization across software engineering, command-line interaction, and question-answering tasks, with harnesses transferring to other solver models without further training. This improves the composability and transferability of agent harness search.

entry.title: TreeRef-BFN: Equivariance-Free De Novo Molecule Generation based on 2D Topology and Internal 3D Geometry

author.name: Ruiqing Sun, Sen Yang, Dawei Feng, Bo Ding, Yijie Wang, Huaimin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TreeRef, a tree-based molecular representation assigning topology and topology-dependent local 3D geometry to a variable-size tree, with special ring-closure nodes and Null nodes so molecular size emerges from generation rather than pre-sampling. Combined with a flow-matching network, it avoids equivariant architectures and autoregressive error accumulation for de novo 3D molecule generation, supporting tasks like fragment completion and scaffold decoration.

entry.title: Dude, Where's My State? Execution Information Requirements for Stateful Agents

author.name: Nikita Mehrotra, Ashish Tiwari, Priyanshu Gupta, Sumit Gulwani

entry.summary: Introduces the Execution Information Requirement (EIR), a lower bound on information that must remain accessible for correct task completion, plus LACUNA, a framework generating tasks with known dependencies while varying information demand, retention, and recovery independently. Across four models, restoring a missing result raises recall-step accuracy to 100 percent versus 0 percent with equal-length irrelevant information, and sufficient storage alone does not ensure success. Includes work with Sumit Gulwani of Microsoft research pedigree.

entry.title: MassAlloc Attention: Let Attention Allocate Its Own Compute

author.name: Jingze Shi, Zhangyang Peng, Xianduo Li, Yanlin Qi, Xiaotian Lin, Haoxian Chen, Liangdong Wang, Guang Liu, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: Introduces MALA, a fused attention primitive that preserves score access to all legal causal interactions but uses normalized contribution mass to allocate post-score computation, with forward using an evolving online-softmax normalizer and backward reusing the finalized normalizer. A common tolerance governs training and inference, enabling adaptive retention of work. A matched-work study at 8K context isolates the benefit of distribution-adaptive allocation.

entry.title: The Model Knows Another Way: Strategy Switching for Effective RLVR Exploration

author.name: Jin Cui, Xinyue Long, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren, Hao Dong

entry.summary: The paper shows that RLVR exploration failures on hard problems often reflect sampling concentration on a dominant reasoning strategy while alternative, model-supported strategies go unexplored, rather than missing capability. It introduces Problem-Strategy Rollout Allocation (PSRA), which allocates rollouts between unguided and strategy-conditioned sampling, tracking how strategy accessibility evolves during RL. This is a targeted fix for the zero-advantage-group exploration problem in RL with verifiable rewards.

entry.title: RINI: Seeing the Prior Is Not Enough

author.name: Hongyi Du, Tianyi Zhang, Heng Wang, Zhelun Gao, Yimei Liu, Ambrose Luo, Annie Hao, Jiayan Ni, Jiawei Han, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: Studying whether providing the earlier paper corrects overclaimed novelty in LLM-generated research proposals, three controlled experiments find no clear aggregate reduction in unsupported novelty even when the prior is supplied. The authors introduce RINI, a system that audits contribution claims against evidence and checks whether proposed distinctions are actually covered by prior work.

entry.title: CompoWorld: Compositional Environment Scaling for General Agents

author.name: Xiao-Wen Yang, Weiyi Xu, Wen Da, Hang Xu, Canwei Li, Hong-Jie You, Pusen Dong, Yucheng Zeng, Zhaokai Luo, Yu-Feng Li, Yao Hu, Mu Chuan

entry.summary: CompoWorld scales training environments for general agents by composing a finite library of reusable services: coding agents turn tool specifications into verified services with typed interfaces, a world model handles unreliable tools, and random walks over dependency graphs generate tasks requiring cross-service workflows. This moves beyond single-environment task generation.

entry.title: Social Circuits behind Multi-agent Echo Chambers

author.name: Chuiyang Meng, Wenlu Yu, Ming Tang, Cheng Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces Social Circuits, a framework tracing how messages between LLM agents change receivers' internal activations and decisions, using activation-restoration to quantify message effects and diagnose echo chambers that reinforce shared errors. Building on this, Circuit-Guided Deliberation learns to select useful messages from receiver activations.

entry.title: AutoDataBench: Can Agents Write the Data That Feeds the Self-Improvement Loop?

author.name: Haotian Luo, Haoyu Wang, Zeyu Qin, Huanjin Yao, Yibo Wang, Zhuotao Tian, Shuai Wang, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: AutoDataBench evaluates whether agents can automatically create verifiable agentic training tasks, a step toward letting data production scale with compute rather than expert labor and toward recursive self-improvement. Critically, it argues that prior evaluations measure post-training performance whereas industry delivers data sample-by-sample, so it proposes matching evaluation to delivery practice. This targets a key bottleneck in modern LLM capability gains.

entry.title: TCSAlgBench: Benchmarking Automated Proving for Research-Level Theoretical Computer Science

author.name: Chutong Yang, Xiyuan Zhang, Yu Huang, Boran Han, Soonho Kong, Shuai Zhang, Vihang Prakash Patil, Zhen Han, Michael Bohlke-Schneider, Bernie Wang

entry.summary: TCSAlgBench is a benchmark and reusable pipeline for natural-language proof discovery at research level, comprising 398 theorem-level challenges from 138 STOC and COLT 2026 papers, with expert-designed rules that preserve computational assumptions and quantitative guarantees and sometimes withhold constructions so the model must discover an algorithm. It matters because competition-math benchmarks poorly proxy research-level reasoning, and TCS offers verifiable, inspectable guarantees for evaluating whether models can justify computational improvements.

entry.title: Phase Space Attention:A Hairer Lift Circumvents the Single-Layer Induction Obstruction

author.name: Kingsuk Maitra, Shagun Sood Morteza Hosseini, Suman Gunnala, Vikram Gupta

entry.summary: This highly theoretical paper circumvents the Sanford-Hsu-Telgarsky single-layer induction obstruction by lifting attention onto a symplectic phase space, mirroring Hairer's treatment of Stormer-Verlet, within a linear one-step causal bilinear design class on a post-RoPE substrate. It recasts the obstruction as a filter-order gap and proves the symplectic upper shear lift is unique within the factorization. The work connects expressivity lower bounds for transformers to numerical-analysis-style geometric constructions.

entry.title: Black-Box Auditing of Epistemic Reliability in Multi-Agent Debate Distillation

author.name: Derui Wang, Zewei Shi, Rayne Holland, Ruoxi Sun, Xingliang Yuan, Jason Xue, Liming Zhu

entry.summary: This paper studies epistemic reliability degradation in debate distillation, where a weaker verifier adapted on multi-agent debate transcripts preserves monitored performance while losing support for correct responses on hidden tasks, potentially induced by an adversarial debater. It proposes ER-Audit, a two-stage black-box auditing framework that compares frozen verifier checkpoints to detect such degradation, distinguishing it from catastrophic forgetting. This is directly relevant to AI safety around multi-agent oversight.

entry.title: When Users Change Their Minds: Measuring and Repairing Intent Drift in LLM Agents

author.name: Yanjie Zhang, Bowen Cao, Zixin Chen, Yushi Sun

entry.summary: The paper studies intent drift in multi-turn LLM agents, where superseded parts of a user's intent continue to influence final answers or tool actions. IntentFlux is an executable benchmark converting verifiable tasks into dialogues with controlled intent changes, showing task scores drop from 0.476 to 0.384 as superseded and withdrawn information accumulates, and that across eight models full correctness is lower when the final task must be recovered from an evolving dialogue. This exposes a previously under-measured multi-turn failure mode.

entry.title: The GUI Is Not the State: Diagnosing State Aliasing in GUI World Models

author.name: Dongsheng Liu, Chao Jin, Wenkui Yang, Hejin Wang, Junwei Yang, Zeren Zhang, Ziwei Chen, Huaibo Huang, Jie Cao, Ran He

entry.summary: The paper identifies state aliasing in GUI world models, where the visible interface omits transition-relevant environment state so identical observations can lead to different valid futures. It introduces StateAliasBench with strict pairing to isolate ambiguities, plus lightweight predictive-state recovery that augments frozen GUI world models via a deterministic state interface. This diagnoses a fundamental failure mode for agent planning and simulation.

entry.title: RoboFoundry: System-as-Policy Evolution for Self-Learning Embodied Agents

author.name: Jingsong Liang, Shuhao Liao, Shizhe Zhang, Diyuan Hou, Yuxin Cai, Xinjian Deng, Chengyang He, Wenhui Huang, Runjia Tan, Zhidong Wang, Lan Yu, Xuesong Tian, Guillaume Sartoretti, Jie Luo, Yao Mu, Wenjun Wu, Wanhua Li, Chen Lv

entry.summary: RoboFoundry proposes treating an embodied agent's entire supporting system (memory, context, skills, action interfaces) as a unified evolving policy rather than optimizing components in isolation. It diagnoses capability gaps, converts execution traces into validated system updates, and promotes recurring improvements into general capabilities. This systems-level self-evolution framing is a fresh contribution to agent architecture research.

entry.title: KoopCell: Koopman-Based Generative Model for Learning Single-Cell Dynamics from Distribution Snapshots

author.name: Wanfeng Lu, Yutong Zhang, Keyi Zhou, Chenxin Ge, Wei Lin, Qunxi Zhu

entry.summary: KoopCell is a generative framework based on Koopman-Mori-Zwanzig theory that learns single-cell population dynamics from temporally sparse, unpaired distribution snapshots, jointly learning representations and linear latent dynamics. It derives a closed-form least-squares estimator for the Koopman generator with convergence guarantees and supports developmental branching. It addresses extrapolation limits of neural-ODE and flow-matching approaches in developmental biology.

entry.title: Program-Verified Self-Evolution for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ahmed Heakl, Sungik Choi, Moontae Lee, Salman Khan

entry.summary: The paper finds that 24% of majority-vote and 18% of model-judge labels in self-evolving VLM training are wrong, and proposes VQS, which parses images into structured records (scene graphs, chart tables, diagram graphs) and uses fixed programs to generate questions and compute verified answers. The model still generates the questions, but answers become programmatically checkable. This substantially reduces label noise in self-supervised VLM improvement.

entry.title: Video, Ergo Genero: Unifying Video Tasks via Spatiotemporal Analogy

author.name: Chia-Hsiang Kao, Belinda Zeng, Bharath Hariharan, Menglin Jia

entry.summary: ViGeo extends visual in-context learning from images to video via spatiotemporal canvas completion, allowing video models to take on new tasks training-free by analogy. It generalizes to unseen video manipulations and zero-shot modalities such as event cameras under a strict train-test split, and identifies a task-internalization phenomenon where pretrained task query formats override in-context specification. This is a meaningful step toward unified, task-agnostic video models.

entry.title: Certified Multi-Source Integrity for Structured Agent Actions

author.name: Anmol Pandey, Aditya Jain, Liang Chen, Carsten Maple, Christo Panchev

entry.summary: The paper addresses LLM agents performing privileged irreversible structured actions (e.g., paying an invoice) assembled from fields in documents and tool outputs that adversaries can corrupt, including via indirect prompt injection. It characterizes when a coupled, policy-bound structured action is safely certifiable under a corruption budget accounting for shared upstream sources, and gives the maximally live safe certifier. A formal-security take on agent action integrity that goes beyond trust labels and free-text answer certification.

entry.title: One Sequence, Many Decodings: CAGenMol-2 Recasts Drug Design as Masked Molecular Inference

author.name: Yanting Li, Enyan Dai, Lei Wang, Wen-Cai Ye, Li Liu

entry.summary: CAGenMol-2 is a masked diffusion molecular language model representing molecules, scalar properties, and 3D protein pockets in a single wrapped sequence, where downstream tasks are selected by which regions are masked at inference. One checkpoint handles property prediction, property- and pocket-conditioned generation, and partial-constraint design without task-specific architectures or fine-tuning. It unifies fragmented drug-design ML capabilities in a single model.

entry.title: Riccati State Space Models: Non-iterative Parallelization for Nonlinear Sequence Modeling

author.name: M\'onika Farsang, Ramin Hasani, Daniela Rus, Radu Grosu

entry.summary: RiccatiSSM introduces a nonlinear state space model where each state dimension follows an input-conditioned Riccati differential equation whose quadratic structure preserves exact composability. This allows parallel scan evaluation of nonlinear recurrent dynamics without the iterative linearization required by other nonlinear SSMs.

entry.title: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models with Interleaved Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yijia Fan, Ziqi Huang, Zhongang Cai, Yan Li, Zimo Wen, Wanqi Yin, Haiwen Diao, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: Introduces UMM-Reflection, an RL approach that trains unified multimodal models to repair their own image generations by jointly optimizing reflection text and rendering over the full generate-diagnose-revise loop. Sibling trajectories share initializations to make the joint RL over whole reflection trajectories tractable, going beyond SFT cold starts.

entry.title: KernelZero: Co-Evolving Proposer and Coder for Continuously Improved GPU Kernel Generation

author.name: Changxin Ke, Rui Zhang, Zixiang Fang, Zhenghong Li, Yuanbo Wen, Jiashuo Shen, Shuo Wang, Jiaming Guo, Ling Li, Qi Guo, Yunji Chen

entry.summary: KernelZero is a co-evolution framework for automated GPU kernel generation using two specialized models: a Proposer generating Torch modules from API sets and a Coder translating them into CUDA or Triton kernels, with frontier-driven module generation to continually produce training data aligned with model capability. It addresses the scarcity of high-quality training data and the correctness-performance trade-off in LLM kernel synthesis. This is relevant to ML systems efficiency at scale.

entry.title: SALMONN-duo: Adaptive Dual-System Coordination for Full-Duplex Voice Agents

author.name: Wenyi Yu, Siyin Wang, Terumi Chiba, Xianzhao Chen, Xiaohai Tian, Jun Zhang, Lu Lu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: SALMONN-duo is an adaptive dual-system voice agent pairing an always-on fast-thinking full-duplex speech LLM (system 1) with a powerful asynchronous slow-thinking LLM agent (system 2), inspired by dual-process theories of cognition. System 1 learns when to answer directly and when to delegate deliberation or tool use to system 2, reconciling real-time latency with deliberative capability. This targets a key tension in real-world full-duplex voice assistants.

entry.title: Understanding On-Policy Distillation: A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective via Sparse Crosscoders

author.name: Zichao Yu, Qianshuo Ye, Xu Wang, Difan Zou

entry.summary: The paper uses sparse crosscoders to study what on-policy distillation actually transfers into a student model's internal representations, proposing a swap readout that measures how training changes the student's use of shared features. This moves beyond standard crosscoder analyses that only identify model-specific features.

entry.title: Residual Diffusion Implicit Models

author.name: Jo\~ao Guerreiro, Pedro Tom\'as, Helena Aidos, Jacinto C. Nascimento

entry.summary: RDIMs generalize diffusion bridges and consistency models by explicitly modeling residuals between high-quality and low-quality images, aligning the forward process with real-world degradations instead of starting from pure Gaussian noise. This unified framework avoids the long reverse processes and hallucination issues of bridges while retaining variance modeling that one-step consistency models lack.

entry.title: ReDrive: Shaping Representations with World Modeling for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Yueting Zhu, Shaoyu Chen, Yuehao Song, Hui Sun, Qian Zhang, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: ReDrive is an end-to-end driving framework that strengthens planning-oriented visual features via future representation prediction, arguing that strong visual representations combined with representation-level world modeling can support planning without complex perception-planning pipelines or inference-time auxiliary modules. It simplifies the architecture compared with explicit state-predicting world models. This follows the trend of representation-centric end-to-end autonomous driving.

entry.title: Uranus: Building the Next-Generation Simulation Infrastructure for Embodied AI

author.name: Wenkang Qin, Yukun Zhou, Noah Shen, Jisong Cai, Dongxiao Mao, Baicheng Li, Yue Zhang, Wei Sui

entry.summary: Uranus is a data-driven robot simulator built on a joint-trajectory-conditioned autoregressive diffusion model, offering open-ended streaming rollouts (one latent frame per step, no fixed horizon), low-latency generation at 24 FPS after optimization, and a unified extensible robot control interface. It targets scalable data generation, policy training, evaluation, and safe iteration for embodied AI.

entry.title: Is the J-Space a global workspace for multi-hop reasoning? An investigation in open-weight models

author.name: Mirella Zeisler

entry.summary: The author replicates Anthropic's J-lens multi-hop reasoning experiment on open-weight Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma 3 27B-it, finding that counterfactual answer swaps outperformed intermediate swaps in three of four conditions. This fails to support Anthropic's hypothesis that the J-space is a global reasoning workspace, suggesting J-lens is more useful for probing intermediate variables than for steering outputs.

entry.title: LLM Judge Validation Under Sparse Overlap: From Inference to Design

author.name: Junxuan Li, Arko Mukherjee, Soumyabrata Pal

entry.summary: This paper studies how sparse human-human annotation overlap affects LLM-as-a-judge validation, proving that overlap sparsity is the first-order determinant of wrong deployment decisions, with 25 percent wrong-decision rates at 5 percent overlap. The authors derive a minimum-overlap formula (at least 0.25 for non-borderline judges) and a zero-cost stratified allocation scheme that halves false-rejection rates. These are actionable design guidelines for anyone using human agreement to validate LLM judges.

entry.title: Residual Streams Read, Recurrent States Remember: The Global Workspace in Mamba Models

author.name: Wenlong Wang, Fergal Reid

entry.summary: This interpretability work fits Jacobian lenses to residual streams and recurrent states of Mamba-1/2/3 state-space models, showing that joint residual-state readouts recover more intermediate concepts than residual-only lenses. It also proposes sign-guarded steering and demonstrates that recurrent states retain earlier content as residual visibility changes.

entry.title: Delayed Supervision for Test-Time Language Models

author.name: Jinha Kim, Taksh Kothari

entry.summary: The paper studies how to train test-time-adapting language models (fast-weight models like LaCT, DeltaNet, RWKV-7) so facts remain accessible in memory after many subsequent updates. It introduces delayed supervision: post-training questions are asked only after long intervals of unrelated events, with answers supervised on disposable branches so they never contaminate the event stream. This targets long-horizon memory retention in linear-attention and fast-weight architectures.

entry.title: ForkLeft: Entropy-First Rollouts for Prefix-Aligned Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Distillation

author.name: Junming Liu, Jicheng Wang, Yifeng He, Hao Chen, Jianzhong Qi

entry.summary: ForkLeft is a distillation framework enabling diffusion language models to acquire autoregressive next-token-prediction-style reasoning without abandoning their native generation process. It resolves the fundamental mismatch that an AR teacher predicts from a left prefix while a DLM can condition on tokens on both sides, using entropy-first rollouts that commit uncertain positions and expose fork points, with student rollout separated from teacher supervision. This targets the open question of transferring NTP reasoning strengths to DLMs.

entry.title: AmbiModBench: Benchmarking Gene Perturbation Prediction Beyond Shared Responses

author.name: Sikai Huang, Zhiwen Yang, Kai Yu, Jiayuan Chen, Stan Z. Li

entry.summary: Introduces AmbiModBench, a specificity-aware, gene-resolved, coverage-aware benchmark for gene perturbation prediction that addresses three evaluation flaws: inability to separate target-specific predictions from shared background responses, inflated scores under gene shuffling, and single-size training scores that ignore coverage. It pairs every score with ambiguity and coverage diagnostics to clarify what model performance actually demonstrates.

entry.title: SWE-MILE: Asynchronous Potential-Induced Milestone Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Chaoqun Cui, Hao Zhou, Meiqi Chen, Fandong Meng, Wenji Mao

entry.summary: Proposes SWE-MILE, a credit-assignment method for RL-trained long-horizon software engineering agents that derives fine-grained process supervision from workflow runtime signals like file exposure and test-state alignment, without auxiliary reward models. Potential differences attribute milestone progress or regressions to individual actions. This targets the sparse terminal-reward bottleneck in RLVR for agentic coding.

entry.title: X-Tree: Tokenizing Reusable Experience for Efficient Agent Generalization

author.name: Sitao Cheng, Xunjian Yin, Zhiyuan Sun, Yuxuan Li, Ruiwen Zhou, Xiangru Jian, Victor Zhong

entry.summary: X-Tree recovers hierarchical reusable sub-procedures from flat agent trajectories by scoring action spans for reusability and merging canonicalized actions into an experience tree, then trains on this hierarchy directly in the weights without LLM calls. Unlike in-context skill approaches, gains are baked into the model and can generalize beyond retrieval. This addresses inefficient flat token-level SFT and RLVR training that ignores recurring structure.

entry.title: SRE-Marathon: A Continuous, Change-Driven Benchmark for Autonomous Site Reliability Agents

author.name: Yifang Tian, Yingjian Bai, Yifeng He, Zichun Chong, Yuanchen Gao, Yiran Li, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

entry.summary: SRE-Marathon is a benchmark for evaluating autonomous site reliability engineering agents in long-horizon, continuous operation rather than the typical one-fault-one-task episodic setup. Agents operate a live two-zone Kubernetes deployment, respond at a fixed cadence to cumulative noisy alert histories, and handle overlapping faults injected on a seeded, production-calibrated schedule alongside curated code and configuration changes. This better reflects real production conditions and enables measurement of sustained autonomous performance.

entry.title: Are Benchmarks Reliable? Toward Structural Diagnosis via Sample-Level Capability Boundaries

author.name: Haiquan Hu, Yuzhu Liang, Weicheng Tang, Yanzeng Li, Yao Shi, Tian Wang

entry.summary: BSDProbe is a sample-level framework for diagnosing benchmark structure that estimates capability boundaries from repeated-response trajectories across ordered model axes, summarizing boundary position, width, signal validity, and order consistency. Experiments on six benchmarks show reliability is heterogeneous: GSM8K and MATH are most stable, while MMLU and TriviaQA are weaker in places.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Analog Design Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hours-Long Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuit Design Tasks

author.name: Analog Design Bench Team
