entry.summary: The paper targets language-model synthesis of Clifford circuits, where exact classical verification is possible, using Aaronson-Gottesman chain-of-thought traces checked by an exact verifier and continued training on verifier-accepted model generations. Across two model families (3B and 7B), verified AG-CoT supervision multiplies greedy-decode state-equivalence accuracy.

entry.title: The Price of Locality: Why Forward-Forward Underperforms Backpropagation?

author.name: Zhaoxian Wu, Haichuan Liu, Tianyi Chen

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses two structural failure modes of the Forward-Forward algorithm versus backpropagation: an optimization floor from concurrent local updates inducing inter-layer representation-distribution drift, and a geometric collapse of layer representations driven by the local contrastive mechanism. It proves per-layer PL inequality satisfaction while explaining the persistent depth-worsening gap.

entry.title: Towards Identifiable Representations under Misspecified Structure

author.name: Yuke Li, Yujia Zheng, Ziyi Chen, Kun Zhang, Heng Huang

entry.summary: The paper extends latent variable identifiability theory to misspecified structure, where conditional independence of observations given latents fails, treating misspecification as a perturbed factor analysis problem. It establishes subspace and component-wise identifiability under spectral separation, structural sparsity, and controlled perturbation, plus approximate guarantees when precise conditions fail.

entry.title: MoGround: Measuring and Mitigating Modality Distraction in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Luca Zhou, Bo Zhao, Rose Yu, Emanuele Rodol\`a, Roberto Dess\`i

entry.summary: MoGround is a vision-language dataset across four domains where every question is answerable from exactly one modality, enabling clean measurement of modality distraction (correct single-modality answers flipping wrong when irrelevant cross-modal content is added). Across seven open-source VLMs, distraction is model-dependent, tracks the weaker-grounded modality (r = +0.86), and scales inversely with grounding quality.

entry.title: Geometric Identification in Predict-Then-Optimize Learning

author.name: Jiaxiao Xu, Changhong Mou, Keji Liu, Dinghua Xu, Yeyu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical characterization of when decision-focused learning surrogates, specifically the convex SPO+ population risk, uniquely identify the underlying optimal decisions without recovering the quotient report itself. The authors derive conditions under central symmetry under which the centered mean class is the unique Bayes minimizer, separating face-crossing behavior from selected-oracle disagreement, and extend identification results to non-symmetric and conditional settings. This deepens the foundations of predict-then-optimize learning, an area relevant to decision-making under prediction uncertainty.

entry.title: Hamiltonian JEPA: Action-Conditioned World Models with an Inherited Control State

author.name: Tamim Zoabi, Ameen Ali, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: H-JEPA separates perception from control in action-conditioned JEPAs: a wide perceptual code is regularized with a Bures-Wasserstein prior, and a fixed orthonormal slice serves as a control state evolving under phase-conditioned dissipative port-Hamiltonian dynamics. This organizes the planner-scored state by how actions move the system, improving planning from pixels.

entry.title: Approximating Softmax in Pretrained LLMs: Model Sensitivity and Kernel Acceleration

author.name: Shangzhen Zhu, Muyan Hu, Tomasz Kozlowski

entry.summary: This study characterizes how accurately pretrained LLMs actually need softmax evaluated, testing ten frozen decoder-only models from 0.5B to 72B on NVIDIA Blackwell B200 hardware where exponential throughput lags tensor cores by two orders of magnitude. It finds that the number of positions assigned probability and within-row resolution can be cut substantially, with placement near the row maximum mattering as much as budget size.

entry.title: Rethinking Contextualization by Reinterpreting Attention Head Channels

author.name: Hakaze Cho, Haolin Yang, Zhun Sun, Naoya Inoue, Benjamin Heinzerling, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: Proposes a global principle for how transformer contextualization works: words carry different amounts of information, and less-informative words absorb more contextual information, with channel-level selectivity enabling precise routing between matched words. The work reinterprets attention head channels to characterize contextualization behavior beyond per-head dictionary views.

entry.title: MISHAP-Bench: A Hallucination Benchmark for Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Zhi Wen Soi, Giulio Segalini, Jian-Jia Chen, Lydia Chen

entry.summary: Introduces MISHAP-Bench, a 12,000-question benchmark with open-ended audio-question pairs that distinguishes context hallucinations (claims not grounded in the audio) from knowledge hallucinations (claims lacking external factual support), with a rigorous evaluation pipeline for open-ended responses. This disentangles hallucination from simple audio-understanding failures in large audio-language models.

entry.title: Vision--Language Signals in Constrained RL: Safety Gains Without Anticipation

author.name: Samuel Tetteh, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: VLM-Safe-RL integrates frozen CLIP signals into PPO-Lagrangian via reward shaping and an augmented multiplier update for safe reinforcement learning in driving. Notably, the paper's analysis questions whether VLM scores actually anticipate collisions, finding safety gains arise without genuine hazard anticipation, and it addresses the failure mode where episodic costs favor policies making little task progress.

entry.title: Transfer Calibrated Prediction Powered Inference

author.name: Aditya T. Vadlamani, Jae Ho Chang, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, Subhadeep Paul

entry.summary: TC-PPI extends prediction-powered inference to settings where the AI predictor was trained on a different source domain, adapting it to the target via cross-fitting with gold-standard samples using methods like linear calibration, LoRA, or fine-tuning. The proposed Joint-TC-Cross-PPI++ preserves unbiasedness while remaining at least as efficient as classical baselines.

entry.title: X-MoD: Practical Scaling Laws for Sparse-Depth Routing Beyond Mixture-of-Depths

author.name: Bowen Dong, Yilong Fan, Tengyu Pan, Yike Zhang, Zhenyu Li, Zijian Zhang, Xuewei Li, Mei Yu, Jianyong Wang

entry.summary: X-MoD extends Mixture-of-Depths by decoupling token sparsity from anchor stride so total parameter count can grow while active-equivalent capacity stays fixed, combining dense anchors, variance-scaled gating, and depth-wise token balancing to make deep sparse routing trainable. It also formulates sparse-depth routing as a conditional architecture-design problem and derives practical scaling laws.

entry.title: Epistemic Learning from Imprecise Annotation

author.name: Kaizheng Wang, Siu Lun Chau

entry.summary: This paper proposes learning from credal supervision, where convex sets of plausible labelling distributions (credal sets) are used as training supervision and the model learns sets of predictive distributions rather than collapsing ambiguity into one. It instantiates this with a pessimistic-optimistic credal classifier combining two heads trained on worst- and best-case losses, whose output spread provides calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

entry.title: ZonoGPT: Towards An Abstract Domain for Verifying Large GPT Models

author.name: Hai Duong, Thanh Le, ThanhVu Nguyen

entry.summary: ZonoGPT introduces an abstract domain for formal verification of large Transformer models whose space complexity is independent of network depth, using structured zonotopes and generator reduction to preserve correlations, plus block-wise precision techniques. This extends neural network verification beyond the small or restricted Transformers that prior work has been limited to.

entry.title: Brain-Conditioned Action Policies for Neural Motor Decoding

author.name: Luyao Jin, Running Zhao, Huan Zhao, Vincent C. K. Cheung, Wei-Hsin Liao

entry.summary: BrainVLA adapts a pretrained vision-language-action model (OpenVLA-OFT) to motor brain-computer interfaces via language-mediated alignment, constructing datasets pairing neural activity, actions, language instructions, and rendered visual observations. This mitigates the scarcity of paired neural-action data for paralyzed users controlling devices.

entry.title: AgentPerfBench: A Benchmarking and Evaluation Suite for Inference Performance of Agentic LLMs

author.name: Cheuk Hang Lau, Zeyu Cao, Kevin Wong Cheuk Yin, Yao Lai, Haoran Wu, Nicholas D. Lane, Robert D. Mullins, Ilia Shumailov, Yiren Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces AgentPerfBench, a benchmark suite for LLM serving performance in the agentic era, using real traces from SWE-Bench and TerminalBench alongside chat baselines to capture multi-turn requests with growing context lengths. It exposes the mismatch between existing single-turn chatbot workload benchmarks and modern agentic serving demands.

entry.title: When Sparse Reward Meets Dense Distillation: Training Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xinke Jiang, Tao Feng, Zhibang Yang, Zhixin Zhang, Weixuan Xu, Haoyu Zhang, Xu Chu

entry.summary: Studies the interaction between sparse verifiable-reward RL and dense token-level teacher KL distillation in LLM post-training, using neural tangent kernel analysis to explain why joint training can destabilize. The work identifies dynamics of hybrid reward-distillation training and presumably proposes stabilization. It is timely given the growing use of on-policy distillation to complement RLVR.

entry.title: GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Haodong Zhu, Yangyang Ren, Changbai Li, Sheng Xu, Linlin Yang, haiguang liu, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: GraphHCA provides a model-free realization of hindsight credit assignment for LLM agent training, eliminating the need for explicit hindsight-distribution estimation via auxiliary models or extra passes. It attributes credit through ratios of hindsight to behavior-policy probabilities in a closed form, targeting sparse terminal-reward agentic tasks.

entry.title: $\lambda$-JEPA Spectral Anti-Collapse Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Berker Demirel, Cl\'ementine Domin\'e, Valentino Maiorca, Marco Fumero, Marco Mondelli, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: Identifies that joint-embedding self-supervised learning can suffer dimensional collapse in the backbone even when the projection head prevents it, limiting downstream transfer. The paper introduces SACReg, a spectral anti-collapse regularizer grounded in an analysis of lambda-balance of weight matrix scales, with theory in two-layer linear networks. This addresses a known failure mode of SSL methods with a principled fix.

entry.title: Persistent Partners Raise Prices Among Learning Agents

author.name: Paul-Peter Arslan, Yubin Kim, Xiao Xiao

entry.summary: A pre-registered randomized experiment on algorithmic collusion in the Bertrand duopoly setting of Calvano et al., testing how platform matching policy affects learned pricing. Keeping the same partner raises average profits by 0.27 of the competitive-to-monopoly gap, with tight confidence intervals across all twenty paired runs, while randomizing partner persistence, price visibility, and messaging. Directly relevant to economics and AI policy on algorithmic collusion.

entry.title: Deep Epistemic Value Functions for Optimistic Exploration

author.name: Leander Diaz-Bone, Marco Bagatella, Jonas H\"ubotter, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: This systematic study examines how epistemic uncertainty over value functions is represented, propagated, and optimized in deep RL, identifying distinct failure modes on each axis. The findings motivate DEVOTE, a model-free optimistic-exploration algorithm that controls uncertainty generalization, stabilizes temporal propagation, and preserves additivity, improving deep exploration robustly.

entry.title: FOCUS: Fixed-Confidence Online Causal Learning Using Sequential Adaptive Interventions

author.name: Haijie Xu, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: FOCUS addresses fully online fixed-confidence causal discovery starting from zero samples, where a learner sequentially selects interventions to recover both the causal DAG and edge weights under a linear-Gaussian structural equation model. The authors establish an instance-dependent lower bound and prove FOCUS is (epsilon, delta)-correct with expected stopping time matching the lower bound, using a novel computable concentration inequality for KL divergence of parameters shared across interventions. A strong theoretical result in best-arm-identification-style causal learning.

entry.title: JEPA Learns What the Mask Leaves Unrecoverable

author.name: Peng Xie, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: The paper gives a theoretical account of why joint-embedding predictive architectures are highly sensitive to mask design, modeling masks as linear measurements in a wavelet basis where hidden-region atoms fall in the null space. It shows the JEPA loss admits shortcuts recoverable by low-level priors unless targets retain coarse-scale content the mask leaves unrecoverable, explaining why block masks work and scattered masks do not.

entry.title: SAGE: Semantic Audio Generative Encoder

author.name: Francesco Brigante, Luca Cerovaz, Davide Marincione, Giorgio Strano, Luca Zhou, Emanuele Rodol\`a, Michele Mancusi

entry.summary: SAGE is a compact 105M-parameter audio autoencoder that shapes its latent space by distilling embeddings from a pretrained audio-text model, trained only on publicly available music. It matches the listening-test quality of an autoencoder 8x larger and 4x slower while running at the inference cost of Stable Audio Open, better balancing reconstruction quality, semantic latent structure, and speed.

entry.title: Can Tabular Foundation Models Amortize Statistical Inference?

author.name: Kai Ye, Shijin Gong, Hongyi Zhou, Valentina Zangirolami, Chengchun Shi

entry.summary: Proposes TabCon, an amortized inference system built on a tabular foundation model that produces confidence intervals for new datasets in a single forward pass, using a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture and RL-based post-training to calibrate coverage. This reframes classical statistical inference as an amortized prediction problem.

entry.title: Neural Scaling Laws of Transformer Operator Network

author.name: Haoran Yan, Zhongjie Shi, Yuanzhe Xi, Peng Chen, Wenjing Liao

entry.summary: This work builds a theoretical framework for approximation and generalization error scaling of transformer-based operator learning for physical systems, leveraging a local-to-global approximation principle aligned with softmax attention. It derives universal approximation and scaling-law results with discretization-invariant outputs. This gives one of the first rigorous scaling-law treatments for transformers in scientific operator learning.

entry.title: Tokens Change, Structure Endures: Spectral Watermarking for Generated Speech

author.name: Kanghwi Lee, Kyeongseok Jeong, Jeongmin Liu

entry.summary: Redwing is a training-free, token-level watermarking method for AI-generated speech that remains robust to retokenization by building a graph of observed token substitutions and watermarking in the Laplacian eigenbasis so tokens likely to substitute for each other carry similar values. This addresses the main weakness of token-level watermarking, which erodes when audio is decoded and re-encoded.

entry.title: 3D Point Tracking with State Space Models

author.name: Masahiro Ogawa, Qi An, Atsushi Yamashita

entry.summary: The paper presents a monocular, pose-free 3D point tracker achieving metric accuracy in absolute meters on a single commodity GPU. It composes two frozen front-ends, dense optical flow for 2D correspondence and a monocular metric-depth network, and learns only a residual component using state space models, exploiting the observation that metric accuracy is governed by depth along a point's pixel ray once the 2D trajectory is fixed.

entry.title: The Model Knows When to Stop: Training-Free Early Stopping for Long-Context Reading

author.name: Muath Alyobi, Mohamed Eltahir, Almoayyad Abuljdail, Riyadh Almutawa, Tanveer Hussain, Naeemullah Khan

entry.summary: The paper introduces Answer-Convergence Stopping (ACS), a training-free rule that lets a frozen language model stop reading long-context chunks when its current answer state is both confident and stable. Unlike learned sufficiency predictors or trained exit gates, ACS only requires output-side generation and token log probabilities, with a single shared configuration across models and benchmarks. This can substantially reduce wasted computation when sufficient evidence has already been acquired.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Next-Token Prediction under Markovian Data

author.name: Masoud Kavian, Abdellatif Zaidi, Milad Sefidgaran

entry.summary: The paper develops an information-theoretic framework for generalization in next-token prediction under temporally dependent data, considering trajectories from finite-memory Markov processes. It distinguishes algorithmic dependence (mutual information) from temporal dependence (mixing) and derives expected generalization bounds for cross-entropy loss using Donsker-Varadhan variational representation and a McDiarmid-type concentration inequality for Markov chains. Refinements capture the joint effect of context length and mixing, and extend through a rate-distortion formulation.

entry.title: Convex Optimization Is Free When Accuracy Is Expensive

author.name: Arthur Paing, Arthur Jacot

entry.summary: This theory paper studies convex optimization when gradients can only be approximated by a hierarchy of algorithms whose cost scales as delta to the minus gamma. In the Harder-Than-Monte-Carlo regime (gamma greater than 2), it shows optimization costs no more than a single gradient evaluation at the required accuracy, and introduces a randomized multilevel oracle making variance an independently priced dial.

entry.title: Learned Preconditioning for a Primal-Dual Interior-Point Method

author.name: Abhinav Madabhushi, Jialin Liu, Minxin Zhang

entry.summary: The authors present pdLIP, an interior-point method for smooth nonlinear programs that combines a learned coordinate-wise recurrent network predicting a diagonal preconditioner with pdProj, an all-shifted primal-dual projected-search method. The work tackles the difficulty that logarithmic barrier singularities make learned optimization updates unreliable near constraint boundaries. It is a concrete step toward learned components inside classical second-order optimizers.

entry.title: IndicFDB: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Voice Agents across Indian Languages

author.name: Rajarshi Roy, Shobhit Banga, Jonathan Raiman, Supriya Paul, Bhaskar Singh, Manmeet Kaur, Sagar Jain, Hanuman Sidh, Pranav Sharma, Aditya Singh, Aaditya Pareek, Manas Dhir, Adi Margolin, Niket Agarwal, Bryan Catanzaro

entry.summary: IndicFDB extends Full-Duplex-Bench to ten Indian languages with 12,350 samples, nearly 17 times the original, mined from roughly 50,000 hours of channel-separated conversational audio to test pause handling, turn taking, backchanneling, and interruption behavior. It solves three technical challenges: detecting conversational events in multilingual speech, evaluating timing without reliable word-level alignment, and cross-lingual response judging. This enables rigorous evaluation of real-time voice agents beyond English.

entry.title: Locally Sound, Globally Insufficient: The Local-Global Gap in Multi-Hop Reasoning

author.name: Bohao Chu, Hendrik Damm, Qianli Wang, Hui Wang, Shuning Zhang, Christoph M. Friedrich, Norbert Fuhr

entry.summary: This paper defines and measures the local-global gap (LGG) in multi-hop QA: reasoning traces where every step is locally supported by evidence and prior steps, yet the trace fails to establish the submitted answer globally. In a human-adjudicated diagnostic of 2,598 responses across three multi-hop benchmarks and three models, LGG occurs in every combination and accounts for nearly half of globally insufficient responses. It provides an important new failure taxonomy for reasoning reliability and evaluation.

entry.title: On the Behavioral Traits of LLM Agents

author.name: Haokai Zhao, Jie Gao, Yunze Xiao, Xintao Wang, Weihao Xuan, Aditya Joshi, Mark Dredze, Jen-tse Huang

entry.summary: This paper proposes A-B-D, a framework for inferring agent personality traits bottom-up from behavioral data recorded in real trajectories, addressing the gap between self-reports and actual behavior and the cost of informant ratings. From 345,667 real-world trajectories spanning 80 models, 12 tasks, and 50 harnesses, it extracts 318 candidate behavioral features. Large-scale behavioral characterization of agents is valuable for both product understanding and safety monitoring.

entry.title: Shared Experience, Separate Learning: Companion Confidence Calibration for LLMs

author.name: Shiyu Ni, Keping Bi, Jiafeng Guo, Yilong Xu, Jingtong Wu, Zengxin Han, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: The paper targets concurrent confidence calibration, where confidence is learned alongside capability during RLVR training rather than post-hoc. The authors argue existing methods couple two distinct learning problems in shared policy parameters and instead propose separate learning from shared experience, with a companion model learning confidence while the policy improves. This addresses a core reliability issue: LLMs remaining confident when wrong.

entry.title: InfiMed2: A Generalist Medical Multimodal Foundation Model from Contextual Evidence and Stability-Aware Supervision

author.name: Guanghao Zhu, Zeyu Liu, Zhitian Hou, Pengkai Wang, Zhijie Sang, Shuo Cai, Yang Yu, Yuanyi Wang, Yanggan Gu, Congkai Xie, Jianmin Wu, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: InfiMed2 is a family of 4B and 27B generalist medical multimodal foundation models built around stage-aware data design across continued pretraining and post-training, with a curated 55.68M-instance corpus. It emphasizes stability-aware supervision for informative, answer-consistent medical explanations rather than short-form VQA.

entry.title: OLED-MoE: Accelerating MoE-Based dLLM Inference via Inter-Iteration Locality-Aware Expert Offloading

author.name: Jingyuan Xiao (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Jiayue Wang (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Yitao Hu (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Xinning Wang (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Shi Chen (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Ziqi Gong (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Zhengchao Wang (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Guotao Yang (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Sheng Chen (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Keqiu Li (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China)

entry.summary: Targets inference efficiency for mixture-of-experts diffusion language models, where block-wise denoising breaks the layer-wise prefetching assumptions of autoregressive MoE serving systems. OLED-MoE uses inter-iteration locality-aware expert offloading to fit large expert footprints within memory-constrained GPUs.

entry.title: Measuring the evolution of camera distance across a century of film

author.name: David Bamman, Allison Cooper, Dan Hickey, Madison Mar

entry.summary: Using computer vision on 5,205 digitized films from 1922 to 2025, the authors trace how camera-subject distance has evolved, finding abrupt shifts tied to sound and television technologies. The analysis also quantifies gender disparity, showing women receive less screentime but are disproportionately framed in closer shots.

entry.title: Devol-ONE: One Autoregressive Mixture of Transformers to Unify Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling

author.name: Hongyi Cai, Yi Herng Ong, Tingshiuan C. Wu, Lim Chiew Hui, Hanxia Li, Kehong Guo, Sze Yuan Cheong

entry.summary: Devol-ONE unifies vision-language understanding, latent world dynamics prediction, and action generation in a single autoregressive Mixture of Transformers architecture, closing the gap between world models and policies that prior designs kept architecturally separate. Instead of separate video prediction or independently trained latent forecasting modules, all three capabilities share one framework.

entry.title: OpenMASC: An Open-Source Pipeline for Cross-Trajectory Metal-Aware Sampling and Correction in Accelerated MRI

author.name: Zhengyi Lu, Ming Lu, Chongyu Qu, Junchao Zhu, Junlin Guo, Marilyn Lionts, Yanfan Zhu, Yuechen Yang, Tianyuan Yao, Jayasai Rajagopal, Bennett Allan Landman, Xiao Wang, Xinqiang Yan, Yuankai Huo

entry.summary: OpenMASC is an open-source pipeline covering data generation through deployment for metal artifact reduction in accelerated MRI, where implants corrupt k-space across sampling trajectories. It includes a physics-based module converting CT volumes into paired clean and metal-corrupted MRI data in Cartesian and radial formats, plus MA-VarNet, an unrolled reconstruction network with per-cascade DC rectification.

entry.title: UnStep: Training-Free Acceleration of Causal Video Diffusion with Fewer Steps Than Distillation

author.name: Youssef Mansour, Enis Simsar, Fadime Sener, Markos Georgopoulos, Albert Pumarola, Ali Thabet, Edgar Schoenfeld

entry.summary: UnStep is a training-free wrapper that accelerates few-step causal video diffusion models by running fewer DiT steps than used during distillation and limiting the KV-cache temporal window in attention. Quality is recovered via renoising latent frames toward a clean level and reusing existing states, enabling near real-time streaming generation.

entry.title: Latent Space Is Not Flat: Rethinking Latent Structure for 3D Medical Image Synthesis

author.name: Haowen Xue, Hao Chen, Hexuan Hu, Qian Huang, Yi Han, Qing Meng, Zaipeng Xie, Chao Li, Haoli Xu

entry.summary: Shows that the flat Euclidean assumption in latent generative models for 3D medical image synthesis is inaccurate: latent space is strongly anisotropic, with sensitive variation concentrated in a low-rank subspace capturing spatially coordinated structure. The paper builds a synthesis method exploiting this asymmetry between dominant low-rank and orthogonal residual components.

entry.title: Rethinking the Fully Hyperbolic Vision Transformer in Polar Coordinates

author.name: Ahmad Bdeir, Niels Landwehr

entry.summary: This paper identifies numerical instability in Lorentzian inner products at large radii as the reason hyperbolic vision transformers underuse the geometry's hierarchical capacity, and reformulates transformer blocks in polar coordinates where distances and attention centroids avoid numerical cancellation. This enables fully hyperbolic models to exploit large-radius regions stably.

entry.title: RepFlow: Reciprocal Supervision Improves Generation and Representation in Flow Models

author.name: Weili Zeng, Feng Tian, Shengqi Liu, Yichao Yan

entry.summary: RepFlow learns a stable visual representation from a flow-matching generator's evolving computation via a timestep-free encoder trained to recover generator states across depths and noise levels from masked clean images, then uses this representation to guide generation. This reciprocal supervision improves both generation quality and representation quality, addressing the entanglement of noise level and network depth in generator states.

entry.title: OPERA: A Unified Omnimodal Progressive Spatio-Temporal Reasoning Agent for Referring Video Segmentation

author.name: Jingchen Ni, Yuji Wang, Shannan Yan, Haoru Li, Sitong Chen, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: Presents OPERA, a unified reasoning agent on a single MLLM for referring video segmentation with heterogeneous queries spanning text, audio, and reference images. It performs dual-axis progressive reasoning through temporal coarse-to-fine key-frame filtering, cross-modal semantic distillation, and GRPO-enhanced grounding. This raises the ceiling on multimodal query support for video segmentation.

entry.title: TT-VidT: Decoupling the Temporal Axis for Efficient Motion-Centric Video Pretraining

author.name: Shih-Ying Yeh, Daniel Z. Kaplan, Xuehai Wang, Fu-En Yang, Min-Hung Chen, Shang-Hong Lai

entry.summary: TT-VidT is the product of a carefully controlled 24-configuration architecture-objective study (~170M-190M encoders, ~1.7M clips) designed to isolate which choices yield motion-prioritized video representations. The method combines a DINOv3-initialized per-frame spatial path with a compact Temporal Transfer Layer trained via a Diff Compression reconstruction objective.

entry.title: Learning Multimodal Embeddings with Evidence-Aligned Readout

author.name: Zirong Chen, Fuda Ye, Enjun Du, Junfu Pu, Xinlei Wang, Xinyu Zuo, Lisheng Duan, Haijin Liang, Jin Ma, Jiachuan Wang, Yongqi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces EviAlign, which couples semantic evidence generation with boundary readout in a shared multimodal LLM: evidence is organized into five semantic units, contextualized states are read at each unit boundary, and aggregated into a single normalized embedding for contrastive retrieval. Joint generation and retrieval objectives train the shared structure. This connects a model's generated reasoning traces to where representations are read out.

entry.title: Position Aware Layer Queries for Test Time Training in Vision Language Models

author.name: Rajat Modi, Priyank Pathak, Xin Liang, Yogesh Singh Rawat

entry.summary: Introduces the Layer Query Network (LQN), a lightweight student model that adapts a frozen VLM teacher in a single forward pass via Position-Aware Distillation, exploiting intermediate layer outputs that already carry more signal than augmented-view final embeddings. It avoids the costly multiple forward/backward passes of existing TTT methods for VLMs. This makes test-time training far more computationally tractable.

entry.title: WorldGuide: Learning Success-Failure Boundaries in Latent World Models for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Lin Liu, Lu Zhang, Ziying Song, Wu Yang, Yuzheng Zhuang, Yunzhi Zhuge, Shuai Tao, Wulong Liu, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: WorldGuide trains a latent world model predictor on both successful and failed trajectories with contrastive learning on matched success-failure pairs, then uses the predictor's differentiable reward to guide vision-language-action policy optimization. The predictor is discarded after training, adding no inference cost.

entry.title: Scaling Versatile 3D Assets Editing with a Million-Scale Dataset

author.name: Badi Li, Tianxin Huang, Yu Zhou, Wei-Shi Zheng, Yi Ma, Shenghua Gao

entry.summary: Alchemy3D presents a unified framework for 3D asset editing including Alchemy3D-1M, a dataset of 1.25M assets and 1.38M editing pairs across seven editing types, a family of generative flow models supporting image- and text-conditioned edits, and benchmark evaluation protocols. This addresses scarce data and missing evaluation standards in controllable 3D editing.

entry.title: CAR-VLA: Complexity-Aware and Risk-Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiaolei Chen, Zhuolin He, Yuxuan Liang, Xu Li, Haotian Chen, Shi Fan, Mengyang Zhao, Wenjuan Meng, Zisheng Chen, Zhihao Zhu, Zhounan Jin, Hengli Wang, Qingfan Wang, Jiamei Liang, Bin Li, Xiangyang Xue

entry.summary: CAR-VLA is a driving Vision-Language-Action model that jointly uses scene complexity and dynamic risk to decide reasoning depth, urgency, and focus, mapping complexity-risk categories to three modes: Fast Intuition, Slow Thinking, and a third urgent mode for time-critical situations. It improves on prior adaptive reasoning methods that only decide whether to reason.

entry.title: Clinical Trajectory Alignment for Medical Vision-Language Pre-training

author.name: Huimin Yan, Xian Yang, Zhi Wang, Liang Bai

entry.summary: MedCTA reframes medical vision-language pre-training from visit-level image-report matching to learning longitudinal clinical change, aligning patient histories so models capture whether abnormalities improve, stabilize, or worsen over time. This addresses the challenge that temporal semantics are implicit in free text and evolve asynchronously across conditions.

entry.title: RRG-SLAM: Real-time Reflection-aware Gaussian SLAM for Indoor Scenes

author.name: Yong Liu, Keyang Ye, Zhexi Peng, Ruixian Mei, Kun Zhou, Tianjia Shao

entry.summary: Introduces the first real-time reflection-aware Gaussian SLAM system for indoor scenes, using a TSDF-Gaussian hybrid representation that explicitly separates diffuse appearance from planar reflections via reflection Gaussian groups. Rendering proceeds in three passes combining TSDF raycasting with order-independent Gaussian rendering under reflection masks.

entry.title: Counterfactual Attention Policy Distillation for Temporal Video Grounding

author.name: Shaobo Ju, Haiyang Yu, Xuecheng Wu, Qiong Wu, Jiacong Wang, Fan Shi, Peng Jun, Yiyi Zhou

entry.summary: This work targets temporal video grounding in MLLMs, where repeated actions and visually similar contexts in long videos confuse timestamp prediction. It proposes Counterfactual Attention Policy Distillation, an on-policy distillation regime that provides dense teacher supervision on student trajectories while identifying which video segments support each predicted timestamp via counterfactual attention analysis.

entry.title: Projective Normal Fields: A Convex Optimization Method for Constructing Smooth UDFs

author.name: Jiayi Kong, Chen Zong, Fei Hou, Junhui Hou, Wenping Wang, Ying He

entry.summary: PNFs introduces an orientation-free representation for estimating bidirectional normals from raw point clouds, encoding each normal axis as a rank-one projector invariant to normal reversal and relaxing the non-convex projector set to a convex hull. This yields a convex optimization method for constructing smooth unsigned distance fields without surface connectivity or oriented normals.

entry.title: WM-VLM: Probing Internal World Models for Interleaved Visual-Textual Reasoning

author.name: Yuheng Zha, Yilei Wang, Qiyue Gao, Junrong Chen, Yujia Wu, Zhengfeng Lai, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric P. Xing

entry.summary: WM-VLM equips a pretrained vision-language model with a lightweight world model branch that generates intermediate visual states, enabling mental-simulation-style spatial reasoning rather than purely language-mediated reasoning. A two-stage training regime first teaches next-visual-state generation and then uses those states for reasoning, evaluated on programmatically constructed spatial tasks with verifiable intermediate states. The work is a direct test of whether VLMs can build and exploit internal world models.

entry.title: Sprout: Building Dynamic Memory While Reasoning for Agentic Video Understanding

author.name: Wei Chen, Xuanyu Zheng, Yancheng Long, Haoyang Xu, Kaiyu Jiang, Bin Wen, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Long Chen

entry.summary: Sprout is an agentic framework for long video understanding that builds memory while reasoning, growing a temporal tree with detailed nodes as questions are answered, instead of the costly build-then-reason pipeline where memory is constructed offline and never updated. This adapts memory construction cost to question load and lets knowledge learned while answering benefit later questions. Agentic, question-adaptive video memory is a timely direction for long-video MLLMs.

entry.title: Learning to Reason with Persistent Object States for Video Instance Segmentation

author.name: Yongxue Xu, Boxue Yang, Ziqian Liu, Shaoqiu Zhang, Rui Qian, Haopeng Chen

entry.summary: POSReasoner is a trainable plug-and-play module for video instance segmentation that maintains persistent object states (identity, confidence, absence history) and uses Propose-Verify reasoning on a sparse state-observation graph. It explicitly decides when observations should change object state, reducing persistent identity drift under occlusion and reappearance.

entry.title: GeoVerse: World-Consistent Novel View Synthesis in Geometric Latent Space

author.name: Kerui Ren, Tao Lu, Linning Xu, Changjian Jiang, Mu Huang, Chunhua Shen, Mulin Yu, Bo Dai

entry.summary: GeoVerse synthesizes world-consistent novel views by generating within the geometric latent space of a pretrained 3D foundation model while injecting appearance priors from a video generative model (extracting multilevel features from Wan2.2 VACE). It reconciles faithful reconstruction of observed regions with plausible completion of unseen content.

entry.title: ANaLOG: Anisotropic Native-Latent Operator Guidance for Solving Inverse Problems

author.name: Darshan Thaker, Lachlan Ewen MacDonald, Ren\'e Vidal

entry.summary: ANaLOG improves native-latent guidance for solving inverse problems with latent diffusion models by replacing uniform guidance across latent dimensions with uncertainty-aware, anisotropic guidance. It learns an input- and timestep-dependent covariance so that guidance strength respects which directions the measurements actually inform. This improves efficiency over image-space forward evaluations that require decoder passes at each step.

entry.title: Q-WAM: 4-Bit Quantization of World Action Models with Action-Subspace Protection

author.name: Arash Akbari, Arman Akbari, Jingwu Luo, Yuhao Lei, Yi Gao, Weiwei Chen, Xuan Zhang, Zhenman Fang, Geng Yuan, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: Q-WAM enables 4-bit weight-activation post-training quantization of world action models used in robotic manipulation, where existing PTQ techniques like smoothing and rotation fail to preserve action precision. Its key novelty is the Action Observability Gramian, which measures how rounding errors in each weighted channel combination affect the final generated actions, guiding quantization to protect the action-relevant subspace. This directly targets the prohibitive deployment cost of video-plus-action diffusion models.

entry.title: mmHRI: Towards Privacy-Preserving Human-Robot Interaction with Millimeter-Wave Radar

author.name: Junqiao Fan, Yuxuan Hu, Bofan Lyu, Yanshuo Lu, Pengfei Liu, Jiarui Zhang, Fangqiang Ding, Lihua Xie, Gen Li, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: mmHRI is the first multi-modal robot manipulation framework using millimeter-wave radar to sense human gestures through privacy barriers without identifiable imagery, targeting privacy-critical environments like hospitals and restaurants. It replaces camera-based HRI with radar-guided gesture recognition for tasks such as object delivery.

entry.title: Assisting for Open-Ended Tasks: Goal-Oriented Shared Autonomy as a Particle Filter

author.name: Mengxue Fu, Ethan Xu, Sam Iyer-Singh, Yinlong Dai, Michael Hagenow, Dylan P. Losey

entry.summary: Formulates shared autonomy for open-ended, dynamically changing goals as a particle filter where particles represent candidate human goals, with a transition model that proposes new goals as interaction evolves and human actions updating the belief in real time.

entry.title: CLAP: Closed-Loop Alignment with Pressure for Precise Suction Manipulation

author.name: Yixian Zou, Chongyang Xu, Yuling Xin, Ziliang Feng, Fanman Meng, Shuaicheng Liu

entry.summary: Adds a pressure module tapped into the vacuum line so a VLA policy can observe suction attachment state and abandon an action already underway, addressing occlusion limits of vision during stacking and palletising. The decoded pressure reading conditions the policy in place of the suction command.

entry.title: FailPatch: Failure Residual Patching for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Peng Yu, Jiacheng Wang, Ziheng Zhang, Xuchong Zhang, Baoting Li, Zhuoyuan Yu, Yuxiang Chen, Tiancai Wang, Hongbin Sun

entry.summary: FailPatch adapts VLA policies using deployment failure trajectories rather than only successful demonstrations, decoupling action supervision from execution-reliability supervision. The key insight is that action hidden representations are linearly separable between reliable and failure-associated states, enabling a lightweight residual patching mechanism. This lets the policy learn when its behavior becomes unreliable from data that lacks corrective action labels.

entry.title: HOI-Retarget: Contact-Centric Retargeting for Human-Object Interaction

author.name: Jihwan Shin, Adri\`a L\'opez Escoriza, Junzhe He, Matthias Heyrman, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: HOI-Retarget is a contact-centric retargeting method that transfers human-object interaction demonstrations onto humanoid robots for large-scale motion-data generation. Its windowed trajectory optimization treats every labeled contact as a target in the object frame while balancing body tracking, foot support, and smoothness under kinematic limits. The method can augment single demonstrations across object sizes, absorb contacts reconstructed from monocular video, and extend to multiple robots manipulating one object, with public release of code and data.

entry.title: Uni-VLaT: Whole-Body Tactile Adaptation of VLA Policies for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Zihao Wang, Shutong Liu, Siqi Zheng, Liu Cao, Ruoqi Chen, Rundong Liu, Yanchao Yang, Mengdi Xu

entry.summary: Uni-VLaT integrates distributed whole-body tactile sensing into vision-language-action policies for contact-rich humanoid loco-manipulation, where vision and proprioception are insufficient, especially under occluded contact. Its tactile pathway is trained both for action generation and to predict future tactile, proprioceptive, and visual representations, providing a predictive objective. This advances multimodal grounding for humanoid control.

entry.title: CollisionSplatting: Collision-Aware Motion Planning in 3DGS Scenes with Image-Conditioned Objectives and Adjustable Conservatism

author.name: R. Khorrambakht, Joaquim Ortiz-Haro, Stephan Weiss, Ludovic Righetti

entry.summary: CollisionSplatting introduces a modular, GPU-accelerated, probability-inspired distance metric with tunable conservatism that operates directly on 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, unifying collision-aware costs with image-conditioned learned rewards in MPPI and other planners. This bridges the gap between geometric planners that discard visual richness and learned visual models lacking geometric interpretability. It connects the fast-growing 3DGS scene-representation ecosystem to motion planning.

entry.title: DexRoam: Learning Mobile Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Whole-Body Human Demonstrations

author.name: Rui Zhou, Yibo Yuan, Junkai Zhao, Fangyuan Zhao, Xiaoguang Zhao, Shanghang Zhang, Sirui Han

entry.summary: DexRoam is a complete system for learning mobile bimanual dexterous manipulation from egocentric whole-body human demonstrations, preserving continuous, coupled whole-body motion through the human-to-robot transfer rather than simplifying it. It includes a tracker-free capture pipeline to make large-scale human demonstration collection practical. This directly targets the demonstration bottleneck for one of the hardest robot manipulation settings.

entry.title: Plug-and-Play Methods Provably Converge Even with Improperly Trained Denoisers: Convergence by Architectural Design

author.name: Henry Pritchard, Rahul Parhi

entry.summary: This work strengthens the theoretical foundations of Learned Proximal Networks, whose denoiser architectures are exactly proximal operators of learned regularizers, extending the framework to broader activation classes. It analyzes practical control mechanisms such as averaging with the identity and scaling the implicit regularizer, yielding plug-and-play imaging methods with convergence guarantees even for imperfectly trained denoisers.

entry.title: AI: cognitive labor glut + new guys

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A conceptual essay arguing that AI differs from prior technologies in two ways: it industrializes the supply of cognitive labor (making it cheap and scalable like agriculture did for food), and it introduces genuinely new kinds of cognitive labor rather than substituting for existing human work. The author uses this framing to explain why AI may be more transformative and worrying than past technological shifts.

entry.title: 3 Tips to Improve Activation Oracle Results

author.name: Adam Karvonen

entry.summary: Practical guidance for using Activation Oracles (LLMs trained to answer questions about other models' activations): feed multiple tokens rather than one, sample several times and check consensus to reduce hallucination, and use AUC rather than accuracy for binary classification. The author also compares AOs to natural-language ablations and links to a broader evaluation effort.

entry.title: Ireland’s GDPR regulator will still be investigating when AGI arrives

author.name: Michael Z

entry.summary: An empirical policy analysis showing that Ireland's cross-border GDPR cases take a median 6.2 years to decide, with 66% of 2018-2020 cases still open at 4.5 years, while Metaculus forecasts strong AGI at a median 4.5 years out. Because most major AI labs have EU headquarters in Dublin and the EU AI Act is enforced similarly, the author concludes oversight must occur before models ship rather than through post-hoc investigation.

entry.title: Choir: An Open Protocol for Distributed Multi-Agent Autoformalization

author.name: Yidi Qi, Melanie Weber

entry.summary: Choir is an open-source protocol for distributed autoformalization, where independent contributors each run their own AI agent on tasks decomposed from a formalization project, coordinating through a GitHub repository with deterministic merge gates. It supports Lean 4, Isabelle, and Rocq and shifts formalization from centralized teams to open collaboration. This could substantially lower the cost barrier for large-scale theorem formalization efforts.

entry.title: Fracast-0: Fractal Weight Sharing for a Time Series Foundation Model with Only 85K Parameters

author.name: Tianxiang Zhan, Huanyao Zhang, Yuanpeng He

entry.summary: Fracast-0 is a probabilistic time-series forecasting foundation model of only 85K parameters that exploits temporal self-similarity, reusing a single shared operator across scales via geometric dilation ladders with scale conditioning. Pretraining across six corpora preserves multi-domain breadth, multi-scale structure, and probabilistic output at an extremely small footprint.

entry.title: Function Over Form: Distributional Orthogonalization in Mixture-of-Experts with Replica Expert Mechanism

author.name: Jinfan He, Yunzhuo Liu, Kai Zhang, Weidong Han, Key, Rayying

entry.summary: The paper introduces DO-loss, an auxiliary regularization for MoE models that represents each expert's token assignment history as a binary load signature and penalizes signature overlap to prevent expert collapse and encourage functional specialization. It complements this with a Replica Expert Mechanism aligning algorithmic design with system efficiency. The approach shifts focus from static weight diversity to dynamic routing behavior.

entry.title: DAAF: From Failure Localization to Editable System Assets in LLM Agents

author.name: Xiaoyang Yuan, Qi Liu, Yubin Ruan, Xinyi Mou, Zhuomeng Zhang, Wenjin Wang, Hanying Jiao, Di Wu, Mingye Xu, Yi Bin, Ke Feng, Zixun Sun

entry.summary: Addresses the gap between failure localization and repair for deployed LLM agents by targeting versioned, addressable system assets (routing rules, knowledge segments, prompts, skills) through component-attribute failure attribution. DAAF learns the effects of valid attribute replacements and amortizes intervention evidence into deployment-time diagnosis to decide which asset to edit.

entry.title: Contract Memory Compiler: Resolve, Then Traverse

author.name: Zhi Song, XiMing Xing, Chunhan Li, Weian Mao, Zhenchao Tang, Hanbo Huang, Fan Xu, Jiale Zhou, Jiahui Guan, Zejian Ding, Chen Ma, Lusheng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces the Contract Memory Compiler (CMC) for external memory in long-context agent systems: before seeing a question, a model indexes relations in the history, and later updates resolve current relations so multi-hop questions can be routed to the correct original records, including records about entities absent from the question. This targets update-dependent evidence selection, a harder problem than simple fact retrieval. Evidence is passed to the answer model in a single call.

entry.title: Feedback Makes Perfect: A Closed-Loop Framework for NL-to-STL Translation

author.name: Bowen Ye, Xiang Yin

entry.summary: This paper reformulates natural-language to Signal Temporal Logic translation as a closed-loop feedback process, translating each generated formula back into natural language to expose ambiguities and intent mismatches, since one-shot open-loop translation hits an accuracy ceiling. The iterative loop substantially improves translation correctness for cyber-physical system specifications.

entry.title: SWE-Game: Can Coding Agents Build the Games We Want?

author.name: Xiaoyu Chen, Lai Wei, Jin Wang, Xiangyu Zou, Ruochen Fan, Enze Luo, Mingzhe Yao, Jiahui Zhu, Yuhua Wen, Linghe Kong, Weiran Huang

entry.summary: Introduces SWE-Game, a benchmark of 247 tasks grounded in 41 executable Godot reference games across 13 genres, covering development from briefs, implementation from design documents, skeleton completion, fault repair, and Godot-to-Unity porting. Evaluation combines engine-state checks, certified input replay, and agent-authored demonstrations to assess mechanic correctness and playability.

entry.title: Towards Certificate-Driven Software Porting: A Self-Improving Agentic Harness for Scientific Program Optimization

author.name: Piyush Jha, Aishik Ghosh, Vijay Ganesh

entry.summary: CDES extends LLM-driven evolutionary search for porting legacy scientific code by recording enforceable restrictions (certificates of assumptions, checker evidence, and justified restrictions) from failed candidates, enforced via rejection, backtracking, and targeted repair. Applied to CPU-to-GPU translation of particle simulation functions, it prevents repeated errors that prompt-only feedback allows.

entry.title: RAGWarrant: Evidence-Preserving Governance for RAG Policy Promotion Under Quality, Cost, Latency, and Risk Constraints

author.name: Richard Krueger, Lucas Krause, Zach Pocquette

entry.summary: RAGWarrant is an open-source promotion-control framework treating RAG deployment decisions as constrained evidence decisions rather than leaderboard choices, with predeclared quality gates, risk gates, evidence-class claim ceilings, and auditable PROMOTE/BLOCK/REJECT/INCONCLUSIVE outputs. It preserves negative outcomes and is evaluated across multiple RAG benchmarks.

entry.title: CORTEX: Learning to Share and Specialize in Dense Language Models

author.name: Chuiyang Meng, Ming Tang, Vincent W. S. Wong

entry.summary: CORTEX learns internal modularization within dense LLMs by partitioning trainable matrices into parameter groups whose module assignments are learned from domain-conditioned gradients and cross-domain gradient similarity. It introduces selective lesion scores and module-domain mutual information to characterize specialization and sharing across heterogeneous data domains.

entry.title: What does FFN compression change downstream? Same-state causal restoration in diffusion language models

author.name: Shaurya Omar

entry.summary: The paper introduces Same-State Causal Restoration (SSR), a method that restores original FFN computation on the exact input reached by a compressed diffusion language model and measures downstream trajectory changes. This provides the first direct closed-loop measurement of which removed FFN computations matter to denoising trajectories, beyond local approximation error. It is relevant as diffusion LMs attract more compression work.

entry.title: Continual Learning via Self-Probe Gradients

author.name: Dongkyu Cho, Rumi Chunara, Sungmin Cha

entry.summary: CPLUS addresses catastrophic forgetting by having a frozen model self-probe: it generates new inputs from retained past samples and records its own predictions, using self-probe and past-sample gradients to scale down parameter updates that conflict with prior behavior. Experiments across five language models and four benchmarks show self-probes preserve more prior behavior as gradient evidence. This is a lightweight alternative to replaying stored samples.

entry.title: VPTwin: Real-Sim-Real Video Prediction for Robotic Manipulation Planning

author.name: Zhenghao Xiao, Minting Pan, Nantian He, Dongzhan Zhou, Yunbo Wang

entry.summary: Proposes VPTwin, a Real-Sim-Real framework that anchors real-world video prediction using simulation twins: a VLM reconstructs an executable digital twin from a demonstration, Isaac Sim rolls out multiple dynamics under randomized physical configurations, and the resulting data corrects compounding errors and physical hallucinations in long-horizon action-conditioned prediction.

entry.title: Policy Plasticity Matters in Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning: Refitting Offline Policies for Online Adaptation

author.name: Yuheng Huang, Yunpeng Qing, Yixiao Chi, Yilun Kong, Changqing Zou

entry.summary: Studies offline-to-online RL from the perspective of network plasticity, showing via controlled experiments that prolonged offline optimization reduces policy adaptability even after offline performance saturates, and that lower plasticity correlates with worse online adaptation. Proposes refitting offline policies to restore plasticity before online fine-tuning.

entry.title: OOD Generalization as a Bifurcation Problem

author.name: Nguyen-Thanh-Luong Doan, Quang-Vu Nguyen, Tang-Phu-Quy Le, Cong-Phap Huynh

entry.summary: The paper shows that compositional binding in continuous-time generative models is a localized phase transition, identifying a semantic bifurcation window where joint and decomposed classifier-free guidance vector fields diverge. Its surgical guidance strategy applies exact multi-pass scoring only during this critical window, improving OOD composition at reduced cost.

entry.title: SlimWise: Decoupling Expert Pruning Across Prefill and Decode for Efficient MoE Serving

author.name: Gunho Park, Kyoungho Jeun, Juntaek Oh, Byeongjun Shin, Baeseong Park, Minsoo Rhu

entry.summary: SlimWise is a serving framework that decouples expert pruning by inference phase: prefill runs the full MoE model while decode uses a pruned expert pool, reusing the prefill-generated KV cache without conversion. This avoids sacrificing compute-bound prefill quality and narrows accuracy gaps versus the full model across two MoE backbones and three pruning criteria. A training-free approach to reducing expert-weight traffic in batched decoding.

entry.title: A Unifying Framework of Concept-based Explainable AI with Completeness Guarantees

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch K\r{u}r, Adam Kuku\v{c}ka, Tom\'a\v{s} Br\'azdil, V\'it Musil

entry.summary: The paper introduces a theoretical framework that expresses diverse concept-based explainability approaches in a common mathematical language, using a concept autoencoder view where reconstruction error measures concept discovery quality. It provides shared analysis of properties and completeness guarantees across concept-based XAI methods.

entry.title: Planarian: Managing Agent State with Statepoints

author.name: Jinnan Guo, Hao Mark Chen, Kapil Vaswani, Andrew Paverd, Peter Pietzuch

entry.summary: Planarian is an agent runtime with unified state management that lets agents and users recover from erroneous actions and explore alternative executions over consistent local and remote environment state. It introduces statepoints, an abstraction for managing changes across files, local tools, and remote services.

entry.title: GPUPhysBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Correct and Efficient GPU Physics Simulation

author.name: Yuchen Sun, Jinjin He, Sinan Wang, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces GPUPhysBench, 50 tasks testing whether coding agents can write correct and fast GPU physics simulation code across fluids, deformable solids, and granular materials, evaluated with execution on real NVIDIA hardware against expert-optimized references. Frontier model-harness pairs pass many tasks but produce implementations substantially slower than expert code.

entry.title: Balancing Early Performance Sacrifices with Long-Term Gains: Scaling Learning-Rate Warmup Duration Across Training Horizons

author.name: Kristi Topollai, Anna Choromanska

entry.summary: The paper analyzes learning-rate warmup duration in language-model training using a quadratic model whose modes respond differently to peak learning rate, showing warmup removes persistent error in directions near the stability edge. It derives a compact horizon scaling law for warmup duration, resolving when warmup should stay fixed versus grow with training length. This replaces heuristics with a principled scaling rule for LLM training.

entry.title: Unlocking Few-Step Diffusion for Faithful Previews

author.name: Jing Jia, Sifan Liu, Guanyang Wang

entry.summary: The paper finds that frozen 3-4-step diffusion samplers can closely reproduce their full-step outputs merely by optimizing the initial noise, indicating the failure of few-step sampling is not a reconstruction-capacity limit. It learns corrections to initial noise and denoising updates with endpoint supervision, enabling cheap faithful previews for screening candidates before full-step generation, with corrections transferring across sampling budgets.

entry.title: Adjoint Guidance Flow: Amortized Critic Guidance for VLA Policies

author.name: Jeongsol Kim, Youngjun Jun, Kyumin Choi, Youngmin Kim, Seonghyun Jin, Sunwoo Park, Jangho Park, Kwanyoung Kim, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Proposes AGF, which amortizes trajectory-aware critic guidance for flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies into a lightweight guidance network, formulated as a deterministic optimal control problem whose optimal guidance is a costate carrying terminal critic gradients backward. This avoids expensive one-step surrogates and per-step backpropagation of critic ensembles while preserving the pretrained policy. It aims to improve long-term task return beyond behavior cloning.

entry.title: Before Answering: Evidence Sufficiency under Size-Matched Memory Construction

author.name: Joyanta Jyoti Mondal, Md. Shifatul Ahsan Apurba, Mridul Banik, Md Masud Al Mahmud, Ibne Farabi Shihab

entry.summary: This paper shows that benchmarks testing whether agents recognize when evidence is missing from memory leak labels through memory size: on MuSiQue, a classifier counting only paragraphs reaches 0.979 AUROC for detecting unsafe memory. The authors propose a size-matched construction that provably removes this shortcut and introduce MemSafe, a cross-encoding estimator with set-transformer aggregation, evaluated across three multi-hop question answering datasets. A rigorous benchmark-hygiene contribution with a practical method.

entry.title: ARS: Agentic Reward System for Robot Learning

author.name: Sheng Hu, Weiyi Lu, Lingbing Zeng, Gan Weng, Weiwei Zhang, Kai Xie, Xiaofeng Mou, Yi Xu

entry.summary: ARS is a training-free inference framework for progress reward modeling in robot learning that uses general-purpose VLMs: a subagent proposes a task-relevant event timeline from an offline trajectory, a primary agent verifies and revises it, and per-frame progress rewards are estimated with optional terminal outcome labels and visual refinement. It distinguishes meaningful state changes from failed or irrelevant actions without training a dedicated reward model.

entry.title: The Right Lesson at the Right Step: Deriving Control Updates for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Yunhe Su, ZiYi Dong, Tong Yu, Weijian Deng, Hao Li, Bowen Jiang, Pengxu Wei

entry.summary: EvoCUE represents an agent as an explicit state-machine controller whose nodes perform model or tool calls and whose edges define control flow, enabling experience reuse as localized, editable control updates rather than global prompts or memories. Each learned lesson is applied at precise locations in long tool-use workflows.

entry.title: Rubric Rewards from Item Response Theory

author.name: Milad Yazdani, Yaser Souri, Xiren Zhou, Pranit Chawla, Dena Shahriari, Subhojit Som, Xia Song

entry.summary: The paper addresses how to aggregate rubric-based judge verdicts into scalar rewards for reinforcement learning, arguing that simple point-summing conflates distinct verdict patterns and encodes fixed criterion weights that do not reflect how strongly a verdict discriminates current rollouts. It proposes Rubric Response Theory (RRT), adapting ideas from item response theory to measure quality and select criteria when rubric criteria act as monotone indicators of a shared latent quality. This also reduces the number of judge requests needed as rubric size grows.

entry.title: OmniFysics-Captioner Technical Report: Grounding Omni-Modal Understanding in the Physical World for Better Captioning

author.name: Kaixiang Qiu, Minghao Han, Keliang Liu, Yizhou Liu, Jinghan Han, Yue Jiang, Xuecheng Wu, Shunli Wang, Lihua Zhang, Dingkang Yang

entry.summary: Presents a physics-aware audiovisual captioning framework spanning data construction, training, and evaluation, using an OmniFysics-Agent pipeline that coordinates audio, visual, and physical-perception tools to collect spatiotemporally aligned evidence about contacts, support, deformation, and state transitions. Aims to give omni-modal models fine-grained physical supervision.

entry.title: AnesTRACE: Benchmarking Intraoperative Anesthesia from Multimodal Perception to Multi-step Decision-Making

author.name: Ziwei Huang, Qi Gao, Zhe Ji, Yuanyuan Yao, Fengjiang Zhang, Min Yan, Zhongle Xie, Gang Chen

entry.summary: Introduces AnesTRACE, an evaluation suite with a benchmark and an open-ended evaluator covering intraoperative perception, single-point, and multi-step anesthesia decision-making, built from public perioperative datasets with anesthesiologist annotation. AnesTRACE-Eval scores responses on clinical correctness, evidence grounding, task completeness, safety, and temporal consistency.

entry.title: Uncovering Ordinal-Matching Bias in Audio-Visual LLMs

author.name: Jihoo Jung, Youngjoon Jang, Hyebin Cho, Suho Yoo, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: Using a synthetic diagnostic dataset of multiple speakers each uttering a single word, the authors find that recent open-source audio-visual LLMs attribute speech to speakers by matching the order of utterances to the left-to-right, top-to-bottom arrangement of faces rather than using lip synchronization. They name this failure mode ordinal-matching bias and analyze mitigation.

entry.title: When Does an Image Determine the Answer? Benchmarking Visual Answerability across Charts and Scenes

author.name: Sungguk Cha, Mintae Kim, Youngsub Han, Byoung-Ki Jeon, Sangyeob Lee

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for visual answerability requiring models to answer when evidence suffices and abstain when it does not, using original and edited image pairs across PlotQA, CLEVR, and GQA with executable witnesses proving that masked charts give different answers despite identical pixels. It evaluates six model configurations over 72,000 responses under strict all-or-nothing scoring.

entry.title: DynaTokens: Teaching Dynamics to Camera-Controlled Video Models at Test Time

author.name: Ma Ziqi, Chen Hongqiao, Gkioxari Georgia

entry.summary: DynaTokens adds a lightweight set of learnable scene-specific tokens to existing camera-controlled video generation models to teach scene dynamics at test time. It exploits the asymmetry that camera motion affects the whole view globally while object dynamics are localized, fixing issues where objects are static or move incorrectly under camera control.

entry.title: Learning Geometry-Aware Virtual Fixtures From Sparse Demonstrations

author.name: Maximilian M\"uhlbauer, Marcella Piacentino, Raffaella Mancino, Paolino De Risi, Bernhard Weber, Margarida Campos, Thomas Hulin, Sylvain Calinon, Freek Stulp, Alin Albu-Sch\"affer, Julian Klodmann, Fanny Ficuciello, Jo\~ao Silv\'erio

entry.summary: Proposes learning virtual fixtures for teleoperation from only a few via-points by leveraging a linear quadratic tracking motion prior, reformulating LQT on Riemannian manifolds to handle orientation guidance. Probabilistic interpretation yields covariance estimates along trajectories.

entry.title: MM-ABC: Towards Generalist Mobile Manipulation via Seeing, Coordinating and Imagining

author.name: Qiwei Liang, Guangyu Chen, Shaolong Zhu, Zikuan Xiao, Jinxuan Lu, Yifan Xie, Renjing Xu, Wenbo Ding, Tianxing Chen

entry.summary: MM-ABC is a foundation model for mobile manipulation built around Seeing, Coordinating, and Imagining Arm-Base Collaboration, addressing spatially grounded perception under continuous ego-motion and coordinated control of heterogeneous arm and base actions. It argues for representations supporting efficient cross-stream collaboration rather than pure decoupling of mobility and manipulation. This targets generalist mobile manipulation, a major open challenge in embodied AI.

entry.title: DriveHierarchy: A Benchmark for Diagnosing VLM Driving Capabilities from Open-Loop Understanding to Closed-Loop Execution

author.name: Chengkai Xu, Jiaqi Liu, Yicheng Guo, Peng Hang, Jian Sun

entry.summary: DriveHierarchy is a hierarchical benchmark for vision-language-model-based autonomous driving organized into four ranks: perceptual grounding, contextual memory, mental reasoning, and closed-loop execution. Unlike prior benchmarks that test open-loop understanding or closed-loop driving in isolation, it provides structure for explaining how these abilities relate and how failures propagate. This supports diagnosis and targeted improvement of driving VLMs.

entry.title: Toward Interactive Understanding of Code APIs

author.name: Dhananjay Ashok, Jesse Thomason, Jonathan May

entry.summary: The paper introduces PAU, a benchmark where models must understand black-box code APIs purely through exploratory querying, without read access to source code. It reframes code understanding as unsupervised tool understanding via interaction, a more realistic setting for agents working with external APIs.

entry.title: Train4Merge: A Controlled Single-Teacher Study of RL vs. SFT Teachers for OPD-Based Model Merging

author.name: Jingyuan Huang, Zuming Huang, Yucheng Shi, Zhongzhi Li, Xiaoming Zhai, Wei Chu, Ninghao Liu

entry.summary: The paper examines whether domain experts built via supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement learning make better teachers in on-policy distillation for model merging, training comparably performing SFT and RL teachers from Qwen3.5-9B across Agentic, Reasoning, and Perception domains. RL-guided students outperform SFT-guided students by 4.27, 1.50, and 0.86 percentage points at best checkpoints.

entry.title: ALLOT: Budgeted Hybrid-Memory Routing for Knowledge Updates in LLMs

author.name: Shanfeng Huang, Zhou Fang, Song Xiao, Hai Du

entry.summary: ALLOT introduces a hybrid-memory routing framework for LLM knowledge editing that separates learned write priority from a hard parametric budget, deciding which facts to write into parameters versus keep in external retrieval. Using a memory-aware router over frozen text representations, retrieval confidence, and relation metadata, it achieves 0.760 accuracy on CounterFact with Qwen3-4B at a 20% parametric-write budget, recovering 78.4% of the oracle gain with 80% fewer parametric writes. This directly addresses the cost of parametric adaptation when retrieval already suffices.

entry.title: Multi-Agent System Search via Active Substructure-aware Policy Optimization

author.name: Beicheng Xu, Bowen Fan, Weitong Qian, Lingching Tung, Bin Cui

entry.summary: ASPO is an RL framework for query-level search over multi-agent system designs, addressing weaknesses of approaches that traverse fixed training-query sets with workflow-level rewards. It introduces an Adaptive Query-Selection Mechanism that focuses on queries with high learning potential and a substructure-aware reward that identifies which agent-role substructures improve solution quality. This enables learning policies that construct query-specific MAS without manual design expertise.

entry.title: Separating Diagnosis from Disease Representation: Dual-View EEG Learning with Neural-Dynamics-Guided Deformation

author.name: Jiaying Wang, Shouqian Shi, Yutong Chen, Xu Yang, Jie Chen, Xingyu Pan, Lei Zhang, Sheng Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes DMD-EEG, a dual-view architecture for EEG-based closed-loop neuromodulation that keeps a fixed scalp spectral expert for diagnosis while modeling disease representation in source space as a low-rank, sparse deformation of a healthy neural-dynamics baseline. This decouples predictive accuracy from anatomical interpretability, yielding subject-specific structured states (deviant regions, frequencies, lags) rather than a single disease probability.

entry.title: RepoMAS: Solving Progressively Specified Tasks with Issue-Driven Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yuchen Song, Andong Chen, Wenxin Zhu, Muyun Yang, Tiejun Zhao

entry.summary: This paper tackles progressively specified tasks, where user requirements are incomplete at the start and only emerge during execution. The authors introduce ProgSpec, a benchmark that scores final outputs against both initial requirements and later-clarified requirements, and RepoMAS, a multi-agent framework modeled on open-source issue tracking that records newly discovered requirements as issues and routes them to appropriate agents. It matters because real-world LLM agent deployments rarely receive fully specified instructions, making this a practical gap in current agent evaluation.

entry.title: MA-FPPO: Multi-Agent Flow-Pretrained Policy Optimization

author.name: Guowei Zou, Haonan Chen, Haitao Wang, Beiwen Zhang, Na Yan, Hejun Wu

entry.summary: Proposes MA-FPPO, which fine-tunes flow-matching-pretrained multi-agent policies online with explicit action likelihoods for discrete and continuous actions, enabling adaptation and coordination beyond what fixed offline datasets cover. This bridges offline multi-agent flow policy pretraining with online policy optimization for out-of-distribution situations.

entry.title: From Scene Graphs to Answers: Selective Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yiyao Wang, Pei Liu, Fangzhou Liu, Jun Ma

entry.summary: Introduces a query-adaptive neuro-symbolic framework for autonomous-driving question answering that allocates computation based on whether a query admits exact symbolic solutions or needs semantic interpretation. It uses a hierarchical spatiotemporal scene graph separating persistent object identities from frame-specific states. The work argues against uniformly delegating all reasoning to a single neural process.

entry.title: IGSD: Environment-Verified Hindsight Self-Distillation for Search Agents

author.name: Angqing Jiang, Gaoming Zhang, Chaoqun Zhang, Jianchun Song, Liyuan Kong, Kena Qi, Wei Lin, Defu Lian

entry.summary: Proposes Information-Gain-Gated Self-Distillation (IGSD) for search agents: before distilling hindsight-conditioned teacher proposals, the method verifies each query's executed retrieval consequence via environment feedback, treating query tokens as micro-actions. This fixes a flaw in prior self-distillation where hindsight teachers prefer queries that do not actually improve retrieval from the student's state. It densifies agent training without external teachers.

entry.title: Can LLMs Predict the Future? A Brier Score Analysis of Prediction Markets

author.name: Yuanbo Li, Zekun Li, Xiaoyan cong

entry.summary: The authors build a benchmark of 3,000 resolved prediction-market binary questions and evaluate six Claude and Qwen variants zero-shot using Brier scores, Murphy decomposition, and paired comparisons stratified by training cutoff. Post-cutoff, Claude models beat a base-rate predictor by 0.024-0.033 while a Qwen 32B variant does not. This provides a rigorous, calibration-focused measure of whether model upgrades improve real-world forecasting.

entry.title: On Device Agentic Operation Caches -- Classifier-Centric NL-to-Action Generation

author.name: Moghis Fereidouni, Anthony Arnold, Sumit Gulwani, Mark Marron, A. B. Siddique

entry.summary: The paper proposes an on-device alternative to cloud-hosted frontier LLMs for translating natural language into software operations, using a classifier-centric operation-cache approach. This reduces latency, addresses privacy concerns, and lowers the cost of embedding agentic features in applications.

entry.title: Unmask the State: When Does State Adaptation Matter for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Injin Kong, Sunghwan Choi, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: This arXiv paper studies inference-time unmasking strategies for masked diffusion language models (MDMs), organizing existing approaches along five axes: score, cardinality, region, commitment, and planning. The authors introduce the concept of strategy reversals and define adaptation opportunity as the one-step utility advantage of switching to the best candidate action versus a fixed, validation-selected strategy. This provides a principled framework for determining when adaptive decoding decisions actually improve generation quality in MDMs.

entry.title: What Shared Prefixes Hide: Trajectory Dropout for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zzizhuo Lin, Quanling Liu, Yi Yang, Yawei Luo

entry.summary: The paper identifies Prefix-Induced Supervision Attenuation (PISA) in on-policy distillation: shared reasoning prefixes weaken token-level teacher feedback, either because high student confidence dampens corrective gradients or because tokens dependent on earlier reasoning receive weak learning signals. The proposed Trajectory Dropout mitigates this. On-policy distillation is an increasingly popular training recipe, so diagnosing this failure mode is timely.

entry.title: JustQuant: You Don't Need Smoothing, SVD, or Rotation for 4-Bit Activation Quantization

author.name: Kaicheng Yang, Kaisen Yang, Chunyu Liu, Xianglong Yan, Haotong Qin, Junyi Wu, Tianao Zhang, Xun Zhang, Shaoqiu Zhang, Youbang Sun, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that 4-bit activation quantization for generative models can be achieved without the extra operators (smoothing, SVD branches, rotations) or special formats like NVFP4 that recent PTQ/QAT methods require, using only plain low-precision computation. This removes hardware and inference-engine barriers that have limited low-precision deployment.

entry.title: Skill2Env: Capability-Oriented Environment Synthesis from Skills for General Agents

author.name: Weiyi Xu, Xiaowen Yang, Wen Da, Hang Xu, Canwei Li, Hongjie You, Pusen Dong, Yucheng Zeng, Zhaokai Luo, Mu Chuan

entry.summary: Skill2Env is a framework that synthesizes executable tasks and environments for agent post-training by starting from reusable skills and using agent capability demands to guide task construction. It represents difficulty patterns and instantiates them into task blueprints, addressing the scalability bottleneck of building training environments for tool-use agents.

entry.title: StateGuard: Analytical-State Management with Validity-Aware Intervention for Long-Horizon Data Agents

author.name: Wenle Liao, Zhao Wang, Jingchao Zhang, Jiajie Jin, Yimeng Xu, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: StateGuard externalizes an agent's analytical progress into a state graph tracking constraints, variables, and conclusions so stale artifacts can be detected and invalidated before they silently propagate errors downstream. It targets a real reliability problem in long-horizon, multi-stage LLM data-analysis workflows.

entry.title: Same Winners, Different Success Rates: Evaluating How LLM Agents Recover from Failures

author.name: Dong Xu, Zhangfan Yang, Jiantao Wu, Shipeng Zhang, Zexuan Zhu, Jiangqiang Li, Jun Zhang, Junkai Ji

entry.summary: The paper proves that set agreement, the ordinal measure used by checkpoint-based recovery benchmarks, can create an illusion of stability when all actions fail since tied zero-reward sets look stable despite near-zero recovery success. It formalizes this via a set-path symmetry result showing equal set agreement can hide very different success probabilities.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling via Budgeted Multi-Attribute Verification

author.name: Bo Xue, Ji Cheng, Shen-Huan Lyu, Yuanyu Wan, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: The paper formulates LLM answer verification under a shared budget as a multi-attribute good-arm identification problem: deciding which candidate answers to inspect and which costly verification attributes to evaluate. The proposed BMA-GAI algorithm combines cost-aware selection with adaptive attribute sampling and anytime-valid certification, with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: The Marathon of Scientific Reasoning: Robustness of Scientific Agents to Perturbations in Multi-Turn Interactions

author.name: Xiaoting Lyu, Xinbo Ma, Yufei Han, Hangwei Qian, Ziyang Lin, Bin Wang, Bin Wang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: SciARP is a benchmark evaluating LLM-based scientific agents under 13 types of scientifically plausible perturbations across multi-turn problem solving, transforming 620 problems into interdependent task chains. It measures how robust agent reasoning is when imperfections arise mid-task rather than only at the start.

entry.title: DGF-Bench: A Benchmark for Simulating and Auditing Deception Against Multi-Agent Governance Boards

author.name: Jeremy Canale

entry.summary: Introduces DGF-Bench, where a board of LLM agents with specialist and general gates reviews synthetic project dossiers under executable rules while an attacker plants deceptive content in non-authoritative evidence. Attacks never change authoritative values, so every gate is certified decidable from records, enabling systematic auditing of deception resistance in multi-agent governance.

entry.title: Action-Space Shaping for LLM Agents: Measuring and Mitigating Tool-Schema Bias

author.name: Yinhong Liu, Zhili Tan, Zilin Wang, Zhijiang Guo

entry.summary: The paper identifies schema bias: LLM agents behave inconsistently when the same executable action is exposed through functionally equivalent but differently written tool schemas. It introduces an executable transformation framework with nine operators (merging, splitting, re-expressing tools) to systematically measure this bias, plus mitigation strategies. This is an important robustness finding for the tool-use agent ecosystem.

entry.title: Using Context Is Not Enough: Test-Time Training for Personalized Reward Modeling

author.name: Bohao Wang, Xiaoyan Zhao, Yang Zhang, Jinghang Guo, Chun Chen, Can Wang, Jiawei Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies a key limitation of in-context personalized reward models: supplying a user's historical preference pairs as context fails to capture the preference relations they convey. It proposes Preference-Aligned Test-Time Training (P-TTT), which explicitly encodes these relations into user-specific fast weights at inference time for personalized reward prediction.
