entry.summary: PROUR formulates proactive agent behavior as uncertainty routing among ACT, CLARIFY, and VERIFY decisions, decomposing action uncertainty into user-goal disagreement (user-side ambiguity) and within-interpretation entropy (missing world evidence). A question-generation mechanism acquires information from the routed source, unifying clarification and verification strategies.

entry.title: LocalProp: Neuro-Localized Memory-Efficient Backpropagation

author.name: Diana-Nicoleta Grigore, Iuliana Georgescu, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: Proposes LocalProp, a training procedure that locally updates model weights in a pre-training (I-JEPA-based) then fine-tuning paradigm, with pruning used to propagate learning signals from higher to lower blocks, motivated by biological locality and memory efficiency versus end-to-end backpropagation. Experiments span vision and other modalities to test whether localized updates can rival standard training.

entry.title: Learning from a Thoughtful Teacher: Adaptive On-Policy Self-Distillation for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Jiacheng Du, Weiwei Xie, Tianyi Du, Shaoxiong Guo, Qibing Ren, Jiaheng Zhang

entry.summary: Improves on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for math reasoning by diagnosing a gap between teacher utility and student learnability: a small fraction of high-disagreement tokens dominates the distillation signal, and short teacher continuations leak privileged information as shortcuts. The proposed AOPSD adaptively modulates how privileged information is used at the token level. This yields dense on-policy supervision without a larger external teacher.

entry.title: AgentHabit: Characterizing Distinct Behaviors of Agents on Everyday Tasks

author.name: Woojung Song, Hoyeol Yang, Jeonghoon Shim, Sungjib Lim, Jonggeun Lee, Yunho Choi, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: The paper introduces HABIT, a taxonomy of 23 behavioral axes across five categories (e.g., whether agents ask clarifying questions or search the web), derived bottom-up from 408 agent trajectories across 17 domains by three human and three LLM annotators. On held-out tasks, HABIT distinguishes models more clearly than existing human-values or agent-action taxonomies, and AgentHABIT profiles each agent's behavioral tendencies as a benchmark. It shifts agent evaluation from task success alone to how agents behave.

entry.title: Learning to Sell: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Large Language Model Agents in Multi-Product Markets

author.name: Shuze Daniel Liu, Claire Chen, Jiuqi Wang, Thorsten Joachims

entry.summary: The paper develops an RL approach for training LLM seller agents in multi-item bargaining environments, where a seller negotiates a catalog of substitutable products across independent buyers with private heterogeneous valuations under communication-turn budgets. The seller must dynamically match buyers to profitable products while strategically allocating its limited interaction budget.

entry.title: RelaxKV: Recomputation Guided by the Query with Sparse Context Attention for Efficient KV Cache Reuse

author.name: Ruoling Qi, Yirui Liu, Xuaner Wu, Yuxin Jin, Jian Chen, Jiayu Qin, Yin Chen, Jiawei Shao

entry.summary: RelaxKV formulates selective KV cache repair for position-independent caching in RAG as a joint allocation problem over repair targets and recomputation context, guided by the user query and identifying layer-specific needs. Existing methods fix the recomputation context to the full causal prefix and focus only on selecting states. This improves cross-request cache reuse while recovering missing cross-chunk interactions.

entry.title: Does Adversarial Training Improve Generalization in Multi-View VLAs? Revealing and Mitigating View Collapse

author.name: Futa Waseda, Shuhei Kurita, Isao Echizen

entry.summary: Studies adversarial training in multi-view vision-language-action models across seven LIBERO-Plus shift axes, finding that direct AT improves robustness to camera viewpoint and sensor noise shifts, the two shifts affecting visual input, but can cause view collapse, and proposes mitigation. It clarifies when AT helps natural distribution-shift generalization in VLAs.

entry.title: How code helps different tasks? A decompositional lens on LLM post-training

author.name: Zheng Yu, Yiwei Li, Yishen Chen, Xiang Li, Jiale Han, Benyou Wang, Jingbang Chen

entry.summary: This study decomposes an execution-verified code corpus into interpretable categories by computational pattern and runs controlled fine-tuning experiments comparing individual categories against balanced mixtures. The resulting response maps show which code data types help question answering, math, and code generation, and whether gains persist when combined.

entry.title: Evo2Team: When Do Evolved Skills Transfer? From Selection to Deployment

author.name: Renxiang Wang, Jiaming Cui

entry.summary: Evo2Team studies when evolved routing and communication skills from one multi-agent team transfer to another, selecting, adapting, and confirming source skills across 28 transfer directions using GPT and Qwen model ladders of 4-32 agents. It shows target-side exploration costs below evolving a new skill bank in every direction, with many successful transfers.

entry.title: SAGE: Structured Strategic Reasoning for Efficient LLM Game Playing

author.name: Zhiwei Chen, Tianchun Wang, Zhongtao Rao, Haiming Zhu, Ding Cao, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: SAGE is a training-free inference-time framework that structures LLM strategic reasoning around three operations: anchoring to an equilibrium-based policy prior, adapting to opponent behavioral tendencies, and recalibrating from interaction history. It aims to avoid unsupported assumptions, inconsistent opponent estimates, and interference from irrelevant history in game-playing agents.

entry.title: After the Fix: How Corrected Agent Histories Transfer to Related Tasks

author.name: Yanfei Zhang, Xu Lin

entry.summary: Through 3,300 runs across ThinkingBox and APEX agent pairs under eleven conditions, this paper studies whether repaired failed episodes become better memory for related tasks. It finds large apparent correction gains often stem from worse uncorrected baselines rather than better corrected memory, with many upward transitions merely restoring baseline success.

entry.title: UniOPSD: Unifying Outcome and Hindsight Feedback for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zenghuang Fu, Zhaoyang Li, Qiuyuan Ai, Xiaofeng Han, Zelong Zheng, Haoyu Wu, Tianyu Fu, Chenxu Zhao, Minghui Wu, Guannan He, Changwei Wang

entry.summary: Extends on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for agentic RL by unifying sparse outcome rewards with dense hindsight feedback through adaptive local credit arbitration. Diagnostics show outcome and hindsight signals agree on average but disagree locally, motivating per-decision allocation of influence between the two feedback sources.

entry.title: Reliability Engineering for AI Systems: Challenges, Methods, and Directions

author.name: Rong Pan, Yili Hong, Min Xie

entry.summary: A position paper adapting classical reliability engineering methods (failure definitions, operational envelopes, FMEA, accelerated testing, field monitoring, reliability estimation) to AI systems whose function now includes retrieval, memory, tool use, permissions, and human oversight. It argues average benchmark accuracy cannot quantify the broader reliability claim for increasingly autonomous systems.

entry.title: Jev thinks "I don't know'', but doesn't say it: Introducing Sys1Cal-v1 Dataset for Probability Calibration

author.name: Riccardo Porcedda

entry.summary: The paper introduces Sys1Cal-v1, a dataset of True/False questions with probabilities known by construction, used to test whether the System-1-style model Jev returns properly calibrated option probabilities through its Noul, Choice, and Score primitives. It argues existing benchmarks measure confidence calibration rather than the numerical meaning of every returned probability, and finds calibration claims unverified.

entry.title: What Next-Event Accuracy Cannot See: Closed-Loop Evaluation of Emergency Department Trajectory Simulators

author.name: Zhen Xuen Brandon Low

entry.summary: EDSim-Bench systematically quantifies compounding-error effects in clinical trajectory simulators, which standard next-event accuracy metrics miss because simulation conditions on a model's own generated events. Using 425,028 MIMIC-IV-ED stays with external replication on MC-MED, it evaluates termination, event composition, timing, conditional fidelity, and occupancy forecasting, including an order-3 n-gram baseline. The evaluation protocol and scoring code are released.

entry.title: Parser, Chunking, and Embedding Interactions in Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Indian Government Regulatory Documents

author.name: Shubham Kumar Singh

entry.summary: A controlled factorial study of how document parser, chunking strategy, and embedding model choices jointly affect RAG retrieval quality across four Indian government regulatory documents, with 800 question instances and automatic evidence validation. The work addresses the common practice of assembling RAG components independently without joint evaluation. It offers practical guidance for building RAG pipelines over complex regulatory text.

entry.title: Depth Any Seen: Which Surfaces and How Far?

author.name: Xiaohao Xu, Xiaonan Huang

entry.summary: The paper addresses monocular depth estimation when multiple surfaces lie along a single ray, jointly predicting both which surfaces are present and their metric depth. It introduces an image-conditioned multi-Bernoulli depth set representation and an auxiliary-free Exact Multi-Bernoulli (ExactMB) objective that learns depth and presence via one-to-one assignments to complete, distinct targets. The authors extend real and synthetic layered-depth benchmarks and show ExactMB reduces overprediction relative to depth stacking baselines.

entry.title: On Evaluating and Improving Conversational Agents in Production

author.name: Kasra Hosseini, Wen-Sen Cheng, Marco-Andrea Buchmann, Emir Mulabegovic, Weiwei Cheng

entry.summary: Authors from a production shopping-assistant team present a framework for evaluating and improving a large-scale multi-agent conversational system, addressing three obstacles: logged conversations cannot be replayed against modified systems, stochastic LLM components and dynamic product/personalization state confound comparisons, and aggregate quality scores obscure which behavior changed. The paper reports practical lessons from deploying the framework. This is valuable ground truth about real-world agent evaluation.

entry.title: Rondo: Unsupervised Discovery of Recurring Temporal Structure

author.name: Yingtian Shi, Ankith Chandra, Thomas Pl\"otz

entry.summary: Rondo is an unsupervised approach for discovering hierarchical recurring structure in time series, capturing both short recurring units and complex sequences composed of them. Unlike prior methods that treat temporal scales independently and assume complete static sequences, Rondo operates online and evolves as new observations arrive. This reduces the need for costly human annotation in temporal data interpretation.

entry.title: STAMP: Predicting Out-of-Distribution Generalization without Target Data

author.name: Md Kawsher Mahbub, Milon Biswas

entry.summary: STAMP is a source-only, target-label-free criterion that predicts out-of-distribution generalization by computing an output-space correlation ratio over semantically stable versus random pairs of source-domain images. Across 44 chest X-ray models spanning CNNs, ViTs, and foundation models, temporal STAMP achieves Spearman correlations of 0.844-0.855 with downstream OOD performance. This offers a practical way to select models likely to generalize without target data.

entry.title: ParallelPilot: Supporting Coordination and Monitoring in Parallel AI Coding

author.name: Tao Long, Weili Shi, Hussein Mozannar, Maya Murad, Rafah Hosn

entry.summary: Studies how developers supervise multiple concurrent AI coding agents, deriving the PILOT framework of five supervisory practices (Planning, Isolating, Logging, Observing, Triaging) from a formative study, then building ParallelPilot with a planning interface, run-logger, and ambient dashboard. A within-subjects study with 16 participants showed 63% higher ticket throughput and one more concurrent agent supervised.

entry.title: ZeroGAR: Benchmarking the Adversarial Robustness of Zero-Shot Graph Models

author.name: Zhongjian Zhang, Xiao Wang, Busheng Zhang, Bo Yan, Xingtong Yu, Yue Gao, Jia Li, Chuan Shi

entry.summary: ZeroGAR is the first systematic benchmark for adversarial robustness of zero-shot graph models, evaluating 13 representative models across three paradigms on target graphs under adversarial manipulation. It reveals how transferable graph knowledge holds up when unseen graphs are attacked, a question ignored by clean-graph evaluations and supervised robustness benchmarks. Security-relevant for deployed graph foundation models.

entry.title: Quizzing the Translation: A Prover-Grounded Evaluation Metric for NL$\rightarrow$FOL

author.name: Pu Suo, Ali Emami

entry.summary: SIV is a new evaluation metric for natural-language-to-first-order-logic translation that generates positive and contrastive probes from the target formula and verifies candidate translations with a theorem prover. It fixes a key flaw of BLEU, BERTScore, and Smatch++, which can score more broken translations higher due to surface-overlap rewards.

entry.title: ARCH-B: Architectural Representation, Comprehension and Hierarchy Benchmark

author.name: Kieran Sagar Parikh, Jose Luis Garcia del Castillo y Lopez

entry.summary: ARCH-B is a benchmark of 354 four-choice questions across 11 cross-representational archetypes testing whether multimodal models can recognize the same building across photographs, floor plans, elevations, sections, and renderings. It evaluates 25 multimodal models against 5,830 human responses, finding model accuracy from 10.45% to 83.90% versus a 35.35% human baseline, with models strong on outlier detection but weaker elsewhere. It fills a real gap in characterizing cross-representational visual understanding.

entry.title: LLMs are not stochastic parrots: Evidence for meaning-mediated abstraction from conlang-like tasks

author.name: Julia Witte Zimmerman, Calla G. Beauregard, Tabia Tanzin Prama, Parisa Suchdev, Kathryn Cramer, Elisabeth Kollrack

entry.summary: The paper tests the strong stochastic parrot hypothesis by giving LLMs only natural-language descriptions of fictional languages combining statistically uncommon or unattested features, with no example outputs, and observing rule-following behavior. Success on such tasks would imply models cannot be relying solely on superficial statistical pattern matching, supporting meaning-mediated abstraction. A provocative conceptual contribution to debates about LLM cognition.

entry.title: SAIL: Spatial Audio Intelligence with Large Language Models via Disentangled Acoustic-Spatial Encoding and Dual-Stream Q-Former

author.name: Zhengding Luo, Jinyang Wu, Haozhe Ma, Yanghao Zhou, Woon-Seng Gan, Wenwu Wang

entry.summary: SAIL is a spatial audio LLM framework preserving acoustic-spatial structure and source-level correspondence from audio encoding through LLM alignment, using disentangled spatial acoustic encoding and a dual-stream Q-Former. It targets embodied agents, wearables, and immersive systems that must localize sounds and reason about spatial relationships in multi-source scenes. Existing early-fusion designs lose sound-event-to-location correspondence, which SAIL fixes.

entry.title: FlexLoop: Depth-Elastic Looped Policies for Adaptive Test-Time Computation in Deep RL

author.name: Xun Wang, Ruishuo Chen, Yu Chen, Zhuoran Li, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: FlexLoop identifies that pretrained looped RL policies suffer severe recurrent-depth specialization, with reliable decisions concentrated near the full trained depth, tying deployment computation to that depth. It introduces depth-elastic looped policies enabling reliable decisions across recurrent depths with adaptive computation at deployment. This addresses an underappreciated limitation of looped architectures for test-time compute scaling.

entry.title: ESTHER: Egocentric Stereo Hand Estimation and Reconstruction in the Wild

author.name: Hongyu Ma, Hairong Qu, Shiqi Zhao, Yongsong Yang, Peng Yin

entry.summary: ESTHER provides an end-to-end model for metric 3D hand reconstruction from wearable egocentric stereo video, combining stereo geometry, temporal reasoning, and purpose-built output representation, trained on pseudo-labels from a calibrated pipeline. It also releases ESTHER3D, an in-the-wild training set paired with a motion-capture test benchmark, filling a gap for robotics, AR, and VR perception.

entry.title: Still There, No Longer Seen: Exposing Compression-Induced Risk in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Qiankun Li, Yuechen Zhang, Bowen Chen, Shilinlu Yan, Zhenhong Zhou, Kun Wang, Li Sun

entry.summary: Defines compression-specific failures in LVLMs as adversarial inputs that remain correct under full-token inference but fail after visual token compression, framing compression-induced risk as a paired failure attribution problem. Counterfactual diagnostics show retained-set allocation causally changes compressed correctness, motivating the proposed CIRA mitigation.

entry.title: Multi-Attractor GNNs: Set-Valued Expressivity Beyond Unique Equilibria

author.name: Jialin Liu

entry.summary: The paper shows that recurrent and equilibrium GNNs with multiple equilibria can represent set-valued equivariant maps, with different initializations converging to different valid solutions. Under regularity assumptions, it constructs globally Lipschitz, permutation-equivariant dynamics converging almost surely to valid solutions.

entry.title: Do Coding Agents Reuse Existing Code or Reinvent the Wheel?

author.name: Dongsheng Ma, Sizhe Wang, Xinyi Huang, Zhengren Wang, Yuhan Wang, Luyang Si, Xincheng Wei, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: RepoReuse is a multi-turn benchmark auditing whether coding agents reuse existing code in real repositories, where requirements unfold turn by turn and the workspace accumulates. It is built by an automated pipeline combining AST-based dependency graphs, evidence collection, and execution-verified task synthesis.

entry.title: Spontaneous Context Restoration: How Language Models Recover from Corrupted Inputs

author.name: Pranjal Garg, Jacob Beck

entry.summary: The paper studies context restoration: models producing correct outputs despite deleted, replaced, or misspelled inputs. Using attention-only transformers and five pretrained LLMs (1B-32B), it shows restoration emerges spontaneously without denoising training and follows a two-phase process of localizing corruption then accumulating repairs.

entry.title: OMP-MoE: Efficient Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs via Orthogonal Matching Pursuit

author.name: Dezhi Li, Lujun Li, Qiyuan Zhu, Hao Gu, Bei Liu, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Reformulates MoE expert pruning as a sparse signal reconstruction problem solved with Orthogonal Matching Pursuit, treating expert contributions as dictionary atoms and greedily selecting experts that minimize reconstruction error while accounting for inter-expert dependencies. The method is training-free and targets the memory footprint of MoE LLMs.

entry.title: Grounding Vision-Language Models in Driving Semantics: A Multi-Dataset Predicate Framework for Explainable Reasoning

author.name: Mohamed Chouai, Fazli Faruk Okumus, Stefan Kugele

entry.summary: Introduces a deterministic predicate framework that derives driving-scene semantics from measurable geometric, kinematic, temporal, map, and traffic-control evidence, materialized in a common Predicate Knowledge Graph across nuPlan and nuScenes. Enables verifiable, explainable evaluation of vision-language model outputs against actual traffic situations.

entry.title: Averaged Mirror Descent and Dual Gradient Methods: Convergent Algorithms for Entropic Gromov-Wasserstein Problem

author.name: Joanna Mark, Gabriel Rioux, Riccardo Passegger

entry.summary: Provides convergence guarantees for mirror descent and dual gradient methods applied to the entropically regularized Gromov-Wasserstein problem, whose convergence had previously been assumed despite a lack of analysis. Proposes averaged variants and establishes convergent algorithms for this widely used optimal transport distance between metric measure spaces.

entry.title: FUND: Density Flow for Sampling Unnormalised Distributions

author.name: Vikas Kanaujia, Vipul Arora

entry.summary: FUND learns Boltzmann distributions without true samples, inspired by flow matching but matching distribution trajectories rather than sample trajectories. It iteratively reshapes the target distribution using model geometry, aiming to overcome MCMC limitations like critical slowing down and poor mode-mixing, and constraints of Boltzmann Generators. This is relevant to sampling from complex physical systems.

entry.title: Muon Under Gradient Noise and the Limits of Orthogonalization Near Optima

author.name: Xiaohui Xie

entry.summary: This theoretical analysis examines what Muon's orthogonalization of the momentum buffer does near an optimum where minibatch noise dominates. Under Gaussian noise, the expected Muon update reduces to a scaled gradient step, but a Hermite expansion reveals a nonlinear residual uncorrelated with input noise whose covariance momentum partially suppresses.

entry.title: How Synthetic Labels Improve Conformal Prediction: A Perspective on Conditional Coverage

author.name: Qianyi Chen, Bo Li

entry.summary: The paper studies whether cheaply generated synthetic labels (from domain or language models) can improve conditional coverage in conformal prediction when trusted calibration data are scarce, introducing prediction-powered quantile learning that estimates pinball risk on a synthetic pool and corrects bias with paired trusted outcomes. It shows population conditional coverage can improve under this scheme.

entry.title: HiLoRe: What to Store, Compress, or Recompute for Efficient GRPO Training

author.name: Xinrui Chen, Mengyang Li, Ou Wu, Ji Zhang

entry.summary: HiLoRe improves memory efficiency of GRPO training by allocating activation fidelity based on policy-update exposure, linking GRPO loss coefficients to state-level approximation sensitivity before the backward pass. This addresses the waste in fixed gradient-checkpointing schedules, which the paper notes can leave substantial GPU memory unused while paying recomputation overhead.

entry.title: Augmented Feature Boosting for Multicalibration

author.name: Ira Globus-Harris, Inbal Livni Navon

entry.summary: Analyzes a discretization-free feature-augmentation boosting paradigm for multicalibration, avoiding the rounding sensitivity of standard audit-and-repair approaches that repeatedly discretize a predictor's range. The theoretical work characterizes how boosting with augmented features achieves residuals unbiased globally and conditioned on predictor level sets under rich test-function classes.

entry.title: T-SNN: Temporal Simplicial Neural Network for EEG Decoding

author.name: Nikita Malik, Shubhajit Roy, Mohit Kataria, Isuru Herath, Suraj Yadav, In\'es Garc\'ia-Redondo, Dhananjay Bhaskar

entry.summary: T-SNN represents EEG recordings as sequences of evolving simplicial complexes, combining simplicial convolutions with recurrent updates to capture dynamic higher-order interactions among brain regions. It outperforms convolutional, recurrent, graph-based, and Transformer baselines on the seven-class SEED-VII emotion recognition task.

entry.title: KVCMAS: Efficient KV cache Correction for Shared Context in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Hyesung Jeon, Hyeongju Ha, Seoyoung Lee, Beomseok Kang, Jae-Joon Kim

entry.summary: KVCMAS corrects KV caches for shared context in prompt-specialized multi-agent systems, where agent-specific prefixes alter caches of the same shared context and force costly repeated prefill. It improves on selective recomputation and prior delta-correction methods by supporting first-seen shared context without out-of-workflow reference caches or memory-intensive online correction states.

entry.title: Rotated Manifold Optimization for Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Yuhui Ding, Javier Zazo, James Hensman

entry.summary: This paper proposes an optimizer for LoRA that explicitly incorporates the gauge symmetry of low-rank factorization by extending recent matrix optimizers for full-parameter training to the fixed-rank matrix manifold, interpreting rotation and normalization under a rotated basis. The optimizer converges faster to lower held-out loss with better or comparable downstream performance on supervised finetuning and RL tasks.

entry.title: QAMM: Adjoint MeanFlow Matching for Few-Step Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuehu Gong, Shutong Ding, Mokai Pan, Yimiao Zhou, Jiashu Hou, Ye Shi, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: QAMM converts critic-derived adjoint signals into supervision for MeanFlow's average velocity, letting a flow policy learn finite-interval transport directly and generate actions with very few network evaluations. It derives the adjoint MeanFlow target and trains with offline actor-critic, achieving competitive two-call policies on HumanoidMaze tasks.

entry.title: When Can Attention Heads Be Statically Defined?

author.name: Weixian Waylon Li, Yintao Tai, Marcio Fonseca, Shay B. Cohen

entry.summary: Identifies attention heads with low pattern variance during pretraining and introduces Selective Attention Freezing (SAF), which replaces such heads' attention weights with fitted post-softmax means stored via linear-in-length position/distance representations. Replacing 25% of heads yields about 1.056x faster training at matched token budgets with a fused kernel handling mixed execution.

entry.title: QiYao-M: Multimodal Time Series Foundation Model with Role-Aware Modeling of Endogenous and Exogenous Modalities

author.name: Hanyin Cheng, Linfeng Wang, Zhengbo Qu, Yang Shu, Zhongwen Rao, Meng Wang, Yijie Li, Xin Jiang, Bin Yang, Chenjuan Guo

entry.summary: Presents QiYao-M, a multimodal time-series foundation model that treats endogenous and exogenous modalities with distinct mechanisms rather than shared ones. It uses an Endo-Multimodal Predictor/Supervision to learn how endogenous signals evolve, and an exogenous module designed to generalize across domains and modality types despite scarce pretraining data. This role-aware separation targets a real shortcoming of existing multimodal TSFMs.

entry.title: MaPP: A Unified Marginalized Posterior-Predictive Framework for Data-Efficient RLVR

author.name: Yangyang Ren, Haodong Zhu, Sheng Xu, Yanjing Li, Nikolai Yu. Zolotykh, Wentao Zhang, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes composition noise in GRPO-style RLVR, where a response's advantage depends on randomly sampled peer outcomes, showing this introduces a non-vanishing variance component with an irreducible lower bound. MaPP provides a marginalized posterior-predictive framework for online prompt selection that accounts for how reliably learning signals are extracted, improving data efficiency. This targets the high rollout and update costs of RLVR.

entry.title: AIM-ZO: Activation-Informed Subspace Maintenance for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yue Xie, Zhi Zheng, Yunpeng Ba, Xuyang Wu, Xialiang Tong, Zhichao Lu, Tao Zhong, Zhenkun Wang

entry.summary: AIM-ZO improves zeroth-order (memory-efficient, backprop-free) LLM fine-tuning by maintaining a high-quality activation-informed subspace for perturbations, addressing failures of overly compressed or poorly maintained low-dimensional subspaces. It uses activation statistics to keep update directions informative, reducing wasted forward evaluations.

entry.title: Provable Benefits of Regularization: Fast Rates for Adversarial Imitation Learning

author.name: Hanbin Zhou, Shangzhe Li, Alexander Braverman, Weitong Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes fast finite-sample rates for jointly regularized adversarial imitation learning in finite-horizon MDPs with general function approximation, explaining why reward and entropy regularization empirically help methods like GAIL. Its model-free Dually Regularized AIL algorithm combines KL policy regularization with an occupancy-weighted quadratic reward penalty.

entry.title: Unifying Distributional Training for One-Step Visual Generation

author.name: Chi Zhang, Haoyang Shi, Yueyi Liu, Ruichuan An, Junkang Zhou, Chang Li, Xiuyuan Lu, Yichi Zhang, Bo Wang, Yuhang Wu, Sen Cui, Miao Liu

entry.summary: Develops a unified theoretical framework for distributional training of one-step visual generation, separating distribution modeling from matching discrepancy via Wasserstein gradient flow, and recovering FD-Loss and Gaussian-kernel Drifting as special cases. It introduces MGFlow, which models feature distributions with Gaussian mixtures at adjustable granularity and supports both optimal transport and sample-based matching.

entry.title: HERO-MoE: Historical Expert Routing with Scale-Preserving Fusion

author.name: Junxiang Qiu, Zhengsu Chen, Xinting Hu, Shuo Wang, Hengheng Zhang, Shaofeng Zhang, Changcheng Li, Boyu Shi, Qi Tian

entry.summary: HERO-MoE injects historical routing priors into Mixture-of-Experts routers by reusing detached dense routing distributions from preceding MoE layers, preserving the original token-conditioned routing branch while adding the historical signal. The approach exploits evidence that MoE routing reflects input semantics across depth, which standard routers ignore.

entry.title: The Key Handoff: Retrieval in Hybrid Language Models

author.name: Kaan Kale, Oguzhan Baser, Sriram Vishwanath

entry.summary: Investigates how hybrid language models, which replace most attention with a recurrent state, resolve and use key entities in two-hop retrieval questions compared to dense transformers. Across twelve dense and hybrid models, the authors transplant hidden states between stories to trace whether information flows through a computed bridge entity or prompt position.

entry.title: Beyond One-Step Accuracy: State-Affine Latent Transition for Reliable Visual Planning

author.name: Boyuan Zhang, Yingjun Du, Xiantong Zhen, Ling Shao

entry.summary: The paper analyzes error propagation in joint-embedding world models used for visual planning, decomposing multi-step rollout error into per-step errors and their propagation. It shows state-affine dynamics, transitions with state-independent Jacobians, eliminate the nonlinear propagation residual so error operators depend only on the action sequence. This motivates a more reliable training objective for planning under recursive rollout.

entry.title: Controlling Speaking Rate in Autoregressive TTS via Activation Steering

author.name: Francesco Verdini, Antonis Asonitis, Aref Farhadipour, Marzieh Razavi, Pierre-Edouard Honnet, Vijeta Avijeet, Juan Pablo Zuluaga Gomez

entry.summary: The paper shows that speaking rate in autoregressive TTS can be controlled at inference time without retraining by clamping a single decoder block's activation along a discovered speed axis, learned from synthetically time-stretched and compressed speech. The steering preserves speaker identity and naturalness and generalizes across architectures.

entry.title: Physics-Attested Federated Learning: Securing Collaborative Anomaly Detection in Critical Water Infrastructure

author.name: Jeff Nijsse, Shu Su, Benjamin Oholeguy, Sreenivas Sremath Tirumala

entry.summary: The paper addresses data poisoning in federated learning for industrial intrusion detection by repurposing cyber-physical process invariants, such as conservation laws and actuator couplings, into verifiable admission requirements for federated updates, mined automatically from clean operational data. Existing defenses operate only in update space and cannot distinguish updates derived from fabricated telemetry. The admission gate is evaluated on two physical water testbeds (SWaT, WADI) and the BATADAL benchmark across seven aggregation rules.

entry.title: TopoEP: Topology-Aware Load Balancing for Expert-Parallel MoE Training

author.name: Jiacheng Zhu, Xie Zhao, Gongming Zhao, Hongli Xu, Yao Fei, Jin Fang

entry.summary: TopoEP is a GPU-native, topology-aware load-balancing system for expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts training that avoids CPU-side planning, device-host transfers, and cross-rank synchronization. It accounts for hierarchical scale-up and scale-out communication costs of modern GPU clusters to prevent hot-expert stragglers from prolonging the expert-parallel stage.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multi-Turn Image Editing

author.name: Liangbing Zhao, Le Zhuo, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: The paper identifies a train-test mismatch in multi-turn image editing: models trained on clean source images must condition on their own imperfect outputs recursively, causing rapid degradation. MT-OPSD trains on self-generated conditioning states with clean-conditioned teacher supervision, requiring no multi-turn annotations, and introduces the LME-Bench evaluation.

entry.title: TeacherGRPO: Closing the Capacity Gap in Reasoning Distillation via Teacher Alignment

author.name: Zhenyu Lei, Zihan Chen, Yaochen Zhu, Shangbin Feng, Zaiyi Zheng, Ruocheng Guo, Yushun Dong, Jundong Li

entry.summary: Identifies the Gap Curse in reasoning distillation: as teachers grow more sophisticated, their distributions diverge from what students can approximate, degrading distillation outcomes. Proposes Teacher Alignment, adapting the teacher toward the student's distribution using GRPO-style RL (TeacherGRPO) while avoiding the catastrophic collapse of teacher reasoning that naive alignment causes. Avoids the data filtering or intermediate-assistant compromises of prior mitigations.

entry.title: In-Context Adaptation of Encoder-Decoder Models in Speech Recognition

author.name: Yen Meng, Sharon Goldwater, Hao Tang

entry.summary: This paper asks whether in-context adaptation for ASR, previously shown in some LLM-based speech models, is an inherent capability of all encoder-decoder models. Testing collated and interleaved speech-text demonstrations across six models spanning cross-attention and LLM-based architectures, the authors find all models adapt out of the box to new speakers, accents, and domains. This suggests inference-time adaptation is a general property rather than an artifact of LLM-based speech models.

entry.title: Neural Language Models Learn the Contextual Distributions of Dependency Structures: a statistical learning theory to compositionality

author.name: Wang Bojun, Junjie Chen, Holly Jenkins, Elizabeth Wonnacott

entry.summary: The authors propose a statistical learning account in which acquired dependency structures become new distributional units that language models track contextually, encoding structural meaning independent of lexical semantics. They test this with a synthetic grammar where structures have contextual distributions unrecoverable from component-token statistics.

entry.title: RemTraceNet: Few-Shot Forensic Detection of Invisible Watermark Attacks

author.name: Jidong Yang, Huaike Yu, Qi Li, Yuantian Miao, Wei Zong, Yang-Wai Chow, Willy Susilo, Chunpeng Wang, Suo Gao

entry.summary: Companion defense work arguing that watermark removal and forensic stealth are distinct objectives: a specialist model trained per known removal pipeline can separate attacked outputs from paired clean and unattacked watermarked controls in a few-shot setting. Provides complementary evidence for provenance and ownership verification when watermark verification fails.

entry.title: The Earth in One Gaze: Training-Free Active Focus for UHR Remote Sensing Understanding

author.name: Yao Zhang, Pengyu Dai, Wei Guo, Jian Liang, Jian Song, Yafei Ou, Hongruixuan Chen, Naoto Yokoya

entry.summary: The paper tackles ultra-high-resolution remote sensing understanding in multimodal LLMs by redistributing pixels within a continuous full-scene view rather than pruning tokens or cropping. A pilot study shows frozen MLLMs already make useful question-guided spatial requests, motivating a training-free active-focus mechanism that refocuses within one global view.

entry.title: EgoTSR++: Egocentric Spatiotemporal Reasoning for Task Progress Understanding

author.name: Xiaoda Yang, Can Wang, Yuxiang Liu, Pengfei Zhou, Jianwen Lou, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: EgoTSR diagnoses and improves VLM understanding of egocentric task progress, requiring models to judge which of two observations is closer to the goal from object configurations and spatial relations rather than timestamps. It introduces SpatialLogic-Bench with order-swapped evaluations and a framework to make progress judgment robust to non-monotonic retries and regressions.

entry.title: ProDyGS: Dynamic Gaussian Splatting from a Single Static Monocular Camera

author.name: Ugo Leone Cavalcanti, Fabio Tosi, Matteo Poggi, Andrea Conti, Vladimir Zlokolica, Valerio Cambareri, Stefano Mattoccia

entry.summary: ProDyGS performs dynamic 3D Gaussian splatting from a single static monocular video, where multi-view supervision is absent, by synthesizing proxy multi-view images from temporally consistent monocular depth estimates. A deformation network warps canonical Gaussians to learn temporal dynamics for novel view synthesis.

entry.title: FocusDrive: Reasoning with Visual Focus for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhiyuan Liu, Zehong Ke, Yuanxin Tian, Hao Cheng, Jinhao Li, Yining Xing, Yanbo Jiang, Zhenhua Xu, Wenhao Yu, Jianqiang Wang

entry.summary: FocusDrive is a structured multimodal reasoning framework for end-to-end driving that organizes planning around explicit visual focus, pairing descriptions of decision-relevant objects with image-patch references. This makes the correspondence between visual evidence and driving decisions concrete rather than implicit in text rationales.

entry.title: FeCoSplat: Feedback-Guided Compression for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yuxuan Li, Yihang Chen, Yufeng Zhang, Jianfei Cai, Weiyao Lin

entry.summary: Proposes a feedback-guided compression framework for feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting that compresses compact intermediate features rather than input images or heterogeneous Gaussian primitives, balancing compression efficiency against receiver-side reconstruction cost. Rendered views of an intermediate reconstruction guide the compression via feedback. This targets practical transmission of 3DGS representations for novel-view synthesis.

entry.title: SphMind: Towards Robust, Training-Free VLM-based Spatial Reasoning with a 360 Camera

author.name: Shriram Damodaran, Soumyaratna Debnath, Cheston Tan, Lin Wang

entry.summary: SphMind is a training-free, plug-and-play framework enabling multimodal LLMs to perform spatial reasoning on 360-degree camera imagery by decoupling semantic perception from geometric reasoning, avoiding the need to internalize spherical distortions. It addresses the mismatch between MLLMs trained on 2D perspective images and the non-Euclidean geometry of omnidirectional views.

entry.title: ENet-GP: Unified Document Image Restoration

author.name: Sujal Burad, Aakanksha, A. N. Rajagopalan, Sumit Shekar

entry.summary: Introduces GutenDoc, a large-scale dataset of high-resolution dense-text documents with physically grounded compound degradations jointly modeling geometric warping, non-uniform illumination, and blur, alongside ENet-GP, a unified restoration model. Existing methods handle these degradations independently on single-distortion benchmarks. The dataset and model push document restoration toward realistic capture conditions.

entry.title: Natural Image Autoencoder-Based fMRI Representations for Trait and State Prediction

author.name: Juhyeon Park, Yeonwoo Kim, Peter Yongho Kim, Yansen Wang, Mingqing Xiao, Dongqi Han, Dongsheng Li, Taesup Moon

entry.summary: FReD derives fMRI representations from a frozen Deep Compression AutoEncoder pretrained only on natural images, paired with simple readouts: temporal statistics with linear probing for trait prediction and a shallow Transformer over frame tokens for state prediction. The work probes how much fMRI-specific pretraining is actually needed and finds natural-image features transfer surprisingly well.

entry.title: AGILE-GS: Anchor-Guided Fast Next-Best-View Selection for Active 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Amirhossein Mollaei Khass, Nader Motee

entry.summary: AGILE-GS separates information seeking from camera selection in next-best-view planning for 3D Gaussian Splatting: a virtual anchor pose is optimized on SE(3) via Riemannian gradient ascent on expected information gain, then candidates are scored against the anchor and distilled into a non-redundant shortlist without rendering. This substantially reduces the cost of active view planning.

entry.title: Rate-Distortion Adaptive Primitive Selection for Omnidirectional Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yulong Cheng, Youneng Bao, Junfeng Zhou, Mu Li, Jie Wen

entry.summary: Introduces OIC-GS, an omnidirectional Gaussian splatting codec using a hierarchical HEALPix primitive grid with anchored spherical locations, supporting coarse-to-fine reconstruction and layered transmission. It adds rate-distortion adaptive primitive selection that accounts for per-primitive coding cost, improving quality and enabling efficient viewport decoding for VR.

entry.title: XFlow: A Workflow Model for Instruction-Guided Lesion Segmentation in Chest X-rays

author.name: Geon Choi, Hangyul Yoon, Hyunki Park, Sang Hoon Seo, Edward Choi

entry.summary: XFlow improves instruction-guided lesion segmentation in chest X-rays over ROSALIA by adopting a workflow-based, iterative delineation process that mimics how radiologists perceive lesions step by step, producing higher-quality masks with less scattered noise and handling absent-target instructions.

entry.title: DBCF: Dual-Branch Complementary Fusion of Foundation Models for Generalized Deepfake Detection

author.name: Fengming Gu, Mingjie He, Zonghui Guo, Jie Zhangb, Shiguang Shan

entry.summary: DBCF fuses complementary foundation models for deepfake detection: CLIP provides robust global semantic cues while DINO captures detailed local facial features, and a dual-branch fusion combines them to generalize across domains and unseen manipulations. The work responds to the generalization limits of small-scale forgery detectors.

entry.title: Resolution as a First-Class Decision: Task-Conditioned Routing for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Zhiqiang Xia, Yang Li, Xinyuan Zhang, Yuchen Liu, Haoyu Lu, Jiaming Xu, Runyu Shi, Ying Huang

entry.summary: TCRR reframes visual compression in multimodal LLMs as a task-conditioned decision, using a lightweight cross-modal router that modulates backbone visual representations with textual semantics to predict the minimal sufficient input resolution per query. This attacks an upstream inefficiency that token-compression methods ignore: resolution is typically a static, task-agnostic hyperparameter despite quadratic cost scaling. The idea of per-query adaptive resolution is elegant and complementary to token pruning.

entry.title: Proxy2World: Learning to Generate Worlds From Lightweight Proxies without Seeing Them

author.name: Hongli Xu, Weilong Yan, Anbang Wang, Chunyu Zou, Siyu Hong, Jingwei Huang

entry.summary: Proxy2World is a controllable world model that learns to generate detailed, natural visuals from lightweight scene proxies trained only on ordinary posed RGBD videos, without requiring authored proxy-video pairs. It jointly learns depth-conditioned RGB generation and joint RGBD generation via cross-modal flow matching, enabling proxy-camera hybrid denoising that follows proxy structure while producing rich appearance. It also introduces ProxyBench for evaluation.

entry.title: When Should the Count Change? Learning State Maintenance for Causal Video Counting

author.name: Pengyiang Liu, Dongyue Lyu, Junbo Niu, Zhongyue Shi, Jiahao Xie, Si Liu

entry.summary: StaMina learns to maintain counting state over continuous video through state-conditioned updates handling visibility, persistent identities, and completed-event records, with differentiable recurrence trained over legal transition paths constrained by count endpoints. It introduces a multi-source data pipeline (39.8K spatial queries) and evaluates on SVCBench with partial overlap and held-out groups. Reframing video counting as state maintenance with causal event transitions is a fresh formulation.

entry.title: Mind the RefGAP: Correcting Reference Attention in Diffusion-Based Visual Editing

author.name: Yanan Wang, Shengcai Liao, Guangyi Liu, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: The paper identifies that diffusion-based reference-guided editors under-use reference information — e.g., edit-region queries in LoomVideo attend less than 1% to the reference — and proposes RefGAP, a training-free online correction that applies logit offsets to reference attention based on measured attention mass, strengthening reference use in edit regions and limiting spillover elsewhere.

entry.title: Awaken, Then Scale: Tiny Adaptation for MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Mohammed Wattad, Tamir Shor, Alexander M. Bronstein

entry.summary: Dormant Awakening (DA) specializes an MRI reconstruction model to a new dataset by fitting only a small set of zero weights from a single labeled slice, yielding PSNR gains around 0.43-0.51 dB across fourteen U-Net and ViT sources. The authors analyze how scaling the fitted correction changes evaluation PSNR and derive a capping rule that bounds RMSE changes on new images without an evaluation reference. They compare DA against sparse adaptation and LoRA at a 10 percent adaptation budget.

entry.title: From PDF to Evidence: Structure-Aware Retrieval for Clinical Practice Guidelines

author.name: Xingyu Lin, Dehui Du

entry.summary: The paper casts evidence retrieval from clinical practice guidelines as document image analysis, parsing page images into typed structural elements (sections, table rows, flowchart paths, graded recommendations) rather than flattening PDFs into fixed-size chunks. Structure-aware evidence units retain their layout context so a retrieved result points to a specific element instead of a page. Evaluated on 26 guidelines (3,619 pages, Chinese and English) with 199 queries, it improves gold-element ranking over chunk-based baselines.

entry.title: Grasp2Twist: Learning Bimanual Dexterous Jar Opening by Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mo Xu (University of Wisconsin-Madison), Yunfu Deng (University of Wisconsin-Madison), Jianuo Wang (Independent Researcher), Josiah Hanna (University of Wisconsin-Madison), Bilge Mutlu (University of Wisconsin-Madison)

entry.summary: Grasp2Twist learns bimanual dexterous jar opening with RL, tackling unified multi-stage policy learning, sustained lid twisting, and sim-to-real transfer. It introduces a continuous enclosure measure and binary indicator derived from object-convex-hull geometry to guide grasp formation and the grasp-to-twist transition, plus finger repositioning strategies for sustained twisting.

entry.title: SurgFlow: 3D Object-Centric Contact Flow for Surgical Robot Manipulation

author.name: Changwei Chen, Xiao Liang, Yinuo Yang, Nicole Shen, Peihan Zhang, Sara Wickenhiser, Zekai Liang, Soofiyan Atar, Michael Yip

entry.summary: SurgFlow learns 3D object-centric contact flow from stereo surgical video without action labels, predicting per-point future 3D trajectories plus contact scores that indicate where and when a tool should engage an object. It addresses the scarcity of paired video-action data in surgery, where robots perform only about 1 percent of procedures. This is notable as an embodiment-agnostic route to leveraging abundant surgical video.

entry.title: MonoEgo: Monocular Metric Egocentric Demonstration Capture with Passive Wrist Constellations and Sparse Workstation Anchors

author.name: Jie Xu, Kangjin Yu, Ziyi Jin, Beichen Wang, Zhongpu Xia

entry.summary: MonoEgo is a demonstration capture system that replaces active wrist instrumentation with offline monocular reconstruction using a single 90-FPS global-shutter camera observing passive wrist constellations and sparse workstation anchors. The MonoTag SLAM pipeline combines marker corners with ORB geometry and rejects ambiguous planar-marker poses, while a metric Atlas supports scale re-anchoring, verified map merging, and retrospective localization. This lowers the hardware and synchronization burden for collecting image-aligned metric robot demonstrations.

entry.title: Memory in the Sky: Low-Altitude Question Answering with Multi-Agent Memory Aggregation

author.name: Chengyang Li, Yujie Wan, Shuai Wang, Kejiang Ye, Weijie Yuan, Boyu Zhou, Yik-Chung Wu, Chengzhong Xu, Huseyin Arslan

entry.summary: This paper defines low-altitude question answering (LAQA), where distributed UAV memories are aggregated at a ground server to answer questions about long-horizon observations, requiring an explicit measure of memory value. It proposes a generative adversarial exam that uses forward simulation to score memory quality without accessing internals of the black-box captioning, retrieval, and reasoning pipeline, then builds resource allocation on this metric. It opens a new problem formulation at the intersection of UAV systems and embodied memory.

entry.title: A Weak Notion of Symmetry for Control Systems

author.name: Jake Welde, Riley Link, Pieter van Goor

entry.summary: The authors introduce weak invariance, a relaxed notion of symmetry for control systems in which the non-symmetric residual dynamics are captured by another control system evolving on the symmetry group. Weakly invariant systems strictly generalize classical invariant systems while retaining many favorable estimation and control properties. This provides new theoretical flexibility where classical symmetry is broken by external forces or partial dynamics.

entry.title: Decentralized Master-Mind: Joint Action Refinement through Iterative Intent Denoising in Multi-Agent Pathfinding

author.name: Valeriy Vyaltsev, Anton Andreychuk, Taisia Zlotnikova, Konstantin Yakovlev, Aleksandr Panov, Alexey Skrynnik

entry.summary: DMM addresses a subtle failure in decentralized multi-agent pathfinding: independently sampling per-agent actions can recombine locally valid choices into incompatible joint actions. It replaces one-shot sampling with discrete, iterative refinement of action intents across communication rounds, inspired by diffusion-style denoising. This improves learned MAPF policies under partial observability.

entry.title: PastForward: Faster On-Device GUI Agents via Computational Experience Reuse

author.name: Taehwan Park, Changmin Lee, Hayeon Lee, Taesik Gong

entry.summary: PastForward accelerates on-device GUI agents by reusing validated, fine-grained computational experience from ordinary task execution during decoding, avoiding full VLM inference at every action step. This keeps sensitive screen data local while reducing the latency and compute costs that make edge deployment difficult.

entry.title: World Models with Predictable Long-Horizon Marginals

author.name: Yuhao Du, Shunian Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a world-model formulation that explicitly constrains the behavior-averaged transition to preserve a fixed Gaussian reference stationary law, ensuring rollouts retain the data distribution rather than merely making good one-step predictions. For controlled systems, a conditional action chart preserves behavior occupancy, and the authors derive an absolute convergence bound. Evaluated across 216 settings.

entry.title: PlanGuard: A Guardrail for Multi-Step Plan Safety in Embodied Agents

author.name: Junchi Chen, Changtao Miao, Yuxiao Xiang, Zhenchao Jin, Haojie Yuan, Qi Chu, Tao Gong, He Liu, Bo Zhang, Jiansheng Cai, Zhe Li, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: PlanGuard is presented as the first pre-execution detector that evaluates the physical safety of a complete multi-step plan in its environment, addressing compositional risks that general semantic-harm guardrails and per-subtask embodied detectors miss. The authors build the MSP-Safe dataset via paired task construction, diverse planner generation, and three-judge safety annotation, then train detectors with task-oriented SFT. It fills a real gap in embodied agent safety pipelines.

entry.title: Diagnosing Sampled LLM Reasoning in Formal Geometry: Coverage, Realization, and Validity Evidence

author.name: Xiao Yue, Guangzhi Qu

entry.summary: The CRV protocol evaluates sampled LLM reasoning in formal geometry along three axes: coverage (answer availability in the pool), realization (readout accuracy on a frozen candidate pool), and validity evidence (label-blinded critic judgment of derivational support). Applied to HardShift441, a 441-problem set where a reference solver leaves 406 unsolved, it dissects where pass-at-k succeeds numerically but fails evidentially. This matters because repeated sampling can mask unsupported derivations.

entry.title: QureRadEmbed: Structuring Radiological Similarity through Attribute and Reasoning Supervision

author.name: Janhavi Prabhu, Sahil, Shivam Ashok Shukla, Manoj Tadepalli

entry.summary: QureRadEmbed is a 4B radiology-aware embedding encoder trained with deterministic attribute-decomposed ranking targets (RadSim) plus report-alignment with hierarchical reasoning descriptions (RadThought), via a three-stage curriculum. It achieves 0.996 mean ordering accuracy across ten controlled synthetic attributes and improves correlation metrics on real data. This addresses the gap where broad biomedical similarity models ignore qualifiers like laterality, lobe, and severity.

entry.title: PPG-LM: A Photoplethysmography-Language Model with Multi-Level Clinical Alignment

author.name: Xiaoda Wang, Minxiao Wang, Maxwell A Xu, Patrick Langer, Kaiqiao Han, Defu Cao, Xiao Luo, Yuzhe Yang, Yan Liu, Xiao Hu, Yizhou Sun, Wei Wang, Carl Yang

entry.summary: PPG-LM is a language-model-based foundation approach for photoplethysmography signals that aligns local observations, care events, and entire visits with PPG representations using both signal-derived physiological supervision and clinical context from EHRs. It moves beyond task-specific prediction heads of existing PPG foundation models. This enables scalable physiological assessment from a signal widely captured by monitors and wearables.

entry.title: ParaAgent: Reinforcing Parallel Acting in Open-World Tool Environments

author.name: Shengbin Yue, Hongru Wang, Siyuan Wang, Xiaoxin Chen, Wei Chen, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: Presents ParaAgent, which trains agents to coordinate exploration and execution across granularities via a structured parallel-action loop combining phase-level exploration-execution cycles with action-level parallelism. Training combines multi-agent cold-start demonstrations with RL under multi-level advantage decoupling for open-world tool environments.

entry.title: Designing Reliable LLM-as-a-Judge Measurement Systems for Multi-Turn Business Agents

author.name: Kaiwen Luo, Ming Gao

entry.summary: The paper presents an integrated methodology for production-grade LLM-as-a-judge evaluation of multi-turn business agents, spanning evaluation specification, modular atomic judges sharing versioned evidence, intent-preserving user simulation, and human-in-the-loop governance with explicit failure-ownership attribution. It shifts focus from one-shot judging to maintained measurement systems.

entry.title: ReplayLens: Auditing Agents' Use of Outcomes

author.name: Dong Xu, Zhangfan Yang, Jiantao Wu, Shipeng Zhang, Zexuan Zhu, Jiangqiang Li, Jun Zhang, Junkai Ji

entry.summary: ReplayLens is a black-box audit that perturbs one relationship in stored agent history at a time (outcome reassignment, pair transport, renaming, key-slot reassignment) to determine which relationship drives changed decisions when agents reuse logged experience. It disambiguates whether decision changes reflect scores, action names, or record positions.

entry.title: PowerBench: A Benchmark for Agentic Retrieval and Reasoning in Power Systems

author.name: Xijing Wang, Yinsheng Yao, Jinru Ding, Yidong Jiang, Ziwen Xu, Yiwen Jiang, Jie Xu, Dawei Cheng

entry.summary: PowerBench provides a generation framework and synthetic dataset for evaluating LLM agents in power systems, with 761 devices across 100 types, 13.35 million hourly telemetry records over two years, and 24,939 operational documents linked through dependency chains. It enables rigorous agentic retrieval and reasoning evaluation where real operational data is confidential.

entry.title: MechReasoner: A Simulator and Benchmark for Mechanistic Reasoning in Qualitative Physics

author.name: Danilo Gusicuma, Andr\'e Freitas

entry.summary: MechReasoner provides a confluence-based qualitative physics simulator plus a 1,120-item benchmark testing whether LLM answers preserve simulator-licensed ambiguity, quantified claims, causal transition evidence, and trace support across 18 mechanisms and six task families. It targets the gap between fluent mechanistic descriptions and constraint-respecting causal reasoning.

entry.title: JRDB-AVR: An Active Visual Reasoning Benchmark for Embodied Agents in Real-World Environments

author.name: Zhixi Cai, Fucai Ke, Sukai Huang, Maria Garcia de la Banda, Peter J. Stuckey, Gholamreza Haffari, Hamid Rezatofighi

entry.summary: JRDB-AVR converts existing real-world JRDB robotics data into an active visual reasoning benchmark where an embodied agent with a limited field of view must actively acquire evidence across time, viewpoint, and objects before answering. It exposes the gap where models can give plausible answers without ever observing the supporting evidence. Built via a structured question-generation engine, it enables evaluation of active evidence acquisition in realistic settings.

entry.title: The Argument and the Letterhead: Source-Position Coherence in AI Evaluation

author.name: Michele Loi

entry.summary: Using preregistered studies with 2,976 evaluations of six fixed texts under varying source attributions, this paper tests whether AI evaluators separate argument quality from speaker identity. Results show the source gap changes with the argument (e.g., a national-security argument rated differently under two sources while a civil-rights argument was not), indicating interactions beyond a constant source preference.

entry.title: TMCS: Tool-Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Compositional Chemical Problem Solving

author.name: Shengqin Wang, Jie Jin, Yu Cheng, Yihang Chen, Weilin Luo, Yuan Xie, Zhizhong Zhang

entry.summary: TMCS formalizes rigorous combinatorial chemistry problem solving as an interpretable, tool-augmented multi-agent workflow covering quantitatively constrained molecular modification, candidate validation, and systematic revision after failed attempts. It provides a unified loop for property-driven molecular optimization and workflow-level composition.

entry.title: SRHarness: A Harness for Agentic Symbolic Regression

author.name: Zihan Yu, Shixuan Zhou, Hao Huang, Jingtao Ding, Yong Li

entry.summary: SRHarness is a domain-specific runtime harness for LLM-driven agentic symbolic regression, built around composable scientific actions, persistent scientific state retaining evaluated hypotheses, and trajectory lifecycle management. It targets the infrastructure layer that determines whether agentic scientific search succeeds, independent of the underlying model. This matters because agentic discovery systems are increasingly bottlenecked by runtime support rather than raw model capability.

entry.title: SciFlow-Bench: Evaluating Structure-Aware Scientific Diagram Generation via Inverse Parsing

author.name: Tong Zhang, Honglin Lin, Zhou Liu, Chong Chen, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: SciFlow-Bench is a structure-first benchmark evaluating text-to-image models on scientific diagram generation directly from pixel outputs, built from real scientific PDFs. Each figure is paired with a canonical ground-truth graph and evaluated via a closed-loop round-trip protocol involving inverse parsing, exposing that modern image models produce visually plausible but structurally incorrect diagrams. It fills a gap left by image-centric or subjective metrics.

entry.title: Can't Find Waldo: Evaluating VLMs' Sensitivity to Image Resolution and Detail Level

author.name: Alexandra Schild, Gerard de Melo

entry.summary: This paper introduces a controlled framework disentangling resolution-related degradation from task difficulty in vision-language models, using semantics-preserving transformations. It proposes two metrics, Area Under the Scaling Curve and Prediction Variance Score, to quantify scaling robustness and prediction instability. This provides a systematic account of why VLMs fail on high-resolution, detail-dense scenes.

entry.title: DOHF: Online Diffusion Fine-tuning with Doob's $h$-transform Guidance

author.name: Zhengyi Guo, Jiayuan Sheng, Wenpin Tang

entry.summary: DOHF turns Doob's h-transform into a practical online fine-tuning algorithm for reward-based diffusion model training, assigning optimality weights to samples and distilling estimated local corrections into the generative model. Theoretically, it characterizes population-optimal DiffusionNFT updates and classifier-free guidance variants through a unified h-transform perspective, and the framework accommodates black-box and non-differentiable rewards. This provides both theory and a practical algorithm for rare-outcome diffusion fine-tuning.

entry.title: VoiceNet: Fine-Grained Voice Understanding Beyond Emotion at Scale

author.name: Christoph Schuhmann, Robert Kaczmarczyk, Gollam Rabby, Felix Friedrich, Maurice Kraus, Gijs Wijngaard, Kourosh Nadi, Huu Nguyen, Kristian Kersting, S\"oren Auer

entry.summary: VoiceNet is a human-annotated benchmark for fine-grained voice performance understanding, addressing the gap where expressive speech synthesis has outpaced speech perception evaluation. It includes VoiceNet-Emo with a 40-emotion taxonomy and expert ratings, and VoiceNet-Ext scoring 57 talking-style attributes such as speaking rate, tension, and breathiness, plus an emotion-annotated dataset release (Emolia). This enables evaluation of expressive TTS beyond basic emotion categories.

entry.title: What Does a ProcGen Generalization Gap Measure? Action Rules, Convergence, and the Missing Random Floor

author.name: Abhisek Keshari

entry.summary: This single-author methodological paper argues that reported generalization gaps in RL need a measured random floor reference: the return of a uniform-random policy on the same levels under the same harness. On ProcGen, the floor changes the meaning of standard numbers, and switching between sampled and greedy test-time actions moves held-out return in both directions, with greedy evaluation dropping to or below the floor in three environments. It is a useful corrective to sloppy evaluation practice in RL generalization research.

entry.title: InterTab: Interleaved Visual-Structure Alignment for Multi-Modal Table Reasoning

author.name: Hanqian Li, Sirui Huang, Chen Ling, Jungang Li, Yu Huang, Kening Zheng, Yonghua Hei, Xiangrong He, Shiyi Wang, Pengcheng Zhu, Dongnan Liu, Wei Zhou, Linjian Mo, Nai Ding, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: InterTab is a framework for chain-of-thought reasoning over table images that interleaves reasoning steps with tool calls cropping structure-aligned table regions, allowing row-, column-, and cell-level evidence gathering as the question unfolds. The authors also release InterTab-22K, a dataset supporting this interleaved structure-aware reasoning. It addresses the limitation that current MLLMs encode the whole table image only once before reasoning.

entry.title: ECG-Scroll: A Long-Horizon, Streaming Benchmark and Agent Environment for Interpretation of Ambulatory Electrocardiograms

author.name: Haitao Li, Chenglin Li, Zhengyao Ding, Ziyu Li, Yiheng Mao, Zhengxing Huang

entry.summary: Recasts long-duration ECG interpretation as a long-horizon, online, streaming task where clinically decisive paroxysmal events must be caught as traces stream in, since recordings spanning hours to days cannot fit in one context. Provides a benchmark and agent environment requiring models to decide what to measure now, commit evidence to memory, and report events in real time.

entry.title: TAO-DA: Towards Autonomous Operation--A Dual-Arm Vision-Language-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation

author.name: Yongsheng Zhao, Han Gao, Baoping Cheng, Jingyao Tang, Dian Zhou, Deng Liang, Ji Ge, Xuanzhang Wen, Lei Zhao, Ye Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a symmetric Dual-Arm Expert architecture on a shared VLM backbone with decoupled arm-specific expert towers and a two-stage dual-arm intent routing scheme (explicit language routing then implicit state-based routing) to prevent cross-arm interference in coordinated bimanual manipulation. Targets autonomous operation across diverse coordinated tasks.

entry.title: TerMeZO: Ternary Sparse Zeroth-Order Optimization for Fine-tuning BitNet Models at the Edge

author.name: Houssem Sifaou, Prabodh Katti, Bipin Rajendran, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: TerMeZO enables memory-efficient fine-tuning of BitNet models with ternary weights by extending sparse zeroth-order optimization to respect the ternary structure, updating only a subset of latent weights without requiring first-order gradients. This aligns fine-tuning memory footprint with inference memory, targeting edge deployment.

entry.title: Dynamic Kuramoto-Hodge Operators for PDEs on Complex Geometries and Topologies

author.name: Xiang Li, Yue Song

entry.summary: The Dynamic Kuramoto-Hodge Operator (DKHO) is a neural operator for PDEs on complex domains that encodes fields on their native cochain supports, evolves Kuramoto-inspired relation states through Dirac-operator boundary and coboundary maps, and decodes responses in orthogonal Hodge subspaces. Topology constrains where information flows while learned coordination captures condition-dependent coupling. It advances neural PDE solvers on irregular geometries.

entry.title: HARMONIA: Interpretable Graph Learning through Mixtures of Neural Bases

author.name: Quan D. Bui, Nguyen Do, An Nguyen Dang, Huyen Nguyen, Nhu Duc Minh Nguyen, My T. Thai

entry.summary: HARMONIA is an interpretable-by-design graph learning framework introducing a Mixture of Neural Bases that routes features to specialized basis experts, enabling parameter sharing with feature specialization. It addresses scalability and explicit source-to-target contribution decomposition limitations of prior interpretable graph additive models. The work targets the tension between expressivity and interpretability in graph learning.

entry.title: WorldGraph: Graph-Native World Modeling

author.name: Zezhong Ding, Yipeng Li, Xike Xie

entry.summary: WorldGraph formulates graph world modeling (GWM) where the evolving graph itself constitutes the world dynamics, covering observed graph evolution, latent graph states, and heterogeneous graph-transition predictions, in contrast to prior work that merely uses graphs to organize internal states. It provides a benchmark suite (GWM suite) for this setting. Extends the world-model paradigm to relational, graph-structured environments.

entry.title: P2P: Cross-View Population Denoising for Unpaired Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction

author.name: Haojie Yang, Ran Su

entry.summary: P2P addresses perturbation response prediction for AI virtual cells by using stochastic cell-set views as supervision units instead of individual cells, exploiting that two views from the same condition share a reproducible population effect. This handles the fundamental unpaired nature of Perturb-seq data and absorbs sampling variation without confusing it with the estimated effect. It improves the fidelity of learned cellular simulators.

entry.title: Summarize Before Grounding: Query-Guided Chunk Condensation for Long-Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Nanxing Hu, Xiaoyue Duan, Qiwei Yan, Kailin Lyu, Jinchao Zhang, Guoliang Kang

entry.summary: SumGround proposes summarizing before grounding for long-video temporal grounding: query-guided chunk condensation removes redundant information that disturbs LVLMs, avoiding both the prohibitive memory of dense frame sampling and the evidence-miss risk of sparse sampling. This improves query-relevant evidence mining for localizing video intervals. It addresses a core memory-accuracy tradeoff in video reasoning.

entry.title: CoDrive: Cross-Vehicle World-Consistent Video Generation with Precise Trajectory Control for Cooperative Driving

author.name: Yu Meng, Baining Zhao, Junta Wu, Tengfei Wang, Rongze Tang, Haiyu Zhang, Wenqiang Sun, Chen Gao, Zhibo Chen, Xinlei Chen, Yong Li, Xiao-Ping Zhang, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: CoDrive is a cross-vehicle, multi-view driving video generation framework that jointly generates observations for multiple vehicles sharing one dynamic scene, interleaving per-vehicle local attention with global cross-vehicle attention for consistency, with camera trajectories encoded in a shared spatial coordinate system. It targets world-consistent synthetic data for cooperative autonomous driving.

entry.title: DivOPD: Spread Wide, Look Close for Asynchronous On-Policy Distillation of Multi-turn Agents

author.name: Hanyang Wang, Zeyuan Liu, Zhengyu Chen, Jingqing Ruan, Chaoxu Pang, Zhongda Su, Wulin Xie, Zhizhao Zeng, Ke Zeng, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: DivOPD is a learner-side batch-selection method for asynchronous multi-turn on-policy distillation that spreads a fixed turn budget across more rollouts and prioritizes turns with high cumulative teacher-student disagreement, excluding turns without usable teacher feedback. It prevents early or long rollouts from dominating updates and reduces wasted stale experience without changing losses or optimizers.

entry.title: OPIS: An Input-Grounded Benchmark for Multi-Object Memory in Video World Models

author.name: Hao Wang, Tao Yu, Liuzhou Zhang, HeXin Wang, Haopeng Jin, Yuxuan Zhou, Xinming Wang, Hongzhu Yi, Xinye Li, Yuanlei Wang, Ping Nie, Yan Huang, Yuxuan Zhang, Pengfei Zhou, Yanyan Zou, Wei Yang

entry.summary: Introduces OPIS, an input-grounded benchmark that anchors evaluation of multi-object memory in video world models to a fixed set of object instances from the initial observation, avoiding confounds from generated histories, video references, or selected revisit viewpoints. It comprises 500 cases across real-world, embodied-robotic, and game domains with dense annotations for 12,672 instances.

entry.title: eval-unlearn: Benchmarking unlearning in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Mansi, Nikhil Raghavan, Zixia Huang, Kai Sheng Ong, Ji Shen Lim, Brandon Siao Xiang Ling, Francesco Leofante

entry.summary: eval-unlearn is an open-source Python library providing unified, reproducible benchmarking for concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models, integrating twelve published techniques and nine evaluation metrics spanning erasure, adversarial robustness, generative quality, and retention. Its plugin architecture supports third-party extensions.

entry.title: Let the Neurons Die: Exploiting ReLU-Induced Model Degradation

author.name: Kexin Li, Wenjun Qiu, Joshua Abraham, Aditi Maheshwari, David Lie

entry.summary: The paper presents three training-time availability attacks exploiting dying ReLU neurons: a data-ordering attack that greedily pushes units toward negative pre-activations, and two poisoning attacks using gradient inversion to synthesize class-conditioned samples. This exposes a new training-time attack surface that degrades models without modifying labels in the basic variant.

entry.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution

author.name: Chaoqian Ouyang, Ling Yue, Libin Zheng, Huanghui Guo, Shengxiang Xu, YiShu Wang, Ran Li, Jian Yin, Shaowu Pan, Shimin Di

entry.summary: Presents TokenCast, a method that learns composable per-segment cost representations for LLM agent executions, capturing both a segment's own token consumption and the context growth it induces, so cumulative costs can be forecast and revised as a run unfolds. This addresses the fact that token usage varies by over an order of magnitude across identical task runs.

entry.title: FIDAL: Diversity-Aware Federated Active Learning Under Real-World Distribution Shifts

author.name: David Due\~nas Gaviria, Shadi Albarqouni

entry.summary: Presents FIDAL, an open-set federated active learning framework combining calibrated global-local evidential uncertainty, support-set diversity weighting, and adaptive OOD rejection using a foundation-model Gaussian-coverage signal thresholded per client and round. Targets federated clinical settings where annotation costs, domain shifts, and class imbalance co-occur.

entry.title: Model-Agnostic Online Certificate-Driven Calibration for Time Series Forecasting Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Chenfeng Huang, Zixuan Ma, George Michailidis

entry.summary: Proposes a model-agnostic online martingale PAC-Bayesian framework that yields finite-sample risk certificates for time series forecasting under temporal dependence, covariate shift, and concept shift, where standard PAC analyses fail. Enables certificate-driven calibration so forecasters remain quantifiably reliable as deployment dynamics drift from training conditions.

entry.title: Not All Errors Matter: Decision-Relevant Prediction Error Predicts Planning Quality

author.name: Linhao Wang, Yiyan Fan, Dongjin Huang

entry.summary: The paper shows that total prediction error in world models can be a misleading proxy for planning quality, since models with similar total error can differ widely when errors fall on different state dimensions. It introduces Decision-Relevant Prediction Error (DRPE) and an iso-error evaluation protocol, testing 55 controlled and learned models in a factored gridworld with a standardized planner. This challenges standard world-model evaluation practice.

entry.title: Retimed Bellman Flows: Escaping the Impossible Triangle of Velocity Bootstrapping

author.name: Boyang Xu, Shengzhe Chen, Hao Yan

entry.summary: The paper identifies a structural dilemma in flow-based critics for value learning: on straight paths, no residual-free affine mapping can both preserve Gaussian initial noise and maintain an unbiased Bellman target. Retimed Bellman Flows (ReBF) resolve this by querying the teacher critic at a dynamically shifted earlier flow time, yielding a provably conditionally unbiased velocity target.

entry.title: SMAT: Simple and Efficient Merge-Aware Training

author.name: Yanggan Gu, Yuanyi Wang, Zhen Li, Shuo Cai, Yuhang Liu, Junzhuo Li, Zihao Wang, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: SMAT frames common model-merging methods via three operations (Scale, Mask, Perturb) and trains experts to jointly optimize task loss and expected loss at simulated merged parameters by sampling scaling coefficients and perturbations. This improves post-merge performance without the overhead of prior merge-aware training methods.

entry.title: Reachability is not enough: Diagnosing long-range behavior in GNNs

author.name: Filippo Maria Bianchi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a framework measuring how strongly inputs at each graph distance affect GNN predictions, separating architectural limits from finite approximation, training, and numerical execution effects. It shows local message passing can spread influence slowly so practical implementations rely on nearby inputs even when the ideal computation uses the whole graph.

entry.title: DuoOPD: Learning from Joint Teacher-Student Outcomes for Multi-Task On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Ao Yu, Weibo Gao, Heng Zhou, Linan Yue, Rui Li, Suyi Liu, Yu Yan, Yizhong Zhang, Qi Liu

entry.summary: DuoOPD improves on-policy distillation by using the student's outcome to set feedback direction and the joint teacher-student outcome to shape teacher support — e.g., when only the teacher succeeds, its verified answer becomes context for scoring the student's failed response. This avoids the baseline failure where OPD pushes down even the student's correct responses.

entry.title: ChemOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Task Chemical Reasoning

author.name: Yaoyao Xu, Xinjian Zhao, Xiaozhuang Song, Xuemin Chen, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: Introduces ChemOPD, a framework for consolidating multiple specialized chemical reasoning capabilities into one LLM via multi-teacher on-policy distillation. It estimates task affinities from SFT gradients and solves a mixed-integer program to form partially overlapping specialist groups, while retaining a generalist teacher whose supervision anchors the distillation.

entry.title: GPARA: Graph-Posterior-Aligned Refinement and Active Acquisition for Grounding Diffusion Priors

author.name: Wangqian Chen, Hao Wang, Yumeng Zhang, Jiajia Guo, Junting Chen, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: GPARA learns a context-dependent graph surrogate over diffusion prediction residuals to actively ground frozen diffusion priors, inducing a reusable posterior response operator that propagates measurement innovations and evaluates candidate measurements via weighted posterior-risk reduction. This avoids repeated ensemble generation required by posterior-ensemble acquisition methods.

entry.title: Routing Without Embeddings: Fast And Interpretable Routing With Regular Expressions

author.name: Yifan Lu, Qiyue Zhang, Haotian Shan, Hanjie Chen, Jiarong Xing

entry.summary: The paper observes that scaling Qwen2.5 routing encoders from 0.5B to 72B parameters yields little routing-accuracy improvement, motivating REGEXROUTE: a pipeline that uses sparse autoencoders to discover interpretable regex features from unlabeled text, with an LLM converting grouped SAE latents into refined regex extractors for fast, interpretable LLM routing without neural encoders.

entry.title: M3OS: A Monte Carlo Graph Search-Orchestrated Multi-Agent LLM System for Evidence-Traced Molecular Optimization

author.name: Junjie Wang, Yaowei Jin, Ruohui Tang, Guonan Cui, Haojie Wang, Penglei Wang, Dingyan Wang, Duo An, Shuangjia Zheng, Qian Shi

entry.summary: M3OS is a multi-agent LLM system for small-molecule optimization that decouples design reasoning from optimization-state management using Monte Carlo graph search over a persistent graph of candidates, transformations, and evaluation evidence. It combines tool-driven candidate generation with LLM-assisted parent selection guided by rewards and visit statistics.

entry.title: SOLAR: A State-Driven Online Learning Rate Scheduler for LLM Pretraining

author.name: Qiulin Shang, Binyu Wang, Yongqi Qiao, Songde Rao, Zhoutong Wu, Kun Yuan
