The authors prove that incorporating a measurement never increases state uncertainty and that no measurement can induce arbitrarily large updates, instantiating the parametrization with a recurrent neural architecture with amplitude gates.

entry.title: Is H&E Image-to-Spatial Transcriptomics Simpler Than It Looks?

author.name: Duc T. Nguyen, Thanh Ha Do, Phuong M. Cao, Hieu Pham

entry.summary: Analyzes why simple estimators often match sophisticated architectures in predicting spatial gene expression from H&E histology, using an MSE error decomposition. It shows differences in average gene expression account for much of aggregate performance, and the key unresolved challenge is recovering within-slide variation, clarifying where model complexity is actually needed.

entry.title: Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer Actor--Critic: Diffusion Policy Improvement with Finite-Sample Analysis

author.name: Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Jincheng Ying

entry.summary: This paper proposes SFAC, an offline-to-online reinforcement learning method that performs KL-regularized policy improvement using conditional diffusion policies. It combines a minimax Bellman critic for advantage estimation with a Doob h-transform framework that expresses the policy update as a correction to a reference diffusion drift, estimated via paired self-normalized importance sampling, and provides finite-sample statistical guarantees for the resulting actor-critic algorithm.

entry.title: Let CSP Be Your ANCHOR: Adaptive Crystal Search over Frozen Structure Priors

author.name: Emma Lei Hovmand, Jonas Elsborg, Melih Kandemir, Arghya Bhowmik

entry.summary: ANCHOR separates where to search from how to generate in de novo crystal discovery: a frozen crystal structure prediction model acts as a fixed physical prior while a GRPO-trained composition policy explores with multi-objective rewards. It introduces continuous adaptive novelty (CAN), a graded novelty score against known structures and a growing discovery history. The approach targets more reliable materials-discovery pipelines.

entry.title: Prompt-Anchored Residual Adaptation for Biomedical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jingxuan Kang, Qianying Yue, Che Liu, Chen Qin

entry.summary: The paper proposes PARA, a few-shot adaptation method for biomedical vision-language models that keeps the frozen prompt-based prediction as a support-invariant semantic anchor while learning a visual residual prediction on top. This addresses the sensitivity of few-shot adapted predictions to the composition of the small labeled support set, which matters for biomedical classification tasks that hinge on subtle visual differences.

entry.title: Recursive LLM Degradation in Biomedical Question Answering: A Cross-Generation Study

author.name: Bibek Bhandari, Kshitij Lingthep

entry.summary: This study empirically examines model collapse from recursive synthetic-data training in biomedical QA using two Qwen2.5 sizes (0.5B and 3B), comparing recursive generations G0-G3 against a human-controlled condition across multiple seeds and a fixed expert-labeled evaluation set. It measures degradation in extraction, QA quality, and distributional properties as errors and biases are reintroduced across generations.

entry.title: On the Numerical Reliability of Differentiable Physics-Based Optimization for Robotic Material Manipulation

author.name: Xintong Yang, Minglun Wei, Yu-Kun Lai, Ze Ji

entry.summary: The paper studies the numerical reliability of gradients propagated through long, contact-rich differentiable physics simulations used in robotic material manipulation, using two Material Point Method system-identification benchmarks. It shows that GPU many-to-one sums whose order depends on thread scheduling can change long-horizon gradients and even reverse the sign of a parameter gradient. These findings raise important caveats for gradient-based optimization built on differentiable simulation.

entry.title: Beyond Reconstruction Loss in Post-Training Quantization: Balanced Fitting for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Minchan Kang, Kyeonghye Park, Seungyeon Sa, Seoyoung Cho, Daeshik Kim, Yucheol Cho

entry.summary: The paper proposes Balanced Fitting, a post-training quantization framework for large vision-language models that treats quantization effects as potentially beneficial regularization for certain layers and modalities rather than purely an error to minimize. Standard PTQ minimizes reconstruction loss against the full-precision model, which can over-preserve FP behavior and calibration-specific bias. The framework balances precision and regularization beyond reconstruction loss.

entry.title: When Text Matters: Design Principles for Visual Token Pruning in Vision-Language Model

author.name: Minchan Kang, Kyeonghye Park, Seoyoung Cho, Daeshik Kim, Yucheol Cho

entry.summary: The paper studies visual token pruning in large vision-language models and finds that applying textual guidance too early limits its ability to identify answer-relevant visual regions, while text-to-visual attention becomes more informative at intermediate decoder depths. Motivated by this analysis, it proposes a training-free method that separates early vision-guided pruning from later text-guided selection. This yields design principles for when and where text guidance helps in token pruning.

entry.title: G$^3$-LoRA: Organizing Reward-Weighted Video Data with Gradient-Guided Grouped LoRA

author.name: Jia Song (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Wenhow Li (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Lichen Bai (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Bada Ye (Tencent), Zeke Xie (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)

entry.summary: This work tackles post-training text-to-video models on heterogeneous reward-weighted data by probing category-level gradients, removing the shared update direction, and clustering categories by residual gradient compatibility. It trains group-specific LoRA experts per compatible cluster and consolidates them, avoiding the fragile assumption that all data categories induce compatible updates.

entry.title: Beyond Energy: When Sustainability Dimensions Reshape LLM Serving Decisions

author.name: Tianyao Shi, Xipeng Shen, Yi Ding

entry.summary: PRISM is a unified framework for characterizing and optimizing LLM serving across energy, carbon, water, and biodiversity impacts. The key finding is a fundamental distinction: computing configurations determine energy use, while deployment location and timing determine carbon, water, and biodiversity outcomes, which can change optimal serving decisions.

entry.title: CoSE-E: A Benchmark for Code-switched Speech Evaluation in Enterprise Settings

author.name: Shama Gupta, Hoang H Nguyen, Chelsea Huang, Lindsay Devon Brin, Fanny Riols

entry.summary: This paper introduces COSE-E, a synthetic benchmark and multidimensional evaluation framework for code-switched automatic speech recognition in enterprise contexts, covering five language pairs. Its key contribution is evaluating how code-switching transcription errors propagate into downstream voice agent task failures rather than just measuring edit-distance WER. This operational framing is useful for organizations deploying multilingual voice agents.

entry.title: Quantization Thresholds Replicate, Failure Modes Do Not: A Three-Model Study of Agentic Tool Use in Polish from 8-bit to 2-bit

author.name: Jakub Prejzner

entry.summary: Using PolAgentBench, a deterministic Polish-language agentic tool-use benchmark with adversarial probes and an arithmetic isolation ladder, the author measures three models (Bielik-11B, its distilled 7B variant, and Llama-PLLuM-8B) at six GGUF precisions from Q8_0 to Q2_K. The central finding is that while all models collapse between 3-bit and 2-bit quantization, the specific failure modes do not replicate across models. This suggests collapse thresholds generalize but downstream degradation is model-specific.

entry.title: A model of rational interlocutors: Unification of comprehension and production

author.name: Hanlin Wu, Zhenguang G. Cai

entry.summary: The paper proposes the rational interlocutor model, a computational account unifying speaker modeling in comprehension and audience design in production as a single rational computation. An interlocutor maintains a partner model defined by identity, fidelity, and knowledge parameters that govern expected messages, forms, and reliability of message-to-utterance mappings. The framework bridges two previously separate psycholinguistic literatures.

entry.title: KinyaMed: Seeds, Not Rows -- What a Corpus Requirement Written in the Wrong Unit Fails to Constrain

author.name: Marius Bayizere

entry.summary: This paper describes a failed attempt to build a Kinyarwanda medical triage urgency classifier, showing that a corpus requirement specified as one million generated rows was satisfiable in 130 seconds while violating four to six of nine quality gates, because the binding constraint should have been the count of distinct authored seed sentences. The authors report the specification failure and the per-language instruments that detect it rather than a working classifier. It matters because it exposes how dataset-scale requirements written in the wrong unit can create a false appearance of adequate low-resource language data.

entry.title: FA-Bench: A Benchmark for Word-Level and Phone-Level Forced-Alignment and ASR Timestamps Under Clean and Noisy Conditions

author.name: Wei Chu, Yuanzhe Dong, Ke Tan, Dong Han, Yichao Zhou, Ruchao Fan, Bingshen Mu, Jingbei Li, Vishwas Shetty, Sarthak Bisht, Ziyue Qiu, Massa Baali, Rita Singh, Bhisha Raj

entry.summary: This paper introduces FA-Bench, an open benchmarking framework for forced alignment and ASR timestamp prediction that standardizes transcript normalization, data splits, phone mapping, and boundary scoring so results across studies become directly comparable. It evaluates 21 open models and 9 commercial APIs under a unified protocol across clean audio and four degradation types, with two tracks (reference transcripts vs. recognizer outputs) and fine-grained scoring of every boundary alongside its neighboring labels.

entry.title: ExpVoyager: Direct Experience Navigation for Dynamic Agent Skill Synthesis

author.name: Kwangwook Seo, Dongha Lee

entry.summary: ExpVoyager reframes agent skill synthesis as dynamic navigation of raw experience, deferring abstraction of past trajectories until downstream demands are known, rather than compressing experience into fixed procedural knowledge upfront. This avoids discarding knowledge that later becomes critical while retaining irrelevant instance details. The idea contributes to the growing area of self-evolving LLM agents that build reusable skill libraries.

entry.title: Knowing Is Not Choosing: What Explicit Verification Adds Beyond Generative Preference

author.name: Yilong Li, Chengpo Yan, Aayan Arish, Suman Banerjee

entry.summary: Decomposes factual recall in LLMs into candidate generation, ranking, and selection, showing pre-generation readouts predict recall but not final selection. Explicit verification via P(True) improves within-question ranking over mean log-likelihood across Gemma, Qwen3, and Llama families, with AUROC gains of 0.08-0.12 and several-point accuracy improvements in a prospective Gemma cohort. This clarifies a real gap between knowing and choosing that matters for reliable QA systems.

entry.title: Calibration, Not Answer Selection: Distilling Internal Confidence in Reasoning Models

author.name: Yadong Xi, Rongsheng Zhang, Tangjie Lv, Ziyang Luo, Ruochen Zhao

entry.summary: This paper examines why reasoning models trained with binary correctness rewards verbalize systematically overconfident confidence scores, showing the issue reflects commitment willingness rather than answer likelihood. The authors use a linear probe on hidden states between the chain of thought and the answer to extract better-calibrated internal confidence, achieving 5 to 38 times lower expected calibration error than verbalized confidence across four benchmarks and two model families. They also probe the limits of this approach when the internal signal is used downstream.

entry.title: Rethinking Token Reweighting for SFT: Suppress, Reverse, and Extrapolate Learned Features

author.name: Cunchun Li, Haonan He, Yifan Gao, Minglei Li, Jingqi Ye, Qingyu Yang, Peng Ye

entry.summary: Shows through a unified policy-loss view that existing token-reweighting methods for SFT assign nonnegative coefficients, allowing suppression or amplification of supervised updates but not reversal of harmful learned features. Argues that larger weights change the optimization trajectory rather than extrapolating a fixed SFT direction, and that reversal and extrapolation require a stable reference frame. Offers a principled lens on fine-tuning dynamics and catastrophic overwriting of pretrained knowledge.

entry.title: Reset Is Not Recovery: Evaluating Recoverability from False Conversational Context via Sycophancy Hysteresis

author.name: Adi Shnaidman

entry.summary: This solo-author paper studies whether instruction-tuned models return to grounded behavior after a user repeatedly pushes a wrong answer and then withdraws that pressure, introducing a recovery-after-pressure protocol and the notion of sycophancy hysteresis. Across seven open-weight models and two factual benchmarks, ordinary conversation resets reduce but do not erase residual bias toward the user-advocated wrong answer. This matters for multi-turn assistant reliability and safety evaluation.

entry.title: CARDAMOM: A Micro-Dialectal Arabic Speech Dataset for ASR

author.name: Bashar Talafha, Samar M. Magdy, Aisha Alansari, Alaa Alkhawaldeh, Abdurrahman Juma, Sharaf Makahleh, Nour Gamal, Omar Attia, Hanaa Kurdi, Najwa Rizk, Maysa Anaya, Hessah Altimyat, Layal Alhazmi, Shumukh Alotaibi, Hajar Alhadaris, Rayan Alomari, Rahaf Almalaq, Malak Alkhorasani, Sara alghamdi, Rahaf Alshamrani, Nsrin Ashraf, Ibrahim Jaradat, Nada Qardahji, Yasmin Zaraket, Elmoukhtar Brahim, Sidi Ebeidy, Oumoulmouminin Mahmoud, Yahjeb Bouha Khatraty, Meya Haroune, Mohammad Ghaddar, Mohamad Eldirany, Rashed Alamoush, Tala Chhaytle, Nuha Albadi, Yahya El Hadj, Hamzah Luqman, Fadi A. Zaraket, Mustafa Jarrar, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed

entry.summary: Cardamom is a community-curated dataset of roughly 40 hours of transcribed YouTube speech covering 21 Arabic micro-dialects across six countries, with labels for micro-dialect, code-switching, and perceived gender. It enables fine-grained evaluation and adaptation of ASR systems beyond coarse country-level dialect labels.

entry.title: Decide, Don't Generate: Competitive Dimensional ABSA with Jev's Typed Decisions

author.name: Yiqun Zhang, Peidong Wang, Zihan Wang, Shi Feng

entry.summary: This paper challenges the trend of casting aspect-based sentiment analysis as text generation, instead decomposing dimensional ABSA tasks into typed decision queries answered by a frozen model called Jev, which produces rubric scores, label probabilities, and yes/no judgments. Using 488 coefficients fitted on CPU with no backbone tuning or generation, the system achieves the lowest aggregate valence-arousal regression error across ten corpora in six languages and outperforms fine-tuned Llama-3.3-70B and GPT-OSS-120B baselines on triplet and quadruplet extraction. The result matters because it shows competitive sentiment analysis can be achieved with far cheaper, decision-based inference rather than generative decoding.

entry.title: Scaling Long-Form Story Generation via Narrative State Tracking

author.name: Zhennan Wan, Jianfei Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces NstAgent, a training-free agentic framework that enables LLMs to maintain a structured narrative state (characters, past events, future requirements) to scale creative writing toward full-length novels, where narrative consistency typically degrades. The authors extend an existing benchmark to compare narrative consistency across lengths and evaluate stories ranging up to novel scale with a writing-quality benchmark. Existing methods typically handle stories of only about ten thousand words.

entry.title: Fusion Under Component Failure: Negative Results and Failure Modes in Ensemble AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Suraj Singh, Tushar Verma, Pragyan Singh, Shaurya Bhav, Shivam Kumar

entry.summary: This honest negative-results paper reports that a deployed stacking ensemble for AI-generated image detection failed its own controls: the shipped meta-learner did not beat its best single member out of domain, and fusion only paid off when refitted on the target domain. The authors document how controls overturned their earlier conclusions.

entry.title: PruneForget: Joint Unlearning and Pruning of Vision Models

author.name: Yu-Shan Tai, Amber Yijia Zheng, Raymond A. Yeh

entry.summary: PruneForget proposes jointly solving machine unlearning and model pruning, using the unlearn set as a guide for pruning targets since parameters encoding unlearned samples are natural deletion candidates. This avoids running unlearning and pruning sequentially and makes each aware of the other.

entry.title: Skeletons in Flow: Graph Structured Flow Matching for Human Motion Prediction

author.name: Yixuan Wang, Brandon C. Fallin, Warren E. Dixon

entry.summary: This paper introduces Graph Structured Flow Matching (GSFM), a method for human motion prediction that transports complete future skeletal trajectories through a single conditional velocity field. The approach models the trajectory as a spatiotemporal skeleton graph, using spatial attention over connected joints and temporal attention over time instants to enforce skeletal constraints and coordinated motion. This matters because it offers a principled way to generate diverse yet physically consistent future motions, relevant to robotics, animation, and human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Toward On-Chip Training of Spiking Neural Networks for Dense Event-Based Vision

author.name: Maxime Vaillant, Axel Carlier, Lai Xing Ng, Christophe Hurter, Benoit R. Cottereau

entry.summary: Introduces DELL, a block-wise local learning scheme for spiking neural networks that replaces global backpropagation-through-time with local dense supervision using spatially structured learnable heads. This targets dense event-based vision tasks on neuromorphic hardware where BPTT memory costs make on-chip training impractical.

entry.title: Oracle Gaps in Reliability Coverage: Sampling Noise or Policy Specialization?

author.name: Mert Onur Cakiroglu, Mehmet Dalkilic, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: The authors investigate why oracle policy selection over multiple training seeds appears stronger than any single policy, showing that choosing the largest estimated success rate also selects favorable sampling errors. Using reliability coverage metrics and outcome-redistribution tests on a 7B vision-language model, they quantify how much of the oracle gap is statistical noise versus genuine specialization.

entry.title: EngIntervene: Benchmarking Multimodal Engineering State Understanding and Design Intervention Reasoning

author.name: Jinchang Zhang, Yingda Tao, Jiakai Lin, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark of 3,229 questions across seven engineering domains testing whether multimodal models can reason about system states, constraints, and the consequences of design interventions, organized in four escalating levels from state grounding to intervention reasoning. It targets the gap between engineering perception tasks and full design generation. This highlights a capability frontier for MLLMs in engineering workflows.

entry.title: SciGen-Verifier: A Multimodal Reasoner for Explainable Verification in Scientific Image Generation

author.name: Jiali Chen (South China University of Technology, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Zhengteng Lin (South China University of Technology), Zuqi Wang (South China University of Technology), Shirong Lin (South China University of Technology), Xi Yu (South China University of Technology), Xusen Hei (South China University of Technology), DingBa Fu (South China University of Technology), Jiayuan Xie (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Yi Cai (South China University of Technology)

entry.summary: SciGen-Verifier targets the underexplored problem of verifying correctness of scientific image generation (circuits, geometric constructions, function plots) produced by unified multimodal models. It builds a multimodal reasoner that provides explainable, actionable feedback rather than scalar scores, aimed at educational grading scenarios where drawings must be assessed as carefully as text.

entry.title: In-Token Learning for High-Fidelity Image Restoration via Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Xingfu Yi, Xiaoxue Yu

entry.summary: Proposes In-Token Learning, a framework that adapts a pretrained diffusion transformer for image restoration using conditional rectified flow matching, fusing spatially aligned degraded-image tokens with latent tokens without a ControlNet-style branch. It evaluates super-resolution, denoising, and colorization across standard benchmarks. This offers a simpler, more parameter-efficient conditioning pathway for restoration.

entry.title: Re:Cognize -- Open-Set Comic Character Re-Identification

author.name: Aaditya Baranwal, Madhav Kataria, Yogesh S Rawat, Shruti Vyas

entry.summary: Evaluates comic character re-identification as an open-set, sequential task with four protocols on a single query stream, from closed-set retrieval to a cast the model must build and grow itself as pages arrive. It finds recognition with one reference image is nearly solved, but calibration — knowing what to believe — is where models fail. The setting mirrors how human readers identify characters without a cast list.

entry.title: Advancing Wildlife Conservation through Multimodal Animal Re-Identification with Environmental Metadata

author.name: Yuzhuo Li, Di Zhao, Tingrui Qiao, Yihao Wu, Bo Pang, Yun Sing Koh

entry.summary: The authors introduce MetaWild, a multimodal animal re-identification dataset with 20,890 camera-trap images enriched with environmental metadata such as temperature and circadian rhythms, and propose methods that use vision-language models to fuse these cues with visual identity features. This addresses the blind spot of visual-only Animal ReID benchmarks.

entry.title: CRF Loss is How Networks Should Learn Boundaries in Weakly Supervised Segmentation

author.name: Joshua Li, Yuri Boykov

entry.summary: This paper addresses weakly supervised semantic segmentation, where pixel-level predictions must be learned from image-level tags. The authors argue that prior approaches rely on post-processing steps like DenseCRF or SAM-based refinement that discard uncertainty information in class activation maps, and instead propose integrating CRF-based supervision directly as a training loss to improve boundary accuracy. The work targets a well-known weakness in WSSS pipelines: boundary quality degradation when neighboring pixels share similar colors.

entry.title: DecFlowEdit: Self-Localized Flow-based Image Editing via Guidance Decoupling

author.name: Zheyuan Zhan, Can Wang, Jiawei Chen, Chun Chen, Siwei Lyu, Zeyu Zheng, Defang Chen

entry.summary: The authors observe that FlowEdit's default classifier-free guidance configuration with asymmetric source and target scales causes background leakage, while matching scales improves localization but degrades editability. DecFlowEdit decouples the optimal guidance scales for localization and editing, extracting an edit-relevant prior from CFG-free velocity differences and using it to localize edits while preserving editability.

entry.title: E-WAVE: Event-based Continuous Optical Flow via Warping-Aligned Visual Encoding

author.name: Jiale Wu, Xiaoyang Bai, Haoming Yu, Yiwei Chen, Yifan Peng, Weiwei Xu

entry.summary: E-WAVE is a correlation-free framework for high-temporal-resolution optical flow from event camera streams, motivated by VR/AR dynamic perception. It replaces costly correlation volumes with a warping-aligned visual encoding, reducing memory and compute while maintaining dense temporal tracking.

entry.title: Can Attack Difficulty Be Characterized Before Optimization? A Study of Pre-optimization Difficulty in Person-Vanishing Attacks

author.name: Jingyao Xu, Dongdong Wang, Siyang Lu

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of pre-optimization attack difficulty for person-vanishing adversarial attacks and proposes Quad-CLEVER, a geometry-based estimator using quadratic approximation of the local attack landscape to predict which images are intrinsically harder to attack before any optimization runs.

entry.title: GLF-Q: Global-Local Feature-based Quantization for Vision Transformers

author.name: Peilin Sun, Guang Liang, Jin Tong, Jianxin Wu

entry.summary: GLF-Q is a post-training quantization framework for vision transformers that aligns penultimate-layer representations by propagating quantized block outputs through downstream full-precision layers, avoiding logit overfitting and Hessian truncation errors. This global-local feature supervision improves low-bit-width quantization accuracy without retraining.

entry.title: PanoVLN: Towards Effective Panoramic Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Zhen Wang, Changpeng Wang, Zhe Liu, Zhangyang Qi, Yuxiang Lu, Zimo Zeng, Donglian Qi, Xi Chen

entry.summary: PanoVLN explores vision-and-language navigation with panoramic observations, hypothesizing that wider visual context improves navigation decisions. The paper finds naive panorama substitution yields limited gains, diagnosing that exploiting wider visibility requires modifications to the action space and architecture, and proposes corresponding changes.

entry.title: ControlTrace: Recovering Control Fields for Hidden-Content Recognition

author.name: Zijian Liu, Yaoguang Chen, Liwei Liu, Weixi Wu, Hanming Zhang, Jiashui Wang, Na Ruan

entry.summary: The authors study how hidden content embedded in natural-looking images via spatially conditioned diffusion models can be recovered when vision-language models fail to recognize it. They contribute FreqBlind, a 6,000-image benchmark of contours, real words, and non-words across conditioning strengths, plus ControlTrace, an 8.4M-parameter U-Net that regresses the grayscale control field used during generation so a VLM can then read the hidden content. This has relevance for detecting steganographic or hidden messaging in AI-generated imagery.

entry.title: ReSight-SMC: Two-Stage Power Sampling via Island SMC with Visual Scouts

author.name: Yaowen Zhang, Xiangyu Qiu, Junyi Hu, Zhi Lu, Wenwen Tian, Aoqin Wang, Junhai Luo, Zhenming Peng

entry.summary: The authors transfer power sampling, a training-free technique for eliciting LLM reasoning, to large vision-language model decoding by defining a sequence-power target conditioned on image and prompt. They then address finite-particle pathologies with a two-stage island sequential Monte Carlo scheme that uses visual-scout particles to diversify trajectories through distinct visual cues and avoid genealogy collapse. This extends a promising inference-time reasoning method to multimodal settings.

entry.title: Towards Generalizable 3D Anomaly Detection via Relational Inconsistency Modeling

author.name: KunHo Heo, SuYeon Kim, Hayoung Lee, Chanse Oh, MyeongAh Cho

entry.summary: This paper proposes modeling defects explicitly as violations of geometric consistency among neighboring point cloud structures, instead of the usual normality-only learning. It learns category-agnostic defect cues via pseudo labels, targeting unified and cross-domain 3D anomaly detection settings. This could reduce false positives and negatives in industrial inspection.

entry.title: W2Rep: Learning Visual Representations by Watching the World Change

author.name: Wen Huang, Hang Guo, Jiarui Yang, Zheng Liu, Tao Dai, Shu-tao Xia

entry.summary: W2Rep is a masked feature-prediction framework in which an independently encoded single source image participates in prediction at the same or another moment, conditioned on visible video context, queried location, and signed time interval. The goal is to improve single-image features by watching scene change without sacrificing video representation ability. This is a clean self-supervised objective bridging image and video learning.

entry.title: ReVA: A Scene-Centric Dataset Beyond Repetition for Remote Sensing Video Question Answering

author.name: Zhen Yao, Likai Wang, Yuming Yang, Zhihao Zheng, Bo Lang, Qiuyu Tang, Jialu Sheng, Jingqi Xu, Yuehai Yang, Jumal Barker, Xiaowen Ying, Mooi Choo Chuah

entry.summary: ReVA is a new benchmark for remote sensing video question answering, comprising 2,438 drone videos from 18 cities (580K frames) and 22K high-quality question-answer pairs. It addresses limitations of existing remote sensing benchmarks, which rely on template-driven repetitive questions and static images, by targeting spatiotemporal and reasoning-oriented evaluation of multimodal LLMs on UAV footage.

entry.title: Beyond Isolated Entities: Relation-Aware Multi-Entity Modeling for Unsupervised Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zhongpeng Pan, Xina Cheng, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces INTERACT, an unsupervised video anomaly detection framework that models relations between persons and objects rather than treating entities in isolation. Its POAMI component jointly encodes appearance, motion, and spatial configuration of persons and objects so that abnormal interactions can be flagged even when each entity looks normal individually. This matters for patrol robots and surveillance, where most anomalies are relational rather than per-object.

entry.title: AquaBEV-Nav: Learned BEV Occupancy for Underwater Navigation and Exploration

author.name: Trung Tien Dong, Zhenqi Wu, Sahasra Kondapalli, Jiayi Wu, Yi Sheng, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: This paper introduces AquaBEV-Nav, an underwater robot navigation framework that predicts bird's-eye-view occupancy directly from vision instead of relying on monocular depth estimation as an intermediate step. The authors argue that underwater visual degradation from scattering and wavelength-dependent attenuation makes depth-based pipelines unreliable, and that direct learned occupancy prediction better identifies free space for safe exploration. This matters for autonomous underwater vehicles operating in visually challenging environments where existing exploration systems struggle.

entry.title: FINE: Future-Informed Navigation Encoding for Data-Efficient Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Khang H. Nguyen, Hoang Pham Quang Nguyen, Ha Phuong Nguyen, Khanh Dinh Binh, Xuan Ha Nguyen, Vien Ngo, Duy Ho Nguyen Minh, Huan Nguyen, An T. Le

entry.summary: FINE extracts latent supervision from existing vision-language navigation demonstrations by leveraging future observations, which reveal the instruction-relevant landmarks the agent will encounter. It augments a VLN backbone with auxiliary landmark tokens and complementary representations, reducing the need for costly embodied demonstrations when adapting to new environments. This improves data efficiency in a field where each new route requires human demonstration.

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Control with Constrained Potential Surgery

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhang, Panagiotis Tsiotras

entry.summary: The authors propose a fast interior-point solver for constrained general-sum dynamic games with a second-order correction that increases the probability of converging to true Generalized Nash Equilibria rather than non-Nash saddle points. The work targets scaling game-theoretic multi-agent planning beyond small numbers of agents in real-time.

entry.title: WSM-Aware HRI: An IoT-Enhanced Framework for Early Detection and Norm-Guided Repair of Failures with LLM Guidance

author.name: Hanlin Zhang, Yuquan Wang, Tianwei Zhang, Zhenglong Sun

entry.summary: A modular framework unifying human-robot interaction failures as World-State Mismatches between human instruction-implied assumptions and the robot's grounded world model, augmented via IoT sensing. An LLM makes implicit assumptions explicit, maps them to mismatch types, and specifies repairs.

entry.title: MORPH: Self-Organising Multi-Robot Task Allocation via Neuroplasticity-Inspired Adaptive Topology

author.name: Xuezhi Niu, Didem G\"urd\"ur Broo

entry.summary: MORPH is a training-free multi-robot task allocation (MRTA) framework in which global allocation quality emerges from four local plasticity-inspired rules — synaptic, homeostatic, structural, and metaplasticity — applied to a directed pairwise preference matrix updated from runtime co-occurrence and task-completion feedback. Unlike prior approaches, it needs no prior task knowledge, utility function, cost matrix, or pre-trained policy, making it more robust when task distributions shift. This addresses a real brittleness problem for deploying multi-robot teams in dynamic, unstructured environments.

entry.title: ActionGround: Training-Free Runtime Refinement of Frozen VLA Policies

author.name: Namai Chandra, Madhur Thareja, Shriram Damodaran, Addison Lin Wang

entry.summary: ActionGround is a neuro-symbolic runtime layer that wraps frozen VLA policies without retraining or weight access, using a phase-aware finite-state machine for rule-based corrections plus an inertia-weighted Euler-Lagrange dynamics term, adding under 1 ms per control step. It offers a practical recipe for improving deployed VLA policies at inference time. Its importance stems from the growing need to retrofit deployed policies cheaply.

entry.title: TLC-DiT: Task-Aligned Local Visual Conditioning for Robust Multitask Robot Manipulation

author.name: Xianbo Cai, Hideyuki Ichiwara, Zihang Wang, Yijun Lu, Tetsuya Ogata

entry.summary: TLC-DiT is a plug-in extension for Multitask Diffusion Transformer robot policies that adds explicit, task-aligned local visual feature maps without changing the diffusion objective or action generation. Frozen DINOv2 patch features are modulated by the CLIP task embedding via FiLM and refined by a lightweight CoordConv CNN adapter into spatial maps. This makes task-relevant local visual evidence inspectable and improves robustness under visual change.

entry.title: Contact-Aware Impedance Controller for Robot-Assisted Ultrasound Imaging

author.name: MD Miraj Arefin, M Efe Tiryaki

entry.summary: This paper introduces a contact perception method using B-mode ultrasound images to detect probe-tissue contact without force sensors, paired with a contact-aware impedance controller for robotic ultrasound imaging. The controller continuously estimates the effective contact location on the curved probe surface and updates the interaction frame, enabling visual servoing of the physical contact point. Experiments on an agar phantom demonstrated improved contact-conditioned force taring and reduced residual wrench bias.

entry.title: ExcavaTwin: Training-Free Geometry-Guided Semantic Elevation Mapping for Autonomous Excavation

author.name: Yu Deng, Lingshan Zeng, Tong Hu, Rushi Dai

entry.summary: This paper introduces ExcavaTwin, a training-free, vision-only mapping framework for autonomous excavation that fuses multi-view RGB geometry with semantic observations using frozen vision models. It applies geometry-constrained multi-view semantic fusion to suppress implausible predictions and projects the fused state into a task-oriented semantic elevation map. This matters because excavation autonomy has lacked robust combined geometric-semantic terrain representations in unstructured outdoor scenes.

entry.title: An Online Non-Stationary Simulation Optimization Approach Based on Regime Switching

author.name: Jianglin Xia, Haowei Wang, Songhao Wang, Szu Hui Ng

entry.summary: This paper develops a Bayesian framework for simulation optimization under non-stationary input distributions with regime-switching dynamics across sequential decisions. It uses a Markov Switching Model to approximate the objective function and provides theoretical guarantees including consistency of the approximation while accounting for both prediction and input uncertainty.

entry.title: Identification of Nonlinear and Dependent Latent Factor Structure through Clique Search

author.name: Dale S. Kim, Qing Zhou

entry.summary: The paper proposes a graph-theoretic method for latent structure learning that identifies both the number of latent factors and the nonlinear mapping support from observed-variable dependence measures, using clique search. Unlike prior work limited to linear correlations, it establishes identifiability and consistency for a general class of dependence measures under mild assumptions. This advances nonparametric latent factor modeling beyond linear-Gaussian settings.

entry.title: 9 reasons against a near-term AI slow-down

author.name: Jordan Arel

entry.summary: The author steelmans and lists reasons against a near-term coordinated AI pause, such as warning-shot dynamics, idea inoculation, and overhang effects, while remaining uncertain and acknowledging a slowdown may eventually be wise. It contributes a structured counterpoint to an increasingly one-sided governance debate.

entry.title: AI safety field *visual* impact analysis

author.name: hannarchy

entry.summary: The author built a terrain-style visualization of roughly 3,466 AI safety works extracted from arXiv and LessWrong, clustered in embedding space across 18 sub-fields with hill height driven by log-compressed citation counts, including a time slider covering 2021Q1-2026 and researcher-level filtering. It functions as a meta-science tool for seeing how the AI safety field's output and impact have evolved.

entry.title: A missing lecture in mechanistic interpretability: Feature Attribution and LRP

author.name: hubertjan

entry.summary: An educational post bridging the gap between academic interpretability and mechanistic interpretability by explaining Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP), its relationship to gradients, and how it connects to tools like attribution patching and the newer J-Lens method.

entry.title: EmailBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents on Enterprise Email and Productivity Tasks

author.name: Mukul Singh, Mansi Uniyal, Devin Devlin, Wen Xie, Big Thadawasin, Ritam Dutt, Vivian Lai, Hyeonsu B. Kang

entry.summary: EmailBench provides 206 enterprise email and productivity scenarios across 16 task categories, coupling a typed email API with a deterministic synthetic Enron-inspired corpus and a hybrid evaluation protocol of 258 executable assertions plus 211 LLM rubrics. It evaluates eight LM configurations on multi-step coordination, retrieval, and temporal reasoning. This fills a gap in benchmarks for typed email workflows in self-contained enterprise environments.

entry.title: $T^5$: Twin-Critic Training for Token-Level Thoughts in Reinforcement Mid-Training

author.name: Nan Qiao, Yebin Yang, Weinong Wang, Shuning Wang, Shangpin Peng, Fengyuan Lu, Xinming Wang, Zhehan Kan, Ruixu Zhang, Songyang Zhang, Sheng Yue, Yonglong Tian, Ju Ren

entry.summary: T5 (the proposed method, not the older model) introduces a twin-critic scheme for token-level credit assignment in reinforcement mid-training, where LLMs learn internal thoughts from unlabeled text. The authors analyze how training-inference mismatch and PPO clipping prevent a common advantage-estimate offset from cancelling, causing update drift, and calibrate token-level advantages from a single generated trajectory using two critics combined after warmup and held-out qualification. This avoids the costly repeated rollouts required by group-relative methods.

entry.title: Routing Drift Alone Does Not Diagnose Failure in Merged MoE LLMs

author.name: Yuanyi Wang, Yanggan Gu, Su Lu, Guanghao Zhu, Pengkai Wang, Yifan Yang, Congkai Xie, Zhaoyi Yan, Jianmin Wu, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: This study asks whether routing drift after merging Mixture-of-Experts LLMs actually indicates routing failure, analyzing DeepSeekMoE, OLMoE, and Qwen3-MoE (all existing models) with a routing analysis toolkit for counterfactual interventions and token-level analysis. By crossing source and merged router inputs and parameters, the authors attribute most expert reassignments to input shifts rather than parameter changes, concluding routing drift alone does not diagnose failure. The work provides a rigorous corrective to a common assumption in model-merging research.

entry.title: What Happens During Autonomous Deep Research After the User Steps Away?

author.name: Yimin Liu, Yijia Zhang, Yanmin Li, Tangwen Luo, Yuze Li, Ziling Yao, Zhi Yang

entry.summary: DRaligned is a counterfactual behavioral evaluation framework built on PDR-Bench that studies how initial user-provided information in autonomous deep research is reflected in intermediate actions and final recommendations, by varying one task-relevant user factor under fixed context. It compares acquisition requests, working drafts, and final reports using source-grounded extraction and blinded judgments. Experiments indicate strong users see divergent agent behavior, raising controllability questions.

entry.title: One Latent, Many Tokens: Jointly Learning Compressed Embeddings for Efficient Language Diffusion

author.name: Yulin Yuan, Ying Zhang, Xiangming Meng

entry.summary: Introduces JPEG-DLM, which jointly trains a compressor, a flow-matching model, and a decoder so that compressed embeddings for diffusion language models are structured and reliably decodable, unlike prior two-stage methods that fix the embedding space before diffusion training. This makes continuous diffusion LM generation cheaper with one latent covering many tokens.

entry.title: Thinking Outside the Box: Retention and Transmission of Information in Sliding-Window KV Inference

author.name: Timothy DeLise, Seth Cromelin

entry.summary: The paper experimentally investigates whether information from beyond a fixed sliding KV window persists through cached key/value states in pretrained transformers, testing five open-weight models across Qwen, Llama, Mistral, and the Muse Glimmer model (released 2026-08-10). It finds cached states computed in earlier contexts can transmit out-of-window information to later states, aiding retrieval.

entry.title: Evolving Support Priorities in Empathetic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Pengyu Huang, Zhiyuan Han, Wenwen Tong, Hewei Guo, Jiangnan Chen, Sirui Chen, Lewei Lu, Beier Zhu, Xun Yang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a mismatch in empathetic RL where support priorities evolve with dialogue state but rewards remain fixed, proposing CARE, which generates context-adaptive rubrics adjusting weights across cognitive, affective, and proactive empathy dimensions each turn. The rubric generator is trained via supervised fine-tuning and preference-based RL.

entry.title: Beyond End-to-End Black Box Mapping: An Intentional Agent Framework for Cognitive-driven Facial Reaction Generation

author.name: Hanzhong Zhang, Jindong Wang, Siyang Song

entry.summary: The paper reformulates facial reaction generation as mediated by structured internal-state processes rather than direct stimulus-response mapping, proposing an Intentional Agent that models temporal evolution of latent appraisal/affective states between speaker behavior and listener expression. This aims to produce more diverse and context-appropriate human-like reactions for HCI.

entry.title: PersonaManifold: Revealing and Exploiting Curved Geometry in LLM Persona Representations

author.name: Rui Xu, Yinghui Xu, Libo Wu

entry.summary: PersonaManifold models persona representations as points on a curved low-dimensional Riemannian submanifold in activation space, motivated by documented failures of Euclidean persona-vector methods such as non-orthogonal traits and multi-trait composition errors. This improves inference-time persona control for role-playing and personalized dialogue.

entry.title: Beyond Skill Evolution: Self-Evolving Context Management Policies for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses

author.name: Weiyuan Li, Jinghan Xu, Aili Chen, Xintao Wang, Shuang Liang, Jiaqing Liang, Deqing Yang

entry.summary: ContextEvo learns context management policies from long-horizon agent trajectories by reconstructing model-visible context at decision points, identifying context-related failures, and applying targeted updates. Built on the open-source Pi-agent harness, it matches or beats several prominent agent harnesses across three long-horizon benchmarks.

entry.title: One Readout, Many Repairs: Diffusion-Guided Hierarchical Search for Tool-Agent Repair

author.name: Xiang Xia, Cheng Yan, Fan Xu, Zhijun Fan, Shuyuan Zhang, Wuyang Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates tool-agent repair as hierarchical search over operation supports, allowing repair of failed tool calls without regenerating complete sequences. A diffusion-guided approach reuses operation selection when failures arise from realizations, preserving exploration of alternative operations and their concrete realizations.

entry.title: Beneath the Tokens: A Performance Engineering Study of Multi-Token Prediction in GPU-Accelerated LLM Inference

author.name: Suwesh Prasad Sah

entry.summary: A controlled performance-engineering study comparing two-token multi-token prediction (MTP) against standard autoregressive decoding on a single NVIDIA A10G across 360 requests spanning plain-text, reasoning, and tool-calling workloads. MTP delivered 1.91-2.19x output throughput gains and 10-14% lower time to first output, with profiling telemetry explaining the mechanisms.

entry.title: From Hand-Crafted to LLM-Based Variation Operators in Metaheuristics: A Tutorial

author.name: Camilo Chac\'on Sartori, Guillem Rodr\'iguez-Corominas, Christian Blum

entry.summary: This tutorial systematizes the emerging use of LLMs as variation operators inside metaheuristic search loops, introducing an operator-level framework with two descriptors: prompt-conditioning information type (Numeric, Symbolic, Linguistic) and artifact persistence (Transient, Amortized, Transfer). It includes a build template, method survey, and evidence review for classifying, constructing, and selecting LLM-based operators. It reframes variation in evolutionary computation as a model call.

entry.title: Autonomous Research Project Management as an Agent Skill: A Case Study in Exact Spectral Spatial Regression

author.name: Alexander Chen (University of New South Wales), Jeffrey Meng (University of New South Wales), Bram Hoex (University of New South Wales, GreenDynamics), Tong Xie (University of New South Wales, GreenDynamics)

entry.summary: This case study demonstrates an end-to-end autonomous ML research workflow executed by DeepSeek V4 Flash (an existing released model) orchestrated through an agent skill suite on consumer CPU-only hardware. Using a file-based epic and issue-tracking substrate across 74 sub-agent sessions, the agent completed an FFT-based kernel ridge regression study and recovered from failed hypotheses. It offers a concrete template for autonomous research pipelines.

entry.title: PHIRL: Aligning Learned Rewards with Task Progress for Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hang Yu, James Staley, Cheng Xi Tsou, Xiujin Liu, Wenchang Gao, Jindan Huang, Shijie Fang, Zhegong Shangguan, Angelo Cangelosi, Reuben Aronson, Elaine Short

entry.summary: PHIRL is a data-efficient inverse reinforcement learning framework that jointly leverages human demonstrations and human feedback by using task progress (cumulative completion) as a feedback modality. It iteratively infers rewards from demonstrations via IRL and aligns learned rewards with progress annotations across four dimensions, combining dense policy-level information from demonstrations with precise local critiques from feedback. This offers a practical recipe for reward learning in robotics where both demonstrations and lightweight feedback are available.

entry.title: Evaluating Single and Multi-Omics Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (MOXAI) for Molecular Subclass Classification of Adult-Type Diffuse Gliomas

author.name: Md Zahangir Alom, Quynh T. Tran, Breuer Alexandar, Brent A. Orr

entry.summary: MOXAI is a deep learning framework integrating DNA methylation and copy number variation data from methylation arrays to classify molecular subtypes of adult-type diffuse gliomas, adding within-class risk assessment analogous to tumor grading and locus-level explainability attributing decisions to specific genomic loci. This addresses gaps in existing models that analyze methylation and CNV separately and lack genomic attribution. Potential clinical value for neuro-oncology diagnostics is significant.

entry.title: Learnable Randomization as Commitment Against Adaptive Optimizers

author.name: Zihan Deng, Chuanzhi Xu, Xiaozhen Zhong, Haoyang Li, Junjie Huang

entry.summary: The paper studies unpredictable near-optimal policies (UNOP), which mix uniformly on near-best individually rational actions so that playing the single best action does not reveal a decision-maker's cutoff to adaptive counterparts like pricing systems or recommenders. The mixture functions as a commitment about the response, protecting surplus against adaptive optimizers. This frames strategic interaction with learned predictors as a mechanism design problem.

entry.title: OneSign: Unifying Sign Language Understanding Tasks with One Model

author.name: Shiwei Gan, Yafeng Yin, Xiao Liu, Desibieer Tuerdaken, Lei Xie, Sanglu Lu

entry.summary: Proposes OneSign, a unified model for isolated and continuous sign language recognition and sign language translation, addressing fragmented task-specific pipelines and the modality discrepancy between sign and text tokens that current LLM-based approaches overlook. A single checkpoint replaces multiple specialized models, enabling knowledge sharing across SLU tasks.

entry.title: SMORE: Stability-Promoting Mesh-Agnostic Model Reduction for Time-Dependent PDEs

author.name: Yangyuan Li, Weichao Li, Shaowu Pan

entry.summary: Proposes SMORE, a mesh-agnostic reduced-order modeling framework for time-dependent PDEs whose latent dynamics are trained with Lyapunov-guided stability regularization to promote stable long-horizon rollouts and avoid exploding gradients in backpropagation. Provides theoretical stability guarantees alongside empirical results for many-query tasks like uncertainty quantification and optimal control.

entry.title: What Survives the Codec Shift: Pooled No-Vocals Residuals for Speech Deepfake Detection

author.name: Jiajun Xu, Menglu Li, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies which acoustic representations remain discriminative for speech deepfake detection as synthesis shifts from vocoders to neural codecs, comparing 12 representations with a shared low-capacity classifier. It finds hierarchical XLS-R leads on pooled tests while pooled no-vocals residual statistics generalize best to unseen codecs, and proposes MN-P, a dual-view detector combining these. The analysis clarifies what evidence survives generative-mechanism shifts.

entry.title: Source Anchoring for Physical Consistency in Flow Matching Models

author.name: Giulia Romoli, Filippo Ruffini, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: SAPC is a Functional Flow Matching method that encodes physical constraints into the source noise distribution before generation, rather than correcting the flow afterward, avoiding sample drift from the target solution distribution. It is evaluated on five PDE-governed physical systems and improves physical consistency of generated samples.

entry.title: StoryEngine: A State-Grounded Agentic Framework for Video Storytelling

author.name: Yingrui Wang, Zeqing Wang, Yeying Jin

entry.summary: StoryEngine is an agentic framework for long-form video generation that maintains an explicit video world state, separating authoritative semantic plans from unreliable generated details to prevent visual drift across shots. It propagates the consequences of story events across shots, improving narrative coherence and visual consistency.

entry.title: MinkowskiPE: Minkowski Positional Encoding for Spatiotemporal Perception

author.name: Yuhao Li, Louie Hong Yao, Tianyi Shi, Hanqun Cao, Hongxia Hao, Zhen Zhao, Shengchao Liu

entry.summary: MinkowskiPE is a positional encoding scheme that uses joint temporal and spatial coordinates to parameterize Lorentz transformations applied to query and key features, adding an explicit geometric bias for spatiotemporal coupling. It aims to combine the flexibility of learned architectures with physics-motivated structure across scales from microscopic to macroscopic. This targets physical intelligence and spatiotemporal modeling.

entry.title: EntroPack: Fast and Accurate Entropy-Coded Weight Compression at Arbitrary Bitrates

author.name: Hong Zhang, Zhongjie Duan, Yingda Chen

entry.summary: EntroPack is an entropy-coded weight compressor supporting arbitrary target bitrates without activation calibration or fine-tuning, combining row-normalized E8 lattice quantization with a conditional probability model of lattice coordinates, and using sampled storage estimates for rate selection. This enables finer-grained deployment of large networks under memory budgets than fixed-width quantization. Practical compression tooling for edge and constrained inference.

entry.title: Efficient World Action Model Inference with Adaptive Intermediate States

author.name: Zhinnan Liu, Haozhi Han, Ruge Zhang, Teng Ma, Tao Ma, Zheng Liu, Yifeng Chen, Yunquan Zhang, Ting Cao, Yunxin Liu, Kun Li

entry.summary: WAMACHINE is a training-free framework that accelerates World Action Model inference by preserving and adapting prior inference state rather than reusing it as-is, since changed planning contexts and observations make retained state stale. It reduces the denoising latency of iterative diffusion or flow inference in closed-loop control. This targets a real deployment bottleneck for action models in robotics-style control.

entry.title: CoHuB: A Simulation Benchmark for Multi-Humanoid Collaboration

author.name: Hyunjin Park, Jebeom Chae, Minwoo Park, Sunghyun Park, Hanjun Yoo, Seoyeon Choi, Soochul Yoo, Joohwan Seo, Sarmad Idrees, Jae-Sang Hyun, Jongmin Lee, Roberto Horowitz, Youngwoon Lee, Jongeun Choi

entry.summary: CoHuB is a simulation benchmark for multi-humanoid collaboration under egocentric visual observations, with ten tasks spanning two- and three-humanoid cooperation patterns and synchronized demonstrations collected via multi-operator VR teleoperation. It addresses the gap left by single-humanoid skill benchmarks and enables studying learned cooperative whole-body control.

entry.title: SPIDER: Multi-Layer Semantic Token Pruning and Adaptive Sub-Layer Skipping in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Tianxiang Chen, Zhentao Tan, Zi Ye, Yue Wu, Xiaobing Tu, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang, Tao Gong, Qi Chu, Nenghai Yu, Xipeng Qiu, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: Investigates dual data- and compute-redundancy in MLLMs and proposes SPIDER, which prunes visual tokens using inter-layer semantic shifts (middle-layer tokens capture distinct focus) and skips sub-layers adaptively. It targets finer-grained layer-wise representation dynamics that prior blockwise-importance pruning misses.

entry.title: From Scores to Samples: Elastic Forcing for Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Chi Zhang, Yueyi Liu, Haoyang Shi, Ruichuan An, Haoyu Li, Yuhang Wu, Sen Cui, Miao Liu

entry.summary: The paper removes the need for bidirectional diffusion teachers and online fake-score models in few-step autoregressive video distillation, instead matching rollout distributions to reference videos via MMD in frozen self-supervised representation spaces. The 1.3B model improves VBench Total from 83.80 to 84.64 while retaining 17 FPS generation.

entry.title: Copy the Same, Distill the Difference: Initializing Linear Vision Transformers

author.name: Huaiyuan Qin, Muli Yang, Gabriel James Goenawan, Shiqi Huang, Min Kass Chong, Wahyu Wiratama, Peng Hu, Chen Gong, Wu Liu, Xi Peng, Chun Jian Ho, Hongyuan Zhu

entry.summary: Investigates whether pre-trained Softmax ViT weights can be reused to initialize linear ViTs, finding that attention transfer findings do not hold for Softmax-to-linear transfer. The proposed approach copies shared components and distills what differs, enabling linear ViTs to benefit from foundation model weights without full from-scratch pre-training.

entry.title: EEGAgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Short- and Long-Horizon EEG Analysis

author.name: Huyu Wu, Weining Weng, Yuchen Liu, Yiqiang Chen, Yang Gu

entry.summary: Introduces EEGAgentBench, a unified benchmark evaluating LLM agents on EEG analysis tasks across short- and long-horizon interpretation, testing iterative evidence accumulation, multi-step reasoning, and coordinated tool use with consistent protocols. It fills a gap left by fragmented prior EEG agentic evaluations.

entry.title: Graph Memory: Spectral Associative Memory via Dirichlet Energy

author.name: Zhaoyang Shi

entry.summary: The paper extends dense associative memories from vector-valued patterns to graph data via a spectral formulation, using a log-sum-exp energy induced by Dirichlet energy with spectral norm distances. Retrieval yields a softmax-weighted average of stored Laplacians that remains a valid graph Laplacian, with proven exponential storage capacity and exponentially decaying retrieval error. This bridges associative memory theory and graph learning.

entry.title: Beyond Gaussian Assumptions: Distribution-Aware Channel Capacity for Effective Connectivity

author.name: Jianan Jian, Jacob Kang, Nurahmed Multezem, Benjamin Li, Nan Xu

entry.summary: This work shows that brain signals and their fitted residuals frequently deviate from Gaussianity across modalities and species, which distorts effective-connectivity estimates that rely on Gaussian residual models. The authors introduce a distribution-aware information-theoretic connectivity measure based on channel capacity, estimated with a dual-flow min-max estimator built on normalizing flows.

entry.title: A Function-Level Vulnerability Score Measures Flag Rate More Than the Model: Protocol Effects on Paired Benchmarks

author.name: Maciej Cicho\'n, Bart{\l}omiej Dmitruk

entry.summary: This paper measures how much of the disagreement between published LLM vulnerability-detection scores comes from evaluation protocol rather than model capability. By varying metric, verdict extraction, and output budget on paired vulnerable/fixed-function benchmarks across seven frontier and 61 open models, it shows function-level F1 largely tracks flag rate, exposing protocol sensitivity in security benchmarking.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Operator Families for Structured Representation Learning

author.name: Zuyuan Zhang, Fei Xu Yu, Tian Lan

entry.summary: The paper proposes Geometry-Induced Operator Families (GIOF), a unified framework that converts fixed geometric structure into a family of propagation operators and dynamically selects among them based on context. This aims to bridge generic operator templates and geometry-specific constructions in structured representation learning, making operator design both principled and adaptive.

entry.title: Predicting Block-Coordinate Performance via Cross-Curvature

author.name: Shengkun Zhu, Jinshan Zeng, Zhiqiang Kou, Yongxin Tong, Yang Liu

entry.summary: The paper develops a unified theory comparing Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, and partially sequential block-gradient updates, expressing one-step loss differences through cross-block curvature with O(eta^3) remainder and deriving signed K-iteration loss comparisons. This gives principled guidance on choosing between simultaneous and sequential block updates in training, federated learning, and LoRA.

entry.title: You Only Edit Once: Incentivizing In-Context Capability of LLMs via Local Demonstration Refinement

author.name: Jiarong Wen, Qi Wang, Yun Qu, Yixiu Mao, Heming Zou, Haoang Chi, Lizhou Cai, Yiqin Lv, Kaiyu Zhang, Yuhang Jiang, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: This paper reframes in-context demonstration selection as a constrained local search problem and introduces local demonstration editing (LDE), which applies a single structured edit to an initially retrieved demonstration set instead of costly repeated LLM queries. The approach reduces combinatorial search cost while balancing selection quality and efficiency.

entry.title: Task-Aware Discretization of Differentiable Logic Gate Networks

author.name: Thore Gerlach

entry.summary: Studies how to discretize differentiable logic gate networks at inference time, showing that standard local argmax or confidence-based discretization can be task-suboptimal even for globally optimal relaxed solutions. The paper derives bounds linking task-aware gate selection to tractable interventions and explores using first-order downstream task information for progressive discretization.

entry.title: Beyond Correctness: Evaluating Semantic Knowledge in Cross-Table Transfer

author.name: Seokyong Sheem, Hochang Lee, Suyeong Lee, Daekyum Kim

entry.summary: The paper shows that common semantic ablation evaluations in tabular learning can be misleading: large performance differences under altered semantics do not imply the knowledge was predictively beneficial. It distinguishes semantic sensitivity from predictive benefit across real and controlled experiments in cross-table transfer.

entry.title: Verifying Neural Networks with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hai Duong, Thanh Le, ThanhVu Nguyen

entry.summary: RSB uses reinforcement learning to improve branch-and-bound neural network verification, training an actor-critic agent to refine greedy static branching heuristics by maximizing cumulative future verification efficiency and leveraging accumulating verification data. It targets reliability of DNNs in safety-critical systems.

entry.title: GenMem: Generative Symbolic Memory for Self-Evolving Harness

author.name: Xinke Jiang, Tao Feng, Weixuan Xu, Zhixin Zhang, Zhibang Yang, Wentao Zhang, Runchuan Zhu, Xu Chu, Junfeng Zhao, Yasha Wang

entry.summary: Proposes GenMem, a generative symbolic memory system for self-evolving LLM agents that supports retention, retrieval, reuse, and revision of experience across long-horizon tasks. It addresses sparse hierarchical memory structure, weak lifecycle supervision, and the tension between memory evolution and invariance in stored knowledge.

entry.title: Quality Determines Direction, Length Shapes Magnitude: Length Control for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zijun Weng, Zhongan Bi, Xuanang Gao, Xiaohui Hu, Shuangyong Song, Yongxiang Li, Kaidong Yu, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: Analyzes how RL inflates language model response length and proposes an asymmetric principle where quality determines the direction of reinforcement while length shaping only modulates magnitude, avoiding sign reversal of quality advantages under dense graded rewards. The method targets open-ended RL where no natural success boundary exists.

entry.title: FlexiWorld: Learning and Planning via Flexible Action Chunks Across Multiple Time Scales

author.name: Shidu Ren, Qilin Gu, Zhenghao Ni, Junhan Sun, Jiaqi Wang, Damien Scieur, Yunze Liu

entry.summary: FlexiWorld is a JEPA-based latent world model for long-horizon control that combines mixed-span goal supervision with variable-length action chunks, jointly trained with a causal action encoder and an autoregressive actor. Student Forcing reduces exposure bias during training.

entry.title: NeuronDiscover: Agent-in-Twin for Mechanistic Discovery in Neuronal Microenvironments with World Action Models

author.name: Haowei Xu, Wanyi Fu, Hongbin Han, Zhaoheng Xie

entry.summary: Introduces NeuronDiscover, an agent framework for mechanistic discovery in neuronal microenvironments that formalizes twin confounding, where a real mechanism change and a simulation error look identical in sparse observations. Its World Action Model couples prediction, intervention proposals, and observation design, revising a Mechanism-Intervention-Outcome graph from independently adjudicated outcomes. Ambitious fusion of agents, digital twins, and causal discovery for neuroscience.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Features for CUTLASS Kernel Selection

author.name: Shriram Chandran, Dominic Rinderer, Yakup Budanaz, Alexandru Calotoiu, Marcin Copik, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: The authors build a hardware-aware representation for CUTLASS GPU kernel selection, augmenting candidate configurations with statically computable estimates of induced hardware behavior, and train learning-to-rank models on a 4.9 million-kernel dataset. The approach enables execution-free selection that rivals expensive exhaustive autotuning.

entry.title: GT-VLA: Target-Conditioned Trace Guidance for Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Ninghan Zhong, Jing-Chen Peng, Sriram Vishwanath

entry.summary: Proposes GT-VLA, a framework combining VLA control with generalist VLM common sense by having an external VLM provide semantic guidance for the current skill, converted into a 2D trace that conditions action generation. The goal is to reduce VLA overfitting to training scenes and improve generalization to unseen tasks, configurations, and long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: Active Data Acquisition with Side Information via Discrete Diffusion Priors

author.name: An Vuong, Thinh Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper presents an information-theoretic framework for cost-aware active data acquisition, where a mask policy conditioned on side information chooses which image pixels to measure to maximize mutual information under a budget. A frozen discrete denoising diffusion model (D3PM) supplies the posterior for both the mask policy and downstream analysis, framing acquisition as task-agnostic rather than tied to one model. An elegant formulation bridging active sensing and discrete diffusion.

entry.title: Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation

author.name: Shuo Chang, Yueqi Wang, Zihuan Diao, Ali Montazer, Jiangguo Zhang, Joyneel Misra, Dapeng Hong, Tomer Margolin, Sourabh Bansod, Ningren Han

entry.summary: Proposes a Factorized Latent Value model for short-form video recommendation that treats behavioral signals like watch time as imperfect measurements of latent preference, correcting for confounders such as video duration. The approach aims to prevent raw engagement optimization from amplifying measurement artifacts rather than improving true user value.

entry.title: lapanda: A Matrix-Free Differentiable Solver for Nonconvex Constrained Optimization Layers

author.name: Yuankun Chen, Zifei Nie, Kangyu Lin, J\'{a}n Drgo\v{n}a, Liang Wu

entry.summary: lapanda is a matrix-free differentiable solver for nonconvex optimization with general constraints, reformulating problems as sequences of augmented Lagrangian subproblems solved with first-order inner methods. It improves modeling expressiveness and reduces computation and memory overhead in forward and backward passes compared to existing differentiable optimization layers. This enables end-to-end training pipelines with optimization layers, e.g., in control.

entry.title: Weighted Spline-Expanded Networks with Distributional Balancing for Continuous Treatment Effects

author.name: Shucheng Liu, Chan Park, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: WSENet is an end-to-end neural framework for estimating causal effects of continuous treatments that combines distance-based covariate balancing weights, a spline-expanded structured treatment embedding, and bias-corrected outcome estimation. It targets confounding and model misspecification in observational studies with high-dimensional covariates.

entry.title: A Hierarchy of Entropy-Shapley Games for Multivariate Predictive Uncertainty

author.name: Niklas Koenen, Claudia Battistin, Jeriek Van den Abeele, Martin Jullum

entry.summary: This paper proposes an attribution framework for multivariate predictive uncertainty based on a hierarchy of entropy-Shapley games. Rather than reducing outputs to scalars before attribution, it disentangles whether features drive marginal uncertainty versus dependence structure among output components, relevant for time-series forecasts and risk-aware decisions.

entry.title: GSM: Efficient Language Modeling with Shared Global State

author.name: Yunao Zheng, Bin Wen, Xiaojie Wang, Kaiyu Jiang, Xuanyu Zheng, Changyi Liu, Hongyi Fu, Jianxiong Wang, Tianke Zhang, Haonan Fan, Yingxin Li, Jiankang Chen, Xu Wang, Tingting Gao, Han Li

entry.summary: Introduces the Global State Model (GSM), a causal encoder-decoder architecture that concentrates selection and aggregation of long-range information in an encoding stage forming a shared fixed-window state, which each decoder layer accesses with queries updated from the preceding layer. This avoids repeatedly constructing historical key-value representations, reducing both access cost and repeated history-processing overhead. A novel efficiency-oriented architecture for long-context language modeling.

entry.title: Over-Personalization Is a Decision Failure: Generation-Induced Apply Bias in LLMs

author.name: Haeun Jang, Yonghyun Jun, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: This paper analyzes over-personalization in personalized LLMs, decomposing preference handling into knowing whether a preference applies, deciding on an explicit Apply/Suppress label, and generating a consistent response, measuring each stage separately. Linear probes show the applicability signal is decodable from hidden states, and making the decision explicit reveals that most failures arise during generation rather than knowledge or labeling. This reframes over-personalization as a decision failure with stage-specific fixes.

entry.title: From Weak Task Specifications to Scientific Extraction Agents: Optimizing Task Construction

author.name: Zixiao Dong, Wei Yang, Zihao Liu, Chenshu Li, Longzhang Liu, Tao Tan, Hong Xie

entry.summary: This work addresses the upstream problem of constructing task-specific schemas, extraction instructions, and evaluation rubrics from weak specifications consisting of only a short goal and unannotated documents. The framework keeps schema construction and instructions editable during optimization rather than treating them as fixed preprocessing.

entry.title: Rubric-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Personalization

author.name: Yilun Qiu, Xiaoyan Zhao, Chengbing Wang, Cilin Yan, Rui Zu, Wanyang Zhang, Xiaolong Jiang, Jiayin Cai, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: GRASP is a rubric-aware on-policy self-distillation framework for LLM personalization that uses user-specific rubrics at fine granularity, teaching the model how to generate personalized answers rather than only supervising aspect prediction or a single response-level reward. It bridges the gap between specifying what a personalized answer should contain and generating it.

entry.title: Checking Leakage Witnesses versus Certifying Bounded Non-Leakage

author.name: Chao Feng, Burkhard Stiller

entry.summary: This theory paper formalizes what is required to certify that a language model does not leak information over a declared prompt domain under an executable leakage criterion and decoding rule. It shows that while a supplied leaking execution is polynomial-time checkable, deciding leak existence is NP-complete and deterministic certification is coNP-complete, with exact stochastic certification coNP^PP-complete at fixed rational cutoffs; restrictions such as finite probability tables or bounded attention dependency windows admit tractable certification.

entry.title: PEEL-DDPM: Physics-Enabled Evidential Learning for the Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model

author.name: Ge Wang

entry.summary: PEEL-DDPM adds evidential uncertainty quantification to diffusion models by freezing a measurement-conditioned DDPM and training an evidential network on its reverse-trajectory residuals, learning only the identifiable Student-t coordinates. Repeated scanner-noise and diffusion realizations provide a nested Monte Carlo estimate of aleatoric variance, addressing non-identifiability in normal-inverse-gamma regression.

entry.title: Scalable In-Domain Self-Supervised Foundation Model for Dense Representation Transfer in High-Resolution Plant Imaging

author.name: Junlin Guo, Sharmin Majumder, Isaac Lyngaas, John Lagergren, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: The authors pretrain a masked autoencoder with a ViT backbone on over 10 million multi-view plant image tiles, producing a domain-specific foundation model for high-resolution plant imaging. The representations are benchmarked across dense prediction and global recognition tasks, addressing costly pixel-level annotations in agricultural science.

entry.title: RefCompose: Multi-Reference Image Generation via LoRA-Conditioned Diffusion

author.name: Sai Sri Teja Kuppa, Parth Shinde, Priyadharsan Balaji S, Jinka Harshavardhan, Sriprabha Ramanarayanan

entry.summary: RefCompose is a pixel-space compositional conditioning framework for diffusion models that composes multiple references (actors, locations, props) into a coherent shot using a single fixed-resolution reference canvas, keeping conditioning size constant regardless of reference count. It decouples spatial layout from subject appearance via LoRA conditioning, addressing memory scaling and identity preservation.

entry.title: ReLoc: Rethinking Scene Coordinate Regression Architecture for Robust Outdoor LiDAR-based Localization

author.name: Heejoon Moon, Yurim Cho, Je Hyeong Hong

entry.summary: Revamps scene coordinate regression for outdoor LiDAR localization, replacing scene-classification-based global embeddings that fail to discriminate nearby locations and fixing uniform feature sampling that propagates features from dynamic objects and unstable regions. The result is map-free, robust localization without explicit 3D maps. Relevant to autonomous navigation and SLAM systems.

entry.title: TC-ADA: One-Shot Active Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Weihao Yan, Yeqiang Qian, Yueyuan Li, Tao Li, Chunxiang Wang, Ming Yang

entry.summary: TC-ADA studies a practical one-shot image-level active domain adaptation setting for driving-scene semantic segmentation, selecting and densely annotating a fixed target subset in a single round before uninterrupted adaptation. It uses vision-foundation-model representations in stage 1 for complete-image acquisition and a target-calibrated adaptation stage.

entry.title: Fill2SR: Repurposing Inpainting Diffusion Transformers for Real-World Super-Resolution

author.name: Xingfu Yi, Xiaoxue Yu

entry.summary: Fill2SR repurposes a masked-inpainting diffusion transformer for real-world super-resolution by writing the low-quality observation into the native masked-image slot under a full-image mask, avoiding extra ControlNet-style branches and using LoRA-only tuning. A companion offline pipeline (RCDT) distills degradation descriptors from unpaired real images. It reduces memory and compute versus spatial-conditioning approaches.

entry.title: VastMAT: A Large-Scale Multi-Category Benchmark for Multi-Animal Tracking

author.name: Zhizhen Li, Zan Wang, Huidong Peng, Bohan Tan, Shimin Shan, Yu Liu, Liang Peng

entry.summary: VastMAT is a large-scale multi-animal tracking benchmark with 2,947 videos, over one million annotated frames across 27.85 hours, covering 337 animal categories with 3.66 million bounding boxes and extensive within-video instance associations. It fills a gap left by pedestrian- and vehicle-focused MOT benchmarks.

entry.title: ECHO: Event-Augmented Context with Hindsight and Outlook for Wrist-Only Manipulation

author.name: Xinyue Wang, Yicheng Jiang, Zesen Gan, Junhao He, Jiaxu Wang, Junhao Li, Jingtao Zhang, Tianlun He, Jianan Wang, Isabel Guan, Qiming Shao

entry.summary: ECHO is a wrist-only latent world action model that fuses event camera signals with RGB for robotic manipulation, encoding wrist-mounted event data into compact motion representations providing temporal and spatial context. It addresses placement limits of fixed cameras and the loss of static scene content in wrist-mounted views using hindsight and outlook mechanisms. Event cameras offer high dynamic range that mitigates RGB degradation under extreme exposure.

entry.title: Lagrangian--Hamiltonian Flows for Video Prediction and Image Generation: A Symplectic Perspective

author.name: Jiawei Hu

entry.summary: LHFM is a geometric framework for image dynamics grounded in symplectic geometry and geometric quantization, representing images as exact Lagrangian graphs evolving via image-dependent Hamiltonian flows. LHFM-V achieves the lowest reported FLOP count among comparable recurrent video prediction models, and LHFM-I shows compatibility with flow matching for image generation.

entry.title: Inertia-Corrected Newton Method For Generalized Nash Equilibria in Dynamic Games with Optimality Verification

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhang, Panagiotis Tsiotras

entry.summary: The paper proposes an efficient numerical method to verify second-order sufficient conditions for local Generalized Nash Equilibria by connecting the inertia of the agent KKT matrix with positive definiteness of the reduced Hessian. An inertia-corrected update step helps Newton solvers avoid converging to non-Nash saddle points, supporting reliable multi-agent MPC.

entry.title: Repair Before You Fuse: Frozen-Host Adaptation for Corrupted-but-Present Sensors

author.name: Gia-Huy Thai, Quang-Thinh Ly, Anh-Minh Phan, Tuan Dang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Boundary Feature Repair (BFR), a frozen-host adaptation framework that learns task-supervised residual corrections at the modality interfaces of camera-LiDAR detectors when sensors are present but unreliable. Variants repair camera features, align LiDAR candidates, or compose both, with zero-initialized per-channel scales guaranteeing an exact identity before optimization so only repair modules train. It addresses robustness to degraded sensing without retraining the host detector.

entry.title: AI Harness: Certification under Proposal-Conditioned Information for Foundation-Model Agents

author.name: Hailin Zhong, Shengxin Zhu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes foundation-model agents as emitting semantic proposals that are both action candidates and history-conditioned observations, showing that collapsing this structure into a state-only model can preserve proposal coverage while destroying certifiability of safe interventions. It characterizes when the collapse is lossless via viability-kernel analysis in finite robust interfaces.

entry.title: PINNMorph: Evolving Online Adaptation Policies for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Xu Yang, Mingyang Yu, Jun Zhang, Keqian Li, Jing Xu

entry.summary: Proposes PINNMorph, an online adaptation framework for physics-informed neural networks that uses LLM-guided policy evolution over a population of state-conditioned adaptation policies mapping execution diagnostics to interventions on network topology, representation, and training. This addresses the fact that PINN training behavior changes substantially during optimization while architectures are usually fixed beforehand.
