It formulates adaptation as alternating optimization with theoretical justification and a practical adjoint-based algorithm.

entry.title: Temporal Heterogeneous Graph Pretraining for Relational Deep Learning

author.name: Yixin Peng, Er Jin, Diego Collarana, Stefan Decker

entry.summary: The paper studies temporal signals in relational deep learning over database-derived heterogeneous graphs, distinguishing record age (relative to prediction cutoff) from inter-record intervals. It proposes Multi-scale Time Encoding and Rotary Time Encoding to explicitly capture both signals during pretraining, evaluating effects on downstream tasks.

entry.title: Overfitting of Spectral Gradient Descent: How Matrix Geometry shapes Generalization and Implicit Bias

author.name: Guillaume Braun, Ichiro Hashimoto, Masaaki Imaizumi

entry.summary: The paper analyzes generalization of spectral gradient descent in overparameterized matrix classification with corrupted labels, contrasting collapsed shortcuts that share a singular direction with dispersed shortcuts in distinct directions. Changing only this geometry can reverse which optimizer generalizes better: collapsed shortcuts favor SpecGD while dispersed shortcuts favor GD, with exact orthogonality eliminating signal from late-stage SpecGD directions. A nuanced theory result on how data geometry mediates implicit bias.

entry.title: LieDiscover: Adaptive Symbolic Library Construction for Explicit Open-form Symmetry Discovery

author.name: Xinxin Li, Jianming Ma, Xingyu Cui, Da Li, Juan Zhang, Junping Yin

entry.summary: LieDiscover frames data-driven Lie symmetry discovery as joint optimization over the function library and generator coefficients, using an encoder-decoder architecture to dynamically generate symbolic expressions. This overcomes the fixed-library limitation of explicit methods, capturing symmetries involving high-order polynomials or transcendental functions. It advances automated scientific discovery of governing symmetries.

entry.title: Handwritten Text Recognition Lives in the High-Pixel Variance Subspace

author.name: Carlos Garrido-Munoz, Jorge Calvo-Zaragoza

entry.summary: The paper explains why pixel-reconstruction self-supervised methods beat contrastive methods for handwritten text recognition, arguing discriminative signal in HTR lies in high-variance pixel directions unlike natural images. It tests six SSL methods from three families under matched protocols across six handwriting benchmarks in five languages, with pixel-grounded SSL achieving the lowest CER everywhere.

entry.title: C-HAT-Bench: Benchmarking Chinese AI-Text Detection Beyond Fully Generated Text

author.name: Qing Yang, Zixiang Luo, Zhenyu Mao, Zezheng Wu, Xinghe Cheng, Haibo Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Jiapu Wang, Jingwei Zhang

entry.summary: C-HAT-Bench is a Chinese human-AI collaboration benchmark spanning production settings, domains, and generators, motivated by the fact that most detectors are evaluated only on fully human versus fully AI text, which can overstate reliability when human-AI collaboration weakens or redistributes generation cues. It is the first controlled resource of this kind for Chinese, where detection cues are shaped by tokenization and language-specific distributions. It fills a genuine gap in detection evaluation outside English.

entry.title: Reading Is Not Leaking: Local, Auditable Measurement and Reduction of Inference Exposure from Public Footprints

author.name: Mahmudul Faisal Al Ameen

entry.summary: The paper presents a framework for measuring and reducing inference exposure from public data footprints, running on the owner's CPU with no LLM at analysis time, instantiated for both organizations and individuals. Its key measurement insight is that scoring an inference system against private truth conflates reading ability with leakage, and on a 128-question instrument over sixteen synthetic firms, almost half the questions were never answered correctly by any of six readers, with majority-class guesses accounting for most of each reader's score. The framework therefore separates genuine inference exposure from baseline guessability.

entry.title: RoboSTAR: Next-Scale Autoregressive Sign Language Translation for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Yujia Zeng, Chensheng Peng, Yuxin Chen, Alex Shao, Nathan Jew, Masayoshi Tomizuka

entry.summary: RoBoSTAR is a text-conditioned sign language production framework generating human-centric sign motions that can be retargeted to robotic execution, motivated by scalable accessibility interfaces. It combines part-wise Finite Scalar Quantization with next-scale autoregression to model long-range and local dependencies at multiple temporal granularities.

entry.title: Levy-Driven Correspondence Estimation for Registration

author.name: Qianliang Wu, Jiaqi Yang, Wankou Yang, Le Hui, Jin Xie, Jian Yang, Yaqing Ding

entry.summary: LevyMatch refines point-cloud correspondences under low overlap or non-rigid deformation using Levy-driven random jumps over a soft matching matrix, with a Brownian reference bridge giving explicit update formulas and a Gamma random clock setting step sizes. A front-loaded Gamma policy concentrates costly network evaluations early.

entry.title: Anatomy-Structured Hierarchical MIL for Weakly-Supervised Thoracic Disease Detection in Chest X-rays

author.name: Jeongin Kim, Sohyun Ahn, Seo Young Kang, Jaeyi Sung, Soomin Kim, Sungho Cho, Rena Lee, Kwanchang Kim, Junhyug Noh

entry.summary: ASH-MIL is a weakly-supervised chest X-ray disease detection framework with parallel anatomy-structured observation branches (cardiac, pulmonary, agnostic) and hierarchical multiple instance learning aggregation, injecting anatomical priors as soft spatial biases into decoder cross-attention. This enables anatomically grouped instance discovery and finer localization of small abnormalities than coarse region proxies.

entry.title: One Sensor, Whole Body - 3D Body Pose from a Single Consumer Earbud IMU

author.name: Zhilin Guo, Boqiao Zhang, Oszk\'ar Urb\'an, Josef Bengtson, Hakan Aktas, Wenzhao Li, Siyu Hong, Kyle Fogarty, Chenliang Zhou, Ali Senguel, Cengiz Oztireli

entry.summary: This paper quantifies how much 3D body pose can be recovered from the single head IMU in consumer earbuds, using a multimodal capture pipeline with four-view RGB-D video, an AirPods head IMU, and two insole IMUs, with pseudo-ground-truth from SAM 3D Body across a 35-take single-subject benchmark. Adapting recurrent pose models, a head IMU alone achieves 79.0 mm rigid-MPJPE for lower-body pose. The study also assesses whether adding consumer sensors actually helps, with implications for ubiquitous wearable motion capture.

entry.title: Reduce, Then Encode: Multiscale Volumetric Reduction for 2D Foundation Models in Brain MRI

author.name: Dexuan Ding, Yuankai Qi, Bogong Wang, Luping Zhou, Amin Beheshti

entry.summary: The paper proposes Multiscale Volumetric Reduction, which compresses each anatomical view from D MRI slices into M much smaller complementary 2D components (uncentered-PCA base plus multiscale residual details) before encoding with pretrained 2D foundation models. This reduce-then-encode strategy bridges the 2D-encoder/3D-volume mismatch in brain structural MRI. It offers a practical alternative to costly 3D pretraining for medical volumes.

entry.title: EpiTransfer: Sparse, Training-Free Long-Range Depth Estimation from Temporal Monocular Aerial Frames

author.name: Diksha Aggarwal, Rutvik Dagadkhair, Sanjana Srivastava, Bradley Denby, Kevin Kochersberger

entry.summary: EpiTransfer is a geometrically derived, training-free depth estimation method that uses epipolar transfer with two monocular images and camera pose estimates, synthesizing a virtual stereo pair with a freely chosen baseline from camera motion. This transforms temporal correspondence into stereo triangulation while mitigating degeneracies of direct two-view triangulation. Validated across outdoor drone flights, it addresses the poor out-of-distribution generalization of learned depth models at novel viewpoints and altitudes.

entry.title: Fiber-Normalized Manipulability and Determinant Proxies: Intrinsic Redundancy Optimization Across and Within Task Fibers

author.name: Antonio Franchi, Mirko Mizzoni

entry.summary: This theoretical work establishes that determinant-based manipulability is an exact objective for fixed-task redundancy optimization, showing that determinant proxies and metric-completed manipulability induce the same orderings, critical points, and optimality classifications on task fibers. It introduces fiber-normalized manipulability to enable meaningful comparisons and trajectory optimization across different task fibers.

entry.title: Terrain-Aware Autonomous Planetary Exploration for Exteroceptive-Proprioceptive Mapping with Quadruped Scouts

author.name: Alberto Sanchez-Delgado, Jo\~ao Carlos Virgolino Soares, Victor Barasuol, Claudio Semini

entry.summary: This paper presents a terrain-aware autonomous exploration framework for quadruped robots in lunar-like environments, combining RGB-D-based elevation mapping and geometric traversability with proprioceptive interaction-aware terrain cues. Fused local maps feed navigation costs for autonomous risk- and energy-aware planning. It leverages the DLS Lab (Claudio Semini, IIT) lineage in quadruped planetary exploration.

entry.title: CP-Agent: A Harness-Engineered Agent for Crystal Plasticity Simulation Workflows

author.name: Samuel Onimpa Alfred, Abhishek Kumar, Veera Sundararaghavan

entry.summary: CP-Agent is an LLM agent built with a harness that autonomously executes complete crystal plasticity simulation workflows from natural-language tasks, using a ReAct loop to select and sequence tools while delegating numerical optimization to established solvers. It targets a real bottleneck in materials science where configuring heterogeneous simulation tools is labor-intensive. The work demonstrates how domain-specific agent harnesses can automate scientific engineering pipelines.

entry.title: READ-Bench: Benchmarking Historical Instance Retrieval for Time-Series Diagnosis

author.name: Gerardo Pastrana, Haojun Li, Dhruv Mehta, Anoushka Vyas, Sina Khoshfetrat Pakazad, Henrik Ohlsson, John Paparrizos

entry.summary: READ-Bench is a benchmark for retrieving relevant historical cases in multivariate time-series diagnosis across 12 datasets, defining relevance by shared fault or event type rather than surface signal similarity. It systematically evaluates classical distances, symbolic methods, self-supervised and foundation-model embedders, fusion, and label-aware and language-model rerankers.

entry.title: RAO-Nav: Probing Omni-Language Models for Zero-shot Semantic Audio-Visual Navigation

author.name: Qilang Ye, Meng Liu, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: RAO-Nav is a deployment pipeline applying omni-language models zero-shot to semantic audio-visual navigation, letting an embodied agent hear, see, reason, and act without task-specific training. A test-time Latent Navigation Reasoning module elicits the models' built-in reasoning during decoding.

entry.title: Enabling Timely Guidance before Skill Retrieval: Retaining Helpful Warm Tips in Agent Context

author.name: Feng Liang, Yupeng Li, Runhao Zeng, Francis C. M. Lau, Xiping Hu

entry.summary: TipsWarm complements on-demand skill retrieval for LLM agents by maintaining a budgeted pool of skill-derived keypoints, or warm tips, injected into context every turn so guidance arrives before the agent commits to a bad approach. It separates event-triggered LLM assessment from lightweight tip selection to reduce maintenance overhead compared to general memory methods. This addresses the gap where metadata-only skill mechanisms deliver guidance too late.

entry.title: Interpretable Physics Informed WiFi Indoor Localization: Learning an Effective Access Point Geometry and Using It to Prune

author.name: Arshia Eftekhari zadeh, Rezvan Nasiri, Hadi Moradi

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical deep learning framework for WiFi fingerprint-based indoor localization that jointly predicts user location and learns an effective geometry of access points from RSSI data without knowing true AP coordinates, then uses the learned geometry to rank and prune APs. Achieves 7.07 m mean 3D error on UJIIndoorLoc, a 26-36 percent reduction versus baselines, with improved interpretability.

entry.title: Adaptive Consistency Graph for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Jiecong Wang, Hao Peng, Zhanyi Wang

entry.summary: The Adaptive Consistency Graph (ACG) helps LLM agents stay on track over long-horizon tasks by incrementally storing execution evidence and provenance in a persistent graph, then constructing a temporary, requirement-centered view under a bounded context budget for each decision. ACG augments rather than replaces the agent's planner and tool executor, mitigating drift from the original objective across dependent actions and tool calls. It targets a well-documented failure mode of agent systems.

entry.title: FinancialAuditBench: Benchmark Construction under Differential Privacy Using Real-World Priors

author.name: Jerry Huang, Sarvesh Babu, Matt Van Buren, Alexander Wang, Pranav Pillai, Arush Jain, James P. Burton, Julia Hockenmaier

entry.summary: FinancialAuditBench is a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on financial statement audit tasks, built with a framework that generates synthetic engagements from differentially private aggregate statistics of historical audits plus authoring priors. This sidesteps the privacy constraints that limit most financial benchmarks to public or simplified data while keeping tasks grounded in real-world distributions. It aims to delineate where financial agents can be reliably deployed versus where professional oversight remains necessary.

entry.title: Planner-as-Router: Joint Plan-Time Model Routing for Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Workflows

author.name: Vivek Kumar Singh, Preeti Priyam, Gautam Bhowmick

entry.summary: Planner-as-Router folds model-tier selection into the planning step of multi-agent LLM workflows, assigning small, mid, or frontier tiers to subtasks while dependency structure is visible, rather than routing per call downstream. This exploits plan-time information that cascade-style per-call routers lack. The motivation is reducing cost, since frontier models can cost 25x more per token than small ones.

entry.title: Large Language Models Substantially Compress Well-Being Inequality but Largely Preserve Its Socioeconomic Structure

author.name: Nattavudh Powdthavee

entry.summary: Using 93,901 World Values Survey respondents across 66 countries, the author has six LLMs predict life satisfaction from demographic and attitudinal profiles, finding that models substantially understate dispersion of life satisfaction yet, after scale normalization, largely reproduce the socioeconomic structure of the inequality. This nuances concerns that LLM-generated synthetic populations are unusable due to compression. It matters for social-science applications of synthetic data.

entry.title: Multi-Dimensional Comparative Scale Construction for Efficient Personalized Subjective Judgment in High-Traffic Applications

author.name: Xianglong Shi, Shifeng Liu, Sirui Zhao, Shengming Yuan, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a pairwise comparative framework for building multi-dimensional scales of subjective intensity that capture both fine-grained intensity and individual variation across users. It optimizes offline scale construction via sparse Elo comparisons with multi-judge voting (reducing cost from O(N^2) to O(NK)) and optimizes online inference for high-traffic deployment.

entry.title: Naturalness-guided Manifold Flow Matching for Sign Language Production

author.name: Jiayi He, Shengeng Tang, Sisi You, Yanbin Hao, Lechao Cheng, Richang Hong

entry.summary: SignNMFlow addresses sign language production by constructing flow matching paths on the rotational manifold of human joints instead of linear interpolation in Euclidean space, guided by a naturalness signal. This respects the geometry of valid joint rotations and better preserves the motion distribution. It is a solid methodological improvement for generating realistic sign motions from text.

entry.title: CoViST: Visual Token Compression via Composable States

author.name: Qi Zhang, Xiandong Meng, Ronggang Wang, Siwei Ma

entry.summary: CoViST is a training-free framework for visual token compression in vision-language models that represents a compressed image as a composable visual state, explicitly encoding how much visual information each compressed token carries and its original spatial context. This addresses the opacity of prior compression methods, especially when compression repeats across decoder layers. The training-free design makes it easy to adopt for inference cost reduction.

entry.title: EverMine: Dissecting the Self-Evolution of Research Capabilities in Long-Horizon Alpha Research

author.name: Siyuan Li, Jiangfeng Zhang, Rui Yao, Weihua Qiu, Mingyang Xu, Zixuan Yuan

entry.summary: EverMine is an empirical framework for studying whether self-evolving agents' accumulated skills, tools, and rules continue to improve later research, using long-horizon alpha (quantitative factor) discovery as a state-dependent testbed where portfolio changes alter the value of past experience. It decomposes research state into history, current factor portfolio, and reusable capabilities, and compares ablated runs under matched resource limits. This brings controlled evaluation to self-evolving research agents.

entry.title: OSCC: Certified Observation-Safe Coupling Optimization for Gradient-Noise Control in Imperfect-Information Learning

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Rui Chen, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces OSCC, a framework for counterfactual coupling in imperfect-information environments that defines an admissible class of couplings via marginal preservation so hidden state is not leaked, and optimizes return-covariance contrast after projection through policy-gradient geometry rather than raw variance reduction. It aims to make common-random-number constructions a general learning primitive.

entry.title: SpecRead: A Benchmark for Measuring Whether Language Models Understand Hardware Specifications

author.name: Feilian Huang (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: Presents SpecRead v2.1, a benchmark isolating specification comprehension from code generation: 385 questions over 10 OpenTitan IP blocks covering retrieval, cross-section reasoning, contradiction detection in mutated specs, and spec-RTL consistency checking, with distractor and consistent-RTL controls built from real RTL mutations.

entry.title: Laya as a Typed Probabilistic Assessor: An Independent Reproduction and a Preregistered Study of Calibration and Selective Escalation

author.name: Gowthamkumar Nandakishore

entry.summary: An independent, preregistered reproduction of the Laya 421M-parameter typed-decision assessor finds it is uniformly under-confident, contradicting the model card's stated over-confidence risk. A single temperature fit (T=0.469) reduces held-out ECE from 0.204 to 0.037 and outperforms the shipped calibration table.

entry.title: GenoMorph: Pathway-Grounded Genomic Disease Reasoning via Adaptive Latent Computation

author.name: Tanmoy Kanti Halder, Akash Ghosh, Arijit Roy, Sriparna Saha

entry.summary: GenoMorph shifts genomic disease prediction from memorized gene-disease associations toward pathway-grounded reasoning, coupling a frozen DNA foundation model with question-conditioned cross-attention, self-adaptive latent reasoning, a residual reasoning gate, and rejection capabilities. It targets robustness when molecular identifiers are unavailable.

entry.title: Behavior-Grounded Semantic Enrichment for Financial Fraud Modeling and Reasoning

author.name: Linbo Shao, Huilin He, Yating Lou, Dawei Cheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multi-agent semantic enrichment framework that generates interpretable financial semantics grounded in original transaction behavior, addressing the scarcity of rich, realistic semantics in public fraud datasets due to privacy constraints. It enables multimodal fraud modeling and contextual reasoning with consistency refinement.

entry.title: PersMem: Internalizing Personality into Dual-Pathway Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: Hanzhong Zhang, Ziwei Xiang, Weicheng Xie, Shizhe Liu, Siyang Song

entry.summary: PersMem integrates predefined agent personality into the memory-processing pipeline of role-playing LLM agents, mapping personality to operation-specific parameters controlling memory prioritization and retrieval across a four-step dual-pathway process. This makes memory handling consistent with persona and enables validating whether agent behaviors follow the defined personality.

entry.title: Escaping Local Views: Discovering Latent Concepts for Interpretable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yijie Sun, Sanquan Sun, Yanda Zhu, Yuanyang Zhu, Yaohua Hu, Chunlin Chen

entry.summary: The ELV framework introduces semantically structured latent concepts into multi-agent RL under partial observability, where each agent extracts low-dimensional concepts from local observations and trajectories, jointly encoded via a VAE into a contextual latent variable. This renders policy decisions transparent and supports more efficient cooperation.

entry.title: Remember Before You're Asked: MemDream for Self-Probing Memory Evolution

author.name: Mingfei Lu, Mengjia Wu, Runsong Jia, Zhe Luo, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: MemDream enables LLM agent memory systems to proactively self-test rather than only repair memory after retrieval failures. It periodically runs offline dream cycles where Dreamer, Analyst, and Consolidator agents probe, diagnose, and repair a memory graph, with a policy trained via group-relative reinforcement learning.

entry.title: SpeechCritic: Learning a Diagnostic Speech Judge from Limited Human Preferences

author.name: Mingyue Huo, Shivam Mehta, Bhavin Jawade, Yinghong Lan, Haoqi Li

entry.summary: SpeechCritic learns a diagnostic speech quality judge that decides which of two candidates is better, along which perceptual dimensions they differ, and which audible cues support the decision. It works in a reference-conditioned cross-lingual setting from only about 300 human-annotated examples, addressing unreliability of prompting frontier audio models.

entry.title: SeLMRoute: Probabilistic Semantic Evidence for Large Language Model Routing

author.name: Vasilis Perifanis, Nikolaos Pavlidis, Symeon Symeonidis

entry.summary: Proposes SeLMRoute, an LLM router that first extracts interpretable, candidate-independent semantic evidence about a query (e.g., reasoning needs, external knowledge use) and then learns candidate performance and deployment objectives on top of those judgments. This contrasts with routers that learn directly from embeddings or preference clusters.

entry.title: Can We Trust the Teacher? Decoupled Credit Direction-Magnitude for Self-Distillation

author.name: Yugu Li, Zehong Cao, Peizhen Li, Yang Zhang, Siyi Hu, Jianglin Qiao

entry.summary: Proposes DCSD, which decouples credit direction from contribution magnitude in self-distillation for RL with verifiable rewards, calibrating privileged teacher supervision with belief-margin signals. Theoretical analysis shows coupling makes step-level credit vulnerable to teacher judgment errors and preference variance.

entry.title: Proactive Dialogue Policy Optimization via Cognitive-State Transition

author.name: Minghui Ma, Mengqi Chen, Bin Guo, Jingqi Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Cog-Sim, a user simulator that explicitly models the evolution of user cognition across turns, paired with a policy-optimization method for proactive dialogue that goes beyond high-level strategy labels. This improves consistency and state dependence of simulated feedback in multi-turn policy learning. It matters for training dialogue agents that adapt to user feedback while pursuing task goals.

entry.title: From Migration to Calibration: Preserving Agent Capabilities across Models, Jurisdictions, and Scale

author.name: Yaxiao Liu (PwC China AI Center), Pengbo Liu (PwC China AI Center), Yiwen Liu (PwC China AI Center), Yihua Guan (PwC China AI Center), Jiaxing Song (Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: A framework paper from PwC China AI Center and Tsinghua that reframes agent redeployment (model swaps, jurisdiction changes, scaling) as constrained behavioral calibration across three layers: information preservation, harness adaptation, and user acceptance. It defines a non-degradation objective on prespecified capability measures rather than treating deployment changes as simple migration.

entry.title: IMC-CLINIC: Coupled Loss-Informed Newton Iterations for Clipping in Analog In-Memory Computing

author.name: Yung-Chin Chen, Chia-Yu Chen, Naveen Verma

entry.summary: IMC-CLINIC addresses ADC quantization error in analog in-memory computing for LLM inference by deriving clipping factors that jointly balance activation rounding, weight rounding, and ADC quantization via loss-informed Newton iterations. This matters because analog IMC is a promising path to energy-efficient LLM inference, but its output-side ADC error is distinct from digital quantization and existing clipping methods are ill-suited to it.

entry.title: FinAutoRubric: Expert-Guided Automatic Rubric Generation for Evaluating Financial Research Agents

author.name: Hoyoung Lee, Suyeol Yun, Jack Haverty, Yunju Cho, Meesong Kim, Daekyung Park, Sumin Kim, Jihoon Kwon, Jasmine Jia Geng, Andrew Chin, Yin Luo, Edward Tong, Yu Yu, Zach Golkhou, Minkyu Kim, Igor Halperin, Young Cha, Alejandro Lopez-Lira, Chanyeol Choi, Yongjae Lee

entry.summary: FinAutoRubric is a framework where finance experts specify reusable evaluation guidance while agent pipelines and enforced code generate, review, and validate query-specific rubrics for evaluating financial research agents. A writer agent researches each expected value with a fixed information cutoff and a reviewer agent verifies it, escalating failures to humans. It addresses the cost and inflexibility of fixed, expert-written rubrics in finance benchmarks.

entry.title: When Does Domain Adaptation Help on Physical Vibration Sensors? A Held-Out-Bearing Study of Neural-Operator and Convolutional Models

author.name: Kumbha Nagaswetha, Rabi Pathak

entry.summary: This study revisits bearing-fault diagnosis benchmarks, showing that commonly reported 99-plus percent accuracies reflect leakage from having the same physical bearing in train and test sets. Under a held-out-bearing protocol, source-only transfer drops to 0.36 against a 0.97 supervised ceiling under shaft-speed change. The paper then analyzes what governs transfer, including computed order tracking and model class choices.

entry.title: From Phase Transition to Systemic Failure: A Decoupled Analytics Framework for GNN Robustness

author.name: Shuai Yan, Dan Peng, Jie Li, Ke Wang

entry.summary: The paper builds a synthetic homophilic graph regression benchmark that manipulates label noise and feature distribution shift independently, running 41 configurations and 410 runs across representative GNNs. It finds qualitatively distinct failure patterns: graceful degradation under additive label corruption versus abrupt phase-transition-like systemic failure under distribution shift. This decoupled framework clarifies GNN robustness mechanisms.

entry.title: Query-aligned video frame selection for long video understanding

author.name: Md. Safayet Islam, Dilip Sarkar, Liang Liang

entry.summary: This paper tackles a core bottleneck in multimodal large language models for video understanding: models typically sample only 8-64 frames uniformly, often missing frames relevant to the question. The authors propose a training-free, model-agnostic method for selecting question-relevant frames from long videos. Better frame selection could improve long-video QA accuracy without retraining or modifying the underlying model.

entry.title: MM-VeriRec: Failure-Guided Fusion for Verifiable Agentic Multimodal Recommendation

author.name: Yufeng Wang

entry.summary: MM-VeriRec introduces a verifiable multimodal recommendation protocol that handles hidden visual constraints, image-text mismatch, and impossible-task abstention, building tasks from real movie-poster and product-image datasets. Recommendations are verified with deterministic visual attributes and failures converted into actionable labels. This targets reliability in agentic multimodal recommenders.

entry.title: Timed Rule-Based Supervision of an End-to-End Autonomous Parking Policy

author.name: Kejia Gao, Liguo Zhou, Lei Yu, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Parametric Safety Shield (PSS), a hand-calibrated timed rule-based runtime supervisor applied to the control outputs of a vision-based Transformer end-to-end parking policy in CARLA. Extensive closed-loop evaluation (384 attempts per configuration across held-out slots and initial poses) shows the shield corrects failure modes such as boundary exits, delayed braking, and stalled control, raising target success from roughly 85% for the retrained policy. It matters because it demonstrates that simple runtime supervision can fix systematic failures of learned policies without retraining.

entry.title: Overview of the TREC 2025 Million Large Language Models track

author.name: Evangelos Kanoulas, Panagiotis Eustratiadis, Jamie Callan, Mark Sanderson, Yongkang Li, Jingfen Qiao, Gabrielle Poerwawinata, Vaishali Pal

entry.summary: This overview describes the TREC 2025 Million Large Language Models track, which envisions ecosystems of millions of specialized LLMs and proposes a retrieval-based paradigm where an assistant agent infers expertise dynamically from interactions rather than static metadata. It frames expert model selection as central to future agentic ecosystems. The track motivates and standardizes evaluation for routing and expert discovery at scale.

entry.title: Amnesia by Design, Memory By Necessity: Persistent State for Document Intelligence

author.name: Souhail Bakkali, Ayoub Merimi

entry.summary: This survey identifies the statelessness bottleneck in Document AI: current systems process contracts, tables, and amendments as one-off stateless functions, so schema, contradictions, and learned experience are never carried forward. It argues this problem goes beyond scaling parameters, extending context, or adding retrieval, since storage and retrieval alone do not consolidate observations into reusable knowledge. The paper formalizes persistent, evidence-grounded document state as a unifying framework for future systems.

entry.title: ReFM: Semantic-Aware Refinement Flow Model for Motion Retargeting

author.name: Jingxiang Qu, Lucie Taglienti, Evan Atherton

entry.summary: ReFM addresses motion retargeting across characters with different skeletons, tackling two gaps: learning source-motion semantics without high-quality paired retargeting data, and formulating retargeting when no reliable paired motion can serve as a regression target. Instead of constraining predictions toward copied motions that entangle articulation cues with skeletal mismatch artifacts, it uses a semantic-aware refinement flow formulation. This advances character animation quality without paired supervision.

entry.title: Spectral Reversal: Counteracting Singular Value Bias for Graph Prompting

author.name: Hanxu Yang, Yuhuan Zhao, Xiaodong He, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: The paper identifies spectral bias in pre-trained GNNs: pre-training optimization disproportionately aligns representations with high singular-value directions, leaving low-energy directions under-exploited for downstream tasks. It proposes counteracting this bias for graph prompting so that parameter-efficient adaptation of frozen GNN encoders can exploit complementary information in low-energy spectral directions. This improves graph prompting without fine-tuning.

entry.title: Active Feature Acquisition With Incomplete Training Data

author.name: Reza Rezvan, Valter Sch\"utz, Han Wu, Linus Aronsson, Morteza Haghir Chehreghani

entry.summary: This paper studies active feature acquisition when training data itself is incomplete, a realistic violation of assumptions in prior AFA work. It shows that under MCAR missingness one-step acquisition values are unchanged while multi-step values can decrease, and analyzes the consequences and remedies. It matters for cost-sensitive prediction in medical and other domains where both features and training labels are missing.

entry.title: Progressive-View On-Policy Distillation for Regional-to-Global Transfer in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Shanfeng Huang, Zhou Fang, Song Xiao, Hai Du

entry.summary: PVD is a distillation method for multimodal LLMs that transfers a teacher's crop-conditioned advantage to student full-image inference by progressively shifting the student's view distribution through aspect-preserving padded crops, with regional-advantage weighting that reallocates token-level supervision based on the teacher-student log-probability gap. It addresses the view-mismatch problem in regional-to-global distillation for image understanding.

entry.title: Explaining Textual Entailment with Lexical Entailments: Using LLMs to Supply Lexical Relations for Formal Proofs

author.name: Jorryt de Jong, Stefan Moraca, Ettore Cesari, Lasha Abzianidze

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether LLMs can identify the lexical knowledge needed to solve natural language inference problems and how much that knowledge contributes to proof search in a logic-based NLI system. It focuses on structured lexical entailments, bridging LLM implicit knowledge with transparent formal reasoning. This probes a key interpretability question: how much lexical knowledge LLMs actually deploy correctly during reasoning.

entry.title: Feature Space Guidance for Breast Cancer Classification in DCE-MRI

author.name: Benjamin Hamm, Yannick Kirchhoff, Maximilian Rokuss, Moritz Langenberg, Constantin Ulrich, Tassilo Wald, Jeremias Traub, Karol Gotkowski, Klaus Maier-Hein

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for breast cancer classification in DCE-MRI that dynamically analyzes latent representations to adapt to protocol-specific acquisition characteristics, mitigating background uptake confounds and soft-tissue misalignment, and exploiting cross-phase latent relationships. This targets the well-known challenge of heterogeneous 4D MRI inputs, small lesions, and site-to-site protocol variation. Clinical deployment robustness is the central concern.

entry.title: Gradient-Guided Decoupled Adaptation for Geospatial Vision-Language Models

author.name: Dongdong Wang, Deepak Balakrishnan, Ravi Srinivasan, Shenhao Wang

entry.summary: G2DA is a gradient-aware multi-task adaptation framework for geospatial vision-language models that partitions tasks into vision- and language-centric groups based on observed gradient heterogeneity, then applies decoupled optimization to reduce task interference. It is motivated by empirical observations of cross-modal gradient differences and intra-branch relationships. The work targets better multi-task performance in Geo-VLMs.

entry.title: TwinS-GCN: Spectral conjugate for Spectral Graph Convolutional Networks

author.name: Chun Hei Michael Chan, Flavia Petruso, Dimitri Van De Ville

entry.summary: TwinS-GCN addresses the tension between oversmoothing in deep graph convolutions and the need for long-range information transport by building filters on the skew-symmetric part of the shift operator, which supports directed, non-attenuating information flow. It introduces a spectral conjugate construction to maintain shift-invariance. This is a theoretical contribution to spectral graph neural network design.

entry.title: Query, Align, and Distill: Navigation-Aware Cross-Modal Interaction for Efficient Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Zhihao Chen, Yiyuan Ge, Ziyang Wang, Pu Cao, Lu Yang

entry.summary: Builds an efficient VLN pipeline in two steps: a teacher model with learnable query slots extracts action-sufficient navigable evidence from panoramic observations and grounds it to instructions, then a compact student is distilled through the explicit query bottleneck. This targets deployment cost of large-scale VLN models while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: SCISSOR: Score-Conditioned Instrument Source Separation for Orchestral Recordings

author.name: Yiheng Lu, Hao-Wen Dong

entry.summary: SCISSOR performs score-conditioned source separation of orchestral recordings by using the musical score to form frame-wise queries per instrument, matched against a shared audio representation with a softmax over instrument and background slots. Queries retain instrument identity even with missing score notes, and the model is trained on SynthSOD plus a small real set. It improves on classic score-informed masking approaches.

entry.title: DataMagic: Authoring Data Videos through Declarative Multi-Agent Orchestration

author.name: Yupeng Xie, Zhenyang Wang, Liangwei Wang, Jiayi Zhu, Zhouan Shen, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: DataMagic is a multi-agent framework for generating data videos that combine dynamic charts, narration, and animations directly from raw data, using a declarative representation of temporal relationships across modalities. It addresses the gap between static visualization tools and end-to-end pixel-level video generation that cannot guarantee data accuracy.

entry.title: Transformer-based Neural Beamforming for Real-Time Speech Enhancement on Smart Low-Power Hearable Devices

author.name: Luca Bompani, Marco Fariselli, Giovanni Oltrecolli, Francesco Conti

entry.summary: This work presents an optimized real-time neural MVDR beamformer for low-power microcontrollers in hearable devices, using six microphones and a three-stage mixed-precision pipeline (float32 MVDR, int8 CNN for weight estimation, float16 Transformer for per-frame correction). It enables accurate spatial speech enhancement under strict latency and resource constraints. It demonstrates edge deployment of transformer-based speech processing.

entry.title: ThinkNet: Compact Architecture Selection and Validation-Gated Ensembles for Subject-Independent MI-EEG Decoding

author.name: Abdul Basit, Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: ThinkNet is a validation-controlled framework for subject-independent MI-EEG decoding that combines train-only normalization, validation-guided evolutionary architecture search, and validation-gated inference to find compact decoders for held-out subjects. It highlights that held-out-subject performance is often overstated when test-subject information leaks into preprocessing or model selection. The evaluation protocol on BCI Competition IV-2a with nine LOSO folds and multiple seeds is notably rigorous.

entry.title: A packet-level digital hardware twin for commissioning megahertz diagnostic edge AI and plasma control system integration in tokamaks

author.name: Semin Joung, Abhilasha Dave, Luca Scomparin, Filipp Khabanov, Zheng Yan, Benedikt Geiger, George McKee, Ryan N. Coffee, David R. Smith

entry.summary: This paper develops a packet-level digital hardware twin for megahertz diagnostic edge-AI architectures in tokamaks, simulating a 64-channel, 1 MHz beam emission spectroscopy diagnostic with full networking, FPGA parsing, packet loss, jitter, and edge inference. It enables commissioning the complete path from diagnostic sampling to control-system handoff without live hardware. It is a substantial systems contribution for real-time ML in fusion science.

entry.title: STITCH-RAG: Spatio-Temporal Influence Tracing over Topic Hypergraphs for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Haodong Yang, Mengzhu Chen, Jia Cai

entry.summary: STITCH-RAG is a hypergraph-based RAG framework that encodes multi-entity co-participation via topic-summary hyperedges, links per-chunk entity states through canonical-name equivalence, and applies spatio-temporal influence bridging to preserve evidence chains across documents for multi-hop retrieval. It targets the gap where chunk-based RAG breaks cross-passage evidence while preserving faithful generation context. A structured approach to improving multi-hop retrieval quality.

entry.title: ReGDiff: Guided Diffusion in Regulated Latent Space for Exploring Metamaterial Voxel Geometry

author.name: Wangzhi Zhan, Jianpeng Chen, Dongqi Fu, Dawei Zhou

entry.summary: ReGDiff couples voxel representation with latent-space regulation and guided diffusion to navigate the plausibility-novelty trade-off in metamaterial geometry generation, producing diverse structures (truss, shell, porous) within a unified cubic discretization while avoiding degenerate geometries. Relevant to AI-driven materials design where exploring novel yet physically plausible structures is the core challenge.

entry.title: Before Agents Act: Assurance-Aware Semantic Scheduling for Evidence Acquisition in Distributed Systems

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: This paper formulates evidence acquisition for tool-using agents as joint witness selection and scheduling under quorum, diversity, freshness, deadline, and resource constraints, with formal guarantees on dispatch-time freshness and finite diagnostic expansion. Its AAS system combines integer-program selection, dispatch-aware scheduling, and receipt-aware repair, producing 1,075/1,200 valid candidates versus 647/1,200 for a baseline. It targets safe, assured agent actions on infrastructure.

entry.title: MASCIT: A Mask-Aware State Space Classifier for Naturally Irregular Time Series

author.name: Yoo-Min Jung, Hyeon-Gi Kim, Jonghun Park

entry.summary: MASCIT is a mask-aware state space classifier for naturally irregular time series with asynchronous observations, missing values, and nonuniform sampling, feeding observation masks to the encoder and excluding invalid steps from gated temporal aggregation. Across 34 datasets it achieved the strongest aggregate results and was the only model with complete three-seed results everywhere. It supports selective state space models for irregular data.

entry.title: SentZero: An Enhanced Sentence-Centric Vision-Language Pretraining for Multi-Task Zero-Shot Chest X-Ray Analysis

author.name: Hangyul Yoon, Hyungyung Lee, Edward Choi, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: SentZero improves sentence-level vision-language pretraining for chest X-ray zero-shot analysis by addressing radiology-discourse characteristics: limited positive-pair diversity and false negatives from clinically equivalent sentences recurring across patients. It targets multi-task zero-shot performance without task-specific fine-tuning. This is a meaningful advance in medical VL pretraining data curation.

entry.title: WeaveData: A Multimodal Data Analysis System with Self-Critiquing and Self-Evolving LLM Plans

author.name: Min Jia, Shihao Zhou, Jun-Peng Zhu, Peng Cai, Kai Xu, Chao Zhang, Li Li, Aoying Zhou, Heng Long, Qiu Cui, Liu Tang, Qi Liu

entry.summary: WeaveData is a system for multimodal data analysis over tables, text, and images that generates typed logical plans via LLMs, critiques them step by step before execution, and checks results against the original question, with plans that self-evolve from feedback. It tackles the error-proneness of LLM-generated analysis plans with a full systems approach.

entry.title: JevVibe: Efficient Classification-Guided Secure Code Generation

author.name: Arshak Rezvani, Sasha Behrouzi, Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi

entry.summary: Evaluates Jev, a decision model that directly selects a CWE weakness label from a declared candidate set and returns probabilities, against six open-weight autoregressive models and the frontier proprietary GPT-5.6-Sol on a controlled 50-way CWE classification task, for use in diagnose-then-repair secure code generation pipelines. It examines output validity, speed, cost, and accuracy trade-offs.

entry.title: TempoKV: Timely Staging of LLM KV Caches for Memory-Semantic Flash

author.name: Jay H. Park, Hyungjun Kim, Dong Kim

entry.summary: Presents TempoKV, a timing-aware resource-commitment layer for LLM serving that stages reusable prefix KV caches in a memory-semantic flash hierarchy. It records cache hits as metadata-only claims and requests commitment when the estimated time until retrieval matches the storage-estimated time to make the KV resident and eviction-protected, avoiding SSD-latency exposure and wasted fast-tier capacity.

entry.title: WavePP: High-Throughput Pipeline Parallel LLM Prefill under Prefix Reuse

author.name: Aaryam Sharma

entry.summary: WavePP is a prefill runtime on TensorRT-LLM that overlaps request admission with pipeline execution and asynchronously finds prefixes reusable across all pipeline stages, addressing cache-state independence between stages. It targets throughput in pipeline-parallel LLM serving with prefix reuse.

entry.title: GLAD: Global-Local Adaptive Detector for Robust Speech Deepfake Detection

author.name: Zelin Zhao, Guanjie Huang, Danny Hin Kwok Tsang, Li Liu

entry.summary: The paper empirically identifies two architectural vulnerabilities in SSL-based speech deepfake detectors: failure to capture localized spoofing artifacts and inflexibility to domain shifts in SSL layer importance. GLAD introduces a global-local adaptive design addressing both, improving generalization to unseen domains.

entry.title: DR-net-Mamba: Selective State-Space Modeling for Long-Range ECG Time-Series Denoising

author.name: Basile Morel, Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Andreas P. Streich, Julia E. Vogt, Thomas Hofmann

entry.summary: Proposes a Mamba-augmented ECG denoiser that inserts selective state-space blocks into a convolutional bottleneck, combining local feature extraction with linear-complexity long-range temporal modeling. The design targets non-stationary noise in ambulatory and long-duration recordings where CNN receptive fields, transformer scaling, and diffusion costs are limiting.

entry.title: Enhancing generalization in endwall film cooling prediction: Incorporating the superposition principle into transformer-based neural operators

author.name: Qineng Wang, Liming Song, Tianyuan Liu, Zhendong Guo

entry.summary: Proposes SDNO, a physics-enhanced neural operator that uses the film cooling superposition principle to decompose turbine endwall temperature prediction into two stages: a Transformer-based Calculate Net for sub-parts with varying film hole counts, followed by a second operator for full-field reconstruction. This improves generalization of cooling layout prediction to unseen hole configurations, relevant to gas turbine thermal design.

entry.title: Understanding the Subspace Stabilization of the Hessian and Gradient Covariance Matrix

author.name: Fangshuo Liao, Anastasios Kyrillidis

entry.summary: Introduces a new instability metric for detecting Hessian top-subspace stabilization independently of parameter-change magnitude, refining explanations of this phenomenon in late-phase training. Also shows the gradient covariance matrix exhibits similar top-subspace behavior, analyzed via between-class and within-class decomposition.

entry.title: Rethinking Cross-Channel Importance in Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yong-Hoon Choi, Kwang-Hyun Park, Youngjin Cho

entry.summary: This paper disentangles three notions of cross-channel importance in multivariate time-series forecasting: statistical relatedness, predictive usefulness, and actual usage by a trained forecaster. It shows these need not coincide, demonstrates that horizon-adaptive source selection improves a controlled Ridge predictor in most conditions, but finds that imposing the same logic on iTransformer yields little gain and poor alignment between selected and used channels. The work raises questions about whether channel-mixing architectures use cross-channel information as intended.

entry.title: HyperLabel: Multi-Label Classification via Hypergraph-Based Label Correlation Modeling

author.name: Peiyu Zhang (University of Southern California), Heng Ping (University of Southern California), Nikos Kanakaris (Amazon Web Services), Yucheng Zhao (University of Tennessee, Knoxville), Shixuan Li (University of Southern California), Wei Yang (University of Southern California), Xiongye Xiao (University of Tennessee, Knoxville), Paul Bogdan (University of Southern California)

entry.summary: HyperLabel explicitly models label dependencies in multi-label classification using a label hypergraph whose sample-defined hyperedges encode multi-way co-occurrence patterns. An encoder-decoder hypergraph neural network uses this structural prior instead of implicit contrastive or pairwise attention learning. This offers explicit structural guidance for capturing high-order label correlations.

entry.title: When the Merge Coefficient Stops Mattering: Proximity Regularized Merging for Continual LoRA Adaptation

author.name: Yixuan Liu, Yuhao Sun, Sen Song, Jin Li

entry.summary: The paper casts rehearsal-free continual learning with adapters as sequential task-vector write-ins and proposes Proximity Regularized Merging (PRM), a proximal penalty added during task-vector training without changing the merge rule. PRM improves accuracy across multiple write-in rules, backbones, and class-incremental settings, with the fixed-coefficient variant competitive with tuned baselines. This simplifies continual LoRA adaptation by making merge coefficients less critical.

entry.title: Fast and Precise Learned Charged-Particle Trajectory Regression at the Large Hadron Collider

author.name: Jonathan Renusch, Benjamin Huth, Daniel Murnane, Eleni Xochelli, Do\u{g}a Elitez, Paul Gessinger-Befurt, Andreas Stefl, Jeremy Couthures, Andreas Salzburger, Lukas Heinrich, Michael Kagan, Markus Elsing

entry.summary: The authors treat charged-particle trajectory parameter regression on LHC detector data as a sequence-modeling task, using a bidirectional learned model to replace or complement classical Kalman-filter and linearized least-squares fits. The work targets matching the classical one-part-in-10^5 precision while improving speed, with contributors from CERN/ATLAS-affiliated institutions.

entry.title: Prioritizing Repeated LLM Evaluation for Hidden Failure Discovery

author.name: Keita Broadwater, Akin Broadwater

entry.summary: The paper formulates LLM reliability evaluation as a budget-constrained discovery problem where each prompt has an unknown per-generation failure probability, since shallow sampling can miss rare but operationally important failures. It proposes a framework that performs shallow evaluation first, then uses trial-level failure outcomes to prioritize prompts for deeper repeated sampling.

entry.title: Predicting the Financial Impact of Supply Chain Risk for Major AI-Related Semiconductor Firms: A Heterogeneous Graph Patch Transformer Approach

author.name: Jianna Hur, Sagar Samtani

entry.summary: The authors build a heterogeneous graph patch transformer that forecasts how supply chain stress propagates into the reported financials of AI-chip semiconductor firms one and two quarters ahead. The model learns from a 15,186-company network over 60 quarters, fusing quarterly fundamentals with macro-trade, event, and disaster signals.

entry.title: Optimal Nonparametric Dynamic Pricing with Censored Demand and Adversarial Inventory

author.name: Mengxiao Zhang, Yingfei Wang, Haipeng Luo

entry.summary: The paper studies online dynamic pricing with censored demand where inventory is adversarially revealed and demand is an unknown, price-dependent distribution. It extends prior sqrt(T)-regret results beyond restrictive linear-demand assumptions to a general nonparametric setting requiring only that expected sales are nonincreasing in price. This is a meaningful advance in the theory of learning-to-price under censoring.

entry.title: DevelopmentODE: Structured Neural ODEs for Early Brain Development Dynamics Across a Decade

author.name: Kaiqiao Han, Haitao Chen, Bryan Quah, Xiaoda Wang, Janelle Liu, John H Gilmore, Wei Gao, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: DevelopmentODE is a structured continuous-time framework that models individual brain development trajectories from sparse, irregularly spaced longitudinal observations, separating population progression, individual variability, and developmental age within a shared structure. Applied to early brain development across a decade of pediatric data, it improves long-term neurodevelopmental forecasting. This has clinical relevance for tracking child development.

entry.title: Deep Learning Techniques for Phoneme Recognition in Italian Children' s Speech

author.name: Nicola Barbaro, Cristina Gena, Francesco Petriglia, Andrea Meirone, Alessandro Mazzei, Arianna Viotti

entry.summary: The paper introduces Broca, a Conformer-based system for transcribing Italian children's speech into IPA to assist speech therapists in diagnosing impairments. Pretrained on about 8 days of adult speech and fine-tuned on only 165 minutes of child speech from standardized diagnostic tests, it achieves a state-of-the-art weighted Phoneme Error Rate of 13.36% on Italian speech.

entry.title: MultiEcho: An Experimental Science of Learned Worlds

author.name: Meng Zhu, Airui Zhang

entry.summary: MultiEcho proposes treating world models as experimental systems, estimating their response laws via controlled counterfactual interventions across nine simulated physical systems and seven frozen model configurations. It distinguishes response predictability, intervention readability, and physical correspondence, finding that locally describable responses can still poorly match physical effects.

entry.title: SchemaMem: Schema-Indexed Recurrent Memory for Delayed State Retrieval

author.name: Sungwoo Goo, Hwi-yeol Yun, Sangkeun Jung

entry.summary: SchemaMem is an attention-based recurrent memory architecture combining chunk-local attention with a persistent schema-indexed phase state, where learned schema embeddings provide shared references for reads and writes, and chunk-boundary commits aggregate bounded phase increments. It targets preserving selected information for delayed retrieval in bounded-state recurrent models.

entry.title: FuseAlign: Forced Alignment in the Wild

author.name: Mithilesh Vaidya, Stephen Bailey, Sumukh Badam, Matthew Bendel, Xingzhe He

entry.summary: This paper argues that existing forced-alignment evaluations understate real difficulty by using short, clean speech and perfect transcripts, and introduces improved metrics, a scoring protocol for error-prone ASR output, and AlignBench covering diverse speakers, acoustics, and text conditions. The work targets word-level alignment used in media editing, subtitling, and speech-data curation.

entry.title: JET: Justification Evaluation in Transformer

author.name: Shenghao Ding

entry.summary: Describes JET, a training-free method that uses pretrained language and vision-language models to select among finite candidate answers by directly evaluating candidate likelihoods with computation shared across candidates. Reported results include Qwen3.6-35B-A3B reaching 87.48% accuracy on the full MMLU test set on consumer hardware, with measured speedups from prefix reuse and input preparation optimizations.

entry.title: Structure-Adaptive Tree Field Integrators

author.name: Millend Roy, Soham Samal, Ivan Zelich, Krzysztof Marcin Choromanski

entry.summary: STAD-TFIs are near-linear algorithms for integrating tensor fields on trees with distance-dependent kernels, exploiting path backbones and single-vertex separators with 2D fast Fourier transforms to compute interactions jointly. The paper provides detailed theoretical analysis plus empirical evaluations showing efficiency gains over existing tree field integrators.

entry.title: The Composition Gap in Dataset Distillation

author.name: Guang Li, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama

entry.summary: This paper identifies and analyzes a composition gap in dataset distillation: the union of separately distilled datasets can fail to match training on the union of real data, even when every source is distilled exactly and the total budget permits an exact joint distillate. It derives exact composition error for quadratic objectives in two-to-one step compression, attributing the gap to nonlinear transformation of source statistics by trajectory compression.

entry.title: Harmonizing Spectral Evolution in Conditional Flow Matching for TTS

author.name: Isha Pandey Varad Deshpande Abhijat Bharadwaj Ganesh Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: The paper identifies incoherent frequency evolution during inference in conditional flow matching TTS models and proposes a training-free fix: a Discrete Wavelet Transform-based strategy that dynamically modulates mel-spectrogram sub-bands during ODE integration. It penalizes aggressive low-frequency growth while boosting lagging high-frequency details, validated across multiple architectures including Matcha-TTS.

entry.title: Retracing Hodgkin and Huxley: State Recovery Does Not Certify Mechanism

author.name: Peiyu Zang, Jiayi Hao, Yongqiang Cai

entry.summary: Using the Hodgkin-Huxley neuron model as a testbed, this paper trains structured latent models while withholding gate identities and shows that good state recovery and prediction do not certify recovery of the underlying physical mechanism. It examines response prediction, state recovery, protocol transfer, and agreement with HH dynamics, finding that recovery depends on which observations the latent chart uses.

entry.title: Deep Weighted Bellman Residual Minimization for $Q^*$ Estimation

author.name: Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Cheng Yuan, Chen Zhong

entry.summary: Introduces a weighted Bellman residual minimization framework for off-policy evaluation in offline RL, using density ratio weighting to integrate expert demonstrations with behavioral data. It relaxes the conventional completeness assumption and establishes sharp convergence rates for density ratio estimation.

entry.title: Universal Dynamic Portfolios

author.name: Yu-Jie Zhang, Yu-Xiang Wang, Peng Zhao, Kevin Jamieson

entry.summary: Generalizes Cover's universal portfolio to compete with arbitrary comparator sequences via dynamic regret minimization for log loss, proving that exp-concavity's classical fast-rate advantage disappears in the dynamic setting and that sqrt(T*P_T) linear-loss-type dependence is unavoidable. It proposes a method achieving the best achievable regret.

entry.title: Structured Neural SDEs for Functional Calibration

author.name: Francesco Piatti, Andrea Iannucci, Thomas Cass

entry.summary: Introduces SLiSDE, a family of Neural SDEs built from structured linear stochastic layers that enable parallel-in-time simulation, with expressivity recovered via gated in-flow stacking. For functional calibration tasks where rare paths dominate the loss, it adds an optional Girsanov tilt acting as learned importance sampling. This addresses costly simulation and unstable gradients in generic neural drift/diffusion networks.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion Modeling for Stochastic Discount Factor Portfolios

author.name: Kelvin J. L. Koa, Xinyang Li, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: RADAR is a retrieval-augmented diffusion framework for portfolio optimization under the stochastic discount factor framework, learning market state representations that capture regime-dependent risk structure. It conditions diffusion modeling on retrieved historical analogs to handle non-stationarity and state-dependent financial uncertainty that isotropic Gaussian noise assumptions miss.

entry.title: Subgroup Rank-1 Lattice for Practical High-dimensional Black-box Integral Approximation

author.name: Yueming Lyu

entry.summary: The paper introduces subgroup rank-1 lattice rules whose Korobov generator with fixed-order scalar enables fast structured feature maps, reducing the O(nd) cost of standard quasi-Monte Carlo point sets for black-box high-dimensional integral approximation. Applications span expectations, kernel mean embeddings, and softmax kernels in self-attention.

entry.title: Latency and accuracy tradeoffs in Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Zhanglu Yan, Zixuan Zhu, Kaiwen Tang, Yuyang Cai, Qianhui Liu, Weng-Fai Wong

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that multi-timestep spiking neural networks are inherently slower than quantized neural networks by overlapping computation across adjacent layers at the timestep level. The tradeoff is that spikes fired on incomplete inputs cannot be withdrawn, so aggressive overlap degrades accuracy. Relevant for low-power edge deployment of speech command recognition.

entry.title: Structured Latent Modeling for Supervised Multimodal Information Decomposition

author.name: Wanting Huang, Sanvesh Srivastava, Weiran Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a multimodal prediction framework that factorizes learned representations into shared, modality-specific, and task-irrelevant components using contrastive or masked objectives, invertible normalizing flows, and a supervised low-rank latent variable model. The approach gives a principled way to isolate target-relative information contributions across modalities.

entry.title: From Experience to Expertise: Adoption-Aware Memory Learning for Data-Scarce NPU Kernel Synthesis

author.name: Longxiao Fan, Tao Zhang, Han Yan, Jiajun Li, Mingcong Song, Guoping Long, Hongjie Si, Weiwei Sun

entry.summary: This paper addresses the transfer gap when LLM coding agents move from CUDA to data-scarce domain-specific architectures like NPUs, proposing an adoption-aware memory-learning scheme that fixes biased credit assignment between adopted and unused experiences. The system improves kernel synthesis quality without costly expert-data post-training.

entry.title: Neural Harmonic Measure Operator

author.name: Jinjin He, Sinan Wang, Yuchen Sun, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes NHMO, a transformer-based neural solver for elliptic PDEs on variable-shape domains that parameterizes the harmonic measure boundary density, supervised by Walk-on-Spheres exit samples. Because the harmonic measure depends only on geometry, one trained kernel handles arbitrary boundary values without retraining, with an extension to Poisson problems via classical decomposition.

entry.title: Suitable Measures for the Potential Operational Utility of AI NWP Rainfall Forecasts Over Africa

author.name: Shruti Nath, Docko Sow, Koomi Toussaint Amoussouvi, Fenwick Cooper, Josiah Kiarie Kimani, John Bagiliko, Florian Pappenberger, Rendani Mbuvha

entry.summary: Presents a calibrated comparison of AI weather models (GraphCast, GenCast, and the Functional Generative Network) against the physical IFS NWP model for African rainfall prediction, using Isotonic Distributional Regression postprocessing and CRPS evaluation against IMERG, RFEv2, and CHIRPS. The work emphasizes operational utility measures relevant to regions lacking infrastructure for physical models.

entry.title: A Unified Optimism-Agnostic Framework for Linear Bandits over Spherical Action Sets

author.name: Arda G\"u\c{c}l\"u, Subhonmesh Bose, John R. Birge

entry.summary: This paper develops a unified framework for linear bandits that treats UCB and Thompson sampling together, showing that if exploration-driven inference quality, encoded in the minimum eigenvalue of the design matrix, grows at least on the order of sqrt(t), the analysis can be made optimism-agnostic. The work connects estimation quality of the unknown reward parameter to regret guarantees over spherical action sets.

entry.title: Federated Subspace Guided Vision-Language-Action Policy Distillation for Non-IID Multi-Robot Manipulation

author.name: Biprodip Pal, Kaushik Roy, Yanming Zhu, Brendan Tidd, Alan Wee-Chung Liew, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: FedDRMan is a federated learning framework letting multiple robots jointly improve manipulation policies without centralized demonstration access, tackling non-IID task distributions that make naive parameter aggregation destructive. It combines a frozen server teacher for local behavior cloning with low-rank multimodal subspace and action-distribution distillation, plus heterogeneity-aware grouping for aggregation. Addresses a real deployment challenge in multi-robot learning.

entry.title: Learning What to Evaluate: Correlation-Aware Decoupling for Multiobjective Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Ashwin Renganathan, Peter Bachman

entry.summary: The paper proposes a correlation-aware decoupling method for multiobjective Bayesian optimization that exploits inherent correlations between objectives and constraints to evaluate only a subset at each round, rather than maintaining independent GPs with fully coupled evaluations. This aims to reduce evaluation cost while preserving sample efficiency of Bayesian decision-theoretic acquisition.

entry.title: Affine Geometry of Gaussian ReLU Networks via Conditional Kac-Rice Formulas

author.name: Recep \"Ozkan, Christian Hirsch

entry.summary: The paper studies how the affine geometry of finite ReLU networks — activation switches and scalar kinks — is created at initialization and reorganized during training, deriving exact finite-width conditional Kac-Rice formulas for expected activation switch counts. For fixed depth with proportionally growing widths, switch intensities converge to explicit deterministic limits.

entry.title: Plan-to-Synthesis: Cross-City Human Mobility Generation via Semantic Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Zhoufu Wang, Baoshen Guo, Zhiqing Hong, Junyi Li, Kailai Sun, Heye Huang, Alok Prakash, Shenhao Wang, Jinhua Zhao

entry.summary: SeMoFlow generates human mobility trajectories (POI visitation sequences) that generalize across cities by encoding heterogeneous POIs into a shared cross-city representation space and using latent flow matching rather than per-city diffusion or costly LLM-based generation. It targets travel behavior modeling, transportation management, and urban planning at practical cost.

entry.title: USAI-Quant: A Quantitative Reasoning Benchmark for Vision-Language Models in Built Environments

author.name: Dongdong Wang, Qingqi Song, Yuzhou Chen, Deepak Balakrishnan, Ravi Shankar Srinivasan, Shenhao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces USAI-Quant, the first benchmark for quantitative reasoning of VLMs on built-environment metrics from high-resolution remote sensing imagery, curated from the 335 largest U.S. cities. It fills a gap left by qualitative VQA benchmarks, showing that current state-of-the-art VLMs struggle with quantitative urban spatial analysis.

entry.title: Machine learning for the LHC physics program: a 2025-2026 stocktake

author.name: Jesse Thaler

entry.summary: A talk by Jesse Thaler taking stock of machine learning for the LHC physics program from May 2025 to May 2026, using an agentic AI pipeline to survey 569 abstracts from the HEPML Living Review, read 103 papers in full, and synthesize six checked claims about the field's state. Notably, most of the document was generated by the AI system under human authorship of the introduction.

entry.title: When Privacy Moves ML-Mediated Decisions On Device: Information and Incentive Misalignment in Auctions

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: This paper examines how moving ML-mediated ad auction decisions onto privacy-preserving on-device clients creates information-structure failures, since shared budget constraints rely on stale, non-global information. Using an auction-faithful simulation with 36 campaigns and 50 devices, the authors show proportional pacing can overspend dramatically (e.g., 17.77% after one tick of staleness) and quantify the effect. It highlights a systemic economic problem introduced by on-device privacy architectures.

entry.title: Taming the Greeks: Option Portfolios with Inductive Biases

author.name: Wee Ling Tan, Stephen Roberts, Stefan Zohren

entry.summary: The authors present an end-to-end deep learning framework for systematic options trading that enforces portfolio-level hedging through a differentiable risk-sensitivity penalty combined with a performance-driven loss, imposing neutrality to selected risk factors. Unlike RL-based hedging, the method operates directly on real market data without simulated market dynamics.

entry.title: Neuron-Level Architecture Growth: A Controlled Evaluation for EEG Time-Series Decoding

author.name: Adam Mounir, Stella Douka, Arnault H. Caillet, Bruno Aristimunha, Sylvain Chevallier

entry.summary: The paper provides the first controlled evaluation of neuron-growing methods for convolutional EEG decoders, growing three backbones across 12 motor-imagery datasets and three protocols against fixed-width references. Results are mixed: growing ShallowFBCSPNet gains 2.9 accuracy points with 0.57x parameters while Deep4Net variants underperform, with outcomes tied to the candidate selection step.

entry.title: The Statistical Cost of Causal Discovery with Feedback

author.name: Sunmin Oh, Seungsu Han, Gunwoong Park

entry.summary: The authors establish the first information-theoretic lower bounds on sample complexity for learning cyclic causal structure in linear non-Gaussian models, specifically exact condensation recovery of the strongly connected component partition and inter-component edges. The bounds distinguish the costs of SCC membership and external-parent selection, and matching upper bounds are given under principal invertibility without correlation faithfulness.

entry.title: Pre-registered tests of solid-state-physics-inspired LLM compression: a cluster-level negative result at small-language-model scale

author.name: Jun-qiang Lu

entry.summary: The author reports a three-month autonomous research-agent program testing five solid-state-physics-inspired compression mappings on pretrained LMs, with predictions committed before pilots and a 3-sigma pass/shelve gate. Most hypotheses were falsified at small model scale, though interesting auxiliary observations emerged, such as stretched-exponential fits to GPT-2 attention-versus-distance in most median-layer heads.

entry.title: Sub-Model Short-Term Memory Convolutions for Keyword Spotting Systems on Device

author.name: Pawe{\l} Warlewski, Artur Czeczko, Artur Szumaczuk, Grzegorz Stefa\'nski, Szymon Klimaszewski

entry.summary: The paper applies the Short-Term Memory Convolutions (STMC) framework to adapt modular CNNs for online, LSTM-like inference in keyword spotting on severely resource-constrained edge devices such as wearables. The approach reportedly cuts power consumption and redundant computation while preserving CNN training stability, with claimed reductions up to 82%.

entry.title: The Hidden Perception Constraint in Task-Aware Compression

author.name: Sahan Liyanaarachchi, Semih Akkoc, Sennur Ulukus, Aylin Yener

entry.summary: This theory-oriented paper identifies perception constraints that arise implicitly in task-aware compression, studying a setting where reconstruction is the primary task and classification is a secondary task. It analyzes the problem under varying levels of domain information and characterizes how these hidden constraints shape compression design. The work connects information theory with neural compression practice.

entry.title: Language Distances are Practical for Equitable Cross-Lingual Transfer

author.name: York Hay Ng, Razan Ahsan Rifandi, Aditya Khan, En-Shiun Annie Lee

entry.summary: This paper presents the first equity-focused evaluation of language-distance measures for ranking source languages in cross-lingual transfer, examining resource-level and task inequality across ten tasks and two multilingual models. It studies whether distance-based rankers remain reliable for low-resource target languages where exhaustive source search is impractical. The work is useful for practitioners deciding transfer sources under resource constraints and for understanding fairness in multilingual NLP.

entry.title: Streamlined Reflective Evolution for Task-Adaptive Self-Refinement Pipelines

author.name: Xiaofan Zhou, Lu Cheng

entry.summary: The paper introduces Workflow-Designing Agents (WDA), a framework that evolves both the instructions and the sequential structure of multi-stage self-refinement pipelines without weight updates, starting from a minimal prompt. It identifies instruction-accumulation bloat from repeated revision and proposes SPLIT, which redistributes redundant instructions across specialized stages, with calibration scores guiding Pareto-based search. This extends prompt optimization from fixed architectures to workflow design.

entry.title: PC-SubMax: Efficient Prompt Compression via Regularized Submodular Maximization

author.name: Ziyi Zhang, Shuang Cui, Haotian Zhang, Xiaoyu Wang

entry.summary: PC-SubMax reframes selective prompt compression for LLMs as regularized monotone submodular maximization, allowing the value of including a sentence to depend on what has already been selected and thereby capturing inter-sentence redundancy. The approach is theoretically grounded, model-agnostic, and avoids the high overhead of autoregressive LLM-based scoring, targeting long-context costs, latency, and the lost-in-the-middle problem.

entry.title: The Text Beside the Image: Detection, Utility and Leakage for Trustworthy Multimodal Medical Data and Beyond

author.name: Andreas Maier, Monica Hinrichs-Mayer, Franziska Weber, Niklas Lackner, Matthias May, Bernhard Kainz, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: Measures identifier detection, downstream utility, and residual identity leakage in pseudonymized medical report text, testing 15 detectors across three release conditions and four corpora in German, English, Chinese, and Arabic. A fixed 13-detector union achieves very high person sensitivity (e.g., 0.9998 at 0.8686 specificity on medical reports). Highlights that protecting medical images without protecting accompanying reports leaves privacy leakage risks.

entry.title: ManiEdit: Sequential Unstructured Knowledge Editing for Language Models from a Manifold Perspective

author.name: Rui Liu, Chenheng Zhang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

entry.summary: Reframes sequential knowledge editing of unstructured long-form knowledge as localized displacement of an edit sub-manifold within the global knowledge manifold, addressing edit forgetting and degradation of general capabilities in existing methods. Decomposes the problem into identifying representative edit points that anchor the sub-manifold and preserving the rest of the manifold. A theoretically grounded approach to continual model editing.

entry.title: The Effects of Incremental Instruction Delivery on Language-Model Creative Writing

author.name: Anshuman Singh, Abrar Eyasir, Haseeb Yaqoob, John Manavalan

entry.summary: This study measures whether delivering creative-writing instructions progressively over 5-9 turns, rather than upfront, degrades output quality, using 160 human-authored tasks across six genres and six open-weight model families for 960 matched pairs. It goes beyond explicit requirement checks to capture how multi-turn interaction harms creative artifacts. The finding that progressive delivery reduces constraint satisfaction extends known multi-turn degradation results to subjective, non-verifiable tasks.

entry.title: Reference-Grounded Data Curation for Instruction-Following Thai-English Machine Translation

author.name: Thodsaporn Chay-intr, Krittapad Harnchang, Mahannop, Thabua, Kobkrit Viriyayudhakorn, Thanaruk Theeramunkong

entry.summary: The authors propose a two-phase data curation pipeline for instruction-following machine translation: IFD scoring retains hard-but-learnable parallel instances, then constraints are extracted from reference translations and only constraint-satisfying generations are kept, producing a 1.97M-instance dataset. This ensures feasibility by construction and addresses the quality-versus-rule-compliance tension.

entry.title: How Well Can LLMs Simulate Real Learner Evaluations of Educational Feedback?

author.name: Momoka Furuhashi, Kouta Nakayama, Takashi Kodama, Saku Sugawara, Kyosuke Takami

entry.summary: The paper tests how well six LLMs can simulate real high-school students' subjective evaluations of feedback on biology questions, at both group and individual levels, with and without learner-specific information like personality traits and example evaluations. Results show limited simulation ability overall: learner profiles and examples improve score calibration and individual-level simulation, but often fail to improve group-level correlation.

entry.title: MDL-Calibrated Significance-Gain Pair Encoding: Replication-Aware Automatic Stopping for Subword Tokenization

author.name: Azam Nouri

entry.summary: The paper extends Significance-Gain Pair Encoding (SG-BPE), which replaces BPE's frequency-only merge selection with a statistical criterion based on how strongly a pair exceeds expected co-occurrence under independence. The new MDL-SG procedure separates discovery, replication, and utility stages, ranking candidate pairs on a discovery partition, testing replication with an exact one-sided hypergeometric test and per-iteration multiple-comparison correction, and using MDL-based calibration to stop merges automatically without an externally specified vocabulary size.

entry.title: CORA: A Protocol for Diagnosing Boundary Robustness in Text-to-Audio Retrieval under Query Reformulations

author.name: Jae Min Woo, Kyongmin Kong, Bogyung Jeong, Minjeong Kim, HaeJun Yoo, Du-Seong Chang

entry.summary: Presents CORA, a diagnostic protocol that rewrites audio captions into five intent-preserving query styles while keeping the target audio fixed, exposing retrieval failures hidden by Recall@k. The RankDrop metric correlates strongly with target boundary margin degradation rather than raw text embedding movement.

entry.title: 3dgs-sc: a controlled static screen-content benchmark for 3d gaussian splatting

author.name: Shicheng Cai, Hao Zhang, Dong Dai, Xuerui Ma, Ying Hu, Tao Zhang

entry.summary: 3DGS-SC is a controlled benchmark of ten procedural scenes testing whether high image fidelity in 3D Gaussian Splatting implies readable screen content, with exact cameras, masks, and transcripts enabling separated evaluation of fidelity, OCR readability, and edge preservation. Across method pairs, screen-PSNR and OCR orderings disagree in seven of ten cases, exposing fidelity-only evaluation failures.

entry.title: Enhancing Visual Reasoning in Chest X-Ray Report Generation Using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Denis Musinguzi, Andrew Katumba, Prasenjit Mitra

entry.summary: The paper applies reinforcement learning to chest X-ray report generation to address hallucinations caused by supervised fine-tuning optimizing lexical similarity over clinical correctness, with attention to rewarding sound reasoning rather than only final answers. It argues RL, successful in verifiable domains like math and code, is underused in open-ended medical generation.

entry.title: Binaural Audio-Visual Instance Segmentation

author.name: Saijun Wang, Guanfeng Tang, Hongbo Zhao, Zhicheng Lei, Yutong Zhang, Wei Ye, Rui Fan
