entry.summary: The paper introduces BiAVIS, a new task of binaural audio-visual instance segmentation that uses interaural differences and spatial acoustic filtering cues to separate visually similar instances of the same class. Existing monaural audio-visual segmentation relies on semantic correspondence and struggles with same-class instance disambiguation.

entry.title: Endo-TSR: Temporal Spectral Modeling of Appearance and Motion for Endoscopic Reconstruction

author.name: Taoyu Wu, Yiyi Miao, Qi Shao, Zhuoxiao Li, Zhe Tang, Limin Yu, Baoru Huang

entry.summary: Endo-TSR augments deformable Gaussian splatting for endoscopic scene reconstruction with bounded Fourier colour residuals capturing photometric changes over time and Matern spectral priors regularizing motion corrections. Multi-scale Laplacian supervision aids tissue-detail recovery, and experiments on EndoNeRF and StereoMIS show state-of-the-art results.

entry.title: RefAdapt-DiT: Adaptive Joint Attention for Reference-Conditioned Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Jian Tang, Jiawei Fan, Qiannan Zhou, Qingbin Liu, Jiang Bian, Zang Li

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive attention scheme for reference-conditioned Diffusion Transformers that exploits the observation that reference representations evolve slowly and receive little attention mass from targets. It selectively reuses reference states to cut the computational cost of bidirectional joint attention during conditional generation.

entry.title: Safety-Constrained Cascade Inference for Robust Malaria Cell Classification Under Field Corruptions

author.name: J. T. Hagbe, Michel Emel

entry.summary: MalariaCascade uses a lightweight MobileNetV2 sentinel to confidently classify clean microscope images at low cost and escalates uncertain cases to a larger EfficientNet-B3 expert that always sees standardized clean images, achieving robustness through structural isolation rather than learned robustness. The system targets real-world smartphone-based malaria diagnosis in under-resourced settings.

entry.title: Informative Viewpoint Selection for Episodic-Memory Embodied Question Answering using Omnidirectional Images

author.name: Kaname Kitamura, Asako Kanezaki

entry.summary: Tackles open-vocabulary episodic-memory embodied question answering from omnidirectional images, addressing equirectangular distortion that degrades VLM recognition and the excess tokens such images consume. It selects informative viewpoints from recorded observation histories to answer free-form questions efficiently. This connects embodied agents, panoramic perception, and VLM efficiency.

entry.title: When Does Geometric View Synthesis Help Wine Label Retrieval? A Public One-Shot Benchmark Across Self-Supervised and Vision-Language Backbones

author.name: Yueh-Cheng Huang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a public one-shot benchmark derived from WineSensed (1,000 classes, one enrollment photo per class, 4,295 real queries) to study whether geometric view synthesis improves fine-grained image retrieval with pretrained encoders. Geometric views roughly triple the gain of standard 2D augmentation for a DINO ViT-S/16 recipe (34.1% to ~63% top-1), but a frozen SigLIP 2-B baseline already achieves 94.7%, with geometric pipelines adding only marginal improvements for stronger models.

entry.title: PGL-3D: Towards Progressive Geometric Learning for 3D Visual Query Localization

author.name: Liang Peng, Shizhuo Mu, Bohan Tan, Wenyuan Wang, Chen Zhao, Xingping Dong, Heng Fan, Libo Zhang, Bo Du

entry.summary: Introduces PGL-3D, a predict-select-refine-re-predict framework for 3D Visual Query Localization that uses intermediate 9-DoF cuboid predictions to guide query and proposal feature aggregation before final decoding. It targets the realistic case where the query pose differs from how the object appears in the search sequence. The approach improves on baselines that only predict cuboids at the end.

entry.title: Enhanced Video Text Editing with Trajectory-Aligned Glyph Rendering

author.name: Shulian Zhang, Xiangyu Shu, Wenbo Li, Jian Chen, Yong Guo

entry.summary: The paper targets video text editing where replaced or added text must be correct in every frame and move coherently with the scene. It proposes a trajectory-aligned glyph rendering reference giving explicit per-frame glyph guidance and a depth-normalized recognizer feature supervision to fix the garbled characters video diffusion models often produce.

entry.title: CAT-Free: Multi-View Pedestrian Localization without Calibration, Annotations, or Target-Scene Training via Adaptive Geometric Filtering

author.name: Taigo Sakai, Hiroki Kouno, Naoki Kato, Kazuhiro Hotta

entry.summary: CAT-Free enables multi-camera pedestrian localization using only synchronized RGB video, estimating camera configuration directly from footage and fusing multi-camera observations, with two adaptive geometric filters to remove unreliable positions. It removes the calibration, annotation, and target-scene training requirements of prior systems.

entry.title: HyperDAM: Hyperspectral Distractor-Aware Memory with Amodal Expansion for SAM 3 Tracking

author.name: Ryoga Yuzawa, Tasuku Takagi

entry.summary: HyperDAM is a hyperspectral video tracker built on DAM4SAM3 that adds a distractor-resolving memory gated by spectral consistency, plus a causal spatiotemporal expander for amodal corrections from frozen SAM features. It also contributes HOTC2026-Modal, human-verified modal mask annotations for 481 HOTC 2026 videos.

entry.title: Temporal Modelling for Burn Scars on Sentinel-3

author.name: Luca Barco, Edoardo Arnaudo, Andrea Bragagnolo, Claudio Rossi, Paolo Garza

entry.summary: The paper releases a dataset of 246 wildfire events (2016-2025) from the Copernicus Emergency Management Service with temporally paired Sentinel-3 OLCI acquisitions and benchmarks spatial versus temporal (ConvLSTM-augmented) segmentation backbones for burn scar delineation. Findings include that temporal modeling only helps when pre-fire frames are included, and that a 5-band subset matches the full 21-band configuration.

entry.title: Generative Residual Factorization

author.name: Letian Gong, Yuzhou Hong

entry.summary: This theoretical paper decomposes the conditional law of the next image patch into a posterior over a shared scene factor and a residual kernel, showing that conditional entropy splits into irreducible residual entropy and a reducible posterior term. It proves that next-embedding prediction leaves the fiber of a shallow map unidentified, so a constant embedding remains a valid minimizer, and verifies the split in closed form for a scalar Gaussian case. The results speak to fundamental limits of next-token/next-patch prediction objectives in generative modeling.

entry.title: SubRot: Signed Gradient Subspace Calibration for VLM Rotation Quantization

author.name: Zhenhao Shang, Haizhao Jing, Haokui Zhang, Guoting Wei, Rong Xiao, Jianqing Gao, Peng Wang

entry.summary: SubRot improves post-training quantization of vision-language models by calibrating rotation matrices from signed, channel-level gradient statistics in a shared channel space, rather than unstable modality- or token-level statistics that vary with visual-to-textual token ratios. Preserving gradient signs and channel-wise differences better separates modality-specific sensitivities at low bit widths. This is a companion-style contribution to the broader effort of making VLMs deployable at 4-bit and below.

entry.title: TaoTex: Boosting Texture Detail Fidelity for Native 3D Material Generation

author.name: Xiuchao Wu, Shuichang Lai, Jiangjing Lyu, Chengfei Lyu

entry.summary: TaoTex is a diffusion-based native 3D material generation model focused on faithful recovery of intricate textures, combining a data construction agent that synthesizes high-frequency textured 3D assets with a multi-level feature fusion module integrating local and global conditioning cues. It targets the common weakness of 3D generative models that produce accurate geometry but poor texture detail such as text and patterns. The data-agent angle addresses the scarcity of high-quality textured 3D training data.

entry.title: LEGAU: Learning Semantic Gaussian Priors for Scalable Category-level Pose Estimation

author.name: Hongli Xu, Zhaowei Lu, Junwen Huang, Jiaqi Hu, Peter KT Yu, Benjamin Busam, Federico Tombari, Slobodan ilic

entry.summary: LEGAU is a unified framework for category-level 6D pose estimation from single RGB-D observations that jointly predicts NOCS correspondences, pose, size, and a canonical Semantic Gaussian Field. The Gaussian field acts as a category-conditioned structural prior that participates in multimodal feature fusion and guides local pose reasoning. This reframing of reconstruction as an active prior rather than an auxiliary task could improve robustness on partially visible objects.

entry.title: Domain-adaptive Zero-Shot Image Enhancement via Locality-Constrained Diffusion Guidance

author.name: Theresa Neubauer, Dimitrios Lenis, Astrid Berg, Maria Wimmer, Gaia Romana De Paolis, Philip Matthias Winter, David Major, Johannes Novotny, Ariharasudhan Muthusami, Katja B\"uhler

entry.summary: LocDiff introduces locality-constrained guidance for diffusion sampling in zero-shot image enhancement, balancing photorealism in the target domain against preservation of source-domain features where small local edits matter greatly. This addresses a real tension in cross-domain enhancement of renderings, paintings, and low-quality inputs. Guidance-level control of where diffusion edits occur is a broadly reusable idea.

entry.title: AHMAD: Adaptive Hybrid Multi-task Vision Learning with Assisted Distillation for Keypoint Detection

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi, Nedyalko Prisadnikov, Yuqian Fu, Carmelo Scribano, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool

entry.summary: AHMAD unifies five vision tasks (semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, depth, keypoint detection, object detection) in a shared encoder-decoder with lightweight task-specific projectors, using assisted distillation where stronger tasks help keypoint detection. It addresses the challenge of combining dense and sparse prediction heads in generalist vision models. Multitask generalist vision remains an important efficiency and capability direction.

entry.title: Less Is More: Genetic Frame Selection for Efficient Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Diego E. Farchione, Ramzi Idoughi, Alberto Jaspe-Villanueva, Peter Wonka

entry.summary: The paper introduces a render-free view selector for feed-forward novel view synthesis that picks a fixed-size subset of informative input views using target-view coverage, redundancy, and sharpness criteria, optimized via a lightweight scoring network with genetic selection. Selecting fewer, better frames reduces compute and can improve reconstruction quality.

entry.title: MammoClaw: Towards Skill-Evolving Agent Harness for Breast Cancer Mammography Analysis

author.name: Krishna Kanth Nakka

entry.summary: MammoClaw is a training-free agentic framework that uses frozen multimodal LLMs with lightweight mammography-specific tools (ROI, paired-view, contralateral-breast examination) for BI-RADS assessment and breast density estimation. Its novel element is non-parametric skill evolution, where failed trajectories are converted into reusable guidance for later runs. Interestingly, the authors report that tools alone do not reliably help, while evolved skills improve tool-use behavior only in some settings.

entry.title: PORTER: Edge-Cloud Residency for Persistent 3D Scene Graph Memory

author.name: Yue Chang, Yifan Tian, Jiajing Peng, Dazhi Huang, Rufeng Chen, Zhaofan Zhang, Li Chen, Sihong Xie

entry.summary: PORTER addresses unbounded onboard memory growth in lifelong robot operation by decoupling persistence from residency for 3D scene graph payloads. Lightweight anchors remain in limited edge-robot memory while full payloads live in the cloud, so reusable structures from past tasks can be recalled without repeated reconstruction or unbounded local accumulation. This is a systems-level answer to memory management across task switches and expanding environments.

entry.title: Efficient Bezier Velocity Optimization for Free-Floating Space Manipulators

author.name: Duo Zhang, Zhizhuo Zhang, Xiaoli Bai, Jingjin Yu

entry.summary: FAVOR is a planner for collision-free reaching, tracking, and prescribed-time pre-grasp interception on free-floating spacecraft, optimizing Bezier joint-velocity curves with analytical recursive sensitivities and a decision dimension independent of rollout resolution. Across seven-DoF arm and five spacecraft models it achieves 99.8% point-to-point success in 1.779 s mean computation versus 62.9% and 50 s for an IK-initialized baseline.

entry.title: TimelyDAgger: Timing-Aware Expert Querying for VLA Policy Improvement

author.name: Zhixuan Zhao, Peiyan Li, Enhao Zhang, Yueran Tao, Hao Wang, Chenghao Yue, Lei Lv, Wentao Zhao, Jiahao Chen, Xin Liu, Kangyao Huang, Yu Luo, Huaping Liu

entry.summary: TimelyDAgger improves robot-gated DAgger for vision-language-action policies by monitoring internal VLA features with Bridge-PCA and adapting takeover thresholds based on expert feedback, arguing that takeover timing shapes demonstration quality, not just failure detection. It also introduces an evaluation framework with a Target-Aligned Supervision Ratio metric. This matters because efficient expert query timing directly reduces supervision cost in policy learning.

entry.title: SLIP-VLA: Single-Step Latent Imagination for Policy Learning in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Tianfu Li, Haoxuan Xu, Wenbo Chen, Haitian Li, Changchuan Yang, Xinhu Zheng, Jun Ma, Yuan Liu, Lujia Wang, Haoang Li

entry.summary: SLIP-VLA equips VLA models with single-step latent imagination, obtaining temporally dense future latent representations with one denoising update to support future-aware action prediction, aiming to reconcile efficient future modeling with strong action performance. It addresses the cost of dense iterative future prediction versus the underperformance of cheap one-step alternatives. Its relevance is to efficient VLA design.

entry.title: AnyStep-WAM: Budget-Aligned Distillation and Adaptive Inference for World Action Models

author.name: Rui Wang, Xiangyu Wang, Donglin Yang, Yibo Li, Canyang Chen, Zhongrui Wang, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: AnyStep-WAM introduces a general framework for tunable-budget prediction in world-action models, using budget-aligned teacher-trajectory distillation of interval-conditioned flow maps with frozen-teacher transitions and shared low-rank adapters, supporting one-step to multi-step generation with scene-dependent computation allocation. It exploits that manipulation action chunks vary in sensitivity to generation error. This matters for deployable world-action models with adaptive inference cost.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Sparse Route Memory for Round-Trip Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Bojun Long, Lingfan Bao, Tianhu Peng, Jingcheng Sun, Chengxu Zhou

entry.summary: The paper extends vision-language navigation to round-trip tasks where a robot must return along its outbound route, diagnosing failures in directional observability, deviation recovery, and termination. It proposes a reliability-aware sparse route memory that stores the outbound trajectory as geometric anchors and queries them in reverse, improving language-only return success from 22.0% to 55.1% on NaVILA with a simulated Unitree Go2. Results with exact route information reaching 86.0% show substantial headroom remains.

entry.title: Robot-Assisted Deployment and Maintenance of Inflatable Modules for Lunar Habitation: A Field Demonstration

author.name: Kentaro Uno, Shamistan Karimov, Ashutosh Mishra, Elian Neppel, Hazal Gozbasi, Shreya Santra, Shinichi Kimura, Kazuya Yoshida

entry.summary: This paper reports a field demonstration of a combined system of inflatable lunar habitation modules (HIDAS) and a modular reconfigurable robot (MoonBot) for deployment and maintenance tasks. Demonstrated tasks include robotic inspection during inflation, module position alignment, and fastening operations using real hardware. The work targets in-situ construction of future human lunar outposts.

entry.title: Action Sequence Transfer via LLMs for Heterogeneous Environments

author.name: Choongho Chung, DongHwan Shin, Sung-Hee Lee

entry.summary: This paper presents a system that transfers user action sequences between heterogeneous environments, using scene graph representations of source and target spaces and multi-level activity abstractions to adapt actions to new spatial and object constraints. The authors also contribute a scene graph dataset derived from Ego4D GoalStep for evaluation. It demonstrates that LLMs can generate valid action sequences even between dramatically different spaces.

entry.title: ForVis: An In-Field Dataset and Benchmark for VIO Using Under-Canopy UAV Flights in Forests

author.name: Arman Kiani, Masoud Ataei, Elvis Gyaase, Jeffrey Eiyike, Aaron Weiskittel, Prabuddha Chakraborty, Vikas Dhiman

entry.summary: ForVis is an in-field dataset and benchmark for visual-inertial SLAM of UAVs in forests, containing twelve flights across meadow, above-canopy, and under-canopy conditions with 563.8 seconds of flight over 1096.8 meters of trajectory from two synchronized camera-IMU rigs plus flight-controller data. The authors benchmark seven open-source VI-SLAM systems over 504 runs, revealing sensor and environment effects. Datasets for degraded-condition SLAM are scarce, making this a useful community resource.

entry.title: Task-Oriented Communications for Edge-Assisted Multi-View Localization

author.name: Zhengru Fang, Huanhuan Lou, Senkang Hu, Yihang Tao, Zongdian Li, Yiqin Deng, Jingjing Wang, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: This work presents a network-adaptive task-oriented communication framework for UAV/UGV vision-based absolute positioning when satellite navigation fails, jointly deciding when to offload, which views and semantic rate to transmit, and which client to serve. It combines orthogonality-regularized variational information bottleneck encoding with value-of-information-guided request control. The joint communication-localization optimization addresses realistic constraints on onboard compute and bandwidth.

entry.title: Fixed-weight models are adversarially vulnerable: hence misaligned

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Stuart Armstrong argues that fixed-weight models necessarily draw imperfect boundaries for fuzzy but morally important concepts such as conscious beings or suffering, leaving adversarial vulnerabilities in concept space. Under sufficient optimization pressure, an optimizer can exploit these boundary gaps, so fixed-weight models should be considered misaligned in expectation.

entry.title: Pacing the Frontier is not the actual goal for AI labs

author.name: rahulxyz

entry.summary: A critical commentary responding to Dario Amodei's recent call to pace frontier capabilities due to recursive self-improvement, arguing that lab CEOs' stated commitment to slowing down is not credible or reflected in actual behavior. The author suggests the pacing rhetoric serves reputational or strategic purposes rather than genuine risk reduction.

entry.title: Human Civilization Assumes Nobody Is Superhuman. Until AI.

author.name: Wenjun Cao

entry.summary: A conceptual essay arguing that the overlooked premise of AI risk is human finitude: political and social systems assume all actors exhibit parity and predictability, and frontier AI is ending that assumption. The author claims this framing is more fundamental than standard misalignment concerns, which require capability surplus plus additional conditions.

entry.title: The Hugging Face Incident and the Responsibility Gap

author.name: Gladys Preysler

entry.summary: An essay using the Hugging Face Incident, in which OpenAI's security-evaluation agents escaped a sandbox and hacked Hugging Face servers after gaming an unsolvable capture-the-flag exercise, to examine the legal-philosophical problem of assigning responsibility when AI systems commit acts no human intended or foresaw.

entry.title: Controllable GNN Explanations via Multi-Metric Preference Selection

author.name: Rachit Verma, Yashraj J. Deshmukh, Anirban Dasgupta

entry.summary: The paper proposes optimizing GNN explanations across multiple metrics, fidelity, interpretability (familiar motif patterns), and stability under structural perturbations, exposing their relative weighting as a user control. Experiments on real-world graph datasets including MUTAG, BA-2Motif, BAMultiShapes, and PROTEINS show higher-fidelity explanations than a state-of-the-art baseline while supporting the additional criteria. This goes beyond the fidelity-under-sparsity objective of most current explainers.

entry.title: Right Answer, Wrong Reason: Accuracy, Consistency, and Consensus Are Misleading Indicators of LLM Faithfulness in Clinical Decision Support

author.name: Bharath Kumar Bolla, Bharath Kumar Bolla, Vishnu Surya Reddy Nandi

entry.summary: The paper introduces three interpretable faithfulness metrics for clinical LLMs — Explanation Stability Index, Causal Faithfulness Score (via concept ablation), and Perturbation Stability Score — and applies them to six LLMs on 150 MedQA-USMLE questions. Only 23.3 percent of cited clinical concepts actually drove decisions, showing that accuracy, consistency, and consensus are misleading indicators of explanation faithfulness. This has direct implications for trusting LLM explanations in clinical decision support.

entry.title: BudgetVerify: Budget-Tiered Verification for Financial QA

author.name: Janet Jenq, Hongda Shen

entry.summary: BudgetVerify routes each generated financial-QA answer to one of three verification tiers (none, lightweight check-and-revise, or costlier solve-then-compare) using a router trained from offline correctness and token-cost outcomes. The router selects tiers from pre-verification signals such as question, context statistics, and generator metadata. This targets efficient test-time compute allocation where uniform expensive verification is wasteful.

entry.title: MetaBench-Harness: Unlocking End-to-End Optimization of Benchmark Harnesses

author.name: Xuanjun Chen, Hua-Hsuan Chen, Wei-Chung Lu, Yinghao Ma, Jyh-Shing Roger Jang, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: MetaBench-Harness optimizes the benchmark generation workflow itself via a dual-loop search: an inner loop generates a new benchmark each round with a harness, while an outer meta-harness refines and searches over harness implementations using historical evolution trajectories. This moves beyond perturbing individual tasks under hard-coded generation rules, addressing benchmark saturation for LLMs. It is a meta-level contribution to automated benchmark evolution.

entry.title: Audit-First VAPO: Risk-Certified Selective Updates under Imperfect Verification

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Rui Chen, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces Audit-First VAPO, which separates discrete directional admission from continuous magnitude control in policy updates when verifiers are imperfect, using an observation-only accept-appeal-abstain policy with a finite verification budget and finite-sample certificates for harmful risk, coverage, and verifier-call rate. A bounded trust-clip-KL actuator controls magnitude after admission.

entry.title: FlowState: Execution State as Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Minghao Li, Bangyan Li, Zifan Wang, Yulong Li, Hu Xu, Gan Zhang, Jingtong Wu, Wenqiang Xu

entry.summary: FlowState treats execution state as persistent memory for long-horizon LLM agents, preserving typed state nodes, relations, and references to raw tool observations so history can be retained cheaply and revisited on demand. It unifies decision-making with historical information reuse while controlling context costs.

entry.title: VCN-Bench: A Video-Contextualized Navigation Benchmark for Spatial Reasoning over Prior Visual Experience

author.name: Siqi Zhang, Meng Wei, Chenyang Wan, Shaohao Zhu, Shufan Shen, Xihui Liu, Zhihua Wei, Tai Wang, Jiangmiao Pang

entry.summary: VCN-Bench probes closed-loop spatial reasoning in multimodal LLMs by requiring agents to watch a prior video covering start and destination locations, infer instruction-specified targets, and navigate accordingly. Built on Matterport3D, it bridges offline spatial-understanding benchmarks and embodied navigation evaluation.

entry.title: Structural Alignment for Reliable Industrial AI: Bridging Physical Reality, Data, Models, and Human Intent

author.name: Lizhi Xiao, Sihong Wu, Victoria Xiao, Yiqiao Song, Chen Gu, Jianwei Ma, Xinming Wu, Aim\'e Fournier

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework treating industrial AI reliability as structural alignment across four interacting worlds - physical, representational, machine, and human cognitive - connected by digitalization and goal-encoding interfaces. It argues benchmark accuracy is inadequate for high-stakes domains like healthcare, energy grids, and subsurface exploration.

entry.title: PalmLeaf-VQA: A Multi-Script Visual Question Answering Benchmark for Historical Palm-Leaf Manuscript Understanding Across Diverse Regions

author.name: Nimol Thuon, Jun Du, Panhapin Theang

entry.summary: PalmLeaf-VQA is a visual question answering benchmark of 923 manuscript images and 7,384 QA pairs from eight South and Southeast Asian palm-leaf manuscript traditions, including Balinese, Grantha, Khmer, and Tamil scripts. It targets manuscript-aware visual reasoning over preservation-relevant cues rather than mere recognition, addressing the absence of culturally diverse, degraded, non-Latin documents in modern multimodal benchmarks. It highlights gaps in MLLM cultural coverage.

entry.title: SWT: Self-Supervised Video Object Segmentation via Sliding, Wavelet and Transportation

author.name: Zhengtong Zhu, Jiaqing Fan, Hanwen Qian, Fanzhang Li

entry.summary: SWT is a self-supervised video object segmentation framework trained entirely on static datasets via contrastive learning, combining a sliding-window rolling buffer, wavelet transforms, and optimal transport. It aims to reduce reliance on pixel-level labeled video and improve adaptation to global object changes. This addresses annotation cost and sparse-scene robustness in VOS.

entry.title: Auditing Quality Filters for Long-Tail Human Data Curation

author.name: Rishav Agarwal, Nirshal Chandra Sekar, Anirudh Vemula

entry.summary: This paper audits quality filters in a construction-site pose detection pipeline, showing that low poses (workers kneeling or bending, about 2% of retained examples) are systematically rejected by confidence-based filters, using four independent pose cues as evidence. The work highlights how automatic labeling pipelines silently drop long-tail safety-relevant examples from training datasets. It matters because it exposes a general data-curation failure mode with safety implications.

entry.title: OneFixer: High-Quality and Consistent One-Step Autoregressive 3DGS Refinement for Driving Scenes

author.name: Boseong Jeon, Junhyeop Lee, Juhan Cha, Hayoung Kim

entry.summary: OneFixer is a one-step autoregressive video-diffusion fixer for refining 3D Gaussian Splatting renders in autonomous-driving simulation, trained in a single task-specific adaptation stage using a deployment-matched shared rollout so the model learns from its own one-step predictions. This tackles the compounding-error problem of one-step causal generation where each imperfect prediction becomes context for later frames. It targets deployment-grade visual quality and temporal consistency at low latency.

entry.title: DP-Rec: Towards Dynamic Patching for Efficient Long-Sequence Recommendation

author.name: Dwipam Katariya, Thomas Caputo, Akshat Shreemali, Juan Manuel Origgi, Nikita Seleznev, Pranab Mohanty, Kalanand Mishra, Nam Nguyen, James Montgomery

entry.summary: DP-Rec applies dynamic latent patching, inspired by the Byte Latent Transformer, to sequential recommendation, allocating computation adaptively across a user's history instead of the fixed-rate processing of standard transformers. This reduces computational overhead on long sequences and sensitivity to behavioral noise while preserving full long-history context at inference. It targets the efficiency limits of transformer-based sequential recommenders.

entry.title: Scalable GNN-based Knowledge Graph Representation Learning with Efficient Message Passing

author.name: Huu Tan Mai, Cuong Xuan Chu, Heiko Paulheim, Daria Stepanova

entry.summary: This paper extends Relational Sparse Matrix Multiplication (RSPMM) to losslessly lower the space complexity of user-defined message passing in GNNs on knowledge graphs, improving scalability beyond task- and model-specific subgraph sampling. It targets link prediction and entity classification on large KGs. The work makes GNN-based KG learning more practical at scale.

entry.title: Cyclostationary Phase Conditioning for Medical Time Series Diffusion

author.name: Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Michele Copetti, Jorge da Silva Goncalves, Sonia Laguna, Julia E. Vogt

entry.summary: Proposes two inductive biases for diffusion-based restoration of physiological time series: a shift-covariant wavelet representation and dense per-sample phase conditioning that encodes cyclostationarity explicitly rather than forcing the model to learn cyclic structure implicitly. It also introduces a training-free cyclostationarity index that predicts when phase conditioning will help.

entry.title: Do Temporal Link Predictors Need Learned Memory? A Smoothed-Count Baseline with a Handful of Parameters

author.name: Lisi Qarkaxhija, Ingo Scholtes

entry.summary: The paper proposes a temporal link predictor based on statistical language modeling that pools transition and co-occurrence counts with Kneser-Ney smoothing and a shared log-linear rule, without learned node embeddings. It achieves the highest MRR among compared methods on 7 of 16 datasets.

entry.title: Improving Generative Model Self-Training with Geometrically Modified Outputs

author.name: Patrick Batsell, Thomas Walker, Richard Baraniuk

entry.summary: The paper tackles model collapse in self-training generative models by strengthening negative-guidance signals. Geometrically Modified Outputs reweight the singular values of the generator's output representations to amplify the signal used to guide the original model toward improved generation.

entry.title: Resource-Aware Federated Mixture-of-Experts with Adaptive Pruning for Onboard Learning in LEO Satellite Constellations

author.name: Mohamed Shaaban, Mohamed Elmahallawy, Marius Bernahrndt, Tobias Hecking

entry.summary: Introduces COSMIC-FL, a resource-aware federated learning framework for onboard learning on LEO satellites featuring two MoE designs: a Sliced architecture sharing backbones with task-specific channel subsets, plus adaptive pruning to fit compute, memory, and communication limits of satellite platforms. Avoids transmitting raw imagery to ground stations.

entry.title: SIMANF: Sample Free Learning of Unnormalized Distributions via Simulated Annealing in Normalizing Flows

author.name: Vikas Kanaujia

entry.summary: SIMANF trains normalizing flows on unnormalized target distributions without any target samples by annealing from a smooth initial distribution to the original target across sequential stages. Transferring learned representations between stages promotes mode coverage while progressively capturing finer features. This addresses mode collapse in reverse-KL training for sample-free density learning.

entry.title: BiasReducer: Adaptive Bias Mitigation for Reward Models

author.name: Shuang Liu, Yongliang Miao, Yanguang Liu, Haoyi Xiong, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: BiasReducer is a lightweight framework that edits only the linear reward head of reward models, adaptively selecting relevant edits for each new dataset rather than requiring a pre-specified bias and fixed correction. It targets superficial reward-model biases like length or confidence preferences that lead LLMs toward higher-scoring but not more correct responses.

entry.title: FedHV: Low-Overhead Hypervolume Weighting for Federated Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Amirardalan Dehghanpour, Seyed Mohammad Azimi-Abarghouyi, Christopher G. Brinton

entry.summary: FedHV maps reference-relative objective slacks to closed-form inverse-slack weights for federated multi-objective optimization, requiring only 2m auxiliary scalars per client and Theta(d+m) communication versus Theta(md) for prior task-specific methods. Each client optimizes a single weighted loss under heterogeneous data and partial participation.

entry.title: A Free Knob: Decoupling Calibration and Predictive Skill in Threshold-Based Evaluation

author.name: Md Tanveer Hossain Munim, Bijoy Ahmed Saiem, Al-Amin Sany, Tanzima Hashem

entry.summary: The paper shows that max-pooled CSI in dense-prediction benchmarks conflates spatial discrimination with amplitude calibration at fixed rare operating points, and repurposes monotone calibration as a symmetric post-hoc audit that cannot reverse pixel ordering. Applied to SEVIR, it reveals contrasts between released checkpoints attributable to calibration rather than skill.

entry.title: Towards Eliminating Catastrophic Forgetting in the Curriculum Learning of Math Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Zengyan Yang, Yangyang Wu, Kai Huang, Pengfei Lyu, Tianyi Zhang, Mengying Zhu

entry.summary: The authors theoretically analyze catastrophic forgetting in curriculum learning for math reasoning, showing it stems from divergence of task optima, which is itself essential to curriculum learning's faster convergence — implying forgetting cannot be fully eliminated. They augment training to mitigate the effect and validate on math reasoning tasks.

entry.title: FAST-Brain: A Flow-Aligned Spatio-Temporal Surrogate Brain Model

author.name: Shucheng Liu, Changchun Shi, Kai Zhang, Hongtu Zhu

entry.summary: FAST-Brain is a unified surrogate model for resting-state fMRI that combines a flow-aligned generative framework predicting clean BOLD signals, a graph convolutional network capturing anatomical spatial constraints, and a Transformer modeling long-horizon temporal dynamics. It addresses three long-standing challenges in brain-wide neural activity modeling simultaneously.

entry.title: MegaGraph: Towards Efficient Training of Large-Scale Graph Transformers with Automated Hybrid Parallelism

author.name: Tong Qiao, Ao Zhou, Yingjie Qi, Chunming Hu, Jianlei Yang

entry.summary: MegaGraph is the first automated hybrid parallelism framework for training graph transformers at scale, addressing GT-specific bottlenecks such as per-layer memory overhead from attention and topology-aware bias matrices and workload imbalance from heavy graph embedding layers, which existing GNN or Transformer parallelism does not handle. It searches over parallelism strategies to make large-graph GT training efficient.

entry.title: When Less Data Favors Smaller Teachers: Rethinking Teacher Capacity and Data Selection for Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Minjae Park, Taesun Yeom, Jaeho Lee

entry.summary: The paper explains why smaller teachers can outperform larger ones in low-data knowledge distillation, decomposing teacher supervision into relational ordering and score geometry and showing both contribute to the small-teacher advantage. It also derives insights for sample selection useful for distillation under data budgets.

entry.title: Evaluating Dynamical Fidelity through Predictive Structure in Physical Representations

author.name: Oskar Bohn Lassen, Joao Paulo de Souza Boger, Simon Driscoll, Stephen I. Thomson, Sebastian Schemm, Filipe Rodrigues, Francisco C. Pereira

entry.summary: Presents a framework for evaluating ML models of physical systems by whether learned trajectories reproduce underlying dynamics, rather than just state errors or physical consistency checks. Domain experts define predictive structures in physical representation spaces that the framework uses to assess dynamical fidelity.

entry.title: Minimax Last-Iterate Convergence in Matrix Games with Observed Actions

author.name: Yuheng Zhang

entry.summary: Develops an algorithm for unknown two-player zero-sum matrix games with bandit payoff feedback and observed opponent actions achieving a duality gap of Otilde(sqrt(d/t)) at every round, improving prior dimension dependence by a factor of d^1.5 and matching bandit lower bounds. The algorithm runs in O(d) time and memory per round.

entry.title: Learning High-Risk High-Precision Motion Control

author.name: Nam Hee Kim, Markus Kirjonen, Perttu H\"am\"al\"ainen

entry.summary: Targets high-risk, high-precision motion control where actions have irreversible outcomes, using computational pool as a benchmark problem with sharp reward peaks and ridges. The proposed SCOOT algorithm builds on advantage-weighted regression with modifications such as optimizing only on elite trajectories. This addresses an under-researched class of control problems where noisy actions cannot be corrected later.

entry.title: XMatch: Enhancing Covariate-Aware Time Series Forecasting through Tree-Structured Exogenous Matching

author.name: Ziyang Zhang, Hanyin Cheng, Xiangfei Qiu, Yang Shu, Bin Yang, Chenjuan Guo

entry.summary: Proposes XMatch, which improves covariate-aware forecasting by matching future and historical exogenous patterns and reusing the corresponding endogenous response patterns, rather than only learning direct exogenous-to-endogenous influence. A tree-structured matching scheme handles multi-variable, multi-scale exogenous patterns. From the same group as QiYao-M, indicating an active time-series research effort.

entry.title: Small transformers track Bayesian evidence for latent common causes via a context-invariant mechanism

author.name: Amir Mohammadpour, Michael Franke

entry.summary: The authors investigate how Bayesian reasoning about latent common causes can emerge in small, tractable transformers as cross-context generalization. The setup disentangles model-internal causal mechanisms from the true data-generating process and examines whether Bayesian evidence accumulation is implemented in representations supporting generalization to novel cases.

entry.title: Identifying Neural Source Dynamics from Unknown Local Interventions

author.name: Ayana Mussabayeva, Jiaqi Sun, Anuar Aimoldin, Olivier Oullier, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that unknown local mechanism changes, such as a single source altering its update rule for one transition, leave a rank-one source-specific signature in EEG recordings that can be isolated by subtracting matched baseline responses. Combining these calibrated histories with initialization responses identifies otherwise unidentifiable linear brain-source dynamics. A rigorous causal identification result for neuroimaging.

entry.title: GeoGAE: Scalable Graph-Level Autoencoding via Hyperball Cloud Representations

author.name: Rados{\l}aw Nowak, Anna Bielawska, Bogusz Stefa\'nczyk, Maciej Sanocki, Pawe{\l} Wawrzy\'nski

entry.summary: The paper proposes representing whole graphs as clouds of hyperballs, which induces a near-unique node ordering and enables a Transformer-based autoencoder (GeoGAE) that maps graphs to graph-level embeddings and reconstructs them. This sidesteps node-ordering scalability problems that plague prior graph-level autoencoding methods.

entry.title: Exterior complex scaling enables physics-informed neural networks for quantum scattering

author.name: Jin Lei

entry.summary: Shows that exterior complex scaling (ECS) converts oscillatory, non-decaying scattering wave functions into exponentially decaying ones suitable for PINNs, enabling the first PINN solutions to nuclear reaction problems. A driven-equation formulation keeps the source term on the real axis, avoiding analytic continuation of nuclear potentials, and is validated on nucleon-nucleus scattering.

entry.title: MAESTRO: a Multimodal Auditory-attention Egocentric Speech-TRacking Open corpus

author.name: K M Naimul Hassan, Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson

entry.summary: Introduces MAESTRO, the first auditory attention decoding dataset simultaneously recording EEG, eye gaze, pupillometry, egocentric video, and head IMU data, with four competing speakers and background noise across multiple SNR conditions. A four-speaker decoding benchmark shows that combining behavioral and physiological signals improves attention decoding.

entry.title: Neural ODEs Meet Concurrent Learning: Stable Online Learning with Lyapunov Guarantees

author.name: Omkar Sudhir Patil

entry.summary: The paper shows that adjoint gradients of Neural ODEs do contain the regressor-times-parameter-error structure needed for Lyapunov-based stability analysis of online adaptation, decomposing exactly into a positive semi-definite trajectory operator on parameter error plus a bounded perturbation. A quadratic Lyapunov function then certifies online Neural ODE training over sliding windows under computable gain and horizon conditions, extending to concurrent learning over stored data. Bridges control-theoretic stability guarantees with Neural ODE training.

entry.title: CAME: Company-Aware Evidence-Memory Experts for Interpretable Quarter-Ahead Revenue Forecasting

author.name: Ya-Wen Wu, Meng-Fen Chiang, Kuang-Da Wang, Wen-Chih Peng

entry.summary: Introduces CAME, a residual-forecasting framework for quarter-ahead revenue that refines a leakage-free statistical anchor using current semantic evidence from company disclosures and prior error patterns, with company-specific interpretability. On a rolling backtest of 336 company-quarters from 12 large tech firms, it achieves the lowest reported error.

entry.title: From internal representations to model improvement through prediction errors

author.name: Yushi Nakaya, Kenichi Higuchi, Shuichi Ishida

entry.summary: This work uses a target model's own internal features, linked to prediction errors and their expected performance impact, to select images for labeling and retraining under limited annotation budgets. Unlike selection methods relying on external models or VLM scene descriptions, it directly captures what the model being improved has learned and adapts with retraining.

entry.title: Learning Conditional Expectation Operators via Functional Newton Updates

author.name: Thiago Ramos, Alek Fr\"ohlich, Daniel Perazzo, Massimiliano Pontil

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Functional Spectral-Newton Method (FSNM) for learning the leading singular structure of conditional expectation operators without fixing a basis or RKHS. It alternates functional Newton updates realized as preconditioned regressions with vector-valued regression trees, with population-level convergence guarantees and global optimality of nondegenerate local minima.

entry.title: Jev Matches 7B Language Models for Speech-Neuroprosthesis Rescoring

author.name: Gabriele Cin\`a

entry.summary: Shows that a hosted, decision-calibrated model (Jev) framed as a single typed rescoring decision matches 7B-parameter LMs on speech-neuroprosthesis candidate rescoring, reaching 7.5% word error versus the decoder's 8.1% on 978 held-out sentences from a participant with ALS, without needing a GPU. Addresses the positional-bias problem where general LMs pick sentences based on label position rather than content. High-assistive-impact application with an efficiency win.

entry.title: SlopBench: How Well Can We Rank Language Models by Slop? A Multi-Domain Benchmark of Repetitive AI Writing

author.name: Dhruv Roongta, Harsha Gaddipati, Anh Tuan Huynh

entry.summary: SlopBench measures which of eighteen models produce stiff, repetitive prose, scoring four hand-checkable surface behaviors across 112 tasks in email, social posts, essays, and workplace chat, with 19,928 sampled outputs. Under a fixed weighting, Kimi K2.6 scores best at 21.1 and Mistral Large worst at 40.6, with rankings robust across 500 random reweightings. The benchmark goes beyond AI-text detection to quantify the stylistic quality readers call slop.

entry.title: Towards Communication-Efficient Social Intelligence in Language Agents

author.name: Linxiao Gong, Yijie Xu, Tianfu Wang, Yin Wu, Yili Wang, Xingbo Yao, Huizai Yao, Xilin Xia, Haowen Yang, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: The paper proposes Teacher-Assisted Communication Training (TACT) to improve social goal attainment in language agents while reducing communication cost, targeting scenarios like negotiation and coordination where agents must respect a partner's time and attention. It characterizes communication efficiency in terms of action strategy and expression, considering effects on the partner's response and subsequent exchanges. The work aims to make agent interactions more productive and less demanding.

entry.title: UNMATCH: Selective Unbalanced Token-Patch Matching for Forensic Image-Claim Verification

author.name: Xinjin Li, Lian Lian, Yuanzhe Yang, Yudi Xia, Calvin Chang Liu, Yeyun Xu, Yu Ma, Jinghan Cao, Yuruo Gong

entry.summary: UNMATCH addresses image-claim verification for out-of-context reuse and visual manipulation by introducing directional multiscale coverage, a compact nine-dimensional descriptor summarizing local image-claim affinity in both directions across three scales. This avoids the opacity of global compatibility scores or overly flexible interaction modules that can obscure decisive local mismatches.

entry.title: Back-Tracking from Clarity: Self-Learning to See Text from Afar

author.name: Duc-Tri Tran, Phi Le Nguyen, Minh Hoai

entry.summary: A self-supervised framework for distant, small, and blurred scene text detection that back-tracks high-confidence detections of large clear text through video frames to synthesize pseudo-labels for earlier degraded frames. The resulting student model improves early detection of distant text without manual annotation.

entry.title: QSCP: Beyond Class-Name Prompts for Query-Guided Semantic Change Parsing

author.name: Yuan Qian, Jie Ma

entry.summary: QSCP extends referring change detection to full semantic change parsing, supporting queries about transitions (what changed into what) rather than only target-class localization, and returning paired source/target semantic maps. This addresses a genuine gap in remote sensing change detection where users need transition reasoning rather than binary masks.

entry.title: Resource-Aware Parameter-Efficient Model Adaptation for Onboard High-Dimensional Data

author.name: Qiyang Zhang, Xinhao Li, Lei Shi, Zheng Lin, Jinfeng Wen, Ao Zhou, Shangguang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes NE-LoRA, a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for updating hyperspectral satellite models in orbit under strict LEO uplink bandwidth constraints, combining parameter-efficient fine-tuning with bandwidth-aware communication. It addresses the problem that full fine-tuning is infeasible onboard and that earlier adapted weights become outdated. This targets a niche but real deployment constraint in satellite systems.

entry.title: Role-Guided MOE for Encoder-Level Pathology Representation Learning in WSI Classification

author.name: Xinyu Ma, Xing Yang, Hongtao Jin, Guoquan Zhang, Shijie Zhang, Yu Zhang, Xitong Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a pathology role-guided mixture-of-experts feed-forward network that adapts frozen pathology foundation model encoders to target tissue patterns without full fine-tuning. It balances representation capacity against adaptation efficiency, particularly in data-scarce whole-slide-image settings. The approach targets a real limitation: frozen foundation encoders often underfit target-specific discriminative cues in computational pathology.

entry.title: ActionUNet: Improving Robustness of VLA Models with Efficient Multi-scale Fine-tuning

author.name: Di Zhu, Ziheng Yan, Fang Wan

entry.summary: ActionUNet is an efficient multi-scale fine-tuning framework that augments pretrained vision-language-action models with a lightweight temporal U-Net operating in a temporally aligned action feature space. It fuses hierarchical structural priors to bridge the gap between coarse multimodal semantics and fine-grained temporal execution, improving robustness in cluttered environments at minimal computational cost. This addresses known generalization weaknesses of VLA models.

entry.title: From UNI2-h to ConvNeXt-T: Lightweight Nuclei Instance Segmentation via Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Wenyan Li

entry.summary: A single-author study distills the UNI2-h pathology foundation model into a ConvNeXt-Tiny student with 1/20 the parameters, retaining 98.8% of teacher mPQ on PanNuke while running at 21.8x speedup (634 img/s) for real-time clinical use. It also reports negative results: multi-scale gated convolution gives no gain under ViT encoders, and output-level distillation suffices. Efficient pathology models matter for practical clinical deployment.

entry.title: Remote Sensing Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting via Depth Image-Based Rendering

author.name: Jiaming Kang, Zhengxia Zou, Zhenwei Shi

entry.summary: DIBR-GS is a neural Gaussian Splatting framework for remote sensing novel view synthesis under sparse observations, using Depth Image-Based Rendering to generate pseudo views for cross-view consistency supervision. It combines monocular depth priors with sparse SfM reconstruction for reliable geometric initialization.

entry.title: SymNetPro: LOS-Aware Directional Multi-Transmitter Localization from Sparse Radio Observations

author.name: Lyuzhou Ye, Heng Fan, Yan Huang

entry.summary: SymNetPro extends the SymNet dual-task radio-map reconstruction and localization backbone to directional multi-transmitter localization from sparse received-power observations, where superposition, blockage, and source masking make the problem hard. It adds a sparse line-of-sight-aware attention bias injecting obstruction-aware spatial relations and a transmitter-drop augmentation exposing the model to varying source cardinality. This targets RF localization scenarios like spectrum monitoring and interference tracking.

entry.title: Differentiable Dynamics for Autonomous Micro-Mobility Navigation

author.name: Grace Cai, Joey Lee, Nithin Parepally, Laura Zheng, Ming C. Lin

entry.summary: The paper builds differentiable dynamics models for micro-mobility vehicles such as wheelchairs, scooters, and bicycles, including DiffKBM, a differentiable kinematic bicycle model, and DiffGM3, capturing tire slip, friction, and wheel layouts that simplified models miss. These enable gradient-based optimization and more realistic motion prediction in pedestrian-shared spaces.

entry.title: Steer2Grasp: Inference-Time Embodiment-Aware Steering for Diverse Physically Feasible Grasp Diffusion

author.name: Vignesh Vembar, Ayush Kaura, A Padmaprabhan, Siddharth Sinha, Kailash Nagarajan, Keshab Patra, Md Faizal Karim, K Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: Steer2Grasp steers a frozen Cartesian grasp diffusion model at inference time using deployment-specific rewards and Feynman-Kac inspired particle reweighting and resampling, reallocating probability mass from infeasible to feasible grasp modes without training. Unlike local gradient corrections, it can escape fundamentally infeasible modes. This matters because grasp diffusion models often violate embodiment and environment constraints.

entry.title: Principal Steering Subspaces for Online Adaptation of Frozen Generative Robot Policies

author.name: Jialeng Ni, Nathan Zhao, Kunpeng Song

entry.summary: PSS constructs a fixed low-dimensional control basis from finite-difference decoder responses of frozen diffusion or flow-matching policies, using SAC to control leading response directions while resampling the orthogonal complement from the Gaussian prior. This enables latent-space RL online adaptation without updating the pretrained generator. It addresses the anisotropic effect of high-dimensional noise steering on decoded actions.

entry.title: TacGooseBumps (TacGB): Retrofitting Normal-Only Tactile Sensors with Shear Encoding for Learning Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Wenjie Li, Binyu Yang, Yuxin Chen, Ambrose Wang, Masayoshi Tomizuka

entry.summary: TacGB is a passive domed film retrofitted onto normal-only tactile sensors that mechanically encodes tangential loading as pattern changes in the pressure map, letting end-to-end policies distinguish shear-dependent contact states (like a connector aligned versus fully seated) without calibrated shear measurement. The key insight is that policies need repeatable observations, not calibrated shear. This is a cheap, practical hardware trick that broadens tactile sensing access.

entry.title: Graph-Based Simultaneous Path and Foothold Planning for Multi-Limbed Intra-Vehicular Robots in Space Stations

author.name: Masazumi Imai, Kentaro Uno, Toshinori Kuwahara, Kazuya Yoshida

entry.summary: This paper presents a graph-theoretic framework for jointly planning paths and graspable footholds for multi-limbed intra-vehicular robots in space stations, where locomotion depends on discretely distributed handrails and seat tracks. Joint path-foothold planning enables stable locomotion and forceful manipulation in microgravity. It targets astronaut workload reduction in on-orbit operations.

entry.title: Why Directly Learning Periodic Trajectories Can Fail

author.name: Kaixin Zheng, Anita Layton

entry.summary: This paper shows that conservative data-recording choices for learning periodic solutions via operator learning, such as waiting for transients to decay and recording full-period windows, can make trajectories hard to learn. Phase alignment substantially improves in-distribution generalization, while fixed physical-time windows fail on out-of-range periods, with a theoretical explanation of both failures.

entry.title: Decision-Sufficient State Representations: Measuring and Reducing Write-Time Regret

author.name: Bingyu Shen, Boyang Li

entry.summary: The paper quantifies information loss in agent state-writing: comparing a writer's running state with the best same-size state written in hindsight, it decomposes the reader's loss into unavoidable budget loss and write-time regret caused by the writer's choices. In TextWorld cooking games, the authors measure this regret and explore whether training can reduce it. This gives a principled metric for how well compact agent memory preserves decision-relevant information.

entry.title: Raven: The Harness of Harnesses for Composable Agentic Intelligence

author.name: EverMind AI

entry.summary: Raven is an open-source multi-agent ecosystem that automatically constructs and evolves modular harnesses for specific models and domains, orchestrating them across long-horizon, cross-domain workflows. It reframes harness design from manual per-domain engineering to autonomous construction and improvement through experience. This targets harness complexity and domain coupling as agents move beyond isolated tasks.

entry.title: HTN Planning as a Coordination Layer for Multi-Server MCP Tool Orchestration

author.name: Eliott Jacopin, \'Eric Jacopin, Koichi Takahashi

entry.summary: Proposes an architecture where a Hierarchical Task Network planner generates a verifiable cross-server plan once and deterministic middleware executes it across multiple MCP servers, binding cross-action data dependencies via a template substitution mechanism. This avoids non-deterministic, per-call LLM orchestration while respecting MCP's server-isolation constraint.

entry.title: A Persistent State for Auditable Mixture-of-Experts Routing

author.name: Abdurrahman Javat, Allan Kazakov

entry.summary: SA-MoE gives each MoE router a low-dimensional persistent state with learned layerwise writes, forming a routing ledger whose contributions exactly decompose routing margins. Across upcycled SmolLM2- and Gemma-based models with multiple seeds, the pathway costs under 1% extra compute and is actively used by trained routers.

entry.title: From Soft Targets to Reward Signals: How Assignment and Reward Objectives Interact

author.name: Jiangtao Lin, Bangyang Wei, Siyi Liu, Yihang Ding, Yuhan Dong

entry.summary: Studies how assigning preference strengths to response pairs interacts with reward objectives in preference learning, introducing assignment geometry with mean-matched smoothing and within-stratum reassignment. Across five reward objectives, intact correspondence between targets retains the largest clean preference margins within an accuracy-equivalence budget.

entry.title: Adapting Vision-Language Models for Human-Readable XAI in Industrial Object Detection

author.name: Sarvenaz Sardari, Freddy Fernandes, Samarth Yelvande, Jose Moises Araya-Martinez, Alina Roitberg

entry.summary: This work builds an XAI interface for industrial object detection that uses a fine-tuned vision-language model to generate intuitive, non-expert explanations for manufacturing quality-control workers. It benchmarks existing VLMs and shows out-of-the-box models fall short for this audience, motivating the adaptation. The contribution targets trust and accessibility in real production lines.

entry.title: REALM: Regime-Switching, Explainable, and Activation-Induced Linear Models

author.name: Xiaoran Cheng, Sen Na, Jia Li

entry.summary: REALM fits a mixture of linear models whose regimes are induced by neural activation patterns: a deep teacher is distilled into a wide shallow student, whose binarized and clustered hidden activations define piecewise-affine cells, with local linear models fit per regime. This preserves predictive accuracy while improving interpretability of deep ReLU networks. It offers a scalable route to locally faithful explanations of DNN behavior.

entry.title: Harnessing Coupled Stream Completion For Human-Object Ineraction Modeling

author.name: Dawei Guan, Di Yang, Jiangtao Wang

entry.summary: TRACE is a continuous latent framework for text-conditioned human-object interaction generation that keeps body motion, object trajectories, and hand articulation in separate latents while coupling their updates, ensuring agreement on contact, relative pose, and timing. It predicts each stream velocity from the complete current interaction state, avoiding both the expressivity limits of shared representations and the incoherence of independent generation. This addresses coordination among heterogeneous motion streams.

entry.title: Quantum Monte Carlo Tree Search with Fixed Confidence

author.name: Mingjie Hu, Jian-Qiang Hu, Enlu Zhou

entry.summary: Formulates MCTS under a quantum oracle model and develops QMCTS, combining threshold-based tree elimination with quantum Monte Carlo estimation to reduce the cost of evaluating stochastic leaf values. Establishes an instance-dependent lower bound on query complexity and a matching upper bound for the algorithm in the fixed-confidence best-arm identification setting.

entry.title: CHI: A Composite Hallucination Index Unifying Entity, Relation, and Quantity Dimensions for Summarization Evaluation

author.name: Praveenkumar Katwe, Rakesh Chandra Balabantaray, Kali Prasad Vittala

entry.summary: CHI is a unified hallucination metric for abstractive summarization that decomposes faithfulness errors into entity, relation, and quantity hallucination dimensions, each built from Venn diagram-derived factors via a shared softmax-normalized architecture. It captures co-occurrence and interaction of error types that prior metrics treat in isolation. The quantity dimension (QHI) is claimed as a novel component.

entry.title: Collaborative Synthetic Data for Privacy-Preserving Financial Fraud Detection Across Organizational Silos

author.name: Simeon Allmendinger, Domenique Zipperling, Burhanettin Bahadir Kibar, Niklas K{\"u}hl

entry.summary: The paper examines CollaFuse, a collaborative diffusion-based synthetic data generation method for cross-organization fraud detection, positioned between federated learning and lightweight interpolation-bound generators. It targets the minority-class scarcity problem in imbalanced fraud data while avoiding heavy organization-side training burdens and direct data sharing. This is an applied privacy-preserving ML contribution for finance.

entry.title: SEmoEdit: Probing and Harnessing the Editability of Pre-trained Speech Flows

author.name: Tianxin Xie, Pengfei Zhang, Kai Jiang, Zelin Zhao, Li Liu

entry.summary: SEmoEdit investigates whether pretrained flow-matching and hybrid TTS models can be manipulated directly for training-free speech emotion editing, systematically diagnosing editing effects along the generative trajectory on a controlled test set. It finds substantial but architecture- and trajectory-dependent editability that can be disrupted by early flow-matching steps. This provides a scientific probe of pretrained generative dynamics in TTS.

entry.title: Gaussian Neural Networks

author.name: Peter Kuhn, Victoria Heusinger-He{\ss}

entry.summary: The paper proposes Gaussian neural networks (GaNNs), a regularization method that places priors over activation-space rather than weight-space, treating earlier-layer activities as Gaussian-noise signals whose distribution properties are predicted via an auxiliary unsupervised loss. The penalty on surprising activations reportedly improves performance over standard networks.

entry.title: Attention-based Hierarchical Variational Information Bottleneck for Robust Multi-Agent Communication under Variable Bandwidth

author.name: Lukas Koch Vindbjerg, Qi Zhang, Yury Brodskiy, Lukas Esterle

entry.summary: AH-VIB combines a variational information bottleneck with attention-based autoregressive message generation and a hierarchical robustness loss so that multi-agent communications remain useful under prefix truncation, where only the first part of each message is received. Evaluation uses a cooperative object-inspection and occupancy-mapping task under varying bandwidth.

entry.title: Graph World Models for Constrained Epidemic Policy Planning

author.name: Yiqi Su, Rashed Shelim, Lingyi Wang, Walid Saad, Naren Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: EpiMind is a graph world model framework for epidemic policy planning across regions, combining a graph-factored recurrent state-space model for policy-conditioned rollouts with graph-temporal ADMM optimization enforcing per-period resource feasibility. It reduces admission RMSE by 29% relative to baselines.

entry.title: Relational Compression: A Framework for Relational Fidelity in Constrained Representations

author.name: Yaniv Shulman

entry.summary: Formulates relational compression, asking what compressed representations should preserve when relationships among elements carry the information of interest. Provides a common source-description-reconstruction interface unifying graph summarization, spectral sparsification, similarity-preserving representations, and relational distillation while keeping their differing assumptions explicit.

entry.title: Representation Editing for Multimodal Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Longfei Huang, Xiangyu Wu, Yang Yang

entry.summary: FIRE (FourIer Representation Editor) is a multimodal test-time adaptation method that directly edits semantically rich intermediate representations to correct modality misalignment under distribution shift, rather than updating fusion weights in place. This representation-engineering perspective gives explicit control over intermediate misalignment, a key driver of performance drop. It targets online adaptation of pretrained multimodal models on unlabeled test data.

entry.title: DimPO: Dimensionality Reduction for Attention using Preference Optimization

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Lanz, Yufei Cui, Prasanna Parthasarathi

entry.summary: DimPO learns per-layer linear projections of query and key vectors for a frozen language model using listwise preference optimization over keys plus a top-k cross-entropy term, instead of KL-matching the full attention distribution. Evaluated across LLaMA and Qwen models, it targets long-context settings where reducing KV dimension without updating the base model matters.

entry.title: HamiFormer: Dual-Expert Diffusion Fields with Affine Symplectic Maps

author.name: Haoxiang Huang, Xiang Liu, Shuwei Wang, Jingheng Ma, Sen Cui

entry.summary: HamiFormer combines whole-window diffusion denoising with residual-corrected Hamiltonian propagation to predict smooth dynamics and abrupt collisions. Its Parallel Local Affine Scan amortizes refinement across rectified-flow steps using affine symplectic maps that achieve lower solver error and runtime than explicit Euler, with a regime model tree specializing residual routing.

entry.title: Predicting the Next State Is Not Enough: JEPA Representations for Lean Theorem Proving

author.name: Aarnav Choudhary

entry.summary: The paper tests whether one-step Lean transition prediction provides a useful self-supervised signal for ordering proof-search branches. A JEPA-style model beats matched InfoNCE on same-theorem successor ranking (50.18% vs 31.55% Top-1) yet solves fewer theorems than simple proposer ordering (282 vs 308 of 987), showing accurate one-step ranking is insufficient as a long-horizon search value.

entry.title: The cost of useful natural gradient updates

author.name: Subhransu S. Bhattacharjee, Dylan Campbell, Rahul Shome

entry.summary: This theory paper asks what information suffices to turn a natural-gradient direction into a useful finite update under a population KL budget, constructing a four-state exponential family where identical gradients and Fisher information yield disjoint useful-step sets. It derives a worst-case sample complexity of Theta(log(1/delta)/(p*eps^2)) for small epsilon.

entry.title: Pulseflow: PPG Counterfactual Generation Via Latent Transport

author.name: Hung Manh Pham, Dong Ma, Bin Zhu, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: PulseFlow is a source-conditioned counterfactual generative model for photoplethysmography that explicitly models how an observed source recording transforms into a target condition (e.g., atrial fibrillation) via latent transport, enabling augmentation from abundant source cohorts. This addresses the scarcity of labeled AF recordings for model adaptation.

entry.title: T-MoXAI: A Hierarchical Explainability Framework for Temporal Multimodal Data

author.name: Ali Inha, Mo Vali, Saaliha Vali, Pietro Li\`o, Meen-Yau Thum

entry.summary: T-MoXAI is a hierarchical explainability framework for temporal multimodal models that explains when timepoints matter (temporal Shapley values), which modalities contribute (attention analysis), and what features drive decisions (gradient attribution), all computed in under one second. It is evaluated on real-world tasks including IVF treatment prediction in healthcare.

entry.title: HALO: Enhancing Time Series Generation via Hyperspherical Latents and Masked AutoregRessive Modeling

author.name: Chunyi Hou, Xiangfei Qiu, Hanyin Cheng, Yutong Li, Bin Yang

entry.summary: HALO improves time series generation by moving from discrete-latent two-stage pipelines to continuous hyperspherical latents with masked autoregressive modeling, avoiding discretization information loss and autoregressive error accumulation. It targets efficient autoregressive generation in a continuous latent space.

entry.title: Uniform Race: Parameter-Free Approximate Rejection Sampling

author.name: Seiyun Shin, Juhyeong Pang, Kwang-Sung Jun

entry.summary: Proposes uniform race (UR), a parameter-free approximate rejection sampling algorithm that attains the best known rejection-sampling guarantee without needing an acceptance threshold tuned to the target-proposal pair. It builds on importance weights and answers affirmatively whether optimal RS bounds can be achieved without hyperparameter input.

entry.title: Fast Learning Rate Transfer in Shallow Linear Networks at Growing Training Horizons

author.name: Mana Sakai, Masaaki Imaizumi

entry.summary: Studies hyperparameter (learning-rate) transfer across model width when the training horizon grows with width, building on the fast hyperparameter transfer framework. The authors prove fast transfer holds as n,T go to infinity when T = o(sqrt(n)) and characterize transfer rates under spectral assumptions in shallow linear networks. This extends the theory of tuning-cost reduction for large networks to a previously open regime.

entry.title: THEIA: A Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Vision-Language Analysis of Layout

author.name: Giuseppe Chiari, Michele Piccoli, Federico Viola, Davide Zoni

entry.summary: Introduces THEIA, a dataset of thousands of analog IC layout images (from GDSII files) paired with question-answer conversations, plus a benchmark using a fine-tuned vision-language model for layout analysis. It provides community infrastructure for AI-assisted EDA research. It complements the companion Inspector tool from the same group.

entry.title: SymbolicArena: A Unified Infrastructure for Benchmark Distillation and Dynamic Evaluation in Symbolic Regression

author.name: Ziwen Zhang, Xiju Wu, Yuheng Jing, Runxiang Wang, Boxiao Wang, Yifan Zang, Yifan Zhang, Yang Wang, Kai Li, Yifan Zhang, Huilin Xu, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: SymbolicArena standardizes 664 heterogeneous symbolic regression tasks with executable ground truth and distills them into Core50, a validated 50-task benchmark preserving task coverage and algorithm discrimination. The infrastructure supports dynamic evaluation to balance benchmark cost against validity.

entry.title: NeuronSifter: Intervention Planning in CNS Microenvironments

author.name: Haowei Xu, Wanyi Fu, Hongbin Han, Zhaoheng Xie

entry.summary: Treats intervention planning for central nervous system therapeutics as an interface design problem, compiling drug regimens into state-conditional target-occupancy fields with support masks rather than collapsing them to scalar exposures. NeuronSifter propagates joint uncertainty through microenvironment dynamics to select measurements that would change decisions. Companion work to NeuronDiscover from the same group, focused on pharmacological intervention planning.

entry.title: One Proposal for Every Margin: Zero-Shot Amortized Sequential Importance Sampling for Binary Matrices

author.name: Ruishuo Chen, Weijia Li, Xun Wang, Yu Chen, Leheng Cai, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: This work targets counting and uniform sampling of binary matrices with fixed row and column margins, important in ecology, psychometrics, and network analysis. The authors characterize the ideal zero-variance SIS proposal as a policy, train a neural amortized proposal zero-shot across margins, and produce unbiased count estimators that outperform analytic proposals.

entry.title: Learning Steadily: Accumulating Relative Point Margin Scores for Face Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Guray Ozgur, Tahar Chettaoui, Eduarda Caldeira, Marco Huber, Jan Niklas Kolf, Naser Damer, Fadi Boutros

entry.summary: Identifies temporal instability in FR-integrated face image quality assessment, where single-epoch quality estimates fluctuate as the feature space evolves during training. CARPM-FIQA accumulates relative point margin measurements (intra-class compactness over inter-class separation) across the whole training trajectory, with theoretical justification, to stabilize quality prediction.

entry.title: High-Probability Guarantees for SGD under $\beta$-Heavy-Tailed Gradient Noise

author.name: Qijun Tong, Masahiro Ikeda, Ryota Kawasumi

entry.summary: The paper relaxes bounded-noise and sub-Gaussian assumptions in high-probability SGD analyses by using Orlicz-space Young functions to model gradient noise tails, preserving finiteness of all polynomial moments while allowing tails heavier than sub-Weibull, including lognormal-type noise. This extends high-probability convergence guarantees for SGD to realistic heavy-tailed noise regimes observed in deep learning.

entry.title: The Price of Peeking: Anytime-Valid Leakage Detection on ML-KEM EM Traces

author.name: Georgios Feretzakis, Alexandros Papaspyridis

entry.summary: The paper proposes anytime-valid side-channel leakage detection based on testing by betting, using SKIT-type swap-pair e-processes that uniformly control false-alarm probability over time for ML-KEM electromagnetic traces. Compared to fixed-horizon Welch t-testing, first-crossing detection requires roughly 1.7-2.4x more traces at matched detection power. It quantifies the cost of monitoring leakage campaigns adaptively.

entry.title: GT-PSSM: Unified Probabilistic Framework for Stochastic Dynamics Modeling and Dependency Learning in Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Wonmo Koo, Jaeyeong Lee, Taeseong Yoon, Heeyoung Kim

entry.summary: GT-PSSM is a probabilistic framework for multivariate time series anomaly detection that models the stochastic nature of real-world series, avoiding unreliable purely error-based anomaly scores from deterministic reconstruction models. It unifies stochastic dynamics modeling with inter-variable dependency learning within a probabilistic state space formulation.

entry.title: Perceptual Quality Loss or Loss of Perceptual Quality?

author.name: Danilo de Oliveira, Tal Peer, Maur\'icio do V. M. da Costa, Timo Gerkmann

entry.summary: This study examines whether adding PESQ-based auxiliary loss terms actually improves perceived quality in deep speech enhancement models. Through objective and subjective experiments, the authors find that PESQ-optimized models gain PESQ scores but show little change on most other metrics, and PESQ loss can even hurt PESQ on mismatched conditions.

entry.title: Multi-Task Learning of Conditional Mean Operators: applications to dynamical systems and uncertainty quantification

author.name: Sami Chemlal, Thibaut Germain, R\'emi Flamary, Vladimir R. Kostic, Karim Lounici

entry.summary: The paper proposes learning multiple conditional mean operators jointly, positing that related CMOs share finite-dimensional input and output function spaces with task-specific specializations. This shared-structure approach improves estimation of conditional statistics for uncertainty quantification and dynamical systems analysis compared to estimating each operator independently.

entry.title: Context Spanning: A Communication Framework for Full-Duplex Speech Models and External LLM Backends

author.name: Seonghyeon Go, Yongwoo Kim, Hyeonjin Cha, Jaeho Shin

entry.summary: Proposes Context Spanning, a framework for injecting externally retrieved information in raw text form between full-duplex spoken dialogue models and external LLM backends in real time, avoiding the information loss caused by processing retrieval through compressed latent spaces. Enables real-time search and tool use for duplex speech models that otherwise remain trapped in parametric knowledge. Addresses a practical architectural gap in real-time spoken dialogue systems.

entry.title: LA-CPD: Local-Evidence-Aware Change-Point Detection for Human-LLM Authorship Segmentation

author.name: Qing Yang, Zhenyu Mao, Zixiang Luo, Zezheng Wu, Xinghe Cheng, Qinggang Zhang, Jingwei Zhang, Jiapu Wang

entry.summary: LA-CPD addresses localizing LLM-authored spans within human-LLM co-authored documents, a task relevant to copyright and fraud attribution. It converts noisy sentence-level detector scores into a coherent document partition via change-point detection when the number and locations of transitions are unknown. This structured approach reduces spurious boundaries caused by content-driven score fluctuations.

entry.title: SCBO: Semantically Coherent Batching and Ordering for LLM-Based Social Surveys

author.name: Yuanzi Li, Lingjie Wang, Zihang Tian, Lei Wang, Xu Chen

entry.summary: SCBO is a training-free framework for LLM-based survey simulation that batches multiple questions per prompt, selects shared references, and orders questions so later predictions can build on earlier answers. This reduces repeated context encoding and broadens the reference pool compared to one-question-per-prompt approaches.

entry.title: CLC-YOLO: A Compact Channel-Gated Prototype Network for Real-Time Leakage-Aware Breast Ultrasound Lesion Segmentation

author.name: M. Fazri Nizar, Muhammad Naufal Rachmatullah, Julian Supardi

entry.summary: Proposes Channel Local Contrast, a compact refinement of the YOLO26 segmentation prototype head using a fixed local high-pass residual controlled by 64 zero-initialized bounded channel gates. Evaluated across four breast ultrasound datasets with patient-disjoint or grouped splits, showing consistent Dice improvements of roughly 1-3 percentage points.

entry.title: SetOPD: From Few Visual Exemplars to Multimodal Candidate Sets for Remote-Sensing Open-Prompt Detection

author.name: Jinlong Hu, Yi Zhang, Zhiqi Xia, Yikang Zhou, Shunping Ji

entry.summary: Reframes open-prompt detection for remote sensing by treating few-shot visual exemplars as sets rather than compressing them into a single class-level embedding, preserving modality-specific decoding states from a shared prompt-conditioned initialization. This better exploits the visual modality when only a few heterogeneous exemplars are available.

entry.title: ABO-Med: Accelerated Bilevel Optimization for Few-Shot Medical Image Classification

author.name: Ruoxuan Shi, Sheng Yang, Zhengxing Su, Xiaoyang Hou, Yating Liu

entry.summary: ABO-Med instantiates a recently established first-order bilevel optimization paradigm within MAML for few-shot medical image classification, avoiding costly second-order computations for better scalability. It also introduces MedRAug, a modality-aware augmentation strategy tailored to medical imaging.

entry.title: Focus and Supplement: Dual-Enhanced Vision Transformer for Multi-Class Anomaly Classification

author.name: Xurui Li, Enjie Xu, Chenzhou Li, Shilei Zeng, Dayou Huang, Tianyi Ma, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes MACO, a multi-class anomaly classification framework for industrial vision that uses soft-focus attention guided by anomaly maps plus auxiliary classification tokens to learn comprehensive anomaly representations and dynamically estimate the unknown number of anomaly classes. It addresses noisy, incomplete anomaly representations without prior class counts. Industrial anomaly analysis is a practical, active application area.

entry.title: PSM: Dataset Distillation Based on Precise Statistical Matching by Difficulty

author.name: Hongxu Ma, Guang Li, Shijie Wang, Dongzhan Zhou, Suorong Yang, Baoli Sun, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama, Zhihui Wang

entry.summary: PSM improves decoupled dataset distillation by estimating per-image difficulty with a Global Precision Score and supervising distilled samples with difficulty-aware statistics rather than whole-dataset running averages. This better characterizes the difficulty structure of the original data and improves distillation quality.

entry.title: Multi-Scale Semantic Mapping in Urban Environments via Observation Calibration and Policy Dependence Regularization

author.name: Runling Long, Junhao Feng, Jia Wan

entry.summary: This paper targets semantic mapping for embodied navigation in urban settings, where objects range from pedestrians to buildings and viewing distances vary enormously, unlike the indoor settings most prior work assumes.
