It proposes observation calibration to handle scale/distance mismatch and policy dependence regularization to improve mapping robustness. This fills a real gap since most semantic mapping datasets and methods are indoor-focused.

entry.title: Mixed-Prior Decision Risk for Open-Set Recognition

author.name: L. A. Erlygin, P. D. Proskura, A. A. Zaytsev

entry.summary: This paper analyzes open-set recognition under three coexisting error types (false acceptance, false rejection, misidentification) and shows that KL-divergence-based uncertainty summaries in Bayesian gallery-aware models like HolUE are not generally monotone in decision risk, with linear fusion of KL components yielding negative filtering quality. It proposes uncertainty scoring grounded directly in mixed-prior decision risk. This is a corrective contribution to how selective recognition systems should rank uncertain probes.

entry.title: DrawingsDreamer: A Unified Multi-View Engineering Drawings Generation Model

author.name: Shurui Liu, Weide Chen, Changwang Yi, Ancong Wu

entry.summary: DrawingsDreamer is an LLM-driven framework that formulates multi-view vector-based engineering drawing (SVG) generation purely as sequence modeling with hierarchical postfix tokenization, avoiding raster image encoders. It targets the geometric fidelity and cross-view spatial alignment that artistic SVG generators lack, which is essential for industrial CAD. Applying sequence modeling to engineering-grade vector graphics is a useful niche bridge between generative AI and CAD.

entry.title: Reliability-Gated Fusion of Consumer Head and Foot IMUs for Lower-Body 3D Pose

author.name: Zhilin Guo, Boqiao Zhang, Oszk\'ar Urb\'an, Josef Bengtson, Hakan Aktas, Wenzhao Li, Siyu Hong, Kyle Fogarty, Chenliang Zhou, Ali Senguel, Cengiz Oztireli

entry.summary: The paper studies camera-free motion capture from consumer devices (an earbud head IMU plus two smart-insole foot IMUs), showing that reliability problems are channel-level — foot acceleration is the most informative input while firmware-fused foot orientation degrades results. It introduces per-stream, per-channel temporal gates that let the model learn trust levels, evaluated on a new 35-take benchmark with SAM-3D-Body pseudo-ground-truth.

entry.title: Path Planning with Motion Primitives in Dynamic Environments: SIPP on Lattices

author.name: Marat Agranovskiy

entry.summary: This paper adapts Safe Interval Path Planning (SIPP) to operate on state lattices with precomputed kinodynamically smooth motion primitives, addressing the kinodynamic sub-optimality of grid-based stop-and-turn planners in dynamic environments. Moving obstacle swept volumes are rasterized onto the spatiotemporal grid for efficient collision handling.

entry.title: Traceable Human-to-Humanoid Sign Language Benchmarking

author.name: Ao Liu, Shengeng Tang, Lechao Cheng, Yanbin Hao, Bingkun Bao, Richang Hong

entry.summary: The paper introduces HumanoidCSL-20K, a benchmark of 20,648 sentence-level Chinese Sign Language sequences with four aligned versions (source video, repaired human motion, direct robot reference, geometry-repaired robot reference), enabling provenance tracking of errors across the retargeting pipeline. It targets the costly and poorly-scaling sign data collection problem for humanoid signing. It matters as a reusable, diagnostic resource for human-to-humanoid motion transfer.

entry.title: ReSync: Re-Aligning the Two Clocks of Asynchronous World-Action Models

author.name: Xi Lin, Feihong Zhang, Yulong Shi, Yanghong Mei, Zuxing Lu, Xiaofan Zhu, Zihao Liang, Zhirui Gao, Zhaowen Li

entry.summary: ReSync formalizes the asynchronous denoising schedules of joint video-action world models as a two-clock inference problem, introducing the commitment-evidence gap, a quantity readable from the model's own sampling schedule that predicts when an executable action outruns its justifying future prediction. This diagnostic framing of when actions commit before evidence is a sharp conceptual contribution to world-action model inference. It matters for reliable real-time deployment of such models.

entry.title: CSI-Agent: LLM-Assisted Few-Shot Adaptation for Cross-Domain Wi-Fi CSI Sensing

author.name: Tianya Zhao, Chuan Liu, Xuyu Wang

entry.summary: CSI-Agent reformulates cross-domain Wi-Fi CSI sensing adaptation as a deployment-time decision-making problem handled by an evidence-seeking LLM agent, selecting adaptation strategies per class under scarce labels rather than applying one fixed offline method. This addresses brittleness of sensing models when users or environments change. It exemplifies a pattern of using LLMs as reasoning controllers over sensing pipelines rather than signal classifiers.

entry.title: Porimon: An LLM-Based Pok\'emon Battle Agent Enhanced by Long/Short-Term Knowledge Augmented Generation

author.name: Dongyin Zhuo, Fengjunjie Pan, Nenad Petrovic, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: Using Pokemon battles as a testbed, this paper studies how to improve LLM agents in opponent-aware planning without fine-tuning. It proposes LSTKAG (Long/Short-Term Knowledge Augmented Generation), which lets an agent use past states of the current task and retrieve experience summaries from similar prior task instances, and evaluates the resulting Porimon agent over 15,000 tournament battles with an external API for precise damage calculation. The domain is a game, but the memory and experience-retrieval mechanism is relevant to general agent planning.

entry.title: Prediction Limits and Koopman Closure of Geometry-Induced Soft State Abstractions

author.name: Mohit Kumar, Somayeh Kargaran

entry.summary: Analyzes when simplex-valued soft state abstractions admit accurate finite-dimensional linear dynamics, deriving a computable lower confidence bound on minimum prediction error over matrices under a spectral-norm constraint. The bound combines within-class variation with deviation of soft coordinates from one-hot labels and requires no fitted prediction matrix. It connects state abstraction geometry to Koopman-style linear closure theory.

entry.title: Action Shaping: Policies Absorb What They Can Express

author.name: Yanjun Chen, Jinghan Wang, Xiaoyu Shen, Wenjie Li, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes action shaping — adding a training-time action offset that is dropped at deployment — as an analogue of potential-based reward shaping, and proves a principle stating that offsets expressible by the policy's own output layer can be removed without changing returns. Its minimal instance is a zero-initialized gated linear head behind an actor trained with a learned action-value function. This gives a theoretical guarantee previously missing for the action channel.

entry.title: Forecasting Intraday USD/CAD Exchange Rate with News-Derived Monetary-Policy Signals

author.name: Maya Kodeih, Aliaa Alnaggar, Mucahit Cevik

entry.summary: This paper builds an intraday forecasting model for the USD/CAD exchange rate that converts unstructured central-bank communication and monetary-policy news into quantitative signals. Its main contribution is a statistical attribution methodology that decomposes monetary-policy communication into interpretable channels, allowing the authors to identify which dimensions of central-bank messaging actually drive forecasting improvements rather than just measuring aggregate gains.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Counterfactual Fragility and Demographic Bias in Clinical Evaluation of LLMs

author.name: Chaitai Deb Purkayastha, Bharath Kumar Bolla, Vishnu Surya Reddy Nandi

entry.summary: This evaluation study tests six LLMs on 150 MedQA USMLE questions using counterfactual validity (minimal plausible clinical changes) and demographic-robustness perturbations. Only 25.3 percent of 900 counterfactual attempts were valid, and 20.3 percent of 5,400 demographic comparisons changed answers, revealing fragility and demographic sensitivity that accuracy metrics miss. The findings caution against relying on exam accuracy alone for clinical LLM deployment decisions.

entry.title: Rank Collapse Is Recoverable, Growing $|Q|$ Is Not: Out-of-Sample Early Warning for Value Divergence in High-UTD Soft Actor-Critic

author.name: Tianqi Bu, YuXuan Peng, Junteng Tu, Henghui Xiao

entry.summary: The paper disentangles two components of plasticity loss in high update-to-data (UTD) Soft Actor-Critic: representation collapse (rank collapse), which is shown to be survivable — critics with most units dormant at UTD 16 keep learning — and growing value magnitude |Q|, which precedes divergence. Early |Q| growth by step 15k ranks runs by how soon a training guard flags them, enabling out-of-sample early warning of value divergence. This provides an actionable diagnostic for high-UTD RL instability.

entry.title: Structure-Mapping-Guided Self-Explanation for Learning Mathematical Procedures

author.name: Shinhaeng Lee, Christopher J. MacLellan, Daniel Weitekamp

entry.summary: This work offers a computational account of self-explanation from worked examples, using structure mapping over typed relational structures to anchor abductive search toward structurally corresponding explanations, drastically reducing the search that naive simulation faces (thousands of spurious numerical explanations). It grounds in cognitive-science theory (structure mapping) to model how learners infer the procedures behind demonstrated steps. It matters as a cognitively plausible model of procedural learning from examples.

entry.title: Cross-modal Translation via Conditional Latent Denoising for Video Deepfake Detection

author.name: Xinzhe Li, Youzhi Tu, Kong Aik Lee

entry.summary: CTCLD improves video deepfake detection by exploiting intrinsic audio-visual dependencies, connecting heterogeneous modality distributions in latent space via a Bayesian formulation and conditional latent denoising for cross-domain information transfer. Rather than treating audio and visual signals as independent indicators, it uses their correspondences as detection cues. This addresses a growing security threat with a multimodal approach.

entry.title: When Does the Concept of "Dog" Emerge in an Audio LLM?

author.name: Zhe Wang, Shiqi Liu, Ruiyun Zhong, Tiechong Zhu, Yihua Tan

entry.summary: Using Jacobian lens readout and directional interventions on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, the authors define a dog direction in hidden states, show dog-related information is decodable without prompt cues, and that adding or removing this component modulates response tendencies and some final answers, with effects concentrated in late layers before generation. The study covers species classification and vocalization judgments. It offers mechanistic insight into how audio LLMs represent semantics.

entry.title: EAT: Expert Account Tracker for Efficient MoE Inference

author.name: Yuexian Li, Yifei Yang, Zouying Cao, Hai Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces EAT, which uses history-aware per-expert performance metrics and adaptive thresholding to dynamically select only the most important activated experts in mixture-of-experts models, reducing compute while preserving performance. It outperforms the existing Top-P expert-selection baseline across multiple models.

entry.title: RSD-Poker: Structure-Adaptive and Shift-Robust Risk-Utility Certification for Residual Policies in Imperfect-Information Games

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Peng Zhang, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces RSD-Poker, a certification framework for residual policy adaptation in imperfect-information games that learns a policy-visible partition on a separate structure split and provides weighted simultaneous upper certificates for risk and lower certificates for utility, remaining robust to deployment-distribution shifts. This addresses heterogeneity hidden by shared scales and fixed subgroups.

entry.title: Jev in Medicine: A Benchmark Evaluation. Preliminary Results

author.name: Alfredo Madrid-Garc\'ia, Beatriz Merino-Barbancho

entry.summary: This preliminary benchmark evaluates Jev 1.13, a non-generative System One model that assigns probabilities to fixed answer options, against GPT-6 Sol (released 2026-09-22) on four medical benchmarks including MetaMedQA and NEJM Case Challenges, measuring accuracy, calibration, selective prediction, and unanswerable-question recognition across 8,469 requests. Jev matched GPT-6 Sol on PubMedQA but trailed elsewhere.

entry.title: PainterBench: A Figural Divergent-Thinking Benchmark for Tool-Using Language Models

author.name: Shane K. A. Dalumura Hettige, Jonas Oppenlaender

entry.summary: PainterBench ports the human incomplete-drawing creativity task to agentic settings, where LLM agents draw via tool calls on a canvas containing an unerasable starting shape and decide when the open-ended drawing is complete. It tests incremental visual planning and transfer of creative ability from pretraining to multi-turn tool use.

entry.title: PairPref: When Should Memory Guide the Answer? A Benchmark for Contextual Preference Use

author.name: Mingfei Lu, Mengjia Wu, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: PairPref is a benchmark testing whether memory-augmented assistants apply retrieved user preferences only when contextually appropriate. Pairs of situations keep the preference and request fixed while changing applicability, with selection and free-generation tracks. This targets an overlooked gap between memory retrieval and correct preference application.

entry.title: ResonAct: Streaming Metrics for Runtime Diagnosis and Self-Healing in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Tarun Chintada, Neelamadhav Gantayat, Ishaan Romil, Renuka Sindhgatta, Soujanya Soni, Sameep Mehta

entry.summary: ResonAct is a runtime self-healing framework for enterprise multi-agent systems that ingests execution traces and interactions as streaming operational metrics to continuously monitor, diagnose, and remediate failures from tool degradation, context propagation errors, and coordination breakdowns — moving remediation from post-hoc to during execution.

entry.title: STRIDE: Automated Evaluation of Text-to-Trajectory Alignment across Diverse Contexts

author.name: Wanchun Ni, Tao Qi, Leonel Aguilar, Jiugeng Sun, Marlene Wagner, Verena Zimmermann, Mennatallah El-Assady

entry.summary: Proposes STRIDE, the first framework for evaluating context alignment between scenario descriptions and generated pedestrian trajectories, addressing the impracticality of collecting real human trajectories for every scenario. It argues existing pedestrian metrics do not transfer to text-to-trajectory generation and provides context-dependent evaluation without ground-truth data.

entry.title: AUV-Bench: Aesthetic Understanding and Generation Evaluation for User Interfaces

author.name: Zhijie Deng, Ling Li, Junhao Ji, Siwei Lyu, Zhipeng Xu, Zulong Chen, Rongyao Fang, Shuai Bai, Xuming Hu, Jiaheng Wei

entry.summary: Introduces AUV-Bench, a benchmark testing whether multimodal foundation models connect aesthetic judgment of user interfaces with design actions like diagnosis, repair, and creation, grounded in professional design principles. It argues existing evaluations assess these abilities in isolation, hiding whether task success reflects shared aesthetic understanding.

entry.title: AX is the New AEO

author.name: Ido Finder, Assaf Elovic, Gad Shalev

entry.summary: This position paper argues that answer-engine optimization (AEO) is giving way to agent experience (AX): as AI agents fetch and read business websites during multi-round search, the deciding factor for being recommended is whether agents can effectively access and parse the site itself. It reframes web optimization advice for the agentic search era. The thesis is timely given the shift from retrieval-augmented answers to autonomous agent workflows.

entry.title: Safe Greenhouse Climate Control Using Lagrangian-Constrained PPO with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Hangzun Liu, Yuling Fan, Fang Tian, Zhilong Bie, Zaiwen Feng, Yongliang Qiao

entry.summary: The paper frames greenhouse climate regulation as a Constrained MDP and applies a Lagrangian safe-RL framework (RCPO-PPO) with Kolmogorov-Arnold networks to separate economic optimization from cumulative climate-constraint satisfaction. This avoids the brittleness of fixed reward penalties, which either make policies overly conservative or permit persistent deviations harming crops. It demonstrates safe RL applied to a concrete agricultural control problem.

entry.title: Training-Free Clinical Reasoning through Medical Ontologies and Cognitive Mapping: A Symbolic-Probabilistic Knowledge Graph Framework

author.name: Surajit Das

entry.summary: CKG Reasoner is a training-free diagnostic paradigm mapping patient observations onto explicit medical knowledge via a symbolic-probabilistic knowledge graph, with evidence feature nodes, bounded information gating, knowledge-weighted evidence accumulation, and missing-aware normalization distinguishing absent from unavailable evidence. Candidate ranking is decoupled from clustering over derived evidence coordinates.

entry.title: A.D.A.M.O. (Agent for language-Driven Actions with Multimodal Observations): A Visual-Symbolic Framework for Virtual Humans

author.name: Alessandro Emmanuel Pecora, Stefano Calzolari, Francesco Strada, Andrea Bottino

entry.summary: A.D.A.M.O. is a visual-symbolic framework for language-driven virtual humans that uses a pretrained vision-language model with tool calling to unify perception, reasoning, and action in one control loop, grounded by a dual visual-symbolic world model in interactive 3D environments. It also introduces a diagnostic evaluation setup. It matters as a systems contribution for embodied virtual agents, though it builds largely on existing VLM capabilities rather than new modeling techniques.

entry.title: Source-preserving alignment for robust evidence localization in scientific PDFS

author.name: Zihao Liu, Wei Yang, Zixiao Dong, Chenshu Li, Longzhang Liu, Tao Tan, Hong Xie

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework for locating extracted evidence strings within the original scientific PDF despite representation mismatches like line wrapping, Unicode variants, superscripts, and citation markers, by normalizing text for robust matching while preserving provenance for accurate localization, with line-break-aware token alignment as a fallback. It matters because evidence grounding in source documents is a prerequisite for trustworthy scientific information extraction systems.

entry.title: Measure Learning at Steady State: A BIRD-SQL Formula 1 Case Study

author.name: Manoj Bajaj

entry.summary: The paper critiques continual-learning benchmarks that score short-horizon gains, instead scoring in-context learning as one memory system over a long shared-world schedule on BIRD-SQL Formula 1 questions using gpt-5.6-luna, an existing model. It decomposes steady-state learning into exploration efficiency, task reward, and delivery cost, finding late SQL probes fall from 4.6-5.6 to 0.95 while ICL context grows to roughly 95k tokens with cost roughly doubling. Short-horizon scoring understates late savings and misses the cost inversion.

entry.title: STAR: Adaptive Spatial-Temporal Normalization for Unified Microservice Incident Management

author.name: Xinhua Miao, Linyu Zhu, Bowei Yang, Zhengong Cai

entry.summary: STAR is a self-supervised representation-learning framework for microservice observability data (metrics, logs, traces) that unifies anomaly detection, failure triage, and root cause localization. It introduces Temporal Adaptive Normalization for non-stationary time series and a coupled spatial mechanism for heterogeneous service dependency structures. The work targets robust incident management at large scale.

entry.title: Age-Adaptive Handwriting Reconstruction from an IMU-Based Digital Pen through Shared Representations and Domain-Specific Heads

author.name: Florent Imbert (LUT), Yann Soullard (IRISA, UR2, SHADOC), Eric Anquetil (INSA Rennes, IRISA, SHADOC), Hui Han (LUT)

entry.summary: The paper tackles handwriting reconstruction from IMU-sensing digital pens, where signal variability between adults and children degrades reconstruction quality. It proposes shared representations with age-specific heads to handle this domain shift, motivated by classroom handwriting acquisition support. The approach is relevant to human-computer interaction and educational technology.

entry.title: PRIME-ANC: Path-Ratio-Informed Modeling for Efficient Neural Filter Synthesis in Active Noise Control

author.name: Yaokun Huang, Chunyang Xu, Haowen Hua, Sen Lin, Shichao Hu, Mengyao Zhu

entry.summary: PRIME-ANC is a shared neural synthesizer that learns bounded, path-dependent log-magnitude corrections to a regularized path-ratio base for active noise control filter design, producing FIR filters via minimum-phase reconstruction. It achieves strong held-out noise reductions (about 18 dB) across ten dataset splits and improves 7.89 dB over the base method on earphone measurements. The work advances neural approaches to adaptive acoustic filtering.

entry.title: CueKFS: Agentic Cue-Driven Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Weitai Kang, Hanieh Deilamsalehy, Yumo Xu, Dewang Sultania, Serdar Cellat, Yan Yan

entry.summary: CueKFS is a training-free agentic method for question-conditioned keyframe selection in long-video QA, addressing the problem that question-similarity ranking fails when relevant information is distributed across frames or implicit. It uses cue-driven agentic search rather than static question decomposition, which suffers from inaccurate decomposition due to fixed initial context. The work targets a concrete bottleneck in long-video understanding and offers a practical training-free solution.

entry.title: Interactive Distributionally Robust Multi-Agent Learning with General Function Approximation

author.name: Debamita Ghosh, George K. Atia, Yue Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies online learning in general-sum distributionally robust Markov games with general function approximation and phi-divergence uncertainty sets, addressing model misspecification amplified by strategic multi-agent interactions. It proposes RoMEX-phi, a model-free framework combining equilibrium-based exploration with dual fitted learning via a functional dual representation of the robust multi-agent Bellman operator. This advances theoretical tools for robust multi-agent reinforcement learning in large state and joint action spaces.

entry.title: Tracing Decoder Artifacts for Compact Synthetic Speech Screening

author.name: Yi Chen Liu, Jian Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight front-end screening system for synthetic-speech detection that exploits predictable spectral artifacts introduced by learned upsampling and inverse STFT synthesis in vocoders. Rather than replacing expensive high-accuracy detectors, the compact screen cheaply processes all recordings and forwards only suspicious ones for deeper analysis. This is a practical cascade approach to scaling deepfake-speech defense.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Selection of Online Algorithms with Simulator Ensembles

author.name: Yongyi Guo, Zifan Xu, Ziping Xu, Kelly W. Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies how to select online RL algorithms when design choices affecting exploration must be validated in a simulator fitted to limited offline data. Rather than the naive plug-in rule of picking the best algorithm on a single fitted simulator, it proposes uncertainty-aware selection using an ensemble of simulators, e.g., via bootstrap resampling, choosing the algorithm with the best average ensemble performance. This addresses reliability of algorithm selection under limited offline data.

entry.title: Supporting and Performing Culture from the Inside

author.name: Lea Frermann, Steven Bird

entry.summary: This paper applies the anthropology distinction between emic (insider) and etic (outsider) perspectives to systematically analyze assumptions across the NLP-for-culture research pipeline, from task selection through data collection, system design, and evaluation. It critiques the internal culture of NLP itself and proposes pathways toward more culturally attuned AI. It matters as a reflective methodological contribution to culturally-aware NLP.

entry.title: Measurement Boundaries in LLM Financial Agent Evaluation: Fixed-Tape Execution and Multi-Defect Auditing

author.name: Weicheng Xue

entry.summary: This methodological study examines what controls are needed to interpret LLM financial agent evaluations, showing that comparing independent runs under different execution rules conflates execution effects with fresh model responses, with parsed decision paths agreeing in only 19.8 percent of 450 pairs. Replaying stored response tapes through both execution conditions isolates the effect, finding stressed execution changes total return by about 10.4 percent of the idealized baseline. It provides a careful auditing template for agent evaluation in finance.

entry.title: De-biasing Skeleton-based Action Recognition with Convex Hull Adaptive Shift

author.name: Mengyuan Liu, Yuhang Wen, Yi Zhang, Songtao Wu, Hong Liu, Junsong Yuan, Beichen Ding

entry.summary: The paper identifies entity bias in skeleton-based action and interaction recognition, tracing it to the choice of origin in the world coordinate system, which violates the i.i.d. assumption behind weight-shared entity encoders. It proposes a Convex Hull Adaptive Shift to remove this bias, improving recognition across bodies, hands, objects, and robots. The diagnosis of a coordinate-system-induced bias is a concrete, actionable insight for the field.

entry.title: Radiomap Blind Prediction under Incomplete Observation: Error Characterization and Correctable Propagation-Prior Learning

author.name: Xiaojie Li, Yu Han, Han Fang, Shangqing Liu, Guangxu Zhu, Shi Jin, Chao-Kai Wen

entry.summary: The paper establishes a population-level theory for radio map blind prediction under incomplete observation, identifying the conditional mean as the optimal target and separating prediction error into reducible approximation error and irreducible uncertainty from missing physical information. It characterizes the train-test risk gap and proposes a correctable propagation-prior learning framework. This provides a principled foundation for wireless environment modeling.

entry.title: Efficient Message Passing for Partial Differential Equation Priors

author.name: Anna Kazachkova, Leonhard Hennicke, Rainer Schlosser, Ralf Herbrich

entry.summary: The authors propose solving PDEs via probabilistic inference on factor graphs, where a governing PDE encodes prior knowledge as explicit factors and observed data shapes the parameter posterior. Approximate inference is performed with moment-matching message passing, avoiding posterior sampling or global gradient-based optimization. The approach is demonstrated on first-order advection and second-order semi-linear Fisher-KPP equations.

entry.title: Environmental Impact of Generative and Agentic AI: An in-Depth Analysis and Green Solutions

author.name: Abderaouf Bahi, Amel Ourici, Ibtissem Gasmi

entry.summary: The paper surveys the environmental footprint of generative and agentic AI across energy, carbon, water, and e-waste over the full lifecycle of LLMs, multimodal models, and agentic workflows, contributing a lifecycle taxonomy and order-of-magnitude estimates based on published data. It proposes green solutions for each stage. Importantly, it is a conceptual analysis without original measurements.

entry.title: MedRouter: Demystifying Knowledge Differences Across Medical LLMs for Routing-Based Reasoning

author.name: Lang Cao, Binghang Lu, Yuhao Shen, Yue Guo

entry.summary: Introduces MedRouter, an agentic system using an embedding-based multi-label router to select specialist medical LLMs whose responses feed a generator for final answers, exploiting heterogeneity in specialist competence rather than only balancing quality and cost. Also proposes SCALE to analyze specialist knowledge differences across medical domains.

entry.title: BERT4DTI : BERT-based Model for Predicting Drug-Protein Interactions

author.name: Thanina Hamitouch, Khadidja Henni, Abdelkrim Arie, Amina Selma Haichour, Neila Mezghani, Lina Abou-Abbas

entry.summary: BERT4DTI predicts drug-protein interactions by encoding SMILES with ChemBERTa and protein sequences with ProtBERT, applying bidirectional mutual attention between the two representations before classification. It targets practical limitations of DTI models: scarce labels, costly fine-tuning of large encoders, and lack of pair-specific interaction modeling. Relevant to drug discovery and repurposing pipelines.

entry.title: AutoHGNN: Robust and Efficient Neural Architecture Search for Hypergraph Neural Networks

author.name: Sirui Li, Pietro Li\`o b, Xinsheng Li, Baisong Liu, Chengbin Peng

entry.summary: AutoHGNN is a neural architecture search framework for hypergraph neural networks, introducing a Hyper-Interaction Module in the search space and a Hypergraph Stable Topological Distance criterion for architecture selection. It automates the design of higher-order relational architectures where manual crafting is labor-intensive and often inadequate. This targets robustness and efficiency in hypergraph learning.

entry.title: A Light Bilevel Refinement Aligns Self-Supervised Representations for Stronger Task-Specific Learning

author.name: Gustav Wagner Zakarias, Zheng-Hua Tan

entry.summary: The paper improves on the BiSSL framework for aligning self-supervised representations with downstream tasks by replacing costly implicit hypergradient approximations in bilevel optimization with a lighter refinement procedure. This makes the transitional alignment stage more scalable while retaining performance benefits.

entry.title: Compressing Value Predictions for Learning-Augmented Metrical Task Systems

author.name: Sizhe Li, Yecheng Li, Kun He

entry.summary: This algorithms paper studies learning-augmented metrical task systems where predictions of dual values are available only at m landmark states, reconstructed elsewhere via a Lipschitz extension. It derives additive excess cost bounds in terms of the landmark covering radius and prediction error, showing compressed predictions retain algorithmic value.

entry.title: When Noise Meets Long-Tail: Feature-Threshold Dual Calibration for Robust Pseudo-Labeling

author.name: Ping Guo, Zhiqi Huang, Xinran Li

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why pseudo-labeling in semantic segmentation collapses when imaging noise and long-tailed class distributions co-occur, tracing a vicious cycle where noise lowers confidence and fixed thresholds systematically filter out tail classes. It proposes a dual calibration of features and thresholds to break this cycle. This is a practical robustness fix for real-world semi-supervised segmentation.

entry.title: SR4-Fit: A Unified Interpretable Rule-Based Machine Learning Framework for Informative and Trustworthy Decision-Making

author.name: Shyam Sundar Murali Krishnan, Dean Frederick Hougen

entry.summary: SR4-Fit extends RuleFit-style approaches with sparse relaxed regularized regression to produce intrinsically interpretable rule-based models for classification and regression, aiming to close the gap between transparency and predictive performance in high-stakes applications. It argues against reliance on post hoc explanations that do not reflect a model's actual computations. The contribution is a more stable, stronger rule-based alternative to trees and RuleFit.

entry.title: WhiteCon: Semi-Supervised Domain Adaptation Regression Through Whitening Transform and Dual Consistency

author.name: Se Jin Sim, Seoung Bum Kim

entry.summary: WhiteCon tackles semi-supervised domain adaptation for regression, an underexplored setting compared to classification, by combining domain-specific whitening transforms with dual consistency regularization. The whitening transform reduces model parameter variance while consistency regularization stabilizes training under distribution shift with limited labeled target data. Useful for industrial and scientific regression tasks where labeled target-domain data is scarce.

entry.title: AlphaPareto: Formulaic Alpha Discovery with LLM-Guided Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yingbo Zhao, Zeyu Yang, Zhoufan Zhu

entry.summary: AlphaPareto formulates formulaic alpha discovery for quantitative trading as multi-objective RL, augmenting the state with the evolving alpha pool to handle non-stationary rewards and optimizing pool-level properties beyond single-factor predictive power, with LLM guidance. It addresses the underexplored problem of finding alphas that work well together rather than individually. Niche but technically interesting application of RL and LLMs to finance.

entry.title: SkillPE: Creativity-Oriented Cinematic Skill Evolution for Text-to-Video Prompt Engineering

author.name: Yanwei Huang, Mingxuan Zhu, Shujie Li, Shiyuan Liu, Yuanxing Zhang, Arpit Narechania

entry.summary: SkillPE evolves reusable cinematic skills from expert seed prompts for text-to-video generation, encoding shot logic, composition, lighting, and sound design in fine-grained format. It retrieves movie references as resonators, dissonants, and divergents, with the latter inspiring creative alternatives while preserving user intent. The work targets helping non-experts achieve professional-quality video generations.

entry.title: GenNVS: Geometry-enhanced Novel View Synthesis via Disentangled 3D Prior

author.name: Yajiao Xiong, Youyu Luan, Xiaoyu Zhou, Yongtao Wang

entry.summary: GenNVS addresses single-image novel view synthesis by modeling foreground objects and background with 3D Gaussian Splatting aligned through coarse-to-fine geometric optimization, conditioning a video diffusion model via a Dual-Stream Masking mechanism. This preserves geometric structure and spatial coherence of foreground objects better than pure diffusion approaches. It combines explicit 3D priors with generative synthesis.

entry.title: Predictive Dual Smoothing for Column Generation

author.name: Senne Berden, Noah Schutte, Andrea Lodi, Tias Guns

entry.summary: The authors propose a predictive dual smoothing method for column generation in large-scale linear programming, addressing oscillations in dual solutions that slow the pricing subproblem. Unlike classical smoothing that averages past duals, the method uses predictive stabilization to avoid the drawback of lagging behind current duals.

entry.title: Drug-Target Interaction Prediction via Hierarchical Sequential Cross-Attention over Chemical and Protein Language Models

author.name: Khadidja Henni, Hamza Abdelali, Abdelkrim Aries, Neila Mezghani, Brigitte Vannier, Sara Magdouli, Lina Abou-Abbas

entry.summary: Combines two pre-trained language models, ChemBERTa for drug SMILES strings and ESM-2 for protein sequences, with hierarchical sequential cross-attention to explicitly model cross-molecular dependencies for drug-target interaction prediction. The approach improves over late-fusion baselines that process drugs and proteins independently.

entry.title: CTP-FL: Common-Trajectory Gradient Prediction for Federated Learning

author.name: Junkang Liu

entry.summary: CTP-FL proposes a federated learning scheme where clients evaluate the global objective along a shared predicted trajectory rather than advancing independent local models. This makes aggregated updates interpretable as gradients of the global objective even under heterogeneous data.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Automated Cross-Domain Machine Learning Task Type Identification: A Benchmark Dataset and Evaluation

author.name: Petros Tsialis, Steffen Limmer, Tobias Rodemann, Martin Heckmann

entry.summary: The authors evaluate whether LLMs can infer data domain and downstream prediction task from dataset-level information given only a target feature, releasing a 625-dataset annotated benchmark spanning tabular and time-series data. Evaluation covers comparison with AutoML heuristics, cross-domain settings, and deployment with smaller local models.

entry.title: AutoRef: Harness Optimization for Agentic Multi-Reference Image Generation

author.name: Yuta Oshima, Ku Onoda, Yusuke Iwasawa, Masahiro Suzuki, Yutaka Matsuo, Hiroki Furuta

entry.summary: AutoRef optimizes harnesses for image generation agents that combine generation models, reasoning models, and executable scaffolds for multi-reference image composition. It addresses failure modes like missing or duplicated subjects and unnatural pasting by optimizing how references are interpreted, generation is executed, and outputs are diagnosed and selected.

entry.title: Cross-Material Support Transfer for Core-Loss Prediction Under Waveform Covariate Shift

author.name: Cong Yao, Chunye Gong

entry.summary: Analyzes the MagNet Challenge case where magnetic core loss models must generalize from sinusoidal training waveforms to trapezoidal and PWM excitation, showing material D suffers a 15.9% p95 error due to missing information under covariate shift rather than model inadequacy. Proposes cross-material support transfer to address the characterization-deployment mismatch.

entry.title: Simple Extensions of Single-Objective Acquisition Functions and Hedge Strategies for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Haris Moazam Sheikh

entry.summary: Shows that specialized multi-objective acquisition functions may be unnecessary by extending standard single-objective acquisition functions to multi-objective Bayesian optimization via a hypervolume-based transformation, and extending hedge strategies to the multi-objective regime. Requires minimal modification to existing BO pipelines.

entry.title: Handwritten Digit Leakage from Smartphone Motion Sensors Across Unseen Users and Phone Models

author.name: Constantino \'Alvarez Casado, Erkka Rantahalvari, Matteo Pedone, Matti Matilainen, Manuel Lage Ca\~nellas, Le Nguyen, Simo Hosio, Olli Silv\'en, Miguel Bordallo L\'opez

entry.summary: This privacy study shows that handwritten digits drawn on smartphone touchscreens can be inferred from motion sensor readings, generalizing across unseen users and phone models. Using 19,628 recordings from 481 participants in the HuMIdb dataset, a compact sensor patch transformer achieves about 58 percent top-1 and 83 percent top-3 accuracy on unseen participants and phones. The findings expose a concrete side-channel privacy risk from sensors not intended for input capture.

entry.title: Arithmetic Simplicity in Stochastic Gradient Methods

author.name: Bin Fu, Pengfei Gu, Jose Nunez, Fabian Vazquez

entry.summary: The paper defines an arithmetically simple gradient method as one using only addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by powers of two, which is attractive for chip implementation. It shows how to transform AdaGrad, Adam, and AdamW into arithmetically simple forms, deriving convergence guarantees for a static arithmetically simple Adam variant. This bridges optimizer theory with low-cost hardware-friendly numerics.

entry.title: Topology-Adaptive Hyperbolic Graph Attention Networks Guided by the Hyperbolic Sombor Index

author.name: Haifang Cao, Boan Tao, Xiyuan Gao, Timing Li, Yu Wang, Pengfei Zhu

entry.summary: HSO-GAT introduces the Hyperbolic Sombor Index as a lightweight structural prior capturing degree-based hierarchy in graphs, combined with node-wise curvature adaptation in hyperbolic space. It unifies geometric adaptation and message propagation for hierarchical graph representation. This targets the common limitation of hyperbolic GNNs that use shared curvature and purely feature-driven attention.

entry.title: Editable Map-Conditioned Trajectory Generation for Human Mobility Simulation

author.name: Takayuki Mizuno, Shouji Fujimoto, Mikito Hiruki, Atushi Ishikawa

entry.summary: The paper formulates human mobility simulation as map-conditioned autoregressive generation where a road raster conditions a decoder emitting mesh-cell tokens at one-minute intervals, supporting held-out and locally edited maps without retraining. It trains ResNet-50 and ViT configurations on 87,400 smartphone-derived trajectories from Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan. This enables geospatial simulation of infrastructure interventions with editable maps as an explicit condition.

entry.title: What Should Federated LoRA Share? FedSAIL via Input-aware Subspace Alignment

author.name: Junye Du, Shuaida He, Long Feng

entry.summary: This paper shows that previously reported similarity of LoRA projection matrices across federated clients is largely an artifact of shared initialization, collapsing under independent initialization. It proposes FedSAIL, which aligns leading singular directions of an input-aware action matrix weighted by second-moment statistics of local inputs, revealing a more robust shared subspace structure.

entry.title: Trapped by Their Own Rollouts: Understanding Aggregation--Rollout Feedback in Federated On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jinqian Chen, Jihua Zhu, Chang Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies federated on-policy distillation for language-model adaptation and finds collaboration gains can be masked by learning-rate sensitivity, with FedAvg sometimes no better than local training at small learning rates. It explains this via the student's dual role as learner and generator of its own future training data, where aggregation-induced optimization lag delays access to teacher supervision and slows subsequent learning.

entry.title: Equivariant Neural Primal-Dual Assignment for Maximum Common Edge Subgraphs

author.name: Jiaqing Xie, Yanchao Li, Zhuo Yang, Yuxin Wang, Tianfan Fu, Yuqiang Li

entry.summary: ENPDA learns a shared matching policy for maximum common edge subgraph problems between labeled graphs, applying it to new graph pairs without per-pair retraining and answering queries roughly three orders of magnitude faster than a strong per-pair-trained baseline. The policy recomputes exact objective marginals for candidate matches and learns corrections and step sizes.

entry.title: Learning When to Recur: Token-Adaptive Recursion for Imbalanced Ophthalmic Domain Incremental Learning

author.name: Nanxi Yu, Kang Li, Ye Du, Xiaowei Hu, Weihua Yang, Shujun Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes ToRe, a rehearsal-free, parameter-efficient framework for ophthalmic domain incremental learning that uses frozen foundation models with token-adaptive recursion to handle both style-driven domain shift and severe label distribution shift from clinical referral imbalances. It decides dynamically when to apply recursive computation per token.

entry.title: The Impact of Stochasticity on the Rashomon Effect in Machine Learning

author.name: Andrea Apicella, Francesco Isgr\`o, Andrea Pollastro, Roberto Prevete

entry.summary: This empirical study examines how different sources of training stochasticity, such as weight initialization, contribute to the Rashomon effect, where multiple near-optimal models yield different behaviors. The authors quantify multiplicity along three dimensions: solution-space, predictive, and decision-basis multiplicity. Understanding these differences has implications for model reliability, fairness, and interpretability.

entry.title: CalibHyper: Chance-Corrected Relational Hypergraphs for Few-Shot Molecular Property Prediction

author.name: Linyu Li, Zhi Jin, Yuanpeng He, Dongming Jin, Huanyu Liu, Huanyao Zhang, Haoran Duan, Heng Tian, Gadeng Luosang, Nyima Tashi

entry.summary: CalibHyper improves few-shot molecular property prediction by building relational hypergraphs from chance-corrected joint label distributions rather than raw label agreement, subtracting an independence baseline and shrinking residuals by observation count. This better captures true dependence between properties for context-aware few-shot learning.

entry.title: StarBOA: Real-Time Mamba State-Space Unrolling for Sparse Radar Micro-Doppler in ISAC Networks

author.name: Mustafa Bora \c{C}elik, Ceren \c{C}elik, Orhan Gazi

entry.summary: StarBOA replaces attention with a causal Mamba state-space model for radar micro-Doppler reconstruction in ISAC networks under severe chirp subsampling (up to 90% missing data), maintaining persistent state that integrates 100x more temporal history at no extra per-step cost. It outperforms an attention baseline across sparsity levels with growing SSIM gains.

entry.title: GraphSelect for Budgeted Representation Selection in Multimodal Graph Inference

author.name: Xu Wang, Xunkai Li, Yinlin Zhu, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: GraphSelect studies budgeted selection of text and image representations for multimodal graph predictors, choosing subsets under per-modality capacity constraints while preserving predictions from the full input. The method handles the coupling where a representation's contribution depends on other selected inputs and graph propagation spreads effects across nodes, using iterative score updates.

entry.title: ResDiffFRG: Residual Diffusion for Multiple Appropriate Facial Reaction Generation

author.name: Shizhe Liu, Jiayan Gu, Xiangyu Kong, Siyang Song

entry.summary: Addresses generating multiple plausible listener facial reactions in dyadic conversations with a residual diffusion approach: instead of denoising from random Gaussian noise, the model anchors to a base reaction prediction and diffuses residuals, simplifying the denoising trajectory. This targets more aligned and diverse one-to-many facial reaction generation for human-agent interaction.

entry.title: RICE-Alpha: Reliability-Informed Correction with Event Graphs for LLM-Agent Stock Forecasting

author.name: Tong Liu, Lanmiao Liu, Xiang Hu

entry.summary: RICE-Alpha is a point-in-time stock-scoring framework that pairs a history-aware multi-view base scorer with a reliability-calibrated residual correction derived from LLM-agent analysis of historical corporate event graphs. It explicitly models event continuity and information availability to improve LLM-based financial forecasting.

entry.title: ExpertoRhythm: Morphology-Aware Learning for Waveform Reconstruction and Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation from Single-Channel PPG

author.name: Amir Arjomand, Kenneth B. Kent, Georgiy Krylov

entry.summary: ExpertoRhythm is an attention-enhanced 1D U-Net that reconstructs arterial blood pressure waveforms from single-channel PPG and derives systolic/diastolic BP directly, using a composite morphology-aware objective with range-weighted reconstruction and a window-range regularizer. This targets accurate cuffless BP monitoring for wearables.

entry.title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models

author.name: Zirui Zhu, Hailun Xu, Xuanlei Zhao, Yong Liu, Yingxuan Ren, Kanchan Sarkar, Kun Xu, Yang You

entry.summary: This paper analyzes low-rank adaptation of looped (weight-tied) language models and finds a pronounced late-loop bias where the shared LoRA update is more effective at later loop positions. Loop Dropout couples stochastic masking of adapter applications with rescaling so expected update strength stays consistent, improving adaptation of recurrently applied transformer blocks.

entry.title: Riemannian Difference-of-Convex Optimization for K-Means Clustering

author.name: Meng Xu, Bo Jiang, Hanfu Zhang, Ya-Feng Liu, Anthony Man-Cho So

entry.summary: The paper reformulates k-means clustering as a cardinality-constrained problem on a compact embedded submanifold, replacing the constraint with a difference-of-convex penalty and proving a global error bound ensuring equivalent global minimizers. It then proposes RADA-DC, a Riemannian alternating descent-ascent method with dual regularization and DC linearization, with convergence guarantees under standard assumptions.

entry.title: Distribution-Conditioned Task Routing for Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Longhuan Xu, Zhipeng Zhou, Wei Ji, Chunyan Miao, Peilin Zhao, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper tackles task routing in parameter-efficient class-incremental learning without task identity at inference, proposing training-free, inference-time distribution-conditioned routing that requires no retraining or separate router. It identifies and addresses multiple sources of routing error, an underexplored post-hoc calibration problem.

entry.title: KiT: A Foundation Model for Financial Time-Series Forecasting using DiffusionTransformers

author.name: Boyu Zhang, Haorui Li

entry.summary: KiT is a K-line (candlestick) diffusion Transformer foundation model for financial forecasting that reformulates future prediction as conditional generation to avoid autoregressive error accumulation, tailored to the low signal-to-noise, heterogeneous nature of market data. It addresses shortcomings of general-purpose time-series foundation models on candlestick tasks.

entry.title: When local gains fail to transfer: Frozen Earth-observation embeddings across wildfires

author.name: Philipp Stark, Alexandros Sopasakis, Ola Hall

entry.summary: Shows that within-region spatially blocked cross-validation does not predict accuracy of frozen Earth-observation embeddings (TESSERA, AlphaEarth) when transferred to new wildfire regions in Greece and Spain. Using Copernicus burned-area maps and Sentinel-2 baselines, it identifies when embeddings beat simple index summaries locally yet fail to transfer, and proposes a linear-probe protocol for diagnosing transferability.

entry.title: Edge-Level Automorphism in GNNs: A Quantitative Framework and Effective Designs For Link Prediction

author.name: Chen Shao, Donald Loveland, Tobias K\"afer, Danai Koutra

entry.summary: Introduces a quantitative framework for GNN expressiveness in link prediction based on edge-level automorphism, addressing the node automorphism problem where structurally identical nodes collapse into indistinguishable representations. It formalizes edge-level expressiveness and derives designs that improve link prediction performance.

entry.title: Inspector: Conversational and Lightweight Analyzer of Analog Circuit Layouts Using LLM and CNNs

author.name: Abril Cano Castro, Giuseppe Chiari, Michele Piccoli, Federico Viola, Davide Zoni

entry.summary: Proposes a framework combining fine-tuned LLMs and CNNs to analyze industry-standard GDSII files of analog integrated circuits, enabling a conversational interface for designers within EDA tools. This automates layout analysis that was previously manual or algorithmic. It targets the tape-out-critical analog IC design workflow.

entry.title: Propagate, Then Sharpen: Post-Hoc Refinement of Frozen Node Classifiers

author.name: Preben Johnsen Bentdal, Nello Blaser, Xue-Cheng Tai

entry.summary: This paper proposes Propagate, Then Sharpen (PtS), a post-hoc method that improves frozen graph node classifiers using only the graph and predicted class distributions, without access to features or model internals. It decomposes Potts energy into a Dirichlet term and a Gini (indecision) term, alternating probability propagation with mass-preserving node-wise sharpening using a single extra hyperparameter.

entry.title: ProtoSeam: Lifting Classifier Training with Latent Gaussian Mixture Models

author.name: Robert Lampel, Timon Klein, Sebastian Sager

entry.summary: ProtoSeam splits a classifier at a single interface, inserting one learnable prototype per class with a quadratic consensus penalty and a second-stage classification loss on samples drawn around prototypes, with no gradient crossing the interface. Prototypes are discarded at inference, so the deployed architecture is unchanged, and lifted training improves accuracy on CIFAR-10/100 and TinyImageNet with ResNet and ViT backbones.

entry.title: SpikeCredit: Temporal Credit Carrier for Reinforcement Learning with Sparse Rewards

author.name: Yingchao Yu, Pengfei Sun, Wenxuan Pan, Wei Chen, Yitian Hong, Kuangrong Hao, Yaochu Jin

entry.summary: Proposes SpikeCredit, a framework that uses spiking neural network membrane traces as Temporal Credit Carriers to solve credit assignment in RL with sparse rewards. It combines task-adaptive carrier selection with a fast reading pathway constrained by local behavior feedback. This is a novel bridge between SNN dynamics and the classic sparse-reward credit assignment problem.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Conditional Diffusion Model for Rare Event Synthesis and Diagnosis for the Water-Gas Shift Reaction

author.name: Md Abrar Rafid Siddique, Bibek Aryal, Qiugang Lu

entry.summary: The authors propose a physics-guided conditional diffusion model that synthesizes realistic rare-event trajectories (fouling, catalyst degradation, thermal runaway) for the water-gas shift hydrogen production reaction, addressing the scarcity of abnormal-condition process data. The generated data supports fault diagnosis and improved process safety in an industrially relevant chemical system.

entry.title: Bidirectional Neural Networks for Global Nucleon-Nucleus Optical Model Calculations

author.name: Jin Lei

entry.summary: Presents a fully differentiable neural emulator (BiLNN) mapping optical potential parameters to scattering wave functions for nucleon-nucleus calculations. A phase-space coordinate normalization allows a single network to span projectile energies from 1 to 200 MeV, supporting gradient-based uncertainty quantification and parameter optimization in nuclear data evaluation.

entry.title: Data Processing for Offline Evaluation in Recommender Systems: a Survey

author.name: Alberto Carlo Maria Mancino, Angela Di Fazio, Danilo Danese, Matteo Attimonelli, Daniele Malitesta, Antonio Ferrara, Claudio Pomo, Tommaso Di Noia

entry.summary: A systematic survey of data processing practices preceding offline evaluation in recommender systems, covering dataset selection, interaction filtering, and preprocessing decisions. It argues these under-scrutinized choices determine what information algorithms see and materially affect comparability and reproducibility of experimental results.

entry.title: Panoptic Scene Program Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Chika Maduabuchi

entry.summary: Introduces PSP-DiT, a diffusion transformer that treats a panoptic scene program as a first-class latent variable, jointly denoising image and scene-program latents through coupled transformer streams with panoptic grounding and cycle-consistency objectives. It targets compositional text-to-image failures involving instance identity, attribute ownership, counting, spatial ordering, and role-sensitive relations.

entry.title: Identifiability Limits of Gravitational Wave Phase Deviations: Multiclass Classification with a Multihead Neural Network

author.name: Lavinia Heisenberg, Shayan Hemmatyar

entry.summary: The authors use a multihead neural network with classification and regression heads to identify gravitational-wave phase deviations from general relativity across six parametrized post-Einsteinian families, predicting coupling magnitudes from waveform-mismatch response functions. Tested on 262 sources with Advanced LIGO design noise and 132 sources with measured O3 Hanford spectrum plus recorded strain injections, the work maps out identifiability limits for tests of general relativity.

entry.title: Kernel-Based Steering of CLIP with Vision-Language Model Preferences

author.name: Sajjad Ghiasvand, Haniyeh Ehsani Oskouie, Sina Mansouri, Mahnoosh Alizadeh, Farzan Farnia, Ramtin Pedarsani

entry.summary: The paper introduces ASK, a kernel-based method that transfers pairwise visual-similarity judgments from large vision-language models into CLIP embeddings without accessing teacher embeddings or new human annotations. It builds positive semidefinite target kernels within small image groups, combines visual kernel matching with an image-text distributional anchor, and uses low-rank adapters that regularize toward frozen CLIP, preserving original retrieval capabilities. A neat preference-distillation technique for VLM alignment.

entry.title: AECSF: Adaptive Ensemble Conditional Score Filtering for High-Dimensional Nonlinear Data Assimilation

author.name: Yangwen Zhang, Shiwei Ni, Xiaoping Zhang, Xiaofei Guan, Lili Ju

entry.summary: AECSF is a training-free score-based diffusion filter for Bayesian state estimation in high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems, constructing an analytically tractable score estimator that accounts for state uncertainty of noisy reverse particles. It aims to avoid particle weight collapse and the Gaussian posterior limitations of ensemble methods without heuristic likelihood corrections.

entry.title: Agnostic Smoothed Online Regression with Adversarial Responses

author.name: Xuanyu Chen, Yue Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes Hedge-Cover, an information-theoretic algorithm for smoothed online prediction with bounded adversarial responses, achieving sublinear regret scaling with pseudo-dimension and a covariate smoothness parameter. It aggregates a constructed family of experts via Hedge with a prior linked to disagreements between a consistent selector and a target function.

entry.title: Domain Adaptation with Target Information via Doubly-Anchored Distributionally Robust Optimization

author.name: David Kepplinger, Anand N. Vidyashankar

entry.summary: The paper introduces a doubly-anchored DRO framework for domain adaptation whose ambiguity set intersects phi-divergence balls centered at the source law and at a source-completed target reference law. It derives dual-induced adversarial bridge geometries, including a novel KL/squared-Hellinger pairing yielding a Lambert-W geometry with asymmetric source-target roles.

entry.title: CollisionGAT: Controller-Agnostic One-Step Collision Screening for Multi-Agent Motion

author.name: Alan Debbas, Edwin Meriaux, Gregory Dudek

entry.summary: Presents CollisionGAT, a graph-attention network that scores collision risk for each agent's proposed next step in multi-agent robot motion, usable by any controller to accept, repair, or replan steps. Training labels come from exact geometric checks, which also independently audit every executed step, providing a learned-but-verified safety layer.

entry.title: MorphAtt: A Neuromorphic Accelerator for Efficient Multi-Head Attention Processing in Spiking Vision Transformers

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Amirhesam Jafari Rad, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: MorphAtt is a digital hardware accelerator that speeds up multi-head self-attention in spiking vision transformers through cascaded modules: a spiking QKV generator, a low-complexity spiking attention engine, and reparameterization convolution. It targets energy-efficient edge inference where SViT parameter counts and attention costs are bottlenecks. The work bridges spiking neural network design and accelerator co-design.

entry.title: Local LMO is Secretly a Projection Method!

author.name: Peter Richt\'arik, Ammar Mahran

entry.summary: The paper shows that the local linear minimization oracle (Local LMO) step for constrained convex optimization is, under a radius condition, equivalent to a Euclidean projection onto the feasible set intersected with a separating half-space, computable via a linear oracle alone. This reframes Local LMO as a member of a family of projection methods indexed by half-space depth. The result unifies projection-free and projection-based optimization perspectives.

entry.title: Non-Adaptive Learning of Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi Graphs via Affine Splitting

author.name: Hoang Ta

entry.summary: This work studies reconstructing unknown edge sets from group queries and gives a non-adaptive scheme for Erdos-Renyi graphs using O(kbar log n) queries with fast decoding, improving over worst-case quadratic lower bounds that hold for general graphs. It is a theoretical contribution connecting group testing ideas to graph learning under stochastic sparsity assumptions.

entry.title: Adapting neural operators for mechanics decisions under changing operating conditions

author.name: Prashant K. Jha, Koffi Enakoutsa, Ian Galloway, Henry Anderson

entry.summary: This work studies reusing high-fidelity finite-element solutions gathered during deployment to adapt neural operators that surrogate nonlinear mechanics simulations, with an empirical error estimator deciding which predictions are safe to use for command selection. It is demonstrated on two hard-magnetic soft-material systems, showing improved downstream decision quality as operating conditions drift beyond the training range.

entry.title: Hierarchical Clustering and Signal Denoising on Digraphs

author.name: Yi Wang, Sippanon Kitimoon, Hrushikesh N. Mhaskar, Xiaosheng Zhuang

entry.summary: The paper represents a directed graph as a Hermitian matrix derived from its adjacency matrix, capturing both connectivity and edge orientation. Based on spectral decomposition, it introduces a digraph clustering algorithm with k-means and a recursive hierarchical version producing consistent nested partitions, plus hierarchical edge-count measures for denoising. This extends spectral graph methods to directed graphs.

entry.title: Accelerator Choice Is Not Enough: AlphaFold2 Inference on Cloud TPUs

author.name: Lorenzo Pazienza, Ihab El Bani

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks one AlphaFold2 inference workload across a Colab CPU runtime, an NVIDIA T4 GPU, and an eight-chip Cloud TPU v5e slice, finding a large raw hardware advantage for TPUs (0.47s per call per chip versus 13.1s on the T4). However, it shows three software-layer issues, including the default execution path using only one of eight chips, mean users often realize far less of the hardware advantage, and at list prices idle capacity can make the TPU slice cost roughly as much per prediction. The work argues that software configuration, not accelerator choice, is the dominant practical decision.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth-Averaged Avalanche Dynamics

author.name: Pradyumn Singh Sikarwar, Vishal Sharma, Gaurav Bhutani

entry.summary: The paper develops a physics-informed neural network framework for the Savage-Hutter model of depth-averaged granular flow, relevant to avalanche hazard assessment, progressing from 1D analytical verification to 2D experimental validation. Three 1D problems of increasing complexity are verified against analytical solutions, including coupled prediction of height and velocity fields using the conservative formulation. The coupled formulation learns both fields without prescribing either.

entry.title: Recommendation Ranking Off-Policy Evaluation under Ranking-Dependent Examination via Examination-Relevance Decomposition

author.name: Riki Okamura, Toshiharu Sugawara

entry.summary: This work addresses bias in off-policy evaluation for recommender rankings caused by the inability of logged clicks to distinguish unexamined items from examined non-clicks. It proposes two estimators, LE-IIPS and a doubly robust extension ED-DR, that decompose clicks into examination and relevance components, with ED-DR unbiased whenever examination probabilities are correctly specified.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Cardiac Model Personalisation from Ultrafast Ultrasound

author.name: Camilla Ferrario (CHU Bordeaux), Maelys Venet (CHU Bordeaux), Olivier Villemain (CHU Bordeaux), Maxime Sermesant (EPIONE)

entry.summary: The paper frames cardiac model personalization from ultrafast ultrasound shear wave elastography as a statistical inference problem using simulation-based inference and neural posterior estimation. With a subject-adapted 0D cardiovascular model, it estimates posterior distributions over unobservable mechanical parameters, addressing the ill-posedness of mapping stiffness dynamics to model parameters.

entry.title: Statistical Learning of Contractive Dynamical Representations for Composite Adaptive Control

author.name: Min Kim, Jos\'e Leonardo Brenes, Fred Hadaegh, Soon-Jo Chung

entry.summary: The paper presents a representation-learning framework for composite adaptive tracking control under coupled disturbances, connecting classical disturbance-accommodating control with last-layer adaptive disturbance rejection. It introduces a hard-EM procedure with a Kalman smoother to learn latent disturbance representations with uniformly contractive evolution. The approach targets control applications such as aerospace systems.

entry.title: A literature-guided descriptor-based framework for filtering composition search spaces

author.name: Lei Zhang, Markus Stricker

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework that mines latent materials knowledge from scientific literature using a literature-trained word embedding model, selecting descriptors to build a Pareto-based filter that shrinks composition search spaces for materials discovery. The approach turns textual associations in large corpora into practical screening tools. It demonstrates how scientific text can directly inform experimental search.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Ontology-Driven Knowledge Graph Construction from Unstructured Text

author.name: Abdelhadi Belfadel, Maxence Gagnant, Joseph Kattan, Sana Tmar

entry.summary: The authors present an ontology learning pipeline combining compact open-source LLMs (7B to 32B parameters), reusable prompting strategies, and open knowledge bases to extract and structure knowledge from industrial text. They evaluate the pipeline on a private French corpus of power-grid incident reports, covering extraction, enrichment, and evaluation stages. The work targets locally deployable, privacy-preserving knowledge graph construction.

entry.title: The Ongiini-Eval-OW Benchmark: A Concept Paper for the Planned Benchmarking of Machine Translation and Large Language Models on Oshindonga and Oshikwanyama

author.name: Sebastian K\"upers (Common Intelligence Foundation)

entry.summary: This concept paper announces Ongiini-Eval-OW, a planned 600-item English-to-Oshindonga and English-to-Oshikwanyama benchmark with native-speaker references from two independent translators, an inter-translator agreement set, and error tags. It documents that major commercial and open MT systems completely lack coverage of these Bantu languages spoken by over a million people. The paper establishes the case and methodology before data release.

entry.title: DualGuard: Dual-Mode Quality Control for Logic-Preserving Data Augmentation

author.name: Shenghao Li, Lin Zhao

entry.summary: DualGuard proposes a dual-mode quality-control framework for LLM-generated logical reasoning data augmentation, treating retain/filter/repair decisions as an explicit control problem after quality judgment. One mode uses the current instance and candidate batch for selective retention and targeted feedback, while the second accumulates information over time. It addresses a real reliability problem in synthetic reasoning data pipelines.

entry.title: How to Reduce Whisper Hallucination

author.name: Husein Zolkepli

entry.summary: A single-author empirical study of Whisper hallucinations, showing whisper-large-v3 emits words on 61.9 percent of pure room-tone clips and some output on all of them, and critiquing pseudo-label distillation pipelines that filter hallucinations from training corpora — which leaves the failure mode in place while deleting the evidence. It evaluates remedies including non-speech audio training and alternative checkpoints. Practical value for the many production systems still relying on Whisper.

entry.title: Focusing Condition: Inference-Time Self-Contrastive Steering Elicits Better Conditional Text Embeddings in LLMs

author.name: Zifeng Cheng, Lingyun Qian, Zhiwei Jiang, Cong Wang, Yafeng Yin, Fei Shen, Ao Zhou, Qing Gu

entry.summary: The paper proposes Self-Contrastive Steering (SCS), an inference-time plug-and-play method that constructs unconditional general text embeddings and uses them to refine conditional embeddings, making them more focused on the target condition than prompt-only conditioning achieves. This requires no additional data or fine-tuning. It offers a practical improvement for extracting conditional representations from LLMs.

entry.title: Where Do Test-Time Scaling and Training Fall Short in Individual Stance Prediction?

author.name: Yuyang Zhao, Xuan Liu, HaoYang Shangm Haojian Jin

entry.summary: Evaluates test-time scaling and post-training methods (SFT, RL) for predicting an individual's stance from discussion history, identifying four failure modes: incorrect consensus, selection failure, response overfitting, and others across generation, selection, and learning stages. Shows that advances driving coding and math reasoning do not transfer straightforwardly to stance prediction. Relevant to personalization and social computing applications of LLMs.

entry.title: Language Discrimination Improves Linguistic Learning in Multilingual Speech Models

author.name: Maureen de Seyssel, Jie Chi, Zakaria Aldeneh

entry.summary: Shows that adding language discrimination signals during pretraining (an auxiliary language classifier or per-language k-means targets) closes much of the gap between multilingual and monolingual self-supervised speech models under matched data budgets, using a controlled English/French HuBERT setting. Phone discrimination error decreases across interventions while cross-language sharing is preserved. Offers actionable insight for multilingual speech model pretraining recipes.

entry.title: When Do Agents Help? Embedding, LLM and Agentic Alignment of Classical Texts and Their Translations

author.name: M\'at\'e Metzger

entry.summary: This work compares seven alignment systems for matching classical texts (Pali, Sanskrit, Mishnaic Hebrew, Tibetan) with their translations, using 9,833 human-aligned units across 452 texts. Generative workflows recover 93-94% of reference correspondences versus at most 77% for embedding pipelines, while an autonomous agent improves over a direct LLM call by only about 0.5 percentage points. The ceiling analysis showing sentence boundaries limit embedding approaches is a useful methodological contribution.

entry.title: Understanding Clinical Cognitive Dialogues Using Large Language Models

author.name: Vishalakshi Arumugam, Dan Schumacher, Veronica Rammouz, Enrique Gonzalez Guerrero, Jeremy Davis, Anthony Rios

entry.summary: The paper releases a de-identified corpus of 33 cognitive assessment conversations with 8,250 utterances annotated for three speaker roles and 56 dialogue acts, and benchmarks LLMs on fine-grained dialogue-act classification and next-patient-utterance generation. It also tests whether out-of-domain instruction data and explanation-augmented training transfer to this clinical setting. The resource enables studying clinician-patient interaction dynamics at scale.

entry.title: Papers Without Code: Availability of GitHub Repositories Linked in *CL Publications

author.name: Selina Meyer, Michael Roth

entry.summary: This squib examines the long-term availability of GitHub repositories linked in ACL, CL journal, and co-located publications over ten years. Counterintuitively, more recent ACL publications show repository unavailability rates similar to older ones, partly due to a rise in empty or placeholder repositories.

entry.title: Tracing the Evolution of Oracle Bone Characters Across Three Millennia

author.name: Tianhao Fu, Xinxin Xu, Spike Wang, Cunyi Kang, Jian Cao, Xixin Cao

entry.summary: The paper proposes the Manifold-based Script Evolution Framework (MSEF), which models the evolution of Chinese characters across five script stages (Oracle Bone, Bronze, Seal, Clerical, Regular) as continual evolution of a manifold space, rather than comparing Oracle Bone glyphs to a single historical period. This addresses structural and semantic changes occurring in uncertain dynasties. Applied to the roughly 2,900 still-undeciphered Oracle Bone Inscription characters, the framework could aid decipherment efforts in digital humanities.

entry.title: Improving Audiovisual Speech Recognition through Synthetic Visual Data Augmentation

author.name: Pol Buitrago, Pol G\`alvez, Javier Hernando

entry.summary: The paper explores synthetic visual data augmentation for audiovisual speech recognition using an audio-driven talking-head pipeline that generates lip-synchronized visual content from existing audio, addressing the scarcity of labeled audiovisual datasets. The approach is evaluated for Spanish and Catalan both as an augmentation strategy and as a standalone training resource. Results show relative Word Error Rate improvements when real AV data is augmented with synthetic samples.

entry.title: Video Captioning in Low-Light Conditions through Efficient Uncertainty-Aware Caption Correction

author.name: Arefeh Rezaei

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight correction framework for VideoChat2 captions under low-light conditions: a sparse Gaussian process module between the projection layer and language model estimates residuals against verified target representations, adaptively scaled via a new uncertainty formulation, without fine-tuning the underlying VLM.

entry.title: HGPTrans: Hierarchical Graph-Pooling Transolver for Automotive Aerodynamic Drag Coefficient Prediction

author.name: Bo Liu, Qiuli Luo, Lianrui Nie, Fengli Zhang, Wenjiang Wang

entry.summary: HGPTrans is a hierarchical graph-pooling network with Transolver-based attention that predicts automotive aerodynamic drag coefficients directly from surface meshes, capturing both local geometry and long-range interactions as a fast alternative to hours-long CFD runs. It targets early-stage vehicle design exploration where many candidates must be evaluated.

entry.title: PredRA: Fast Medical Image Translation by Deterministic Component Extraction and Controlled Stochastic Refinement

author.name: Jianhai Zhang, Pattarawut Charatpangoon, Donghao Zhang, Bijoy K. Menon, Wu Qiu, M. Ethan MacDonald, Aravind Ganesh

entry.summary: PredRA frames strongly paired medical image translation as separating a directly predictable deterministic component from residual detail, using deterministic prediction as a stable reference and extracting further deterministic structure from the residual during generative refinement. The aim is higher fidelity than pure deterministic prediction while avoiding harmful stochastic variation from generative models.

entry.title: Type-Balanced Federated Learning for Visual Analog Meter Reading

author.name: Weida Zhao, Logan Bellamy, Yazhou Tu, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: This paper presents a federated learning framework for automatic analog dial meter reading that allows multiple industrial sites with heterogeneous meter types and limited labels to collaboratively train a shared reader without pooling sensitive raw images. A type-balancing strategy addresses skewed distributions of meter types across participating sites.

entry.title: FSS-UBrain: Multi-region Few-Shot Brain Tumor MRI Segmentation

author.name: Truong Viet Vu, Nguyen Phuc Nguyen, Dang Thi Thu Hang, Tran Thien Thanh, Vo Nguyen Quoc Bao, Nguyen Thai Anh, Ngo Hoang Tu

entry.summary: FSS-UBrain performs region-wise one-shot segmentation of whole tumor, tumor core, and enhancing tumor in multimodal MRI, using a labeled support slice to condition binary query segmentation with foreground and background descriptors. Episodic training with hard-negative and fully negative queries plus empty-query regularization suppresses spurious activations when references are unrepresentative.

entry.title: CityToolVQA: Tool-Augmented Visual Question Answering for 3D Spatial Cognition in Urban Low-Altitude Environments

author.name: Boao Yu, Yingzhen Nie, Yue Hu, Zhengqiu Zhu, Rusheng Ju

entry.summary: Presents a tool-augmented VQA framework for urban low-altitude scenarios where VLMs answer qualitative questions directly and route quantitative questions to an external visual-geometric toolchain performing grounding, segmentation, and depth back-projection. Includes a 73,324-question benchmark and an 8B-model fine-tuning variant adapted to tool-conditioned inputs.

entry.title: CFCH: Coarse-Fine Collaborative Hierarchical Learning for Anterior Segment Disease Analysis

author.name: Peng Wang, Haohan Zou, Yanlin Wu, Xueshuo Xie, Yan Wang, Tao Li

entry.summary: CFCH is a dual-branch hierarchical learning framework for classifying anterior segment diseases from slit-lamp images, explicitly modeling the dependency between anatomical regions (cornea, conjunctiva, lens) and disease manifestations instead of treating the task as flat multi-class classification. It targets variability in real-world ophthalmic imaging conditions. The work is practically relevant for automated ophthalmic screening and diagnosis where structured anatomical-disease reasoning matters.

entry.title: dKFD: Phase-Structured Evidence Allocation for Fixed-Budget Localized Event Understanding

author.name: Aditya Bagri, Ashutosh Kumar, Chaitanya Lakhchaura, Avinash Anand, Zhengkui Wang, Rajiv Ratn Shah

entry.summary: The paper studies fixed-budget frame selection for temporally localized event videos, showing that globally competitive Top-K selectors produce unstable event evidence even when recognition and grounding metrics look fine. dKFD structures the budget across pre-event context, the event, and post-event consequences, improving selector-event alignment on the DoTA benchmark.

entry.title: PIC-UIE: Predicting Image-Adaptive Corrections for Lightweight Underwater Image Enhancement

author.name: Cunhao Zhu, Dongliang Xu, Xiangtao Kong, Xiaoyan Lu, Tianyu Wang, Yue Yao

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight predictor-executor framework for underwater image enhancement that predicts image-adaptive corrections from a small RGB thumbnail and applies them at native resolution in YCbCr space, producing seven spatially varying outputs. It avoids dense image-to-image prediction for edge deployment and decouples degradation estimation from luminance/chroma correction. Relevant for practical underwater robotics and edge vision systems.

entry.title: LoopLUT: 3D Lookup Tables with Progressive Region Refinement for Real-Time 4K Image Enhancement

author.name: Yang Ye, Jiajun Ma, Chen Wu, Wei Wang, Dianjie Lu, Guijuan Zhang, Linwei Fan, Zhuoran Zheng

entry.summary: LoopLUT is a region-cascaded 3D LUT method for real-time 4K image enhancement that applies a global LUT followed by K-1 loop iterations, where a gating head predicts regions still needing correction and builds residual corrections. This overcomes the spatial invariance limitation of single global LUTs under tight compute budgets. It targets deployment-grade efficiency rather than raw benchmark accuracy.

entry.title: Analytical and Convolutional Neural Network-Based Motion-Vector Propagation for Efficient Video Object Detection

author.name: Ashiyana Abdul Majeed, Mahmoud Meribout, Neethu Joseph

entry.summary: This work presents a hardware-software methodology for embedded video object detection that reuses codec motion vectors between detector invocations, comparing an analytical propagation model against a learned CNN-based one. The analytical approach achieves an F1 of 0.909 with 9.03 ms latency and 0.177 J per frame, targeting continuous analytics under tight power budgets.

entry.title: HUMAN-TCI: Hierarchical Multi-Stream Motion-Aware Network with Torso-Centered Interaction for Text-to-Motion Retrieval
