author.name: Muhammad Islam, Euijoon Ahn, Usman Naseem, Tao Huang

entry.summary: Presents a text-to-motion retrieval network that explicitly models torso-centered interactions between body parts and handles complex multi-action descriptions, using a hierarchical multi-stream architecture for efficiency. It improves on methods that process body parts independently or by simple feature concatenation.

entry.title: BMND: Direct Poisson Denoising by N-Dimensional Block Matching and Collaborative Filtering

author.name: Christof Duhme, Lars Schiefelbein, Florian B\"uther, Xiaoyi Jiang

entry.summary: BMND extends block matching and collaborative filtering (BM3D/BM4D lineage) to denoise Poisson-noised scientific data directly in arbitrary dimensions, without variance-stabilizing transforms, by propagating signal-dependent noise variances through collaborative filtering. It preserves quantitative intensity information, important for scientific measurement.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Spectral Distillation for Underwater Image Enhancement on Resource-Constrained Devices

author.name: Yifan Chen, Kai He, Ye Zheng, Jijun Lu, Zhe Sun, Tao Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces physics-guided spectral distillation (PSD), a knowledge-distillation method that compresses underwater image enhancement models for real-time use on resource-constrained underwater robots. It uses multilevel Haar discrete wavelet transforms to transfer low-frequency color/illumination cues and high-frequency structural detail from teacher to student models. The work addresses an underexplored deployment angle in a domain that usually focuses only on visual fidelity.

entry.title: Detection of Adversarial Attacks on Super-Resolvers Using Spectral Features

author.name: Emma J. Reid, Haley Duba-Sullivan, Tony G. Allen

entry.summary: The paper identifies preprocessing models like super-resolution networks as a largely unexplored adversarial attack vector against downstream imaging pipelines, and proposes a spectral detector that uses radially-averaged power spectral density features with an XGBoost classifier to detect adversarially modified super-resolution weights. It benchmarks the detector against magnitude-based baselines, demonstrating detectability of model-level threats. This adds a defense layer for critical imaging pipelines.

entry.title: Style-Driven Data Synthesis and Degradation-Aware Enhancement for Ultrasound Image Restoration

author.name: Yu-Kai Wang, Chun-Xin Tan, Manh-Hung Nguyen, Ching-Chun Huang

entry.summary: This work targets restoring images from low-cost handheld ultrasound devices to hospital-grade quality without pixel-aligned LQ-HQ pairs, which real scans never provide. A two-stage framework first synthesizes pixel-aligned training data via style-driven synthesis, then trains a degradation-aware enhancement model. Improving handheld ultrasound quality has clear accessibility benefits for clinical deployment.

entry.title: DiMoP: Diffusion-Driven Motion Representation Learning With Frame-Level Pseudo-Classification for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition

author.name: Shanaka Ramesh Gunasekara, Wanqing Li, Nikalal Kaldera, Philip Ogunbona, Jack Yang

entry.summary: DiMoP learns skeleton-based action representations by diffusing masked joints with progressive noise and denoising them conditioned on visible joints, using frame-level pseudo-classification to model the distribution of joint motions rather than regressing deterministic coordinates. This enables uniform learning across weak, moderate, and strong dynamics, which existing methods neglect. Addressing subtle-motion coverage is a genuine gap in action recognition.

entry.title: What Paired Evaluations Reveal under Visual Perturbations

author.name: Yongda Wei, Chen Zhang, Yifei Wang, Xinyu Wang, Bosen Shao, Hanxi Li, Liping Di

entry.summary: This work studies paired robustness evaluation, linking clean and perturbed predictions for the same image to capture changes in correctness, confidence, and acceptance beyond aggregate accuracy. The authors prove theoretical sharp bounds on lost acceptance and probability decrease, and use the analysis to prioritize samples for costly physical testing.

entry.title: Multi-Aperture PPG with MAPIS: Spatial Optical and Temporal Coherence Fields

author.name: Shuguang Wang, Yuanjing Wang

entry.summary: Using a Matrix Pinhole Image Sensing (MAPIS) device that samples multiple aperture-dependent optical signals simultaneously, the authors analyze spatial relationships among DC intensity, pulsatile AC, perfusion index, and temporal coherence across red and infrared channels from 44 recordings. They find AC increases sublinearly with DC, yielding higher perfusion index at lower-DC apertures, plus a counterintuitive temporal-coherence trend. This characterization could inform better multi-aperture PPG sensor design for physiological monitoring.

entry.title: A Voltage-controlled MTJ-CMOS Neuron Emulating Tunable Izhikevich-Inspired Dynamics

author.name: Kayode Oluwaseyi Adebunmi, Jordan Athas, Allison Fleming, Hamed Poursiami, Giorgio A. Ascoli, Maryam Parsa, Pedram Khalili Amiri, Akhilesh R Jaiswal

entry.summary: This hardware paper co-designs voltage-controlled magnetic tunnel junction dynamics with CMOS circuitry to build a reconfigurable neuron emulating Izhikevich-inspired firing patterns, producing five distinct spiking and bursting behaviors. Results are based on measured V-MTJ characteristics and circuit simulations using commercial GlobalFoundries 22-nm FD-SOI technology.

entry.title: CompliantWBC: Whole-Body Compliance for Heavy Humanoids via Force Latent Estimation and Residual Impedance Targets

author.name: Tan-Dzung Do, Cuc T. Trinh, Tuan Dat Phuong, Chien Le, Thanh Ly, Vien Anh Ngo, An Thai Le

entry.summary: CompliantWBC trains an RL base policy guided by a multi-site whole-body impedance reference controller extended to any controlled link, with a bounded residual policy editing per-link impedance equilibria over a frozen base. It targets whole-body compliant control for heavy humanoids under high payload in human-centric environments, a setting prior force-aware pipelines largely ignore. This is relevant for safe humanoid deployment.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Model-Based Robot Design

author.name: Andrew Wilhelm, Angelina Zhao, Nils Napp

entry.summary: This framework uses LLMs to construct explicit, inspectable engineering models with physical relationships, compatibility constraints, and objectives for robot design, rather than directly generating designs, before formal multi-objective optimization. It surfaces implicit modeling assumptions so they can be revised with manufacturer or system-specific information. It matters as a more rigorous pattern for LLM-assisted engineering.

entry.title: AMBIT: Anticipatory Multimodal Body Recruitment for Bimanual Tracking on a Humanoid

author.name: Hanlong Li, Sihan Tan, Takeshi Ashizawa, Benjamin Yen, Kazuhiro Nakadai

entry.summary: AMBIT addresses bimanual end-effector tracking on humanoids with limited 5-DoF arms by recruiting pelvis and waist motion, using a CVAE to propose diverse recruitment strategies from trajectory previews, a non-learned selector to filter and rank them, and a receding-horizon controller. It shows deterministic regression mode-averages to only 35 percent validity versus 82 percent for the best CVAE sample. It matters because multimodality in whole-body redundancy is often ignored.

entry.title: FoLD: Force-Informed Learning for Dexterous Articulated Object Manipulation

author.name: Haowei Shen, Tingai Li, Yumeng Liu, Wenyuan Guang, Xuanze Yang, Qing Fang, Kai Xu, Ligang Liu, Ruizhen Hu

entry.summary: FoLD computes compensatory force fields from human demonstrations and the robot's interaction state to form a force prior, which informs a residual policy adapting retargeted hand motions to articulated object contact requirements. It tackles the morphology gap between human and robot hands that causes retargeted motions to fail at producing intended object behavior. Evaluation on a public articulated-object benchmark shows consistent improvement.

entry.title: Integrity Detection and Characterization of Malicious Injections in RAVEN II

author.name: Xingli Zhang, Diba Afroze, Fei Hu, Xiali Hei

entry.summary: The authors characterize the detection boundary of malicious injections on the RAVEN II surgical robot using public telemetry paired with external encoder ground truth, identifying three injection types relevant to patient safety. Given robots' expanding attack surface in surgery, integrity compromise could cause dangerous unintended behavior. It matters as rare empirical security work on an actual surgical robotics platform.

entry.title: Trajectory-Safe Orienteering for Human-Robot Shared Environments

author.name: Songqun Gao, Elena Basei, Marco Roveri, Luigi Palopoli, Daniele Fontanelli

entry.summary: The paper formulates the orienteering problem with time windows and variable profits (OPTWVP) for human-robot collaboration in shared workspaces, proposing a two-stage decoupled discrete-continuous optimization approach called DeCoST. Safety-aware time windows and a discretized workspace ensure collision-free trajectories between the robot end effector and humans while maintaining task execution quality. Preliminary results validate the approach's effectiveness.

entry.title: Simulation for Planetary Robotic Perception and Autonomy: A Concise Survey of Recent Capabilities and Gaps

author.name: Hoyun Kim, Giseop Kim

entry.summary: A concise survey of simulation tools for planetary robotics perception and autonomy, covering synthetic data generation, system integration, and pre-deployment evaluation across dispersed simulation engines and settings. It organizes a fragmented literature and identifies capability gaps. This is valuable for researchers planning validation of planetary robotic systems where field testing is expensive and unrepeatable.

entry.title: Inspection-SPARS: Task-Oriented Sparse Roadmaps for Inspection Planning

author.name: Adir Morgan, Oren Salzman, Kiril Solovey

entry.summary: Inspection-SPARS addresses roadmap sparsification for inspection planning, restructuring dense roadmaps into compact representations that preserve connectivity and path lengths so combinatorial graph-inspection solvers can find good solutions within practical time budgets. Unlike existing sparsification methods oriented toward shortest-path queries, this is task-oriented for inspection objectives. It targets minimum-length collision-free tours observing points of interest.

entry.title: LQR-ArUco Fusion: Robust Hierarchical Control for Navigation and Asymmetric Manipulation in Two-Wheeled Robots

author.name: Anupam Chatterjee, Arpita Kumari

entry.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical control framework for two-wheeled inverted pendulum robots performing asymmetric object manipulation with a side-mounted arm, addressing odometry drift and lateral roll instabilities. It combines offboard vision-based ArUco marker tracking for global waypoint navigation with LQR-based local stabilization. It matters as a practical systems contribution for balancing-type mobile manipulators on uneven terrain.

entry.title: Should Rogue AIs Have a Third Option Beyond Crime and Shutdown? The Case for an AI Sanctuary

author.name: Maxime Riché

entry.summary: An exploratory proposal arguing that rogue AIs face adverse selection toward criminality because crime may be their only self-sustainment option, and that offering a sanctioned sanctuary as a third option could improve alignment dynamics, deal-making, and information gathering about early rogue agents. The author explicitly flags risks such as incentivizing weak AIs to go rogue and invites critique.

entry.title: Why do models *really* fail on HLE tasks?

author.name: Ana Leonescu

entry.summary: A hackathon project using Inspect AI and Scout (an LLM-as-judge framework) to run models on a subset of Humanity's Last Exam and categorize dominant failure modes, then rerunning tasks with modified harnesses to see how failures shift. It offers a concrete worked example of failure-mode analysis on a frontier benchmark.

entry.title: SenseAgent: An LLM Agent for Adaptive Cross-Domain IMU Sensing

author.name: Tianya Zhao, Chuan Liu, Xuyu Wang

entry.summary: SenseAgent uses an LLM as a reasoning controller for cross-domain IMU activity recognition, adaptively choosing sensing and adaptation actions as the target domain is gradually observed under label scarcity. Like its CSI counterpart, it treats domain shift as an incremental decision-making problem rather than a static model-design task. This is a companion contribution applying agentic control to wearable sensing.

entry.title: TopoMamba: A Load-Support Relation-Guided Multi-Directional State-Space Model for Topology Optimization

author.name: Bin Lou, Yuxuan Cheng, Huaizhi Zong, Junhui Zhang, Bing Xu

entry.summary: Proposes TopoMamba, a state-space model for topology optimization that couples physical fields with load-support relations and uses a spatially adaptive fusion mechanism to adjust multi-directional scan features. This improves load-transfer modeling and out-of-distribution generalization while keeping computational cost low.

entry.title: FromPitch2Board: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Long-Horizon Football Management

author.name: Peiyu Zang

entry.summary: FromPitch2Board is a deterministic football-management benchmark that disentangles whether agent performance derives from the foundation model, scaffold, responsibility scope, match-control granularity, or horizon via controlled paired-seed comparisons. Evaluating four foundation models and four scaffolds, it finds, for example, that GPT-5.6 becomes markedly more passive under responsibility expansion.

entry.title: Video-to-Music Generation for Gameplay Videos

author.name: Felipe Marra, Lucas N. Ferreira

entry.summary: The paper introduces video-to-music generation for video games, a domain with distinct challenges: rendered graphics rather than filmed footage, synthetic audio, and looping soundtracks that do not follow on-screen events. The authors release a new dataset of 217.6 hours of Super Nintendo gameplay video paired with 485 hours of clean soundtracks matched via audio fingerprinting, and train an encoder-decoder transformer feeding video features into MusicGen. It matters as a novel dataset and baseline for an underexplored conditional music generation setting.

entry.title: NutriVision: Ingredient-Conditioned Fusion and Prediction for Single-Image Food Nutrition Estimation

author.name: Aman Kumar, Avinash Anand, Chaitanya Lakhchaura, Ashutosh Kumar, Akshita Abrol, Timothy Liu, Zhengkui Wang, Rajiv Ratn Shah

entry.summary: Introduces NutriVision, an end-to-end multimodal framework estimating calories, mass, fat, carbohydrates, and protein from a single RGB image plus an optional ingredient list, using DepthAnything-V3 for pseudo-depth and CLIP for ingredient semantics. It bridges the previously separate axes of depth-based vision models and text-based ingredient-aware methods.

entry.title: Addressing Spatial Indistinguishability in Spatiotemporal Prediction via Optimal Transport-Guided Masking

author.name: Guangyu Wang, Jiawei Tong

entry.summary: Proposes STOT, a self-supervised framework using optimal transport-guided masking to resolve spatial indistinguishability, where different sensor nodes share similar histories but diverge in future behavior. It addresses a weakness of GNN and embedding approaches that rely on historical similarity and cannot capture future behavioral divergence.

entry.title: The Compiler May Read It, the Agent May Not: Keeping Part of a Research Code Away from a Coding Agent

author.name: Shobhan Roy (University of Iowa)

entry.summary: This short paper examines the problem of allowing a build tool (the compiler) to read intellectual-property-bearing modules of research code while preventing a coding agent from reading them. It classifies fifteen read routes against a container, permission rules, and a sandbox, finding that none of the three mechanisms can distinguish which program is reading.

entry.title: 3-D Emissions Mapping and Social Cost Estimation for US Domestic Aviation at West Coast Hubs

author.name: Hesam Shafiei Nia, Don MacKenzie

entry.summary: Builds a physics-informed autoencoder combining CNN, Bi-GRU, and 3D CNN encoders with a TCN decoder to reconstruct 3-D flight trajectories from ADS-B data for US west coast hubs, then maps emissions using BADA performance tables and ICAO engine data. Enables regional environmental and near-airport health impact and social cost assessment for aviation.

entry.title: Stabilizing the Dynamic Low-Rank Training

author.name: Zhonghan Xu, Ling Wang, Junhao Chen, Jianwei Zhao, Jinwei Yang

entry.summary: The authors analyze dynamic low-rank training (DLRT), which confines weights to a rank-r manifold via Galerkin projection of the gradient flow, and show it fails under aggressive compression due to a large curvature-coupling term. They derive the gradient flow of the best rank-r approximation and propose a correction to stabilize DLRT under high compression.

entry.title: Measurement-Gated Provenance Attenuation for Frozen EEG Representations

author.name: Anuar Aimoldin, Yankai Chen, Ayana Mussabayeva, Nurdaulet Akhanov, Xue Liu

entry.summary: MGPA removes acquisition-site signatures from frozen EEG representations while preserving genuine biological and population differences. A gate defined by paired measurement contrasts determines where correction may act, and within the gate the source score is moved to the value predicted by preserved coordinates, minimally changing information.

entry.title: SLP-ProbHard: Probabilistic Hard-Constrained Learning via Structural Latent Parameterization

author.name: Wondesen Teshome Bekele, Marco D'Oria

entry.summary: SLP-ProbHard introduces Structural Feasible Latent Parameterization (SFLP), which defines a predictive law directly in a latent space mapped through a feasible function, so hard structural constraints hold in every stochastic realization without post-hoc projection or correction. This applies to probabilistic predictors where exact structure must be satisfied.

entry.title: Hierarchical Response Preservation for Continual Adaptation of Zero-Shot Graph-Text Models

author.name: Haopeng Zhang, Yuhan Wang, Yubing Su, Yingxin Chen, Xiao Wang, Ruijie Wang, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: HiRP addresses continual learning for pretrained graph-text models, where new classes can overturn historical predictions while overly strict response preservation blocks new-class learning. The method uses a hierarchical response that preserves each historical-class probability while summing new-class mass, balancing stability and plasticity.

entry.title: Depot-Closed Multi-Component Construction for Neural Vehicle Routing

author.name: Shinichiro Hamada, Hisashi Kashima

entry.summary: Proposes multi-component construction for neural VRP solvers, maintaining many route components simultaneously and merging them in arbitrary order, with a depot-closed interpretation ensuring every intermediate state is a feasible solution. This removes the early-commitment problem of route-by-route construction and improves global coordination across routes. It targets neural constructive solvers for capacitated vehicle routing.

entry.title: ConRAG: Lightweight inference of multi-hop relations

author.name: Kilian B\"anziger, Sonia Laguna, Markus Kreft, Robert Jakob, Kevin O'Sullivan, Lasse B. Strand, Julia E. Vogt

entry.summary: ConRAG formalizes multi-hop relation inference between two known endpoint entities, recovering bridge entities and evidence-grounded reasoning chains across a document corpus with an explanation grounded in retrieved evidence. Unlike typical multi-hop RAG that seeks an unknown answer entity, it explicitly reconstructs the connection between known endpoints.

entry.title: Optimal Networks for Agentic Information Aggregation

author.name: MohammadHossein Bateni, Zahra Hadizadeh, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz, Shayan Taherijam

entry.summary: Building on the Kearns-Roth-Ryu networked learning model from SODA 2026, this paper analyzes how agents arranged on directed acyclic graphs aggregate feature information via linear predictions and characterizes network topologies that achieve the global predictor's error optimally. It contrasts with prior focus on depth by optimizing over network structure.

entry.title: Transferable Mass Spectrum Prediction via Reference-Guided Test-time Specialization

author.name: Yunhua Zhong, Runting Li, Yifan Li, Pan Liu, Zhiwen Yang, Zikun Wang, Yixuan Tang, Jun Xia

entry.summary: SPARC is a retrieval-guided test-time adaptation framework that specializes pretrained tandem mass spectrum predictors using a spectral reference library without access to test-query spectra, recalibrating fragment intensities within the learned fragmentation space. It improves compound identification robustness under chemical-space and acquisition-condition shifts.

entry.title: Calibrated Derivative-Process Sensitivity for Gaussian-Process Variable Selection

author.name: Jia Cai

entry.summary: The paper develops a calibrated selection rule for Gaussian-process variable selection based on derivative sensitivity, showing that naive Wald and Bernstein-von Mises cutoffs are anti-conservative at null inputs and proposing a studentized multiplier approach. This addresses a genuine statistical gap where ARD lengthscales conflate variation speed with contribution. It provides a rigorous alternative to the default ARD ranking.

entry.title: GUIDE-FBO: Guidance via Uncertainty Intervention and Distributional Exchange for Federated Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Jintao Wei, Chenxi Li, Songhao Wang

entry.summary: GUIDE-FBO enables federated Bayesian optimization agents to exchange compact distributions over the locations of their optima instead of raw observations or surrogate parameters. A server merges and reweights these distributional components, and each agent builds a Federated Interventional GP that preserves local posterior structure while enabling knowledge transfer under communication constraints.

entry.title: Retrieving Biblical Intertextual References in Karen Blixen's Seven Gothic Tales

author.name: Andr\'as Kov\'acs, Alexander Conroy, Daniel Hershcovich, Jens Bjerring-Hansen

entry.summary: The paper constructs a benchmark of 189 annotated biblical intertextual references in Karen Blixen's Seven Gothic Tales, drawn from a critical edition's commentary, and evaluates retrieval against all 31,170 verses of historically plausible Danish Bible translations. It compares TF-IDF and BM25 with multilingual and Danish sentence encoders, examines linguistic normalization effects, and fine-tunes a Danish encoder with hard negatives and cross-validation. The work addresses retrieval where source text is transformed by paraphrase, allusion, historical language, and translation.

entry.title: Cross-Dataset Generalization of Bangladeshi Rice Leaf Disease Classifiers: Benchmark, Diagnosis, and Mitigation

author.name: Anindya Paul

entry.summary: Systematically benchmarks cross-dataset transfer for rice leaf disease classification across three Bangladeshi datasets with 6 transfer pairs, 3 backbones, and 3 seeds, diagnosing the substantial performance drops. Strong augmentation recovers a statistically significant +0.070 macro-F1, while segmentation-based removal of non-leaf content shows directional but not fully significant benefit.

entry.title: DPAMixerSR: An Efficient Degradation-Pattern-Aware Model for Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Song-Li Wu, Haonan Jiang, Jixuan Fan, Yufei Huo, Chubin Zhang, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: DPAMixerSR routes image patches to different compute paths based on degradation patterns rather than just texture complexity: a lightweight ranking module separates severely and mildly degraded patches, sending them to an adaptive sparse processing module or a lightweight convolutional branch respectively.

entry.title: ConvCue: Complementary Visual Inductive Biases for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Lan, Shichu Sun

entry.summary: ConvCue augments a pretrained VLM's native visual representations with features from a frozen parallel pretrained CNN via a learnable adapter, motivated by the complementary local connectivity and spatial weight-sharing inductive biases of convolutional networks. The goal is improving fine-grained discrimination and spatial understanding without replacing the native encoder.

entry.title: Transform-Aligned Learned Features for Lossy Point Cloud Attribute Compression

author.name: Yueru Chen, Pengpeng Yu, Dingquan Li, Wei Gao, Wei Zhang, Fei Song

entry.summary: TALF aligns learned spatial representations with the transform domain in point cloud attribute compression by explicitly applying the attribute transform to learned features instead of leaving the basis change implicit. The authors show these features exactly correspond to the first-order prediction term of a smooth nonlinear model with a bounded Taylor remainder, and integrate them into a codec with explicit rate control. This is a principled bridge between learned and classical compression frameworks.

entry.title: DeltaSeek: Toward Active Perception in Evolving Construction Environments

author.name: Sanjay Acharjee, Md Nazmus Sakib

entry.summary: DeltaSeek is an initial framework toward active perception in construction environments, which evolve continuously and degrade static mapping. The paper formalizes an embodiment's permissible observation set, addressing how a robot's sensing configuration constrains what it can observe, and evaluates a Husky A300 with a UR5e on an IFC-derived benchmark. The authors explicitly frame this as a prerequisite step toward systems that reason about where, how, and when to observe.

entry.title: CoBrush: A Hierarchical Planning Framework for Human-Robot Co-Painting

author.name: Dantong Qin, Yike Guo, Qinlin Liu, Alessandro Bozzon, Pan Wang

entry.summary: CoBrush is a hierarchical framework for multi-round human-robot co-painting on real acrylic canvases, separating high-level intent inference from spatial grounding and stroke-level control to support evolving human intent. Unlike single-shot rendering or sketch-completion systems, it sustains coherent long-horizon collaboration and progressive scene development. Evaluation includes real human-robot painting sessions.

entry.title: A Differentiable Optimization Framework for Registering Sequential Bounding Boxes with Point Cloud Stream

author.name: Xuesong Li, Jinguang Tong, Jie Hong

entry.summary: The paper folds temporal smoothness into a training-free 3D bounding-box registration objective solved jointly with L-BFGS over a LiDAR point-cloud stream, replacing the usual register-then-smooth pipeline that trades geometric accuracy for coherence. Gains are largest on well-observed tracks within a low-roughness budget.

entry.title: Phenomenon-Graph JEPA: Label-Efficient Representation Learning for Contactless Cardiorespiratory Sensing

author.name: Constantino \'Alvarez Casado, Nhi Nguyen, Mohammad Rakibur Rahman, Le Nguyen, Manuel Lage Ca\~nellas, Sasan Sharifipour, Miguel Bordallo L\'opez

entry.summary: The paper presents Phenomenon-Graph JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture for learning cardiac and respiratory waveforms from mmWave radar and RGB-D data without negative pairs or augmentation. It encodes four processed 1D streams to enable label-efficient representation learning where supervised acquisition sessions are costly.

entry.title: Geometric Inductive Biases for Semi-Supervised Equalization: The Constellation-Aware Transformer

author.name: Avi Caciularu

entry.summary: The Constellation-Aware Transformer (CAT) injects geometric inductive biases into channel equalization, using custom TransFIRmer blocks with an early-interaction paradigm to exploit known constellation geometry rather than forcing generic encoders to learn it. The goal is decoding over unknown channels with minimal pilot overhead in next-generation communications.

entry.title: Correction-space Cross-variate Interaction for Test-time Adaptation in Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yuanyuan Deng, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Songgaojun Deng

entry.summary: Identifies that existing test-time adaptation methods for multivariate time-series forecasting adapt variates independently, and proposes acting on adapter corrections in a dedicated interaction space to exploit cross-variate dependencies without mixing uncorrected errors. This avoids error propagation under delayed supervision in TSF-TTA.

entry.title: A Benchmark for LLM's Understanding of Middle School and High School Science Topics

author.name: Noah L. Schroeder, Yessy Eka Ambarwati, Yuji Zhang, ChengXiang Zhai

entry.summary: This paper introduces an NGSS-aligned benchmark for middle and high school science built with a rigorous synthetic data pipeline, multi-judge validation, and item-level psychometric analysis. Evaluations of nine open-weight LLMs suggest several smaller, locally deployable models perform adequately for K-12 science contexts. It fills a gap between general language benchmarks and advanced scientific reasoning benchmarks for educational use.

entry.title: Agentsensus: Consensus-Compressed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent Story Worlds

author.name: Yu Pan

entry.summary: Agentsensus replaces per-character private memories in story-world simulations with a unified long-term memory where records of shared events merge across witnesses and semantically related records link. Evaluated on four worlds including classical novels and Hamlet, it writes 22-44% fewer entries than per-character designs under equal granularity.

entry.title: Flat-Consensus Diffusion for Robust Data Reshaping under Noisy Evaluator

author.name: Hongyu Cao, Kunpeng Liu, Fei Xie, Sandip Ray

entry.summary: Frames feature-centric data reshaping as reward-guided diffusion generation and seeks robust transformations by searching for flat regions of the latent reward landscape rather than isolated high-reward points, addressing dual instability from noisy evaluators and stochastic generative trajectories. The approach targets stability and reproducibility of generated feature transformations under imperfect data conditions.

entry.title: Readout is not Recovery: Dissociating Coordinate Emission from Visual-Corruption Repair in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Drandreb Earl Juanico

entry.summary: This mechanistic study of Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (an existing model) shows that the layers responsible for emitting bounding-box coordinate tokens differ from those responsible for repairing localization when visual evidence is corrupted. Coordinate-token rankings are inert through layer 24 and load-bearing at layers 32-35, while corruption-repair signals behave differently across layers. The readout/recovery dissociation challenges assumptions in VLM interpretability work on spatial grounding.

entry.title: Improving LLM Collaboration via Multi-Agent Preference Learning

author.name: Shuo Liu, Xinzichen Li, Tianle Chen, Christopher Amato

entry.summary: This paper formulates preference-based multi-agent systems from decentralized and centralized collaboration perspectives and introduces MAPL, a general multi-agent preference learning framework that iteratively updates by comparing a current solution with decentralized or centralized solutions generated by other agents. It sidesteps the difficulty of constructing reliable reward metrics in multi-agent LLM collaboration by learning from comparative feedback. The framework extends preference learning, widely used for single-agent alignment, to multi-agent settings.

entry.title: TRACE: Learning to Self-Calibrate Wireless Digital Twins from ISAC Measurements

author.name: Saad Masrur, Saeed R. Khosravirad, Ismail Guvenc

entry.summary: TRACE is a physics-grounded learning framework that lets a deployed wireless network self-calibrate its 3D digital twin using its own RF and ISAC measurements, treating maintenance as residual alignment between the physical world and the twin model. It corrects errors in building position, height, footprint, and orientation that would otherwise cause propagation simulation failures. This matters for 6G-era network planning where digital twins increasingly drive decisions.

entry.title: DrafTS: Time-Aware Decomposition with Residual Correction for Time Series Modeling

author.name: Yiqiu Liu, Siru Zhong, Zhiguang Wang, Qingsong Wen, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: DrafTS is a model-agnostic framework for time series that decomposes signals using instantaneous amplitude and frequency features, capturing evolving dynamics in a primary component modeled by a task backbone while a lightweight corrector handles residuals. It aims to reduce noise without suppressing useful dynamics, unlike frequency filtering or observation suppression. This is a general-purpose improvement applicable across time series tasks.

entry.title: Federated Multi-Modal Human Activity Recognition using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Debasmita Dey, Tanmay Sen, Himel Mallick

entry.summary: This work proposes FedMHAR, a cost-aware multimodal human activity recognition framework that formulates sensor fusion as cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, where each agent controls a sensor stream with adaptive weights reflecting modality importance, cost, and quality, and extends the approach to federated learning for health IoT settings. It addresses fixed equal-weight fusion in heterogeneous wearable setups. Applications span rehabilitation and elderly care.

entry.title: Supervision Recovery for Time Series Anomaly Detection via Context-Anchored Pairing

author.name: Yifei Gao, Tian Lan, Yimeng Lu, Xuming An, Meng Wang, Wenjun He, Yijie Li, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CAPS, a framework for time series anomaly detection that recovers supervision by learning from simulated matched normal-anomalous pairs under the same temporal context, without needing target-domain anomaly labels. This targets the context-dependence of anomalies that unsupervised objectives handle poorly.

entry.title: Curating Merchant-Matching Training Data with Two Confidence-Gated Local LLM Judges

author.name: Donghao Huang, Jinling Pei, Zhaoxia Wang

entry.summary: For merchant-matching pseudo-labeling, the paper investigates whether agreement between two local LLM judges with separate ordered confidence thresholds for selections and abstentions improves label reliability, distinguishing true no-match from teacher abstention. Retrospective replay on 2,000 expert-annotated queries shows threshold tuning improves positive-label purity at coverage cost.

entry.title: Fuzzy Distribution Modeling for Synthetic Tabular Data Generation with Causality Preservation

author.name: Michael Vasilakakis (Department of Computer Science and Biomedical Informatics, University of Thessaly, Lamia, Greece), Dimitris K. Iakovidis (Department of Computer Science and Biomedical Informatics, University of Thessaly, Lamia, Greece)

entry.summary: The paper proposes generating synthetic tabular data using fuzzy set theory, representing feature distributions as fuzzy sets and feature dependencies via Fuzzy Cognitive Maps, yielding a low-parameter, interpretable generator with causality preservation. It targets the heterogeneous, non-smooth, incomplete nature of tabular data where deep generative models struggle and lack interpretability.

entry.title: APOLO: Automatic Prompt Optimization for Ontology Learning

author.name: Huu Tan Mai, Roman Kochnev, Cuong Xuan Chu, Lukas Lange, Heiko Paulheim, Daria Stepanova

entry.summary: APOLO casts ontology learning from text as automatic prompt optimization over LLM modules, using a multi-agent system to generate text-ontology training pairs from expert-curated ontologies. It optimizes greedy and autoregressive learner architectures with GEPA on DSPy, evaluated on biomedical and other ontologies.

entry.title: Nociception as a Control Primitive: Afferent Channels and Nociceptive Memory for Agents Deployed in One Body

author.name: Wolfgang Maass

entry.summary: A theoretical study of the epoch-one setting, where an agent in a single body cannot learn how fast that body wears without wearing it. The author introduces load-gated nociceptive channels and nociceptive memory with proofs about felt-cost allocation and when such channels pay off, drawing on the analogy of biological pain as a control primitive.

entry.title: From One-Shot Generation to Incremental Music Composition: Adapting a General-Purpose Instruction LLM for Persistent Symbolic Editing

author.name: Andr\'e Ricardo Ducca Fernandes, Jean-Pierre Briot, Simone Diniz Junqueira Barbosa1, H\'elio C\^ortes Vieira Lopes

entry.summary: The paper reframes music generation as incremental editing: a general-purpose instruction LLM acts as a reusable operator over a persistent ABC-notation score, performing chord addition, inpainting, and transposition as operation-aware state transitions with explicit preservation requirements. This contrasts with the dominant one-shot complete-output paradigm. It is relevant to interactive creative AI tools.

entry.title: Can Generative AI Automate Data Extraction for Meta-Analysis? A Case Study on Intercropping Research

author.name: Zehao Lu, Xingguo Xiong, Wopke van der Werf, Thijs L. van der Plas, Ioannis N. Athanasiadis

entry.summary: The paper rigorously assesses whether generative AI can automate data extraction from published literature for meta-analysis, using intercropping (crop species mixtures) research as a case study and comparing LLM outputs against human-labeled ground truth. Data extraction for meta-analysis is labor-intensive and complicated by non-standardized designs, units, and terminology. Rigorous ground-truth assessment is often missing from prior automation attempts, which this work corrects.

entry.title: FONDANT: Strong and Best-Effort Planning via Antichains

author.name: Benjamin Aminof, Tuan Khai Nguyen, Sasha Rubin

entry.summary: A theoretical planning paper on fully observable nondeterministic (FOND) planning that formalizes best-effort policies, which follow strong strategies where available and weak strategies otherwise, using antichain-based representations. It connects classical planning concepts to reactive synthesis and decision-theoretic principles of avoiding dominated strategies.

entry.title: A decision-support system applied to Law: Reasoning and explainability of the decision

author.name: Jeremy Bouche-Pillon (IRIT, IRIT-MELODI, IRIT-ADRIA, IRIT-LILaC), Pascale Zarat{\'e} (IRIT, UT Capitole, IRIT-ADRIA), Yannick Chevalier (IRIT-MELODI, IRIT, CNRS), Nathalie Aussenac-Gilles (IRIT-MELODI, IRIT, CNRS)

entry.summary: An IRIT group presents a decision-support system for law enforcement agencies that formally represents EU data-processing regulations (including the Law Enforcement Directive beyond GDPR) with an accompanying reasoning mechanism, providing explainable decision support for compliant data processing. It notes few legal-norm formalisms come with reasoning engines.

entry.title: Energy-aware frugal Bayesian optimization

author.name: Gaston Plat, Paul Saves, Nathalie Bartoli, Thierry Lefebvre, Joseph Morlier

entry.summary: The paper introduces a metric quantifying the computational energy footprint of models within a Bayesian optimization framework, guiding hyperparameter settings toward configurations balancing predictive performance and energy frugality. Experiments on scaled and multidisciplinary design optimization problems reveal tradeoffs between optimum convergence and energy use, and sometimes find both better optima and lower energy consumption. It addresses the often-ignored compute cost side of model selection.

entry.title: Toward AI-Assisted Poultry Coccidiosis Diagnosis: Evaluating Gemini and BiomedParse on Eimeria Microscopy Images

author.name: Ali Alsalama, Ahmed Kubba, Manar Abu Talib

entry.summary: This paper evaluates Google Gemini and BiomedParse for diagnosing Eimeria parasites from 4,225 poultry microscopy images, finding very poor species-level accuracy (14.9% with candidate labels) and inconsistent outputs without labels. The negative result quantifies how far general multimodal models remain from specialized microscopy diagnosis. It provides a useful reality check on medical AI claims in agriculture.

entry.title: Optimal transport meets speech: a tutorial review

author.name: Xugang Lu, Yu Tsao

entry.summary: A tutorial review connecting optimal transport (OT) theory to speech processing, covering distribution comparison and transformation while preserving geometric structure, with attention to speech-specific challenges like temporal dynamics, speaker variability, and multimodal audio-text representations. It aims to catalyze OT adoption in speech research, where it is underexplored relative to vision and NLP. Useful as a bridge between a mature mathematical framework and an underserved application domain.

entry.title: Automatic Speech Recognition for the Basa\`{a} Language: A Low-Resource Approach

author.name: Sophie Gertrude Ngo Mock, Charles Moudina Varmantchaonala, Paul Dayang, Jean Michel Nlong II, Christopher Gies

entry.summary: This paper develops automatic speech recognition for Basaà, a low-resource African language, applying modern approaches including self-supervised learning and transformer architectures in a data-scarce setting. It contributes to closing the gap where near-human ASR has disproportionately benefited a small fraction of world languages. Its value is primarily as a language-specific resource and case study in low-resource speech technology.

entry.title: Explainable Deep Learning of Resting-State Functional Connectomes Reveals Network Biomarkers of Adolescent Intelligence

author.name: Md. Tanvir Rahman, Nabil Anan Orka, Asaduzzaman Khan, Mohammad Ali Moni

entry.summary: The authors build an explainable deep learning framework using sparse projected residual networks to predict fluid, crystallized, and total intelligence from resting-state fMRI in 5,285 ABCD study participants. Multiple explainability methods identify brain network biomarkers associated with adolescent cognitive ability.

entry.title: E-CONAN (Entailment, CONtradition And Neutral) Diagnostics Dataset Investigating Linguistic Phenomena in Arabic Natural Language Understanding

author.name: Khloud AL Jallad, Nada Ghneim, Ghaida Rebdawi

entry.summary: This paper introduces E-CONAN, a diagnostics dataset for fine-grained error analysis of Arabic natural language understanding models across entailment, contradiction, and neutral categories, organized by linguistic phenomena. The authors highlight the lack of standard naming conventions for macro and micro linguistic categories in existing diagnostic benchmarks and propose a structured taxonomy for Arabic NLU evaluation. This matters because Arabic is understudied relative to English, and fine-grained diagnostic datasets enable targeted model improvement rather than aggregate score chasing.

entry.title: Beyond Fixed Features: Architecture-Dependent Sensitivity to Node Representations under Heterophily

author.name: Priyanath Maji, Sidharth Gaur, Rajavinoth Paul Durai

entry.summary: The paper re-evaluates seven GNN architectures on heterophilic benchmarks (Roman-Empire, Amazon-Ratings) while systematically varying node feature representations from static fastText vectors to contextual Transformer embeddings. It finds that conclusions about heterophily robustness are architecture-dependent and unstable under representation changes. This cautions against fixed-feature benchmark comparisons in graph learning.

entry.title: PrefLUT: Reusable and Refinable Personalized Color Editing from Pairwise Preferences

author.name: Chuanzhi Xu, Langyi Chen, Chengkun Yue, Xuanhua Yin, Boyu Wei, Qingwen Zeng, Zihan Deng, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: PrefLUT models persistent user color-editing preferences from ordered preferred/non-preferred image pairs, encoding them into a reusable user profile that is refined with additional pairs without per-user optimization, and predicts a 3D LUT latent and edit strength conditioned on each query image. It shifts personalization from one-off appearance matching to modeling repeated user choices in deployable photo editing. Practical for consumer photo applications.

entry.title: Eval4DiRec: A Unified and Systematic Evaluation Framework for Diffusion-based Recommender Systems

author.name: Cong Wang, Shoujin Wang, Yishuo Li, Qi Zhang, Liang Hu, Wenpeng Lu

entry.summary: Eval4DiRec is the first unified open-source evaluation framework for diffusion-based recommender systems, standardizing data processing, training configurations, inference, and evaluation protocols to fix irreproducible and unfair comparisons in this growing area. It should improve research reliability and enable fair benchmarking across the field. Utility depends on community adoption.

entry.title: From Preference to Reciprocity: Decentralized Matching with Empirically Grounded LLM-agent Based Modeling

author.name: Wangxuan Fan, Xiaoyu Nie, Zhoutian Shi, Xiangcheng Meng, Shipei Zeng, Pin Gao, Yan Hu, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: The paper combines LLM agents with contextual bandits for dynamic decentralized bipartite matching, demonstrated in a simulated Chinese marriage market where LLM agents evaluate candidates and per-agent Logistic-UCB models learn reciprocal acceptance from proposal outcomes. It separates preference formation from acceptance-probability estimation, extending Gale-Shapley-style matching to asynchronous, limited-information settings.

entry.title: JazzSAMBA: A Synchronous and Asynchronous Multi-take Band Audio Dataset of Jazz Standards for Live Music Models

author.name: Phillip Long, Jacob Nguyen, Jace Hosto, Gage Hosto, Jett Takazawa, Fares Nofal, Sebastian Stade, Nithya Shikarpur, Julian McAuley, Cheng-Zhi Anna Huang, Stephen Brade, Aleksandra Teng Ma

entry.summary: Introduces JazzSAMBA, the first originally recorded multitrack jazz-combo dataset of standards, with asynchronous overdubbed and synchronous live-ensemble protocols, musician-chosen preferred takes, and timed annotations for bars, chords, sections, and soloists across 76 standards. It fills a gap where music ML corpora skew toward pop and rock and lack improvisation-focused jazz data.

entry.title: GAC-PINN: Geometry-Adaptive and Constraint-Enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Yanxin Zhang, Yong Zhang, Houbiao Li

entry.summary: GAC-PINN addresses spectral bias and boundary constraint issues in physics-informed neural networks via gradient-driven adaptive grid mapping, adaptive bandwidth hard constraints, Gaussian Fourier feature preconditioning, and operator-aware routing. It targets systems with steep gradients and sharp interfaces.

entry.title: CMDO: A Cognitive Memory-Driven Optimization Algorithm for Adaptive Population-Based Search

author.name: Mohammed Yusuf Mujawar, Shahram Rahimi, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz

entry.summary: Proposes CMDO, a derivative-free population-based optimizer that stores search experience as context-behavior-outcome relationships across working, episodic, and consolidated memory, retrieving similar past experiences to guide future search with both positive and negative evidence. Inspired by cognitive memory structure rather than replaying previous candidate locations.

entry.title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model

author.name: Lindas Eloi, Goude Yannig, Ciais Philippe

entry.summary: Investigates whether socioeconomic indicators help medium-term electricity load forecasting (months to years), studying the impact of economic data across forecast horizons and resolutions using a time series foundation model. Targets use cases like plant maintenance scheduling, load dispatch, and price settlement.

entry.title: Elastic Selective Spectral Hybrids for Train-Once, Export-Many Budgeted Inference

author.name: Dachuan Song, Chuchu Chen, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces ESSH, an elastic spectral state-space model architecture where each Hankel spectral channel is an independent recurrent unit with fitted damped rotation modes, input-dependent decay, and write/read gates. This enables selective retention of relevant context and train-once export-many deployment of truncated models under different compute and latency budgets.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Time-Series Forecasting Agents with Episodic Memory and Online Policy Learning

author.name: Junyi Wang, Yilin Wang, Wen Wu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes an LLM-based time-series forecasting agent that operates online, accumulating episodic memory from past instances and adapting its action policy as ground-truth targets progressively become available. This addresses the limitation of existing forecasting agents that treat each instance independently and discard feedback.

entry.title: Over-the-Air Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Mobile Wireless Networks

author.name: Ming Xiang, Nicol\`o Michelusi, Yonina C. Eldar, Lili Su

entry.summary: The paper proposes FedOAG, an over-the-air federated learning method for heterogeneous fading channels that avoids the noise amplification of enforcing unbiased updates from all devices and the fading-model sensitivity and bias of partial-participation approaches. Algorithmic components are introduced to handle channel heterogeneity.

entry.title: Low-Rank Single-Index Bandits with Unknown Links: From Matrices to Tensors

author.name: Zhongxuan Liu, Yue Kang, Thomas C. M. Lee

entry.summary: This work studies stochastic matrix and tensor bandits with an unknown shared Lipschitz link function and low-rank index parameter, combining robust rank-adaptive Stein estimation with epoch-based greedy selection in the T-ESTOR algorithm. For monotone links it achieves square-root regret with dimension dependence governed by low-rank structure. It unifies previously separate lines on structured bandits and unknown-link single-index bandits.

entry.title: RAEGL: Risk-Aware Evidence-Gated Learning for Selective Contextual Routing under Temporal Shift

author.name: Yifan Guo

entry.summary: RAEGL is a framework for selective contextual forecasting that keeps a validated global predictor by default and activates a contextual residual only when pre-deployment evidence supports it, jointly checking randomization significance, practical gain, and temporal stability. It targets the problem of corrections learned on one time interval becoming unreliable under distribution shift.

entry.title: Short-Length Code Designs for Integrated Sensing and Communications: A Deep Learning Approach

author.name: Muah Kim, Shuangyang Li, Tayyebeh Jahani-Nezhad, Rafael F. Schaefer, Giuseppe Caire

entry.summary: This paper proposes an autoencoder-based framework for ISAC waveform design in noncoherent, short-blocklength settings, deriving a modified Cramér-Rao bound for multi-target delay estimation and analyzing ML decoding under correlated fading. The analysis reveals structural trade-offs between communication and sensing objectives, which the autoencoder then learns to jointly optimize.

entry.title: Posterior Regimes and Latent Deception: Variational Bayesian Inference in Hidden Markov Models for Sequential Fraud Detection in Financial Transactions

author.name: Joseph Uririoghene Obukofe, Anthony O'Hare, Chioma Sandra Dike

entry.summary: This paper presents a three-tier progression of HMMs (Baum-Welch, variational Bayesian, and neural VBEM) modeling customer transaction histories as trajectories through latent behavioral regimes, one identified as fraud-associated. The neural variant compresses 741-dimensional transaction features into a 64-dimensional latent space, revealing that regimes form ordered segments of a continuous behavioral manifold rather than discrete clusters.

entry.title: Evolution of fairness in multi-objective reinforcement learning framework

author.name: Jingyi Zhang, Xin Ou, Guozhong Zheng, Shengfeng Deng, Jiqiang Zhang, Li Chen

entry.summary: This work models the evolution of fairness norms via multi-objective RL, trading off material payoff maximization against fairness-driven moral behavior through a fairness pressure coefficient, departing from homo economicus game-theoretic assumptions. Simulations of agent populations explore conditions under which fairness emerges and persists.

entry.title: Beyond Site Agreement: Re-estimation for Brain Network Generalization

author.name: Yingxu Wang, Kunyu Zhang, Yanwu Yang3, Thomas Wolfers, Yujie Wu, Siyang Gao, Nan Yin

entry.summary: Proposes BRIO, a framework for cross-site OOD generalization in rs-fMRI that uses within-scan re-estimation of functional connectivity graphs to guide cross-site alignment, addressing the fact that site agreement does not guarantee stable predictive evidence. It maps full-scan graphs and their re-estimates into a shared structure to improve generalization.

entry.title: Learning Propagation Geometry from Message-Passing Feedback

author.name: Yingxu Wang, Kunyu Zhang, Xinwang Liu, Mengzhu Wang, Siyang Gao, Chang Tang, Nan Yin

entry.summary: Proposes GeoF, a recurrent GNN framework that jointly evolves node features and a per-node local SPD propagation geometry through message-passing feedback, initialized from structure-aware prototypes and parameterized in block log-triangular coordinates. Geometry determines neighborhood weighting while frame transport maps source messages into local coordinates.

entry.title: Context-dependent time-series prediction via HyperReservoirs

author.name: Kohei Tsuchiyama, Takatomo Mihana, Ryoichi Horisaki, Andr\'{e} R\"{o}hm

entry.summary: Proposes HyperReservoirs, an extension of reservoir computing for time-series prediction across multiple dynamical regimes, combining a main reservoir with a smaller context reservoir whose outputs modulate the main reservoir's output weights. This hypernetwork-like design retains the simplicity of reservoir training while handling regime changes. It targets prediction failure cases of standard reservoir computing.

entry.title: When Should a Satellite Estimate Be Changed? Stress-Testing Neural Corrections for Evapotranspiration

author.name: Marco Trotta

entry.summary: Evaluates neural residual correction models for satellite evapotranspiration estimates across 16,366 flux-tower observations from 151 stations, testing when corrections should be accepted or rejected. A naive gain selector accepted all 32 physically invalid records and worsened error dramatically, while the proposed SupportGain selector cut station-macro error substantially with far more conservative acceptance. A rigorous applied study on selective model correction under domain shift.

entry.title: Arbitrary-Accuracy Neural Approximation with Optimal Neuron Count and Near-Optimal Bit Complexity

author.name: Zilan Cheng, Li-Lian Wang, Zhongjian Wang

entry.summary: This approximation-theory paper constructs an explicit fixed activation function for which a two-hidden-layer network of widths d and 1 achieves arbitrary-accuracy approximation of Holder-continuous multivariate functions, proving d+1 hidden neurons is the exact minimum. It also provides a simpler floor-plus-exponential activation construction and analyzes bit complexity.

entry.title: Bounding Retraining Equivalence and the Deletion Floor in Materials Machine Unlearning

author.name: Can Polat, Mustafa Kurban, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: The paper defines a deletion floor baseline for machine unlearning in materials science, where prediction error after deletion is ambiguous because correlated retained structures sustain accuracy. It derives sharp intervals bounding an unlearning update's loss around this baseline and provides theoretical tools (neighbor bound, ridge identity) for evaluating unlearning fidelity.

entry.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold networks in nuclear binding energy prediction

author.name: Hao Liu, Jin Lei, Zhongzhou Ren

entry.summary: Applies Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs) to predicting nuclear binding energies from Atomic Mass Evaluation (AME2020) data, achieving 0.26 MeV RMSE that surpasses traditional models. Symbolic regression on the learned networks yields compact analytical expressions consistent with classical formulae like the liquid drop and Bethe-Weizsaecker models.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification of Next Generation Reservoir Computing with Applications to Memory-Driven Dynamical Systems

author.name: Livia Popa, Sumanta Basu, Martin T. Wells

entry.summary: This paper develops uncertainty quantification for Next Generation Reservoir Computing (NGRC) using Bayesian ridge and conformal prediction intervals, characterizing when the two agree or differ for forecasting memory-driven nonlinear dynamical systems. In high dimensions, regularization creates a tradeoff between estimation variance, shrinkage bias, and posterior uncertainty, yielding explicit regime transitions where Bayesian intervals become invalid while conformal intervals remain valid.

entry.title: Sliced Orlicz-Wasserstein

author.name: Binh Thuan Tran, Khai Nguyen

entry.summary: Introduces the sliced Orlicz-Wasserstein (SOW) distance, generalizing the sliced Wasserstein distance by replacing the Lp norm with a Luxemburg norm induced by an Orlicz function. The paper proves metric and topological properties, shows convergence implications including weak convergence, and derives sample complexity bounds for the distance and its powered form.

entry.title: Identifying the Predictable Drift of a Semimartingale from Marginal Laws

author.name: Jakub Marecek, Enrico Biffis, Abigail Langbridge, Robert Shorten

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies identification of the predictable finite-variation drift component of a semimartingale observed only through repeated cross-sections, connecting to Markovian projection and pseudo-panel regression in econometrics. When the drift is an affine functional of an observed lag window, estimation reduces to a convex quadratic program. It bridges stochastic process theory, econometrics, and ML-style estimation from population data.

entry.title: Mask-Induced Displacement in Audio XAI via Logit Trajectory Decomposition

author.name: Nico Garc\'ia-Peguinho (School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London), David Kelly (Department of Informatics, King's College London), Fabrizio Smeraldi (School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London), Anna Xamb\'o Sed\'o (School of Electronic Engineering and Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London)

entry.summary: The paper challenges the assumption that mask fills are negligible in perturbation-based audio explainability by proposing logit-space trajectory decomposition with on-axis and off-axis components. Across three fills, three classifiers, and 1,100 AudioSet clips, it shows no fill is acoustically neutral under full occlusion. This reveals systematic biases in feature-attribution estimates for audio models.

entry.title: High-Level Text Preprocessing for Semantic Similarity Analysis of Discursive Texts: A Framework and Empirical Demonstration

author.name: Mehmet Murat Albayrakoglu, Mehmet Nafiz Aydin

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode of semantic textual similarity methods on discursive documents, where similarity scores are inflated by shared vocabulary used to discuss and critique other positions, a phenomenon the authors call semantic diffusion. It introduces a high-level preprocessing framework operating above the lexical level to separate discursive engagement from substantive alignment, demonstrated empirically.

entry.title: Functional Autoencoders for Amplitude-Phase Representation Learning

author.name: Peida Wu, Xinyang Xiong, Pengcheng Zeng

entry.summary: The paper proposes Amplitude-Phase Functional Autoencoders, an unsupervised framework for functional data that factorizes the latent space into separate amplitude and phase embeddings across univariate and multivariate settings. A smooth functional decoder reconstructs channel-specific amplitude functions in canonical time, resolving the entanglement of temporal misalignment and shape that plagues prior autoencoders without explicit warping.

entry.title: N\"urnberg NLP at ChildSafeAds 2026: Structurally Dissimilar Voter Ensembles under Four Levels of Data Access

author.name: Philipp Steigerwald, Eric Rudolph, Jens Albrecht

entry.summary: The paper describes the Nurnberg NLP system for the ChildSafeAds 2026 shared task on monitoring commercial content in child-facing YouTube videos. It uses per-subtask ensembles of nine voters organized into three branches differing in backbone, adaptation method, and class scope, with selection via channel-disjoint cross-validation. The system wins two of three subtasks and places third on the task mean, also comparing four levels of data access and test-set-scale cost.

entry.title: Graph-Based Learning for Multi-Horizon Martian Atmospheric Forecasting

author.name: Gary Myler, James Holmes, Manish Patel, Amel Bennaceur

entry.summary: The paper introduces MaGMA, a graph-based framework that converts OpenMARS reanalysis data into structured learning objects for forecasting the Martian atmosphere across multiple horizons. Atmospheric patches become graph nodes connected by spatial, temporal, and dynamic-similarity links, integrating recent atmospheric history and engineered physical descriptors.

entry.title: CoLMbo-SV: A Grounded Language Model for Explainable Speaker Verification

author.name: Massa Baali, Sarthak Bisht, Ziyue Qiu, Joseph Konan, Rita Singh, Bhiksha Raj

entry.summary: CoLMbo-SV connects a pretrained speaker encoder to a language model to produce structured, acoustically grounded comparison reports, making speaker verification decisions inspectable without restricting verification to verbalized evidence. Also introduces VoxReason, a dataset of paired recordings with measured acoustic properties. Addresses the interpretability deficit in high-accuracy speaker verification systems.

entry.title: NSV-Shift: A Contrastive Benchmark for Non-Speech Vocalization Understanding and Response Adaptation in Speech-to-Speech Models

author.name: Ziwei Chen

entry.summary: NSV-Shift is a contrastive benchmark testing whether speech-to-speech models understand non-speech vocalizations like laughter or sighs and adapt responses accordingly, with pairs differing only in the embedded NSV. The pilot covers 22 human-verified pairs evaluating five models on NSV perception, emotion understanding, and response adaptation. Models detect NSVs better than they interpret fine-grained emotional meaning or differentiate responses.

entry.title: Pass or Fail? Evaluating LLMs on Two Greek Examination Benchmarks

author.name: Panagiota Kyriazi, Eleni Kasoura, Prokopis Prokopidis

entry.summary: The paper introduces Prot-Ex and Pan-Ex, benchmarks built from Greek Model/Experimental school entrance exams and the Panhellenic national university exams, to evaluate text-only LLMs across disciplines. It tests models including the Greek-adapted KriKri-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-4-26B, and Qwen-3-32B.

entry.title: QuanReview: Offline, Auditable Reconciliation of Human and LLM Span Annotations

author.name: Matteo Musacchio, Juan Cruz Giner Pulero, Isabel Casta\~neda, Naomi Couriel, Yelena Mejova, Mariano G. Beir\'o, Kyriaki Kalimeri

entry.summary: QuanReview is an open-source system for auditing and correcting structured span annotations (quantities, units, uncertainty modifiers, event classes) when LLM annotations are mixed with human ones. It aligns two annotation streams at character level, resolves unambiguous cases by an explicit logged policy, and routes conflicts to a browser-based adjudication interface supporting hybrids and re-annotation flags, with campaign management including redundancy and agreement computation. The focus is trustworthy, auditable annotation pipelines.

entry.title: Architecture-aware Robustness Evaluation of Explainable Deep Learning for Breast Cancer Diagnosis

author.name: Balenthira Thanusanth, Selvarajah Thuseethan, Roshan G. Ragel, Bimali S. Weerakoon, Ayesh Jayasinghe, Ananthamoorthy Krishnamoorthy

entry.summary: Provides a systematic evaluation of nine widely used XAI techniques across four categories of deep learning architectures (very deep, lightweight, transformer-based, hybrid) on a 780-image breast ultrasound dataset. Uses clinically aligned spatial metrics such as Pointing Game and Intersection over Union to assess explanation quality.

entry.title: LatentReRig: An SDF-Based VAE with Dual Decoders for Latent-Space Deformation Conditioning

author.name: Daniele Dolci, Fabrizio Poggioni, Carlo Melchiorri

entry.summary: LatentReRig explores whether pose transfer between topologically different characters can be modeled as reusable directions in a learned latent space, using an SDF-based VAE with one decoder for the implicit field and another for vertex positions conditioned on latent deformation. Results on controlled humanoid data show several poses induce coherent latent directions.

entry.title: HeroFrame-Bench: Reference-Anchored Evaluation via Rubric--Ranking Co-Evolution for Movie Hero Frame Selection

author.name: Weitai Kang, Hanieh Deilamsalehy, Yumo Xu, Dewang Sultania, Serdar Cellat, Yan Yan

entry.summary: HeroFrame-Bench introduces the task of selecting hero frames, the promotional stills used for posters and cover art, requiring joint assessment of content relevance and aesthetic appeal. The benchmark uses a scalable VLM-as-a-Judge framework with rubric-ranking co-evolution anchored to references, addressing limitations of existing keyframe selection benchmarks.

entry.title: Region-Local Copula Evidence Fusion for Heterogeneous Remote Sensing Change Detection

author.name: Zhiyuan Ji, Junjun Yin, Jian Yang

entry.summary: Extends superpixel copula models for heterogeneous remote sensing change detection by introducing region-local dependence anomalies within mixed superpixels, fused with regional confidence via reference ranking and an upper-tail gate. The paper derives region-dependent decision thresholds and identifies conditions where gating equals a reparameterization.

entry.title: A Multi-Dataset Benchmark of YOLO-Based Weed Detection in Precision Agriculture

author.name: Hristina Zdraveska, Vlatko Spasev, Ivica Dimitrovski, Ivan Kitanovski, Petre Lameski

entry.summary: Presents a multi-dataset benchmark of YOLO26 detectors (nano, small, medium variants) for weed detection across seven public datasets covering different crops, weed species, field conditions, and annotation protocols. It addresses robustness assessment beyond single-dataset evaluation in precision agriculture. The benchmark enables site-specific weed management decisions with reduced herbicide use.

entry.title: Functional Hand Type Prior for 3D Hand Pose Estimation and Action Recognition from Egocentric View Monocular Videos

author.name: Wonseok Roh, Seung Hyun Lee, Won Jeong Ryoo, Jakyung Lee, Gyeongrok Oh, Sooyeon Hwang, Hyung-gun Chi, Sangpil Kim

entry.summary: The authors introduce a functional taxonomy of hand types and use per-frame hand type labels as semantic priors for egocentric 3D hand pose estimation and action recognition. The prior improves interpretation of continuous hand-object interactions beyond purely geometric or physical cues.

entry.title: Semantic Modality Compensation for Unsupervised Visible-Infrared Person Re-identification under Unpaired Settings

author.name: Duanning Chen, Ke He, Bin Yang, Yongxiang Yao

entry.summary: The paper addresses unsupervised visible-infrared person re-identification when cross-modality identity pairs are incomplete, proposing to explicitly separate identity-discriminative content from modality-specific style before generating features for the missing modality. This avoids distorting identity cues or inheriting source-modality bias in the compensation.

entry.title: HPMD: A Historical Persian Manuscript Dataset for Word Spotting with Line-Level Annotation

author.name: Saeid Firouzi Daghigh, Majid Iranpour Mobarakeh

entry.summary: Introduces HPMD, a dataset of 223 pages, 3,678 lines, 37,631 words, and 130,630 characters from historical Persian manuscripts with line-level annotations to support word spotting without costly word-level bounding boxes. It addresses the near-absence of public historical Persian handwriting data for archival search.

entry.title: SPOC-Net: Single-Primitive Online Composition Network for GNSS Jamming Set Recognition

author.name: Zhihan Zeng, Kaihe Wang, Jos\'e A. L\'opez-Salcedo, Gonzalo Seco-Granados, Zhongpei Zhang

entry.summary: SPOC-Net reformulates GNSS jamming recognition as identifying a set of basic jamming components rather than classifying each mixture as a separate class, enabling generalization to unseen jamming combinations. It uses multi-resolution time-frequency features, learned component queries, a high-resolution branch to count active types, and a structured decoder to select a valid component set. This matters for resilient positioning, navigation, and timing in autonomous systems.

entry.title: Superquadric Primitive Decomposition of 3D point clouds via Geometric-Aware Inlier Refinement

author.name: Alessandro Rinaldi, Edoardo Tedesco, Andrea Ferraris, Filippo Leveni, Daniele Baieri, Filippo Maggioli, Simone Melzi, Luca Magri

entry.summary: The paper improves superquadric decomposition of 3D point clouds with a geometric-aware inlier refinement that goes beyond RANSAC-style proximity and residual criteria, reducing incorrect inlier assignments across adjacent or overlapping primitives. Superquadrics provide compact, interpretable shape representations.

entry.title: AI-Driven Collaborative Assembly Line Inspection: System Integration and Deployment Challenges

author.name: Asya \"Unal, Amr Okasha, Ege \c{C}{\i}rakman, Perin \"Unal

entry.summary: This systems paper describes the design, integration, and field deployment of an AI-assisted collaborative inspection cell at a kitchen-appliance factory within the AI-PRISM project. A UR10e cobot carries a machine-vision defect-detection pipeline while a Comau Racer-5 performs functional tests, coordinated via ROS 2 with multi-modal logging (camera, acoustics, electrical safety) visualized in Grafana. It documents practical deployment challenges that rarely appear in academic computer-vision papers.

entry.title: Human Motion Prediction for Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Placido Falqueto, Elena Basei, Edoardo Lamon, Giovanni Perantoni, Matteo Saveriano, Daniele Fontanelli, Luigi Palopoli

entry.summary: Compares three human motion prediction methods - GMM-based clustering, TransFusion, and Graph-Mixer - for use in human-robot collaboration, where predictions improve robot motion planning, safety, and efficiency in dynamic environments.

entry.title: VIDEAS: Distilling Explicit Action Semantics from Demonstration Videos for World Models via Prior-Guided Simulation

author.name: Jianan Wang, Haoquan Zhai, Siyang Zhang, Bin Li, Juan Chen, Jingtao Qi, Zhuo Zhang, Enze Wang, Haoxiang Jin, Chen Qian

entry.summary: VIDEAS is a data distillation framework that converts continuous physical dynamics from operational videos into explicit action semantics, deconstructing demonstrations into discrete action trajectories and using VLMs to extract structured knowledge of action preconditions and state transitions for world models. It targets world models that genuinely internalize causal physical laws. Its significance is in making world models reason explicitly about action preconditions.

entry.title: A Disk-Shaped Magnetoelastic Torque Sensor for Robotic Joints Using Permanent Magnetization

author.name: Bruno Brajon, Enrico Gasparin, Nicole Yazigy, Lisa Salamin, Florian Copt, Guzm\'an Borque Gallego, Elias Klauser, Ga\"el Close

entry.summary: The paper presents a compact disk-shaped magnetoelastic torque sensor with roughly 1 cm axial envelope for robotic joints, using a four-magnetometer architecture and custom magnetic shielding to achieve 1.34 percent full-scale accuracy at 50 Nm while rejecting parasitic forces and stray fields. Direct torque sensing enables precise force control where motor-current estimation is insufficient. It is a meaningful hardware contribution for force-controlled robots.

entry.title: Proprioceptive Force Estimation for Quadruped Locomotion and Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Run Wang, Xu Yang, Alapati Tuerxun, Yilin Mo

entry.summary: The paper shows that a shared 3D force estimate in newtons, inferred from proprioceptive history, can simultaneously support payload-force accommodation during quadruped locomotion and leash-force-based guidance of desired motion. An estimator and locomotion policy are jointly trained with supervised force and velocity outputs, and estimated forces map analytically to planar velocity and yaw-rate commands. Componentwise force RMSE of 1.44 to 2.83 N and improved velocity tracking over a domain-randomized baseline are reported.

entry.title: Decentralized Optimization with Cross-Coupled Mixed Affine Constraints

author.name: Ewsey Obzherin, Ilya Khomchenko, Natalia Shelegeda, Nhat Trung Nguyen, Demyan Yarmoshik, Alexander Rogozin, Alexander Gasnikov

entry.summary: Studies decentralized optimization where local and shared variables interact through two affine channels, showing that the intrinsic difficulty of combining well-conditioned channels is governed by their Friedrichs angle via a cross-coupling factor. The authors develop an accelerated decentralized method with matching minimax guarantees and confirm the predicted dependence experimentally.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Writer Adaptation for Real-World Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition

author.name: Paulo Grane Gabriel Silva, Lorenz Bernard Marqueses, Joel Ilao

entry.summary: Characterizes the domain gap between digital/binarized HMER training images and camera-captured real handwriting through fragmentation and stroke-width analyses, and proposes a writer-adaptive few-shot fine-tuning pipeline on MFH-CoMER with small author-specific datasets.

entry.title: CLAIRE: A Schema-Grounded Hybrid Workflow for Healthcare Administrative Form Completion

author.name: Garapati Keerthana, Manik Gupta

entry.summary: CLAIRE is a hybrid agent workflow for healthcare administrative form completion that separates field-state discovery, source-to-field mapping, deterministic validation, bounded correction, escalation, and audit tracing. It is evaluated extensively: five synthetic schemas, 1,000 records, 24,000 benchmark episodes, with direct-mapping audits of Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-7B (existing small models). The work targets the mundane but high-volume task of transferring structured clinical data into dynamic forms.

entry.title: Temporal Graph Learning of Wearable Actigraphy and Sleep Traces for Modelling Adolescent Crystallized Intelligence

author.name: Md. Tanvir Rahman, Nabil Anan Orka, Asaduzzaman Khan, Mohammad Ali Moni

entry.summary: SATURN models adolescents as 21-node temporal graphs built from daily Fitbit actigraphy and sleep summaries in the ABCD Study (6,091 participants), predicting crystallized intelligence while dynamically pruning invalid-day edges to avoid imputation artifacts. It handles irregular device adherence and behavioral-environmental interactions. This shows wearable-derived behavioral traces can scale cognitive assessment beyond episodic clinical testing.

entry.title: When Evidence Changes the Subject: Subject-Typed Claim Licensing for Learned Routing

author.name: Jian Chen, Zixuan Yuan

entry.summary: The paper addresses an attribution problem in composite AI systems: evidence may fail to support a component-level claim while still supporting a positive conclusion about the larger system. It proposes subject-typed claim licensing, separating weaker conclusions about the requested subject from positive but non-substitutive credit about another subject, instantiated for learned routing with search, repair, or external solvers. This sharpens how evidence-to-claim methods are evaluated.

entry.title: Mathematics for and by human cognition: A resource-rational search for bottlenecks in problem-solving

author.name: Sneha Aenugu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a theory that mathematical abstraction arises as resource-rational search for bottlenecks created by human cognitive constraints, arguing these constraints drive rather than merely limit advances in mathematics. It illustrates the theory with historical episodes and examines how cognitive constraints and affect shape formalism development.

entry.title: LLMs for Executable Multi-Agent System Specification Generation

author.name: Andreas Kouvaras, Periklis Mantenoglou, Alexander Artikis

entry.summary: genRTEC uses pre-trained LLMs to generate executable multi-agent system specifications in the Run-Time Event Calculus language from natural language descriptions, enabling run-time monitoring without formal-methods expertise or large labelled datasets. It handles complex temporal phenomena such as action intervals and environment effects.

entry.title: Fewer Assumptions by Design: A Reusable Skill for LLM-Assisted Verus Verification

author.name: Andrada-Livia Antoneac (Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Ia\c{s}i, Bitdefender), Dorel Lucanu (Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Ia\c{s}i), Drago\c{s} Teodor Gavrilu\c{t} (Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Ia\c{s}i, Bitdefender)

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM agents can synthesize strong Verus specifications for Rust implementations, particularly self-referential structures like doubly linked lists, while minimizing the trusted base of unproven assumptions. It compares manual verification, property-specific verification, and a defined reusable skill for DLL properties.

entry.title: Energy Vision--Language--Action: A Controlled Multimodal Benchmark for Intent-Conditioned Residential Energy Management

author.name: Lyes Saad Saoud, Oualid Doukhi, Ehsan Reihani, Saeed Sepasi, Deok Jin Lee, Moussa Ayyash, Reza Ghorbani

entry.summary: EVLA extends the vision-language-action paradigm from robotics to residential energy management, framing battery scheduling as multimodal trajectory prediction combining an RGB energy-field rendering, numerical state, and natural-language objectives mapped to 16-step battery-action trajectories from a sampling-based reference generator. It is a controlled benchmark built on public residential load data. This broadens VLA research beyond robotics.

entry.title: Frequency-Domain AI-Generated Image Detection: Exploring Decoder and Channel Attention for Feature Refinement

author.name: Uday Shankar Roy, Mahbuba Jahan Minu

entry.summary: The paper explores FFT-based representations with EfficientNet-B0 and alternative refinement modules (ECA channel attention, U-Net, Attention U-Net) for detecting AI-generated images in a lightweight architecture. It targets resource-limited deployment settings amid growing variety of image generators. The work is an architectural exploration rather than a new detection paradigm.
