entry.title: AirLog: Store-Level Indoor Life Logging Made Easy

author.name: Zihui Yun, Jiaying Du, Yue Yu, Zhewei Liu, Zhen Xiang, Longfei Shangguan, Zhenlin An

entry.summary: AirLog is a smartphone-based life journaling system that reconstructs store-level visits in shopping malls without radio maps or dedicated localization infrastructure, using ambient Wi-Fi SSID semantics and indoor directory images fused with inertial dead reckoning, then summarizing trajectories into journals with an LLM. This demonstrates a clever low-cost alternative to conventional indoor localization by repurposing cues already present in commercial spaces. It matters for ubiquitous computing and privacy-sensitive life-logging applications.

entry.title: Extraction of clinical findings from mammography and breast ultrasound reports: a comparison between specialists and Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Lorenzo Farias, Hanna Reckziegel, Daniela Duarte da Silva Bagatini, Daniel Schulz, Gabriela de Andrade Monteiro, Let\'icia Zanatta, Ana Laura Brill Thum, Priscila Schmidt Lora, D\'ebora Oliveira da Silva, Ana Paula Wernz da Cunha M\"uller, Cristiane Drebes Pedron

entry.summary: This study compares LLM-based named entity recognition via few-shot prompt engineering (using the existing Gemini 2.5 Flash model, selected from four candidates in exploratory tests) against manual extraction by health researchers on Brazilian Portuguese mammography and breast ultrasound reports, motivated by report turnaround times affecting breast cancer screening. It provides a practical, regionally relevant evaluation of LLMs for clinical information extraction in a non-English language. Results inform deployment feasibility for low-resource clinical NLP settings.

entry.title: SpikeLite: Lightweight Spiking Neural Networks for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Bang Hu, Changze Lv, Mingjie Li, Xiaoqing Zheng, Wei cao, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SpikeLite, a spiking neural network framework for time-series forecasting with two modules: a Frequency-Selective Spiking Encoder exploiting LIF low-pass filtering for frequency-sensitive encoding, and a Sparse Spiking Channel Attention module for selective cross-channel interaction. It emphasizes keeping SNNs lightweight rather than pursuing accuracy via complex attention or specialized neuron dynamics.

entry.title: Reverse Sequential Proportional Approval Voting Rule: Proportionality and Approximation Guarantees

author.name: Georgios Papasotiropoulos

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the Reverse Sequential Proportional Approval Voting rule in approval-based committee elections, establishing strong negative results for general instances alongside settings where the rule provides meaningful proportional representation and PAV-score approximation guarantees.

entry.title: "Where Can I Trust You?": Boundary-Aware Evaluation of Surrogate Fidelity

author.name: Jackson Eshbaugh

entry.summary: This paper studies where surrogate models disagree with their teachers, finding that agreement fidelity is substantially lower near the teacher's decision boundary across datasets and surrogate classes. It further shows that conditioning agreement on confidence-defined regions better predicts teacher-surrogate agreement when evaluation-set composition changes than a single global fidelity score. The work improves how surrogate (e.g., explanation or distillation) quality should be measured.

entry.title: Compositional Objectives: Learning Structure in Structure

author.name: Pranavchandra Vivekananda, Sumukh Bettadapura, Ajan Subramanian

entry.summary: Building on epiplexity as a measure of learnable structure through a bounded observer, the paper develops a closed-form spectral approximation to compute it and shows that a fixed-trace constraint makes the objective prefer uniform spectral mass distribution. The authors then address the gap between spreading information across directions and actually organizing it compositionally for goal-directed action.

entry.title: CAESAR: Clustering via Autonomous Embedding-Space Agglomerative Reorganization

author.name: Ilan Bacry, R\'emi Devaux, Antoine Jardin

entry.summary: CAESAR trains a reorganization network on pretrained vision or language embeddings to pull mutual nearest neighbors together and push non-neighbors apart, producing an embedding space better suited to nearest-neighbor-graph clustering methods like FINCH. Notably, it requires no prior knowledge of the number of clusters K, addressing a realistic unsupervised constraint.

entry.title: SIFT: Enhancing Time Series Foundation Models via Semantic Invariance and Structural Fidelity Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yi Tang, Tengxue Zhang, Yang Shu, Chenjuan Guo, Chenchen Sun, Yisheng An

entry.summary: SIFT is an adaptation method for time series foundation models that combats overfitting and the mean-prediction trap during fine-tuning. It uses semantic-invariant adversarial augmentation via semantic spectrum decomposition plus structural fidelity preservation, aiming to keep zero-shot generality while improving downstream performance.

entry.title: How Much Imprecision is Enough Imprecision in my Classifier? A Practical Elicitation Procedure

author.name: Victor F. Lopes de Souza, S\'ebastien Destercke, Abdelhak Imoussaten

entry.summary: This work develops practical elicitation procedures to measure how much predictive precision a user is willing to trade for accuracy when receiving set-valued predictions from conformal or imprecise-probabilistic classifiers. An iterative procedure converging to the target parameter is demonstrated on tabular and image data.

entry.title: Hidden Activations are not Enough I: Knowledge Matrices as Higher Representations

author.name: Marco Armenta

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies the knowledge matrix of a trained feedforward network as a higher representation of its inputs, factorizing the network function through a space of quiver representations and analyzing what determines the matrix, its invariances, and the geometry it measures under locally constant slope activations.

entry.title: ZeroCode: On-demand Error-Correcting Code Construction from the Zero Matrix via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ju-Hyeong Lee, Yongjune Kim, Sang-Hyo Kim, Dae-Young Yun, Hee-Youl Kwak

entry.summary: ZeroCode formulates error-correcting code construction as a discrete sequential decision problem, using PPO with action masking to build parity-check matrices edge by edge from the all-zero matrix, enabling on-demand codes meeting application-specific requirements. It achieves roughly 1 dB gain over prior RL-based construction at BER 1e-4 for the (32,16) code and outperforms existing methods.

entry.title: Deep kernel hedging

author.name: Jean-Loup Dupret, Donatien Hainaut, Edouard Motte

entry.summary: This paper combines deep learning flexibility with kernel method structure for hedging in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, parameterizing the kernel via a neural network embedding and supporting path-dependent information through signature features. It derives a generalized representer theorem and develops a random Fourier feature method for scalability.

entry.title: Disentangling Lung-Cancer CT/LDCT AI: A Systematic Evidence Map of Clinical Tasks, Evidence Chains, and Translational Gaps

author.name: Surajit Das

entry.summary: This systematic review maps 293 lung-cancer CT/LDCT AI studies (2016-2026) with role-aware task classification and a Multi-Tier Evidence Graph, finding detection studies dominate while external validation (29%), calibration (20.5%), and decision-curve analysis (13%) are rare. It identifies translational gaps between AI prediction studies and clinical utility.

entry.title: Neural Network-Assisted Refinement of Traditional Schemes for One-Dimensional Scalar Conservation Laws

author.name: Imre Fekete, Ferenc Izs\'ak, Vendel P. Kup\'as

entry.summary: Establishes a link between classical numerical schemes and neural network approximations for 1D scalar conservation laws, with networks that rediscover Godunov's method and emulate second-order slope limiters. The minimal-parameter networks can be composed into deep schemes, greatly reducing complexity versus prior learned-solver approaches.

entry.title: Recovering Lower-Dimensional Semialgebraic Support of a Measure from its Moments

author.name: Ruben Karapetyan, Shenyuan Ma, Ales Wodecki, Jakub Marecek

entry.summary: The authors tackle recovering a probability measure's compact semialgebraic support of codimension at least one from its moments, an open problem in the non-finitely-atomic case. They combine moment-matrix kernel information with Christoffel-Darboux kernels to produce a discrete support approximation, validated on analytic moments and polynomial-optimization pseudo-moments. This complements recent work on algebraic support recovery.

entry.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Information: Revealed versus Hidden Lotteries in School Choice

author.name: Parinaz Naghizadeh, Jingyan Wang

entry.summary: This paper analyzes whether revealing lottery tie-breaking numbers to students in school choice helps or hurts, challenging prior theoretical results that assumed uniform student preferences. Motivated by NYC Public Schools' recent practice of revealing lottery numbers, it shows the effect of revealed information is more nuanced when preferences are heterogeneous.

entry.title: Elicitation and Decision Geometry in Single-Index Bandits

author.name: Sakshi Arya, Cheng Soon Ong

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies two-arm contextual bandits with arm-specific single indices and a shared unknown monotone link, introducing Natural Boundary Learning, a greedy procedure using a sequential Stein contrast to learn the optimal boundary without estimating rewards or the link. It characterizes local Riemannian dynamics via a decision stability coefficient tied to the elicitation geometry of the underlying convex potential.

entry.title: SinBrief: A Hybrid Framework for Abstractive Text Summarisation of Sinhala Legal Documents

author.name: Minduli Lasandi, Nevidu Jayatilleke

entry.summary: SinBrief is a hybrid abstractive summarization framework for Sinhala legal documents that requires no human-annotated training data, combining domain-aware word graph construction with neural sentence scoring. It evaluates five scoring models including mBERT, Llama 3.1, Falcon 7B, LASER, and a continually pre-trained Llama domain-adapted to Sinhala legal text, using reference-free metrics. It addresses a genuinely under-served language and domain combination.

entry.title: BaatCheet: A Multilingual Corpus for Dialogue Translation in Indian Languages

author.name: Priyanka Dasari, Yuvrajsinh D. Bodana, Vandan Mujadia, Arafat Ahsan, Dipti Misra Sharma, Parameswari Krishnamurthy

entry.summary: Introduces BaatCheet, a corpus of roughly 49,000 dialogues for dialogue translation across five translation directions in Indian languages, addressing the sentence-level and formal-text bias of existing Indic translation resources. Fine-tunes five open-source LLMs across seven training configurations and shows fine-tuning improves dialogue translation quality. Valuable for extending machine translation to informal, conversational discourse phenomena.

entry.title: One Model Is Not a Crowd: Multi-LLM and Aspect-Conditioned Diverse Comment Generation

author.name: Nafis Irtiza Tripto, Delvin Ce Zhang, Mahjabin Nahar, Dongwon Lee

entry.summary: Investigates whether synthetic comment threads from LLM agents capture the diversity of human discourse, motivated by risks of homogenized AI content and model collapse. Hypothesizes that combining multiple LLMs with aspect-conditioned generation better approximates comment diversity, and evaluates this against single-model baselines. Relevant to simulating online discourse and preserving diversity in AI-populated comment spaces.

entry.title: Yor\`{u}b\'{a} in Unicode: An Overview of a Problem

author.name: K\'ol\'a T\'ub\`os\'un

entry.summary: This paper documents the long-standing failure of Unicode support for Yoruba and other African languages that require diacritics, where needed precomposed characters are not encoded, forcing reliance on combining sequences that behave inconsistently, corrupt under font substitution, and break search. It identifies Unicode's NFC normalization stability policy as the structural constraint blocking a fix. The problem affects publishing, web platforms, and mobile keyboards.

entry.title: Attribution Gaps in Zero-Training LLM+OVOD Pipelines: A Fine-Grained Analysis of the CAAP--SNAP Discrepancy

author.name: Yu-Feng Yen

entry.summary: This analysis examines why zero-training LLM plus open-vocabulary-detector pipelines show divergent class-agnostic localization accuracy (CAAP) and semantic naming accuracy (SNAP), using the full 5,000-image COCO-Val split rather than a small subset. It finds object visual complexity is not the driver; vocabulary novelty is, with localization accuracy dropping from 80.9% to 31.6% when the LLM's wording falls outside the detector's native categories, concentrated in specific mismatch types. The findings clarify a previously unexplained failure mode in these pipelines.

entry.title: Modernising the Compressed-Domain Video Captioner: A Controlled Study of SigLIP2 and GPT-2 Substitutions

author.name: Ashim Nepal, Ashok B. K

entry.summary: Performs a controlled ablation on the CoCap compressed-domain video captioning pipeline, substituting the CLIP I-frame encoder with SigLIP2 and the BERT-style decoder with GPT-2 under identical training conditions. The narrow question is which component is the binding constraint on accuracy.

entry.title: Dimension-Specific Imbalance and an Adaptive Hybrid Label Strategy for Multi-Task Affective State Recognition in Classroom Video

author.name: Xiangqian Li

entry.summary: The paper reanalyzes class imbalance in DAiSEE-based student affect recognition, showing imbalance magnitude and structure vary across affect dimensions up to roughly 79:1, so uniform fixes like focal loss fail in dimension-dependent ways. It proposes an Adaptive Hybrid Label Strategy mixing four-level and binary targets per dimension.

entry.title: Rate-Adaptive One-Step Diffusion Compression for AIGC Images

author.name: Nitiz Khanal

entry.summary: This is a challenge entry for ultra-low-bitrate compression of AI-generated images at 0.025 bpp, treating the task as rate-perception allocation with four rate-specialized fine-tuned checkpoints of the AEIC one-step diffusion codec and per-image allocation. It targets failure modes of conventional codecs on rendered typography, synthetic edges, and stylized micro-texture.

entry.title: StegGNN: Learning Graphical Representation for Image Steganography

author.name: Abhinav Kumar, Shorya Singhal, Agam Pandey, Tushar Kumar, Sukrit Jindal

entry.summary: StegGNN brings Graph Neural Networks, specifically Vision GNN-style architectures, into deep image steganography, replacing the CNN-based frameworks that dominate the field and suffer from limited receptive fields and spatial locality bias. Treating images as graphs offers long-range dependencies useful for hiding messages imperceptibly.

entry.title: Eyes on the Road: A Naturalistic Comparison of MTW Rider Gaze in Urban Indian Traffic

author.name: Prerak Srivastava, Bhaiya Vaibhaw Kumar, Kavita Vemuri

entry.summary: Presents the first large-scale naturalistic analysis of motorized two-wheeler rider gaze behavior in heterogeneous urban Indian traffic using the myEye2Wheeler dataset, extracting object-level gaze metrics with a YOLOv11 plus SAM2 pipeline under foveal and parafoveal attention modes. It finds functional division between monitoring and selective sampling and differences between novice and experienced riders. Useful for road-safety research and rider-training design.

entry.title: Normalise or condition? Noise-floor front-ends for on-board keyword spotting under UAV rotor ego-noise

author.name: Yida Lin, Bing Xue, Mengjie Zhang, Sam Schofield, Richard Green

entry.summary: The paper studies small-footprint keyword spotting on a UAV airframe where rotor ego-noise drives SNR negative, comparing classical noise-robust front-ends (CMN, PCEN, spectral subtraction), test-time adaptation, and two novel front-ends that track the per-band ego-noise floor and either subtract it or feed it as a conditioning channel. Evaluation includes streaming false-alarm rates over 4.4 hours of continuous rotor noise with cross-vehicle generalization.

entry.title: Reduced Cartesian Kinetostatics for Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots: Residual-Stabilized Full-Shape Propagation

author.name: Ke Wu, Fangju Yang, Xiaohui Zhang, Zhengqiang Zhang, Jingang Yi, Jian S. Dai

entry.summary: The paper presents a reduced Cartesian framework for planar, axially compressible tendon-driven continuum robots that propagates equilibrium backbone configurations along tendon-force and tendon-displacement trajectories. A Taylor-Galerkin reduction yields analytic reduced residuals and Jacobians offline, enabling first-order rate systems without online spatial quadrature or numerical differentiation.

entry.title: Proactive Motion Planning for Human-Robot Cooperation

author.name: Elena Basei, Edoardo Lamon, Matteo Saveriano, Daniele Fontanelli, Luigi Palopoli

entry.summary: Integrates a deep-learning graph-based human motion forecast into a proactive human-aware planning framework using a static roadmap and time-variant A* to modify UR5e manipulator trajectories, enabling proactive collision avoidance.

entry.title: Multi-Terrain Mastery: A Comprehensive Controller for Bipedal Locomotion

author.name: Oluwami Dosunmu-Ogunbi, Aayushi Shrivastava

entry.summary: The paper proposes a single locomotion controller for bipedal robots that handles steep wet grassy slopes and compliant terrains like sand, gravel, and rocks, extending prior work on stance ankle motors for stability. It targets eliminating the need for multiple terrain-specific controllers. Its value lies in practical robustness for real-world bipedal deployment.

entry.title: Why did it get Sparser?

author.name: Ololade117

entry.summary: A small-scale experiment modifying a transformer MLP so the bias term is computed from the input (Flexbias), finding that a 3.7M-parameter network with this change produced sparser representations under a ReLU SAE: fewer active features and lower mean L1, though higher reconstruction MSE. The author explores what this implies about inducing polysemanticity and sparsity at small scale.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient 3D Segmentation of Liver and Liver tumors: Depthwise factorization Scales Better Than Dense Convolution with Spatial Dimensionality

author.name: Adham M. Alkhadrawi, Mohammed A. B. Mahmoud

entry.summary: Shows that depthwise separable factorization avoids the cubic parameter growth of dense convolutions when moving from 2D to 3D, growing only 5% versus 200% for dense U-Nets, and builds a 3D liver segmentation U-Net with 536,990 parameters, 24x fewer than a dense equivalent. Results on MSD Task03 Liver indicate competitive performance at drastically reduced parameter counts.

entry.title: Agentic Network Traffic Monitoring

author.name: Manuel Tsoukatos, Hayden Jananthan, Jeremy Kepner

entry.summary: The paper proposes monitoring AI agents' network traffic as a record of their actions, using complex-valued hypersparse traffic matrices built on DBOS, the OneSparse PostgreSQL database, and GraphBLAS. An agentic simulator with variable numbers of agents surveying a virtual environment demonstrates the approach. It addresses the widening attack surface as agentic AI proliferates across industries.

entry.title: APEX: An Extensible Model for Agent-Assisted Production Scheduling

author.name: Felix J. Grumbach, Stefan G\"orlitz

entry.summary: APEX is an extensible production scheduling framework combining a general model with hybrid multiobjective search, where agents assist both scheduling (data preparation, natural-language scenario exploration) and model refinement (coding agents implementing and testing new constraints and objectives). Eight configurations are benchmarked against classical multiobjective evolutionary algorithms. It demonstrates practical agentic assistance in industrial operations research.

entry.title: SGG-ReflAct: Sub-Goal Guided ReflAct with Structured Planning for Reliable Long-Horizon Reasoning

author.name: Jaeho Jung, Sung Hoon Jung

entry.summary: SGG-ReflAct improves LLM agent reasoning by integrating sub-goals from a single-path LLM planner into the reflection process, addressing belief drift in long-horizon tasks. A beam-search variant, BeamSGG-ReflAct, extends the approach with structured planning over multiple candidate plans.

entry.title: Automated feature engineering, AutoML, and decision-focused learning for improved energy consumption forecasting

author.name: Nasser Alkhulaifi

entry.summary: This thesis establishes a comprehensive feature-engineering pipeline for energy consumption forecasting and introduces AutoEnergy, a domain-tailored automated feature-generation algorithm producing interpretable features from timestamps and lagged consumption, integrated with AutoML and decision-focused learning. It was evaluated across eighteen real-world energy datasets. The work reduces dependence on expert-driven feature engineering in energy management.

entry.title: 5W1H+Which: Context-Valid Semantic Indexing with Progressive Ontology Binding

author.name: Yaxiao Liu (PwC China AI Center), Pengbo Liu (PwC China AI Center), Yiwen Liu (PwC China AI Center), Yihua Guan (PwC China AI Center), Jiaxing Song (Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: From the same PwC/Tsinghua group, this paper proposes a semantic indexing design that separates content extraction (organized by 5W1H questions) from ontology binding (a Which pointer to versioned ontology elements with scope and validation status). This supports rule-based reasoning with checkable premises while avoiding premature commitment to a single business schema.

entry.title: Enhancing Foundation Models for Imbalanced SAR Ship Classification via Targeted Oversampling

author.name: Ch Muhammad Awais, Marco Reggiannini, Davide Moroni

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks remote-sensing foundation models DOFA and SAR-JEPA on the imbalanced OpenSARShip dataset against ImageNet-pretrained baselines under a frozen-backbone protocol, applying four embedding-space oversampling methods to minority classes before training a lightweight classifier head. Oversampling consistently improves Macro-F1 and accuracy, with the largest gain for DOFA using ADASYN. It characterizes foundation-model behavior under severe long-tail imbalance.

entry.title: A Comparative Transfer-Learning Study of CNN Backbones for Partial Face Recognition on the SoF Dataset

author.name: Ahmed Kubba, Ali Alsalama, Abdelrahman Abdalla, Qassim Nasir, Manar Abu Talib

entry.summary: This study compares ResNet-50, VGG-16, and FaceNet backbones fine-tuned for partial face recognition under identical protocols on the Specs-on-Faces dataset. It addresses the practical problem that real-world faces are often occluded or cut off at frame edges. The FaceNet-based configuration performs best under controlled comparison conditions.

entry.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Equity Trading: Benchmarking Actor-Critic Methods with Forward Retraining

author.name: Bicheng Wang, Xinyi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks five deep RL actor-critic methods (A2C, PPO, DDPG, TD3, SAC) for end-to-end equity trading against a supervised price-forecasting baseline, using daily data for 20 S&P 500 stocks from 2000-2020 with technical indicators. Agents are evaluated both trained once and under forward retraining across successive test windows. It provides a useful, methodologically careful comparison in a domain where RL claims often lack rigor.

entry.title: From Granular Revision Operations to Meaningful Revision Units: Evaluating LLMs for Revision Boundary Detection

author.name: Yu Tian, Andrew Potter, Katerina Christhilf, Motahareh Darvishpour Ahandani, Jessica Early, Steve Graham, Danielle S. McNamara

entry.summary: The study evaluates whether LLMs can detect meaningful revision unit boundaries in students' writing process traces, comparing zero- and few-shot GPT-5.5, base and fine-tuned Qwen3-32B, and a majority baseline on 113 draft-revision pairs with 4,344 expert-annotated boundaries. Better revision segmentation improves learning analytics about writing processes. It grounds an educational NLP task in careful human annotation.

entry.title: VL-AcneSeg: A Vision-Language Framework for Region-Aware Acne Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Sukju Oh, Soo Ick Cho, Dae Hun Suh, Sukkyu Sun

entry.summary: VL-AcneSeg leverages CLIP with region-level text prompts to incorporate spatial priors for acne lesion segmentation across the whole face, supporting area-based acne assessment over subjective grading. It reports a single global prompt setting requiring no region annotation as its primary configuration. On an internal clinical dataset it improves Dice scores over general-purpose segmentation baselines.

entry.title: SincDPNet: Interpretable Raw-Waveform Bathroom Activity Recognition for Assistive Living

author.name: Debolina Chowdhury, Suman Samui, Sujoy Saha

entry.summary: Presents a seven-class bathroom acoustic-event dataset with 21,387 annotated clips recorded across five environments, plus SincDPNet, a compact raw-waveform classifier using a learnable sinc filter bank and depthwise-separable convolutions. The model is interpretable (passbands inspectable in Hz) and designed for robustness to room changes, supporting assistive living where video monitoring is undesirable.

entry.title: CarveMix-RC: Addressing Rare-Class Imbalance Through Lesion-Aware Synthetic Augmentation for Brain Metastasis Segmentation

author.name: Md Shibly Sadique, Md Fayaz Bin Hossen, Michael L. Evans, Walia Farzana, Asfaqur Rahman, Ahmed Temtam, Khan M. Iftekharuddin

entry.summary: This work proposes lesion-aware synthetic augmentation to address rare-class imbalance in segmentation of post-treatment brain metastases, targeting the resection cavity class in the BraTS-MET 2026 challenge. It builds on nnU-Net to prevent dominant tumor classes from crowding out low-prevalence subregions.

entry.title: Spectral Super-Resolution using Spatial-Spectral Residual Operator Networks

author.name: Seokhyun Chin

entry.summary: SSRON is a Deep Operator Network that learns mappings from downsampled multispectral satellite spectra to continuous hyperspectral spectra, targeting Sentinel-2A-like to EMIT imagery. It outperforms baselines across metrics, enabling cheaper high-resolution hyperspectral remote sensing.

entry.title: Beyond the Graph: An Adaptive Meta-Learner Fuses Explainability, Weather, and Dynamics for Robust Bus ETA Prediction

author.name: Pratham Payra, Jagadish

entry.summary: Proposes HYB(nm), an adaptive hybrid ensemble that fuses five models including historical baselines, Koopman neural operators, weather-integrated networks, and graph convolutional networks via a real-time context-attuned meta-learner for bus ETA prediction. Evaluated on GPS and weather data from three Kolkata bus routes.

entry.title: Fisher Simplicity in Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks and Multilayer Perceptrons

author.name: Ami Tavory, Meir Feder

entry.summary: The paper compares architectural notions of simplicity in KANs (small or zero basis coefficients, analogous to dead ReLUs in MLPs) with Fisher nullity, a statistical notion of when parameter perturbations are invisible to the task. It proves that the two notions agree for dead ReLUs but diverge for fixed-basis KANs, sharpening what KAN interpretability signals actually certify.

entry.title: AnchorMixGAN: Anchor-Aligned Generative Semi-Supervision for DDoS Detection in Cloud-Integrated IoT Networks

author.name: Jin Yang, Xufeng Liu, Yong Hu, Xueyang Wang, Honglu Yang, Gang Li

entry.summary: AnchorMixGAN is a generative semi-supervised framework for detecting DDoS attacks in cloud-integrated IoT networks when labeled traffic is scarce. It treats each real unlabeled flow as an anchor, creates alternative views by substituting field groups with generated traffic values, and stabilizes pseudo-targets via a frozen reference classifier.

entry.title: Adaptive Ensemble Selection for Noisy Labels on Tabular Data

author.name: Faizaan Ali, Inwon Kang, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: This paper proposes a meta-model that diagnoses dataset quality and selects among diverse label-noise detectors (confidence-based, neighborhood-based, distributional) for tabular data, designed as a data-centric module for automated data science workflows. It matches or exceeds individual detectors on benchmarks with controlled noise. The work targets a practical pain point in AI-augmented data preparation.

entry.title: LTV-CTDNet: Compositional Turning Decomposition for Short-Term Turning-Movement Forecasting

author.name: Md Atiqur Rahman Mallick, Kamrul Hasan, Robert T. White

entry.summary: LTV-CTDNet is a forecasting framework for short-term turning-movement counts at intersections that enforces structurally admissible outputs, avoiding physically impossible negative counts and tying outputs to approach-demand totals. It is evaluated on seven months of 15-minute LiDAR observations from eight corridor locations in Nashville.

entry.title: Cardinality-Stratified Interaction Decomposition for Interpretable Pairwise and Higher-Order Structure in Transactional Basket Data

author.name: Hidetoshi Kawase, Toshihiro Ota

entry.summary: This paper introduces CSID, an interpretable framework for transactional basket data that decomposes log-odds contrasts stratified by remaining item count into item-set-specific and cardinality-common components, avoiding a global joint distribution fit. It uses an information-weighted, gauge-constrained ridge projection to estimate pairwise and triple interactions and diagnose higher-order contributions.

entry.title: LLN: Learnable Lens Networks for Parameter-Efficient Long-Horizon Dynamical Prediction

author.name: Binbin Yong, Zhao Su, Lan Guo, Haoran Li, Jun Shen, Qingguo Zhou

entry.summary: LLN is a physics-inspired architecture that replaces residual feature-space accumulation with learnable optical transport in an augmented position-angle phase space, alternating free propagation with a learnable lens field. It targets parameter-efficient long-horizon dynamical prediction with theoretical guarantees on feature-geometry evolution.

entry.title: EvE: An Alternate Optimizer to Adam

author.name: Shashank Raj, Kalyanmoy Deb

entry.summary: EvE is a steady-state population-of-four differential evolution optimizer with targeted Adam fallback, designed to rank configurations cheaply for hyperparameter and architecture search rather than to out-train Adam on a single run. The authors prove monotone best-so-far improvement on deterministic objectives and bounded per-iteration cost.

entry.title: Accurate Sampling from Diffusion Models

author.name: D\'enes Sexty

entry.summary: Proposes DM-SMC, combining diffusion models trained on samples from a field-theory ensemble with sequential Monte Carlo to achieve accurate sampling despite an approximate diffusion model and finite discretization stepsize. Demonstrated on 2D Z2 scalar field theory near its second-order phase transition, with improved update strategies also explored.

entry.title: All On-Board: Fully On-Chip Neuromorphic Q-Learning with Embedded CartPole Simulation

author.name: Steven C. Nesbit, Giovanni T. Michel, Gerd J. Kunde, Edward Kim, Andrew T. Sornborger

entry.summary: The authors implement a fully on-chip closed-loop reinforcement learning agent on Intel's Loihi 2 neuromorphic hardware, embedding both the Q-learning algorithm and a CartPole-v0 environment simulation on the chip itself. This demonstrates end-to-end, low-power neuromorphic RL for resource-constrained control settings without off-chip compute. A systems demonstration relevant to energy-efficient edge AI.

entry.title: VCRE-Fib: View-Conditioned Regional Evidence for Fine-Grained Ultrasound Grading of Schistosoma japonicum-Associated Liver Fibrosis

author.name: Ziyang Xu, Shuli An, Hao Zhou, Haitian Zhong, Tingting Wu, Tao Wang, Kun Yang, Tieyong Zeng

entry.summary: Presents VCRE-Fib, a view-conditioned framework for fine-grained ultrasound grading of Schistosoma-associated liver fibrosis that integrates anatomical context, local regional evidence, and global image assessment while retaining spatial interpretability. This targets a neglected parasitic disease important in endemic regions.

entry.title: A Visual Classification Dataset and Model Evaluation for Historical Manuscript Illustrations

author.name: Yoav Evron, Michal Bar-Asher Siegal, Michael Fire

entry.summary: The paper introduces a manually labeled dataset of 15,000 illustrations from historical manuscripts spanning 22 categories, along with evaluations of modern vision models on classification. The task is hard due to stylistic diversity and degradation, and the dataset enables scalable exploration of large digitized manuscript collections. It fills a real gap in digital humanities resources.

entry.title: Two-Sample Testing for Inhomogeneous Random Graphs in Non-Integral $L_r$ Norms

author.name: Soham Dan

entry.summary: The paper addresses two-sample testing of network populations under the inhomogeneous Erdos-Renyi model in non-integer Lr norms for r greater than 2, where prior upper and lower bounds did not match. It proposes a test combining two published statistics of orders 2 and the ceiling of r, with thresholds derived via Hoelder interpolation to close the theoretical gap.

entry.title: Toward Embedding-Based Psychometrics: Structural Modeling of Assessment-Item Semantics With Contextual Scores

author.name: Jinsong Chen, Shi-Ting Chen

entry.summary: The paper examines the semantic structure of contextual scores for 40 TIMSS mathematics assessment units using a two-step factor procedure, identifying a persistent seven-group structure with a general dimension. It analyzes how item-to-reference-word similarities organize into recurring, cross-domain, sensitive, and imposed associations. The work proposes embedding-based psychometrics as a bridge between representation learning and educational measurement.

entry.title: Deep Learning Methods in Neuroscience: From Modeling Molecular Mechanisms to Classifying States of Consciousness

author.name: Elena Benderskaya, Anastasiia Alifanova, Svetlana Batalova, Vasilisa Zhuk, Anna Kovalenko

entry.summary: This is a critical review of deep learning approaches for studying conscious states, covering EEG/fMRI-based classification of consciousness, modeling brain dynamics under anesthesia, and identifying neurophysiological correlates of consciousness levels. It comparatively analyzes three major research areas and concludes that deep neural models are increasingly effective for classifying and predicting conscious states.

entry.title: Gaussian Image Steganography via Parameter-Domain Keyed Embeddings

author.name: Tong Wu, Runze Cheng, Xiaoyue Fan, Kaan Ak\c{s}it

entry.summary: This work embeds secret messages within the parameters of 2D Gaussian image representations rather than image pixels, using a secret key to select parameters for fine-tuning. Experiments show correct keys recover the message without error while wrong keys yield a bit error rate near random guessing.

entry.title: Synthetic Thermal Image Generation for Real-Time Animal Detection Under Low-Visibility Conditions

author.name: James Momoh, Khandaker Mamun Ahmed

entry.summary: The paper explores translating a small set of annotated visible-spectrum animal images into synthetic thermal imagery using CycleGAN-Turbo to overcome the scarcity of annotated infrared wildlife data, targeting wildlife-vehicle collision detection at night. It evaluates whether synthetic thermal data can support real-time animal detection where RGB perception fails.

entry.title: Recent Advances in Agentic Agri-Robotic Phenotyping: A Perspective Review from Fragmented Multimodal Sensing to Unified PhenoAgent Intelligence

author.name: Muhammad Owais, Ehtesham Iqbal, Samee Ullah Khan, Muhammad Umraiz, Yusra Abdulrahman, Irfan Hussain

entry.summary: A perspective review of plant phenotyping tracing the shift from manual trait measurement to robotic, AI-driven crop monitoring, arguing that current systems remain fragmented across sensing modalities, traits, and environments. It proposes framing phenotyping as an integrated seed-soil-plant-environment-management intelligence problem and outlines a unified agentic PhenoAgent direction.

entry.title: Evaluating Hierarchy-Aware Deep Learning for the Recognition of Tironian Notes

author.name: Yule Kang, Thomas Gorges, Janne van der Loop, Franziska Marske, Nikolaus Weichselbaumer, Tino Licht, Vincent Christlein

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether structural relationships between Tironian notes, the first Latin shorthand system with a large fine-grained symbol inventory, can improve automatic recognition where training data are scarce. It uses the Supertextus Notarum Tironianarum lexicon and evaluates hierarchy-aware classifiers against flat baselines. The work makes inaccessible historical manuscripts more tractable and doubles as a study of hierarchy exploitation under few-shot conditions.

entry.title: Impact of Patient Orientation in Single- and Multi-View Camera Environments for AI-based Rehabilitation Monitoring

author.name: Miriama J\'ano\v{s}ov\'a, Andreas Lang, Petra Budikova, Jan Sedmidubsky

entry.summary: The authors introduce REHAB26-ViewAngles, a dataset of correct and incorrect rehabilitation exercise executions captured from many camera angles, plus a separability metric quantifying how well pose-estimation algorithms distinguish valid from faulty repetitions. They analyze how RGB pose estimation performs for exercise quality assessment across camera placements.

entry.title: An integrated geometric quantification and shape analysis framework for axillary lymph node metastasis in breast cancer patients

author.name: Zixi Yi, Limeng Qu, Gary P. T. Choi

entry.summary: The paper presents a framework combining topology-aware surface processing with multi-resolution spherical harmonic analysis of CT-derived axillary lymph nodes to quantify morphology associated with breast cancer metastasis. The pipeline produces topology-valid genus-0 surfaces and characterizes them with 20 predefined shape descriptors at multiple SH degrees.

entry.title: Observability-Informed Optimal Sensor Placement for Soft Robots

author.name: Samuel Smocot, James Richard Forbes, Audrey Sedal

entry.summary: The paper applies and experimentally evaluates a convex-optimization method for optimal sensor placement in soft robots, maximizing an observability Gramian-based metric, validated with position and strain sensing on a soft continuum arm where Kalman filter estimates improve reconstruction by millimeter-scale amounts. It demonstrates that classical linear control tools generalize across soft robot morphologies when accounting for dynamics. Its value is a principled, experimentally-grounded placement methodology.

entry.title: Residual Learning-Based Control of Vehicle Platoons with $\ell_2$ Stability Guarantees via Recurrent Equilibrium Networks

author.name: Brian Delgado, Anh-Tu Nguyen, Hamid Taghavifar

entry.summary: The paper proposes residual learning control for heterogeneous vehicle platoons, combining an LMI-designed nominal controller with disturbance-observer compensation and an offline-trained Recurrent Equilibrium Network constrained to satisfy a prescribed l2-gain bound, guaranteeing small-gain closed-loop and string stability. Experiments show reduced spacing and velocity errors. It matters as a certified-safe pattern for learning-augmented vehicular control.

entry.title: Phylogeny-agnostic strain-level prediction of phage–host interactions from genomes using machine learning

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Microbiology research article, based on its title, presenting a machine learning approach that predicts strain-level phage-host interactions directly from genome sequences without relying on phylogenetic assumptions. No body text was supplied, so the analysis relies on the title alone.

entry.title: Re-derivability Decides What a Staged Agent Pipeline Recovers After an Upstream Fault

author.name: Tianqi Bu, YuXuan Peng, Junteng Tu, Henghui Xiao

entry.summary: This paper identifies re-derivability — how much of what a downstream pipeline stage needs can be rebuilt from the original problem — as the variable governing recovery after an upstream fault in staged LLM-agent pipelines. Grounding an inspector agent in the original problem yields large accuracy gains over a blind inspector across four open-weight backbones, tested on 120 gsm_hard items per arm at temperature zero. The authors explicitly frame the head-to-head comparison as exploratory.

entry.title: MAC-Net: A Multi-Task Deep Learning Framework for Modeling Cognitive Function From Task-Based fMRI

author.name: Md. Tanvir Rahman, Nabil Anan Orka, Asaduzzaman Khan, Mohammad Ali Moni

entry.summary: MAC-Net is a covariate-aware deep learning framework for individual-level cognitive function prediction from task-based fMRI, isolating neural features into a dedicated pathway and restricting demographic and scanner variables to a late-fusion pathway. This prevents dominant covariates from suppressing high-dimensional clinical representations. It is evaluated on 6,500 participants from the ABCD Study baseline.

entry.title: GERIS: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Filtering Instance-Dependent Label Noise in License Plate Data Augmentation

author.name: Seyedeh Sara Jalili Shani (Department of Computer Science, University of Alberta, Alberta, Canada), Rouhollah Ahmadian (Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Amirkabir University of Technology, Iran), Amin Rahmani (Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Amirkabir University of Technology, Iran), Mahdi Bideh (Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Amirkabir University of Technology, Iran), Mehdi Ghatee (Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Amirkabir University of Technology, Iran)

entry.summary: GERIS formulates augmentation-instance selection as a non-cooperative game in which synthetic license plate images with noise vectors compete for inclusion in training based on similarity to labeled data and reliability contribution. Pruning low-quality augmented instances reduces instance-dependent label noise. The framework improves license plate recognition training data quality.

entry.title: Sharp Critical Minimax Laws and No-Learning Thresholds in Continuous-Time Adaptive Control

author.name: Chen Jia

entry.summary: Proves sharp minimax improvement laws for episodic continuous-time adaptive control with unknown control gain, establishing a critical rate with matching upper and lower bounds near a no-learning threshold. The analysis uses a uniform deficit-energy inequality and a moving soft-threshold feedback controller attaining the rate.

entry.title: LukeNet: A lightweight CNN integrated with an XAI model for Smart acute lymphoblastic leukemia detection and management

author.name: Md Taimur Ahad (Department of Management Information Systems, North South University, Bangladesh)

entry.summary: LukeNet is a lightweight CNN for acute lymphoblastic leukemia detection designed for edge deployment in Internet of Medical Things environments, integrated with explainable AI and wearable-derived patient monitoring data. The work aims to move ALL detection from theoretical systems to deployable real-time clinical support. It combines diagnostic imaging classification with IoMT-based patient management.

entry.title: Vibe Analysis: Exploring LLM Adoption by Data Visualization Practitioners

author.name: Shani C Spivak, Aditi Krishna, Mahsan Nourani, Melanie Tory

entry.summary: This HCI study conducts semi-structured interviews with Data Visualization Society members about LLM adoption, finding that visualization designers use LLMs for creative and technical aspects of their workflow and documenting an emerging workflow the authors call vibe analysis, analogous to vibe coding. It surfaces key challenges practitioners face with error-prone LLMs in visualization tasks. This offers rare qualitative grounding for how LLMs reshape data work practices.

entry.title: Beyond Tasks: A Vision for Reproducing an Animal-like Behavioral Substrate Using Modern Robot Learning Techniques

author.name: Samiyuru Menik, Hemadri Jayalath

entry.summary: A position paper proposing the ethological behavioral substrate as a lens for studying continual situatedness and behavioral coherence in agents under changing physical, environmental, and social demands, arguing this is underexplored relative to isolated task skills. Suggests robotic animal companions as a target platform for this research agenda.

entry.title: In-game Toxic Detection: Bi-directional Representations with Attention Residuals

author.name: Yuanzhe Jia

entry.summary: This paper presents a shared task for detecting toxic language in in-game chat, where extremely short utterances and heavy game slang challenge generic language models, and proposes BRAR, bi-directional representations with attention residuals, as the best-performing toxic-language slot-filling model. It addresses a practical moderation problem for gaming communities. The contribution is primarily an applied modeling effort.

entry.title: Lagrangian and Hamiltonian Neural Networks With a Dissipative System

author.name: V. Rayamajhi, J. Singal

entry.summary: Evaluates Lagrangian and Hamiltonian neural networks on dissipative systems with explicit time dependence, using damped versus undamped 1D harmonic oscillators. Finds both approaches can predict empirical behavior and partially learn the underlying Lagrangians and Hamiltonians, extending prior results for conservative systems.

entry.title: Age of Learning: Temporal Persistence of Prediction Errors as a Learning Signal

author.name: Chenyang Wang, Stefan Forsstr\"om, Roger Olsson, Di Yuan, Qing He

entry.summary: The paper introduces Age of Learning (AoL), a learning-state variable measuring how long a prediction error has persisted, increasing while an error is unresolved and resetting on a correct prediction. It distinguishes persistent under-learning from transient mistakes and derives AoL-based training strategies for both offline and streaming settings.

entry.title: Knowledge-Driven XRD Phase Identification via Multi-View Retrieval and Explanation

author.name: Doaa Mohamed, Markus Stricker

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-decision framework for X-ray diffraction phase analysis integrating convolutional autoencoder representation learning, similarity-based retrieval, and explainable decision support within a unified reference database. It targets high-throughput materials discovery settings where novel materials lack reference patterns.

entry.title: Singularities of Non-negative Matrix Factorization and their application to Bayesian inference

author.name: Naoki Hayashi, Yota Maeda, Yasushi Esaki

entry.summary: The paper studies the local geometry of the NMF factorization map and derives an improved upper bound on the real log canonical threshold governing Bayesian asymptotics for NMF, strictly improving prior bounds when the true non-negative rank is at least 3. The proof uses a local analytic normal form separating independent linear coordinates, with implications for Bayesian inference in singular models.

entry.title: Automated Species Identification in Camera Trap Images for Wildlife Conservation

author.name: Nowshin Amin, Nafisa Tabassum Oyshi, Tahmid Abrar Zidan, Miftaun Noor, Md. Abrar Rahman Shafin

entry.summary: A thesis-style work presenting an end-to-end framework for detecting and identifying small animals in low-contrast camera trap images, integrating a Swin-BiFPN backbone into a Faster R-CNN network with visual semantic extraction and self-attention. It addresses a real conservation need where small, hard-to-see animals defeat standard detectors. Applied wildlife conservation value is clear even if the architecture is compositional of known parts.

entry.title: QuPID: Quantum Parameter-Efficient Input-Dependent Retrieval Adaptation for Medical RAG

author.name: Hyojun Ahn, Emily Jimin Roh, Soohyun Park, Walid Saad, Hyung-Chul Lee, Joongheon Kim

entry.summary: QuPID identifies why fidelity-based quantum retrieval cannot learn altered rankings when circuits are input-independent, and repairs this via data re-uploading to make the circuit input-dependent and by comparing measurement readouts. It targets adapting frozen image features to a local medical archive with limited data, training classically and running inference on GPUs. This is a hybrid quantum-classical contribution to retrieval adaptation.

entry.title: A Computer Vision Approach to Visual Fraud Detection in Phishing Websites Using YOLOv8

author.name: Basil Sajid Shaikh, Hajar Homayouni

entry.summary: The paper trains YOLOv8 to classify full-page website screenshots as phishing or legitimate based on layout, logo placement, and color scheme, mirroring how victims visually judge pages rather than relying on rotatable URL/HTML signals. This visual framing targets the perceptual cues that actually convince users to surrender credentials.

entry.title: Decision Readouts for Text-Mediated Video Anomaly Detection: An Exploratory Evaluation of Jev and Qwen

author.name: Xukui Qin, Youting Wang, Xinjie He, Ziyang Luo, Runxiong Wu, Yan-Syuan Chen, Zhongyao Chu

entry.summary: This exploratory study evaluates how decision readout format affects text-mediated video anomaly detection on a small sample (40 videos, 400 anchors) from UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, comparing Jev typed decisions against Qwen readouts. Jev Noul achieved 75.99% average precision versus 48.47% for Qwen generated probability on XD captions.

entry.title: Calibrated Uncertainty for Informative Path Planning in Aquatic Environmental Monitoring

author.name: Samuel Yanes Luis, Alejandro Casado P\'erez, Alejandro Mendoza Barrionuevo, Dame Seck Diop, Sergio Toral Mar\'in, Saniel Guti\'errez Reina

entry.summary: This study investigates whether replacing Gaussian Processes with well-calibrated Deep Ensembles improves informative path planning for scalar field reconstruction, such as oil spill monitoring, across five planning strategies sharing a physics-informed ensemble backbone. It examines how uncertainty quality interacts with planner choice.

entry.title: Environmental requirements for the use of social information by artificial life agents using evolved plastic artificial neural networks

author.name: Hugh Charterton, James M. Borg, Aniko Ekart

entry.summary: Using Evolved Plastic Artificial Neural Networks, the paper runs foraging experiments with ANN-based agents to determine the minimal environmental conditions under which social information cues are used, without assuming an imitative teacher-pupil relationship. This probes the origins of social learning from an evolutionary, developmental perspective. It contributes to understanding when social information becomes evolutionarily advantageous.

entry.title: Measurement-Error-Aware Causal Distributed-Lag Quantile Modeling of Indoor Air Pollution and Short-Term Lung-Function Deterioration

author.name: Shayma Alkobaisi, Anas Ali

entry.summary: CAUSALQUANT-ASTHMA is a causal quantile distributed-lag framework linking indoor air pollution to short-horizon peak expiratory flow decline, incorporating nonlinear sensor calibration, propensity-weighted exposure assignment, and a noncrossing quantile model with susceptibility modulation. The authors note no authorized cohort with dense indoor sensing existed, so evaluation relied on constructed data. It is an ambitious statistical-methods integration for environmental health.

entry.title: Toward Agentic Optical Networks: A Vision of LLM Agent-Driven Autonomous Lifecycle Management

author.name: Yao Zhang, Shengnan Li, Yuchen Song, Yidi Wang, Yue Pang, Wenbin Chen, Xiaotian Jiang, Xiao Luo, Meixia Fu, Min Zhang, Yongli Zhao, Shanguo Huang, Alan Pak Tao Lau, Danshi Wang

entry.summary: This is a vision/position paper arguing that LLM agents could automate lifecycle management of optical networks beyond traditional AI techniques, covering reasoning, adaptive decision-making, and multi-task orchestration. It also enumerates open challenges including multi-task coordination, computational cost, data dependence, and reliability concerns. Its value is in mapping a domain roadmap rather than reporting new technical results.

entry.title: Investigating the Effect of k-NN Preprocessing on Developing Graph Neural Networks: A Fairness-Based Perspective

author.name: Nikolaos Zafeiropoulos, Emmanouil Mavrikos, George E. Tsekouras

entry.summary: This work studies how k-nearest-neighbor graph construction affects both classification accuracy and fairness in graph convolutional networks, embedding the equalized odds criterion directly into the optimization objective. It tests the methodology across several application datasets and varies neighborhood size to examine fairness-accuracy tradeoffs.

entry.title: Generative AI-Based Data Augmentation for Oral Lesion Classification: The PhotoMOCI Dataset and Benchmark

author.name: Marco Parola, Mario G. C. A. Cimino, Sabrina Senatore

entry.summary: The paper introduces PhotoMOCI, a curated photographic dataset for multi-task oral cancer diagnosis, and benchmarks how traditional versus generative AI augmentation strategies affect classifier performance. It targets the data scarcity bottleneck in oral cancer screening imaging.

entry.title: Efficient Support Recovery of Mixtures of Sparse Linear Classifiers with Less Measurements

author.name: Xiaxin Li, Arya Mazumdar

entry.summary: The paper studies support recovery in mixtures of sparse linear classifiers: recovering the nonzero coordinates of l unknown k-sparse vectors from random sign measurements. The authors propose adaptive and non-adaptive schemes that reduce the number of measurements required relative to prior work while simultaneously achieving sublinear decoding time. This tightens the sample-complexity and computational trade-offs for an abstract learning-theory problem relevant to feature identification in mixture models.

entry.title: Self-Reconstruction Dynamics for Autoencoder Reconstruction Refinement

author.name: Hitoshi Iyatomi

entry.summary: The paper observes that repeatedly applying a frozen autoencoder to its own reconstruction produces transient image- and latent-space trajectories, termed Self-Reconstruction Dynamics, which contain sample-specific information for correcting reconstructions. SRD-guided Reconstruction Refinement predicts a latent correction from a short SRD with the autoencoder frozen and no per-sample test-time optimization, and introduces an MSE-recovery ratio metric. It is a novel twist on post-hoc reconstruction improvement.

entry.title: STRIDE: State-Transition Representation via Increment Dynamics and Evolution

author.name: Yuchen Xiong, Siming Huang, Jianfeng Sun

entry.summary: STRIDE defines states through derivative fingerprints and learns local transition functions, recasting continuous forecasting as transition prediction. It uses trailing convolution windows for joint-transition frequencies, proper orthogonal decomposition for coordinate paths, and history-anchored inversion to recover future transition distributions for continuous forecasts. Experiments with three seeds compare against unspecified baselines.

entry.title: What Do Latent Predictive Vehicle Representations Retain? Measuring State, Geometry, and Local Response

author.name: Enzo Nicol\'as Spotorno, Josafat Leal Filho, Ant\^onio Augusto Fr\"ohlich

entry.summary: This work proposes a measurement protocol for action-conditioned latent world models of vehicle dynamics, checking whether physical control quantities (position, yaw, speed, yaw rate) are recoverable from latents and whether predictions respond to commands as the vehicle does. It argues that prediction error on latent targets alone measures neither requirement, which matters when latent models are embedded in physically specified controllers.

entry.title: Training and Inference Dynamics of PLDR-LLMs: Row-Map Collapse, Renormalization, and Predictive Reduction

author.name: Burc Gokden

entry.summary: This monograph develops a unified dynamical account of training and inference in Power Law Decoder Representation language models, using exact finite work identities to decompose energy changes of the learned row map into parameter contributions, signed interactions, and numerical defects. It covers predictive renormalization of the conditional training law and conditions for autonomous reductions.

entry.title: Single-Layer MeMo as a Randomized Hamming-Kernel Classifier

author.name: Alessandro Straziota

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical analysis of the single-layer MeMo architecture, showing its ideal retrieval rule is a multiclass classifier based on the positional Hamming kernel with doubly randomized Gaussian code sketches. It bounds errors from context sketching and output decoding and gives margin-based recovery guarantees.

entry.title: Adversarial Consistency-Guided Representation Learning for Multi-view Clustering

author.name: Yuchen Lin, Kunpeng Xu, Ying Fang, Lifei Chen

entry.summary: ACGRL uses a gradient-reversal view discriminator to produce view-invariant reference representations that are frozen and used to disentangle view-specific from cross-view common information in multi-view clustering. This addresses the problem that shared representations still retain view-identifying information.

entry.title: Acoustic domain shift in spoken language identification from systematic domain generalization evaluation to real-world application

author.name: Francois Derrida (X), Rapha\"el Duroselle (X), Thomas Courtat (X), Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Bonastre (X)

entry.summary: Introduces a small-scale speech dataset and evaluation protocol for controlled studies of acoustic domain shifts in spoken language recognition, motivated by the less-structured state of domain generalization evaluation in speech versus vision. It connects systematic DG evaluation to real-world application of language identification.

entry.title: Notes on Generative Modeling for Feedback Control and Planning

author.name: Karthik Elamvazhuthi

entry.summary: Lecture notes viewing control as a dynamically constrained sampling problem on state space, extending generative modeling tools like flow matching, normalizing flows, and diffusion to control and planning problems. Concepts such as controllability and optimal control guide well-posedness analysis, aimed at readers from control theory and robotics.

entry.title: Sparsity by Default: The Theory and Practice of ARD in Gaussian Process Regression for Variable Selection

author.name: Jia Cai

entry.summary: This paper reviews automatic relevance determination in GP regression, tracing its input-pruning mechanism to Bayesian Occam's razor in the marginal likelihood and emphasizing that ARD yields effective rather than exact sparsity. It surveys algorithms, lengthscale-to-selection rules, and asymptotic theory, distinguishing guarantees from practice. It is a synthesis/review rather than a new method.

entry.title: Word Similarity Datasets for Indian Languages: Annotation and Baseline Systems

author.name: Syed S. Akhtar, Arihant Gupta, Avijit Vajpayee, Arjit Srivastava, M. Shrivastava

entry.summary: The authors release manually annotated monolingual word similarity datasets for six Indian languages (Urdu, Telugu, Marathi, Punjabi, Tamil, Gujarati), built via translation and re-annotation of English datasets, plus baseline scores for state-of-the-art word representation models. This addresses a resource gap for major Indian languages beyond Hindi and Bengali.

entry.title: Coordinated Lane-Level Variable Speed Limits and Ramp Metering for Successive Weaving Segments Considering Merging/Diverging Risks: A Hybrid Model Predictive Control and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Guodong Ma, Baofeng Sun, Wenyu Yang, Zhihong Yao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid MPC and multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for coordinating lane-level variable speed limits and ramp metering across successive weaving segments on urban expressways. It introduces a lane-level macroscopic traffic model (L-METANET) and derives analytical collision-risk equations from XGBoost-SHAP plus a random-parameters logit model to balance adaptivity with control resilience.

entry.title: An Evaluation of AI-Supported Evidence-Based Learning for Public Speaking Skill Development

author.name: Sashini Hettiarachchi, Shahbaz Siddeeq, Mika Saari, Pekka Abrahamsson

entry.summary: This study develops an AI speech-coaching system that incorporates speech context into evaluation criteria and generates improved model speeches in text and audio to support example-based learning. A pilot with seven undergraduates practicing the same speech repeatedly over one to three weeks showed improvements in public speaking performance. It addresses known gaps in generic AI feedback for speech training.

entry.title: Preserving Morphemes: Morphology-Guided Pre-Tokenization for Nepali

author.name: Kalash Shrestha, Nikhil Pradhan

entry.summary: Presents Papaya, a finite-state-transducer-based pre-tokenizer built from a published Nepali grammar that splits words into stems and affixes before BPE, improving morphological coherence in tokenization. It achieves 0.96 boundary F1 against native-speaker annotations and yields small but measurable gains (about 1% lower bits per byte) in a 17M-parameter LM. A careful, well-controlled low-resource tokenization study.

entry.title: Do System One Decisions Add Up? A Study of Probabilistic Coherence

author.name: Saman Sarker Joy

entry.summary: This solo-authored study tests probabilistic coherence, whether fine-label predictions agree with probabilities reconstructed through broad categories, in the Jev system and the Laya checkpoint using 72,000 classification questions across TREC, CLINC150, and MASSIVE. Both systems show substantial self-disagreement, with category-level total variation up to 0.689, and consequences differ sharply by dataset. The work highlights a neglected consistency property beyond per-question calibration.

entry.title: Towards Transparent Diagnostics: Investigating Architectural Trade-offs and Explainability in Malaria Detection

author.name: Suman Kunwar, Avishek Dangol

entry.summary: Compares standard deep learning architectures (ResNet18, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B2, VGG19) plus a proposed model for malaria detection from blood smear images on the NIH Malaria dataset. Reports MobileNetV2 reaching 96.35% accuracy with the smallest size and fastest inference, while the proposed model reaches 97.67% accuracy.

entry.title: Two-Stage Multi-View Gait Recognition with a Re-Embedding Network

author.name: Long Hoang Le, Trung Thanh Ngo

entry.summary: The proposed TFTR framework first maps Gait Energy Images into a view-specific 128-dimensional embedding space with a Siamese triplet-loss network, then treats per-view embeddings as tokens for a Transformer encoder that re-projects them with improved cosine separability. This enables fusion of an arbitrary number of views at inference, overcoming fixed-input constraints.

entry.title: Even if others are less responsible you can still make things worse

author.name: testingthewaters

entry.summary: The post enumerates concrete mechanisms by which comparatively responsible AI developers still worsen outcomes by racing, including artificial urgency, legitimizing corner-cutting, entangling their credibility with the technology, and diffusing public attention from less responsible actors. It challenges the common argument that responsible actors must race to stay ahead of reckless ones.

entry.title: Import AI 474: Platonic mindspace; TPUs in space; Zhipu starts an outer RSI loop

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's newsletter covers an iconoclastic paper by Michael Levin proposing a non-physicalist model in which minds are Platonic patterns related to brains as mathematics is to physics, alongside items on TPUs deployed in space and Zhipu initiating an outer recursive self-improvement loop. The newsletter provides commentary contextualizing each item for a research-literate audience.

entry.title: Nutri-ATLAS: Embodied Agent for Tabulated Lookup and Assistance for Smarter nutrition

author.name: Uttej Kallakuri, Boxun Hu, Ankur A. Butala, Najim Dehak, Tinoosh Mohsenin

entry.summary: Nutri-ATLAS is an embodied nutrition-assistance agent combining graph-grounded nutrition reasoning over a unified Food-Nutrient knowledge base, hardware-aware LLM selection, and robot-based evidence acquisition (e.g., sensing food in the real world). It addresses the unreliability of passive text-only LLM nutrition systems when food descriptions are ambiguous or evidence is missing. The system sits at the intersection of agentic IoT, robotics, and digital health.

entry.title: SpecRegMatch: Robust Semi-Supervised Regression for Vehicle Interior Noise Prediction

author.name: Sejin Sim, Jinsoo Bae, Seoung Bum Kim

entry.summary: SpecRegMatch is a semi-supervised regression method for predicting vehicle interior noise that uses a single model to leverage unlabeled data, avoiding the computational cost of multiple model training and data sampling in prior SSR approaches. It targets the high cost of collecting labeled acoustic data in automotive engineering.

entry.title: Latency-Aware Client Assignment for Parallel Split Learning With Global Sampling

author.name: Mohammad Kohankhaki, Valentin Rentschler, Anke Schmeink

entry.summary: This work improves Parallel Split Learning with Global Sampling for cross-silo federated settings by adding latency-aware client assignment: it separates each pooled batch's class targets from the choice of clients supplying examples, formulated as an integral network-flow problem or a fast greedy rule. Both variants preserve target streams and full data usage per epoch, with a planning rule balancing schedule cost against completion-time gains. It targets heterogeneous-latency training environments.

entry.title: Extremely Fast and Compact Binary Graph Representations via Randomized Operator Sketching

author.name: Srajan Agarwal, Megha P, Bikas C Das, Zakaria Laskar, Saptarshi Bej

entry.summary: The paper introduces an algebraic graph hashing method that builds binary node representations directly from graph structure, approximating a high-order structural transition matrix via randomized column sampling in the Nyström style, with no node features or gradient-based training. It aims to address memory and compute costs of dense floating-point GNN representations while retaining global topology.

entry.title: Forecast-Necessary Causal Discovery for Nonlinear Political Panel Data: Feedback, Functional Form, and the Dynamics of Democratization

author.name: Michael Coppedge, Dmitry Zaytsev, Valentina Kuskova

entry.summary: The paper develops an inferential workflow for political panel data combining flexible autoregressive estimation, forecast-necessity testing, functional characterization, and same-data linear benchmarking to disambiguate non-significant coefficients in dynamic panel models. It applies the workflow to democratization dynamics, identifying relationships required for out-of-sample prediction and their functional forms.

entry.title: Simulation-Based Inference for Plate Reverb System Identification

author.name: Dylan Sechet, Marc Evrard, Matthieu Kowalski

entry.summary: The authors use simulation-based inference to solve a DAFx challenge task of recovering physical plate parameters from impulse responses, training a neural posterior estimator on simulator-generated data. For each test observation they run sequential fine-tuning rounds that resample parameters from the current posterior and retrain, enabling inference without further simulator calls at deployment.

entry.title: Working with AI: A Design Framework for Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Yuqian Lu, Regina Lee, Rui Zhou, Lixin Jiang, Andrew McDaid, Amy Lawrence

entry.summary: This white paper presents a practical framework for designing human-AI collaboration in industrial settings, considering the human, AI system, task, organization, and wider societal environment. It emphasizes that successful adoption depends on how people experience and work with AI, not just technical capability. It is positioned as guidance for practitioners designing AI-augmented work.

entry.title: Scalable and Data-Driven Decision Support in the Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul Process

author.name: Houkun Zhu, Helena Ebel, Dominik Scheinert, Florian Schmidt, Jens Altenkirch, Odej Kao

entry.summary: Proposes a Smart Expert System (SES) to assist engineering experts in maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) processes, motivated by cost efficiency, sustainability, and product lifetime extension for components like casted gas turbine parts. The system provides scalable, data-driven decision support for industrial repair planning.

entry.title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification

author.name: Mahesh Neupane, Pragya Dhungana, Pradip Khatri, Swechhya Baskota, Hariom Dhungana

entry.summary: An empirical comparison of four contemporary probabilistic forecasting models for electricity consumption, motivated by rising renewable penetration and smart-grid variability that make point forecasts insufficient. The study highlights trade-offs in uncertainty quantification for power-system planning. Useful applied benchmarking rather than a new method.

entry.title: Analog Computing revisited: A fully analog and minimalistic Damage Detector for Ultrasonic Testing enabling Material-Integrated Structural Health Monitoring

author.name: Stefan Bosse

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully analog, minimalistic damage detector for ultrasonic structural health monitoring that avoids digital ADC and microprocessor pipelines, targeting printed organic electronics for material-integrated deployment. It emphasizes benefits in transistor count, energy use, and resilience to power interruption.

entry.title: Human Activity Recognition via Ultra-Wideband Data: A Framework for Dimensionality Reduction, Pattern Discovery, and Predictive Modeling

author.name: Nahid Sahel Gozin, Reza Sedaghat, Prathap Siddavaatam

entry.summary: The authors propose a framework for human activity recognition from high-dimensional, noisy ultra-wideband radar signals, introducing two new dimensionality reduction techniques including Clustered Polynomial Expansion with Incremental PCA. The framework classifies six activity types with high accuracy while remaining suitable for computationally constrained real-time systems. It is an applied sensing/ML contribution rather than a fundamental advance.

entry.title: Using Machine Learning to Investigate Predictors of Fasting Blood Glucose: Insights into Circadian Timing and Age Interactions

author.name: Viktoriya Bu-Dager, Silvia Cirstea

entry.summary: The study builds an interpretable ML framework predicting fasting blood glucose from NHANES 2017-2020 data using metabolic, hormonal, lifestyle, and circadian variables, with a leakage-resistant pipeline where preprocessing occurs only within training folds. Elastic Net, LASSO, and XGBoost are evaluated with 94 candidate predictors and engineered circadian interaction terms. It highlights circadian timing and age interactions as glucose predictors.

entry.title: Learning the Graph and the Embedding Together: Classifier-Independent Rewiring for Heterophilic Node Classification

author.name: Harshit Kumar, Sujan Chakraborty, Priyanka Saha, Pritam Kar, Saptarshi Bej

entry.summary: The paper proposes an affinity-guided graph rewiring method for heterophilic node classification that jointly learns the graph and node representations, alternating EM-style between training a lightweight GNN and re-weighting candidate edges under a modularity objective with pseudo-label homophily. It emphasizes classifier-independent evaluation to separate topological gains from classifier-specific pairing effects.

entry.title: Price Stability in the European Union: A Systemic Approach Using Random Matrix Theory

author.name: Sami Diaf

entry.summary: Applies Random Matrix Theory to Eurozone monthly inflation indices treated as a system of prices, analyzing eigenvalue properties to denoise correlation structure and uncover systemic price dynamics. The goal is to improve multivariate analysis supporting monetary policy and price stability. It is an econometrics-style application rather than an AI-methods paper.

entry.title: ReCo: When to Relocate Sensor Kits under Deployment Constraints -- A NILM Case Study

author.name: Haokun Chen, Yu Tong, Yehai Chen

entry.summary: ReCo studies the decision of when to relocate limited sensor kits during field data collection, using non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) as a case study where labeled data requires temporarily instrumenting homes. It proposes a constraint-based relocation framework that accounts for deadlines, downtime, and the diversity value of new data.

entry.title: Seeing the Heat: Synthesizing High-Resolution Wood Thermal Responses from Optical Imagery

author.name: Jingren Xie

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end framework that synthesizes high-resolution thermal responses of wood directly from RGB images, exploiting the physical link between wood color variation (cellular anatomy) and localized solid volume fraction. An automated FEM-based data engine maps pixel-level optical intensity to 3D thermodynamic simulation to overcome the resolution and noise limits of infrared thermography.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation for Acoustic Pedestrian Detection

author.name: Yonghyun Kim, Chaeyeon Han, Sancho Gatungay, Subhrajit Guhathakurta, Alexander Lerch

entry.summary: Investigates video-to-audio cross-modal knowledge distillation for audio-only pedestrian detection, introducing Trust-Filtered Distillation (TFD) that selectively suppresses teacher supervision on pedestrian samples. Across ten configurations on the ASPED dataset, most methods yield modest gains, and the paper offers an interpretation of TFD as conditional label smoothing under a shared temperature.

entry.title: Period Segmentation in Transition Network Analysis: A Topological Data Analysis Approach

author.name: Hitoshi Inoue, Koichi Yasutake

entry.summary: Building on Transition Network Analysis for revealing temporal dynamics of learning behavior, this paper uses Zigzag Persistent Homology to find beta-zero change points as data-driven period boundaries in courses. Analyzing 22 courses from the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset, the topological segmentation captures substantially greater between-period variation than time-based segmentation, suggesting utility for identifying intervention windows in learning analytics.

entry.title: Learning Shuffle Ideals with Membership Queries and Contrastive Examples

author.name: S. Mahmoud Mousawi, Pierluigi San Pietro, Sandra Zilles

entry.summary: Studies the learnability of shuffle ideals (formal language classes) with membership queries and a new contrastive query type that returns a similar word in the target language when the queried word is not. The paper proves strong negative results for simple shuffle ideal classes but derives positive learnability results under structural conditions connected to universal words and word combinatorics.

entry.title: PlurVA-LLM-2026 Shared Task Track-1: Pluralistic Value Alignment in LLMs via Multilingual Fine-Tuning and Threshold Calibration

author.name: Vihindi Kotalawala, Nevidu Jayatilleke

entry.summary: A shared-task system report describing fine-tuning Llama 3.1 8B Instruct with 4-bit QLoRA for pluralistic value alignment across Chinese, Indonesian, and Sri Lankan contexts, combining option-permutation augmentation, annotator vote expansion, and SinhalaMMLU augmentation with conditional threshold calibration. The system achieved a macro-average accuracy of 0.805. It is a competent resource-constrained competition entry but primarily an engineering contribution.

entry.title: Classifying Dominant Temporal Orientation without Pretrained Text Embeddings: A Novel Morphosyntactic Inventory Vector Approach

author.name: Jonathan Cleveland, Peter S. Bearman

entry.summary: Proposes Morphosyntacton, a method for classifying a sentence's dominant temporal orientation (past, present, or future) using fixed-length vectors of part-of-speech counts, dependency relation counts, and futurate pattern counts, with no pretrained embeddings, padding, or sequence models. It targets hard cases with competing tense information in embedded clauses. The work matters as a lightweight, interpretable alternative to embedding-based classifiers for a fine-grained linguistic task.

entry.title: Quantitative Measurement of Language Distance among Closely Related Indo-European Languages Using Pretrained Language Models: A Case Study on the North Germanic Branch

author.name: Yiping Bai

entry.summary: This paper proposes a three-metric framework for quantifying language distance among Danish, Norwegian Bokmal, and Swedish using pretrained multilingual models: sentence-level semantic distance via LaBSE and mBERT embeddings, orthographic fragmentation rate, and a third complementary measure. It replaces traditionally qualitative comparisons with a unified computational framework. The approach could generalize to other closely related language pairs.

entry.title: Who Governs Data in the AI Era? A Computational Analysis of the U.S. Privacy Workforce in Job Postings

author.name: Ramazan Yener, Muhammad Hassan, Masooda Bashir

entry.summary: The paper analyzes 1,143 U.S. privacy job postings from LinkedIn and Indeed using rule-based text mining and BERTopic topic modeling, examining titles, salaries, competencies, certifications, education, experience, regulatory references, and AI-related language. It identifies 18 latent themes in four categories and finds that privacy roles are hybrid, combining legal knowledge, technical skills, and interpersonal competence, with AI appearing in more than half of the postings.

entry.title: Devanagari Handwritten Character Recognition Using TrOCR: A Transformer-Based Model with Real-Time Web Deployment

author.name: Amrit Baskota, Samyam Budhathoki, Shubham Ghimire, Abiskar Ghimire, Sarwesh Phuyal, Baskaran P

entry.summary: Fine-tunes the pretrained microsoft/trocr-base-handwritten model on roughly 5,000 Devanagari handwritten character images with standard preprocessing and an 8:1:1 split, deploying the result as a real-time web application. Aims to improve recognition of a complex script with 36 vowels, 14 consonants, and 10 numerals.

entry.title: Facial classification Using Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning
