They propose two complementary frameworks, including FedTMLE-G, which aggregates local gradients to reproduce centralized targeting for a general class of targets, losses, and fluctuation families. This enables efficient, model-respecting statistical inference under data-sharing constraints.

entry.title: Mechanism-Aware Ensemble Conditioning for Data-Limited Emulation of Extreme Events

author.name: Isabella S. Thiel, Juan Bello-Rivas, Yannis G. Kevrekidis, Themistoklis P. Sapsis

entry.summary: The authors propose a mechanism-aware conditioning plug-in framework that turns a nudged coarse ensemble into a non-intrusive sensor of local instability geometry for learning extreme events in chaotic systems from short trajectories. In the small-noise regime, ensemble covariance aggregates the finite-time deformation kernels governing local amplification, and a small FiLM module injects these statistics into an otherwise unchanged backbone simulator. This targets the core difficulty that extreme events are controlled by transient instability rather than bulk dynamics.

entry.title: Aurora-X: Built for Extreme Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xingjian Wu, Chenjuan Guo, Xiangfei Qiu, Zhigang Hu, Hanyin Cheng, Peng Chen, Yang Shu, Jilin Hu, Bin Yang

entry.summary: Aurora-X is a billion-scale time series foundation model with a progressive curriculum: channel-independent pretraining followed by midtraining that introduces cross-variable dependencies, varied context/horizon lengths, and covariates, plus variable-resolution post-training that adjusts temporal span per token at inference with fixed weights. This supports longer histories under a fixed token budget or fewer tokens for short histories.

entry.title: Brenier Meets Adversarial Training: Optimal Transport Geometry for Robust Learning

author.name: Alireza Abdollahpoorrostam, Ehsan Sharifian, Buse \c{S}en, Marco Cuturi, Daniel Kuhn

entry.summary: The paper reformulates a penalized distributionally robust optimization adversary as optimization over transport maps, proving optimal maps are cyclically monotone (Brenier-style structure). It shows standard per-sample adversarial training violates cyclical monotonicity and wastes transport budget, motivating OT-geometric robust training.

entry.title: Encryptability As a Coordinate Choice: Depth-One Homomorphic Federated Learning of Quantum Neural Networks

author.name: Marcel Mordarski, Nathan Mani, Arshad Patel, William Knottenbelt, Roberto Bondesan

entry.summary: The authors show that the high cost of homomorphically encrypted training of variational quantum circuits is an artifact of coordinate choice: in the unit-quaternion (spin) chart, SU(2) rotation composition is exactly bilinear, so encrypted updates cost one multiplicative level instead of thousands of operations per weight or one round per gate. This enables practical depth-one homomorphic federated learning of quantum neural networks with privacy-preserving server-side aggregation.

entry.title: Precision at Speed: Sample-Efficient Online Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Hydraulic Excavator Control

author.name: Claudio Canales, Fang Nan, Marco Hutter, Javier Ruiz-del-Solar

entry.summary: Presents an online model-based RL framework that learns a probabilistic dynamics ensemble from scratch for sampling-based MPC, with a precision-gated contouring objective that conditions progress reward on path accuracy. It achieves higher sample efficiency than model-based RL baselines in simulation and is validated by learning directly on an 11.5-ton hydraulic excavator without demonstrations.

entry.title: EAServe: Encode-Aware Disaggregated Serving for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Kunxiong Zhu, Zhihao Shu, Hangyu Zheng, Minghai Qin, Miao Yin, Gagan Agrawal, Wei Niu

entry.summary: EAServe extends disaggregated LLM serving to the three-stage Encode-Prefill-Decode pipeline required by multimodal LLMs, addressing resource imbalance where every request enters through Encode. It introduces encode-aware scheduling that regulates downstream request flow across GPU pools. This addresses a real and growing infrastructure bottleneck as multimodal serving scales.

entry.title: First-Order Stationarity of Reverse Diffusions

author.name: Zhifeng Chen, Chenyang Jiang, Yazhen Wang

entry.summary: This work develops a first-order theory for diffusion models, showing SDE-based reverse-time flows of overdamped and underdamped Langevin diffusions contract relative Fisher divergences at explicit exponential rates under strong convexity of the noising potential. It establishes averaged first-order stationarity bounds for discretized samplers, analogous to nonconvex optimization guarantees. This deepens the known optimization-sampling connection for diffusion models.

entry.title: Inference-Time Target Speaker Unlearning in LLM-Based Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Bo Su, Yueru Yan, Thai Le

entry.summary: The paper introduces the target-speaker unlearning ASR (TSU-ASR) task: given a multi-speaker utterance and opt-out speakers, the system transcribes everyone except opt-out speakers while still detecting when they are active, protecting privacy at inference time. It proposes a lightweight Enrollment-Conditioned Gating module attachable to a frozen dual-stream speech LLM, handling unseen opt-out speakers dynamically. Experiments on AMI and AliMeeting validate the approach.

entry.title: PIA: A Personal Intelligence Agent Turning Health Conversations into Records and Records into Understanding

author.name: Jeonghun Yoon, Dongchan Kim, Hongyeon Yu, Young-Bum Kim, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: PIA is a health-focused personal intelligence agent that replaces generic summarize-and-embed agent memory with a harness of four controls (extraction, memory, retrieval, understanding) that turn health conversations into typed clinical records and records into synthesized user understanding. The design tackles real failure cases of text-similarity memory, such as resolving relative dates and answering glucose-trend questions. It represents a substantive advance in structured agent memory for health applications.

entry.title: Why Alzheimer's Speech Screening Fails to Generalize: Bridging the Deployment Gap via Cross-Corpus Evidence Anchoring

author.name: Zijian Lu, Sizhe Liu, Yin Zhang, Jixuan Deng, Xinrong Lin, Xinchen Yuan, Chicheng Jin, Yiping Zuo, Yuanchao Li

entry.summary: The paper studies why speech-based Alzheimer's screening models trained on one corpus fail to generalize to unseen languages, tasks, and recording protocols, using a leave-one-corpus-out evaluation over four datasets. It finds that 59 of 70 interpretable speech and language features show direction conflicts between healthy and at-risk groups across corpora, and an XLM-R text baseline drops to AUC 0.520 on the weakest domain. The proposed cross-corpus evidence anchoring approach aims to bridge this deployment gap.

entry.title: Where and When to Force: Routed Forcing for Streaming Avatars

author.name: Zihan Su, Siwen Lu, Junhao Zhuang, Zeyue Xue, Haoyang Huang, Guanghao Li, Xiaofeng Tan, Chun Yuan, Nan Duan

entry.summary: Analyzes how Distribution Matching Distillation causes mode collapse in streaming audio-driven avatar generation, showing the collapse is region-heterogeneous: person regions lose the most dynamics while backgrounds are nearly unaffected. The paper proposes routed forcing, applying forcing adaptively where and when it is needed to preserve motion diversity and audio synchronization in real-time avatar synthesis. Directly relevant to the fast-growing real-time digital human/avatar industry.

entry.title: Who Says What: Symbolic Trimodal Binding Mechanisms in Audio-Visual LLMs

author.name: Jihoo Jung, Youngjoon Jang, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: Investigates how audio-visual LLMs achieve trimodal text-audio-visual binding for multi-speaker dialogue videos, identifying emergent symbolic binding mechanisms where auditory and visual components are encoded into symbolic variables capturing utterance sequences and entity coordinates, with cross-modal linking in this abstract space. Also characterizes how binding failure propagates to downstream errors. Offers interpretability insight into how multimodal LLMs resolve who says what.

entry.title: Forensic Twins: Self-Supervised Residual Learning for AI-Generated Image Forensics

author.name: Javier Mu\~noz-Haro, Ruben Tolosana, Ruben Vera-Rodriguez, Aythami Morales, Julian Fierrez

entry.summary: Forensic Twins is a self-supervised residual learning framework for detecting AI-generated images that uses forensic residual extractors to produce pretext views with minimal semantic content, preserving image-formation micro-statistics that standard augmentations destroy. This improves generalization to unseen generative architectures.

entry.title: RECAST: From Log Replay to Closed-Loop Driving Simulation with View-Complete Actors

author.name: Zijun Zhao, Liewen Liao, Kang Shen, Songan Zhang, Ming Yang

entry.summary: RECAST uses 3D Gaussian Splatting to generate view-complete actors from single segmented vehicle observations in driving logs, enabling reliable rendering when ego and actors deviate from recorded trajectories. It supports planner-in-the-loop closed-loop simulation under controlled ego-actor interactions.

entry.title: Causeway: Restoring Task Accessibility for Instruction Switching in VLA Policies

author.name: Qingzi Wang, Kaixi Feng, Guangyao Shi, Xiyang Wu, Ang Li, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Causeway studies instruction switching in VLA policies, observing that tasks completed reliably from standard initial states can become inaccessible from states left by a preceding task — so-called task islands. It proposes a training-free inference-time intervention that back-propagates through the frozen action-decoding computation and applies a state-directed write in the action-stream representation to restore accessibility. This is a novel, lightweight fix to a real deployment failure mode of VLAs.

entry.title: TACTIC: Understanding Tactile Encoders and Conditioning for Contact-rich Robot Manipulation Policies

author.name: Seongjin Bien, D\'ebora Oliveira Makowski, Carlo Kneissl, Reihaneh Mirjalili, Pankhuri Vanjani, Rudolf Lioutikov, Gitta Kutyniok, Florian Walter, Wolfram Burgard

entry.summary: TACTIC is a comprehensive controlled study of tactile encoders and conditioning/fusion strategies for contact-rich manipulation, training and evaluating all variants under an identical pipeline and real-world experimental protocol. It brings order to a fragmented design space of vision-based tactile sensing architectures. Empirical studies of this kind are rare and highly valuable for the community.

entry.title: AuthGuard-R: Safety-Compliant Mission Hijacking and Dual-Gate Defense for LLM-Controlled Robots

author.name: Saidattu Chepuri, Vikas Srivastava

entry.summary: The paper identifies a novel attack class against LLM-controlled robots called safety-compliant mission hijacking, where an attacker redirects a robot toward unauthorized goals while keeping every action physically safe, evading conventional action-safety defenses. It proposes AuthGuard-R, a dual-gate defense that also verifies mission authorization. This is significant for the emerging field of LLM-robot security beyond purely physical safety.

entry.title: When they can perform a task, AIs are much cheaper than humans

author.name: djbinder

entry.summary: A LessWrong post examining the economics of AI labor, using frontier models GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (both released earlier in September 2026) to build a database of AI task costs. The author argues that since AI systems can now complete tasks requiring months or years of human effort, the decisive question for workforce displacement is cost comparison, and finds AI is already much cheaper than humans for tasks it can perform. The post connects this to risks of mass digital labor and loss of human control over the future.

entry.title: Atelier: Learning Local Self-Supervised Features for CryoEM Volumes via Hypernetworks

author.name: Phillip Lo, Sudarshan Babu, Dari Kimanius, Aly A. Khan

entry.summary: Introduces Atelier, a self-supervised framework that amortizes implicit neural representation fitting for cryoEM maps using a hypernetwork/transformer pretrained on 5,439 EMDB maps. It produces spatially localized, sample-consistent, scale-agnostic volumetric features, overcoming the cost and misalignment problems of fitting a separate INR per map.

entry.title: TISD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Trajectory Intervention

author.name: Taeckyung Lee, Rinat Amankos, Jeonghye Kim, Hyungjun Yoon, Woogyeol Jin, Sung-Ju Lee

entry.summary: Identifies a data-collection bottleneck in on-policy self-distillation: teacher targets are only evaluated on student-sampled rollouts, so teacher-preferred branches are never supervised beyond the branch decision. Using controlled token interventions, the authors show teacher-preferred tokens at peak disagreement improve student continuation success, and propose TISD, which treats teacher-student disagreement as a signal to branch trajectories for additional supervision. Advances teacher-student training for reasoning LLMs.

entry.title: FARE: Forensic Acceptance Region Estimation for Catching Bait-and-Switch Image Generators

author.name: Kai Yao, Marc Juarez

entry.summary: FARE addresses deployment-time integrity auditing of opaque generative image APIs, detecting whether a provider silently swaps a certified generator for a cheaper, lower-quality one. It trains a forensic detector on images from the certified generator and then classifies whether any single generated image is consistent with that generator. This supports post-certification governance of deployed AI services.

entry.title: MVAgent: Multi-Agent Video Generation via Consistent Condition Construction and Shot-Level Policy Optimization

author.name: Xiangyu Kong, Wenjie Zhou, Fengping Tian, Lihua Fang, Haoqin Sun, Chenyang Lyu, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo

entry.summary: MVAgent tackles multi-shot agentic video generation by recasting consistency as a condition-construction problem: a multi-agent pipeline builds typed conditioning inputs so characters, layout, and state persist across shots generated by a frozen video model. A Spatial Grounding agent anchors each shot to matching views from generated camera-traversal clips, and an Observer maintains continuity memory with shot-level policy optimization to correct drift. The approach requires no fine-tuning of the underlying generator.

entry.title: FuseReg: Regularizing Layer Fusion Mitigates the Reconstruction-Generation Gap in Representation Autoencoders

author.name: Hongyang Du, Yunfei Xie, Junjie Ye, Jiawei Yang, Xiaoyan Cong, Haodong Zhang, Yongchao Huang, Haiyu Wu, Zongxia Li, Shihang Gui, Dawei Liu, Runhao Li, Jingcheng Ni, Chen Wei, Randall Balestriero, Yue Wang

entry.summary: FuseReg replaces heuristic selection of encoder layers for representation autoencoders with training over random subsets of layers, regularizing layer fusion. The paper provides theoretical analysis of why subset sampling mitigates the trade-off between pixel-detail preservation and generation quality.

entry.title: Towards Whole-Study Screening for Congenital Heart Disease in Fetal Ultrasound Using Multiple Instance Learning

author.name: Mohamed Azzam, Ruobing Liu, Esther C. Ugwueke, Ziyang Xu, Shibiao Wan, Alex Foy, Abraham Zabih, Jason Christensen, Neil Hamill, Ling Li, Jieqiong Wang

entry.summary: A two-stage framework screens whole fetal ultrasound studies for congenital heart disease without assuming pre-isolated diagnostic frames, combining masked-autoencoder pretraining on unlabeled ultrasound, a disease-robust cardiac frame finder, and transformer-based multiple instance learning for case-level prediction.

entry.title: VisTacAlign: Co-Training Dexterous Policies on Tactile Human and Robot Demonstrations

author.name: Julien Poffet, Matthew Strong, Ankush Dhawan, Baiyu Shi, Shalika Neelaveni, Yujia Yuan, Zhenan Bao, Monroe Kennedy III

entry.summary: VisTacAlign enables co-training of 3D visual-tactile dexterous policies on human and robot demonstrations by retargeting glove-tracked human hand motion to a 17-DoF tactile robot hand, erasing and re-rendering the human hand in stereo views so human point clouds share robot-like errors, and translating capacitive tactile signals between hands. This closes the human-robot modality gap, allowing cheap human data to augment scarce robot data. A thoughtful data-scaling contribution for dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: Bringing AI to Autonomous Systems -- From Cognition to Collective Intelligence

author.name: Joseph Sifakis

entry.summary: A position/framework paper by Joseph Sifakis arguing that autonomous systems represent the culmination of AI development, requiring hybridization of connectionist and symbolic AI with systems engineering. It proposes a generic agent architecture organized around cognitive functions and evolving long-term memory, and discusses implementation challenges such as linking sensory data to structured knowledge.

entry.title: Backbone-Adaptive Evidence Routing for Robust Pairwise LLM Judging

author.name: Zeyan Li, Jing Peng, Jianfeng Xu

entry.summary: Proposes BAER, a method that routes between comparison, reasoning, and reference-based evidence protocols for pairwise LLM judges, adapted per benchmark-backbone combination while preserving candidate symmetry. It separates signed preference from candidate-invariant reliability and uses three symmetric heads selected on development data. Results across four benchmarks show no single judging protocol dominates, motivating adaptive routing.

entry.title: SciHorizon-eLab: An Agentic Protocol-to-Task Compiler for Scalable Benchmarking of Scientific Embodied Agents

author.name: Maokai Qin, Chuan Qin, Qi Zhang, Dianyu Liu, Zirui Liu, Hongting Niu, Yuanchun Zhou, Hengshu Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces SciHorizon-eLab, an agentic compiler that turns natural-language laboratory protocols into executable, verifiable embodied tasks by treating task construction as a compilation problem with semantic-preserving progressive stages. It addresses the bottleneck that existing simulation-based science-lab benchmarks require heavy manual task engineering. Enables systematic, scalable evaluation of agents that automate scientific experimentation.

entry.title: Same Text, Different Numbers: The Divergence of LLM-Based Measures

author.name: Hamid Boustanifar, Sasan Mansouri

entry.summary: The authors test whether LLM-generated textual measures (sentiment, uncertainty, climate risk, etc. from earnings call transcripts) are invariant to model choice across seven LLMs from different providers. They find average cross-model rank correlation of only 0.52, with just 34 percent of score variation shared across providers, suggesting a substantial model-specific component. This is a cautionary result for the growing use of LLMs as measurement instruments in social science and finance research.

entry.title: Mutable Transcripts: Mitigating Context Pollution through Editable Conversation State

author.name: Dan Barry, Andrew Hines

entry.summary: This paper introduces mutable transcripts, a new interaction paradigm in which users can revise earlier conversation turns via natural-language edit requests rather than only appending new messages. The approach targets context pollution, where stale or irrelevant information in an immutable transcript degrades later responses. It reframes conversation history from a passive log into an editable working context.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Best-LLM Identification using Dueling Feedback

author.name: Sarvesh Gharat, Nikhil Karamchandani, Jayakrishnan Nair

entry.summary: This paper formulates best-LLM selection as a multi-armed bandit problem with dueling (pairwise comparison) feedback and heterogeneous querying costs, reflecting the differing prices of calling different models. Assuming a Condorcet winner, the authors propose a Track-and-Stop style algorithm and prove it is asymptotically optimal in cost as error goes to zero, empirically validating the key assumption on real-world datasets.

entry.title: Probing Stability-Plasticity Tradeoffs in Agent Memory through Cognitive Experimental Paradigms

author.name: Jiaqi Ding, Guorong Wu

entry.summary: MemProbe is a cognitive-science-inspired evaluation framework diagnosing stability-plasticity tradeoffs in LLM agent memory systems. It translates memory research insights into four paradigms (interference, misinformation, consolidation strength, reconsolidation window) that test when agent memories should be updated, preserved, or flagged as uncertain. It addresses a real gap where memory evaluation collapses to final-answer accuracy.

entry.title: Estimating and Orthogonalizing Unknown Pre-training Gradients for Continual Fine-tuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Bing Wang, Changchun Li, Xin-Qiang Cai, Lin Yuanbo Wu, Ximing Li, Gang Niu, Masashi Sugiyama

entry.summary: EoupCT addresses catastrophic forgetting during continual fine-tuning of LLMs, noting that orthogonal gradient projection methods fail to preserve pre-trained general knowledge because pre-training data and gradients are unknown. It proposes a framework to estimate the unknown pre-training gradient subspace and project updates to be orthogonal to it, protecting general-purpose capabilities. This offers a practical continual-learning recipe for deployed LLMs.

entry.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Minseok Jeong, Hyewon Choi, Hiroyasu Tsukamoto, SooJean Han

entry.summary: This paper extends the linear representation hypothesis from LLMs to vision-language-action models, developing a signature-based theoretical framework that accounts for the dynamic, closed-loop nature of embodied interaction where representations influence actions and actions alter future representations. It provides theory for measuring and intervening on physical quantities of interest inside VLA policies.

entry.title: AgentRecommender: LLM Agents Enable Customizable Recommender Systems on the User Side

author.name: Ryoma Sato

entry.summary: This paper proposes AgentRecommender, a method that uses LLM agents and their investigation capabilities and internal knowledge to build customizable recommender systems controlled by users rather than platforms. It addresses the problem that platform-side recommenders incentivize clickbait, filter bubbles, and misinformation, and tackles the data scarcity challenge of customizing recommenders for individual users. The work reframes recommendation as a user-sovereign application of LLM agents, a relatively unexplored direction.

entry.title: Towards VLA-Dreamer: Refining VLA Behavior Using World Models

author.name: Parsa Mastouri Kashani, Jan-Gerrit Habekost, Stefan Wermter

entry.summary: This concept paper proposes training a predictive world model on the embedding space of a VLA's vision encoder to improve sample efficiency in robot control. It tests whether VLA embeddings are action-relevant and predictive of future states, framing the absence of an explicit world model as a key limitation of current VLA architectures.

entry.title: Compact Documentation for Coding Agents: A Benchmark, an Optimizer, and Why It Does Not Transfer

author.name: Md Shohel Arman, Igor Molybog

entry.summary: The paper introduces a roundtrip benchmark scoring code descriptions by whether code regenerated from them passes original tests, showing completeness rather than length drives fidelity, and derives an optimized description-writing prompt that reaches full fidelity. However, its headline finding is negative: better documentation does not transfer to improved agent issue-resolution across two model families and ten repositories.

entry.title: Statistical attribute alignment for black-box generative AI via output post-processing

author.name: Kevin Jiang, Morgane Austern, Edgar Dobriban, Jason M. Klusowski

entry.summary: This paper proposes a method to align the distribution of an attribute in generative AI outputs with a user-specified target distribution, using only black-box query access and output post-processing. Applications include fairness constraints on protected attributes and representative synthetic data generation. It matters because it offers alignment guarantees without requiring model retraining or internal access.

entry.title: Learning to Bias: Machine Learning-Enhanced Particle Filters

author.name: Apoorv Srivastava, Eric Darve

entry.summary: The paper introduces Neural Optimal Particle Filters (NOPFs), which learn an amortized approximation to the optimal proposal distribution from offline simulated one-step conditioning tuples and plug it into standard particle filter updates. Learned proposals act as drop-in replacements with standard importance-weight corrections, targeting the well-known sample-efficiency and dimension-scaling problems of particle filters. This bridges learned inference and classical Monte Carlo sequential estimation.

entry.title: Counterfactual Online Conformal Prediction Under Adaptive Logging

author.name: Xinyu Qiao, Yichen Lin, Kaihong Ji, Xue Wang, Tao Yao

entry.summary: The paper identifies that online conformal prediction can systematically miscover counterfactual outcomes of rarely selected actions when predictions influence actions that in turn determine calibration data. It proposes Propensity-Weighted Online Conformal Prediction, with a doubly robust variant, achieving coverage that matches an information-theoretic lower bound up to log factors under positivity.

entry.title: CRNDiff: Count-Native Diffusion Framework via Chemical Reaction Networks

author.name: Yuxuan Qiu, Praful Gagrani, Tetsuya J Kobayashi

entry.summary: CRNDiff is a diffusion framework built on stochastic chemical reaction networks that operates natively on nonnegative integer counts, targeting scientific data like single-cell RNA sequencing. It provides a closed-form forward kernel, reverse sampling via forward-filtering backward-sampling, and inference-time conditioning on rare subpopulations.

entry.title: Generalization behavior of OPTQ and the role of regularization

author.name: Erin George, Rayan Saab

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical analysis of OPTQ, a popular neural network weight quantization algorithm, and its stochastic variant. The authors derive generalization bounds for the expected squared quantization error on test points drawn from a distribution, relating test-time error to calibration-set error under regularization. This grounds a widely used practical compression method in formal statistical guarantees.

entry.title: Low-Rank Friction for Memory-Efficient Transformer Pretraining

author.name: Rajit Rajpal, Benedict Leimkuhler

entry.summary: This paper introduces Rank-1 iKFAD (R-iKFAD), a memory-efficient variant of the recently proposed iKFAD optimizer that replaces adaptive learning rates with adaptive friction in momentum dynamics. By factorizing the full friction tensor as a rank-1 outer product of row and column momentum statistics, optimizer state memory per layer drops from O(mn) to O(m+n), roughly halving total optimizer memory, while experiments on transformer pretraining maintain performance parity with full iKFAD.

entry.title: LocUS: Head Selection and Subspace Projection for Targeted Activation Steering

author.name: Irene Tallini, Lorenzo Basile, Valentino Maiorca, Francesco Locatello, Alberto Cazzaniga

entry.summary: Introduces LocUS, a training-free activation steering method for LLMs that grounds steering directions in a property-specific linear subspace of the unembedding matrix, restricting the intervention geometrically. This mitigates coupling to off-target properties in contrastive data and degradation of unrelated capabilities compared with standard per-layer steering.

entry.title: Not All Memories Are Equal: Hierarchical Collaborative Memory for Validity-Aware Retrieval in LLM Agents

author.name: Yufei Shi, Rujing Yao, Ang Li, Yang Wu, Zhuoren Jiang, Xiaozhong Liu

entry.summary: The paper addresses memory retrieval in LLM agents for team collaboration, where flat semantic-relevance retrieval surfaces outdated or conflicting individual memories that no longer match team consensus. It proposes a hierarchical collaborative memory separating team-level decisions and protocols from individual observations, with validity-aware retrieval prioritizing currently valid memories. This is a relevant contribution to long-lived agent memory design.

entry.title: Feeding BabyLMs Macaroni: Code-Switching Curricula Cause Cross-Lingual Convergence

author.name: Dries Rooryck, Alex Cai, Yonatan Belinkov, David Alvarez-Melis, Kiant\'e Brantley

entry.summary: The authors pretrain small decoder-only transformers on 100M-word multilingual corpora and find that training on LLM-generated code-switched data aligns representations of parallel text, especially across scripts, with alignment persisting through subsequent monolingual training. A curriculum progressing from word-level to sentence-level code-switching further improves this. The work connects human bilingual code-switching phenomena to model cross-lingual alignment.

entry.title: TRACE: Temporal Audit and Condition-aware Evaluation of Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Yibo Ma, Qianqian Zhang, Peng Liu, Tiancheng Zhao

entry.summary: TRACE is a condition-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for streaming video understanding that makes evidence timing, history maintenance, and response triggering explicit. It combines temporally audited visual tasks with instruction-dependent trigger annotations and a unified causal Core-Adapter protocol controlling information availability. This addresses the problem that identical task scores can hide very different workloads and failure modes.

entry.title: Understanding the Role of Prompt Template in Knowledge Distillation for Safety Alignment

author.name: Anjila Budathoki, Manish Dhakal, Benjamin M. Ampel, Yi Ding

entry.summary: The paper studies how prompt template choice during knowledge distillation affects the safety alignment of student models, a previously unexplored factor. It finds significant degradation of pre-existing safety alignment, with chat templates making models more compliant with harmful queries than non-chat templates, consistently across LLaMA, Gemma, and Qwen model families. This highlights a subtle but consequential safety hazard in distillation pipelines.

entry.title: ToolSearcher: Optimizing Tool Selection at Scale via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhenlong Dai, Xujie Song, Zitong Wang, Tong Niu, Jian liu, Weiqiang Wang, Xiu Tang, Sai Wu, Chang Yao, Jingyuan Chen

entry.summary: ToolSearcher tackles large-scale tool selection for LLM agents, where real-world repositories contain thousands of tools exceeding context limits. The authors frame this as a new challenge for agentic RL, arguing existing methods designed for knowledge-based QA are inadequate, and train an RL-based selection approach. Tool selection at scale is a core bottleneck for practical agent deployment.

entry.title: Two Conformal Constructions for Adaptive Within-Document AI-Text Screening

author.name: Marco Mandap, Jerahmeel Hipolito, Arcel Galvez, Charlie Margaret Balagtas, Michael Joshua Buluran, Jeff Roel Durmiendo, Rizzette E. Lopez

entry.summary: The paper develops two finite-sample conformal constructions for AI-generated text screening that control false alerts at the document level, allowing adaptive selection of document prefixes and detectors with optional early stopping within an inspection budget. Construction A allocates a false-alert budget across a family of prefix-detector scores via a union bound over conformal ranks; Construction B calibrates the complete-path maximum of a fixed adaptive policy. The guarantee requires document-level exchangeability only, with no token-independence assumptions.

entry.title: STORM-Bench: Evaluating Online Video QA under Evolving and Incomplete Evidence

author.name: Siru Zhong, Shenghan Tan, Rihong Yan, Xiaohui Lv, Yuzheng Zhuang, Shuai Tao, Wulong Liu, Haohuan Fu, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: Introduces STORM-Bench, with 5,736 questions over 630 change-dense egocentric video episodes plus controlled simulation subsets, evaluating online video QA where models must track state transitions and selectively abstain when evidence is insufficient. It stratifies questions by accumulated change intensity and answerability, and proposes STORM-BR, a harmonic metric over joint answer-status correctness. Targets reliability of video models in streaming, information-limited settings.

entry.title: HyperErase: Scale-Calibrated Hypernetwork for Multi-Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Yi Sun, Xinhao Zhong, Zhiqi Zhang, Yimin Zhou, Junhao Li, Yuxia Qiao

entry.summary: Proposes HyperErase, a hypernetwork-based framework for concept erasure in text-to-image models that maps textual descriptions to prompt-specific LoRA parameters, reframing erasure as prompt-conditioned parameter amortization. This overcomes the parameter interference and poor prompt adaptation of static frozen-adapter erasure methods when scaling to multiple concepts. Relevant to T2I safety, copyright, and harmful-content mitigation.

entry.title: OpenVAM: Open-World Visual Attention Modeling with VLMs

author.name: Kiana Hooshanfar, Amirhossein Kazerouni, Alireza Hosseini, Michael Brudno, Babak Taati

entry.summary: OpenVAM is a unified framework for predicting human gaze that goes beyond dense saliency maps by linking attention peaks to discrete scene elements and explaining why they draw attention. It targets robustness across heterogeneous domains including natural images, commercial content, and UI/web layouts using vision-language models.

entry.title: FeatMark: Feature-level Watermark Protection against Mimicry Attacks with Diffusion Models

author.name: Haoyang Li, Ruoxi Sun, Qingqing Ye, Benjamin Zi Hao Zhao, Yaxin Xiao, Jason Xue, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: FeatMark defends against mimicry attacks on text-to-image diffusion models by embedding watermarks as inconspicuous, scene-consistent semantic micro-features instead of low-energy pixel perturbations. Shifting to feature-level signals provides stronger machine-verifiable protection that resists post-processing and adversarial suppression.

entry.title: Containing Behavioral Cascades from Manipulated Claims in LLM-Powered Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Waleed Bin Khalid, Byung-Cheol Min

entry.summary: This paper examines the security vulnerability of LLM-powered multi-robot systems to semantic manipulation, where an accepted false world-state claim can trigger fleet-wide behavioral cascades such as unnecessary replanning, congestion, or apparent mission infeasibility. The authors propose an active verification framework that generates a structured Verify-Adapt-Hold plan: selected robots inspect consequential regions, a limited subset provisionally adapts, and the rest retain trusted plans. Evaluation occurs in a multi-robot transportation environment.

entry.title: MR. POP: Multi-Robot Parallel Optimizing Planner for Almost-Surely Asymptotically Optimal Planning

author.name: Chih H. Huang, Roy Xing, Brian Plancher, Zachary Kingston

entry.summary: MR. POP introduces a GPU-based almost-surely asymptotically optimal multi-robot motion planner combining dRRT and the AO-x meta-algorithm, using SIMT parallelism to run hundreds of roadmap and tree search iterations concurrently. It reportedly becomes the only planner of its class to retain probabilistic convergence guarantees while scaling computationally to multi-robot settings. This is significant because multi-robot planning with optimality guarantees is a long-standing computational bottleneck.

entry.title: Impedance Cloning: Learning Equilibrium Point Parameters for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Hayato Takahashi, Ryoga Oishi, Yuki Kasuga, Toshiaki Tsuji

entry.summary: Impedance Cloning imitates biomechanical priors — stiffness and equilibrium point parameters — rather than trajectories, extracted from bilateral teleoperation demonstrations via a particle filter without force/torque sensors. Because these parameters encode intent instead of observable outcomes, policies passively absorb contact uncertainty and generalize across unseen surface geometries. Evaluated on two CRANE-X7 manipulators, it offers a compelling alternative to trajectory-based imitation for contact-rich tasks.

entry.title: Kintsugi-VLA: Turning Failed Robot Rollouts into Recovery Data through Interventional Recoverability

author.name: Ivan Snegirev, Elizaveta Semenyakina, Dmitrii Maliukov, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: This paper introduces Kintsugi-VLA, a simulation framework that converts failed vision-language-action policy rollouts into synthetic recovery training data using exact state restoration and branching. It defines interventional recoverability, the probability of completing a task after restoring the simulator to a failed state, to quantify which failures are worth learning from. This matters because it recovers value from data that standard demo pipelines discard, addressing a key gap in robot recovery behavior.

entry.title: The Price of Thought: Does Test-Time Reasoning Pay in LLM Trading?

author.name: Jiayi Chen, Guiling Wang

entry.summary: A controlled study of whether test-time reasoning improves LLM financial decision-making, varying reasoning effort across DeepSeek, GPT, and Gemini family models while holding prompts, information, and portfolio construction fixed. Over 800,000 asset predictions across a year of U.S. equities and three input conditions, it evaluates reasoning as an economic intervention net of trading costs.

entry.title: SkillEvoReg: Regularizing Agent Skill Evolution Against Overfitting

author.name: Guanyu Nie, Fangzhou Zhu, Shixiong Kai, Xiongwei Han, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan

entry.summary: Frames repeated skill-library updates in LLM agents as a learning process prone to overfitting, where locally useful edits accumulate into redundant or task-specific instructions. SkillEvoReg applies neural-network-style regularization to skill evolution: training-time skill dropout, complexity-aware local regularization, and causal counterexample validation to catch harmful updates. A timely contribution to self-improving agent reliability.

entry.title: Accounting for Bias Enables Sustainable LLM Evaluation

author.name: Harshita Katoch, David Antony Selby, Gerrit Gro{\ss}mann, Sebastian Vollmer

entry.summary: The paper argues that LLM-as-a-judge leaderboards compensate for systematic measurement biases (position, verbosity, severity, self-enhancement) by running ever more comparisons, which is statistically unsound and wasteful. It proposes a unified latent variable framework that jointly models pairwise and ordinal data while explicitly correcting for these confounders, recovering reliable rankings from far fewer comparisons. This offers a statistically grounded fix for a de facto standard evaluation methodology.

entry.title: BAT-CLIP: Trimodal Alignment of Brain, Audio and Text

author.name: Suhyun Kim, Jinmo Han, Danny Dongyeop Han, Ahhyun Lucy Lee, Jewoon Lee, Yonghyeon Gwon, Zach Paris, Chun Kee Chung, Saewoong Bahk, Nam Soo Kim, Seong Jae Hwang, Jiook Cha

entry.summary: BAT-CLIP is the first CLIP-style trimodal alignment framework for intracranial EEG that jointly aligns neural embeddings to both pretrained audio and text anchors in a shared frozen audio-text manifold, overcoming the trade-off of single-anchor approaches. It shows strong results on naturalistic speech decoding benchmarks.

entry.title: Dynamic Regret in Online Convex Optimization with Indicator Switching Costs

author.name: Naram Mhaisen, George Iosifidis

entry.summary: The paper studies dynamic regret in online convex optimization under indicator switching costs, a fixed penalty whenever consecutive decisions differ, capturing real system costs like server activation and model deployment. The authors prove that direct extensions of existing static-comparator techniques fail, and propose a meta-learning framework of randomized lazy FTRL base learners restarted at dyadic timescales, aggregated by a movement-aware master algorithm. This yields the first meaningful dynamic guarantees for this cost model.

entry.title: Online Learning via Learned Latent Bayesian Tracking

author.name: Guy Gerson, Tomer Raviv, Nir Shlezinger, Tirza Routtenberg, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: The paper casts online learning in non-stationary environments as Bayesian state tracking over a learned low-dimensional latent dynamics space, identifying the missing low-dimensional representation as the core bottleneck for Bayesian filtering on deep models. It proposes a method (Adaptive Update through learned latent tracking) enabling rapid adaptation under strict compute constraints.

entry.title: AcoustiClaim: A Numeric Claim Benchmark with Instrument Ground Truth

author.name: Sheng-Tse Lin, Siyuan Zhai, Chien-Liang Kuo, Massa Baali, Bhiksha Raj

entry.summary: AcoustiClaim is a benchmark for evaluating whether numeric claims made by audio language models about acoustic quantities (e.g., pitch) are true, scoring each extracted numeric claim against instrument-based ground truth. Testing four open-weight and one closed model across many quantity-corpus-question combinations reveals that most systems emit few distinct values and errors sit at or above a constant-predictor floor, exposing major gaps in factual numeric grounding for audio models.

entry.title: Prompt Injection Detection for Email Agents Through Attack Chain Modeling

author.name: Ahmad Hashmi, Dhyey Patel, Yunting Yin

entry.summary: This work targets indirect prompt injection in LLM email assistants, arguing that binary malicious-text classification misses how harmful agent behavior emerges across a sequence of stages. The authors propose a framework combining a text detector, stage-specific verifiers, rule-based risk signals, user-intent and action-consistency analysis, and a logistic decision policy, with attack-chain labels derived from existing injection datasets.

entry.title: TRACKGRAPH: Online Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs via Image-Space Tracking

author.name: Peder Borge Hellesylt, Albert Gassol Puigjaner, Kostas Alexis, Annette Stahl

entry.summary: Presents TRACKGRAPH, an online system for open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs that maintains 2D mask identity in the image stream using FastSAM/CLIP at sparse keyframes and dense DINOv3 features for high-rate mask propagation, then fuses tracked masks into a class-agnostic 3D segment layer. This avoids per-image segmentation and frequent VL inference, cutting compute for robots reasoning about unknown environments with natural language. Practical efficiency contribution for embodied AI.

entry.title: FlatClip: A Geometry-Aware Surface-Level Baseline for fMRI Representation Learning

author.name: Mo Wang, Wenhao Ye, Zihan Ning, Jiayu Zuo, Junfeng Xia, Hongkai Wen, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: FlatClip renders cortical fMRI activity as geometry-aware flatmap sequences and reuses a frozen SigLIP2 image encoder with only a lightweight probe, avoiding costly fMRI-specific 3D/4D pretraining. It shows image-pretrained encoders can effectively exploit the geometry-constrained organization of brain activity.

entry.title: Audio LLMs Know When They Can't Hear You

author.name: Amirhosein Javadi, Richa Dixit, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Minsik Cho, Devang Naik, Mohammad Samragh

entry.summary: Studies whether audio LLMs can recognize when their own transcriptions are unreliable on degraded input, finding that models are poor self-judges and that existing approaches (quality predictors, uncertainty, transcript-conditioned WER estimation) are insufficient. The paper proposes improved methods for model-conditional transcription reliability detection, apparently from a Meta-affiliated team.

entry.title: A Benchmark and Diagnostic Study of Epistemic Admission in Shared Agent Memory

author.name: Xiaoyang Li, Yiqi Wang, Chencheng Zhu, KE XU, Wencheng Yang, Zequn Sun, Pingan Song, Yiqun Duan, Taotao Cai

entry.summary: Introduces the Correlated Promotion Benchmark (CPB) to test whether agent claims should be admitted to shared memory, addressing how repeated or paraphrased claims can be mistaken for independent evidence. CPB-Static provides a frozen gold-action test split while CPB-Live records writes, retrievals, and source lineage in live multi-agent runs, with a separate consumer answering from the store. Evaluates eight admission policies across four agent families.

entry.title: MoMHa: Multi-Objective Optimization of LLM Harnesses over Accuracy, Safety, and Tokens

author.name: Subhojyoti Mukherjee, Md Mehrab Tanjim

entry.summary: Argues the harness (the surrounding code building prompts, routing calls, and parsing outputs) is a first-class multi-objective design surface, and presents Meta-Harness, which searches harness designs over accuracy, behavioral safety, and token cost using an agentic proposer (Claude Code) with filesystem access to prior source, traces, and scoring artifacts. A key finding is that single-phase joint rewriting underperforms relative to staged approaches. Reframes harness engineering as an optimization problem.

entry.title: Cheap, open agents make LLM pollution harder to mitigate

author.name: Raluca Rilla, Anne-Marie Nussberger, Rui Mata, Dirk U. Wulff

entry.summary: The study evaluates nine survey-completing agent configurations from fully open-weight to closed commercial models to assess the risk of LLM pollution, where synthetic responses contaminate human behavioral datasets. Fully open agents running locally without fees perform competitively with commercial ones, and open and commercial agents fail different detection checks, so no single check reliably detects them. This shows falling deployment costs have removed a key barrier to data pollution, raising stakes for detection methods.

entry.title: Which Influence Are We Estimating? The Role of Counterfactual Specifications in Data Attribution

author.name: Zhe Li, Wei Zhao, Peixin Zhang, Jun Sun

entry.summary: The authors argue that incompatible rankings produced by different influence estimators stem not just from approximation error but from specification mismatch: influence depends on the attributed behavior, the per-example intervention, and the counterfactual training process. They formalize influence as a counterfactual estimand and classify mismatches across specifications. This is a foundational clarification for data attribution, debugging, and valuation.

entry.title: A Flow Matching Framework for Neural Representational Dissimilarity

author.name: Zeyuan Ye, Xue-Xin Wei

entry.summary: The authors show that a variety of neural representational dissimilarity metrics can be unified under the flow matching framework from deep generative models, with distances arising as Jeffreys divergences under different velocity constraints. Flow matching improves estimation for complicated distributions and continuous variables, and enables principled design of new distance metrics. This connects modern generative modeling to neuroscience and model comparison.

entry.title: Strategic Self-Consistency

author.name: Tori Qiu, Ander Artola Velasco, Manuel Gomez-Rodriguez

entry.summary: This paper shows that an unfaithful LLM provider can exploit self-consistency pricing: because providers charge per reasoning path, they have an incentive to inflate path counts. The authors present a simple, efficient algorithm that generates and strategically reorders additional reasoning paths so every path appears necessary to reach the majority answer while evading auditor detection. Experiments with multiple models validate the attack.

entry.title: CARGO: Context-Aware Retrieval-Gated Evaluation of Agentic AI in Production

author.name: Mukul Chhabra, Shail Patel, Luigi Medrano

entry.summary: CARGO addresses reference-instance divergence (RID), a failure mode where LLM-as-a-judge evaluation penalizes deployed agentic systems because the closest reference applies the correct procedure to a different entity. The framework treats retrieved references as procedural exemplars, grounds factual judgments in the live instance's context, assigns three-way claim statuses, and penalizes only contradictions.

entry.title: Subject-Invariant Cross-Modal Decoding of Perceived Speech from Brain Recordings

author.name: Aoke Zhang, Jing Chen

entry.summary: SICMD is a unified method for perceived speech decoding from non-invasive BCI signals that simultaneously addresses rich spatiotemporal neural representation and cross-subject generalization by integrating fMRI and MEG. The paper analyzes fusion methods, fusion positions, and encoder architectures. It advances neural decoding toward robust, subject-independent applications.

entry.title: UltraG-Bench: A Multi-task Benchmark for assessing Large Vision-Language Models on Pixel-level Evidence Grounding in Ultrasound

author.name: Quanhao Zhu, Bo Xu, Rui Lin, Chenyuan Wang, Yu Shao, Boling Zhu, Jiuyan Sun, Liang Zhao, Hongfei Lin, Feng Xia

entry.summary: UltraG-Bench is a large-scale multi-task benchmark evaluating pixel-level evidence grounding of vision-language models in ultrasound, built from 40 public segmentation datasets across 13 anatomical categories. It comprises instruction-guided segmentation, evidence-grounded VQA, and evidence-grounded report generation. It reveals that current VLMs fail to provide pixel-level visual evidence aligned with their semantic predictions.

entry.title: Can Pixels Alone Reveal Image Origin? Minimax Limits and Learnable Interfaces for Passive Provenance

author.name: Kai Yao

entry.summary: The paper formalizes passive image provenance (distinguishing human, generic AI, or specific generator origin) as source-target verification under adversarial distribution shift. It derives an architecture-independent best-case limit based on total-variation distance and explains why deployed public verifiers can fail before reaching that bound.

entry.title: Towards Mitigating Fabricated Consensus: The Active Provenance Gate for Multi-Agent Debate Synthesis

author.name: Jakub Mas{\l}owski, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: The paper studies fabricated consensus in multi-agent debate systems, where summarizing models produce smooth but ungrounded synthesis despite detailed debate logs. It empirically evaluates active post-debate verification gates and whether explicitly signaling divergence is preferable when no reliable compromise exists.

entry.title: Can You Check That? The Checkability Boundary for Local LLM Network Automation

author.name: Maleeha Masood, Momina Nofal

entry.summary: The paper introduces checkability as a criterion for which network-automation tasks suit local small-model inference: a task is checkable if it admits a cheap, deterministic intrinsic check that rejects outputs violating a necessary correctness condition. The Touchstone pipeline uses seven 1-8B SLMs with intrinsic checks and escalates unresolvable cases, balancing privacy (no data egress) against correctness.

entry.title: PALM: Point-in-Time Adaptation for Financial Language Models

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Jaehoon Lee, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: PALM tackles look-ahead bias in financial language model backtests by examining whether the common practice of pretraining one point-in-time checkpoint per calendar year is necessary. The authors find newer checkpoints score no better than older ones on the same evaluation window, motivating a cheaper adaptation approach that avoids a full pretraining run per year. This could substantially reduce the cost of temporally honest financial LLM evaluation.

entry.title: GyroNovo: Error-Guided Fragment Imputation with Mass-Aware Attention for \textit{De Novo} Peptide Sequencing

author.name: Abdellah El Mekki, Laks V. S. Lakshmanan, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed

entry.summary: GyroNovo improves de novo peptide sequencing from tandem mass spectra by guiding fragment imputation with decoder error signals rather than treating imputation as a fixed reconstruction task, and by explicitly modeling mass differences between peaks via mass-aware attention. The approach targets the core difficulty that experimental spectra are sparse, noisy, and leave informative b- and y-ion fragments unobserved. This couples imputation directly to downstream autoregressive decoding quality.

entry.title: Missingness-Aware Conformal Prediction Under Cross-Hospital Distribution Shift

author.name: Liang You, Dongwen Ou, Hengyu Shi, Siyuan Dai

entry.summary: The paper proposes a missingness-aware conformal calibration procedure for mortality prediction under cross-hospital distribution shift, selecting a measurement on an independent sample, grouping patients by whether it is recorded, and applying Mondrian calibration within each group. Evaluated across hospitals in eICU and across care units within a MIMIC-IV hospital with three predictors, the method reduces average worst-group coverage gaps relative to pooled calibration. This addresses the fact that marginal conformal coverage does not ensure coverage within missingness-defined groups.

entry.title: Aligning One-Step Generative Models with Reward-Weighted Transport Distillation

author.name: Austin Wang, Ziheng Cheng, Lexing Ying

entry.summary: RWTD is a post-training method for one-step visual generators that requires only generated samples and scalar reward evaluations, sidestepping the lack of tractable likelihoods or differentiable rewards in implicit generators. It constructs an adaptive target mixing reward-tilted current and reference distributions, incorporating improvements discovered during training while anchoring to the pretrained model.

entry.title: Learning Hierarchical Causal Representations of the Effects of Forcings on Temperature in Climate Models

author.name: Shan Zhao, Ilija Trajkovic, Julia Kaltenborn, Yaniv Gurwicz, Peer Nowack, David Rolnick, Julien Boussard

entry.summary: The authors develop a hierarchical causal representation learning framework for sea surface temperature fields from a state-of-the-art climate model, explicitly separating internal climate variability (atmospheric dynamics) from forced responses to greenhouse gas and aerosol changes. This addresses the black-box trustworthiness of ML climate emulators and enables causal attribution use.

entry.title: Evaluating the accuracy of KV cache reuse techniques

author.name: Samuel Cestola, Tianxiang Xia, Pengfei Zheng, Weiyan Zheng, Bo Wang, Yi Zhao, Diego Didona

entry.summary: The paper shows current evaluations of position-independent KV cache reuse for retrieval-augmented generation fail to faithfully measure accuracy loss, inflating reported effectiveness. It proposes an unambiguous evaluation methodology and Boxoffice, a tool that generates datasets exercising challenging KV reuse patterns.

entry.title: Trust Guided Decision Transformer

author.name: Chainesh Gautam, Raghuram Bharadwaj Diddigi, Chandramouli Kamanchi, Pankaj Dayama, Sumanta Mukherjee, Kameshwaran Sampath

entry.summary: TGDT addresses context drift in Decision Transformers during long rollouts by monitoring the model's own next-state prediction error, which rises when the conditioning context becomes unreliable. It uses split conformal prediction calibrated on held-out offline data to select trustworthy context suffixes, then applies value guidance with a frozen critic on the filtered context.

entry.title: Learning to Replace MCMC in Split-Gibbs Diffusion Posterior Sampling via Deep Unfolding

author.name: Yi Zhang, Rui Guo, Mengchu Xu, Zhaofeng Liu, Yonina C. Eldar

entry.summary: This work replaces the costly iterative MCMC likelihood update in split Gibbs sampling for diffusion posterior sampling with learned Gaussian denoising steps implemented through ODE diffusion, reusing a pretrained denoiser for the prior update and a lightweight deep-unfolded network for the likelihood. The result enables diffusion-based posterior inference for general nonlinear inverse problems with better parallelism and lower computational cost.

entry.title: Open Vocabulary Domain Unlearning

author.name: Sumanth Udupa, Mehrtash Harandi, Yadan Luo, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh

entry.summary: Identifies a flaw in approximate domain unlearning for vision-language models: existing methods are evaluated only on object classes seen during unlearning, so they overfit to seen class-domain pairs rather than removing the domain itself, leaving it recognizable for unseen classes. The paper proposes an open-vocabulary unlearning setting and method to erase a target visual domain while preserving performance on other domains.

entry.title: Symbiotic Architecture for Post-Hoc Audio Extension of Frozen Language Models

author.name: Yotaro Kubo, Qi Sun, Yujin Tang

entry.summary: The paper proposes an architecture that equips frozen LLMs with audio understanding without fine-tuning, by having an injector module write audio-conditioned vectors directly into the KV cache. Injection cost scales with injector width rather than backbone width, and the training scheme decouples audio processing from the LLM. This offers a scalable alternative to full multimodal pretraining of audio-language models.

entry.title: The Shape of Events: Edge-Based Inductive Biases via Cross-Domain Distillation

author.name: Soshun Kihara, Shunsuke Yasuki, Masato Taki

entry.summary: The paper uses knowledge distillation from event cameras to the RGB domain to dissect the inductive bias that event data instills in vision models, exploiting the rich RGB evaluation toolkit. Since event cameras capture only brightness changes, they naturally emphasize contours, contrasting with ImageNet-trained CNNs' texture bias and corresponding fragility under distribution shift. The work systematically characterizes how edge-focused biases transfer and affect robustness.

entry.title: Light Field Primitive for Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Liang Chen, Jiahui Ning, Xun Jiang, Xing Xu, Jimmy Ren, Fenglei Fan, Heng Tao Shen

entry.summary: Introduces Light Field Primitives, a novel view synthesis formulation replacing dense ray databases with a compact set of differentiable primitives in the classical two-plane parameterization, where each primitive condenses a group of rays and rendering composites primitive responses to a query ray. Scenes optimize directly from posed images and render in real time, with structural advantages for optical and appearance effects native to 4D ray space. An alternative representation alongside NeRF/Gaussian splatting.

entry.title: KneePreM: Towards 3D Knee MRI Foundation Models via Large-Scale Unlabeled Pretraining and Label-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Xinxin Wang, Liam Hazan, Jing Li, Simona Rabinovici-Cohen, Xiaojuan Li, Mingrui Yang

entry.summary: KneePreM is a knee-specific 3D masked-autoencoder pretrained on about 19,000 unlabeled OAI MRI series, evaluated on multiple classification and segmentation downstream tasks with reduced label budgets. It demonstrates transfer and label efficiency relative to random initialization and SuPreM baselines.

entry.title: Structured Reasoning Agentic Framework for Interpretable Critical View of Safety Assessment

author.name: Qing Xu, Yuxiang Luo, Zhen Chen

entry.summary: ReasonCVS decomposes Critical View of Safety assessment in laparoscopic cholecystectomy into explicit fine-grained anatomical verification steps using VLM-based agents, replacing holistic black-box prediction. The structured reasoning improves interpretability and compositional generalization for surgical safety checks.

entry.title: TempQ-Jail: Query-Constrained Candidate Ranking for Text-to-Video Jailbreak Attacks

author.name: Tianmeng Fang, Jiancheng Wang, Chen Wang, Liming Wang, Wei Wang, Jiayang Liu, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: TempQ-Jail formulates text-to-video jailbreaking as a query-constrained candidate allocation and ranking problem, scoring candidates on security-gate passage, dangerous content generation, intent preservation, and temporal validity. This lets attackers find high-value bypasses under tight query budgets in guarded T2V systems.

entry.title: GraspTwin: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Grasp Optimization via a Digital Twin

author.name: Daniel J. Evans, Yinlong Dai, Simon Stepputtis, Dylan P. Losey

entry.summary: GraspTwin bridges task-agnostic robust grasping and foundation-model task reasoning via a real-to-sim digital twin pipeline for zero-shot task-oriented grasping. It addresses cases like grasping a mug by its handle to enable pouring, where purely robust grasps ignore task requirements and foundation-model grasp proposals lack fine physical grounding. The digital twin enables optimization of task-appropriate, physically valid grasps without task-specific training.

entry.title: RoboMonitor: Label-Efficient Runtime Monitoring of Robot Task Execution via Predictive Representation Learning

author.name: Abhiroop Ajith, Gokul Narayanan, Kyle Coelho, Tingji Zhao, Yash Shahapurkar, Brian Zhu, Melih Erdogan, Ted Krubasik, Constantinos Chamzas, Eugen Solowjow

entry.summary: RoboMonitor is a label-efficient vision-language execution monitor for robot manipulation that pre-trains on 25 hours of unlabeled multi-camera trajectories using action-conditioned future prediction, inverse dynamics, and masking objectives, then adds light monitoring supervision. It identifies execution phases, failures, and completion, addressing the annotation scarcity problem for policy monitoring. Runtime monitoring is a critical but under-served layer for reliable robot deployment.

entry.title: INTERACT: Interactive Planning for Autonomous Driving via Anchor-Conditioned Prediction and Trust-Region Refinement

author.name: Aron Distelzweig, Andreas Look, Faris Janjo\v{s}, Steffen Hagedorn, Luigi Palmieri, Joschka Boedecker

entry.summary: INTERACT addresses the prediction-planning coupling in dense urban driving by conditioning a single reactive prediction on trajectory intent anchors rather than exact trajectory realizations, then refining plans within a trust region where that prediction remains valid. This avoids task interference from joint training and the proposal-set restrictions of prior separate prediction-planning methods. It offers a practical route to interactive, closed-loop driving behavior.

entry.title: A Synthetic Ground-Truth Framework for the Evaluation of Explainable AI Methods

author.name: Miquel Mir\'o-Nicolau, Francesco Spinnato, Riccardo Guidotti

entry.summary: Addresses the lack of ground-truth explanations in XAI evaluation by proposing a synthetic ground-truth framework. It argues that fidelity-based evaluation only measures whether explanations reproduce model outputs, not whether they reflect the underlying decision process, and provides a way to compare XAI methods against known true explanations.

entry.title: FTB Graph: Determining and Validating First-token Broadcasters and Language-Identity Head Circuits in Multilingual Language Models

author.name: Arjun Pillai, Christian Hoang, Anjelo Laroza

entry.summary: Performs end-to-end structural circuit analysis of how multilingual LLMs resolve response language at the first token, across GPT-2, BLOOM-560M, Pythia-1B/2.8B, and Qwen2.5-1.5B. Using Edge Attribution Patching with FP16 active clamping, verified by exact activation patching over a 2,000-candidate-edge search, it extracts directed acyclic graphs driving first-token language broadcasting, finding deep or mid-to-deep hubs with strongest evidence in Pythia. Advances mechanistic understanding of multilingual generation.

entry.title: Multi-agent Scaling Across Disjunctive and Compensatory Tasks

author.name: Carolina Fortuna, Blaz Bertalanic

entry.summary: This paper applies Steiner's taxonomy of group tasks from social psychology to analyze how multi-agent LLM performance scales with team size, distinguishing disjunctive from compensatory tasks. Modeling agents as conditionally independent yields large-team limits: plurality voting converges to the modal answer and averaging to item-level bias. Experiments with 13 open-weight models and teams up to 30 agents across representative benchmarks reveal qualitatively different scaling behavior by task type.

entry.title: MVVBench: Benchmarking 4D Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hyungjin Chung, Byeongjun Park, Joonseok Lee, Hojun Kim, Jaeho Choi, Byung-Hoon Kim

entry.summary: MVVBench is a benchmark for multi-view video reasoning in vision-language models, built from real-world multi-camera datasets with questions curated to be monocular-ambiguous along both view and temporal axes. Each question is only solvable by jointly integrating spatial and temporal evidence across non-overlapping camera streams. This probes latent 4D continuity reasoning rather than single-frame perception.

entry.title: A Safety-Bounded SDC-to-MCP Gateway for Medical AI Agents

author.name: Bennet Gerlach, Stefan Fischer

entry.summary: The paper presents a gateway that exposes IEEE 11073 SDC medical device state and alarms to MCP-based AI agents as read-only resources, with action affordances limited to policy-validated dry-run tools. The safety-bounded design enforces deterministic constraints so agents cannot execute physical effects on medical equipment.

entry.title: RAZOR: Pruning Replaceable Experts in LLMs

author.name: Mingyang Song, Mao Zheng

entry.summary: RAZOR is a training-free method for pruning mixture-of-experts LLMs that scores each expert's functional replaceability via consensus residuals, deviations of expert outputs from the original weighted mixture, using an exact single-deletion identity that accounts for survivor renormalization and router refill. It argues that usage or magnitude alone does not determine removal damage. This matters because MoE models store full expert pools that are mostly inactive per token.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning of Communication in a Mesh of Small Language Models

author.name: Mehmet Kerem Turkcan

entry.summary: TalkMesh is a decentralized mesh of small language model agents that learns when and what to communicate to overcome the saturation of majority voting over independent samples. Each agent samples a proposal scored by a trained confidence head; the most confident agent broadcasts a hint and lower-confidence agents revise, with gossip consensus approximating confidence-weighted voting without a coordinator. A communication policy is trained with group-based reinforcement learning.

entry.title: SAGE: A sampling-aware global evaluation benchmark for species distribution modeling

author.name: Emilia Arens, Nina van Tiel, Robin Zbinden, Damien Robert, Lukas Drees, Chiara Vanalli, Benjamin Kellenberger, Niklaus E. Zimmermann, Lo\"ic Pellissier, Devis Tuia, Jan Dirk Wegner

entry.summary: SAGE is a global evaluation benchmark for deep-learning species distribution models that accounts for strongly biased community-science occurrence records and species-level performance variability, which aggregated metrics hide, especially for rare species of conservation concern. It enables trustworthy assessment of where DeepSDMs can be relied upon across thousands of species.

entry.title: Benchmarking Attention for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Maximilian Schambach, Clemens Biehl, Sam Thelin

entry.summary: The paper builds a reproducible benchmark for efficient attention in tabular in-context learners like TabPFN and Mitra, where 2D row/column attention patterns differ fundamentally from 1D language-model attention. It analyzes the unique characteristics of the tabular setting, including long row sequences, short column sequences, and strided memory layouts.

entry.title: StarWM: Self-Supervised Trained Attention Routing for Robust World Models

author.name: Zeqiang Zhang, Fabian Wurzberger, Maximilian Otte, Daniel Schmid, Sebastian Gottwald, Arne Peter Raulf, Daniel Alexander Braun

entry.summary: StarWM improves world models by using a cross-attention module trained with self-supervised dynamics objectives to decide where reconstruction should apply, with a dual-stream decoder restricting reconstruction to attended regions and stop-gradient barriers preventing collapse. This addresses the misallocation of representational capacity toward task-irrelevant pixel areas in reconstruction-based world models while avoiding the information loss of reconstruction-free alternatives.

entry.title: Beyond Mean Attention: Diversity-Aware, Layer-Wise Scoring for KV Cache Eviction

author.name: Tianfang Xie, Wei Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a unified KV cache eviction score that augments mean attention with attention dispersion and a redundancy penalty relative to already-selected tokens, giving an MMR-like relevance-diversity balance without extra forward passes. Depth-dependent score profiles tuned on a development split improve over fixed coefficients on 16 LongBench datasets with Mistral-7B.

entry.title: LandscapeSHAP: Which Persistent Homology Class Gets the Credit?

author.name: Nikola Mili\'cevi\'c

entry.summary: The paper introduces LandscapeSHAP, reportedly the first application of Shapley values to explain models trained on topological data analysis features, specifically persistence landscapes. Because landscape coordinates are rank statistics, attributing predictions back to individual persistent homology classes is nontrivial, and the method provides a fair credit allocation scheme. This bridges cooperative game theory, TDA, and explainable AI.

entry.title: Gap-free Differentially Private PCA for Gaussian Data

author.name: Alina Ene, Huy L. Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper presents a gap-free differentially private algorithm for principal component analysis with Gaussian data, removing the eigenvalue-gap assumptions that typically restrict DP PCA guarantees. This extends the practical applicability of private PCA to settings where spectral gaps are absent.

entry.title: All In Good Time: Causality-Aware Framework for LLM-Based Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation

author.name: Amir Hussein, Enas Albasiri, Travis M. Bartley, Nourchene Ferchichi, Ke Hu, Harishchandra Dubey, Myungjong Kim, Zhehuai Chen, Oluwatobi Olabiyi, Sanjeev Khudanpur

entry.summary: The paper proposes a causality-aware simultaneous speech-to-speech translation framework with a data pipeline generating high-fidelity, causally aligned training segments with voice transfer. It contributes a factorized S2ST architecture (FAST), a causality-aware adaptive policy (CAP) replacing fixed translation policies, and new latency metrics. The author list includes NVIDIA speech researchers, indicating industry involvement.

entry.title: Where Does Retrieval-Based Open-Ended Evaluation Fail? Automatic Taxonomy Induction from Long-Form Medical Answer Factuality Verification

author.name: Heyuan Huang, Jirui Dai, Alexandra DeLucia, Sonal Joshi, Mahsa Yarmohammadi, Jie Gao, Bernal Jim\'enez Guti\'errez, Mark Dredze

entry.summary: The paper builds two comprehensive taxonomies of failure modes in retrieval-based medical factuality evaluation, grounded in a case study on the MedExpert dataset, decomposing failures into retrieval-stage errors along five quality dimensions. Unlike prior RAG diagnostics, it requires neither gold answers nor annotated evidence, which suits open-ended settings. This makes hallucination-detection failures in clinical contexts diagnosable rather than hidden behind aggregate F1 scores.

entry.title: I-Parakeet: Integer-Only Conformer ASR on Mobile NPU

author.name: Taichi Nishimura

entry.summary: I-Parakeet is an integer-only implementation of NVIDIA's Parakeet-CTC 0.6B Conformer ASR model that runs on a smartphone NPU without floating-point operators or CPU fallback. Key contributions include an integer formulation of relative-positional self-attention fusing two score branches and the relative shift, plus additional quantization techniques. This enables full exploitation of integer accelerators for edge ASR deployment.

entry.title: ZooWork-ShopRanker: An Open, Preference-Aligned E-Commerce Reranker

author.name: Siqiao Xue, Shuxuan Liu, Ning Hu

entry.summary: ZooWork-ShopRanker is a family of open e-commerce rerankers (0.6B, 4B, 8B) aligned to shopping preferences using pairwise labels generated by a panel of reasoning LLMs serving as a preference oracle, with position-debiased judgments and agreement tiers. It addresses the gap where general web rerankers transfer imperfectly to e-commerce ranking. This offers both a practical artifact and a scalable synthetic-labeling methodology.

entry.title: Timo: $\textbf{T}$aming Mult$\textbf{i}$modal Diffusion Transformer for Human $\textbf{Mo}$tion Generation

author.name: Zhao Wang, Jiangtao Hu, Jack Yu, Tao Yu

entry.summary: Timo adapts multimodal diffusion transformers (MMDiT) to human motion generation, addressing the observation that articulated motion is temporally coherent but weakly correlated across joints, which makes naive MMDiT with flow matching produce jerky, poorly coordinated motion. The framework combines fully shared multimodal attention for bidirectional text-motion modeling with kinematics-aware components tailored to motion structure. This brings joint text-visual modeling advances from image generation into motion synthesis.

entry.title: DAPEVO: Deep Adaptive Patch Frame-Event Visual Odometry

author.name: Luca Gandolfi, Simone Nascivera, Roberto Pellerito, Rong Zou, Chiara Plizzari, Davide Scaramuzza

entry.summary: DAPEVO is a learned visual odometry system that fuses standard RGB frames with event camera data by tracking patches independently in each modality and combining correlation evidence through a learned per-patch gate before motion refinement. This addresses RGB vulnerabilities to blur, poor lighting, and dropped frames while handling the asynchronous nature of event cameras. Relevant for GPS-denied autonomous navigation such as drones and robots.

entry.title: Gauss What You Need: Compact Gaussian Splatting Across Scene Scales

author.name: Afif Boudaoud, Jiayi Liu, Alexandru Calotoiu, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: Introduces TangoGS, addressing the unsolved problem of automatically selecting the number of Gaussian primitives in 3D Gaussian Splatting across capture scales. It combines capture-derived model size planning from known surface extent and resolution with training-time signals from reconstruction quality, since content complexity emerges during optimization. Aims to avoid under- or over-provisioning primitives that hurt detail, storage, and rendering cost on large captures.

entry.title: Enabling a Unified Cross-Domain Representation for Two-Finger Gripper Manipulation via Interaction-Centric Modeling

author.name: Guanlin Li, Shifeng Bao, Yihan Zhao, Haitao Shen, Haoyang Li, Chen Zhao, Tong Yang, Jie Tang, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: An interaction-centric imitation learning framework abstracts two-finger grippers into a parameterized universal gripper, yielding a canonical gripper-frame representation that disentangles task semantics from hardware-specific visual geometry. It combines VLM subtask inference, SAM 2.1 mask tracking, and hybrid potential-field plus point-cloud features for manipulation control.

entry.title: MOCHA: Multi-Objective Co-Design using Hypernetwork Architectures

author.name: Varun Madabushi, Neil Janwani, Maegan Tucker

entry.summary: MOCHA is, to the authors' knowledge, the first RL-based approach computing a family of Pareto-optimal policies across a robot's design space with a single network. It uses a multi-objective design hypernetwork (MDH) that produces policy parameters specialized for a given objective and parameterized robot design, demonstrated on two robot morphologies with six design dimensions and 2-3 objectives, with an evolutionary-search approach for efficiently producing Design Pareto sets.

entry.title: FRAM: Trajectory-Guided Visual Feature Selection for Compact Language-Conditioned Robot Manipulation

author.name: Hiroshi Ito, Hyogo Hiruma, Yoshiki Kanai, Takahiro Yoshida, Akira Kanazawa, Hiroki Yamada

entry.summary: FRAM is a compact (138.7M parameter) language-conditioned manipulation policy that uses predicted future end-effector trajectory image coordinates as spatial pointers to select task-relevant local visual features, organizing information as where, what, and future. Trajectory labels are auto-generated from demonstrations and camera geometry, requiring no manual annotation. It shows competitive manipulation performance at a fraction of typical VLA parameter counts.

entry.title: CRC-Router: Risk-Constrained Routing for Medical Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Xueyang Li, Mingze Jiang, Gelei Xu, Jun Xia, Ching-Hao Chiu, Mengzhao Jia, Danny Z. Chen, Yiyu Shi

entry.summary: Proposes CRC-Router, a risk-constrained, uncertainty-aware routing module for medical imaging AI that decides when a system should act autonomously versus escalate a case for human review. It combines multiple complementary uncertainty signals with predictive performance to prevent autonomous errors from propagating into clinical decisions.

entry.title: PTC-Decoder: Towards Intelligent SLMs on Offline Resource-Constrained Edge Devices

author.name: Minghui Yu, Ke Mu, Gang Wu

entry.summary: Proposes PTC-Decoder, a training-free, plug-and-play decoder for small language models on edge devices that forces plan invocation at the first inference step and uses a finite-automaton-based TC-Decoder to constrain tokens to valid plan-then-act sequences. Motivated by satellite-like offline deployments where SLMs ignore prompt-based plan enforcement. Improves reliability of multi-step agent tasks without additional training.

entry.title: Up and Down the Abstraction Ladder: Code-Based Skills for Language Agents

author.name: Bart{\l}omiej Cupia{\l}, Jens Tuyls, Maciej Wo{\l}czyk, Davide Paglieri, Martin Klissarov, Benjamin Eysenbach, Piotr Mi{\l}o\'s, Karthik R. Narasimhan

entry.summary: This work systematically studies how code-based action abstractions (reusable skills invoked by language models) affect performance, inference cost, and learning of language agents in NetHack, a long-horizon environment. It addresses the tradeoff that abstractions boost productivity but are leaky, requiring occasional fallback to primitive actions. The systematic treatment of when to operate at which abstraction level is a valuable contribution to agent design.

entry.title: Adaptive multi-resolution Gaussian processes: Scalable exact inference with naturally data-sparse covariance matrices

author.name: Yanchuang Cao, Jun Liu, Tengchao Yu, Heng Yong

entry.summary: This work presents an adaptive multi-resolution Gaussian process framework achieving scalable yet exact inference by constructing naturally data-sparse covariance matrices from adaptive multi-resolution basis functions anchored directly to samples. Shrinking support domains limits block sizes and guarantees sparsity, and the inverse is computed exactly and efficiently.
