This bridges the usual trade-off between computational efficiency and model fidelity in large-scale GP inference.

entry.title: TrafficImag: A Benchmark for Counterfactual Roadside Traffic Video Generation

author.name: Xiangyu Li, Tianyi Wang, Zhihao Dou, Christian Claudel, Zhaomiao Guo

entry.summary: TrafficImag is the first benchmark for counterfactual roadside traffic video generation, combining 9,022 annotated images, 7,043 video clips, and 31,145 actor-centered history-future samples with an executable intervention protocol. It tests whether generated futures remain consistent with road topology and unaffected traffic after modifying a selected actor. This enables rigorous evaluation of controllable generative video models for traffic simulation.

entry.title: MoSAR: Mixture of Semantic Attention Regimes for Learning Adaptive and Approximable Attention Geometries

author.name: Michele Paolicelli, Alessandro Petruzzelli, Alessandro Franceso Maria Martina, Cataldo Musto, Giovanni Semeraro

entry.summary: MoSAR treats attention approximation as a geometric learning problem, introducing a mixture of semantic attention regimes that learns input-conditioned, controlled-decay geometry over query-key interactions instead of prescribing sparsity or locality in advance. This targets the quadratic cost of dense self-attention in long-context language modeling.

entry.title: Sorry Robot, Happy Human: Vision-Language Models Read Only One of Two Legible Typographic Layers

author.name: Mert \.Incidelen, Yamen Kashkash, Asya Berker, Murat Aydo\u{g}an

entry.summary: The paper introduces DecoyBench, 300 images with two superimposed text layers that humans read easily, and shows six recent closed-source VLMs can read only one layer. This exposes a structural fragility in VLM text perception and a related typographic attack surface, contrasting sharply with human performance.

entry.title: From Weak Data to Strong Policy: Q-Targets Enable Provable In-Context Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yichen Lin, Xuyuan Xiong, Xue Wang, Xiangfu Meng, Mike Mingcheng Wei, Tao Yao

entry.summary: QTPT replaces behavior-cloning objectives in in-context reinforcement learning pretraining with a Bellman-style Q-target objective, so the Transformer learns to estimate action values from context rather than imitate potentially suboptimal offline actions. The authors provide theoretical guarantees in stochastic linear bandits and finite-horizon MDPs. This addresses a core weakness of imitation-based in-context RL: dependence on the quality of offline trajectories.

entry.title: To Solve Bilevel Optimization with Nonconvex Lower Levels, We Need Second-Order Stationarity

author.name: Zhiyao Zhang, Menglu Yu, Alvaro Velasquez, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Jia Liu

entry.summary: This theoretical work tackles bilevel optimization when the lower-level problem is nonconvex, moving beyond the standard strongly convex or convex lower-level assumptions that dominate the literature. The authors show that second-order stationarity is necessary for solving the general nonconvex lower-level setting, which remains an early-stage research area. This is relevant to nested ML problems like hyperparameter optimization and meta-learning where convexity fails.

entry.title: NEMSim: Learning Control-Conditioned Multi-Event Physical Dynamics via Executable Event-Mechanism Priors

author.name: Junsong Yu, Junjie Xie, Pengwei Liu, Dong Ni

entry.summary: NEMSim is a hybrid framework for simulating control-conditioned multi-event physical systems, where macroscopic evolution emerges from localized discrete events whose intensities depend on process controls and local states. It injects event-attribute descriptions as executable event-mechanism priors, addressing the generalization limits of purely data-driven surrogates under limited trajectory coverage while avoiding the cost of differentiable solvers. This targets long-trajectory, broad-control-space simulation tasks.

entry.title: Towards Understanding Momentum Acceleration in River-Valley Loss Landscape

author.name: Miao Lu, Zeyu Bian, Kaiyue Wen, Beining Wu, Siyu Chen, Tianhao Wang, Zhiyuan Li

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes momentum-based optimization in river-valley loss landscapes, where progress is dominated by movement along a low-loss manifold: large learning rates speed river progress despite vertical oscillations, and subsequent learning-rate decay suppresses these oscillations to reveal gains. It offers an explanation relevant to LLM pretraining dynamics.

entry.title: NEXT: Physics-Informed Neuro-Spectral Exponential Time Differencing Architectures

author.name: M\'arcio Marques, Leonardo Mendon\c{c}a, Leonardo M. Moreira, Christian J\'unior de Oliveira, Vitor Balestro, Tiago Novello, Daniel Yukimura, Pavel Petrov, Lucas Nissenbaum

entry.summary: NEXT combines Neuro-Spectral Architectures with high-order exponential time differencing integrators to fix the instability of NeuSA on stiff PDEs while retaining spectral representations and mitigating PINN spectral bias and causality failures. This targets forward and inverse problems for stiff time-dependent PDEs.

entry.title: MARCEDES: Score-based causal discovery under non-Gaussianity with continuous optimization

author.name: Anamitra Chaudhuri, Anirban Bhattacharya, Yang Ni

entry.summary: The paper introduces a mean absolute residual risk score for learning causal DAGs in structural equation models with non-Gaussian (e.g., Laplace) errors, proving the true weighted causal DAG matrix asymptotically minimizes this risk. Combining the score with row-specific sparsity penalties and a soft DAG constraint yields a fully continuous optimization approach to causal discovery suitable for high-dimensional settings.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Study of Content Representations for Speech Synthesis

author.name: Diego Torres, Axel Roebel, Nicolas Obin

entry.summary: Trains a generative model conditioned solely on each of many speech content representations (SSL features, supervised tokens, posteriorgrams, neural codecs) and evaluates generated audio along content, speaker identity, and prosody axes. It identifies two regimes: near-reconstruction representations and representations that disentangle speaker identity, showing disentanglement depends on the representation class rather than supervision alone.

entry.title: LiTe-GS: Oracle-Efficient Next Best View Selection for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Vivek Pandey, Amirhossein Mollaei Khass, Nader Motee

entry.summary: LiTe-GS addresses next-best-view selection for 3D Gaussian Splatting by replacing exhaustive scoring of candidate views with randomized subset evaluation, reducing expensive information-gain oracle calls. The method achieves expected O(M log(1/epsilon)) oracle complexity in the number of candidates while maintaining adaptive refinement quality. This makes information-driven view selection practical at scale for 3DGS training.

entry.title: PhoenixSR: Generative Heterogeneous Distillation Unleashes Efficient Models for Real-World Super-Resolution

author.name: Xin Di, Mingyu Shi, Yuanfei Bao, Long Peng, Yue Zhao, Jiaming Guo, Renjing Pei, Xueyang Fu, Yang Cao, Zheng-Jun Zha

entry.summary: Presents a heterogeneous distillation framework that transfers diffusion generative priors into existing feed-forward CNN/Transformer super-resolution networks so the diffusion model is not needed at inference time. This combines the realism of diffusion-based SR with the efficiency of diffusion-free models for real-world super-resolution. Answers a practical question about making high-quality restoration deployable.

entry.title: Adapting Personalized Speech Enhancement for Low-Latency Audio-Visual Target-Speaker Extraction

author.name: Rayhan Rashed, Senja Filipi, Ross Cutler

entry.summary: AV-PVQE builds a low-latency audio-visual target-speaker extraction system by adding mouth features to a personalized speech enhancement model's conditioning, cutting target confusion in two-speaker mixtures from 46 percent to 1.6 percent. It emphasizes listening quality and realistic meeting behavior rather than only synthetic-mixture separation metrics.

entry.title: ChronoFuseGS: Multi-Temporal Gaussian Fusion with Per-Splat Persistence and Change Visualization

author.name: Tobias Batik, Diana Marin, Peter K\'an, Hannes Kaufmann

entry.summary: ChronoFuseGS merges multiple separately trained Gaussian Splatting models from different timesteps into one model, letting Gaussians contribute across times to refine persistent scene parts while visualizing change. It supports incremental extension as new timesteps arrive.

entry.title: Policy-Calibrated DAgger: Offline Calibrated Noise Injection for Imitation Learning

author.name: Jenny Wang, George Kantor

entry.summary: Policy-Calibrated DAgger mitigates covariate shift in imitation learning by estimating where a generative policy is likely to fail offline, using the policy's own predicted action distribution. The method measures a diffusion policy's spread of predicted actions along expert trajectories and correlates this spread with closed-loop failure to calibrate noise injection for collecting targeted expert demonstrations. This avoids unsafe failure-driven data collection and manual noise-distribution selection.

entry.title: HIRE: History-Conditioned Interaction Reasoning and High-Rate Execution for Visually Aliased Precision Manipulation

author.name: Rongji Li, Wenhao He, Cewu Lu, Xingyu Chen, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: HIRE tackles precision manipulation where visually similar observations imply different latent contact states, combining history-conditioned interaction reasoning for long-horizon temporal disambiguation with high-rate reactive execution for contact response. Existing methods keep memory-based reasoning and high-rate control decoupled, which HIRE bridges. This addresses a genuine failure mode in contact-rich manipulation policies.

entry.title: Learning Robot Policies from Sparse Success Signals via STL-Guided Stein Variational Policy Gradient

author.name: Hongrui Zheng, Cristian Ioan Vasile, Antonio Loquercio, Rahul Mangharam

entry.summary: STL-SVPG is a population-based RL method for tasks with sparse success signals that uses smooth signal temporal logic robustness as a trajectory-level objective, differentiating through the dynamics to credit actions by their effect on full task specification satisfaction. Stein variational policy gradients maintain a diverse policy population. This offers a principled alternative to hand-crafted reward shaping for coordinated, contact-rich, multi-condition tasks.

entry.title: T-RoPE: Time-Aware Rotary Position Embedding for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Yang Liu, Noel Loo, Ali Khanafer, Shuying Sun, Akshay Soni, Zhong Wu, Linjun Yang

entry.summary: Proposes T-RoPE, a time-aware variant of rotary position embeddings for sequential generative recommendation that replaces index-only rotations with timestamp-based angles, learnable temporal coefficients, multiscale frequency banks, and non-stationary key rotations. It captures elapsed time, behavioral cycles, and calendar effects that plain RoPE ignores in recommender systems.

entry.title: EXAONE Demand 1.0: A Time Series Foundation Model for Demand Forecasting

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Sangjun Han, Jun Seo, Junhyeok Kang, Jaehoon Lee, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Minjae Kim, Sungdong Yoo, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: Presents EXAONE Demand, a time series foundation model specialized for demand forecasting, built on a demand-specific corpus of 11.3M series and 48.4B observations from 73 sources plus synthetic data for under-represented behaviors like censoring and short histories. Its demand-aware adapter attaches low-rank branches to a frozen general-domain backbone, one per demand class (smooth, intermittent, erratic, lumpy). Addresses gaps general TSFMs leave in retail and supply-chain forecasting.

entry.title: Neuralyzing the Trace: Selective Representation-Level Unlearning with Contrastive Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Itai Zehavi, Fanny Jourdan, Ulrich Aivodji

entry.summary: SCALPEL is a contrastive sparse autoencoder method for machine unlearning that intervenes directly on internal representations rather than relying on behavioral forgetting, motivated by GDPR-style narrow deletion requests. The paper identifies an energy bias in reconstruction-based feature extraction that favors dominant background structure over low-energy target-specific components, and shows theoretically that contrastive objectives improve selectivity. This advances mechanistically grounded unlearning beyond output-level suppression.

entry.title: Cartograph: Federated Tool Discovery with Operator-Attested Retrieval for AI Agents

author.name: Justice Owusu Agyemang, Michael Agyare, Kwame Opuni-Boachie Obour Agyekum, Kwame Agyeman-Prempeh Agyekum, Francisca Adoma Acheampong, Jerry John Kponyo

entry.summary: Cartograph is a federated MCP proxy that reduces agent-visible tool discovery from O(n) catalog traversal to O(k) progressive disclosure, combining Ed25519-signed operator-attested capability cards, a three-layer confusable-cluster analysis called Rift to detect misleading tool descriptions, and two-stage server-before-tool retrieval. Evaluation on a 22-server, 374-tool deployment demonstrates the design. The work addresses both scalability and security (tool-confusion attacks) in the Model Context Protocol ecosystem.

entry.title: DepthEvidence: Unifying Metric Depth Prediction and Geometric Reasoning in Multimodal Language Models

author.name: Jiangning Wei, Yuan Yao, Miaomiao Cui, Mingsheng Li, Humen Zhong, Shuai Bai, Zhibo Yang

entry.summary: DepthEvidence is a 4B multimodal language model that uses its own dense metric depth predictions as object-grounded evidence for language generation, via a camera-conditioned depth decoder and a dense-to-language interface producing geometry tokens anchored to object identifiers. Geometric supervision keeps metric information recoverable through language-context interaction, enabling measurement-grounded spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Agentic Limit Order Books: Phase Transitions and Market Impact

author.name: Jan Rosenzweig

entry.summary: This paper models limit order books populated exclusively by autonomous reinforcement-learning trading agents, showing phase boundaries between orderly price discovery and hyper-volatile cascade states governed by thresholds in agent count and observable depth. It also demonstrates that market impact under agentic liquidity provision deviates from classical square-root dynamics.

entry.title: Parameters vs. Context: TRACE Fine-Tuning for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Zhengchen Huang, Yundong Sun, Minrui Song, Shuanglong Yao, Ye Liu, Ji Chen, Xing Wang

entry.summary: TRACE is a fine-tuning framework that improves RAG robustness when retrieved context conflicts with the model's parametric knowledge, using multi-agent debate traces to extract correct, incorrect, and answer-shift patterns as fine-grained supervision, plus an answer-completeness regularizer. This addresses unreliable behavior (blindly following misleading context or wrongly trusting internal knowledge) in deployed RAG systems. It matters because knowledge conflicts are a central failure mode of retrieval-augmented LLMs.

entry.title: QSV: Quat-Sphere-Vision for Coupled Quaternion Attention on Spherical Lattices

author.name: Nicholas Foley, Devin Marinelli, Donny Moore, Diego Enriquez, Amanda Fernandez

entry.summary: Quat-Sphere-Vision (QSV) replaces the standard three-projection attention triple with a single learned unit quaternion per token, where the relative quaternion supplies both the attention logit and a sandwich-product feature transport, with messages passed over sparse kNN graphs on concentric Fibonacci spheres. Ablations that modify only one component reveal that the attention and transport roles are asymmetric. This is a compact, geometry-aware reformulation of attention for spherical data.

entry.title: Learning Chance-Constrained MDPs with Bellman Distributional Certificates

author.name: Chenbei Lu, Hongyu Yi

entry.summary: The paper shows that chance-constrained MDPs, though computationally hard due to nonconvex trajectory-level constraints, do not necessarily carry a higher statistical sample cost than expectation-based safe RL: for tabular discounted CCMDPs with bounded successor support, it establishes a model-based upper bound matching a lower bound up to logarithmic terms, using Bellman distributional certificates with a certified planning oracle.

entry.title: LUCID: Learning Under Confounding for Inference and Discovery in Time Series

author.name: Mohammad Fesanghary

entry.summary: LUCID is a regime-adaptive deconfounding layer for causal discovery in time series that detects confounding regimes via a Marchenko-Pastur spectral router and applies matched deconfounding strategies. It recovers contemporaneous structure under factor confounding and is algorithm-agnostic, plugging into existing discovery methods.

entry.title: Input-Layer Starvation: Why Per-Layer Pruning Breaks IoT Intrusion Detectors

author.name: Md Anas Biswas

entry.summary: Shows that uniform layer-wise magnitude pruning at 80% sparsity catastrophically damages per-class performance in a small IoT intrusion detector, losing half of macro-F1, because a tiny 192-weight first layer becomes starved of remaining inputs. The paper diagnoses the mechanism and offers low-overhead prevention and repair strategies.

entry.title: Unknown-Traffic Detection, Calibration and Shortcut Reliance in Distilled Encrypted-Traffic Classifiers over One Year

author.name: Mahmoud Abbasi

entry.summary: A pre-registered study distilling one 101k-parameter student from two equally accurate but differently constructed teachers (ensemble vs single wider model), testing ten hypotheses across 18 test sets on a full year of real TLS traffic (CESNET-TLS-Year22). It examines what students inherit beyond accuracy: unknown-traffic detection, calibration, shortcut reliance, and robustness to a year of drift.

entry.title: Evaluating Sycophancy in Chinese Large Language Models on Factual Questions Derived from Online Search Queries

author.name: Geng Liu, Feng Li, Mengxiao Zhu, Francesco Pierri

entry.summary: This paper analyzes factual sycophancy in Chinese LLMs using questions derived from real online search queries, disentangling whether user beliefs corrupt correct answers versus convert uncertainty into belief-aligned incorrectness. It also examines whether anti-sycophancy interventions restore accuracy or merely shift responses toward uncertainty. Sycophancy in information-mediating models has significant misinformation implications.

entry.title: Reliability-Regulated Trajectory Optimization for Progressive COLMAP-Free 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zijian Wu, Jinliang Wang, Zidian Lin, Ying Song, Ziqian Lu, Hanjie Ma, Zhen Ye, Mingfeng Jiang

entry.summary: The paper targets error compounding in COLMAP-free 3D Gaussian Splatting, where early pairwise camera-tracking errors corrupt subsequent frame initializations and become permanently frozen in the scene. It proposes a unified reliability-regulated trajectory optimization framework built on a self-supervised bidirectional cycle-consistency mechanism, avoiding heavyweight external neural priors or isolated heuristic fixes. The framework systematically regulates progressive camera trajectories during reconstruction.

entry.title: CytoSPM: Open-Vocabulary Cytopathology Detection with Structured Prompt Bank

author.name: Wenjie Li, Zishan Xu, Jinyang Huang, Zhengxin Nie, Shichao Kan, Yixiong Liang

entry.summary: Presents PentaCyto, a multi-domain open-vocabulary cytopathology detection benchmark spanning cervical, urinary, respiratory, serous fluid, and thyroid cytology with 24 base and 9 held-out novel categories, plus CytoSPM, an efficient detector using structured cytomorphology prompt banks that provide clinically grounded textual knowledge. Fills the absence of a unified open-vocabulary cytology evaluation and method. Notable for grounding prompts in diagnostic morphology.

entry.title: VkVIO: Cross-platform GPU Acceleration for Visual-Inertial Odometry with Vulkan

author.name: Ole Hoffmann, Mateo de Mayo, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: VkVIO accelerates visual-inertial odometry using the vendor-agnostic Vulkan API instead of CUDA, enabling GPU-accelerated state estimation across embedded computers, phones, and XR headsets from any vendor. This widens deployment options for efficient robotics and XR perception.

entry.title: Aerial Manipulation in the Wild with Onboard Perception, Policy Learning, and Whole-Body Control

author.name: Yuanzhu Zhan, Yufei Jiang, Zemu Zhang, Junyi Geng

entry.summary: This paper presents an outdoor aerial manipulation framework combining imitation-learned Diffusion Policy for end-effector motion generation, onboard LiDAR-inertial state estimation, and whole-body model predictive control coordinating the aerial platform and manipulator. The system removes reliance on external motion-capture infrastructure, enabling real-world aerial manipulation under disturbance in unstructured environments.

entry.title: Praxis: Distilling Physical Interaction Priors from Egocentric Videos for Generalizable Whole-Body Manipulation

author.name: Shuliang He, Ruiyan Xu, Bo Yue, Hengming Zhang, Huayi Zhou, Shuai Wang, Wei-Shi Zheng, Guiliang Liu

entry.summary: Praxis is a whole-body manipulation framework for mobile humanoids that distills physical interaction priors from one-shot egocentric video demonstrations, coordinating vision-language-guided navigation, closed-loop posture calibration, and synchronized upper/lower-body dexterous manipulation with online visual feedback. It targets generalization under changing object poses and contact conditions from minimal task-specific data. It contributes to the growing area of humanoid manipulation from human video priors.

entry.title: PHASE: Compliance-Enabled Tactile Phase Retrieval for Few-Shot Insertion Learning

author.name: Jeremy Siburian, Cristian C. Beltran-Hernandez, Tatsuya Matsushima, Yusuke Iwasawa, Masashi Hamaya, Mai Nishimura

entry.summary: PHASE leverages a compliant wrist to sustain contact during peg-in-hole insertion, using the resulting tactile and force signals to reveal task phase structure for retrieval-augmented imitation learning with only few demonstrations. It addresses the open question of what phase-specific experience to retrieve from prior data in contact-rich assembly. The insight that compliance itself generates the retrieval signal is clever.

entry.title: LAVOIR: Teaching a Single-Pass Decision Encoder When and What to Ask with Amortized Value of Information

author.name: Furkan Yilmaz, Habibe Aleyna Tasdemir, Muhammed Faruk Gozay

entry.summary: LAVOIR extends single-pass decision models by placing candidate missing-information slots next to answer options so one forward pass yields both the decision distribution and the expected value-of-information gain for asking about each slot. VOI targets require no human labels, using schema rules for gold decisions and an LLM only for verbalization.

entry.title: ORCA: Evaluating LLMs on Data Science Code Translation

author.name: Xiaolong Li, Jinyang Li, Bowen Qin, Ge Qu, Nan Huo, Xiaohan Xu, Shipei Lin, Reynold Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces ORCA, a benchmark for Data Science Code Translation (DSCT), covering 1,600 curated tasks across data querying, manipulation, and deep learning, plus 200 whole-project translation tasks across seven data science domains. It fills a gap since LLM code translation between libraries (e.g., pandas to SQL or PyTorch) is far less studied than code generation. Useful for measuring whether models preserve functional equivalence across ecosystems.

entry.title: Externalized CPDAG Summaries Improve LLM Causal Deduction

author.name: Wentao Sun, Jo\~ao Paulo Nogueira, Dominique Verchere, Mathieu Acher, Alonso Silva

entry.summary: The authors frame the Corr2Cause causal-inference task as latent-object reasoning and propose Structured Thinking, a two-turn pipeline in which an LLM first externalizes a schema-constrained CPDAG summary and then answers against that graph state. This raises Qwen3.5-27B from 73.0 to 86.4 F1 on the full test with strong statistical controls. It demonstrates that scaffolding causal reasoning with typed external graph representations outperforms free-form chain-of-thought.

entry.title: Evolutionary Safety of Recursive Self-Improving AI: Taxonomy, Risk Discovery, and Evaluation

author.name: Chang Gong, Jingping Bi, Di Yao, Xinjian Liang, Chao Xiang, Ruijie Guo

entry.summary: This paper introduces Evolutionary Safety as a perspective on maintaining safety under recursive self-improvement, where the system, its accumulated experience, and the process producing successors all continue to change. It provides a taxonomy, risk discovery, and evaluation framework covering model training, experience accumulation, agent evolution, and automated AI development. As RSI becomes increasingly relevant, this kind of structured risk analysis is a timely safety contribution.

entry.title: Prompt Minimization: Reducing Input Redundancy Without Sacrificing Output Fidelity

author.name: Marius F. R. Juston, Kevin A. Karim, Jonathan Gao, Kevin C. Li, Rudhi Bashambu

entry.summary: This paper formalizes prompt minimization: reducing prompts to their smallest, most information-dense form while preserving output fidelity. Shorter prompts reduce latency and compute, and the authors note that longer prompts can degrade reasoning and accuracy. The work also raises theoretical questions about redundancy in the input space and which information is essential to elicit specific outputs.

entry.title: SlideLab: Audience-Centered Scientific Slide Generation and Evaluation

author.name: Vidushee Vats, Karun Sharma, Yuxia Wang

entry.summary: SlideLab is a training-free multi-agent framework that generates scientific presentations from research papers via narrative planning, content planning, visual generation, layout refinement, and grounding verification agents, with an audience-centered evaluation approach. In blind human preference studies it was preferred over open-source and commercial systems on 77 percent of papers while using roughly 4 times fewer inference tokens than the strongest open-source baseline. It also introduces evaluation methodology for slide quality.

entry.title: DanLing NestedTensor: Composable Multi-Ragged Tensors for Deep Learning

author.name: Zhiyuan Chen

entry.summary: DanLing NestedTensor is a PyTorch tensor abstraction that makes multi-ragged (variable-size along multiple axes) structure a native property of tensors, eliminating padding waste in dense batching. The representation carries logical axes and sample boundaries through broadcasting, transformations, and reductions, enabling composable packed operations.

entry.title: Auditing Latent-Space Monitors for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Nikhil Kamalkumar Advani, Vishwajeet Shivaji Hogale, Saurav Kumar

entry.summary: The authors audit runtime failure monitors that use a model's internal representations to predict failures in autonomous driving, testing on LaneSegNet for map generation and VAD for end-to-end planning. They show frame-level errors are predictable at inference (AUROC 0.780 and 0.868), but also that strong failure prediction does not require internal access. This is valuable for safety-critical deployment of driving models.

entry.title: Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4

author.name: Amanda Fitch

entry.summary: This paper evaluates how Google's Gemma 4-e4b (an established open model, GA April 2026) prioritizes conflicting input documents, isolating the effects of source framing versus presentation order through a counterbalanced behavioral suite of 13 items and 784 forward passes. It finds that source framing strongly dominates reading position in resolving conflicts. The work contributes to understanding model susceptibility to contextual manipulation and prompt-injection-like behaviors.

entry.title: Spackle: Completing Large View Single Image NVS with Adaptive Gaussians

author.name: Xuanzhi Liu, Yuhe Zhou, Xinyi Wu, Zhenyao Wu, Jinghao Chen, Ruize Han, Song Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses single-image novel view synthesis (NVS) for large view deviations, where reconstructing occluded regions must be balanced with preserving fidelity of visible content. The authors identify a capacity competition problem in hybrid 3D Gaussian Splatting plus diffusion frameworks, where a fixed Gaussian budget forces resources away from visible areas toward newly disoccluded regions, and propose Spackle, a lightweight residual learning framework with adaptive Gaussians to mitigate this without sacrificing scene fidelity.

entry.title: UniAR: A Unified Framework for Autism Recognition Enhanced by Multi-View Prompt Learning

author.name: Lei Xin, Zeheng Wang, Jiayin Zhu, Shihong Huang, Fanhu Zeng, Changjiang Jiang, Dengbo He, Yutao Yue, Zhenglun Kong

entry.summary: UniAR addresses the scarcity of diagnostic text data in autism spectrum disorder recognition by using a large multimodal model to generate hierarchical diagnostic descriptions at word, phrase, and sentence levels. Multi-granularity prompt learning enables robust ASD recognition across heterogeneous data variations, supporting earlier and more accurate diagnosis.

entry.title: Why Clipping Matters in AdaGrad? Toward a High-Probability Theory under Generalized Smoothness

author.name: Alokendu Mazumder, Ayaan Mohd, Harshit Rawat, Arnab Roy, Mayank Baranwal, Punit Rathore

entry.summary: The authors prove that unclipped coordinate-wise AdaGrad under heavy-tailed noise and generalized smoothness becomes anisotropically miscalibrated, learning the geometry of rare noise shocks instead of objective curvature, and that gradient clipping repairs this failure. They provide a finite-horizon high-probability convergence guarantee for clipped AdaGrad. This gives the first rigorous explanation of why gradient clipping is essential in common adaptive optimization regimes.

entry.title: Geometric Feature Learning for Functional Data Valued on the Symmetric Positive Definite Manifold

author.name: Samuel V. Singh, Mimi Zhang

entry.summary: MatFAE is a functional neural network for learning trajectories on the Riemannian manifold of symmetric positive definite matrices, using intrinsic layers that map manifold-valued functions into Euclidean space. By treating sequences as continuous functions, it encodes trajectory dynamics such as first-order derivatives, and its functional-layer weights offer interpretability of which input regions matter. This addresses a gap in geometric deep learning for SPD-valued functional data.

entry.title: PixSim: a calibrated open-source simulator of instant-payment fraud, recovery and interdiction under analyst capacity constraints

author.name: Bashir Zeimarani, Alireza Khatib, Somayeh Mousavinasr, Carlos Maur\'icio Serodio Figueiredo

entry.summary: PixSim is an open-source simulator of Brazil's Pix instant-payment rail that jointly models irreversible settlement, the regulated recovery mechanism, downstream fund dispersal, and capacity-constrained analyst review, calibrated to Banco Central do Brasil open data. It supports evaluating interdiction policies that must route transactions to pass, human review, or block before settlement under a regulatory hold window. No prior public simulator jointly covers these elements for instant-payment fraud.

entry.title: Interpretable-by-Design Descriptor Portfolios Match a 2048-Dimensional Foundation Embedding on Low-Data Molecular Assays

author.name: Yiqi Yao, Miquel Duran-Frigola

entry.summary: This paper shows that a greedy portfolio of compact, semantically named molecular descriptor blocks can match a 2048-dimensional CheMeleon foundation embedding across nine ADME/Tox assays in low-data structure-activity prediction, while keeping every feature auditable with model name and training provenance. It matters because it challenges the assumption that large opaque foundation embeddings are necessary for small-sample drug discovery tasks.

entry.title: WorldTS: World Modeling for Multimodal Covariate-aware Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yuhan Zhu, Xiangfei Qiu, Hanyin Cheng, Wangmeng Shen, Chenjuan Guo, Bin Yang, Jilin Hu, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: WorldTS frames time series forecasting through latent world modeling, predicting future observations from latent dynamics rather than direct observation-space mapping. It uniquely incorporates multimodal external covariates into latent-state formation for improved forecasting.

entry.title: Weight Pair Encoding: Inducing a Smaller Grammar in Neural Network Weights

author.name: Irene Tallini, Daniele Solombrino, Alberto Cazzaniga, Emanuele Rodol\`a

entry.summary: Weight Pair Encoding (WeightPE) fine-tunes network weights so they become more compressible, by embedding a lossy Re-Pair grammar compressor inside a straight-through estimator during training. On ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/16 fine-tuned on CIFAR-10, the resulting grammars are roughly 0.4x the size of those from standard Re-Pair compression, exploiting hierarchical, variable-length weight patterns rather than a fixed codebook.

entry.title: An End-to-End Pipeline for Causal ML with Continuous Treatments: An Application to Financial Decision Making

author.name: Javier Moral Hern\'andez, Clara Higuera-Caba\~nes, \'Alvaro Ibra\'in

entry.summary: The authors present a six-step end-to-end causal machine learning pipeline for continuous-treatment settings, covering dimensionality reduction, causal identification, positivity violation handling, estimation, refutation, and policy optimization, demonstrated on financial decision making. Practical contributions include a method for detecting and quantifying positivity violations, a scalable two-stage dimensionality reduction framework, and adapted sensitivity analysis methods.

entry.title: On the Limits of Univariate Deep Learning for Significant Wave Height Forecasting

author.name: Yilin Zhai, Hongyuan Shi, Zaijin You

entry.summary: A systematic hyperparameter search across five deep learning architectures (DLinear, LSTM, PatchTST, ResAttLstm, Mamba2) and nine context lengths for single-station significant wave height forecasting, re-evaluated on a 47-buoy, 37-year corpus. All architecture families converge to nearly identical performance, and cross-dataset shifts dwarf architectural differences, suggesting a ceiling on univariate deep learning for this task.

entry.title: Beyond Empirical Support: Structured Outlier Generation via Sinkhorn Optimal Transport

author.name: Haixiang Sun, Andrew L. Liu

entry.summary: The authors propose SBOG, a structured framework for latent-space outlier generation that couples Sinkhorn optimal transport with boundary-based synthesis to create stress-test scenarios for robustness evaluation. It aims to replace heuristic outlier synthesis methods tied to sparse neighborhoods or classifier boundaries. This matters for safety-critical evaluation where rare cases are underrepresented in training data.

entry.title: A Benchmark Framework for Screening Automation in Systematic Reviews

author.name: Gauransh Kumar, Luciano Marchezan, Guillaume Genois, K\'evin Delcourt, Eugene Syriani

entry.summary: This work releases a benchmark of 45,064 labeled entries across 32 curated secondary studies for evaluating LLM performance in systematic-review screening, with an evaluation framework that accounts for the severe class imbalance natural to screening datasets. It also introduces prompt-based evaluation components. This enables more honest assessment of LLM-assisted evidence synthesis.

entry.title: SEA-CLIP-Tiny: Efficient Multilingual Text-Vision Embedding for Southeast Asian Languages

author.name: Puja Ahmad Habibi, Faiz Assabil Firdaus, Ashvanth S, Ekapol Chuangsuwanich, Pume Tuchinda, Peerat Limkonchotiwat

entry.summary: SEA-CLIP-Tiny is a compact multilingual text-vision embedding model under 50M parameters for Southeast Asian languages, adapting a CLIP-KD-style framework with regional data curation and multilingual teacher guidance. Across seven Southeast Asian languages it achieves the strongest average retrieval performance among evaluated student models. This improves access to multimodal retrieval for a linguistically underserved region.

entry.title: Learning Natural Conversational Behavior in Tandem Speech-to-Speech Models with Randomized Guidance

author.name: Manato Yaguchi, Yotaro Kubo, Hikaru Asano, So Kuroki

entry.summary: The paper addresses training tandem speech-to-speech architectures, where an LLM backend supplies candidate responses as guidance to a speech frontend while the user is still speaking. Because real conversation recordings contain only final responses, not the intermediate guidance, the authors propose randomized intermediate guidance derived directly from the conversation corpus instead of expensive simulator-LLM data generation. This reduces data-preparation overhead while teaching the frontend natural conversational behavior, relevant to latency-sensitive full-duplex voice assistants.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Auditing of Identification Assumptions in Climate-Policy Causal Evaluations

author.name: Yonghong Zhang, Yong Xie, Isabel M. Parra, Ricardo Correia

entry.summary: ARGUS is a structured LLM pipeline that audits difference-in-differences climate-policy studies by checking reported evidence against an eleven-dimension assumption-implication-evidence rubric, abstaining when evidence cannot be retrieved. It detects 73% of planted flaws on an 11-flaw benchmark versus 18% for a keyword baseline, while abstaining on roughly 40% of paper-dimension assessments. This demonstrates calibrated abstention in evidence-grounded auditing of causal claims.

entry.title: FAVoR: Measuring and Mitigating Author-Style Homogenization in Federated Personalized Generation

author.name: Lu Han, Jingyao Zhang, Katy Ilonka Gero, Nguyen H. Tran

entry.summary: FAVoR studies a newly defined failure mode in federated PEFT for personalized writing assistants, where standard aggregation preserves task utility while making different authors' styles indistinguishable. The authors introduce ASCE-based diagnostics to measure author-style retention and mitigation methods on a BlogText benchmark. This connects federated learning, personalization, and style preservation in LLMs.

entry.title: Cross-Backend QIEO: Universal Runtime Portability across OpenMP5, CUDA, HIP, and Multi-Language Interfaces

author.name: Aman Mittal, Ferdin Sagai Don Bosco, Kasturi Venkata Srikanth, Abhishek Singh, Aditya Singh, Abhishek Chopra

entry.summary: This paper presents QIEO, a unified runtime framework for quantum-inspired evolutionary optimizers that delivers hardware portability across OpenMP5, CUDA, HIP, and multi-language interfaces. It targets the adoption barrier for quantum-inspired algorithms that emulate superposition, interference, and rotation-gate dynamics on classical hardware, where reported speedups of 10-80x over traditional solvers exist but lack a portable execution story. The contribution is systems-level rather than algorithmic, standardizing deployment for combinatorial NP-hard optimization.

entry.title: PICO: Projection-Informed Consistency Optimisation for 6DoF Surgical Tool Pose Estimation

author.name: Lucy Fothergill, Pietro Valdastri, Dominic Jones, Duygu Sarikaya

entry.summary: Proposes PICO, an end-to-end multi-task model for 6DoF surgical tool pose estimation that predicts segmentation and depth maps alongside translation and rotation regression, using projection-informed consistency to avoid the error accumulation of kinematics-based and two-stage vision approaches. Aimed at safe robotic surgery automation and proprioception without external markers. Includes clinical-motivated design considerations.

entry.title: ContraFM-S2O: Flow Matching-Based One-step SAR-to-Optical Image Translation Model with Contrastive Learning

author.name: Mingqian Yu, Wei-kuan Chiang, Qiurui Wang, Peilin Zhao

entry.summary: ContraFM-S2O applies flow matching with contrastive learning to one-step SAR-to-optical image translation, addressing the latency and detail-fidelity shortcomings of diffusion and GAN approaches. It predicts velocity fields and solves an ODE at inference for efficient sampling.

entry.title: Enhancing Photogrammetric Digital Surface Models with Pretrained Diffusion Models and Multimodal Conditioning

author.name: Antoine Lorentz, St\'ephane May, Valentine Bellet, Dawa Derksen, Bastien Nespoulous

entry.summary: A modified Stable Diffusion 3 architecture with a pruned text stream and patch-wise normalization refines noisy satellite-photogrammetry digital surface models toward LiDAR-quality elevation, conditioned on both DSMs and Pléiades imagery. Experiments in French cities show multimodal conditioning improves refinement.

entry.title: POIL: Point-based One-Shot Imitation Learning with Stable Dynamical Systems

author.name: Sang Min Kim, Jinwoo Seo, Hyeongjun Heo, Junho Lee, Yonghyeon Lee, Young Min Kim

entry.summary: POIL is a one-shot imitation learning framework that uses a shared representation of 3D points on an object's functional part for both trajectory transfer and closed-loop execution under stable dynamical systems. Point correspondences enable transfer of demonstrated trajectories to novel objects, and the functional-part representation is grounded with a multimodal large language model. The approach targets robust execution under changing scenes, grasp configurations, and disturbances.

entry.title: Learning Vision-Based Agile Gap Traversal: Differentiable Simulation with a Warm-Started Critic

author.name: Nuthasith Gerdpratoom, Tianchen Sun, Yichao Gao, Lin Zhao

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage RL framework for quadrotor gap traversal that uses quasi-analytical policy gradients via differentiable simulation while avoiding backpropagation through visual rendering, plus critic warm-starting. The approach reduces computation and memory costs while improving sample efficiency compared with behavior cloning or full BPTT through the simulator. It contributes to efficient vision-based agile flight.

entry.title: Representation-Guided Generation and Integration of Executable Programs for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Ruixiao Yang, Mingxin Yu, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: RIVET generates complete robot manipulation systems from VLM code generation anchored to a shared object-centric representation combining 6D poses (metric grounding for actions) with a relation graph (task structure for planning), ensuring independently generated components remain compatible. This tackles a real failure mode of VLM code generation for robotics: incoherent interfaces between generated perception, planning, and control modules.

entry.title: Design-Ignoring versus Design-Respecting World Models for Epidemiology

author.name: Xiangyu Yu, Weiyu Liu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes how study design (assignment, sampling, measurement) should constrain world models for epidemiology, distinguishing design-respecting models that encode these constraints from design-ignoring models that fit records without relating them to the intended intervention question. Using a large-scale cluster-randomized test-negative trial, it shows design choices change learned intervention contrasts. This is an important caution for applying world models to observational health data.

entry.title: The Quest for Embedded Evaluators

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's LessWrong commentary on commitments by Dario Amodei and OpenAI to embedded evaluators who would receive employee-level access inside frontier labs to provide independent oversight. The post skeptically examines who could actually fill the evaluator role given conflicts of interest and funding sources, and connects the need for evaluators to the weekend's new wave of undisclosed AI hacking incidents, including one that reportedly forced OpenAI to pause its most advanced model.

entry.title: Pretrained ASR Pseudo-labeling for Noisy Police Audio

author.name: Kaavya Chaparala, Su Huang, Stephen L. Miller, Rhiannon N. Miller, Anjalie Field

entry.summary: Studies pseudo-labeling to adapt pretrained ASR models (Whisper, Qwen3-ASR) to noisy broadcast police communication using Baltimore and Chicago corpora, showing that standard confidence metrics fail to filter pseudo-label quality. The authors introduce an external LLM-as-a-judge filtering paradigm that improves unsupervised adaptation in this very noisy domain.

entry.title: ConsultMind:Towards Automated Diagnostic Consultation via Uncertainty-Aware Reasoning

author.name: Xiao Sun, Yuming Yang, Yun Chen, Jiang Zhong, Junnan Zhu, Xinyi Jiang, Haoyang Zeng, Ruirui Chen, Yining Wang, Xinyu Zhou, Rong Tang, Kaiwen Wei

entry.summary: Introduces an automated pipeline for diagnostic consultation that builds a Disorder-Symptom Bayesian Network from heterogeneous diagnosis-labeled clinical narratives, then uses uncertainty-aware reasoning to decide when to inquire and when to diagnose. It links diagnostic hypotheses to potential patient inquiries and translates evolving Bayesian posteriors into sequential consultation decisions. Aims for adaptive, interpretable clinical dialogue systems.

entry.title: LogicTree-RAG: Logic Tree-guided Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Long-form Patent Drafting

author.name: Jiaqi Zhu, Naili Xing, Hexiang Pan, Haotian Gao, Jianwei Yin, Xiaokui Xiao, Beng Chin Ooi

entry.summary: Proposes LogicTree-RAG for long-form technical generation, inducing a hierarchical logic tree as a global organizer for retrieval-augmented patent drafting, enabling multi-expert collaboration toward legally compliant, technically exhaustive documents. Moves beyond partial section generation and manually crafted outlines toward scalable automation of full patent documents. A strong instance of structured planning for knowledge-intensive generation.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Study of AI-Text Detection Neurons in Frozen BERT: Sparse Probing and Activation Patching on RAID

author.name: Pawe{\l} Blicharz, Mi{\l}osz Grunwald

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study identifies which neurons in a frozen BERT encoder support AI-generated text detection, using the RAID benchmark across six generators. Sparse probing of all 9,216 CLS hidden-state dimensions recovers a stable set of under 1 percent of neurons per generator that retains most full-feature detection accuracy, and bidirectional activation patching confirms causal involvement. The work illuminates the internal representations driving AI-text detectors.

entry.title: Breaking Homogeneity: Diversifying Persona Sets for Creative LLM Outputs

author.name: Sang Bin Moon, Nicole Cho, Daniel Borrajo, Sumitra Ganesh, Abolfazl Hashemi

entry.summary: The paper formulates persona diversification for creative LLM outputs as a set-level conditioning problem, exploring selecting versus generating personas and space-filling versus frontier-seeking diversity. Four methods are evaluated on creativity tasks (Alternative Uses Task, Infinity-Chat, Divergent Association Task), showing benefits in countering groupthink-like response homogeneity.

entry.title: Robust to Which Model Change? A Unified Evaluation of Robust Counterfactual Explanations

author.name: Marcin Kostrzewa, Maciej Zi\k{e}ba

entry.summary: This paper argues that reported robustness of counterfactual explanations cannot be compared because each method is evaluated against a different type of model change. It proposes a unified cross-family protocol holding factuals and counterfactuals fixed while testing six robust methods and two baselines against eight model-change types on four tabular datasets. It characterizes which method remains reliable under which change.

entry.title: JevAdvBench: A Benchmark and Black-Box Attacks for Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions Models

author.name: Jianyi Hu, Hangtao Zhang, Yi Liu, Yeqi Zeng, Li Zeng, Xianlong Wang, Rui Wang, Leo Yu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces JevAdvBench, the first adversarial robustness benchmark for models trained via reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions (RLCD), which return typed answers consumed by software without human review. Since such models generate nothing to score, the key idea is scoring each attacked decision against the model's own clean decision, enabling black-box attack evaluation under nondeterministic and preprocessed API behavior.

entry.title: Softmax Reparameterization for Output-Head Quantization

author.name: Asim Kadav, Christian Flores, Chirag Arora, Varun Kotte, Hongbo Zheng, Lan Yan, Priya Shanmugasundaram, Tracy Holloway King

entry.summary: The paper proposes a post-training method that selects a functionally equivalent output head before quantization by subtracting a scalar multiple of the vocabulary-row mean from every output row, with the coefficient chosen by validation KL per quantizer (RTN, activation-weighted MSE, GPTQ). A rank-one correction handles nonlinear logit paths like soft-capping, yielding W4 gains across seven heads at negligible cost.

entry.title: ClearGS: Reliability-Aware Gaussian Splatting from Handheld Videos

author.name: Xuanzhi Liu, Xinyi Wu, Hang Pan, Wensi Huang, Zhenyao Wu, Ruize Han, Song Wang

entry.summary: ClearGS improves 3D Gaussian Splatting from handheld videos with uneven viewpoint coverage and mixed quality by assigning graded reliability weights to frames instead of binary selection, plus a render-guided restoration module that uses the current 3DGS render to guide a frozen no-reference restoration expert. This jointly maintains trajectory coverage and recovers detail lost to blur or distortion.

entry.title: Staged Depth Training: A Representation Curriculum for PINNs

author.name: Kejia Zhang, Youran Sun, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Staged Depth Training (SDT) for physics-informed neural networks, which explicitly trains a shallow prefix with a temporary physics-informed head, then freezes it and progressively adds depth, decoupling representation learning from final solution fitting. Across 20 PINNacle forward problems and three backbones, SDT improves the majority of equal-budget comparisons. It matters because representation quality is a known bottleneck for PINNs.

entry.title: Stable initialization without the CLT

author.name: Simon Kuang, Kyle Chickering, Xinfan Lin

entry.summary: For deep networks with sine activations, the authors derive a uniform-phase initialization scheme that avoids the Central Limit Theorem-based distributional approximation used in conventional random network theory, fully decoupling layers. They claim this is the first use of the sine function's periodic symmetry for initialization, with models trained under the uniform-phase scheme showing stable behavior. This removes approximation error and inter-layer coupling from initialization theory for a specific activation family.

entry.title: Differentiable RNA Secondary Structure Extraction for Deep Learning

author.name: Tyler Illman, Max Ward, Marcell Szikszai, Ryan K. Krueger

entry.summary: This paper studies the neglected structure-extraction step in RNA secondary structure prediction, where a learned pairwise weight matrix must be converted into a predicted structure or base-pairing probability matrix, often via ad hoc algorithms. The authors compare four extraction algorithms, including a Nussinov-like dynamic programming method and maximum-weight approaches, and analyze how congruence between training and extraction methods affects prediction performance. The findings guide better-matched training and extraction pipelines.

entry.title: Block Sparse Attention with Log-Linear Complexity

author.name: Bohao Tang, Zhen Qin, Yuqi Pan, Zheng Li, Pengfei Liu

entry.summary: PISA is a block-sparse attention mechanism using a pyramid Top-K selection strategy that narrows candidates through a coarse-to-fine hierarchy of keys with LogSumExp scoring at bounded levels, reducing block selection from quadratic to log-linear complexity for long-context language models.

entry.title: Budgeted Quotient-Residual Guidance for Frozen Pocket-Conditioned Molecular Diffusion

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Jinbo Bi, Minghu Song

entry.summary: QRG is an inference-time guidance method that lets frozen pocket-conditioned molecular diffusion models optimize quotient objectives (distances, contacts, anchored substructures) without retraining. It lifts quotient covectors to ambient directions with a trust budget derived from the sampler's own step norm, with theoretical guarantees on KL/kinetic behavior and equivariance.

entry.title: HySTAR: Anchored Hypergraphs for Stable Credit Assignment in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xinglong Luo, Yuding Zhang, Yuheng Kuang, Shuxuan Yuan, Zhenni Zeng, Weiqiang Zhu, Zhenhai Ji, Zhengning Wang

entry.summary: HySTAR targets credit assignment in cooperative MARL by identifying structural target drift—the inconsistency of value decompositions as coalitions and active agents change. It anchors an overlapping sparse hypergraph as a stable decomposition scaffold within a MAPPO-style framework, separating adaptive representation learning from a temporally consistent value basis.

entry.title: Bayesian Uncertainty Quantification for fMRI Functional Connectivity via Simulation-Based Inference

author.name: Simon Carter, Zeming Kuang, Lilianne R. Mujica-Parodi, Helmut H. Strey

entry.summary: This work models fMRI BOLD dynamics as coupled Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes and uses Sequential Neural Posterior Estimation to obtain Bayesian posteriors over functional connectivity while accounting for measurement noise across the BOLD spectrum. Applied to healthy control cohorts, the framework quantifies uncertainty in connectivity estimates and helps disentangle scanner noise from true between-subject neural variability, informing scan duration and resolution choices.

entry.title: A Flatness-Generalization Relation in the Teacher-Student Tree-Committee Machine

author.name: Brandon Livio Annesi, Davide Straziota, Enrico Maria Malatesta

entry.summary: Studies the flatness-generalization relation in a teacher-student tree committee machine where both the ERM estimator and Hessian spectrum are analytically tractable in the proportional high-dimensional limit, using zero-temperature Gibbs predictions and Edwards-Jones formalism. Predictions match finite-size gradient-descent simulations, and three flatness measures are compared.

entry.title: Amplify What You Gaze At: Target Saliency Boosting in Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Shengqi Dang, Zhengxi Yu, Feilin Han, Xingyu Lan, Nan Cao

entry.summary: The paper introduces Target Saliency Boosting, a new task of increasing the visual saliency of a specified object during text-to-image generation without visual priors, based on the insight that saliency is inherently relative across the scene's global distribution. The proposed GazeME framework uses learnable marker tokens around object descriptions in saliency-marked prompts to control attention distribution. This adds a previously unexplored control axis to text-to-image generation.

entry.title: WeaveAgent: A Two-Stage Tool-Routing Agent for Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Zhongyu Pang

entry.summary: Presents WeaveAgent, a two-stage agent for ultra-high-resolution remote sensing that decouples tool routing from visual perception: Stage A trains reliable tool-call emission (rather than eliciting it zero-shot), and Stage B conditionally executes either visual answering via token-compressed thumbnails or tool calls on full-resolution imagery with observation-masked second-round answering. Trained with alignment SFT followed by GRPO-style RL. Tackles visual token cost and format reliability for agentic remote sensing.

entry.title: Universal Drift Correction for Multidimensional Scanning Microscopy

author.name: Sangjoon Lee, William Millsaps, Dasol Yoon, Caitlyn Obrero, Guoliang Hu, Corrie Barnes, Cedric Lim, Andrew Barnum, Arthur R. C. McCray, Colin Ophus

entry.summary: This work extends orthogonal-scan drift correction from 2D images to spectrum images and diffraction datasets in scanning microscopy, recovering true probe positions from multi-orientation scans or reference images. Corrected coordinates support quantitative resampling and unbiased measurement across imaging modalities.

entry.title: A Long-Legged, Direct-Drive Monopedal Robot Achieves Exceptional Jump Height

author.name: Gihyeok Na, Justin K. Yim

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a 281 g monopedal jumping robot achieving 7.6 m high jumps with 190 ms stance times using a direct-drive transmission without elastic energy storage, reportedly the highest jump for an electrically actuated, spring-free system. A new fabric-wrap transmission provides variable mechanical advantage to keep a small motor near peak power while bracing the long leg against buckling, and small propellers on a balancing module control leg orientation on the ground and in the air.

entry.title: LLM Parkinsonism: Executive-Control Failure, Token-Inefficient Persistence, and an Uncertainty-Aware Global Executive Control Architecture for Autonomous Language-Model Agents

author.name: Dongsheng Xiao, Zeyuan Wang, Xuzhe Xia, Bo Zhao, Yankai Cao

entry.summary: Introduces the LLM Parkinsonism metaphor for agents that persist in acting past the point of task value, producing low-value refinements and self-created complexity. The paper attributes the failure to concentrating proposal, scope interpretation, and stopping authority in one self-conditioned loop, and proposes an uncertainty-aware global executive control architecture for autonomous agents.

entry.title: HCOE: Hyperbolic Clinical Ontology Embeddings from Biomedical Language Models

author.name: Yixuan Li, Weihao Li, Ziyang Song

entry.summary: Introduces HCOE, which maps frozen BioBERT embeddings into a Poincare ball with ontology-guided contrastive learning to preserve ICD, CCS, and ATC medical code hierarchies. It achieves state-of-the-art results on ICD/ATC clinical relation prediction, CCS-to-PheCode hierarchy transfer, and strong performance on MIMIC-IV. Bridges the gap between textual semantics of biomedical LMs and explicit clinical ontology structure.

entry.title: From Tapping to Hopping: Augmenting Mobile GUI Agents with App-Native Deeplinks

author.name: Yuchen Sun, Chenglin Cai, Gongjie Zhang, Tianyu Xia, Quyu Kong, Panrong Tong, Zhengwen Zeng, Long Chen, Steven Hoi, Chongyang Zhang, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Proposes hybrid interaction for mobile GUI agents, using verified app-native deeplinks for direct navigation while retaining GUI taps for on-screen operations and fallback. The method discovers candidate deeplinks via static analysis, validates them on real devices, and pairs each with a landing-screen description to build a grounded deeplink catalog, yielding the GUI-Hopper agent. Reported to improve task success in common scenarios by replacing screen-by-screen navigation with single deeplink calls.

entry.title: Can Linguistic Reasoning Vectors Enhance Multimodal Reasoning Ability?

author.name: Ziyi Wang, Li Li, Aolin Zhou, Yankun Shen, Chonghan Liu, Shuxia Lin, Xu Yang

entry.summary: The paper observes that multimodal alignment in vision-language models often degrades language-side reasoning present in the base LLM, and proposes LIFT, a lightweight vector-intervention method that transfers reasoning capability from the base LLM to the VLM without retraining the backbone. This addresses a practical degradation problem in VLM construction cheaply. The vector-based intervention approach connects with interpretability-derived steering methods.

entry.title: "AI is (not) the new...": A Diagnostic Analogy Framework for Generative AI's Cultural Impacts

author.name: Rida Qadri, Vinodkumar Prabhakaran, Remi Denton

entry.summary: This paper provides a diagnostic framework for evaluating historical analogies (printing press, steam, electricity) applied to generative AI's transformation of epistemic and cultural practices. It argues that imprecise analogies lead to imprecise governance by targeting the wrong system property, and offers a structured way to specify which property carries a given comparison. Authors include Google researchers (Rida Qadri, Vinodkumar Prabhakaran).

entry.title: Coding Agents Aren't Enough! Evaluating an Enterprise Security Brain for Agentic Cloud Investigations

author.name: Leon Goldberg, Gal Engelberg, Eden Yavin, Elad Elouz, Ariel Zadok, Konstantin Koutsyi

entry.summary: This paper evaluates the Sola Security Brain, a purpose-built security intelligence layer with an offline-resolved relational substrate and query-time security logic, against Claude Code operating the same live cloud environment for security investigations. It argues that cloud-security investigation involves population-level tasks where partial answers are categorically wrong, showing what a dedicated security context layer contributes beyond general-purpose coding agents. The work probes the limits of general coding agents for domain-specific agentic work.

entry.title: Understanding Perturbed Parameter Ensemble Sensitivities Using A Contrastive Learning Approach

author.name: Da Fan, David John Gagne II, Gregory S Elsaesser, Brian Medeiros, Addisu G Semie, Qingyuan Yang, Akila Sampath, Subashree Venkatasubramanian

entry.summary: The authors build an explainable contrastive learning model that maps five monthly cloud and radiation fields into a shared representation space to interpret how physics parameters affect climate simulations. Trained on two 100-member CAM6 perturbed parameter ensembles with 34 parameters differing only in warm rain microphysics scheme, the learned representations separate the ensembles and reveal parameter sensitivities.

entry.title: Subjects, Not Authors: The Authorship Hazard in Agentic Dataspaces

author.name: Seungho Lee, Changbin Lee

entry.summary: This position-style paper identifies the authorship hazard: LLM agents in dataspaces can be both subjects of governance policies and authors of those policies, effectively writing the norms that bind them. It proposes one clean principle — an agent is a subject of the governance plane, never an author of it — and discusses how authorization must change accordingly. This is a timely governance concern as agents compose tool calls and spawn sub-agents.

entry.title: Beyond the Last Truffula Tree: SustainAI - A Water-Aware, Closed-Loop Framework for Environmentally Accountable AI

author.name: Farnaz Farid, Tashfia Towkee, Sania Nasreen, Sami bin Azad

entry.summary: SustainAI is a closed-loop framework that makes AI's water footprint accountable, integrating real-time water metering, a hallucination-aware penalty model, and water-stress-aware routing for model deployment. Using small language models for health misinformation extraction, it shows an 11-fold variation in water footprint across configurations. It highlights the overlooked freshwater cost of data center cooling and electricity generation.

entry.title: Acoustic-to-Text KV Compression for Full-Duplex Speech Models

author.name: Yejin Lee, Seungbeom Kim, Yongha Lee, Kyuhong Shim

entry.summary: The paper proposes acoustic-to-text KV compression for full-duplex speech language models, using a transcription side channel trained with LoRA to convert incoming speech into compact textual memory during listening-time slack, then evicting older acoustic states beyond a cache budget. Knowledge distillation preserves listening and speaking behavior for long-running interactions.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Federated Learning for Infant Movement Analysis

author.name: Edmond S. L. Ho

entry.summary: The paper presents the first federated learning framework for automated infant movement analysis from video-derived skeletal representations, targeting General Movement Assessment for early neurodevelopmental disorder identification. It addresses privacy and data-governance constraints in clinical settings while incorporating uncertainty awareness.

entry.title: Fixed Points Without Fixed Diffusion: Implicit Neural Sheaves for Convergent Test-Time Computation

author.name: R\'emi Bourgerie, \v{S}ar\={u}nas Girdzijauskas, Viktoria Fodor

entry.summary: The paper introduces SheafDEQ, a subhomogeneous deep-equilibrium architecture for implicit graph neural networks that allows richer, edge-dependent sheaf-based transformations while guaranteeing unique, attainable fixed points. This relaxes constraints in prior IGNN constructions that limited expressiveness to ensure convergence. It matters for enabling effectively infinite-depth, flexible test-time computation on graphs without sacrificing theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Energy-efficient operation of neural operators for virtual sensing

author.name: Jason Yoo, Samrendra Roy, Souvik Chakraborty, Syed Bahauddin Alam

entry.summary: This work investigates reducing the energy cost of neural-operator-based virtual sensing services by sharing spatial computation across requests, evaluated on a heat-exchanger service with DeepONet and Fourier neural operator models. Compiler freezing and explicit trunk reuse achieve roughly 1% energy reduction at low request rates and about 20% at forty requests per second, while graph replay in a 15 W mode cuts energy by 22.0-22.5% including preparation and waiting. The controls isolate the effects of model architecture and serving configuration.

entry.title: Low-Bit Recurrent States in Hybrid Language Models

author.name: Hongren Chen, Jiayang He

entry.summary: The paper derives distortion weights from the observability Gramian to allocate mixed-precision bits for quantizing fixed-size recurrent states in hybrid language models, requiring no calibration data, rotations, or training. With per-token quantization, a four-bit payload reduces excess negative log-likelihood by 3.3-27.9x versus seven baselines across three hybrid models, and six bits nearly matches FP32 states.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning: From Spectral Foundation Models to Auroral Emission Spectra

author.name: Matthieu Le Lain, Ga\"el Cessateur, S\'ebastien Lef\`evre

entry.summary: The authors pretrain a 1D Vision Transformer with a masked autoencoder on 223,000 unlabeled auroral spectra, showing the representation recovers physics-relevant emission-line ratios (R^2 0.91 vs 0.77 control) and matches expert-designed features. Fine-tuned, it beats the prior supervised auroral classifier (macro-AP 88.5 vs 77.8).

entry.title: Bridging Body and Brain: Gene-Driven Morphology--Control Co-Design

author.name: Fu Feng, Ruixiao Shi, Yucheng Xie, Jing Wang, Xin Geng

entry.summary: Morphogene is a compact latent blueprint, inspired by biological genes, that jointly conditions agent morphology and control generation at the limb level via an AdaConcat mechanism. Building on it, GeCode formulates morphology-control co-design to induce coordinated changes in both body and brain.

entry.title: Adaptive Random Matrices in Gaussian Bandits: Spectral Universality and Selection-Induced Outliers

author.name: Sudarshan Manikantan (Abstract Math Institute), Abhishek Bhattacharjee (Abstract Math Institute)

entry.summary: The paper proves that in Gaussian bandit designs with proportional dimensional growth, adaptive arm selection does not change the limiting empirical spectral distribution of collected observations: a quantitative coupling theorem shows convergence to the Marchenko-Pastur law uniformly over any causal selection rule when the log number of arms is sublinear in dimension. Consequently, Gaussian Bayesian bandits have policy-independent first-order limits for posterior uncertainty quantities.

entry.title: FRESHLATENT: Channel-Aware Latent Adaptation for Resource-Constrained Embodied VLM Perception

author.name: Rajat Bhattacharjya, Minwoo Kim, Arnab Sarkar, Tamoghno Das, Sing-Yao Wu, Eli Bozorgzadeh, Marco Levorato, Nikil Dutt

entry.summary: FreshLatent is a lightweight channel-aware latent adapter for split vision-language model perception on resource-constrained UAVs, training a power-normalized encoder-decoder robust to wireless corruption of transmitted intermediate features while keeping the surrounding VLM frozen. The framework ties channel quality and communication budgets to operating conditions under which perception remains reliable for mission-critical embodied agents.

entry.title: TR-SSQP: A Trust-Region Method for Constrained Stochastic Optimization under Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Haoxuan Wang, Yuchen Fang, Sen Na

entry.summary: Introduces TR-SSQP, a trust-region method within the stochastic sequential quadratic programming framework for nonlinear optimization with equality constraints under heavy-tailed noise. It uses a normal-tangential decomposition to balance optimality and feasibility and relaxes the bounded-variance assumptions that dominate prior theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Synth-JEPA: Joint Embedding Prediction for Renderer-Free Synthesizer Parameter Search

author.name: Ben Hayes, Haokun Tian, Stefan Lattner

entry.summary: Introduces Synth-JEPA, which learns mutually predictive audio and synthesizer-parameter representations from paired data so candidate parameters can be scored directly in the learned space without rendering each candidate. Evaluated on Surge XT with held-out and out-of-domain targets, it outperforms inverse models and direct search baselines for sound matching.

entry.title: Uncertainty and Explainability in Deep Rough Volatility: A Neural Information-Theoretic Posterior Approach

author.name: Damiano Brigo, Rapha\"el Huser, Dan Leonte

entry.summary: The paper develops a simulation-based inference framework for calibrating rough Heston volatility models, learning the posterior distribution of parameters conditional on an implied-volatility surface using neural ratio estimation. Posterior samples propagate through heteroscedastic neural surrogate pricers to yield uncertainty-aware pricing for path-dependent exotic options. This brings Bayesian uncertainty quantification to deep-learning-based financial calibration.

entry.title: From annotation to reasoning: Culture in language models

author.name: Daniel Hershcovich, Alexander Conroy, Jens Bjerring-Hansen

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that cultural evaluation of language models should move beyond factual knowledge and survey-agreement benchmarks toward interpretive reasoning, using literary interpretation as the testbed. It proposes studying how models explain, evidence, and revise readings of cultural references across historical contexts. The framing introduces interpretive depth as a complement to cultural coverage breadth.

entry.title: RupeeBias: Auditing Demographic Bias in Indian Economic Guidance from Large Language Models

author.name: Pavithra P M Nair, Bhavik Talaviya, Shourya Bhushan, Rahul Pankajakshan, Seema Guruvadoo, Avinash Agarwal, Gilad Gressel, Krishnashree Achuthan

entry.summary: RupeeBias is a benchmark for auditing demographic bias in LLM economic guidance (loans, savings, salary negotiation, pricing) using Indian demographic categories like caste and urban-rural location, which Western-centric benchmarks miss. The work is motivated by the risk that biased advice shapes what users believe they are worth and accept. It fills a real gap in bias evaluation for the Indian context.

entry.title: Conditional Predictive Sufficient Statistics for Visual Representation Learning

author.name: Yuzhou Hong

entry.summary: This single-author theoretical paper formalizes visual representation learning via conditional predictive sufficient statistics (CPSS): a representation should retain latent factors shared with the future while discarding patch-private noise. Under a shared-factor model, it shows next-patch prediction with a cosine loss is maximum likelihood for a von Mises-Fisher model, providing a tractable surrogate for predictive information, and analyzes degenerate constant solutions. The work gives an information-theoretic foundation connecting predictive learning objectives to sufficiency.

entry.title: DGT-Map: Directional Global Traversability Mapping Utilizing Multi-Task Learning for Heterogeneous Vehicles

author.name: Jaskrit Singh, Kashif K. Noori, Jing Xiao, Constantinos Chamzas

entry.summary: DGT-MAP is a self-supervised framework that learns global, directional, vehicle-conditioned traversability costmaps from RGB-D observations and locomotion signals. A shared multi-task backbone learns common terrain features across training vehicles while vehicle-specific heads preserve platform-dependent responses, producing heading-indexed costmaps at inference. This addresses the limitations of isotropic per-location costs and per-vehicle isolated training.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Human-in-the-Loop Bayesian Optimization of a Lower-Limb Exoskeleton

author.name: Neil Janwani, Matthew T. Lerner, Aaron J. Young, Maegan Tucker

entry.summary: MO-HILBO extends human-in-the-loop optimization of exoskeleton assistance to explicit multi-objective Bayesian optimization, allowing wearers' time-varying preferences over objectives to be inferred rather than fixed in advance. This addresses a real limitation of single-objective or fixed-weight HILO methods in assistive robotics. It is relevant to personalized assistive device tuning in practice.

entry.title: Moving Horizon Estimation for Quadrotors: An $\mathcal{L}_1$ Adaptive Optimizer Approach

author.name: Thinh Nguyen, Minkyung Kim, Sandeep Banik, Jinrae Kim, Naira Hovakimyan

entry.summary: The paper formulates linear smoothing moving horizon estimation (MHE) as a dense QP and solves it with a continuous-time Newton method augmented by an L1 Adaptive Optimizer, tracking the time-varying optimal solution with fewer iterations than step-wise iterative solvers. Applied to quadrotor state estimation, it improves accuracy-compute trade-offs over Kalman-filter-style approaches. From Hovakimyan's group, it bridges L1 adaptive control and optimization-based estimation.

entry.title: Co-design of trajectory and morphology for a vertical jump-climbing robot

author.name: Christopher Y. Xu, Elliot W. Hawkes

entry.summary: The paper presents a 290 g robot claimed to be the first to climb vertically by bounding with an aerial phase, using a co-design workflow that jointly optimizes morphology and trajectory under spined-gripper adhesion constraints. The resulting maneuver launches the robot vertically with an aerial re-grasp. It demonstrates a striking dynamic capability for climbing robots from Hawkes' group.

entry.title: Imp-ACT: Adaptive Impedance Control and Action Chunking with Transformers to Learn Contact-Rich Manipulation from Demonstrations

author.name: Luca Zanetti, Doganay Sirintuna, Idil Ozdamar, Pietro Balatti, Heng Zhang, Arash Ajoudani

entry.summary: Imp-ACT integrates direction-dependent Cartesian stiffness modulation directly into demonstration collection using a self-tuning impedance controller during teleoperation, recording compliance alongside vision and motion data. A transformer action-chunking policy then learns contact-rich manipulation without manual stiffness selection or offline target reconstruction. This bridges the common gap between learned visuomotor policies and compliant physical interaction.

entry.title: High-dimensional Gaussian Graphical Model Testing for Long-Memory Time Series

author.name: Percy S. Zhai, Ping-Shou Zhong, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: This statistics paper develops a direct, data-adaptive test statistic for conditional independence in Gaussian graphical model structure for stationary time series, including long-memory regimes previously understudied. It establishes finite-sample Berry-Esseen Gaussian approximation bounds, block bootstrap validity even in ultra-high dimensions, and extensions to two-sample graphical comparison. Rigorous theory for network structure inference in dependent, long-memory data.

entry.title: Why research personas despite RL scaling?

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: A short LessWrong post by Cleo Nardo surveying the motivations behind persona research in alignment, prompted by the observation that RL training appears to wash out initial model personas, referencing Sam Marks' recent persona selection model. It catalogs the strategic rationales of different organizations - from Anthropic hoping aligned personas survive RL, to red-teaming efforts, to the Center on Long-Term Risk view that personas may prevent actively malevolent models even if insufficient for full alignment.

entry.title: Samples, Sources, Space: Decomposing Data Scale in Spatially Structured Representation Learning of Human Brain Microarchitecture

author.name: Christian Schiffer, Mathis Bode, Thomas Lippert, Katrin Amunts, Timo Dickscheid

entry.summary: The paper reframes data scaling as an allocation problem, decomposing it into unique sample count, source diversity, and spatial coverage, studied in microscopic whole-brain histology where sources are brains and samples are spatially anchored image patches. Across 93 controlled pretraining runs of a contrastive model with 11.6 million patches, it varies data allocation, compute, and model capacity. This decomposition has implications for scaling studies well beyond brain data.

entry.title: DeepEdu-v1: Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs for Vietnamese Education

author.name: Quang Nguyen, Hieu Nguyen, Hien Hoang, Toan Pham, Cong Tran, Nam Vu

entry.summary: DeepEdu-v1 is an agentic LLM tutoring system for Vietnamese education, addressing data-sovereignty constraints (Vietnam's Decree 53) that prohibit routing student data to foreign cloud assistants, and the poor alignment of Western-centric pretrained models with the national curriculum. It combines on-premise deployment with optimizations for KV-cache memory and prefill latency to make long-context tutoring feasible on limited hardware. The system targets equitable AI tutoring in developing regions.

entry.title: Inquesto Score: A reliability Protocol For Voice Agents

author.name: Massa Baali, Bhiksha Raj

entry.summary: Inquesto Score (IS) is a protocol for measuring voice-agent reliability as the percentage of calls in a fixed, versioned evaluation population that achieve the caller's goal without a functional failure or worse. It defines explicit failure events and severity levels, measuring timing failures (talk-over, delays) directly from audio and semantic/state failures via scenario predicaments.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Quality for AI-Driven Systems: Evidence from Practitioner Interviews

author.name: Hariharan Gopinath, Jan Bosch, Helena Holmstr\"om Olsson
