author.name: Luc Bouteille, Frederic Jonske, Jens Kleesiek, Alexander Jaus

entry.summary: BiCC is an instance-aware segmentation loss that pairs annotation-derived and prediction-derived connected-component partitions, so false-positive components receive instance-level penalties in addition to boosting small clinically critical lesions. This addresses a gap in prior losses like blob loss and CC-DiceCE that only score annotated instances. It matters for computer-assisted medical review where false-positive burden and precision matter alongside recall.

entry.title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval

author.name: Xinyuan Xie

entry.summary: The paper sharpens the classic Kahn-Komlos-Szemeredi count of Boolean threshold functions to T_n = 2*C(2^n-1, n)(1+O(n^-99)), giving a single threshold neuron capacity of n^2 - log2(n!) + 1 bits with dramatically improved error terms. This underpins questions of how much a single neuron can memorize and how many memories networks retrieve without false memories. It is a strong pure-mathematics contribution to neural network theory.

entry.title: TAPESIM: Efficient Simulation of Adhesive Tape Dispensing for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhaofeng Luo, Xinyu Lu, jaehoon Choi, Zhehuan Chen, Trinity Chung, Xiaowen Qiu, Hugh Nicholas Perkins, Gianna Calderon, Alexis Duburcq, Sanghyun Son, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Yi-Ling Qiao, Minchen Li

entry.summary: TapeSim is a simulator for adhesive tape dispensing in robotic manipulation, addressing the costly challenge of resolving thin adhesive layers by concentrating deformation near the unwinding region and released strip while modeling wound material as a rigid cluster with a deformable collar. This enables repeatable simulation of a common but previously underserved industrial task such as wire harness securing and package sealing. Source code release is planned.

entry.title: Outcome-Sensitive Motion Search for Impact-Aware Dexterous Catching

author.name: Guorui Pei, Jinsong Wu, Songyuan Su, Jiaming Qi, Sichao Liu, David Navarro-Alarcon, Bin Liu, Peng Zhou

entry.summary: The paper tackles impact-aware robotic catching with RL by characterizing how small pre-contact motion variations produce substantially different impact and grasping outcomes, formalized as interventional outcome sensitivity. It introduces an outcome-sensitive motion search to produce better deployable demonstrations from privileged-state RL teachers for imitation-learning students.

entry.title: C-space Analysis using Tropical Geometry

author.name: Abhilash Nayak

entry.summary: This paper applies tropical geometry to analyze configuration spaces of one-degree-of-freedom mechanisms, focusing on identifying singular points where the C-space self-intersects and motion branches split. Tropical methods handle difficult tangential, cuspidal, and inter-dimensional intersections that defeat transversal-intersection approaches. The work provides new mathematical tools for mechanism analysis.

entry.title: Temperament Engineering: Designing Strategic Behavioural Diversity in Robot Swarms

author.name: Edmund R. Hunt

entry.summary: This perspective paper proposes temperament engineering, a bio-inspired framework for robot swarms that treats the distribution of individual behavioral differences across the swarm, rather than the single individual controller, as the primary design object. It borrows five evolutionarily validated axes of animal temperament (shyness-boldness, exploration-avoidance, activity, aggressiveness, sociability) as a design vocabulary, reframing hardware- and calibration-induced behavioral variance as a strategic resource rather than an imperfection to minimize.

entry.title: Contact as a Decision Variable: Capability-Tradeoff Contact Selection for Legged Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Al Jaber Mahmud, Shuai Li, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: The paper formulates joint selection of an environmental support contact and whole-body configuration for legged loco-manipulation, balancing residual wrench, end-effector reach, base mobility, and contact acquisition cost. To avoid repeated whole-body optimizations for every candidate, CTCS screens candidates, groups similar ones, and evaluates representatives. This makes capability-aware contact selection computationally tractable.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards for Small Search Agents

author.name: Gaurisankar Jayadas, Aske Plaat, \'Alvaro Serra-G\'omez, Sandheep P

entry.summary: This paper tests whether the reason-over-search RLVR recipe works below one billion parameters without distillation, training Qwen3.5-0.8B with GRPO and an interleaved Wikipedia search tool on MuSiQue while varying only reward shape across three seeds. It systematically evaluates checkpoint behavior across reward designs. The result informs whether RLVR is broadly accessible to small models or dependent on scale.

entry.title: From Static Personal Values to Contextualized Personalization: Bayesian Personalized Value Alignment for LLMs

author.name: Hanze Guo, Aixuan Song, Jing Yao, Xiangxu Zhang, Xiaoyuan Yi, Xing Xie, Xiao Zhou

entry.summary: BaCVA is an inference-time Bayesian method for personalized value alignment that treats static personal values as priors and context-dependent preferences as posteriors, inspired by Lewin's Field Theory, so value salience varies across situations rather than being a fixed profile. This addresses a real limitation of static alignment approaches. The Bayesian contextualization is an elegant reframing of personalized alignment.

entry.title: Speculative Evaluation of Stochastic LLMs

author.name: Qianli Shen, Xiang Li, Ruomeng Ding, Yanxi Chen, Daoyuan Chen, Yaliang Li

entry.summary: The paper formalizes benchmark evaluation of stochastic LLMs as minimizing the variance of a fixed-budget mean and proposes a Hierarchical Bayesian Neyman (HBN) policy that allocates rollouts across tasks using posterior variance estimates, with an asynchronous variant to mitigate the pilot synchronization barrier. This yields more accurate benchmark scores under fixed rollout budgets.

entry.title: SARFusion: Scene-Aware Routing Fusion for Robust Camera-LiDAR 3D Object Detection

author.name: Yuting Zhao, Ziyi Zheng, Shuxiao Li

entry.summary: SARFusion reformulates robust camera-LiDAR fusion as scene-aware branch routing, avoiding tightly coupled multimodal query decoding that makes detectors vulnerable when one modality degrades. It adaptively routes fusion decisions at global-scene and per-object-query granularity for more reliable 3D detection under corrupted driving conditions.

entry.title: Generalized Graph Variational Autoencoders: Bounded Divergences Control Posterior Collapse

author.name: Kleyton da Costa, Bernardo Modenesi, Ivan F. M. Menezes, Helio Lopes

entry.summary: Proposes GGVA, which replaces the KL term in variational graph autoencoders with members of the Renyi-Tsallis divergence family, showing the VGAE is the q=1 special case so any difference is attributable to a single scalar. The analysis identifies boundedness of the divergence, rather than its order, as the operative property controlling posterior collapse.

entry.title: BranchShine-CR: Compact Multilingual IPA Transcription with Self-Conditioned CTC and Consistency Regularization

author.name: Nikhil Navas, Sergio Chevtchenko, Talisson Damiao, Saeed Afshar

entry.summary: BranchShine-CR is a 25M-parameter model for multilingual transcription into the International Phonetic Alphabet, combining a rotary E-Branchformer encoder, intermediate self-conditioned CTC, and consistency regularization. It achieves 4.47% IPA character error rate, a 22.3% relative improvement over ZIPA-CTC-NS with about one-twelfth the parameters, beating a similarly sized NeMo Conformer baseline across all 41 languages.

entry.title: Precise Convergence Speed of Clipped SGD

author.name: David A. R. Robin

entry.summary: This paper provides a tightened convergence analysis of clipped gradient descent on (L0, L1)-smooth functions with quantitative constants, simplifying proofs around an l2-projection-based bias control and extending validity to learning rates up to 1/beta, matching classical smooth-function analysis. It also strengthens the convergence criterion from best-iterate to averaged gradient norms. Clipped SGD underpins much robust deep-learning practice, so sharper theory here is broadly useful.

entry.title: Graph-Based Inference and Topology-Aware Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Large-Scale Railway Network Management

author.name: Giacomo Arcieri, Gregory Duth\'e, Christophe Muller, Konstantinos G. Papakonstantinou, Daniel Straub, Eleni Chatzi

entry.summary: Proposes a graph-based framework for large-scale railway infrastructure asset management combining a hierarchical Bayesian environment model (with Gaussian process components for spatial deterioration correlations) with topology-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning for scalable decision support. It addresses the failure modes of centralized approaches (intractable at scale) and decentralized approaches (poor coordination). The work targets realistic sequential decision-making for infrastructure asset management.

entry.title: Automatic Harness Evolution for Hardware Design Verification: Can LLMs Consolidate Gains Across Discovered Harnesses?

author.name: Kidus Seyoum, Ajay Mittur

entry.summary: This paper studies whether LLM agents can reliably improve their own surrounding harnesses for hardware design verification tasks, using 12 proprietary root-cause localization tasks. Automatically evolved harnesses increased completed attempts by 71-76% and task coverage by 80-100%, but correct attempts rose only 18-24% and gains were not consolidated across tasks, with later candidates trading gains rather than preserving them. It offers a sobering empirical look at self-improvement limits in agentic workflows.

entry.title: TraceGuard: Adaptive Multimodal Poison Filtering through Cross-Feature Rank Agreement

author.name: Haoyang Li, Yaxin Xiao, Linyan Dai, Jiawen Fu, Zi Liang, Jason Xue, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: TraceGuard analyzes what properties a stealthy multimodal poisoning attack must preserve to remain effective, framing poison impact via occurrence frequency and joint training influence. It derives six corpus-level cross-modal features and uses rank agreement among them to adaptively filter poisoned image-text data.

entry.title: Framing by Wording, Framing by Selection: A Large-Scale Two-Dimensional Audit of French News Headlines, 2022-2025

author.name: Amr Sobhy

entry.summary: This study introduces a two-dimensional framework separating salience framing (wording devices like loaded vocabulary and threat framing) from selection framing (outlet-level story choice) in news headlines. Using an LLM-assisted 10,000-headline supervision set validated against blind human studies, the classifier is applied to 902,111 French headlines from 25 outlets for a large-scale media audit.

entry.title: Clinical Intent Extraction: A FHIR-Aligned Representation and the CIRCA Benchmark

author.name: Alexander Apartsin, Yehudit Aperstein

entry.summary: Defines Clinical Intent Extraction, the task of recovering prospective clinical actions as complete structured records, and introduces the Clinical Intent Representation aligned with HL7 FHIR that decomposes actions into verb, type, coded target, timing, condition, plus request-intent and a modality scale of clinical strength. It unifies five heterogeneous prior corpora into the CIRCA benchmark.

entry.title: Adaptive Fisher-Whitened Cross-Covariance for Low-Resource Speech Recognition

author.name: Asmee Mishra, Mengjie Qian, Brechtje Post, Kate Knill

entry.summary: This work applies Fisher-Whitened Cross-Covariance Analysis to adapt multilingual speech foundation models (Whisper and Qwen3-ASR) to low-resource languages, introducing Asymmetric-Coupled FCCA and Adaptive-Rank FCCA as extensions that use downstream task information to define the adaptation subspace. This task-informed PEFT alternative to generic low-rank methods like LoRA targets languages poorly represented during pre-training. It advances parameter-efficient adaptation for low-resource ASR.

entry.title: PePESeg3D: Perception Prior Enhances Multi-Scale Segmentation for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Sungjae Choi, Seunghee Koh, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: PePESeg3D injects perception priors (monocular depth and mask constraints) into both upstream 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction and downstream contrastive multi-scale segmentation feature learning. This makes geometry aware of semantic structure and reduces dependence on incomplete mask supervision. The result is improved open-vocabulary multi-scale segmentation of 3DGS scenes.

entry.title: Ego-Exo4D Human Meshes Dataset: 4D Human Motion Reconstruction for Ego-Exo Captures

author.name: Abhiram Maddukuri, Georgios Pavlakos

entry.summary: The authors release Ego-Exo4D-HM, a large-scale dataset of 4D human motion reconstructions for the Ego-Exo4D multi-view ego-exocentric captures, along with the reconstruction pipeline. It fills the gap left by the original dataset's sparse 3D pose annotations.

entry.title: Activation-Flexible ANN-to-SNN Conversion with Finite-State Markov Neurons

author.name: Ruiyu Jia, Zhuo-Cheng Xiao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a finite-state continuous-time Markov chain neuron framework whose stationary spike flux can uniformly approximate any continuous nonnegative monotone activation on a compact interval, with explicit error bounds, enabling ANN-to-SNN conversion independent of a fixed activation-to-neuron correspondence. Two- and three-state CTMCs fit ReLU, sigmoid, softplus, and clipped ReLU. This generalizes ANN-to-SNN conversion beyond standard rate-coding assumptions.

entry.title: TRACE: Interactive Bi-Directional Tracing of Monochrome Cables Amid Clutter

author.name: Nidhya Shivakumar, Ethan Ransing, Josh Zhang, Shamak Gowda, Kevin Yang, Miles Hua, Anika Agrawal, Justin Yu, Ken Goldberg

entry.summary: TRACE combines bi-directional cable tracing with interactive perception primitives (Divergence Push and Cluster Dilation) to resolve ambiguities when estimating the state of multiple monochrome cables amid occlusions and crossings. Evaluation across 110 physical experiments shows increased percentage of correctly traced cable length, relevant to data centers, manufacturing, and surgery.

entry.title: Global Convergence of Third-Order Langevin Dynamics for Non-Convex Optimization via Simulated Annealing

author.name: Yingli Wang, Kelvin Shuangjian Zhang, Lingjiong Zhu

entry.summary: This theoretical work establishes global convergence guarantees for third-order Langevin dynamics on non-convex objectives using simulated annealing with fixed friction and decreasing noise. Under dissipativity, regularity, and low-temperature functional-inequality assumptions, logarithmic cooling drives objective values to the global minimum at a barrier-controlled kinetic rate, preserved under specific discretizations. It extends Langevin-based optimization theory to a third-order regime.

entry.title: Riemannian Gradient Descent for Gaussian Mixture Models with unknown diagonal covariances

author.name: Romane Giard, Yohann De Castro, Roland Denis, Cl\'ement Marteau

entry.summary: This paper addresses numerical resolution of the Beurling-LASSO, a convex sparsity-promoting framework over measures, applied to estimating Gaussian mixture models with an unknown number of components and unknown diagonal covariances. The method combines Conic Particle Gradient Descent with Riemannian gradient descent respecting the Fisher-Rao geometry of Gaussians. The authors prove exponential local convergence under a non-degeneracy condition and relate it to BLASSO's exact support recovery guarantee.

entry.title: AI in research and publishing (Sep 2026)

author.name: Jason Fantl

entry.summary: The author synthesizes recent reporting on AI usage in research and publishing, noting Anthropic's claim that 26% of AI R&D work is now AI-led under human oversight, up from under 1% six months earlier, and OpenAI's claims about an automated research intern with 70% of researchers running four or more concurrent agents. The post aggregates multiple sources with explicit acknowledgment of weak methodology, including reliance on Pangram detection and self-reporting. It offers a snapshot of rapidly shifting AI-assisted research practice.

entry.title: TWIST: A Proposed Benchmark for Intervention Quality in Conversational Memory, with a Human-Validated Draft-Alignment

author.name: Subrat Panda

entry.summary: TWIST is a proposed benchmark measuring intervention quality in conversational memory systems: whether a deployed system correctly acts at belief-change points across four tracks including unprompted tension detection, draft vetting, and governing sensitive recall. It extends LoCoMo with matched do-not-over-detect controls that price false interventions. This targets an unmeasured property of memory systems beyond recall.

entry.title: Claim-Gated Source-Risk Auditing for Generative Search

author.name: Kainan Zhou, Chuhong Xu, Gangzhen Qian, Zhaoyi Li

entry.summary: This work specifies a formal audit procedure for generative search answers that checks whether a query-source-answer tuple omits a material source relationship even when the cited passage is supported, resolving omissions only when relationship evidence, answer adoption, materiality, and disclosure are all observed. A reference checker makes the specification executable, validated against exhaustive synthetic predicate combinations and malformed records.

entry.title: BiGraph-Diffuse: A Bidirectional Diffusion Language Model with Graph-Structured Retrieval For Mental Health Counseling

author.name: Yuxiang Cheng, Quanwei Tang, Lvhui Lu, Dong Zhang, Shoushan Li, Erik Cambria

entry.summary: The paper proposes BiGraph-Diffuse, a bidirectional diffusion language model combined with graph-structured retrieval for mental health counseling dialogue. It targets two failure modes of autoregressive systems: inability to revise early interpretations when clients progressively disclose deeper trauma, and poor incorporation of relational clinical knowledge. The approach is motivated by limited access to professional counseling worldwide.

entry.title: Decoding Imagined Speech: A Strictly Subject-Independent Approach Using EEG

author.name: Frederik M{\o}llskov Trier, Xiaopeng Mao, Sadasivan Puthusserypady

entry.summary: Presents a transparent baseline for imagined speech decoding from EEG under strictly subject-independent evaluation, comparing time-domain statistical and frequency-domain spectral bandpower pipelines with random forest classifiers and trial-level voting. The spectral pipeline performs better under honest cross-subject protocols.

entry.title: Jev-Mobile: Jev as an Executor for Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Linghua Zhang

entry.summary: Jev-Mobile restructures mobile GUI agents into low-frequency VLM planning plus high-frequency execution by a fast typed decision model (Jev) operating over the accessibility tree's structured action space. This lets many GUI actions execute per VLM decision, cutting latency and serving cost while keeping interaction adaptive, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

entry.title: DocuTeam: Mixed-Initiative Multi-Agent Discussions around Evolving Documents

author.name: Heechan Lee, Juhyeon Choi, Tae Soo Kim, Juho Kim, Joseph Seering

entry.summary: DocuTeam is a mixed-initiative multi-agent discussion system where both users and agents initiate and steer conversations, with agents monitoring document changes to proactively start discussions as work evolves. A within-subjects study (N=20) shows participants produce significantly more novel outcomes compared to baselines, advancing human-AI collaborative writing and problem solving.

entry.title: agentic-ger: terminology recovery in long-form speech using global context

author.name: Yanqiao Zhu, Wupeng Wang, Zhifu Gao, Xiangang Li, Xie Chen

entry.summary: Presents Agentic-GER, an LLM-based agent that corrects domain-specific terminology in long-form ASR transcripts by using global transcript context to flag suspicious terms, selectively re-transcribing source audio to verify candidates, and propagating accepted edits. Experiments across four LLMs and two ASR systems on GigaSpeechBench show consistent terminology improvements.

entry.title: CoSWA-YOLOv12: Scale-Invariant Tiny Object Detection and Segmentation of Malaria Parasites

author.name: Ahmed Tahiru Issah, Carine Mukamakuza

entry.summary: Presents CoSWA-YOLOv12, a compact YOLOv12-based detector addressing the systematic under-detection of tiny early-ring-stage malaria parasites, where uniformly applying Normalized Gaussian Wasserstein Distance supervision degrades localization of larger objects. The method balances scale-invariant label assignment and regression so tiny-class gains do not come at the cost of overall slide accuracy.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Domain Adaptation of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) for Adolescent Health Communication in Ghanaian Languages

author.name: Stephen E. Moore, Akwasi Asare, Mich-Seth Owusu, Paul Azunre, Joel Budu, Lawrence A. Adu-Gyamfi

entry.summary: Benchmarks five ASR systems, including language-specific Wav2Vec2 models and multimodal LLMs Gemma 3n and Gemma 4, on Ghanaian-language adolescent sexual and reproductive health data in Twi, Dagbani, and Ewe, then performs supervised domain adaptation using a compact fine-tuned Qwen3-ASR-0.6B. The study provides an end-to-end pipeline from benchmarking to adapted low-resource ASR.

entry.title: S2Planner: Multi-Scale Semantic Planner for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhaowei Lu, Liguo Zhou, Yujie Guo, Lei Yu, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: Presents S2Planner, an end-to-end trajectory planner combining a fine-tuned DINOv3 backbone with a spatial tuning adapter and a coarse-to-fine decoder using trajectory self-attention and camera-projected cross-attention. The contribution is integration of ego-conditioned trajectory initialization with geometry-guided sampling of multi-scale features; the authors transparently note that the reported 88.03 PDMS on NAVSIM was selected on navtest and is expected to be optimistic.

entry.title: Mind What Matters for Reasoning: Aligning Cross-Modal Attention via Selective Probability Mass Concentration

author.name: Jiaqi Deng, Zonghan Wu, Zhan Heng, Xiaoshui Huang, Huan Huo, Guandong Xu

entry.summary: This paper improves multimodal LLM reasoning by strengthening implicit visual grounding without directly supervising the reasoning process. Motivated by functional specialization of attention heads, it selectively guides only the heads most responsive to visual evidence using a probability-mass concentration objective, reducing hallucination and over-reliance on language priors. This offers a lightweight alternative to reasoning-oriented supervision or inference-time fixes.

entry.title: Learning Better Reasoning for Generative Recommendation with Semantic IDs

author.name: Mengdan Zhu, Yufan Zhao, Sophie Di, Yao Zhao, Tao Di, Yulan Yan, Sridhar Iyer, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: This paper tackles the problem that reasoning traces before Semantic-ID generation in generative recommenders are not always beneficial, since inaccurate or uninformative reasoning can mislead item generation. The authors propose a method for a recommender to select and learn from reasoning that actually helps subsequent item prediction. It is a careful refinement of the increasingly popular reasoning-enhanced generative recommendation paradigm.

entry.title: Guardrails or Roadblocks? Effects of Pedagogical Style and Context Awareness in AI Teaching Assistants for Programming

author.name: Madeleine Eastwood, Harshith Narne, Joseph Hilby, Paul Denny, Ashish Aggarwal, Amanpreet Kapoor

entry.summary: A randomized controlled trial with 132 students in an introductory programming course examining how guardrails, pedagogical style, and context awareness in LLM-based teaching assistants affect learning experiences. The study probes whether overly restrictive or poorly contextualized support pushes students to bypass approved tools for general-purpose LLMs. The findings inform the design of educational AI systems where helpfulness must be balanced against pedagogical constraints.

entry.title: SpaFactor: Lightweight Spatial Context-Aware Gene Program Modeling for Histology-to-Transcriptomics Inference

author.name: Shiting Ruan, Xitong Ling, Qiming He, Ziyou Yan, Huaitian Yuan, Tian Guan, Ying Xiao, Xu Guan, Yonghong He

entry.summary: SpaFactor is a lightweight low-rank factorization framework that predicts spatial transcriptomics gene expression from routine H&E histology images, modeling morphology programs and gene programs rather than fitting high-dimensional gene outputs independently. It avoids the computational heaviness of graph-network approaches while capturing biological coordination among genes.

entry.title: When Does Unsupervised Learning Succeed or Fail? A PoS Perspective on Reconstruction-Based Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mehmet Yama\c{c}, Yagmur Mustu, Muhammad Numan Yousaf, Lei Xu, Marcel van Gerven

entry.summary: Using the Pursuit of Subspaces hypothesis, the paper characterizes two opposing failure modes of reconstruction-based anomaly detection (join blindness and meet preference) via the meet, union, and join geometry of nominal components. It proposes Dynamic Push and Pull learning from controlled perturbations and nested manifold carving without anomaly labels.

entry.title: Decoupled Learning and Selection in Slate Recommendation for Privacy and Stability Under Noisy Scores

author.name: Sam Urmian, Qinyi Liu, Mohammad Khalil

entry.summary: This paper formalizes slate recommendation as a randomized score learner followed by deterministic selection, deriving when differential-privacy guarantees pass through selection via post-processing and giving a logged margin certificate that bounds score-induced objective movement below the greedy decision margin to guarantee slate stability. It includes controlled fixed-margin tests showing near-linear exponent scaling. The work provides principled privacy and robustness guarantees for recommendation systems.

entry.title: Diverse Geometries, Frozen Weights: Robust Heterogeneous Treatment-Effect Estimation via Causal Expert Ensembles

author.name: Ali Haghpanah Jahromi, Mohammad Taheri

entry.summary: Introduces GeoACE, a five-expert ensemble for heterogeneous treatment-effect estimation that combines a common anchor-correction estimator with complementary overlap-aware and outcome-guided geometries, with task-level weights learned only from internal validation and frozen before test evaluation. An outcome-free expert, O-Phi-ACE, contributes an overlap-aware statistical projection. The framework addresses the fact that the right inductive bias varies with overlap, imbalance, and sample size in observational causal inference.

entry.title: An Order-Theoretic Characterization of Consistent Inductive Inference

author.name: Zhou Lu

entry.summary: The paper answers when a learner can make only finitely many prediction errors along every infinite sequence labeled by a fixed unknown target, for arbitrary binary hypothesis classes without uniform mistake bounds. It gives a ZFC characterization via a single linear order on finite realizable traces satisfying well-foundedness and conflict-separation conditions, which induce a learner whose selected evidence decreases with each mistake, and conversely any consistent learner yields such an order via Kleene-Brouwer ordering. This settles a foundational question in inductive inference in full generality.

entry.title: Paging the Experts: A Reproducible Characterization of Flash-Backed MoE Inference on iPhone

author.name: Musa Shams

entry.summary: Routide is a Swift/MLX runtime that runs the text path of a quantized Qwen3.6-35B-A3B checkpoint on an iPhone, keeping expert weights in flash storage with a byte-budgeted subset in memory. The characterization shows apparent memory capacity cliffs are cache-policy and workload interactions rather than universal requirements.

entry.title: Machine Unlearning for Gibbs Supervised Learning Algorithms

author.name: Yaiza Bermudez, Samir M. Perlaza, I\~naki Esnaola

entry.summary: The paper proposes a variational method for exact machine unlearning in Gibbs supervised learning algorithms, formulated as empirical risk maximization over the data to be unlearned with relative-entropy regularization toward the original algorithm. The resulting solution is provably distributionally identical to retraining without the forgotten data.

entry.title: Path-specific harm decomposition: A partial identification framework

author.name: Ruizi Yan, Dennis Frauen, Maresa Schr\"oder, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: Introduces a path-specific analogue of the fraction of negatively affected (FNA) that disentangles total treatment harm into direct and mediator-induced components in causal mediation settings. Since these quantities depend on joint distributions only partially identified from data, the paper develops a partial identification framework relevant to do-no-harm treatment policy design.

entry.title: Agentic Detection of Online Conspiracies

author.name: Lior Biton, Oren Tsur

entry.summary: The paper proposes an agentic framework for detecting conspiratorial discourse that infers speaker intent (illocutionary force) rather than just surface claims, using tools that query relevant social contexts. It is demonstrated on a large unique dataset of Hebrew tweets spanning 2018-2023, showing that the same content may express endorsement, concern, criticism, satire, or mockery.

entry.title: DP-IPI: A Hybrid Differential Privacy Text Rewriting Mechanism for Indirect Personal Identifiers in Clinical Texts

author.name: Ibrahim Baroud, Stephen Meisenbacher, Sebastian M\"oller, Florian Matthes, Roland Roller

entry.summary: DP-IPI introduces a utility-preserving differential privacy text rewriting method for clinical texts that selectively privatizes only spans containing indirect personal identifiers rather than perturbing all tokens indiscriminately. The approach reduces re-identification risk from indirect identifiers while maintaining text quality and usability in clinical settings. This addresses a real gap between blanket DP rewriting and practical clinical data sharing.

entry.title: JevOut: Natural Context Can Flip Decision Models

author.name: Zixiang Xu

entry.summary: This paper shows that dedicated decision models like Jev, which map language to probability distributions over finite choices for routing and tool selection, can be flipped by short, natural context additions even when the correct answer is unchanged. The authors refine fluent context additions that redirect initially correct decisions using the model's own option probabilities. The finding exposes a robustness vulnerability in decision-model deployments with real-world contextual inputs.

entry.title: BiMamba2 Masked Discrete-Unit Prediction for Multilingual Speech Representation for Unsupervised Speech in the Wild Challenge

author.name: Prakriti Subedi, Howard Prioleau, Saurav K Aryal

entry.summary: A 47.88M-parameter bidirectional Mamba-2 encoder trained with HuBERT-style masked discrete-unit prediction on 250 hours of unlabeled speech across 67 languages, submitted to the Interspeech 2026 UPS Challenge. The system combines masked k-means pseudo-label prediction with language identification supervision and VICReg regularization, achieving an Adjusted Rand Index of 0.735 that beats four baselines on speaker clustering. Language ID and character error rate remain below supervised baselines.

entry.title: Exploiting Target Knowledge from MLLMs for Robust Few-Shot Segmentation

author.name: Yijun Hu, Heng Fan, Libo Zhang

entry.summary: MK-FSS enhances few-shot segmentation by mining target knowledge through multimodal LLM reasoning and injecting it into SAM 2, going beyond appearance-based support-query matching. Two complementary knowledge forms help handle appearance discrepancies and occlusions in query images. The framework improves robustness of segmenting unseen categories from few examples.

entry.title: ImCorr: Sub-pixel Semantic Correspondence via Implicit Feature Decoding

author.name: Yusung Choi

entry.summary: The paper argues that the plateau of semantic correspondence methods at fine-grained thresholds stems from grid-tied patch readout in ViTs, quantifying a quantization ceiling across all 499,188 SPair-71k keypoints. ImCorr introduces implicit feature decoding to query exact keypoint locations instead of nearest grid features, enabling sub-pixel correspondence.

entry.title: SALI: Shot-Aware Late Interaction for Cross-Shot Relation Matching in Text-to-Video Retrieval using Film-Grammar Knowledge

author.name: Toya Oyama, Rainer Lienhart, Shin'ichi Satoh

entry.summary: SALI improves text-to-video retrieval for relational queries by extracting query subject and object and matching their embeddings against per-shot visual embeddings with greedy max or optimal-transport matching, plus a film-grammar penalty during fine-tuning. It handles cross-shot relations like shot/reverse-shot dialog that single clip embeddings lose.

entry.title: ConPro: Contrast Projection Pretraining for Label-Efficient Vessel Segmentation in DSA Sequences

author.name: Xinge Guo, Yuanhao Wang, Liqi Shu, Yang Liu, Min Xu

entry.summary: ConPro exploits temporal contrast flow in unlabeled DSA sequences by defining a self-supervised pretext whose target is the contrast projection, the normalized per-pixel drop below the temporal median. It improves label-efficient vessel segmentation over from-scratch training and competing semi/self-supervised methods across multiple label fractions.

entry.title: FMCW-LIO: A Doppler LiDAR-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Mingle Zhao, Jiahao Wang, Tianxiao Gao, Chengzhong Xu, Hui Kong

entry.summary: FMCW-LIO is a LiDAR-inertial odometry system that exploits intrinsic per-point Doppler velocity measurements from FMCW Doppler LiDARs, adding motion compensation and a Doppler-aided observation model instead of relying purely on geometric features. It represents a shift as Doppler LiDARs provide motion measurements, not just ranges. It matters for robust localization and mapping in autonomous systems.

entry.title: An Analysis of Streaming Deep Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Continual Learning in Robotics

author.name: Teeratham Vitchutripop, Alyssa Quarles, Wenhe Zhang, Richard Xue, Daniel Rakita

entry.summary: This paper presents the first analysis of stream-based deep RL, where updates use only the most recent experience, as a continual learning framework for adapting robotic policies to novel scenario changes after deployment. It contrasts streaming adaptation with the conventional approach of growing offline training datasets for robustness.

entry.title: Anthropomimetic Soft Robotic Forearm with Independently Articulated Carpal Bones Enabling Human-Like Adaptive Stiffness Modulability

author.name: Yoshinobu Obata, Yinlai Jiang, Hiroshi Yokoi, Shunta Togo

entry.summary: This paper builds an anatomically accurate anthropomimetic soft robotic forearm with eight independently movable carpal bones, 22 actuated muscles, and compliant fingertips to study how wrist morphology produces adaptive stiffness modulability. By comparing normal, fused, and ellipsoidal skeletal configurations under different muscle co-activation patterns, it identifies morphological factors underlying human-like stiffness anisotropy. Results inform both bioinspired robot design and biomechanics understanding.

entry.title: UCON: Uncertainty-aware Navigation with Historical Re-association in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Bing Sun, Yue Lin, Yongsheng Yuan, Yang Liu, Dong Wang, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: UCON addresses autonomous navigation in dynamic environments by tackling perception instability and uncertainty-optimization mismatch. It introduces a point-level historical re-association mechanism that uses past point cloud fragments to recover lost targets and maintain identity continuity, then uses a Kalman filter for anisotropic motion estimation with covariance propagation so uncertainty can be principledly incorporated into trajectory optimization. The system improves robustness in crowded dynamic scenes.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Anchoring of Fingertip Sensing to Proprioception and Proactive Actions for Robot Imitation Learning

author.name: Tomohiro Motoda, Masaki Murooka, Keisuke Shirai, Hanbit Oh, Ryoichi Nakajo, Shotaro Miwa, Roman Mykhailyshyn, Hugo Duarte, Yukiyasu Domae

entry.summary: This work studies how to incorporate fingertip tactile and proximity sensing into robot imitation learning using pretrained sensor encoders, exploiting that proximity sensing is informative before contact while tactile sensing is informative after contact. The authors show naively adding sensor signals to a policy can underperform vision alone, and propose self-supervised anchoring of fingertip sensing to proprioception plus proactive actions to use each modality in its informative phase. This yields consistent improvements over vision-only policies.

entry.title: Pairwise Approximation Can Select the Wrong Multi-Robot Plan

author.name: William Teo

entry.summary: This paper quantifies the plan-selection regret incurred when multi-robot coordination methods score joint plans using only singleton and pairwise terms instead of the full set function. Using frozen four-robot trajectories on an indoor exploration benchmark, the author replays all 16 robot subsets to compute exact delivered coverage and two pairwise approximations (exact order-2 Mobius truncation and a least-squares two-additive fit). Ranking by pairwise scores changes the selected plan on six of seven maps, demonstrating concrete failure of common approximations.

entry.title: Shrinking-Tube Concentration for Adaptive Markovian Stochastic Approximation

author.name: Jin Li, Ye Luo, Xiaowei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper establishes a shrinking-tube concentration bound for projected stochastic approximation driven by an adaptive Markov chain, guaranteeing that all iterates after a chosen time stay within a tolerance that tightens over time. A matching lower bound shows the polynomial exit-probability exponent cannot be improved under finite second moments, identifying a sharp tradeoff between tolerance shrinkage and exit probability decay. This covers algorithms that make decisions while reshaping the data-generating dynamics.

entry.title: When Does Action Credit Need Updating?

author.name: Hongye Yang, Boxiao Huang

entry.summary: This paper asks when historical action credits in tool-using agents become stale after policy updates, observing that a change in action value does not necessarily change the decision if policy drift is too small to overturn the action ranking. It introduces pairwise branch sensitivity to detect when downstream decision rankings would actually change, avoiding expensive recomputation. An efficiency-oriented contribution to continual agent training.

entry.title: Decision Hijacking: Prompt Injection Attacks on Jev's Typed Probabilistic Decisions

author.name: Tiantong Wu, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: The paper studies prompt injection effects on Jev, a non-generative model with schema-defined typed probabilistic decision outputs, using 510 reconstructed InjecAgent cases. Malicious content shifts action probabilities but rarely flips the chosen action; adaptive attacks using score feedback double mean attacker-target probability though fresh-validation success stays low (1.8% to 3.5%), with success linked to small decision margins and observation control.

entry.title: Learnable Time-Frequency Masks for Explaining Time-Series Classifiers

author.name: Theresa Dahl Frehr, Francisco Pelayo, Lukas Raad, Alicia Garc\'ia Sanz, Thea Br\"usch, Tommy Sonne Alstr{\o}m

entry.summary: The paper proposes XACT, a general explainability framework that learns sparse attribution masks over coefficients from arbitrary invertible time-frequency transforms (STFT, continuous and discrete wavelet transforms), and extends the virtual inspection layer approach so LRP can attribute through wavelet transforms. This addresses the gap that existing attribution methods operate only in the time domain or fixed transforms.

entry.title: AquaMend: Minimal Re-probing and Conditional Rollback for Latent-Belief Failures in Embodied Agents

author.name: Yufan Liu, Shang Luo, Yang Liu, Haoxuan Jia, Feiyu Han, Qian Li, Chen Li, Yingguang Yang, Chongyang Zhang, Hao Zheng, Kefu Xu, Bin Chong

entry.summary: AquaMend formalizes recovery from invalidated embodied-agent beliefs as a decision over re-probing, rollback, or supported continuation on a probe-belief-action graph under an expected-loss objective spanning sensing, physical recovery, and uncorrected failures. In 32 paired scenarios it recovers in 28 cases and reduces mean complete loss by 21.6% versus restarting, with analysis of when the per-belief three-way optimum is achievable.

entry.title: BaseCamp --- An Agentic AI Framework for Automating DNA Sequencing Data Pipelines

author.name: Eranga Bandara, Xueping Liang, Asanga Gunaratna, Tharaka Hewa, Abdul Rahman, Peter Foytik, Safdar H. Bouk, Sachini Rajapakse, Isurunima Kularathna, Pramoda Karunarathna, Chalani Rajapakse, Ng Wee Keong, Kasun De Zoysa, Amin Hass, Wathsala Herath, Ross Gore, Ravi Mukkamala, Nihal Siriwardanagea, Gihan Siriwardanagea, Aruna Withanage, Nilaan Loganathan, Sachin Shetty

entry.summary: BaseCamp is an agentic AI framework that automates the manual decision layer of DNA sequencing pipelines, such as choosing quality thresholds, adjudicating borderline variant calls, and triaging expert review, by decomposing the pipeline into six specialized agent roles. This targets judgment-intensive, inconsistent, and undocumented decisions that workflow systems leave to human operators. It is a meaningful applied contribution for bioinformatics operations.

entry.title: AlphaDiverse: Post-Training Local Quantitative Research Agents for Diverse Exploration in Alpha Factor Mining

author.name: Qingzhuo Wang, Zikun Wei, Zhihua Wei, Wen Shen

entry.summary: AlphaDiverse post-trains local agents for alpha factor mining, using a multi-agent research system with varied plan portfolios and environments to collect diverse research paths, then warm-starting local Planner and Realizer agents with SFT followed by further training. It targets both the cost and confidentiality limits of API-dependent systems and the research path collapse where loops keep revisiting a few successful economic mechanisms. A thoughtful approach to diversity in automated quantitative research.

entry.title: ASIRF: An Agentic Framework for Context-Dependent Sensitive Information Redaction

author.name: Sudha Priyadarshini, Mohamed Chahine Ghanem

entry.summary: ASIRF treats sensitive-information redaction as domain- and intent-dependent, retrieving domain-specific definitions from a flexible knowledge base at inference time instead of fixing a taxonomy at training, so it adapts without retraining. Two architectures (a three-call multi-agent pipeline and a single-agent variant) are evaluated across ten small open-weight models and eight datasets, compared against the OpenAI Privacy Filter baseline.

entry.title: When No One Owns the Judgment: Accountability Under Contribution Dissolution in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Hengzhi Ye

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that debates over AI disclosure and detection miss a deeper problem: unowned judgment, where evaluations, decisions, and creative directions are shaped by AI with no accountable human or institution behind them. It develops the argument through cases of AI-assisted peer review and concealed AI use in creative work, exposing limits of disclosure rules.

entry.title: C3M: Cross-Session Multimodal Memory Maintenance for Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Xueshu Chen, Yan Wang, Zihao Xue, Jiefu Li, Zhenfang Liu, Jayden Chen, Zhen Bi, Jungang Lou

entry.summary: C3M organizes cross-session multimodal memory for long-horizon agents, maintaining a bounded active index over persistent source text-image evidence with relation-aware updates that consolidate redundant records while preserving complementary and incompatible ones. At query time, budgeted routing selects index pages and expands source evidence under a fixed reader budget, preserving provenance. It targets the problem that compression can discard fine-grained visual cues or conflate similar but incompatible observations.

entry.title: Certified Task-Conditioned Active Observability

author.name: Linzhe Zhang, Changming Xu

entry.summary: The paper formalizes task-conditioned active observability: the minimum worst-case expected interaction cost to identify task-relevant states of an unobservable physical system under certified error and safety constraints. It addresses when passive observations cannot break latent degeneracies, when interventions are necessary, and when an agent should abstain.

entry.title: TOLA: Text-aware One-Step Latent Adaptation for Diffusion-based Text Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Yike Xu, Yue Shi, Yong Guo, Jiezhang Cao

entry.summary: TOLA replaces multi-step diffusion for text image super-resolution with a one-step latent adaptation framework, avoiding the error-reinforcement loop where an incorrect text prior gets repeatedly injected and amplified into semantically wrong characters. This cuts inference latency substantially while improving fidelity of recovered text.

entry.title: Segment-Level Risk Discovery in Online Handwriting for Alzheimer's Disease Detection

author.name: Changqing Gong, Huafeng Qin, Moun\^im A. El-Yacoubi

entry.summary: Introduces NormPaST-Risk, a normative state-space network that reformulates Alzheimer's detection from online handwriting as discovery of local disease-relevant segments rather than whole-trajectory classification. This segment-level formulation aims for better interpretability and robustness to writing style and acquisition noise.

entry.title: Generative Evolutionary Design of Voxel-Based Soft Robots with Provable Optimality

author.name: Junru Song, Huan Xiao, Yang Yang, Guozhen Li, Wei Peng, Xiaoya Zhang, Tingsong Jiang, Weien Zhou, Ying Wen, Feifei Wang, Wen Yao

entry.summary: Develops MISCO, an evolutionary framework combining an estimation-of-distribution algorithm with a position-aware, multi-task variational autoencoder to optimize voxel-based soft robot designs, with theoretical optimality guarantees. The design targets the vast design spaces and expensive evaluations that make VSR optimization difficult.

entry.title: CATCH: Counterfactual Anatomical Tissue Inpainting with Conditional Haar Diffusion

author.name: Simon Winther Albertsen, Hjalte Bjoernstrup, Said Djafar Said, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi

entry.summary: Presents CATCH, a conditional 3D diffusion model in an invertible Haar-wavelet domain for BraTS-style local synthesis that replaces tumor regions in brain MRI with plausible tumor-free tissue while preserving observed anatomy via hard compositing and a hole-focused loss. It systematically compares masking strategies including tumor-component augmentation and weighted mask mixtures.

entry.title: Graph, Loop, and Harness Engineering for Zero-Trust Agentic Data Engineering and Analytical Processing

author.name: Sagar Srinivas Sakhinana, Venkataramana Runkana

entry.summary: Presents two zero-trust frameworks for LLM agents in cloud data workflows: one generating and verifying complete data-engineering solutions from natural language, and one for governed OLAP analytics where production promotion requires evidence-bound validation including same-snapshot execution. Completion is conditioned on repository, deployment, runtime, and policy evidence.

entry.title: ReCalMatch:Reliability-Calibrated Semantic Guidance for Semi-Supervised Fine-Grained Recognition

author.name: Yundi Hong, Hongyang He, Zheng Fang, Xuanyu Liu, Victor Sanchez

entry.summary: Proposes ReCalMatch, which improves semi-supervised fine-grained recognition by using semantic compatibility from textual representations to calibrate pseudo-label reliability, rather than relying solely on classifier confidence signals that are blind to whether a predicted class is semantically compatible with the visual representation. This targets overconfident pseudo-label errors that consistency regularization otherwise reinforces.

entry.title: SEEK: Skill-Routed Evaluation with Evolvable Knowledge for Industrial Search

author.name: Zhongxin Huang, Songyang Li, Renzhe Zhou, Feiran Zhu, Chenglei Dai, Zhen Xiao, Xuanping Li, Jingwei Zhuo

entry.summary: Proposes SEEK, an LLM-based search quality evaluation system for industrial search that routes evaluation across specialized skills rather than packing all criteria into one prompt, and maintains evolvable knowledge bases to avoid costly retraining when evaluation rules change. This addresses criterion interference and rigid post-training approaches.

entry.title: ADATEX4D: adaptive texture capacity allocation for 4D gaussian splatting

author.name: De Jiang, Peiqiang Wang, Kehong Yuan, Shaohua Ma

entry.summary: AdaTex4D introduces adaptive texture-capacity allocation for deformation-based 4D Gaussian Splatting, giving each Gaussian packed RGBA triplanes whose resolution grows independently according to visibility-normalized screen-space gradients and deformed local scales. Experiments on N3DV and PanopticSports show more than half the texture storage is saved while preserving reconstruction quality, and quality improves under fixed memory budgets. This is a practical efficiency advance for dynamic 3D scene reconstruction.

entry.title: Automated Regulatory Compliance Question Answering in Financial Services with Domain-Adapted Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Tobias Deu{\ss}er, Abhishek Pillai, Aurelio F. Bariviera, Dhananjay Bhardwaj, Lorenz Sparrenberg, David Berghaus, Christian Bauckhage, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: This paper builds a domain-adapted RAG pipeline for compliance question answering in financial services, using a three-stage retriever on LegalBERT (entailment tuning, contrastive tuning, and BM25 score fusion) paired with compact on-premise-deployable generators. The work addresses the problem that compact models firms can realistically deploy are prone to hallucinating regulatory obligations, requiring verifiable grounding in authoritative rulebook text. It demonstrates a strong applied RAG recipe for a high-stakes domain.

entry.title: Does a model's stated reason for rejecting a candidate do any work?

author.name: Archit Rastogi

entry.summary: This paper tests whether a language model's stated reason for rejecting a candidate actually causally influences its choice: the author inserts a real corpus sentence stating the named missing fact into the rejected profile and re-asks under greedy decoding, with controls separating content from placement. Across six open models on 2WikiMultihopQA, supplying the named fact at the named profile moves the choice more than irrelevant controls, indicating stated reasons are not purely confabulated. This is a clever, judge-free probe of post-hoc rationalization in LLMs.

entry.title: To Trust or Not to Trust: Retrieval-Augmented Fact Checking in Speech

author.name: Debajyoti Mazumder, Mamta, Abhirama Subramanyam Penamakuri

entry.summary: The paper introduces VeriSpeak, a benchmark of 3,879 spoken claims for studying fact verification in large audio language models, testing whether verification ability transfers from text to speech and whether retrieval-augmented LALMs can use textual evidence to verify spoken claims. It finds a consistent gap between text and speech performance.

entry.title: Evaluating Cross-region Generalization for Wavelet-Diffusion Precipitation Downscaling

author.name: Weikang Qian, Yixin Wen, Chugang Yi, Zhi Li, Lingcheng Li, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: This study tests how well wavelet diffusion models for kilometer-scale precipitation downscaling generalize to unseen U.S. regions and precipitation regimes (convective, winter, tropical, atmospheric river). Models trained only on Oklahoma are compared against all-region training and interpolation baselines using MRMS radar data.

entry.title: A Concentration Bound for Two-Timescale Actor-Critic Algorithm

author.name: Prashansa Panda, Shalabh Bhatnagar

entry.summary: The paper derives a uniform all-time concentration bound for two-timescale actor-critic algorithms with function approximation in the average-reward setting, showing that after finite time the actor parameter enters a safe region and remains there with high probability. This complements existing asymptotic and non-asymptotic convergence analyses.

entry.title: TinyCardioUNet: IMU-to-ECG Translation with Graph-Encoded Inter-Axis Dependencies and Tensor Decomposition-Based Parameter Reduction

author.name: Seungwoo Han, Ingon Chanpornpakdi, Motoi Noda, Puwadej Leelasiri, Ibuki Hiruma, Toshihisa Tanaka

entry.summary: TinyCardioUNet is a lightweight UNet that reconstructs ECG signals from chest-worn IMU data, using a graph neural network to model inter-axis dependencies across all six IMU axes and tensor decomposition with variational Bayesian rank selection to compress parameters. It achieves RMSE 0.098 with only 36k parameters and is robust to noise. The work enables electrode-free continuous heart-rate monitoring on resource-constrained wearables.

entry.title: Lightweight Probabilistic Downscaling from a Deterministic Base Model

author.name: Joseph McLean, Tiffany Vlaar, Sigrid Passano Hellan, Linus Ericsson

entry.summary: This paper adapts recent training techniques from ML weather forecasting to build lightweight probabilistic downscaling models on a modified U-Net, evaluated on CORDEX-ML-Bench for temperature and precipitation across the Alps, New Zealand, and South Africa. It finds that a two-stage training curriculum improves results. Bringing uncertainty-aware, efficient downscaling to climate applications is valuable for regional climate impact studies.

entry.title: Active Client Selection in Federated Trajectory Prediction with Uncertainty-Awareness and Heterogeneous Complexity

author.name: Yiming Xie, Muzi Peng, Fei Miao, Ningfang Mi, Lili Su

entry.summary: This paper proposes active client selection methods for federated learning of autonomous-vehicle trajectory prediction, progressively incorporating per-client scene uncertainty and cross-scene complexity heterogeneity to prioritize informative clients. It addresses the practical problem that trajectory data is fragmented across regions and vehicles. Combining uncertainty estimation with client selection is a sensible, well-motivated contribution to applied FL.

entry.title: EvoTreeNAD: Genealogy-Guided Evolution for LLM-Driven Neural Architecture Discovery

author.name: Lishan Yu, Derek Jiu, Qizhen Lan, Xiaoqian Jiang

entry.summary: EvoTreeNAD is a genealogy-guided evolutionary algorithm in which LLM agents grow a persistent tree of neural architectures starting from an empty root, without a seed model or hand-designed search space. It addresses how to direct iterative LLM-driven design toward cumulative progress under costly evaluation.

entry.title: Decoupled Early Exits for Task-Dependent Compute Allocation in Flow-Matching VLAs

author.name: Riccardo Andrea Izzo, Rimvydas Rubavicius, Gianluca Bardaro, Subramanian Ramamoorthy, Matteo Matteucci, Alessandro Suglia

entry.summary: The paper proposes jointly configuring backbone depth, action-expert depth, and denoising steps in flow-matching vision-language-action models for adaptive compute allocation, noting prior work only exits early in the VLM backbone. This decoupling lets robot controllers trade compute across all three dimensions depending on task demands.

entry.title: Return or Revise? Learning When Revision Helps Retrieval-Augmented QA

author.name: Nicholas Kashani Motlagh, Tim Anderson, Jeremy Gwinnup, Grant Erdmann

entry.summary: Addresses the decision of whether to return a draft answer or revise it with retrieved evidence by introducing recoverability, a paired measure grading both the draft and its candidate revision under the same correctness judge. Policies trained to predict recoverability achieve better accuracy-revision-rate tradeoffs across 25,870 held-out questions and three revision setups.

entry.title: A Nearly Quadratic Lower Bound for Linear Optimization over Convex Bodies in the Membership Oracle Model

author.name: Santosh S. Vempala

entry.summary: This paper proves nearly quadratic lower bounds for randomized linear optimization and uniform sampling over convex bodies when access is via membership oracles. The linear optimization bound matches known upper bounds up to polylog factors, settling the complexity almost tightly, and the construction also yields improved lower bounds for uniform sampling and volume estimation.

entry.title: Large Language Models for Programming: Actually Fixing or Reimplementing Incorrect Code?

author.name: Alexandru Stefan Stoica, Traian Rebedea, Marian Cristian Mihaescu

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs truly repair buggy code or instead generate largely new solutions, by matching roughly 3000 buggy Codeforces submissions with their human-written fixes and measuring similarity between buggy code, LLM patches, and human patches. The study reveals a bias toward generating entirely new solutions rather than localized repairs.

entry.title: Confident but Wrong: A Constrained Decoding Diagnostic for Low-Resource Automatic Post-Editing

author.name: Isuru Wijesiri, Nisansa de Silva, Kavindu Warnakulasuriya, Aloka Fernando, Surangika Ranathunga

entry.summary: This paper introduces a black-box, inference-time diagnostic for automatic post-editing in low-resource languages that distinguishes whether more training would help or whether training data is too inconsistent to learn from, without retraining or annotation. The method varies an edit-distance penalty and reads the shape of the TER-vs-penalty curve plus constraint-variant orderings as diagnostic signals. It is a clever, practical tool for deciding when to invest further in APE systems.

entry.title: What, When, and How: Audio Description as Constrained Global Optimization

author.name: Igor Sterner, Mirella Lapata, Alex Lascarides, Frank Keller

entry.summary: This paper formalizes audio description generation for visually impaired audiences as a constrained optimization jointly deciding what visual content to narrate, when to insert narration without overlapping dialogue, and how to phrase it within available time - unlike prior local video-to-text systems. A hybrid system uses LLMs to propose and ground visual elements, estimate salience, and fit constraints. The coupled formulation is a meaningful advance over treating content and timing as pre-given.

entry.title: ARGUS: Role-Aware Event Knowledge Graphs for U.S. Employment-Discrimination Complaints

author.name: Sriram Kannan, Swetha Saseendran, Vishnu Vardhan Reddy Kandi, Leslie Barrett, Madhavan Seshadri, Enrico Santus

entry.summary: ARGUS builds document-level Event Knowledge Graphs from U.S. employment-discrimination complaints using a 5W1H-inspired schema, legal-domain models, and LLM-based structured generation over CourtListener data, capturing participant, temporal, and causal structure. Graph-structured classifiers outperform raw and lexical baselines on claim classification and legal QA, evaluated with human and multi-model assessment. It demonstrates concrete downstream utility of structured event representations in the legal domain.

entry.title: Spooftral: Can Voxtral Audio-Language Model Detect Speech Spoofing?

author.name: Avishai Weizman, Yehuda Ben-Shimol, Itshak Lapidot

entry.summary: This study probes whether the Voxtral audio-language model can detect speech spoofing attacks, extending countermeasure capabilities into the audio-language-model framework. The authors propose an instruction-guided approach using label-sequence likelihoods to distinguish bonafide from spoofed speech, finding that without task-specific adaptation the LLM layers emphasize semantics over spoof-discriminative cues. Experiments on ASVspoof databases show promise but highlight adaptation needs.

entry.title: Token Clustering and Semantic Sequence Mamba for Hyperspectral Image Classification

author.name: Yimin Zhu, Mahmood Elahi, Lincoln Linlin Xu

entry.summary: STMamba improves hyperspectral image classification by organizing tokens into semantically coherent sequences rather than predefined spatial neighborhoods, combining token clustering with a Mamba-based sequence model. A hierarchical encoder-decoder progressively selects semantic tokens to handle spectral-spatial heterogeneity. The design addresses limitations of existing vision state-space models in remote sensing.

entry.title: RGBD20K: A Large-Scale Benchmark for RGB-D Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Shaohua Dong, Zexuan Meng, Haiyan Sun, Bing Fan, Cuicui Zhang, Dylan Joseph, Kewei Sha, Yunhe Feng, Heng Fan

entry.summary: RGBD20K is a new RGB-D semantic segmentation dataset with 20,000 RGB-D image pairs and 160 fine-grained categories, far exceeding NYUv2 (40) and SUN RGB-D (37). It is designed to promote more generalizable segmentation models through expanded semantic coverage and scale.

entry.title: Recoverable Geographic Location Information in Earth-Observation Embeddings

author.name: Peiwen Zhang, Kristie Hu, Jovana Knezevic, Shunde Yin, Kyle Gao

entry.summary: The paper tests whether earth-observation foundation model embeddings (Tessera v1, Tessera v1.1, AlphaEarth) encode geographic coordinates, using 284 quality-verified European solar farms to link cosine and geodesic distances and predict projected EPSG:3035 coordinates. This probes both the value of location-aware information and privacy/generalization risks of geolocation leakage in EO representations.

entry.title: Industrial Anomaly Detection via Defect-Grounded Reasoning in Visual Latent Space

author.name: Jaron Yeh, Yen-Wei Chang, Jiang Liu, Shao-Yuan Lo

entry.summary: Anomaly-LR is a defect-grounded latent reasoning framework for multimodal industrial anomaly detection that first builds a global understanding and then performs fine-grained reasoning directly in visual latent space, avoiding iterative revisiting of image regions and preserving local defect evidence through the reasoning chain. It targets description, explanation, and reasoning over fine-grained defects with MLLMs.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Mesh-Guided Repair of Broken Vessels

author.name: Gniewosz Drwiega, Wojciech Szymanski, Marek Wodzinski

entry.summary: The paper proposes a post-processing framework that repairs connectivity errors in nnU-Net vessel segmentations by fitting a deformable template mesh in physical space as a geometric scaffold to guide conservative reconnection of disconnected components. This targets downstream analyses needing centerlines, branches, and graph structure.

entry.title: OceanXL: Large-scale Underwater 3D Gaussian Splatting via Block Partitioning and Adaptive Pruning

author.name: Haoran Wang, Shaoyu Cai, Adrian Azzarelli, Zhuodong Jiang, Guoxi Huang, Eng Tat Khoo, Brett Seymour, Fan Zhang, David Bull, Nantheera Anantrasirichai

entry.summary: OceanXL scales 3D Gaussian Splatting to large underwater scenes using divide-and-conquer block partitioning with global geometric consistency plus adaptive pruning to control memory. It addresses underwater challenges like light attenuation, scattering, and limited capture coverage for marine exploration and subsea inspection.

entry.title: Dynamical Diversity for Reservoir Computing in Reconfigurable Nanomechanics

author.name: Humayun Ahmed, In\^es S. Garcia, Filipa C. Mota, Muhammad Asim, Ghaith Mahook, Suleyman Celik, Yunus Selcuk, Filipe S. Alves, Alper Demir, M. Selim Hanay

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates reservoir computing using two interacting modes of a single NEMS resonator read through one port, introducing dynamical diversity by replaying the same input under different drive-amplitude allocations between modes and concatenating responses, expanding readout representational capacity without extra devices. It combines Duffing nonlinearity with fading memory in nanomechanics. It advances physical reservoir computing hardware efficiency.

entry.title: Human-in-the-Loop Geospatial Annotation for Rapid Dataset Construction in Field-Deployed UAV Systems

author.name: Morgan Masters, Nikolaas Bender, T. Luca Altaffer, Colleen Josephson, Steve McGuire

entry.summary: BirdsEye moves expert annotation out of images and into the field: a UAV operator records target world coordinates with RTK positioning, and calibrated projective geometry propagates each observation to all frames where the target is visible. The paper derives a first-order mapping from camera-pose uncertainty to pixel uncertainty, validated against Monte Carlo simulation, which doubles as a sensor design tool linking annotation requirements to hardware choices.

entry.title: CALM: Current Aligned Link Manipulation for Single Arm Oversized Object Lifting

author.name: Jun Hu, Sihan Chen, Kosta Jovanovic, David Navarro-Alarcon, Xueqian Wang, Jia Pan, Peng Zhou

entry.summary: CALM enables a single robot arm to lift oversized objects using whole-arm contacts (forearm, elbow) rather than just the end effector, learning long-horizon contact-rich manipulation with motor current as joint-load feedback. Three stage-specific policies trained with privileged simulation information handle repositioning, grasping, and lifting, sequenced by a stage router.

entry.title: A Tendon-Driven Robotic Jellyfish with Constrained Soft Actuation and Depth Control via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiarui Peng, Yutong Wu, Zelong Wang, Ping Deng, Xiaotian Zhang, Xian Chen, Kecheng Qin, Zhongyi Li

entry.summary: The authors build a tendon-driven soft robotic jellyfish whose constrained actuators achieve bending up to 150 degrees with a nearly linear displacement-bending relationship, enabling stable swimming, attitude adjustment, and self-righting with eight actuators. On top of this linear actuation they train a reinforcement-learning controller for closed-loop depth regulation in both simulation and hardware. The work combines bioinspired soft hardware with learned control.

entry.title: Coupled State-Space Modelling, Control, and Policy Distillation for Hybrid Rigid-Pneumatic Manipulators

author.name: Alan Royce Gabriel Samuel, Pulkit Verma

entry.summary: This paper derives a coupled state-space model for hybrid manipulators that combine motorized rigid joints with pressure-actuated Kresling origami segments, including pneumatic chamber dynamics and crease hysteresis. Using this model, the authors quantify for the first time the cost of the commonly used decoupled per-DOF control approximation, showing that decoupled control fails precisely on strongly coupled joints while a coupled model-based controller achieves substantially better tracking, and they distill the model into policies for practical control.

entry.title: Combining Evasive and Braking Reactions for Safety Reference Models in Automated Vehicles

author.name: Riccardo Don\`a, Konstantinos Mattas, Biagio Ciuffo

entry.summary: The paper proposes FSM-H, a hybrid Fuzzy-Safety Model that integrates longitudinal braking mitigation and lateral evasive steering within a unified behavioral model of careful human drivers. Braking is governed by Proactive Fuzzy Safety metrics while steering is driven by a criticality metric for lane changes, coordinated through a finite-state structure. Such models support scenario-based safety evaluation of automated driving systems, filling the gap left by braking-only reference models.

entry.title: From Target Selection to Digging: A Learning-Based Framework for Continuous Autonomous Excavation

author.name: Shuai Zhao, Ji-an Pan, Quantao Yang, Zheng Wang, Chaoyi Chen, Qing Xu, Keqiang Li

entry.summary: This framework enables continuous autonomous excavation by coupling terrain-aware target selection from LiDAR elevation maps with learned motion controllers. A shared task-conditioned RL policy handles waypoint-guided approach and loaded transport while an imitation-learning policy learns vision-based digging and lifting from expert demonstrations, with an architecture coordinating successive excavation cycles as the pile geometry evolves. The system addresses the full loop from target selection through digging.

entry.title: A Procedure for Classifying Attachments and Affective Social Bonds in Human-Robot Dyads

author.name: Imran Khan, Elisabeth Blagrove

entry.summary: The paper proposes a standardized four-question procedure, grounded in developmental, ethological, and neuroendocrine criteria, for classifying human-robot ties as attachment, affective social bond, or no relationship. It critiques HRI research for using these terms without the behavioral and physiological criteria that give them meaning in their source disciplines. This aims to rein in overclaiming and methodological divergence in HRI studies.

entry.title: Driving Epidemic Models with AI Agents: the Epydemix Agent Framework

author.name: Nicol\`o Gozzi, Ciro Cattuto, Alessandro Vespignani

entry.summary: The Epydemix Agent Framework adds an agent-facing layer over the Epydemix epidemic modeling library, providing model discovery, preventive validation of declarative scenario specifications, execution through tested library code, and result inspectability. This design lets LLM agents run rigorous stochastic compartmental models while keeping reliability grounded in the underlying library. It is a careful pattern for safe LLM-driven scientific computing.

entry.title: Wearable ECG Quality Assessment: A Deep Learning and Ambulatory Context-Awareness Approach

author.name: Xiaopeng Mao, Marike Weisbjerg, Sadasivan Puthusserypady

entry.summary: The paper introduces a deep learning signal quality assessment model that distinguishes clean from noisy ambulatory ECG recordings, trained on CACHET-CADB, claimed to be the first ambulatory ECG database with both physical and patient-reported contextual data. The model shows stable cross-database performance and is used to investigate how contextual data explains complicated ECG noise. Reliable quality assessment is a prerequisite for trustworthy wearable-based cardiac monitoring.

entry.title: Evidence-Driven Differential Diagnosis of Malignant Melanoma

author.name: Naren Akash, Anirudh Kaushik, Jayanthi Sivaswamy

entry.summary: Proposes a modular multi-level framework for melanoma differential diagnosis that integrates lesion, patient, and population-level evidence, including an anatomic-site-aware masked transformer that models all lesions in a patient and learnable demographic embeddings for population statistics. The work explores how different information types influence decisions and metric tradeoffs.

entry.title: BridgeMem: Causal Dyadic Transition Residuals for Temporal Knowledge Graph Forecasting

author.name: Zeyan Li, Libing Chen, Shengda Zhuo, Yin Tang, Jianfeng Xu

entry.summary: BridgeMem forecasts future facts in temporal knowledge graphs by estimating pair-specific transition evidence (how prior relations between an actor and candidate change the odds of a target relation) as a residual added to a frozen full-vocabulary forecaster's log scores. It encodes relation, direction, and lag features of prior pair events into a likelihood-ratio correction with support-adaptive calibration.

entry.title: Limited Structural Reliability in Public Educational Prediction Benchmarks: A Four-Dimension Audit of Seven Datasets

author.name: Yan Ma, Lizhuo Zhang

entry.summary: This paper audits seven public educational prediction datasets using four pre-modeling reliability checks (baseline gap, split instability, null separation, metadata adequacy under group-aware holdout), finding only three pass all checks, with cross-group fragility the dominant failure mode. One dataset's initial failure was traced to group-identifier feature leakage and corrected, demonstrating the audit's diagnostic value. This highlights serious reliability problems in a widely used benchmark domain.

entry.title: Predicting Symptoms of Amotivation and Anhedonia among University Students with a Novel Oversampling Method

author.name: Dang Nguyen, Bao Duong, Arun Kumar, Dat Phan-Trong, Julian Berk, Taylor Braund, Kien Do, Debopriyo Bal, Wu Yi Zheng, Leonard Hoon, Jill Newby, Helen Christensen, Svetha Venkatesh, Alexis Whitton, Sunil Gupta

entry.summary: Develops a machine learning approach with a novel oversampling technique to identify university students with prominent amotivation and anhedonia symptoms, which are frequently undetected but highly debilitating. The goal is enabling earlier, more targeted mental health intervention despite severe class imbalance in symptom severity labels. This connects imbalanced-learning methodology to a concrete public health application.

entry.title: PTC-Bias: Phoneme-Level Temporal Competition for Bias Retrieval and Post-Decoding Correction in Speech LLMs

author.name: Zhiqi Ai, Han Cheng, Shiyi Mu, Yongjin Zhou, Shugong Xu

entry.summary: PTC-Bias is a two-stage contextual biasing framework for speech LLMs that performs frame-synchronous phoneme decoding at prefill to produce a compact bias-word shortlist with speech intervals, then applies selective post-decoding correction via a second local competition. This reduces near-homophone and segmentation errors while preserving correct transcriptions when using large bias lists.

entry.title: FounRef: Robust, Structure-Preserving, and Fast Metric Refinement of Frozen Monocular Foundation Priors with Sparse Anchors

author.name: Dan Halperin, Mirko M\"ahlisch

entry.summary: FounRef is a training-free method that aligns frozen monocular depth foundation priors with sparse metric anchors to produce dense metric depth, instantiated with MoGe-2 priors and LiDAR anchors. Its modular design lets the depth prior, anchor source, and refinement solver be swapped independently, aiming to combine accuracy, geometric fidelity, and speed without full depth-completion training.

entry.title: Anatomy-Aligned Surface Field Learning for Myocardial Reconstruction from Sparse Short-Axis Cine MRI

author.name: Xiaohan Yuan, Xuan Yang, Qingya Li, Yangang Wang, Lei Li

entry.summary: The paper parameterizes epicardial and endocardial surfaces on a shared circumferential-longitudinal UV domain, converting irregular 3D myocardial reconstruction into structured coordinate-field completion with cross-subject and cross-phase correspondence. It enables 4D reconstruction from sparsely sampled short-axis cine MRI.

entry.title: ReVNM: Learning-Based Visual Navigation from a Remote Camera

author.name: Michikuni Eguchi, Kohei Honda, Masafumi Endo, Yasuhiro Yoshimura, Ryo Yonetani

entry.summary: ReVNM is a visual navigation model that uses a single remote surveillance camera as both observation source and implicit environmental map, eliminating pre-built maps and onboard vision processing. The paper addresses the limited field of view and the scarcity of diverse remote-viewpoint training data to achieve collision-free long-range navigation.

entry.title: Control the Harness, Control the Cost: Routing and Governing AI Coding Agents in the Enterprise

author.name: Arian Abbasi, Alan Aqrawi, Ted Kwartler

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how AI coding-agent harnesses (products like Claude Code and Codex) make cost-determining choices about model routing, context, prompt caching, and subagents, and builds a customizable router in which a calibrated classifier labels prompts to control spend at enterprise scale. It reframes harness configuration as an economic governance lever. The perspective is practically valuable for organizations scaling agent deployments.

entry.title: The Last Human Gate: Forward Deployed Engineering for Governance Automation

author.name: Jeremy Canale

entry.summary: The paper develops a task-substitution framework for enterprise governance automation, treating each governance gate as an executable contract with conditions on information accessibility, decision and authority checks, and net reduction of human work after accounting for exceptions and maintenance. It derives a residual-work threshold showing automating most cases can still increase labor, and introduces DGF-Bench for controlled evaluation.

entry.title: Operator Packages, Proposer Strength, and Construction-Family Plateaus in Office-Scale Verified Search

author.name: Roberto I. Ono Filho

entry.summary: Instruments a minimal FunSearch-style verified search loop using a local 30B model on a laptop, running a full 2^3 factorial ablation of proposer-side operator packages (a schematic notebook, named obstacles, and behavioral repulsion from prior constructions) across nine construction problems. The composition closes more of the seed-to-record gap, providing rare controlled evidence on what drives verified search improvements.

entry.title: Revalidation Beats Stateful Routing for Scientific Surrogates Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Harshil Lodhiya

entry.summary: Introduces RegimeShift-Surrogates, a large reproducible streaming benchmark (30,720 model fits across eight tasks, shifting regimes, and diverse surrogates including KANs) for model selection under distribution shift, and shows that simply revalidating candidate models on each new batch outperforms stateful adaptive routing controllers for scientific surrogates.

entry.title: Spectral Graph Neural Networks with Hermite Polynomials: A Comprehensive Study

author.name: Shuang Wu

entry.summary: The paper proposes HermNet, a spectral graph neural network using normalized Hermite propagation with a nodewise predictor that requires neither eigendecomposition nor a learned basis. It analyzes how different complete polynomial bases spanning the same filter space yield different optimization behavior under limited training budgets, via controlled synthetic experiments.

entry.title: Residual Correlation as a Diagnostic for Joint-Uncertainty Gains from GP Coregionalisation

author.name: Fangqin Zhou, Joaquin Vanschoren

entry.summary: Studies multi-output Gaussian processes with coregionalisation (GP-ICM) and finds that their main benefit is joint uncertainty quantification rather than point prediction, and that raw target correlation does not predict when coupling helps. Instead, residual correlation — cross-target dependence unexplained by independent per-target predictors — is the strongest predictor of joint-uncertainty gains, leading to a lightweight diagnostic based on a log-determinant quantity. This gives practitioners a principled test for when to use multi-output GPs.

entry.title: Sufficiently Reduced Distributional Regression

author.name: Alexander Henzi, Tiange Liu, Xinwei Shen
