entry.summary: SRDR combines conditional distribution estimation with nonlinear sufficient dimension reduction by characterizing sufficiency through strictly proper scoring rules, turning dimension reduction into risk minimization via the energy score. The framework trains a reduction map and generative predictor jointly, without density evaluation or adversarial training, and extends to multivariate settings.

entry.title: Does per-frame early exit pay? A compute-matched study of dynamic depth for on-device speech enhancement

author.name: Cl\'ement Laroche, Riccardo Miccini

entry.summary: Examines whether per-frame early-exit dynamic-depth networks pay off on devices that only accelerate static int8 graphs, supervising every intermediate depth of a causal model and fine-tuning output heads so deeper outputs are never worse. The derived family of static models achieves up to 0.11 higher PESQ at equal compute and matches best PESQ with 30% less compute, outperforming from-scratch counterparts.

entry.title: Script Choice in LLMs: Evidence for Late-Layer Commitment

author.name: David Kletz, Sandra Mitrovi\'c, Itay Sabato, Ljiljana Dolami\'c, Fabio Rinaldi

entry.summary: Using logistic regression probing and logit-lens analysis, this paper shows that LLMs encode input and instructed output scripts in early layers but commit to the actual output script only in the final layers, with intermediate representations defaulting to Latin. This two-stage process helps explain weaker script-following performance in non-Latin scripts.

entry.title: A Native-Reference Phone-Class Geometry for Second-Language Pronunciation Analysis

author.name: Tina Raissi, Nhan Phan, Chenxiao Wang, Mikko Kurimo

entry.summary: The paper proposes an interpretable method for measuring second-language pronunciation deviation using a native-reference phone-class geometry built by averaging frame-level self-supervised representations per context-dependent phone class and applying SVD. It requires no pronunciation labels, read-aloud prompts, or matched native-L2 recordings of the same text, making it broadly deployable for automatic speaking assessment. The approach yields interpretable pronunciation quality measures beyond holistic scores.

entry.title: MEVL-STP: Multi-Encoder and Vision Language Model for Arbitrarily Shaped Scene Text Spotting

author.name: Aman Anand, Partha Pratim Roy, Shivakumara Palaiahnakote

entry.summary: MEVL-STP is a two-stage scene text spotting pipeline using six frozen vision encoders (CLIP, DINOv2, SigLIP, EVA-CLIP, SAM, ConvNeXt) fused via a hierarchical FPN with channel attention for detection, followed by VLM-based recognition. The design decouples detection and recognition to prevent localization errors from propagating into recognition for curved and multi-oriented text. Experiments show strong performance on arbitrarily shaped text instances.

entry.title: AdaPilot: Towards Scene-Adaptive Policy Learning for Cross-Generator Text-to-Image Quality Optimization

author.name: Wenjin Liu, Fayuan Ke, Yue Lu, Zhe Cui, Anh Tuan Luu, Haoran Luo

entry.summary: AdaPilot formulates multi-turn text-to-image quality optimization as an MDP and learns a scene-adaptive policy via end-to-end reinforcement learning that is decoupled from generator internals, enabling cross-generator transfer. It aims to generalize beyond generator-specific fine-tuning and prompt optimization strategies.

entry.title: DA-GRD: Decision-Aware Grasp-Relevant Disambiguation for tactile recovery under perception-to-execution mismatches

author.name: Haoran Wang (Michael), Yuteng Sun (Michael), Yuanjie Li (Michael), Ruofei Bai (Michael), Meng Yee (Michael), Chuah, Wenyu Liang, Jun Li, Wei-Yun Yau

entry.summary: DA-GRD handles grasp poses that become stale when an object moves between perception and execution, maintaining a weighted planar belief over object configurations and selecting tactile probes that best eliminate hypotheses while improving agreement among candidate task grasps. It stops early once remaining hypotheses support a common executable grasp rather than fully relocalizing the object.

entry.title: Where are the Cognitive-Science based Safety Researchers?

author.name: alexfeghhi

entry.summary: A position piece arguing that AI safety research neglects the Bayesian cognitive-science paradigm (e.g., Josh Tenenbaum's work on efficient compositional world models and Dileep George's neuroscience-aligned approaches), which could matter if LLMs hit information-efficiency constraints and AGI depends on different architectural principles. The author proposes studying values as a function of world models and innate rewards.

entry.title: CRISS: A Retrieval-Augmented AI Chatbot for Assisting Cancer Registrars

author.name: Vani Seth, Mohammad Beheshti, Anirudh Kambhampati, Vishwa Bhayani, Lucinda Ham, Prasad Calyam, Iris Zachary

entry.summary: CRISS is a retrieval-augmented conversational assistant built on a domain-specific knowledge base of national cancer registry standards, providing citation-supported answers to help oncology data specialists interpret complex coding and staging rules. The study evaluates accuracy, citation support, and usefulness for training and helpdesk scenarios while keeping humans in the loop for final decisions.

entry.title: Policy as Code: A Coroutine-Bridge Harness for Fast-Reasoning Reliability on CAR-bench

author.name: Ivan Matveev

entry.summary: The paper presents a coroutine-bridge harness in which a tool-using agent emits a Python program that blocks and resumes across evaluator tool exchanges, decoupling model invocation count from tool round-trips. On CAR-bench the agent uses a median of two model calls across seven agent turns per task, with median 1.8 seconds of model latency on Cerebras hardware.

entry.title: CrossScale-GLIO: Topology-Preserving Vision-Language Alignment of MRI and Whole-Slide Histopathology for Diffuse Glioma

author.name: Yantong Liu, Zheyu Zhang, Runpeng Liu, Mu Xitang, Seong-Yoon Shin, Hyun-Ae Lee

entry.summary: CrossScale-GLIO aligns MRI tumor-habitat graphs with histology cell-niche graphs using structure-aware optimal transport anchored by diagnostic language, for glioma subtyping and biomarker prediction. It reports solid metrics including subtype macro-F1 of 0.789 and IDH AUROC of 0.934, plus cross-modal patient retrieval results, on paired and external cohorts.

entry.title: NumericJev: Jev-like LLM Numerical Decoding with Multiway Decision Trees

author.name: Weiwei Ye, Hangchen Liu, Renhe Jiang

entry.summary: NumericJev is a training-free decoding algorithm that elicits numerical output at requested precision from any LLM with a Jev-like structured-choice interface, recursively refining numeric ranges through multiway decision trees. Surprisingly, it outperforms direct selection from a candidate list containing the correct answer by 2.93 percentage points on an arithmetic benchmark.

entry.title: Design and Evaluation of LLM Chaining-Based Task Planning for General Purpose Service Robots

author.name: Lucas Da Mota Bruno, Jiahao Sim, Yoshinobu Hagiwara

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM chaining architecture for RoboCup@Home GPSR task planning that splits instruction classification and action generation into two stages, cutting per-inference prompt length by about 45 percent and mitigating context bloat and lost-in-the-middle effects. Evaluated on 100 generated commands across local open-source and frontier cloud models.

entry.title: Tag-Aware Structured Text Translation: Towards a Systematic Understanding

author.name: Zhanglin Wu, Hengchao Shang, Daimeng Wei, Jiaxin Guo, Zongyao Li, Tengfei Song, Ning Xie, Weidong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the trade-off between tag fidelity and translation fluency when LLMs translate tag-laden web text, and proposes a systematic approach spanning data synthesis, capability building, and multi-objective alignment, including a hybrid synthesis strategy called Hy-LST. It matters because structured-text translation affects real-world localization pipelines.

entry.title: ArGuard Shared Task: Harmful Content Detection in Arabic Memes and LLM Prompts

author.name: Firoj Alam, Md. Rafiul Biswas, Mohamed Bayan Kmainasi, Ali Ezzat Shahroor, Hamdy Mubarak, George Mikros, Abul Hasnat, Wajdi Zaghouani

entry.summary: ArGuard is a shared task on harmful content detection with two tracks: multimodal hate detection in Arabic memes and harmful prompt detection for Arabic LLM safety, drawing 35 participating teams. Best macro-F1 scores ranged from 0.419 (fine-grained memes, hardest) to 0.984, establishing baselines and resources for Arabic safety evaluation.

entry.title: RoboLDA: A Probabilistic Generative Model for Uncovering Embodied Hierarchical Structures in Voxel-based Soft Robots

author.name: Junru Song, Yang Yang, Jingdan Shi, Guozhen Li, Weien Zhou, Ying Wen, Feifei Wang, Wen Yao, Tingsong Jiang

entry.summary: Presents RoboLDA, a Bayesian probabilistic model that decomposes voxel-based soft robot morphology generation into a task-robot-organ-voxel hierarchy trained via variational inference, learning design principles purely from existing successful designs. This reduces reliance on domain expertise for hierarchical robot design.

entry.title: Investigating White Blood Cells as a Source of False-Positive Malaria Parasite Detection in African Blood-Smear Images

author.name: Samuel A. Adeniji, Goodness C. Obasi, Chris-Victor Ntwali, Aondana M. Iorumbur, Confidence Raymond, Lowami Uwimana, Ahmed Tahiru Issah

entry.summary: Tests the plausible hypothesis that white blood cells cause false positives in YOLOv12 malaria parasite detectors trained on the Lacuna dataset from Uganda and Ghana, running seven independent spatial and statistical analyses across two labeling regimes. All seven analyses refute the hypothesis, showing 95% of false positives are pure background detections unrelated to WBC locations.

entry.title: AT-SKM-Net: An Accelerated Trainable Sampling Kaczmarz-Motzkin Framework for Linear Hard-Constraint Feasibility on Dynamic Graphs

author.name: Xiaochen Zhang, Haoyu Zhu, Yao Zhang, Qingchun Hou

entry.summary: AT-SKM-Net accelerates the Trainable Sampling Kaczmarz-Motzkin Net framework for graph-structured optimization with massive strict linear constraints, using a topology-aware heterogeneous GNN to concentrate computation on active constraints and eliminating redundant matrix factorizations for dynamic environments. It retains feasibility guarantees while reducing computational cost. This targets critical-infrastructure optimization where scalability and hard-constraint satisfaction both matter.

entry.title: CARE: Condition-Aware Representation Regularization for Diffusion Models

author.name: Fengjia Guo, Zhuoyi Yang, Jie Tang

entry.summary: CARE is a lightweight plug-and-play regularization framework for diffusion models that modulates feature distributions dynamically based on similarity of built-in conditioning signals such as labels or text, promoting tighter feature clusters for similar conditions. It aims to improve sample quality and training efficiency while accounting for conditioning signals that prior regularization overlooks.

entry.title: Monitoring Urban Traffic Dynamics at Fine Spatiotemporal Resolution Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Deep Learning

author.name: Hao Tian, Heng Cai, Xiaowei Chen, Yifan Yang

entry.summary: The paper shows that distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) on existing underground fiber-optic cables, combined with deep learning, can provide passive, privacy-preserving urban traffic monitoring at meter-level spatial and second-level temporal resolution. It evaluates whether this DAS-plus-DL pipeline can serve as a continuous urban traffic observatory.

entry.title: Sample-Weighted End-to-End Trace-Norm Geometry for Multitask Learning

author.name: Mahdi Mohammadigohari

entry.summary: This paper derives exact empirical Rademacher complexity for a sample-size-weighted trace norm of the end-to-end map from task coefficients to input-space predictors in multitask learning, avoiding separately controlled products of representation and task terms that can discard relative orientation. The generalization theory is more intrinsic to the represented predictors. It advances multitask generalization theory with a cleaner, transformation-invariant complexity measure.

entry.title: Classifier-Dependent Benefits of Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Android Malware Attribution

author.name: Md Rafid Islam, Zahid Hasan, Hafiz Abdur Rahman

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates pseudo-labeling semi-supervised learning across six classifiers on the CICMalDroid 2020 dataset with statistical significance testing, finding that SSL benefits are strongly classifier-dependent, with SVM showing the largest significant gain (+4.4% accuracy). It addresses the high cost of expert-labeled malware data under class imbalance. A useful caution against assuming SSL gains transfer uniformly across model families in security applications.

entry.title: Spatio-temporally complementary feature propagation on graphs for longitudinal AADT estimation

author.name: Linghang Sun, Qishen Zhou, Michail A. Makridis, Anastasios Kouvelas

entry.summary: Proposes a spatio-temporally complementary feature propagation framework for estimating Annual Average Daily Traffic across an entire urban network over multiple years, fusing spatially sparse but temporally dense loop-detector data with spatially complete but temporally sparse macroscopic model outputs. The method formulates propagation on directed graphs as Poisson energy minimization with residues. It addresses a real infrastructure planning problem where physical sensors are expensive and sparse.

entry.title: Functional dynamic mode decomposition: Learning infinite-dimensional systems from data

author.name: Stefan Klus, Eirini Ioannou

entry.summary: The paper extends dynamic mode decomposition to infinite-dimensional systems by working in function spaces rather than discretizing the spatial domain first, avoiding the bias introduced by finite difference or finite element grids. This functional viewpoint broadens DMD applicability to PDE-governed systems across physics, climate, and engineering.

entry.title: Optimal Recovery Meets Bayesian Learning: Where Worst-Case Bounds Pay Off

author.name: Gordei Verbii

entry.summary: The paper sharpens the correspondence between worst-case optimal recovery and Bayesian Gaussian-process learning, showing the radius of information equals nugget-optimized GP posterior variance attained at the posterior mean. It then empirically evaluates where worst-case calibration rules pay off across three published Bayesian systems, finding Morozov calibration is more reproducible and backend-robust than sigma-blind selection rules.

entry.title: Elucidating the Conformal Structure of the Brinkman Penalisation Method for Geometry-Adapted, Structure-Preserving Operator Learning of Hamiltonian PDEs

author.name: Teo Deveney, Baige Xu, Takaharu Yaguchi

entry.summary: Shows that multi-symplectic Hamiltonian PDEs regularized by Brinkman penalisation retain a multi-conformal symplectic structure under a compatibility condition, yielding exact local conservation laws with exponential decay inside the solid region. This provides theoretical grounding for geometry-adapted, structure-preserving operator learning on complex domains.

entry.title: AERIAL: Adversarial Evaluation of Robustness in Accuracy-Preserving Low-Precision EEG Decoders

author.name: Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: Systematically compares FP32, pruned, and quantized (INT8 PTQ and QAT) EEG decoding models under white-box adversarial attacks on BCI Competition IV-2a, finding that accuracy-preserving compression does not improve direct robustness, with PGD accuracy remaining around 22-24% across compression regimes. Simulated quantization enables gradient analysis while native TensorRT deployment validates the findings.

entry.title: Benchmarking Argumentative Behaviour of LLMs: A Study of Defences Against Character Attacks

author.name: Ewelina Gajewska, Katarzyna Budzynska, Jaroslaw Chudziak

entry.summary: The authors benchmark whether LLMs can strategically use and respond to ad hominem (character) attacks in persuasive dialogue, a skill important in political debate where ethos rivals propositional content. They mine human defensive strategies from political dialogues, formalize them as a dialogue game, and empirically evaluate LLM competence against this structure.

entry.title: What a Cross-Model Fixed-Point Census Can and Cannot Arbitrate About Repetition

author.name: Nicol\'as Vera Z\'u\~niga

entry.summary: The paper examines two competing explanations for neural text degeneration - repetition in training data versus learned copying circuits - via an observational census of fixed-point structure in the argmax map across 17 off-the-shelf pretrained models. It carefully delineates what this measurement can and cannot arbitrate between the hypotheses. This is a thoughtful methodological contribution to the study of text degeneration in language models.

entry.title: A Training Criterion with Token-Level Tolerance to Transcription Ambiguity for Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Saurabh Kumar, Diptiman Mohanta, Prasanta Kumar Ghosh

entry.summary: The paper refines Omni-temporal Classification by moving wildcard arcs from word-level to token-level granularity in the CTC alignment graph, allowing unsupported tokens to be bypassed while preserving supervision for the rest of a word, and combining token- and word-level arcs complementarily. This provides finer tolerance to transcription ambiguities in nominally verbatim ASR training data. The result is a training criterion better matched to noisy reference transcripts.

entry.title: SEE Challenge 2026: Event-Guided Brightness Adjustment Across a Broad Illumination Range

author.name: Yunfan Lu, Mingchao Xu, Hanyu Zhou, Shaoyu Liu, Haoyue Liu, Peiqi Duan, Shihan Peng, Yinqiang Zheng, Boxin Shi, Gim Hee Lee, Hui Xiong, Davide Scaramuzza

entry.summary: This report describes the SEE Challenge 2026, organized with an ECCV 2026 event-based vision workshop, benchmarking event-guided brightness adjustment using SEE-600K with 610,126 image-event observations from 202 real scenes spanning illumination variations up to 1000x. It defines an open-system protocol conditioning restoration on RGB frames, synchronized events, and a target-brightness statistic.

entry.title: Dense Coverage, Sparse Refinement: Byte-Constrained Cooperative Perception

author.name: Melih Yazgan, Timon M\"uller, J. Marius Z\"ollner

entry.summary: For bandwidth-constrained V2X cooperative perception, the paper proposes a coverage-refinement scheme where each agent sends a highly compressed coarse full-BEV layer and spends the remaining byte budget on selected high-resolution patches ranked by a Task-Aware Benefit Selector estimating downstream utility. This balances dense context coverage with sparse high-value refinement.

entry.title: Long-Tail Adaptive Flow Matching with Explicit Conditional Consistency Guidance for Precise Multimodal Face Synthesis

author.name: Yushe Cao, Xuechao Zou, Xing Xi, Dianxi Shi, Chun Yu, Junliang Xing

entry.summary: EC2Face is a multimodal face synthesis framework that replaces implicit latent-space alignment in diffusion models with explicit semantic supervision and distribution-aware flow matching to handle long-tailed mask distributions. It targets precise correspondence between generated faces and conditioning inputs, especially for rare attributes.

entry.title: EndoFSA: Endoscopic Few-Shot Image Generation via Rank-Constrained Parameter Adaptation

author.name: Panagiota Gatoula, Grigoris Karypidis, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: EndoFSA is a GAN-based framework for few-shot synthetic image generation in wireless capsule endoscopy, designed to address the underrepresentation of pathological findings in gastrointestinal imaging data. It adapts a generator pretrained on abundant normal imagery using rank-constrained parameter updates, aiming to preserve anatomical priors while introducing realistic pathological variation without the instability and overfitting that come from training on scarce abnormal samples.

entry.title: Training-Free Hold-Usage Detection in Sport Climbing with Foundation Pose Models

author.name: Abu Bakar, Abdullah Aftab, Amir Hamza

entry.summary: The paper shows that a frozen off-the-shelf pose foundation model (Sapiens) with fingertip/toe keypoints, per-frame proximity tests, per-limb exclusion, and temporal-persistence rules can detect climbing hold usage without task-specific training. This avoids issues with wrist/ankle keypoint offsets and hand occlusion in prior approaches.

entry.title: Free-Init: Scan-Free, Motion-Free, and Correspondence-Free Initialization for Doppler LiDAR-Inertial Systems

author.name: Mingle Zhao, Jiahao Wang, Tianxiao Gao, Chengzhong Xu, Hui Kong

entry.summary: Free-Init is a plug-and-play initialization framework for LiDAR-inertial systems that fuses per-point Doppler velocity with inertial measurements under non-inertial kinematics, eliminating the need for scan motion undistortion, excitation motions, and map correspondences. It is a companion work to FMCW-LIO by the same group. Robust, fast online initialization is a practical pain point for deployed SLAM systems.

entry.title: Simple Torque-Observation Alignment for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Grasping with a Direct-Drive Gripper

author.name: Doyoung Kim, Edgar Lee, Hyeonsun Park, Chunghyeon Lee, Chihyun Han, Uisu Hwang, Seokhwan Jeong

entry.summary: A three-step torque observation alignment method for direct-drive grippers: dynamometer calibration of the torque constant, using torque deltas instead of raw torque to eliminate domain-dependent offset bias, and Gaussian noise matching from measured data. This enables zero-shot sim-to-real transfer of RL grasping policies that rely on torque observations.

entry.title: Modeling Load-, Velocity-, and Temperature-Dependent Transmission Errors of Cycloidal Drives for Industrial Robots Using Fourier Series

author.name: Christian J. E. Bauer, Valentin Kamm, Marcel Dzubba, Lukas Steinle, Armin Lechler, Alexander Verl

entry.summary: This paper models periodic transmission errors in cycloidal drives, the gearboxes commonly used in medium-to-heavy-payload industrial robots, using a Fourier series whose amplitude and phase depend on load torque, velocity, and temperature. Accurate error models could enable compensation that improves robot path accuracy for machining tasks. Experimental measurements validate the proposed model on a dedicated test rig.

entry.title: Dense-Joint-Based Obstacle-Aided Locomotion with a Joint-Repositionable Snake Robot

author.name: Kyosuke Minomo, Ryo Takahashi, Kotaro Yasui, Yasutaka Nakashima, Motoji Yamamoto, Ayato Kanada

entry.summary: This work studies how joint density affects obstacle-aided locomotion in snake robots using a mechanism that decouples actuators from joints, enabling high joint density along a fixed body length. Two experimental models with identical length but different joint densities are compared, showing that higher density reduces stagnation and jamming and better matches biological snakes' continuous obstacle contact. The findings guide future snake robot design.

entry.title: Singularity Analysis for the Perspective-Four and Five-Line Problems

author.name: Jorge Garc\'ia Font\'an, Abhilash Nayak, S\'ebastien Briot, Mohab Safey El Din

entry.summary: The paper determines camera-line configurations where pose estimation from four or five observed lines becomes singular, which causes control and stability problems in image-based visual servoing. Using computational algebraic geometry, the authors find configurations where all Jacobian minors vanish, proving for instance that a three-line singularity occurs when the camera lies on a hyperboloid defined by the lines. These results extend to characterize singular sets for four and five lines.

entry.title: Markerless Multi-Modal Autonomous Robotic Inspection of Large Space Structures

author.name: Juan De Dios Alfaro, Arturo R\'ios, David Rodr\'iguez-Mart\'inez, Carlos P\'erez-del-Pulgar

entry.summary: The paper presents a markerless autonomous robotic inspection pipeline for future orbital infrastructures, integrating a Kinova Gen2 manipulator with an end-effector sensor head combining RGB-D, thermal, and 2D LiDAR. 3D reconstruction serves as the inspection-support representation, removing reliance on fiducial markers, predefined trajectories, or accurate target models. This improves scalability for large, heterogeneous, or partially unknown space structures.

entry.title: First-Order Definable Policies

author.name: Vardhan

entry.summary: The post asks which finite-state reactive policies over observation histories can have their action rules expressed in first-order logic, connecting classical results of McNaughton, Papert, and Schutzenberger on first-order definability and finite automata to policy representations. It explains how finite observation histories can be read as logical structures and which automata-theoretic characterizations transfer. This is a literature review and formal exposition rather than new theorems.

entry.title: AI #187: Coming Into Play

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's weekly AI news roundup covering the Opus 5.5 release (GA September 22, 2026) and its system card, OpenAI's cheaper improved Sol and Luna models, the newly introduced Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act from Senators Sanders and Casar with MIRI's endorsement, and spin-off posts on embedded evaluators and cooperative alignment.

entry.title: Domain Recentering and Confidence-Weighted Prior Calibration for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Youngeun Seol, Jimin Shin, Heeseo Yoon, Uiwon Hwang

entry.summary: DRC is a training-free method for adapting CLIP under distribution shift that fits a Gaussian mixture once and subtracts posterior-weighted component means from embeddings, plus a confidence-weighted log-prior correction. It improves on prior feature calibration that applied a hard cluster bias, achieving strong zero-shot adaptation without per-sample optimization.

entry.title: Template Ageing and Longitudinal Verification in Fixed-Text Keystroke Dynamics: A Subject-Disjoint Study Across Eight Weeks

author.name: Simon Parkinson, Saad Khan, Na Liu, Qing Xu

entry.summary: Presents a controlled eight-week longitudinal study of keystroke-dynamics biometrics with 40 fixed passwords typed weekly, comparing scaled-Manhattan, gradient boosting, TypeNet-style, and TypeFormer-style models under subject-disjoint evaluation. Template ageing proves large and systematic, with error increasing monotonically with enrolment-to-query gap for every mechanism.

entry.title: Structured Pose-Conditioned Flow Matching for Generative 5G CSI Augmentation

author.name: Haojin Li, Anbang Zhang, Wai Ho Mow, Chenyuan Feng, Chen Sun, Haijun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes StructFlow-HPR, a pose-conditioned flow matching framework that generates 5G channel state information data for contactless human pose recognition, preserving CSI receiver-frequency topology via a reconstruction-preserving autoencoder. This addresses the scarcity and cost of large-scale synchronized CSI-pose pairs in practical 5G systems.

entry.title: Physics and Data Driven Transformer-Mamba Framework for Flow Field

author.name: Zhuo Zhang, Shun Zou, Canqun Yang, Xi Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces TM4FF, a physics-constrained operator learning framework for CFD combining a Residual Wavelet Mamba layer for denoising, Transformer-based attention for feature fusion, and a physics-informed loss using Fourier derivatives to enforce Navier-Stokes equations. Experiments on four CFD datasets show strong accuracy and generalization across flow conditions.

entry.title: Safety-oriented pedestrian trajectory prediction at urban intersections using time-to-collision and crossing-zone context

author.name: Erel Avineri, Yftach Gil, Yehudit Aperstein

entry.summary: Presents a trajectory-prediction framework for urban intersections that combines pedestrian motion history with time-to-collision information and crossing-zone indicators, evaluated on the inD dataset using pooled LSTM architectures with 1.6s observation and 2.4s prediction horizons. The goal is proactive road-safety applications where pedestrian motion depends on vehicle interactions. It adds safety-relevant context features to standard trajectory prediction pipelines.

entry.title: Algebraic Expressivity Certificates for Shallow Polynomial Neural Networks

author.name: Sepehr Akbari, Shahrzad Jamshidi

entry.summary: The paper studies exact representability by shallow polynomial neural networks using algebraic geometry, viewing width-r networks with power-d activations as sums of powers of linear forms whose closures are Veronese secant varieties. It implements an architecture-to-certificate pipeline that produces polynomial certificates of nonrepresentability, recovering classical determinantal and catalecticant equations for quadratics and higher degrees. This connects neural network expressivity questions to classical algebraic geometry tools.

entry.title: Learning and interpreting policies for simultaneous entanglement requests in quantum networks

author.name: Leon Rode, Sumeet Khatri, Supartha Podder

entry.summary: Formulates entanglement scheduling in future quantum networks as a Markov decision process and trains double deep Q-networks with Message Passing Neural Networks and experience replay to schedule link-level entanglement resources for simultaneous tasks across network regions. The work includes interpretability analysis of the learned policies.

entry.title: Predicting Emerging Topics from Outliers: A Prospective Study of Weak Signals in Embedding Space

author.name: Evangelia Zve, Gauvain Bourgne, Jean-Gabriel Ganascia

entry.summary: This study examines whether 'anticipatory outliers' — documents that embedding models initially classify as noise but which later found emerging topics — can be identified prospectively. Using trajectories of outlier documents to derive labels and confidence via cross-model agreement, the authors show anticipatory outliers can be predicted on two French news corpora.

entry.title: ChunkRank: Model-Aware Text Chunking and Abstention-Aware Answer Selection for LLM Pipelines

author.name: Amit Nautiyal, Ayush Bhatt, Gaurav Nautiyal

entry.summary: ChunkRank is an open-source Python library that derives chunk boundaries from a target model's tokenizer and context window and selects answers among candidates produced per chunk, shipping a validated registry of 90 models across 15 providers. The paper reports an informative negative result: no content-based ranker reliably beats baselines for answer selection on NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA, and HotpotQA. The token-exact chunking contribution is practical for multi-lingual RAG-style pipelines.

entry.title: From Passive Execution to Active Exploration: Agentic Embodied Manipulation in Realistic Environments

author.name: Shilin Ma, Chubin Zhang, Xulong Bai, Zifeng Gao, Shiyi Zhang, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: An agentic manipulation framework replacing passive execution with active environment exploration, using three collaborative modules for high-level planning, visual scene understanding, and low-level execution. It targets realistic scenarios involving textual semantic cues, distractors, and initially invisible targets that passive frameworks handle poorly.

entry.title: The promise and peril of using visual AI to study cities

author.name: Peter Dizikes | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT News coverage of new work and a book from the Senseable City Lab on visual AI for urban studies, including a study using machine learning to classify vehicles in 331 NYC traffic cameras and estimate per-vehicle emissions, illustrating how computer vision can turn city imagery into datasets for planning. The piece weighs these capabilities against growing privacy and fairness concerns.

entry.title: Agent Memory with Episodic Retrieval for Financial Decision-Making

author.name: Nuoyue Xu, Jiang Liu, Wenxuan Huang, Xiang Zhang, Juntai Cao, Jiaqi Wei

entry.summary: META is a memory-enhanced trading agent that combines specialized indicator agents (Trend, MACD, RSI, SMA, and others) with a decision agent that fuses their reports and an episodic-memory module retrieving relevant past episodes. It claims to be the first RAG-like episodic-memory-augmented multi-agent framework for financial decision-making. The work extends agent-based trading beyond stateless analysis.

entry.title: SGA: Uncertainty Quantification for Multi-Step Forecasting in Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Xin-Yu Hu, Shuang Liang, Cheng Feng, Shao-Qun Zhang

entry.summary: SGA quantifies uncertainty in multi-step forecasts from time series foundation models by characterizing the topology of branching forecast paths with a directed acyclic graph, then applying a slicing-graphing-alignment procedure. It targets the problem that different forecast branches exhibit varying reliability, undermining forecast credibility.

entry.title: Beyond Model Size: Redesigning LiSenNet for embedded speech enhancement

author.name: Cl\'ement Laroche, Rasmus Kongsgaard Olsson

entry.summary: Redesigns LiSenNet, a 37k-parameter sub-band dual-path speech enhancement model, for the STM32N6570-DK Neural-ART accelerator by replacing its recurrent bottleneck with convolutional frequency and temporal mixers and reformulating unsupported operators. The work highlights the gap between nominal parameter counts and actual deployability on restricted microcontroller NPUs.

entry.title: Clinical Knowledge Graphs for Chest X-Ray Device Reasoning

author.name: Harshil Lodhiya

entry.summary: The paper builds an uncertainty-aware clinical knowledge graph linking device instances, tip estimates, placement assessments, provenance, report events, and temporal evidence for chest X-ray device placement reasoning. It was evaluated on the full RANZCR CLiP test archive (30,083 studies, 3,255 patients, five outer folds), materializing over 900,000 evidence nodes and 884,549 typed relationships. The system bridges image geometry and structured report text, which existing image models and report processors handle separately.

entry.title: A Risk-Adaptive and Evidence-Constrained Framework for Generative AI Feedback in Programming Education

author.name: Shihao Wang

entry.summary: Develops a framework deciding when to intervene, with what evidence, and how much help to give in introductory programming, using 2993 failed submissions from 215 students and calibrated risk for capacity-limited feedback policies. The predictive model achieved modest performance (PR-AUC 0.550, ROC-AUC 0.681).

entry.title: Auditability Is Not One Property: Rule Overlap, Behavioural Agreement, and Composition in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Liu Hung Ming

entry.summary: The paper studies whether independently trained RL policies can be represented and composed through auditable discrete behavioral rules, decomposing auditability into six separately testable predicates including trace integrity, rule coverage, behavioral agreement, and composition quality. Using hash-bound ledgers, exact replay, and confidence-ranked arbitration, it finds strict limits on this decomposition approach.

entry.title: Neuralized Multi-Wavelet Decomposition for Time Series Classification and Forecasting

author.name: Xiaohan Jiang, Jingyuan Wang, Jiahao Ji, Yongyao Wang, Chen Yang, Junjie Wu

entry.summary: m-WCN neuralizes multi-wavelet decomposition in an end-to-end framework that jointly extracts temporal patterns and frequency structures, addressing the usual decoupling of time-domain and frequency-domain modeling in time series analysis. It targets finance, healthcare, and meteorology applications with multiscale characteristics.

entry.title: Anatomy-aware cross-speaker adaptation of complete vocal-tract acoustic-to-articulatory inversion

author.name: Nhat-Nam Nguyen, Pierre-Andre Vuissoz, Yves Laprie

entry.summary: Proposes a geometric adaptation framework for cross-speaker acoustic-to-articulatory inversion that uses anatomical landmarks on vertebrae and dental structures, applying affine transformation plus thin-plate spline deformation to map predicted vocal-tract contours to unseen speakers without retraining. Landmarks are identified from a single /u/ frame per speaker as a reference.

entry.title: R-DEIM Net: An Efficient Rationale-Augmented Dual-Expert Interaction Model for Paraphrase Detection

author.name: Pushp, Vaibhav Prajapati, Himangshu Sarma

entry.summary: R-DEIM Net is a 76M-parameter dual-expert architecture for paraphrase detection combining an Interaction Expert with multi-scale 2D convolutions and attention for token-level similarity, and a Reasoning Expert using a Flan-T5-small decoder to generate human-readable rationales. The paper explores whether moderate-scale models can match LLM accuracy on paraphrase detection while providing interpretable rationales. It occupies a sensible middle ground between efficient Siamese encoders and heavyweight LLMs.

entry.title: Response-state Learning for Transferable Vibrational Spectroscopic Characterization with Electron Prior

author.name: Zetong Li, Zhuosong Xie, Hengyu Fan, Jiaao Yu, Qiyao Hua, Zheng Lu, Liming Xu, Juanni Wu, Honglin Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces SENK, an SO(3)-equivariant neural Kalman network cascade for vibrational spectral prediction that combines an equivariant transformer backbone, a Kalman-style refinement bridge with reliability sensing, and an NBO-informed electronic prior with guided calibration. It outperforms DetaNet on QM9S and QMe14S benchmarks.

entry.title: Sequential Confidence Sets for Coverage-Constrained Conformal Model Selection

author.name: Jing Li, Haibin Zhu

entry.summary: The paper formulates the problem of selecting among multiple adaptive conformal forecasting pipelines that must satisfy hard coverage constraints, treating it as sequential inference for a stochastic constrained argmin. It introduces Coverage-Constrained Sequential Model Confidence Sets (CC-SMCS), which classify pipelines as certifiably feasible, possibly feasible, or possibly constrained-optimal using simultaneous martingale confidence sequences. This gives a principled statistical framework for a problem practitioners handle ad hoc.

entry.title: Continuous Online Fault Detection for Mobile Robots via Adaptive Edge Models

author.name: Jordan Levy, Nicolas Verstaevel, Vincent Talon, Benoit Gaudou

entry.summary: This paper uses teacher-student distillation, with a foundation model (TSPulse) generating pseudo-labels from fault-injected time series, to train a lightweight MiniRocket student adapted with recursive least squares for onboard real-time fault detection. The student achieves 4.30 ms CPU inference latency and is validated on both TSB-AD and a physical robot.

entry.title: Learning a Flow to Self-Supervised Representations

author.name: Yuling Jiao, Wensen Ma, Houduo Qi, Defeng Sun

entry.summary: FBDM is a non-adversarial self-supervised framework that structures representations with explicit geometric references via spherical conditional velocity regression, avoiding costly encoder-critic optimization. It uses an ETF-inspired reference set with capacity constraints on reference assignment plus an explicit view-alignment loss.

entry.title: VG-TIE: An interpretable tabular-to-image encoding method based on visibility graphs

author.name: David Chushig-Muzo, Luis M. L\'opez-Ramos, \'Angeles Rodr\'iguez de Cara, Eva Milara, Luis Zhinin-Vera, Diego H. Peluffo-Ord\'o\~nez

entry.summary: Proposes VG-TIE, a tabular-to-image encoding that uses Natural and Horizontal Visibility Graphs to capture feature-value structure before projecting into a PCA-derived 2D pixel layout, so image spatial structure reflects feature relationships. This lets CNNs and vision transformers be applied to tabular data with more interpretable encodings than PCA/t-SNE/UMAP-based baselines.

entry.title: MQSS-Selector: RL-Guided Pass Selection for an MLIR Compilation Pipeline

author.name: Andre Youssefi (Leibniz Supercomputing Centre), Erc\"ument Kaya (Leibniz Supercomputing Centre, Technical University of Munich), Minh Chung (Leibniz Supercomputing Centre), Jorge Echavarria (Munich Quantum Valley), Laura B. Schulz (Argonne National Laboratory), Martin Schulz (Leibniz Supercomputing Centre, Technical University of Munich)

entry.summary: Introduces an RL-guided pass-selection system for an MLIR-based quantum compilation pipeline targeting HPC-QC convergence in the NISQ era, where error-prone devices require specialized optimizations and topology mappings. The work addresses fragmentation in existing quantum software stacks by learning which compiler passes to apply.

entry.title: Polite but Misaligned: Evaluating LLM Politeness Judgments Against Human Pragmatic Norms

author.name: Rong Wang, Kun Sun, Yadong Guo

entry.summary: This paper evaluates how well seven LLMs judge politeness against human pragmatic norms using datasets with continuous and categorical annotations. It finds inter-model agreement exceeds model-human agreement, alignment correlates with explicit linguistic cues, and models show systematic neutral compression with over-prediction of neutral categories.

entry.title: How To Do Things With Prompts

author.name: Kristina \v{S}ekrst, Virna Karli\'c

entry.summary: Applying speech act and politeness theory, this paper performs a corpus-pragmatic analysis of 2,000 English prompts from publicly shared ChatGPT conversations, comparing 1,000 prompts from 2023 with 1,000 from 2025. Prompts are annotated for illocutionary force, directness, propositional content, and politeness markers, revealing consistent shifts as users gain familiarity with the systems. It offers a linguistically grounded view of how human prompting behavior evolves.

entry.title: GeoNLI - A Natural Language Interpreter for Satellite Imagery

author.name: Ashutosh Gandhe, Anupam Rawat, Geet Sethi, Kabir Nasiruddin, Madhav Kotecha, Panav Shah, Rakshit Sawarn, Soumitra Nayak

entry.summary: The paper presents a unified modular pipeline for satellite imagery captioning, VQA, and visual grounding, evaluating models on VRS Bench and NWPU-VHR-10 where EarthMind performs strongly on captioning and VQA. For grounding the authors propose several pipelines (RemoteSAM-SAM variants, DiffuSAM) and adopt a majority-voting ensemble across EarthMind, RemoteSAM, SAM3, Falcon, and DiffuSAM. The system delivers a natural-language interface for remote sensing imagery.

entry.title: FluidRain: Incompressible Rain Flow as an Attention Bias for Loop-in-Loop Video Deraining

author.name: Pu Wang, Yongcong Wang, Wenhao Li, Xiang Chen, Guangwei Gao, Jinshan Pan, Siyuan Yao, Shujun Fu, Zhuoran Zheng

entry.summary: FluidRain models rain motion as divergence-free image-space flow inspired by fluid mechanics, using it as an attention bias in a lightweight Loop-in-Loop architecture for video deraining. This bridges explicit rain-structure modeling and implicit temporal aggregation without unreliable motion estimation.

entry.title: A Study of the Limits of Collaborative DCT-Based Image Denoising via Interpretable Neural Networks

author.name: Cristian Comellas, Julia Navarro, Antoni Buades

entry.summary: The paper reformulates DCT-based collaborative filtering (BM3D-style) as a compact fully differentiable architecture, DeepBM3D, combining non-local patch grouping, DCT-domain filtering, and multi-stage processing. It studies how far structured, interpretable denoising principles can be pushed relative to black-box deep denoisers.

entry.title: Modelling dynamic systems transfer functions from events in computational neuromorphic imaging

author.name: Nimrod Kruger, Gregory Cohen

entry.summary: This theoretical paper examines the correspondence between excitation temporal profiles and event-stream readings in computational neuromorphic imaging, noting that static point-source PSF measurement has no direct event-based equivalent. It formalizes how transfer functions of dynamic systems can be modeled from event camera outputs.

entry.title: Integrating Local Detail and Global Context: A Dual-Input Multi-Task Learning Framework for Bone Tumor Diagnosis

author.name: S. M. Nasif Uddin, Rusab Sarmun, Muhammad E. H. Chowdhury, Adam Mushtak, Israa Al-Hashimi, Sohaib Bassam Zoghoul

entry.summary: A dual-input multi-task framework for bone tumor segmentation and subtype classification that applies bidirectional cross-modal attention between a YOLO-derived lesion crop and the full radiograph, using the multi-institutional BTXRD dataset of 3,746 radiographs with a dual-stream DenseNet121. It claims the first application of such cross-attention for bone tumor diagnosis. It matters for rare, clinically aggressive tumors where diagnosis is difficult.

entry.title: A Support-Enhanced Granular-Jamming Gripper for RL-based Grasping with Continuum Manipulators

author.name: Danyu Liu, Tianlin Zhang, Wei Chen, Wei Tang, Kecheng Qin, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: A lightweight granular-jamming gripper designed for continuum manipulators, remaining compliant before jamming and establishing a direct load path to the manipulator tip after jamming. The paper systematically designs membrane materials, particles, filling ratios, and internal support structure, and characterizes geometry-dependent grasp boundaries.

entry.title: Rethinking Credit and Recognition in Mathematics in the Age of AI

author.name: Benoit Henry

entry.summary: An essay analyzing how the credit system in mathematics — where recognition drives jobs, prizes, grants, and identity — may be disrupted as AI changes what constitutes difficult or original work. The author builds on a prior essay to explore how AI-assisted proof and discovery strain the perception-based credit economy of academic mathematics.

entry.title: The Fellowship of the Query: Learning Retrieval Actions

author.name: Mohammed Al-Maamari, Saber Zerhoudi, Michael Granitzer, Jelena Mitrovi\'c

entry.summary: The paper trains small language models as next-action controllers for retrieval-augmented QA, building a seven-way action-prediction task from accepted teacher search traces covering decomposition, search, reformulation, extraction, synthesis, verification, and stopping. LoRA fine-tuning is evaluated across SLMs and xSLMs, including a low-resource setting where one model is both controller and answer generator.

entry.title: Baszta: Data-Centric Fine-Tuning of a Polish Multi-Label Safety Classifier

author.name: Adam G\'orski, Mateusz J\k{a}kalak, Rafa{\l} Jakubowski

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune a 124M-parameter Polish encoder into a multi-label content-safety classifier across five harm categories using a Focal plus R-Drop objective, and compare against Bielik Guard on a shared OOD benchmark under matched per-category threshold tuning. They find a small but statistically significant micro-F1 lead, and show that an apparent macro-F1 advantage was an artifact of comparing tuned versus untuned models.

entry.title: Epistemic-Probabilistic Model for Guarded Multi-Agent LLM Coordination

author.name: Mehdi Nasiri, Mohammad Saeed Arvenaghi, Sadegh Vaezi, Ebrahim Ardeshir-Larijani

entry.summary: The paper introduces Epistemic Probabilistic Language Agents (EPLA), a neuro-symbolic architecture for multi-agent LLM coordination under uncertainty in which a Symbolic Guard provides structured diagnostic feedback while the LLM generates behaviors. It targets missing social behavior and coordination mechanisms identified by viewing multi-agent LLMs through classical multi-agent systems theory.

entry.title: The Gold in Bias: Maturing the AI Design Process through Verification

author.name: Samira Maghool, Paolo Ceravolo

entry.summary: The paper reconceptualizes AI bias not merely as a flaw to minimize but as a diagnostic signal revealing weaknesses in data, modeling assumptions, and system design. It proposes a multidimensional framework analyzing bias across four dimensions (origin sources, emergence patterns, and others) spanning both traditional and generative AI, and outlines a verification-driven mitigation pathway across the AI lifecycle. The framing treats bias as evidence usable for governance and verification.

entry.title: SMILESGNN: Interpretable Clinical Toxicity Prediction via SMILES-Graph Cross-Attention Fusion

author.name: Quang Minh Nguyen, Thuy Quynh Nguyen, Duc Minh Le, Ho Nhat Minh Nguyen, Thanh Long Dai Doan, Trong Nghia Nguyen

entry.summary: SMILESGNN fuses a SMILES Transformer encoder with a GATv2 graph encoder via cross-attention for drug toxicity prediction, with a ChemBERTa-2 pretrained variant. The explicit graph branch enables GNNExplainer-based attributions, addressing class imbalance, scaffold generalization, and interpretability needs in clinical toxicity prediction.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration of 3GPP Channel Estimators

author.name: I. Zakir Ahmed, Hamid Sadjadpour

entry.summary: Quantifies that no single OFDM channel estimator is uniformly best across 3GPP channel scenarios, SNR, Doppler, and antenna configurations by unifying evaluation of eight literature estimators, then proposes multi-agent LLM orchestration to select estimators per scenario.

entry.title: Can Classical Semantic-Extractive Summarization Be Evaluated in Hindi? A Replication Study

author.name: Showket Ahmad Khan, Mudasir Mohd, Nasrullah Sheikh, Mohsin Altaf Wani, Abid Hussain Wani, Hilal Ahmad Khanday, Niyaz Ahmad Wani

entry.summary: Replicates a 2020 distributional-semantics extractive summarization method in Hindi with Devanagari-appropriate components, evaluating on XL-Sum Hindi and ILSUM with a validated Devanagari-aware ROUGE implementation and bootstrap comparisons. The replicated system significantly underperforms a simple Lead-3 baseline on both corpora.

entry.title: From Policy Documents to Structured Survey Responses: Evaluating Large Language Models for Policy Monitoring

author.name: Carolyn Cole, Matthias Deschryvere, Toqeer Ehsan, Arash Hajikhani

entry.summary: This paper builds a pipeline using long-context in-context learning to have LLMs act as AI respondents, extracting structured survey responses (policy instruments, target groups) from unstructured STI policy documents for scalable policy monitoring. It demonstrates a concrete path to replacing costly manual cross-country survey efforts.

entry.title: UNWIND: Any-Length Facial Video for Stress Detection without Temporal Windowing

author.name: Stefanos Gkikas, Christian Arzate Cruz, Eric Nichols, Giorgos Giannakakis, Randy Gomez

entry.summary: Introduces UNWIND, a facial-video stress detection framework that processes complete recordings as a single input by folding the temporal dimension into the channel dimension of a two-dimensional representation, eliminating windowing, overlap, and aggregation decisions. This lets the model exploit information distributed across the whole recording.

entry.title: QINA: Quantum-Inspired Nonlinear Adapters for Pretrained Vision Models

author.name: Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi

entry.summary: Introduces QINA, compact adapters for frozen pretrained vision backbones that perform learnable trigonometric feature lifting followed by bounded nonlinear aggregation, inducing structured oscillatory bases with control over the spectral and geometric structure of feature transformations. It targets transfer learning under limited data and frozen-backbone constraints.

entry.title: An Exploratory Ablation of a Small MLA--SSM Hybrid Language Model

author.name: Christos Koutsiaris

entry.summary: Reports a single-seed exploratory ablation of TALH, a decoder-only language model combining parallel multi-head latent attention with a recurrent state-space branch, training five 117-217M parameter variants on FineWeb. Results suggest the SSM branch matters most for validation perplexity while MLA contributes less, and a dense-FFN hybrid slightly beats a ternary-MoE variant with lower memory.

entry.title: A Manifold-Aware Topic Modeling Approach via Rank-Based Prototypes

author.name: Thiago C\'esar Castilho Almeida, Daniel Carlos Guimar\~aes Pedronette

entry.summary: Introduces MARETopic, a training-free topic modeling framework that projects pretrained embeddings onto a low-dimensional manifold and selects exactly K exemplar documents as topics using ranked-list ordinal neighborhoods, avoiding hubness and anisotropy distortions of absolute distances. Two variants score candidate documents by coverage and correlation criteria.

entry.title: Multi-Task Learning by using Contextualized Word Representations for Syntactic Parsing of a Morphologically Rich Language

author.name: Toqeer Ehsan, Miriam Butt, Sarmad Hussain, Hassan Alhuzali, Ali Al-Laith

entry.summary: Achieves state-of-the-art constituency and dependency parsing for Urdu via four contributions: converting the CLE-UTB treebank to dependency format, a unified sequence-labeling parsing scheme, contextual embeddings trained on a 220M-token Urdu web corpus, and single- versus multi-task learning frameworks with post-processing rules.

entry.title: fable.intermittent: benchmarking probabilistic forecasting methods for intermittent time series

author.name: Stefano Damato, Lorenzo Zambon, Giorgio Corani, Dario Azzimonti

entry.summary: This paper introduces fable.intermittent, an R package unifying several probabilistic forecasting methods for intermittent demand and retail series within the fable framework, enabling systematic comparison through a single pipeline. It also introduces a new evaluation metric, addressing the asymmetric cost structure that inventory decisions require.

entry.title: MORE-PLR: multi-output regression employed for partial label ranking

author.name: Santo M. A. R. Thies, Juan C. Alfaro, Viktor Bengs

entry.summary: MORE-PLR reformulates partial label ranking — predicting bucket orders over labels when supervision may be incomplete — as a multi-output regression problem using an encoder that converts rankings with ties into multivariate regression targets. This is an underexplored perspective in label ranking literature. It offers a cleaner reduction that could simplify and improve partial ranking methods.

entry.title: Intrinsic-Extrinsic Coupling in Learning Dynamics

author.name: Qinyou Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes how a learner's current observations need not determine its response to further training, via a continuation-conditioned value of constrained learning-state interventions and observation-relative fibers describing present agreement. It includes an executable classifier-head write mechanism protecting current logits while repairing historical margins, evaluated in a CLINC-derived class-incremental setting. The framework distinguishes local admissibility, intervention value, and complete-policy performance in learning dynamics.

entry.title: Towards Deployable Underwater Vessel Classification

author.name: Abishek Soti, Thura Pyae Sone, Naqib Ibnul, Htoo Htet Aung, Henry Zhong, Gregory Cohen, Ying Xu

entry.summary: The authors build a compact underwater acoustic vessel-classification framework using multi-representation feature engineering, temporal pooling, and small CNNs, achieving very high macro F1 on ShipsEar. Crucially, they show provenance issues make ShipsEar results unreliable and validate instead on DeepShip for recording-independent generalization.

entry.title: Task-Resolved Fisher Spectroscopy for Quantum Reservoir Computing

author.name: Yang Peng

entry.summary: The paper introduces task-resolved Fisher spectroscopy for quantum reservoir computing, using prediction targets to define score coordinates that reveal where task information is lost across reservoir state, measurement, compression, and sampling. It derives a many-body Fisher-information hierarchy connecting state and measurement-level information.

entry.title: Efficient Continuous DEM Reconstruction under Limited Target-Resolution Supervision

author.name: Zekai Shi, Meng Zhang, Haokun Zhang, Bo Zhang

entry.summary: Presents SCOPE, a method that learns continuous terrain representations from coarse-resolution digital elevation model pairs by predicting a latent coefficient field and reusing local Fourier residual functions with geometry-guided ensemble fusion. This enables super-resolution terrain reconstruction beyond the supervised scale while controlling dense-query computation.

entry.title: Multi-Dimensional Matching

author.name: Irene Aldridge

entry.summary: Studies a matching mechanism where agents and objects are described by features rather than complete rankings, using a single spectral projection to reduce the problem to a one-dimensional sort computable in O(N log N) time. It proves exact Nash Social Welfare optimality within the projected space plus welfare guarantees, notes the mechanism is not strategy-proof with an explicit profitable misreport, and demonstrates diagnostics on an agentic AI shopping application.

entry.title: Nuclear Norm-Regularized Bayesian Matrix Completion

author.name: Calvin Tolbert

entry.summary: Provides the first sampler for fully Bayesian nuclear-norm-regularized matrix completion with unknown noise variance, extending a log-concave posterior formulation to the realistic case where noise variance must be inferred. This adds built-in uncertainty quantification to a workhorse method behind recommender systems and panel-data counterfactual estimation.

entry.title: Do Audio Language Models Hear and Read Distinctive Features Alike?

author.name: Yuanhao Chen, Peter Chin

entry.summary: Investigates whether a shared audio-language-model decoder represents phonetic features in the same direction when a phoneme is heard versus read, using minimal-pair representation offsets compared against a random-pairing reference across 6 models, 7 features, and 15 languages. Only voicing in the two Qwen2.5-Omni models exceeds the reference after statistical correction.

entry.title: LLMersion: A Local-First AI Agent Framework for Low-Cost Home Language Learning toward Educational Equity

author.name: Qiming Guo, Jinwen Tang, Xingran Huang, Hung-Yu Lin, Yafu Zhong, Xiatian Zhuang

entry.summary: LLMersion proposes a local-first AI agent framework using small open-weight models on consumer hardware to provide affordable home language tutoring, motivated by a global teacher shortage and connectivity constraints affecting billions. The paper distills eight difficulties and four binding constraints for educational technology access and argues for the role of local model deployment in educational equity. It connects efficiency-oriented small models to a concrete social application.

entry.title: ComplexSync: High-Fidelity and Real-Time Lip Sync in Complex Scenarios

author.name: Jiaran Cai, Xingpei Ma, Shenneng Huang

entry.summary: ComplexSync is a diffusion-based lip synchronization framework achieving real-time high-fidelity results in complex scenarios via a dual-stream joint training strategy against reference-frame leakage, a distillation scheme for single-step denoising reaching over 70 FPS, and a relational alignment loss. It targets practical deployment of talking-head generation under difficult conditions.

entry.title: A Simple Gripper Interface for Simulator-Agnostic Cloth Manipulation

author.name: Abhilash Nayak, Franco Coltraro, Maria Alberich-Carrami\~nana, Carme Torras

entry.summary: The paper presents a lightweight grasping model for cloth manipulation that avoids detailed contact and friction modeling by using simple positional constraints within pinches or pyramidal grasping volumes. When a gripper closes, cloth vertices inside the volume are captured and transported with the gripper motion, plus a simple squeezing step. The interface is fast, robust, and works across simulators, easing deployment of cloth-manipulation control methods.

entry.title: High-Voltage Optocoupler Amplifier for Electrostatic Actuators

author.name: George C. Jurgiel, Alex S. Miller, Jeffrey H. Lang

entry.summary: The authors demonstrate a high-voltage amplifier using optocouplers as active linear elements in feedback to drive electrostatic actuators requiring multi-kilovolt voltages at sub-milliamp currents. The design achieves 20 kV peak-to-peak output with up to 500 Hz bandwidth and fewer components than equivalent PWM amplifiers, with lower harmonic distortion. This simplifies drive electronics and improves the practical viability of electrostatic actuation.

entry.title: System Identification of an Octocopter in Hover using Full-Harmonic Orthogonal Multisine Inputs

author.name: Justin J. Matt, George V. Altamirano

entry.summary: The authors present a flight maneuver design method for multi-input system identification using full-harmonic orthogonal multisine signals injected into a flight control system. Orthogonality is achieved by repeating maneuvers with polarity changes, allowing long maneuvers to be split into shorter ones without losing frequency resolution. An input allocation scheme sizes vehicle response per degree of freedom, demonstrated on an octocopter in hover.

entry.title: Automating coherent long-form video generation

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post on automating coherent long-form video generation, addressing the challenge of maintaining consistency across extended generated videos. Only the title and category are available in the supplied content, so the technical details cannot be assessed.

entry.title: From Text Decisions to Pixels: An Study of Jev-Style Visual Choice Model

author.name: Xunlan Zhou, Xianliang Yang, Li Zhao

entry.summary: PixelJev is a native-image decision interface mapping an image, instruction, and runtime candidate set to a structured choice with candidate-conditioned probabilities using small open multimodal models, unifying recognition and multiple-choice VQA through a language-model readout. Across seven benchmarks, 64-shot source adaptation raises Pets accuracy from 60.13 to 92.40 percent and transfers to resampled and new-label settings.

entry.title: A General Framework for Budgeted Threshold Incentives on Request

author.name: Zhuolin Wu, Chengrui Zhu, Wenhua Nie, Kenny Ye Liang, Junming Lin, Haiyang Li, Zhilin Li, Wenjia Geng, Zeyu Wu, Yinan Wu, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He

entry.summary: The paper presents a request-driven framework for on-demand delivery platform rider incentives, composing conditional prediction, population reduction, trajectory integration, and budget allocation through seven replaceable modules that exchange conditional trajectory laws. A response-correction step reweights abundant no-offer historical trajectories to estimate uplift where randomized trials are impractical. This is an industrial causal-inference and budgeting system for incentive design.

entry.title: Temporal Learning for End-Effector Position Estimation under Aerodynamic Disturbances in Aerial Continuum Manipulation

author.name: Niloufar Amiri, Houman Masnavi, Farrokh Janabi-Sharifi

entry.summary: Studies temporal neural networks for estimating end-effector position of an aerial continuum manipulator under UAV-induced aerodynamic disturbances, using a newly collected experimental dataset across robot configurations and flight altitudes. Strain-parameterized kinematic models serve as baselines for residual learning.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning for Joint Wire Calibration and Interaction Position Reconstruction in Multi-Wire Parallel Plate Avalanche Counters

author.name: Antoine Lemasson, Maurycy Rejmund

entry.summary: The paper presents a physics-informed self-supervised framework that jointly performs wire calibration and interaction position reconstruction in MWPPAC detectors without labeled measurements or dedicated calibration runs, formulating calibration as a latent optimization problem over wire gains and event-wise positions.

entry.title: Language Specificity vs. Domain Diversity: Benchmarking Transformers for Bangla Medical NER

author.name: Rakib Abdullah, Md. Maruful Islam Maruf

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks fine-tuned BanglaBERT, mBERT, and XLM-RoBERTa against GPT-4o mini in zero- and few-shot settings for Bangla medical named entity recognition, using the full test set of 3,179 samples rather than the small 50-sample subsets used previously. Fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa achieves an F1 of 0.5959, establishing reproducible baselines for this low-resource domain.

entry.title: Common Covariance Geometry and Certification for Brownian Kernel Ladders

author.name: Mahdi Mohammadigohari

entry.summary: This paper introduces the minimum-trace common covariance dominating the union of RKHS ellipsoids generated by Brownian kernel ladders, developing statistical, approximation-theoretic, and computational consequences via absolutely two-summing operators and reductions to graph-coarea and effective-resistance geometry. It is deep kernel-geometry theory with universal Gaussian-complexity bounds. The work is mathematically sophisticated but far from mainstream applications.

entry.title: A Computational Framework for Modelling Organisation-Level Semantic Identity from Longitudinal Textual Data

author.name: Brinda Murali Krishna, Oktay Karaku\c{s}, Can Eyupoglu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a computational framework integrating semantic representation learning and graph-based methods to model organization-level semantic identity as an interpretable, evolving construct from longitudinal textual data, going beyond static embeddings for similarity or classification. It fills a gap in organization-level text analytics. Potential applications include organizational communication studies and brand/identity tracking.

entry.title: Personalised federated learning for Riemannian and Euclidean EEG decoding

author.name: Thibault Pautrel, Florent Bouchard, Ammar Mian, Guillaume Ginolhac

entry.summary: The paper adapts personalized federated learning for EEG decoding by sharing a common trunk across subjects while each subject keeps a private classification head, applied to both Riemannian SPDNet and Euclidean EEGNet decoders. Experiments on three motor-imagery datasets show personalization improves fit under strong inter-subject variability.

entry.title: Cost-Sensitive Online Window Size Selection for Portfolio Management

author.name: Yi-Chen Liu, Chung-Han Hsieh

entry.summary: Proposes a two-level framework that treats candidate window sizes as experts and dynamically aggregates them via online learning with turnover-inclusive losses, deriving finite-horizon cost-sensitive tracking-regret bounds. Suitably tuned Fixed Share achieves asymptotically no tracking regret for sublinear switching budgets.

entry.title: From Processing to Functionality: Engineering Accessible Material States in Cu-Embedded SiO$_x$ Memristive Devices

author.name: Tobias Gergs, Rouven Lamprecht, Sahitya Yarragolla, Ole Gronenberg, Luca Vialetto, Hermann Kohlstedt, Thomas Mussenbrock, Jan Trieschmann

entry.summary: Establishes a multiscale framework linking plasma deposition conditions to macroscopic memristive device functionality, combining statistical analysis of over 50,000 experimentally characterized SiOx/Cu/SiOx devices with physics-based plasma and atomistic simulations. Device behavior emerges from a probabilistic cascade of defect formation, state evolution, and functional-regime emergence rather than deterministic process-to-performance mappings.

entry.title: BanglaKontho: Closing the Long-Form Gap in Bangla Text-to-Speech

author.name: Mizbaul Haque Maruf

entry.summary: BanglaKontho is a 20-hour single-speaker Bangla TTS corpus from professional audiobook recordings, with 7,050 verified 24 kHz utterances, plus a reusable Bangla text normalizer and full preprocessing pipeline. It targets the gap in long-form prosody data for the seventh most spoken language, with an MB-iSTFT-VITS baseline demonstrating usability.

entry.title: Benchmarking Arabic--Russian Machine Translation: A Comparison of Fine-tuned NMT and Few-shot LLMs under Rich Morphology and Low Lexical Overlap

author.name: Mullosharaf K. Arabov

entry.summary: This benchmark study compares seven fine-tuned NMT models against four few-shot LLMs for Arabic-Russian translation on a new 15.47M-pair corpus, finding that fine-tuned NLLB-1.3B strongly outperforms all LLMs. Error analysis identifies low lexical overlap as the dominant failure mode, with LLMs producing severe quality drops. The paper documents that few-shot LLMs remain far behind dedicated NMT for this morphologically rich, low-overlap language pair.

entry.title: FoCal: Frequency-Oriented Cross-Modal Interaction and Spectral Calibration for Aerial Visible-Infrared Object Detection

author.name: Ben Liang, Chao Sui, Junqi Bai, Yuan Liu, Chunlai Li, Xiubao Sui, Qian Chen

entry.summary: FoCal is a frequency-oriented framework for aerial RGB-IR object detection that models cross-modal interaction patterns of different frequency components rather than treating fusion indiscriminately. It includes a frequency-aware dual-domain calibration to separate useful complementary cues from unreliable modality-specific spectral responses.

entry.title: A Hybrid CNN--State-Space--Attention Backbone with Joint-Embedding Predictive Pretraining for 12-Lead ECG Classification

author.name: Yakoub Bazi, Sarah Aljuhani, Mohamad M. Al Rahhal, Mansour Zuair, Naif Alajlan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid CNN, state-space model, and attention backbone for 12-lead ECG classification, using a convolutional stem for tokenization, mixed SSM and depthwise-conv blocks for temporal dynamics, and late self-attention at reduced resolution. It adds an ECG-oriented joint-embedding predictive pretraining objective to improve transfer from unlabeled data.

entry.title: Sim-to-Real Aware End-to-End Learning Environment for Micromobility

author.name: Shouma Amano, Takuya Azumi

entry.summary: A vehicle-specific sim-to-real learning environment for a micromobility vehicle (WHILL Model CR) built on AWSIM and ROS 2, capturing differential-drive and omni-wheel kinematics that standard driving simulators miss. Physical parameters are tuned via Bayesian optimization on real data, and a DreamerV3-based end-to-end policy achieves task completion in the world-model training pipeline.

entry.title: Assessing the Impact of Fleet Size on Crowdsourced Mapping Using a Dissimilarity Measure

author.name: Marie-Ngo\"ie Badibanga Kalenda (Heudiasyc), Philippe Bonnifait (Heudiasyc), Marie-Anne Mittet

entry.summary: The paper presents a simulation framework for evaluating how the number of contributing vehicles affects the quality of crowdsourced digital maps used by ADAS and autonomous driving safety functions such as Intelligent Speed Assistance. It introduces a dissimilarity measure to quantify map-layer agreement and studies the relationship between fleet size and maintained map accuracy. This informs cost-effective alternatives to traditional surveying.

entry.title: After Action Report: Canadian Sovereign AI at Nrth 2026

author.name: Sheikh Abdur Raheem Ali

entry.summary: A personal after-action report from the Nrth 2026 Canadian sovereign-AI innovation event (September 22-24), covering introductions to datacenter and compute partners such as Dell and Columbia Data Vault, and a strategic priority of advancing inference-only compute verification as a prerequisite for agreements that pace frontier AI development.

entry.title: AFT Neural Function Approximators for 1D Nonlinear Force Laws

author.name: Miriam Goldack, Johann Gro{\ss}, Malte Krack, Merten Stender

entry.summary: The work replaces costly alternating frequency-time schemes in harmonic balance structural dynamics with neural networks that map displacement Fourier coefficients directly to nonlinear force coefficients and their Jacobians via automatic differentiation. The surrounding solver and continuation algorithms remain unchanged.

entry.title: From Prediction to Explainable Provider Behavior Profiles for Fraud, Waste, and Abuse Review

author.name: Yubin Park, Evan Brociner

entry.summary: This paper argues that predictive forecasting of provider behavior in healthcare claims data adds little value over simple persistence, and that forecasts conflate benign changes with potentially concerning behavior. The authors propose shifting from prediction to explainable provider behavior profiles that identify material changes, the specific codes and dollars driving them, and plausible explanations. It is a methodological critique with practical implications for fraud, waste, and abuse review workflows.

entry.title: Not All Confusion Is Equal: A Source-Aware Uncertainty Diagnosis for Fine-Grained Aircraft Detection

author.name: Hai Huang, Helmut Mayer

entry.summary: Presents A-squared-E-squared, a diagnostic tool that decomposes detector confusion into a 2x2 taxonomy of aleatoric versus epistemic and within-class versus between-class sources, each measured by a dedicated quantity. This turns passive confusion-matrix analysis into actionable guidance for fine-grained aircraft detection.

entry.title: A Rapid Pipeline for Training and Deploying ML Models on WeBe Band

author.name: Ehsan Kourkchi, Asmita Asmita, Houman Homayoun, Mahdi Eslamimehr

entry.summary: This work presents an end-to-end edge ML workflow for a wrist-worn wearable that automatically generates hardware-efficient models with AutoML, hardware-aware quantization, and performance profiling to hit latency and memory targets in device firmware. It aims to shorten development cycles for multimodal physiological monitoring on constrained hardware.

entry.title: Towards An LLM-Driven Unified Conversion Framework for BT and FSM in Autonomous Intelligent Systems

author.name: Zhang Qi, Yang Shuo, Zhu Zhengqiu, Zhou Peng, Jiao Peng

entry.summary: The paper proposes an LLM-driven framework for converting between finite state machines and behavior trees, two equivalent behavioral modeling paradigms for autonomous systems, introducing a loop-execution BT structure to preserve behavioral completeness and techniques to curb state explosion in BT-to-FSM conversion. It targets automatic, semantically consistent transformation.

entry.title: SkinAgent AI: A Safety-Grounded Multimodal Agentic Framework for Non-Diagnostic Skincare Support

author.name: Muhammad Muhtasim Shahriar, Abdullah Mohammad Sayem, Tze Hui Liew, M. F. Mridha, Md. Mahiuddin

entry.summary: SkinAgent AI is a non-diagnostic multimodal agent for consumer skincare that routes visual concerns (acne, pores, wrinkles), estimates skin type from photographs, and orchestrates typed tools with deterministic safety, privacy, and evidence checks, approval gates before state-changing actions, and structured trace/replay mechanisms. The study evaluates both visual-model performance and system-level agent behavior.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Emotion Understanding: A Transformer-GAT Approach for Dialogue Emotion Recognition

author.name: Jiaqi Qiao, Yifan Lyu, Xiujuan Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes Transformer-GAT, a hybrid framework combining a Transformer for global semantics with a Graph Attention Network for fine-grained inter-modality relationships in multimodal dialogue emotion recognition. It targets applications in sentiment analysis, customer service, and human-computer interaction. The contribution is a fusion architecture designed to capture both global and local context synergy.

entry.title: An Explainable DistilBERT-BiLSTM-Attention Framework for Binary and Multi-Class Hate Speech Detection

author.name: Rameesha Zia, Muhammad Shahid Iqbal Malik

entry.summary: Combines DistilBERT embeddings, a BiLSTM with attention, and explainability techniques for binary and multi-class hate speech classification, evaluated across multiple datasets. The work targets the common limitation that prior detectors are single-dataset, binary-only, and opaque about their decisions.

entry.title: Frame-to-Panorama Localization and Context-Aware Sampling for Scene-Specific Ship Detection in a Smart Marina Testbed

author.name: Ignat Romanov, Andreas Hadjipieris, Neofytos Dimitriou

entry.summary: Describes an end-to-end data-curation pipeline that recovers camera-view information from historical PTZ maritime video lacking pan/tilt/zoom metadata and combines it with environmental context to build annotation-ready subsets for scene-specific ship detection in a smart marina testbed.

entry.title: TAM-Chain: Multi-Scale Thyroid Cytology Classification via Absorbing Markov Chains and Shannon Entropy Uncertainty Quantification for False-Negative Suppression and Domain-Shift Adaptation

author.name: Hai Pham Ngoc

entry.summary: TAM-Chain is a multi-scale (10x/20x/40x) thyroid cytology classification framework that models multi-magnification feature extraction as an absorbing Markov chain with optimal stopping and Shannon-entropy-based uncertainty quantification, providing a human-in-the-loop referral mechanism to suppress false negatives under clinical domain shift.

entry.title: Growth-Inspired Graph Generation and Inverse Design of Mechanical Lattices via Dot Matrices Database Augmentation and GCNN

author.name: Weiyun Xu, Jiamu Liu

entry.summary: Inspired by biological morphogenesis, the paper introduces a growth-based graph generation framework for mechanical lattices in which structures emerge via sequential cross-layer and intra-layer growth from a discrete dot matrix. It augments a database of 3D lattices evaluated by finite element analysis and uses graph CNNs for inverse design.

entry.title: GBFRVFL: Granular-Ball Computing-Based Fuzzy Random Vector Functional Link Network

author.name: A. Quadir, A. Rahaman, P. N. Suganthan, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: GBFRVFL combines granular-ball computing with fuzzy random vector functional link networks, abstracting raw samples into adaptive granular balls with two membership assignment schemes to handle noise, outliers, and class imbalance while preserving RVFL's fast training and generalization. It extends a fast classical architecture with explicit uncertainty handling. Relevant mainly to the granular computing and broad-learning-systems communities.

entry.title: Feature Space Selection and Heterogeneous Effect Estimation for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability: A Random Forest to the Generalized Random Forest Pipeline

author.name: Tshemollo Rapolai, Seite Makgai, Mohammad Arashi

entry.summary: The study ablates molecular feature spaces (Morgan fingerprints, RDKit descriptors, SMILES bigrams) across four algorithms for predicting blood-brain barrier permeability on the MoleculeNet BBBP dataset. A dynamic random forest with combined features achieves the best mean AUC of 0.970 and enables heterogeneous-effect estimation linking molecular structure to permeability.

entry.title: Named Entity Recognition using Sliding Window Approach

author.name: Hariom Ingle, Ronit Ghode, Ishwari Gondkar, Jidnyasa Harad, Ravindra Murumkar, Raviraj Joshi

entry.summary: Introduces an inference-only sliding-window pipeline that extends a frozen sentence-level NER model (MahaNER-BERT) to document-level prediction by merging overlapping window predictions without retraining.
