author.name: Abdulmalik Alquwayfili, Faisal AlMeshal, Jumanah Almajnouni, Huda Abdulhadi Alamri, Muhammad Kamran J Khan

entry.summary: MINER is a training-free inference framework that augments frozen dual-encoder (CLIP, SigLIP) global image embeddings with a bank of region-level embeddings and hubness-correcting rescoring, improving retrieval of small, low-salience objects in cluttered scenes. It also introduces ROCS, a re-captioned high-clutter benchmark from Flickr30K and MS COCO.

entry.title: InGuard: Towards Generalized Inner Guardrail for Safe Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Zeyu Wang, Xiaodan Li, Zhiwen Li, Yuefeng Chen, Hui Xue

entry.summary: Proposes Inner Guardrails for text-to-image safety, moving risk checking inside the generation pipeline to leverage the model's own representations rather than external prompt and image classifiers. This improves prompt-screening accuracy, avoids wasted generation cost, and enables repairing flagged prompts into safe images instead of outright rejection.

entry.title: RelCheck: Dual-Evidence Spatial Grounding for VLM Hallucination Correction

author.name: Siddhi Patil, Navrati Saxena, William B. Andreopoulos

entry.summary: RelCheck is a training-free post-hoc pipeline for correcting relational hallucinations in multimodal LLMs, combining learned scene-graph triples from RelTR, deterministic spatial predicates from bounding-box geometry, and a Woodpecker-style object claim layer into a three-layer visual knowledge base that a language model uses for correction. Relational hallucinations have been largely unaddressed relative to object-level ones. This improves multimodal factuality without retraining.

entry.title: Predicting the Progression of Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis

author.name: Owen Pullen, Amir Jamaludin, Andrew Zisserman

entry.summary: A team including Andrew Zisserman trains a transformer model to predict the progression of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from sequences of DXA scans spanning ages 9 to 24. The model is trained on a large-scale synthetic dataset of spine curve time series covering different curve types and progression patterns, and generalizes to real data. This demonstrates a useful synthetic-data strategy for a clinically important longitudinal prediction task.

entry.title: Task-Prototype Guided Flow Matching for Few-Shot Generalization in Vision-Language Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yizhao Wang, Guantao Zhang, Jingbo Wang

entry.summary: Presents TP-Flow, a few-shot robot manipulation framework that converts a handful of support demonstrations into task-prototype tokens guiding flow matching for policy generation, using cross-attention queries, adaptive initial distributions, and gated normalization. The goal is to adapt vision-language manipulation policies to new procedures where language alone underspecifies motion and contact timing.

entry.title: CableVLA: Simulation-Privileged Global-Local Representation Learning for Cable Routing

author.name: Zhifei Teng, Bo Feng, Xiang Zou, Jinpeng Xiao, Min Li, Zhouping Yin, Yiqun Li

entry.summary: CableVLA is an end-to-end vision-language-action framework for cable routing that converts simulation-privileged supervision into deployable representations: a TopoHead distills cable-topology and physics information into causal visual context, while TacSense learns contact dynamics from resistive tactile arrays with simulator-derived supervision. A contact gate activates force-tactile residuals refining the next eight actions of a frozen topology-conditioned policy.

entry.title: Fisheye-VLA: Decoupling Coverage and Acuity for Manipulation with a Single Fisheye Camera

author.name: Ziang Ren, Zike Yan, Raymond Zhang, Xuguo He, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: Fisheye-VLA replaces multi-camera rigs in robot manipulation with a single passive fisheye camera, combining a global workspace view with local perspective crops for detail. A controlled re-rendering study shows end-effector-centered crops capture most of the benefit of a larger candidate pool, motivating a compact allocation around both hands.

entry.title: Sample, Simulate, Select: Physics-in-the-Loop Text-to-Motion for Humanoids Without Training

author.name: Raphael Memmesheimer, Sven Behnke

entry.summary: Proposes S3, a training-free pipeline that samples N motions per prompt from a frozen text-to-motion model, retargets each to a Unitree G1 humanoid via inverse kinematics, rolls them out under full rigid-body dynamics with the pretrained SONIC tracking policy, and keeps the best-executed candidate. It quantifies how much of the text-to-humanoid gap closes purely through deployment-controller-in-the-loop selection.

entry.title: Beyond End-Task Success: How to Audit Visual Experience Retrieval in Robotics

author.name: Eshika Pathak, Leela Krishna

entry.summary: The authors argue that end-task success rates do not reveal whether a robot's experience-retrieval rule is actually selecting good stored experiences, since a rule can score well by reusing one broadly transferable experience. They contribute an exhaustive audit methodology that executes every stored experience in every query scene across manipulation tasks, reuse mechanisms, and library sizes.

entry.title: Efficient Cost-Aware LLM Evaluation via Bayesian Bandit Gittins Indices

author.name: Qian Xie, Yueli He, Nairen Cao

entry.summary: GittinsEval formulates LLM configuration selection across benchmarks as a cost-aware Bayesian bandit problem, using the Gittins index policy to decide which configuration to evaluate next and when to stop, with an anytime LCB-style recommendation rule over partially evaluated configurations. It is computationally efficient via lightweight online updates after offline precomputation and performs competitively on GSM8K, PIQA, AlpacaEval, and MMLU response matrices.

entry.title: ShowTellArena: Evaluating Business Workflow Understanding from Demonstrations

author.name: David Garg, Ritobrata Sarkar, Ehsan Azarnasab, Siddhartha Borah

entry.summary: ShowTellArena is a benchmark protocol and public dataset testing whether AI agents comprehend narrated business workflow demonstrations, with 50 tasks across finance, hiring, procurement, inventory, and logistics, plus 502 questions probing operational rules, boundaries, exceptions, and automation errors. The protocol holds scenarios and quizzes fixed while letting each product teach through its own interface, and includes analysis of 218 selected products or runs.

entry.title: Optimizing the Score, Losing Sight of the Task: Reward Hacking Across Weights, Selection, and Prompts

author.name: Vansh Wahi

entry.summary: A conceptual paper unifying reward hacking across three optimization substrates: parameter updates, inference-time selection, and persistent prompt revisions, building on the Proxy Compression Hypothesis. It formalizes a distance-dependent upper bound on evaluator disagreement to explain when measured progress diverges from true task performance.

entry.title: Toward User-Mediated Self-Repair in Ubiquitous Robots Through Goal-Oriented Agentic AI

author.name: Morten Roed Frederiksen

entry.summary: This paper presents a goal-oriented agentic AI architecture that lets non-expert users repair ubiquitous robots through situated natural-language dialogue. It decouples high-level strategic planning from reactive conversational execution and reports a 95% task completion rate with positive self-efficacy across a 20-participant study on a physical hardware testbed.

entry.title: JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure

author.name: Yubo Li, Yidi Miao, Ramayya Krishnan, Rema Padman

entry.summary: The paper evaluates a decision-only judge (Jev) against sixteen generative and reward-model judges with blinded human adjudication, finding it within three percentage points of a state-of-the-art LLM judge at 0.36% of the cost on preference and factuality tasks. Gaps appear on derivation-checking and resisting elaborate wrong answers, and the paper proposes escalating low-confidence decisions to stronger judges.

entry.title: Multi-Term Fourier Graph Neural Network with Sample Relationship Learning for Enhanced Remaining Useful Life Prediction

author.name: Ya Song, Laurens Bliek, Yaoxin Wu, Yingqian Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a spatio-temporal graph neural network with multi-term Fourier components and learned sample relationships for remaining useful life prediction in predictive maintenance. It addresses two drawbacks of existing ST-GNNs: the need for domain expertise to construct graph structures and fixed-size lookback windows that miss short- or long-term dependencies.

entry.title: Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems

author.name: Sanjay Surendranath Girija, Aniruddh Nath, Li Wei, Yanhao Jiang, Shawn Andrews, Lukasz Heldt, Yi Wu, Aditya Mahajan, Mohit Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces the Light Heads framework, which enables dynamic injection of new prediction tasks into existing multi-task ranking models in production recommender systems, avoiding backbone retraining, cold-starting, and slow experimentation cycles. It is designed for continuous online learning environments.

entry.title: RootQuantV2: Adapting a Vision Foundation Model for Root-Trait Regression from Minirhizotron Imagery

author.name: Kinjalk Parth, Sebastian Varela, Andrew D. B. Leakey

entry.summary: Adapts a vision foundation model to predict root traits (length, surface area) directly from minirhizotron images via regression, bypassing the need for manually traced masks that are locked in proprietary software. This enables high-throughput below-ground crop phenotyping at field scale, a longstanding bottleneck in plant science.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Combinatorial Optimization with Constraints via Frank-Wolfe

author.name: Akbar Rafiey, Yifei Xu, Nikolaos Karalias

entry.summary: This paper proposes a general self-supervised framework for neural combinatorial optimization that removes the need for projection steps onto the feasible polytope. Instead of constraining network outputs to lie within the feasible region, the network predicts arbitrary continuous vectors, and a Frank-Wolfe based procedure handles hard combinatorial constraints during training. This addresses a key limitation of prior continuous-extension approaches that relied on ad-hoc, problem-specific constructions.

entry.title: SE-MSB: End-to-End Unpaired Speech Enhancement using Mamba Schr\"odinger Bridges

author.name: Andreas Bagge, Andreas Nymand, Michael Riis Andersen, Bj{\o}rn Sand Jensen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a speech enhancement framework that requires no paired clean/degraded training data, instead using Diffusion Schrödinger Bridges to learn a stochastic transport process between clean and noisy speech distributions. To address the computational cost of simulating differential equations during training, the authors introduce a high-efficiency Mamba-based diffusion model operating end-to-end on raw waveforms. The work matters because real-world acoustic environments rarely match synthetic degradation assumptions, and unpaired approaches could make speech enhancement far more practical.

entry.title: FairMean: Promoting Fairness in Distributed Learning under Label Poisoning Attacks

author.name: Huigan Zheng, Jiaojiao Zhang, Yongxiang Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies a conflict between fairness-aware distributed learning and robustness to label poisoning: methods that upweight high-loss clients to reduce performance disparities can be exploited by poisoned clients that artificially inflate their losses. The proposed FairMean method weights client gradients with a bounded, nondecreasing function of local loss, promoting fairness while capping the influence of potentially poisoned clients, and the authors provide theoretical guarantees on solution fairness and a stationarity bound under poisoning.

entry.title: Towards Hierarchical GNNs for multi-grid power flow: generalization across operating scenarios

author.name: Carmine Delle Femine, Leire Garin Atxaga, Asier Diaz-Iglesias, Juan Pablo Maroto Herrera, Ane Miren Florez-Tapia, Marco Quartulli. Izaro Goienetxea Urziku

entry.summary: This paper applies hierarchical latent communication in graph neural networks to improve generalization of multi-grid power-flow models to unseen operating scenarios. Using Kron-derived and Quotient-based reduced graphs within a GENCO corrective network, the authors show an 85% reduction in voltage error versus a flat backbone across three grid topologies.

entry.title: When Post-Processing Fairness Constraints Help and When They Harm: Evidence from Eight Cross-Domain Evaluations

author.name: Nithin Raghava Ramachandra Narla

entry.summary: This work introduces FAPE, a four-stage framework for auditing post-processing fairness interventions across heterogeneous production domains. Applying Fairlearn's ThresholdOptimizer across eight domains (criminal justice, credit, healthcare, education, etc.), it characterizes when the intervention improves demographic parity and equalized odds versus when it harms other metrics. It is valuable because fairness interventions are typically validated on a single dataset at deployment time.

entry.title: Graph Learning with Spectral Connectivity Priors for Scarce Data

author.name: Mingxiao Liu (Tsinghua University, China), Bahar Oveisgharan (York University, Canada), Bingyan Zou (Tsinghua University, China), Gene Cheung (York University, Canada), H. Vicky Zhao (Tsinghua University, China), Feifei Gao (Tsinghua University, China)

entry.summary: This paper introduces SCoGL, a graph learning framework that augments the graphical lasso objective with Laplacian spectral priors to explicitly promote global connectivity when learning sparse graphs from scarce data. The authors derive gradients for several connectivity priors and develop a projected gradient descent algorithm with Armijo backtracking. This matters because sparse graph estimation under limited data is a common bottleneck in ML applications relying on graph-structured representations.

entry.title: Learning Where to Look: A Shared Relative-Alignment Module for Time-Series Forecasting and PPG-to-Vital-Sign Reconstruction

author.name: Ragamayi Puli, Shunya Nagashima

entry.summary: ROOSTER is a single conditioning module for sequence-to-sequence tasks that learns the correspondence between target and condition positions via a periodic-comb bias whose center, period, and sharpness are learned per head, instead of hard-coding identity or seasonal alignment. It applies uniformly to PPG-to-vital-sign reconstruction (e.g., wrist PPG to ECG) and long-horizon multivariate time-series forecasting. The work targets transferability of conditioning structure across tasks that currently do not share mechanisms.

entry.title: Learning to Detect Symbolic Failure: Machine Learning and the Limits of Black-Scholes

author.name: Juli Huang, Jake Cheng, Rupert Lu

entry.summary: Uses 2.6 million real option contracts to test whether machine learning can detect systematic deviations from Black-Scholes pricing, comparing learned embeddings, tree-based ensembles preserving domain structure, and neural validation. Tree models with expert features (Greeks, moneyness) outperform kernel embeddings by 21.5 points, and the agreement of deviation labels across methods suggests deviations reflect real market structure.

entry.title: What Changed? Drift Detection with Real, Virtual, and Incomparable Diagnosis

author.name: Kentaro Oda

entry.summary: Shows that cross-evaluated heads on a frozen shared encoder inherit extrapolation confounds: pure input rotations inflate deep exchange scores from about 0 to 0.80 while representation-novelty scores are blind to label-permutation drift. A conditional two-discriminator discrepancy in embedding space resolves both blind spots and, embedded in a mixture-of-heads lifecycle, enables a two-axis drift gate.

entry.title: Spread and Scale: What Determines Whether Test-Time Budget Allocation Pays

author.name: Jinhyung Bae

entry.summary: Analyzes when reallocating a fixed test-time sample budget across instances pays off for neural combinatorial optimization solvers, identifying workload properties that determine reallocation gains and accounting for the cost of the allocation policy itself. It builds on a companion study that exposed bias in standard evaluation of adaptive budget allocation.

entry.title: I-SplineFlow: Learning Monotone Spline Stochastic Interpolant Schedulers for Few-Step Generation

author.name: Md Sakib Hossain Shovon, Md Rifat Ur Rahman, Md Abtahi Majeed Chowdhury, Yunhong Min, Jaesik Choi, Minhyuk Sung

entry.summary: I-SplineFlow parameterizes stochastic interpolant schedulers for few-step diffusion and flow generation using integrated monotone splines, providing local support that avoids the global coupling of polynomial bases. This enables lightweight trajectory-level optimization to accelerate pretrained generative models while preserving required scheduler properties.

entry.title: Learning Holographic Reduced Representations with Clifford Variational Autoencoders

author.name: Mohamed Malek Abid, P. Michael Furlong

entry.summary: Introduces Clifford-VAE, a variational autoencoder that projects data onto a Clifford torus to produce structured vector-symbolic-algebra (VSA) representations. On MNIST, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10 it matches Gaussian and hyperspherical VAEs on semi-supervised classification while outperforming them on VSA benchmarks, addressing how to embed unstructured data into hyperdimensional spaces.

entry.title: Does Graph Structure Earn Its Place in Microservice Root-Cause Analysis? A Controlled Study on RCAEval, and What the Benchmark Was Really Measuring

author.name: Imad Bulji\'c

entry.summary: Runs a controlled comparison of graph versus flat models for microservice root-cause analysis on RCAEval with identical features, optimizers, and scoring heads, isolating a single graph term. It finds no reliable graph-specific effect and audits the benchmark to expose properties driving prior conclusions, questioning whether GNN dominance in RCA is warranted.

entry.title: PEARL: A Lightweight Prompt-based Feature Interpreter Framework for Real-Time, Anonymous, and Heterogeneous Collaborative Perception

author.name: Armin Maleki, Hayder Radha

entry.summary: PEARL addresses heterogeneity in collaborative perception by using prompt embeddings and lightweight multi-stage interpreters that can be assigned to new-joining agents in real time without knowing neighbor configurations. It avoids model retraining and generalizes to unseen agents at runtime.

entry.title: Less Language, More Latents: Annotation-Efficient VLAs for Driving

author.name: Alexey Zakharov, Kemal Oksuz, Puneet K. Dokania

entry.summary: Introduces LADA, a three-stage pipeline that converts abundant unlabeled driving observation-trajectory pairs into language-conditioned control data by learning a vector-quantized latent action model and pseudo-labeling intents with a small annotated subset. This reduces dependence on scarce natural-language driving annotations for training vision-language-action models.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Probabilistic Safety Certification for AI-Based Grid-Edge Coordination

author.name: Yihong Zhou, Hanbin Yang, Thomas Morstyn

entry.summary: The paper develops a finite-sample probabilistic certification framework for black-box AI controllers (e.g., multi-agent RL or imitation learning) in closed-loop power grid operation, reducing the input-AI-grid workflow to a binary unsafe outcome and applying exact binomial statistics. It gives system operators an independent, rigorous deployment-safety decision procedure.

entry.title: Recognized but Not Produced: A Generation Benchmark for Culturally Specific Kinship Terms

author.name: Sahil Pardasani, Madhusudan Singh

entry.summary: This paper shifts evaluation of multilingual kinship understanding from multiple-choice recognition to open-ended generation in Hindi, Tamil, and Korean, testing five open-weight LLMs. It finds a large gap between selecting a correct term (e.g., 90.67% for GPT OSS 120B) and producing an acceptable one (36%), showing that option-supported benchmarks overestimate cultural-linguistic competence.

entry.title: Neither Silence nor Overlap Is Failure: Intent-Conditioned Evaluation of Turn-Taking in Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models

author.name: Kian Shamsaie, Iman Modarressi

entry.summary: TACT is a benchmark of 9,728 episodes (73.2 hours) from five dyadic corpora for evaluating turn-taking in full-duplex spoken dialogue models, replacing binary fixed-window scoring with a strictly proper, intent-conditioned continuous score. It argues that delayed silence or anticipatory overlap can be appropriate depending on the speaker's latent intent.

entry.title: PRISM-VLM: A Multi-Axis Discriminative Benchmark for Compact Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sanghee Park, Kee-Eung Kim

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces PRISM-VLM, a multi-axis benchmark designed to evaluate compact vision-language models more discriminatively than existing frontier-centric suites. It scores models across seven axes covering task quality, behavioral robustness, and capability bottlenecks, combining them into a single PScore, and reuses items from fifteen public benchmarks. The authors show that PScore separates model pairs more reliably than prior single-axis benchmarks across compact VLMs from the past two years.

entry.title: LabourCrew: A Multi-Agent RAG Framework for Trustworthy Adversarial Deliberation and Statutory Reasoning over Labour Law

author.name: Fatema Tuj Johora Faria, Mukaffi Bin Moin, Jubayer Al Mahmud, M. F. Mridha, Md. Alam Hossain

entry.summary: LabourCrew is a multi-agent RAG framework for labour-law question answering built around three grounding mechanisms: a StatuteGraph index linking chapter, section, proviso, and cross-reference structure, an Evidence Exchange Protocol restricting agents to an evidence ledger, and adversarial deliberation. It targets verifiable, evidence-traceable legal claims rather than merely relevant answers.

entry.title: Can LLMs Catch a Rigged Backtest? A Clean-Control Calibration Benchmark

author.name: Makar Ulesov, Vladislav Smirnov, Omar Ibrahim, Arsenii Bobovnikov

entry.summary: This paper introduces a 96-item paired benchmark for auditing backtests of trading strategies, where each flawed backtest is matched with a clean control differing in only one methodological detail. Across 1440 audits from four LLM endpoints, a DeepSeek-based auditor achieves perfect flaw recall but over-flags 93.8% of clean controls under open prompts, revealing a severe calibration gap between detecting problems and avoiding false positives.

entry.title: ContraVis: Evidence-Grounded Visual Analytics for Contradiction Review in Legal Contracts

author.name: Luis Sante, Paula Lima, Mariana Rocha, Jorge Poco

entry.summary: ContraVis is a human-in-the-loop visual analytics system for detecting contradictions in legal contracts, modeling documents as typed paragraph graphs that combine explicit contractual references with semantic relationships between paragraphs. The graph conditions LLM reasoning while also serving as the interactive representation the analyst explores, keeping model context and human inspection aligned across coordinated views.

entry.title: Reporting Under Pressure: Separating Factual and Tonal Sycophancy in LLM Statistical Analysis

author.name: Paras Balani, Subhrakanta Panda

entry.summary: This study tests whether editorial framing in prompts changes not just tone but substance when LLMs analyze data, using a 4x4 factorial design crossing four framing conditions with four ground-truth data patterns and scoring 480 responses along separate factual and tonal sycophancy dimensions. It extends sycophancy research from belief alignment to statistical reporting tasks.

entry.title: Mizar: A 159M-Parameter Audio-Language Model for Audio Understanding

author.name: Kaiyang Li, Shaobo Han, Yue Tian, Shihao Ji

entry.summary: Mizar is a compact 159M-parameter audio-language model connecting a CED-Small audio encoder to SmolLM2-135M via a frequency-merging mapper, trained in three stages using audio-QA datasets like ReasonAQA and AVQA. It targets practical audio understanding on memory- and compute-constrained edge devices.

entry.title: Surgical Kinematics from Monocular Video with Learned Articulated Motion Constraints

author.name: Mehmet Kerem Turkcan, Soham Samal, Zoran Kostic

entry.summary: The paper introduces a network that reconstructs robotic surgery instrument kinematics (position, orientation, jaw angle) from monocular video by combining frozen DINOv3 features with SAM 3.1 landmark pooling, monocular depth, and articulated motion constraints. Separate prediction of displacement magnitude and direction preserves traveled distance for skill assessment.

entry.title: Can Vision-Language Models Analyze Human-Centered Video? Mapping Model Capabilities and Human-AI Collaborative Workflows

author.name: Xiyuan Shen, Jiuyang Lyu, Seokhyun Hwang, Huanfen Yao, Shwetak Patel, Zhihan Zhang, Jacob O. Wobbrock

entry.summary: Systematically studies when vision-language models can autonomously analyze human-centered video versus when human involvement is still needed, grounding the analysis in a survey of 125 video-annotating papers from CHI 2026 and a five-dimensional taxonomy. The result is a map of VLM capabilities and proposed human-AI collaborative workflows for qualitative video research.

entry.title: Visibility-Guided Structured Measure Flow for Class-Conditioned 3D Gaussian Generation

author.name: Yizhao Wang

entry.summary: VISTA-GS formulates 3D Gaussian Splatting objects as structured Gaussian measures weighted by opacity, anisotropic covariance, and multi-view visibility, and generates them directly via a visibility-aware measure flow for class-conditioned generation. This tackles the difficulty of making 3DGS a native generative space given that Gaussians are unordered and rendering-sensitive. It matters for direct, render-efficient 3D content creation without multi-view reconstruction pipelines.

entry.title: MotionSpec: Spectral Trajectory Supervision for Motion-Consistent Video Generation

author.name: Ziqi Ni, Rui Li, Shiqi Jiang, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: MotionSpec introduces Spectral Trajectory Consistency, a motion supervision framework for text-to-video generation that builds dense anchor-relative motion trajectories and transforms them into motion spectral volumes via a transform, providing motion-specific supervision that standard generative objectives lack. It targets temporal discontinuities and implausible action progression in generated videos. Better motion fidelity is a central open problem in video generation.

entry.title: ODPure: Backdoor Purification for Object Detection via Ensemble Corruption Consensus

author.name: Li Zeng, Mingcheng Duan, Longfei Fan, Hangtao Zhang, Xianlong Wang, Yanchun Li, Xia Wen, Leo Yu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper addresses backdoor attacks on object detectors, which can cause object misclassification, disappearance, or generation when triggers are present. The proposed ODPure performs backdoor purification via an ensemble corruption consensus mechanism, extending defense research that has mostly focused on image classification. This is a notable contribution to model security for safety-critical applications like autonomous driving.

entry.title: Combining LLMs and Genetic Search for ARC-AGI-2

author.name: Val Dyachenko

entry.summary: Combines LLM program generation with genetic algorithms for ARC-AGI-2: a quantized 4B Qwen model generates candidate programs in a compact domain-specific language, and those programs seed a population evolved via mutation operators that guarantee executable offspring. This lets the system explore far more candidate programs than LLM sampling alone permits under compute limits.

entry.title: PARTE: Plane-Assisted Robust Transformation Estimation for Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Abolfazl Babanazari, Carson Cramer, Tyler Summers, Carlos Nieto, Kaveh Fathian

entry.summary: PARTE is a global point-cloud registration method that uses planar structures as complementary evidence rather than discarding them, introducing a Plane Context Histogram descriptor and a two-level matching procedure to find reliable plane correspondences. It targets registration under low overlap, repetitive geometry, and noisy correspondences dominated by outliers.

entry.title: Contact-Stable Deformable Tissue Simulation Using Implicit Integration and Live-Pose Grasp Constraints for Laparoscopic Surgery Robot Policy Evaluation

author.name: Juahn Oh, Dongho Yee, Jinseok Lee, Jiyul Lee, Yechan Seo, Seong Jeong, Minsung Kim, Seonho Shim, Younghoon Noh, Hyuk Choi, Youngbin Kong, Hyoun-Joong Kon

entry.summary: The authors build a surgical simulation in which deformable tissue is reconstructed from fixed-view RGB-D recordings, made watertight and tetrahedralised, and operated on by two Franka FR3 arms through trocars; the core contribution is numerical and contact design (implicit integration, live-pose grasp constraints) keeping grasping and lifting stable. The pipeline ran unchanged across thirteen organs from three specimens with no inverted elements.

entry.title: SG-CPG: Severity-Gated Central Pattern Generators for Adaptive Quadruped Locomotion under Continuous Actuator Degradation

author.name: Adarsh Kumar Kosta, Kaushik Roy

entry.summary: Inspired by how animals unload a weakened limb rather than switching gaits discretely, SG-CPG preserves a frozen healthy locomotion policy and adds two severity-driven gates: a residual gate that re-coordinates all four legs and an amplitude gate that progressively shortens the weakened leg's stride. This enables graded adaptation of quadruped locomotion under continuous actuator degradation.

entry.title: Predict Before You Step: Auditable Occupancy Forecasting for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance under Sparse Guidance

author.name: Yuhui Mao, Fen Liu, Shenghai Yuan, Tianxin Hu, Ruimeng Liu, Rong Su

entry.summary: Introduces LOOP, a local avoidance policy for legged robots that forecasts future occupancy over a 1-second horizon from LiDAR and ego-velocity histories, bridging sparse waypoint guidance and a frozen locomotion controller at 50 Hz. The learned flow and visibility gates produce an explicit, inspectable prediction interface, achieving 57.1% head-on success against obstacles moving at 2.5 m/s in Isaac Lab evaluations.

entry.title: Leveraging Vision-Based Point Cloud Map Priors for Camera-Based 3D Object Detection and Online Vectorized HD Mapping

author.name: Markus K\"appeler, Rohit Mohan, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: The authors propose a framework that builds a static point cloud prior map from prior camera traversals (using Pi3X with DINOv3-augmented points) and retrieves local prior patches at runtime to improve camera-based 3D object detection and online vectorized HD mapping. This avoids the expensive LiDAR sensors typically required for explicit point-cloud map priors.

entry.title: Optimal Tradeoffs Between Network Size and Parameter Magnitude in Neural Approximation and Minimax Regression

author.name: Baicheng Li, Zuowei Shen, Haizhao Yang, Shijun Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes sharp tradeoffs between network width and weight-magnitude bounds when approximating Holder-smooth functions, using a simple bounded 1-Lipschitz dyadic-triangular activation. It derives matching upper and lower bounds on Lp approximation error as a function of both width N and parameter cap T, quantifying how two different resources (size and magnitude) jointly determine statistical accuracy.

entry.title: The First American Bill to Ban Superintelligent AI Is Here

author.name: Andrea_Miotti

entry.summary: Reports that Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, the first US bill proposing to ban development of superintelligent AI. The post comes from ControlAI, an advocacy group that has briefed hundreds of lawmakers and previously supported a similar UK bill, and it praises the bill's focus while suggesting a more narrowly tailored version could work better.

entry.title: Efficient Iterative Retrieval with Heterogeneous Batching

author.name: Dohyun Park, Hubertus Franke, Daniel G. Waddington, Swaminathan Sundararaman, Yongjoo Park

entry.summary: Orthrus is a serving system that batches embedding and generative workloads together in a unified inference loop, addressing the low throughput and poor GPU utilization that arise when retrieval pipelines run these model types in isolation. It uses chunked embedding and adaptive batch composition to eliminate computational bubbles under dynamic workloads.

entry.title: SMTB: Fast Structure-Mapping with Tight Bounds

author.name: Daniel Weitekamp, Christopher MacLellan

entry.summary: Introduces SMTB, a new structure-mapping algorithm for analogy-making that is 5-15x faster than the classic Structure-Mapping Engine and about 50% better at finding mappings in large nested domains. It is part of the Cognitive Rule Engine project, a Python-accessible framework wrapping C++ implementations of core cognitive-system algorithms.

entry.title: ChainUQ: Reasoning Consistency-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models

author.name: Dahai Yu, Rongchao Xu, Lin Jiang, Ximiao Li, Guang Wang

entry.summary: ChainUQ is an uncertainty quantification framework for LLM reasoning that measures logical consistency between intermediate claims and final conclusions rather than relying solely on token-level probabilities. It introduces mechanisms to dynamically calibrate confidence using the structural logic of the generated reasoning chain.

entry.title: Identifying Intelligent Processes via Online Sequential Testing

author.name: Aritra Das, Debayan Gupta

entry.summary: This work formalizes the problem of identifying which LLM from a known set is being interacted with, as a two-level active sequential hypothesis testing problem: an outer probe-design stage that selects evaluation environments, and an inner identification stage that uses them sequentially. The framing connects LLM fingerprinting to classical statistical testing theory.

entry.title: MorphoSHAP: Rethinking the Unit of Attribution in Explanation for Deep Visual Models

author.name: Anirudh Prabhakaran, Alexandre Rocchi, Gianni Franchi

entry.summary: Proposes MorphoSHAP, a model-agnostic post-hoc attribution method that uses morphological shapes from the Tree of Shapes as players in a Shapley game, yielding explanations of where evidence lies, what structure carries it, and how strongly it affects predictions. This shared morphological vocabulary enables spatial, textual, and global class-level explanations beyond per-image heatmaps.

entry.title: Does AI Save Time on Product Design? A Randomized Controlled Experiment of AI Prompt-to-Design Workflows

author.name: Remy Stewart, Olabode Anise, Andrew Hogan, Augustus Griffin

entry.summary: This randomized controlled trial with 50 product designers and 50 product managers measured time savings from Figma Make's prompt-to-design workflow on standardized design tasks. Among completers, access to the AI tool was associated with roughly 20% shorter completion times, providing some of the first experimental evidence on AI in product design.

entry.title: QUARTET: Quad-branch cross-Attention and Random-walk Traces for Enhancing Transformers on Relational Graphs

author.name: Kyaw Hpone Myint, Nan Jiang, Xiang Li, Zhe Wu, Alexandre G. R. Day, Pranab Mohanty, Giri Iyengar

entry.summary: QUARTET is a graph transformer for relational deep learning on multi-table databases that applies full self-attention on local subgraphs and enriches global context via cross-attention branches including Causal Random Walk traces, addressing limitations of the RelGT model's loose local sampling and seed-feature-only global memory. It targets state-of-the-art performance on RelBench-style benchmarks.

entry.title: Tail-Aware Geometry Learning for Conformal Ellipsoids

author.name: Xiang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a tail-aware geometry learning framework for multivariate conformal prediction that decouples tail sensitivity in nonconformity-score geometry from the final coverage guarantee. Using a two-split design, it learns the metric matrix via volume minimization under a CVaR constraint, then applies standard conformal calibration to retain finite-sample coverage. This improves efficiency of multivariate prediction sets by accounting for tail residual severity.

entry.title: When Labels Are Scarce: An Oscillatory State Space Model for Vibration Diagnosis

author.name: Mainak Mallick, Seung-Kyum Choi

entry.summary: DualRes is a compact oscillatory state-space model for machine fault diagnosis from vibration signals, combining two spectral views with selective oscillatory memory that learns how long to retain temporal patterns. The encoder has only 39,528 parameters, targeting edge-device inference, and evaluation spans six bearing datasets plus a gearbox benchmark with recording-level splits that separate data efficiency from repeated exposure. It targets low-label industrial condition monitoring.

entry.title: CVaR anchor regression protects against rare shifts

author.name: Malte Londschien

entry.summary: Proposes CVaR anchor regression, which replaces the average of squared mean residuals across environments with a tail average to protect against rare, large distribution shifts without overly shrinking accuracy on common environments. The method provides exact worst-case risk guarantees under linear structure while avoiding pitfalls of applying CVaR or GroupDRO directly to prediction risks.

entry.title: KATOsuper: Surrogate-accelerated neural topology optimization with sensitivity-consistent Fourier neural operators

author.name: Shengyu Yan, Jasmin Jelovica

entry.summary: KATOsuper couples neural-reparameterized topology optimization with a sensitivity-consistent Fourier neural operator, deriving deployed sensitivities via automatic differentiation through the predicted objective field. This fixes gradient inconsistency between objectives and sensitivities that destabilizes prior surrogate-based topology optimization.

entry.title: FairTest: Search-Based Fairness Testing for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Systems

author.name: Xiaotong Wang, Xuan Xie

entry.summary: FairTest is a search-based testing method that uncovers unfair executions of multi-agent RL policies, combining three fitness functions that measure performed unfairness, predict it from abstract state features, and prioritize tests. It addresses the neglected problem that high team return does not imply fair reward distribution among agents.

entry.title: Improving Ensemble Filters with Flow Matching

author.name: Haoyuan Chen, Alexandre Thi\'ery

entry.summary: Introduces the Flow Ensemble Filter (FlowEF), which uses conditional flow matching to transport forecast ensembles from a classical baseline filter to an analysis ensemble in data assimilation, learning a nonlinear update conditioned on baseline ensembles and observations. This overcomes the affine Gaussian restrictions of classical ensemble filters, particularly under sparse observations.

entry.title: Local Geometric Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction with Applications to Diffusion Path Monte Carlo and the Proximal Sampler

author.name: Stefan Oberd\"orster

entry.summary: This theory paper introduces local geometric mixing, requiring geometric convergence to equilibrium over finitely many transitions, and establishes bounds via Dobrushin contraction. It applies the framework to Diffusion Path Monte Carlo and the Proximal Sampler, providing mixing guarantees for both ideal and Metropolis-adjusted variants under minimal assumptions.

entry.title: NADI 2026: The Second Multidialectal Arabic Speech Processing Shared Task

author.name: Peter Sullivan, Bashar Talafha, Ahmed Ashraf, Fethi Bougares, Haroun Elleuch, Chiyu Zhang, AbdelRahim Elmadany, Youssef Mohamed, Salima Mdhaffar, Yannick Est\`eve, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Hamzah Luqman, Nizar Habash, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed

entry.summary: NADI 2026 is the seventh edition of the Arabic dialect identification shared task series, now spanning ASR, spoken dialect ID, TTS, speech translation, and spoken language understanding under realistic low-bandwidth, mixed-dialect, and zero-shot conditions. It drew 21 teams from 13+ countries with 48 test submissions.

entry.title: Evaluating Feedback Focus and Pedagogical Adaptivity in LLM-Generated Feedback on Student Writing

author.name: Norah Almousa, Shayan Peyghambari Oskoui, Raquel Coelho, Gayle Rogers, Xiang Lorraine Li, Diane Litman

entry.summary: The study refines Narciss's taxonomy into seven feedback focus types and uses it to annotate teacher and LLM-generated feedback across three university writing courses, releasing the FeedType benchmark covering six LLMs under three prompting strategies. It examines whether LLM feedback matches expert pedagogical practices in focus and adaptivity, an aspect previously overlooked in evaluation.

entry.title: Diverse by Design: Architectural Constraints for Prototype-Based Interpretability

author.name: Xinmiao Lin, Matthew Wright

entry.summary: DAPL enforces prototype diversity through architectural constraints rather than regularization, using multi-head self-attention with strict one-to-one attention-to-prototype mapping and foreground-aware training to focus prototypes on meaningful regions. It also introduces evaluation metrics for prototype coverage and diversity in case-based-reasoning networks.

entry.title: CereVLA: Cerebellum-Inspired Consequence-Aware Residual Governance for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Execution

author.name: Shuai Zeng, Yuxuan Liang, Hangmiao Hu, Fobao Zhou, Zixiang Wang, Wenxi Hong, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: Presents CereVLA, a framework that adds lightweight flow-based residual refinement and predictive consequence evaluation to frozen vision-language-action policies, correcting accumulated errors in action-chunked execution without retraining. Inspired by cerebellar consequence-aware correction in motor control.

entry.title: GaussianDS: Depth-supervised Semantic Gaussian Splatting for Scene Understanding

author.name: Yufei Zhang, Chenlu Zhan, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: GaussianDS tackles semantic drift and boundary leakage when lifting view-dependent 2D foundation-model outputs into 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, treating semantic lifting as a supervision-alignment problem that jointly optimizes RGB, rendered depth, and compact semantics from scratch. It uses a pose-aware pseudo-video trajectory with SAM2-derived consistent masks. This improves open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding quality.

entry.title: History-Conditioned Flow Matching for Probabilistic Dynamics of Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots

author.name: Hang Yang, Tingcong Liu, Junjie Xiong, Fangju Yang, Ke Wu

entry.summary: The paper develops a history-conditioned, physics-informed flow-matching framework for probabilistic dynamics prediction of tendon-driven continuum robots, predicting distributions of next complete joint configurations from motion and actuation histories and recursively sampling future whole-body motions. It addresses irreducible uncertainty from friction, transmission, and material behavior that deterministic models miss.

entry.title: Dual Covariance Gaussian Splatting SLAM: Decoupling Rendering and Registration for Robust Real-Time Tracking

author.name: Edward Beng Wai Tan, Siew-Kei Lam

entry.summary: The paper identifies a conflict in 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM where one Gaussian covariance must serve both photometric rendering and frame registration. It proposes a dual-covariance parameterization keeping a rendering covariance optimized by the mapper and a tracking covariance from an RGB-D noise model, using tracking covariances as Gaussian anchors for directional constraints.

entry.title: Sometimes You Gotta Run Before You Can Walk: Run-then-Walk Scheduling Strategy for VLM Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuqi Ye, Shangkun Sun, Junhong Lin, Jiayi Zhao, Changhao Peng, Wei Zheng, Guoqing Liu, Tiesong Zhao, Wei Gao

entry.summary: The paper identifies two regimes in GRPO-style RL for VLM driving planners: a progress-seeking Run-GRPO regime and a safety-restoring Walk-GRPO regime, and proposes a two-stage reward scheduling strategy that runs exploration first, then restores safety. This achieves better performance and faster convergence than single-recipe training.

entry.title: Benchmarking Robots for Everyday Environments: From Lab Experiments to Real-World Operations

author.name: Raphael Memmesheimer, Martina Overbeck, Dominik Beyer, Bj\"orn Kral, Sabine Bellmann, Sven Schneider, Jan Zimmermann, Anna-Maria Meer, Medina Klicic, Simone Roth, Carolin Stra{\ss}mann, Alexander Arntz, Marlene Wessels, Johannes Kraus, Paul Schweidler, Tristan Schnell, Christoph Zimmermann, Benedikt Pulver, Wilhelm Stork, Martin Gersch, Sven Behnke, Arne R\"onnau

entry.summary: Introduces an interdisciplinary framework for benchmarking robots deployed in public environments, evaluating three robots across park cleaning, underpass cleaning, and library assistance over a three-year process with seven benchmarking events and six on-site evaluations. The work bridges lab metrics and real-world requirements, assessing both technical performance and societal implications of robots in unstructured human environments.

entry.title: FREESIA: Covariance-Aware Posterior Transport for Expressive and Scalable Data Assimilation

author.name: Shiwei Ni, Yangwen Zhang, Hang Qi, Xiaofei Guan, Lili Ju

entry.summary: FREESIA is a training-free, asymptotically exact posterior transport method for data assimilation that handles multimodal posteriors from nonlinear or non-injective observation operators under high-dimensional sparse observations. It combines a covariance-aware posterior transport scheme with optimal-transport-flavored updates to overcome the distributional limits of ensemble filters and the structural errors of training-free generative filters like EnSF and EnFF.

entry.title: Learning to Fluctuate: Statistical Foundations for Causal Tabular Pretraining

author.name: Zhiheng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes fluctuation-supervised pretraining (FSP) for causal tabular foundation models, where synthetic tables are labeled with average treatment effects plus efficient influence-function fluctuations, enabling deployment as a single frozen forward pass. It proves an endpoint transition showing full fluctuation supervision makes the Gaussian label observable and reduces causal label-priori ambiguity relative to shrinkage-style supervision.

entry.title: MedGate-Fusion: Integrating First-Encounter Semantic Narratives and Physiological Biomarkers for Prospective Stroke Risk Stratification

author.name: Hemn Khdr, Mohammad Noaeen, Karim Keshavjee, Aziz Guergachi, Zahra Shakeri

entry.summary: MedGate-Fusion is a multi-modal gated architecture combining transformer embeddings of first-encounter clinical narratives with ten routine biomarkers for five-year stroke risk prediction in primary care. It uses a large Canadian primary care dataset (over 100,000 patients derived from roughly 800,000 encounters) and takes explicit care to reduce target leakage from diagnostic mentions in notes.

entry.title: ChatT2: An Adaptive Framework for Developing a Large Language Model-Based Agent for Natural Product Domain Research

author.name: Yihan Wang, Qiandi Gao, Yihui Zhuang, Liangjun Ge, Heqian Zhang, Jiaquan Huang, Zhiwei Qin

entry.summary: Introduces ChatT2, an LLM-based agent for bacterial type II polyketide research built in a mentor-executor-evaluator multiagent framework that automates bioinformatics and data-analysis workflows for novices. It targets a structurally distinct, therapeutically important natural-product family.

entry.title: TCMaster: Confidence-Aware Querying and Workload-Guided Physical Design for Multi-Source Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Zheng Chen, Yuzhu Li, Haoxuan Li, Zhongde Zhang, Lianshun Jin, Peiwu Qin

entry.summary: Builds a Traditional Chinese Medicine knowledge graph of roughly 221K entities and 723K edges integrating pharmacopoeias, prescriptions, molecular databases, and LLM-extracted micro-semantics, with provenance-level confidence on edges. It adds confidence-aware Cypher query rewriting, multi-hop path ranking policies, and workload-guided physical design optimizations on Neo4j.

entry.title: CausalLoss-Fin: Attributing Financial-Agent Loss to Decisions and Infrastructure Faults

author.name: Abhishek Sharma

entry.summary: This work critiques agent-step attribution methods that charge all financial losses to agent decisions even when infrastructure faults (e.g., dropped settlement messages) were the true cause. On a replayable benchmark with an explicit fault process, it uses interventions on both agent and infrastructure actions and a telescoping identity to split loss exactly into infrastructure effect, policy differential, and other components.

entry.title: When Big Data Becomes a Curse: Spatial Heterogeneity and the Limits of Learning from Passive Acoustic Monitoring Data

author.name: Gabriel Spadon, Wayne Renaud, Priyanka Aravindan

entry.summary: Analyzing 908,072 AIS-labeled recordings from 38 deployments in Atlantic Canada, this paper shows that passive acoustic monitoring archives are so confounded by deployment, season, and hardware that cross-season transfer performs barely above chance for the ecological target (AIS contact) while the same descriptors easily identify stations and hydrophone models. It is a cautionary demonstration that big, clustered datasets can encode spurious spatial heterogeneity rather than signal.

entry.title: Predictive Uncertainty for Neural CAE Surrogates

author.name: Kaustubh Tangsali, Mohammad Amin Nabian, Kelvin Lee, Carmelo Gonzales, Sanjay Choudhry

entry.summary: Evaluates how established uncertainty quantification methods, including a Gaussian-process-based approach, Monte Carlo dropout, and deep ensembles, behave when adapted to geometry-conditioned neural surrogates for computer-aided engineering. It compares them on three large industry-relevant CAE datasets for external aerodynamics and crash dynamics, assessing uncertainty magnitudes and spatial localization.

entry.title: A Practical Recipe for Semi-Supervised Federated ASR: Online Pseudo-Labels with Server Update Stabilization

author.name: Wonho Bae, Zakaria Aldeneh, Martin Pelikan, Jan "Honza" Silovsky, Tatiana Likhomanenko, Sheikh Shams Azam

entry.summary: Studies semi-supervised federated learning for ASR, showing that closing the gap to fully-supervised federated training hinges on two coupled design axes: the teacher generating pseudo-labels and the server-side anchor updates stabilizing training. A per-client online teacher diverges alone but matches or beats broadcast global teachers once stabilized.

entry.title: RGSQ: Riemannian Geometry-Sensitive Quantization for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhiping Wu, Dongdong Ren, Yangchengyu Zhou, Zhengjie Zhang, Wenbin Li, Hongbing Pan, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Proposes RGSQ, which reformulates post-training quantization for large vision-language models as reconstruction on a Riemannian geometry rather than under an isotropic Euclidean error assumption, addressing uneven bit-width distribution and inconsistent low-bit performance when adapting unimodal PTQ methods to VLMs.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Hyperbolic Residual Quantization

author.name: Alessio Colombo, Melika Ayoughi

entry.summary: Proposes a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual vector quantization that fixes geometric inconsistencies in naive hyperbolic extensions, including non-associative hyperbolic addition and geometry-blind gradient estimation. The method aligns the coarse-to-fine structure of residual codes with hierarchical latent geometry in both forward and backward passes.

entry.title: TraceVIC: Causal Reasoning over Code Evolution for Identifying Vulnerability-Inducing Commits

author.name: Fnu Tanish, Samiha Shimmi, Samikshya Chapagain, Hamed Okhravi, Mona Rahimi, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: TraceVIC reframes vulnerability-inducing commit identification as causal reasoning over how vulnerability-relevant code evolves across revisions, rather than positional heuristics like git blame's earliest or most recent modification. The approach traces code evolution across multiple revisions to locate the commit that introduced the vulnerable condition.

entry.title: The Drift Contract: Spectral Updates for Depth-Robust Local Learning

author.name: Fabien Polly

entry.summary: The paper applies Muon-style spectral update geometry (momentum orthogonalization with spectral step scaling) to per-layer local learning, an unexplored intersection. On CIFAR-10 MLP benchmarks, a single step-size setting works across widths 128-2048 and depths 12-48, while local Adam requires per-depth retuning and collapses at depth 48.

entry.title: Data-driven discrete-time deep recurrent neural network-based modeling for dissipative systems

author.name: Tuan Luong, Hyungpil Moon

entry.summary: DissipNet is a deep discrete-time recurrent network that enforces dissipativity through structural weight constraints and a dedicated training algorithm, preserving stability of learned dynamics with formal Lyapunov-theoretic analysis. It targets the physical AI goal of models that both predict accurately and respect fundamental physical properties. This contributes to trustworthy learned models of real-world dynamical systems.

entry.title: Live Assistant: Learning Whether, When, and Whom to Assist in Real-World Live Social Streams

author.name: Shujian Gao, Jiamei Yan, Yuchen Yang, Penghao Zhou, Qinglei Wang, Tiehan Fan, Yuan Wang, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-gang Jiang

entry.summary: Live Assistant formulates assistance in livestreams as four coupled decisions: whether to act, when to act, whom to address, and what to communicate, using an autoregressive policy over audio, video, comments, gifts, and room metadata at 10-second intervals. The policy chooses among observing, memorizing a private semantic update, or answering. It represents an ambitious mixed-initiative assistant benchmarked in real-world social streaming environments.

entry.title: Active Learning for Biodiversity Monitoring: From Label Efficiency to Reliable Ecological Inference

author.name: Ben McEwen, Shiqi Zhang, Dan Stowell

entry.summary: This paper addresses how limited expert annotation budgets in biodiversity monitoring should be divided across model training, validation, and ecological inference, arguing that active learning for label efficiency alone does not guarantee reliable downstream ecological conclusions. It contextualizes passive acoustic and camera-trap data flows against expert capacity constraints. The work reframes active learning evaluation toward end-to-end monitoring-program needs.

entry.title: Efficient Linear Bandits via Cluster-Aware Sketching

author.name: Hantao Yang, Hong Xie, Defu Lian

entry.summary: CS-LB improves computational efficiency of high-dimensional linear bandits with finite arm sets by combining matrix sketching with a clustering mechanism that preserves full covariance information per cluster, avoiding the vacuous linear regret that fixed-size sketches like SOFUL can incur with heavy spectral tails. The method guarantees regret convergence while reducing the O(d^2) per-round update cost. It is a theory-aware efficiency contribution to the bandit literature.

entry.title: When Adaptation Hurts: Split Sensitivity and Person-Level Negative Transfer in Federated Wearable Onboarding

author.name: Rahil Aftab, Vineet Kumar Rakesh, Soumya Mazumdar, Tapas Samanta

entry.summary: Evaluates six federated wearable onboarding strategies under a leakage-controlled protocol and shows that favorable average accuracy masks person-level negative transfer: one user's balanced accuracy reaches 95-97% while others average only 78-83%, and completing outer-person rotations changes prior conclusions. The paper highlights how frozen folds and window-level evaluation can overstate personalization benefits.

entry.title: A Shared Encoder Is Not a Shared Task: Conditional Comparison for Deep Expert Pools

author.name: Kentaro Oda

entry.summary: Demonstrates that sharing a deep encoder does not resolve the extrapolation confound in task-comparison scores, with input rotations inflating deep exchange scores while representation-novelty scores miss label-permutation drift; a conditional two-discriminator discrepancy in the embedding space corrects both. The two-axis gate is applied to a mixture-of-heads lifecycle for conditional task comparison.

entry.title: Linear RNN Scaling Laws: When Longer Sequences Beat More Sequences

author.name: Ziyan Chen, Zhongzhu Zhou, Peilin Liu, Ding-Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: This theoretical work derives scaling laws for autoregressive language models in a tractable teacher-student setting where a latent linear RNN generates data and a sketched linear recurrent student is trained on next-token prediction. It analyzes how sketch dimension (model size) and sequence length/count trade off under power-law spectral assumptions.

entry.title: Log-Depth Recurrent Language Modeling

author.name: Yiqin Wang, Nuri Cingillioglu, Charles Pert

entry.summary: This paper extends balanced-tree recursive operators from sequence encoding to autoregressive language modeling, computing all prefix representations with logarithmic depth and linear runtime. Initial experiments show robust length extrapolation and performance approaching ALiBi-based transformers, positioning it as an alternative architecture.

entry.title: Even Sharper Bounds for Transductive Learning and Its Applications

author.name: Yingzhen Yang

entry.summary: Introduces Sharper Transductive Local Complexity (STLC), a localized complexity method giving excess-risk bounds for transductive learning under sampling without replacement. Using log-Sobolev inequalities and peeling arguments, it removes logarithmic confidence factors present in earlier transductive bounds, matching inductive local Rademacher complexity guarantees.

entry.title: Tight Regret Bound for Online Inverse Linear Optimization via Multiscale Matrix Weights

author.name: Shinsaku Sakaue

entry.summary: Gives a randomized algorithm for online inverse linear optimization achieving O(sqrt(d)) expected regret against a fixed unknown linear utility, without horizon knowledge, using matrix multiplicative weights on polynomial feature scales. The dependence on dimension is optimal up to constants given the known Omega(sqrt(d)) lower bound.

entry.title: Median Temporal Ensembling: Training-Free Robust Aggregation for Action-Chunked Visuomotor Policies

author.name: Yuhang Jiang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the vulnerability of exponentially weighted temporal ensembling in action-chunked visuomotor policies, showing its breakdown point is zero under corrupted predictions. It contrasts metric versus combinatorial robustness guarantees and proposes a training-free median-based aggregation plus encoder adversarial fine-tuning.

entry.title: Benchmarking Active Spot Selection for Cost-Efficient Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Zheyu Zhu, Junchao Zhu, Fengbei Liu, Tianyuan Yao, Gelei Xu, John Cannon, Haichun Yang, Yuankai Huo, Mert R. Sabuncu, Ruining Deng

entry.summary: A retrospective benchmark comparing active learning strategies (MC-dropout uncertainty, temporal output discrepancy, CoreSet, TypiClust-style diversity) against uniform random sampling for selecting spots in spatial transcriptomics. It highlights how high-dimensional continuous expression and spatial correlation complicate standard active learning assumptions.

entry.title: The Type-II Error of Test Supermartingales: e-Power versus the Chernoff-Stein Exponent

author.name: Patrick Forr\'e

entry.summary: Studies anytime-valid sequential hypothesis testing with test supermartingales, proving that e-power (the mean log growth rate maximized by Kelly-type e-variables) by itself bounds nothing about type-II error, constructing counterexamples of fixed e-power with near-certain non-rejection. It contrasts e-power with the Chernoff-Stein exponent framework.

entry.title: EvEMTBench: An Open Benchmark for Machine Learning in Power System Protection

author.name: Julian Oelhaf, Georg Kordowich, Christian Bergler, Andreas Maier, Johann J\"ager, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: EvEMTBench is an open, versioned benchmark for ML-based power system protection spanning four grids from 20-345 kV, with 12 protection and event-analysis functions instantiated as 24 scored tasks. It fixes evaluation choices, defines distribution shifts and cross-grid transfer settings, and includes leakage controls for reproducible comparison.

entry.title: ForgetMimic: Motion Unlearning for Reinforcement Learning Humanoid Control

author.name: Xukun Luan, Zhongxiang Lei, Chen Gong, Shaowei Li, Yuanguo Bi, Jinyan Liu

entry.summary: ForgetMimic is the first motion-level unlearning method for physical humanoid control, enabling removal of specific motions from RL policies trained on human demonstrations to address safety, privacy, and copyright concerns such as GDPR right-to-be-forgotten. The work extends machine unlearning concepts into embodied control.

entry.title: Realize What Matters: Principled Context Representation for Large-Scale Reasoning

author.name: Michael Theologitis, Dean Light, Shuyue Stella Li, Benjamin Newman, Yulia Tsvetkov, Dan Suciu

entry.summary: Drawing on the cognitive theory of relevance realization, this position-style paper proposes principles for designing AI systems that construct effective representations of very large context (graphs, textual memories, retrieval collections) for reasoning in science, medicine, law, and finance. It argues representation design, currently ad hoc, determines what downstream reasoning is possible.

entry.title: Phonemizing User-Generated Text: A Benchmark, Taxonomy, and Compositional Approach

author.name: MinJu Jeon, Younghan Park, Han Sung Park, Jong-Hwan Kim, Dong-Jin Kim, Hoyeon Lee

entry.summary: UGTPhon is the first G2P benchmark for user-generated text (abbreviations, slang) in English, Vietnamese, and Korean, with an inference-grounded taxonomy for diagnosis. It reveals a systematic canonical-to-non-canonical gap of up to 66.8 PER points even in frontier LLMs and proposes a compositional lookup-plus-staged-decoding baseline that improves ByT5 and Qwen2.5-0.5B backbones.

entry.title: The Path Matters: Evaluating Small Language Models Beyond Answer Accuracy in KGQA

author.name: Eduin E. Hernandez, Sergio A. Diaz, Luis F. Garcia, Nurassyl Askar, Stefano Rini

entry.summary: Using the THESEUS framework, the authors isolate graph navigation from other KGQA stages by using frozen small language models as local action policies that select executable graph actions hop by hop. This decoupling reveals whether SLMs can faithfully execute reasoning paths and attributes failures to navigation rather than answer generation, going beyond end-to-end accuracy.

entry.title: Complementary Roles of Activation and Parametric Memory in Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Miaohe Niu, Runsong Zhao, Xinyu Liu, Bo Jin, Yucheng Qiao, Chunliang Zhang, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: The paper systematically investigates how test-time activation memory (KV caches) and parametric memory (updated parameters) interact in LLM few-shot learning. It finds activation memory superior for factual recall, parametric memory not consistently better for task learning, and that composite tasks like Conditional Arithmetic require synergy of both memory types, supported by neuron-level analysis.

entry.title: Agentic Governance and Adversarial Verification for Policy-Constrained LLM Healthcare Appeal Generation

author.name: Harshil Lodhiya, Alex McManus, Reese Walker

entry.summary: AGVF proposes a multi-agent architecture for medical-necessity appeal generation that models the task as a Constrained Markov Decision Process over five agents covering policy formalization, evidence retrieval, gap analysis, adversarial critique, and synthesis. The system targets a costly healthcare workflow where single-agent LLM pipelines introduce unsupported clinical details and lose hierarchical policy structure.

entry.title: Anatomy-Aware Synthesis of Post-Contrast Breast MRI from Pre-Contrast Images

author.name: Zhengbo Zhou, Dooman Arefan, Lin Gu, Ufara Zuwasti Curran, Shandong Wu

entry.summary: An anatomy-aware image-to-image translation framework synthesizes post-contrast breast MRI from pre-contrast scans, using breast mask consistency plus lesion- and background-parenchymal-enhancement supervision, validated on 649 patients. It outperforms Pix2Pix, Pix2PixHD, and diffusion baselines and improves downstream Ki-67 classification.

entry.title: Beyond Balanced Accuracy: A Resolution and Parity-Controlled Benchmark for Vision-Language and Vision-Only Defect Assessment in UAV Power-Line Inspection

author.name: Linghao Zhang, Siyu Xiang, Junwei Kuang, Peiyu Yi

entry.summary: Re-examines claims that VLMs outperform task-specific vision backbones for UAV power-line defect assessment using ElecVQA-Bench with 56,972 items and six controlled evaluation choices. When vision backbones are given the same pixel budget as the VLM preprocessor, gaps against InternVL3.5-8B shrink dramatically, undermining naive superiority claims.

entry.title: DMM-Align: Closed-Loop Optimization for 2D-3D Registration with Dual-Role Diffusion

author.name: Chongjian Wang, Junjie Gao

entry.summary: DMM-Align couples correspondence refinement, pose estimation, and representation learning in a closed loop through a shared differentiable geometric state, using diffusion in two coordinated roles for 2D-3D registration. It targets brittle failure under low overlap, occlusion, repetitive structures, and cross-modal ambiguity, where errors propagate across levels. This could make registration pipelines substantially more reliable in challenging real scenarios.

entry.title: A comparative assessment of global building and settlement datasets across geographic and settlement contexts

author.name: Rufai Omowunmi Balogun, Caroline Margaux Gevaert, Capucine Riom, Derrick Mirindi, Aaron Opdyke, Hamed Alemohammad, Pierre Chrzanowski, Edward Charles Anderson

entry.summary: This study benchmarks seven global or near-global building and settlement datasets (Overture Maps, Global Building Atlas, 3D-GloBFP, Google OBT, Microsoft TEMPO, GHSL, WSF Tracker) against harmonized reference footprints across 135 study areas, combining detection, geometric, and aggregate-quantity accuracy with stratified analyses. It provides much-needed comparative evidence for products underpinning population mapping and disaster exposure assessment. The harmonized evaluation design is a community asset.

entry.title: A Unified Framework and Dataset for Oriented Object Visual Grounding in Remote Sensing

author.name: Zeyu Ding, Yong Zhou, Jiaqi Zhao, Wen-Liang Du, Xixi Li, Hancheng Zhu, Rui Yao, Abdulmotaleb El Saddik

entry.summary: The paper introduces O2-VG, a family of models for oriented object visual grounding in remote sensing, addressing the inaccuracy of horizontal bounding boxes for arbitrarily oriented objects. It includes a cross-modality transformer (O2-VG-Trans), a prompt-free variant with universal oriented proposals (O2-VG-Uni), and an accompanying dataset. This provides both a methodological and data contribution for a practical remote sensing capability.

entry.title: Benchmarking Hyperspectral Foundation Models for Hyperspectral Unmixing

author.name: Edgard Dabier, Christophe Kervazo, Pietro Gori, Florence Tupin

entry.summary: The authors benchmark recently released hyperspectral foundation models on unmixing, the task of separating mixed spectra of overlapping materials. They identify a fundamental issue: vision transformer backbones with patchification worsen an already ill-posed low-resolution problem. The study provides a much-needed evaluation of foundation models on an understudied task and clarifies architectural limitations.

entry.title: When Visual Quality Misleads: Intent Recognition under Rendered Avatar Distortions

author.name: Ning-Hsuan Chang, Kai-Siang Ma, Yu-Chih Chen

entry.summary: A behavioral study showing that image/video quality metrics are poor proxies for communicative success in avatar streaming: some distorted renderings score above-average perceived quality yet degrade viewers' ability to recognize the intended action. The authors introduce a Misleading Quality construct and an Intent Quality Score combining recognition correctness and confidence across 2,688 human judgments.

entry.title: GINIO: A Geometric SO(3)-Equivariant Interface for Neural Inertial Odometry

author.name: Chankyo Kim, Minghan Zhu, Tzu-Yuan Lin, Avantika Rattan, Maani Ghaffari

entry.summary: Presents GINIO, an SO(3)-equivariant interface for neural inertial odometry ensuring learned motion measurements and covariances transform correctly under arbitrary IMU mounting rotations, plus a Last-Frame Alignment preprocessing step proven equivalent to world-frame training. The goal is learned inertial measurements usable consistently inside filtering pipelines regardless of sensor mounting.

entry.title: Digital Twin-Driven VR Teleoperation with Multi-View Spatial Perception for Surgical Robots

author.name: Chang Liu, Chenhao Yu, Honghao Zhao, Hao Ding, Haochen Wei, Adnan Munawar, Mathias Unberath, Peter Kazanzides

entry.summary: The paper presents a VR teleoperation platform for robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery where a digital twin built from markerless perception of the surgical environment is streamed to a head-mounted display, enabling multi-view rendering and improved depth perception beyond video pass-through. It could improve surgeon ergonomics and situational awareness.

entry.title: VisForce: Visual Grounding of Current and Desired Forces for Goal-Conditioned Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Jung-Woo Lee, Soo-Chul Lim

entry.summary: VisForce grounds contact forces visually for dexterous hand manipulation by rendering current and desired force cues at corresponding fingertip locations on wrist and goal images, then combining them via goal-conditioned cross-attention to produce force-aware actions. It is evaluated on real dexterous manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Manipulation with Stability Guarantees: Linear Deformable Objects with Non-negligible Physical Response Grasped at Multiple Location

author.name: Daniel Feliu-Talegon, Cosimo Della Santina

entry.summary: Addresses manipulation of linear deformable objects whose dynamics cannot be ignored, such as hoses and wiring harnesses, which most prior work excludes by assuming quasi-static behavior. The paper introduces a closed-loop control architecture recasting manipulation as shape regulation via forces at multiple fixed grasp points, backed by a fully dynamic model and stability analysis.

entry.title: MatchFusion: Explicit-Implicit Instance Matching for Spatio-Temporal Multimodal Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Jiajia Fu, Long Shi, Tianyu Du, Ruihang Li, Xian Wu, Lijun Zhao, Yingtao Zhang, Lining Sun, Ruifeng Li

entry.summary: MatchFusion is a learnable instance matching and fusion module for spatio-temporal, multimodal autonomous driving perception that combines attention-based contextual semantics with efficient structured-object-state association. It aims to produce reliable instance correspondences across LiDAR-camera and past-current interactions despite geometric and semantic discrepancies.

entry.title: Vision Foundation Models with Synthetic-Only Training for Monocular Spacecraft Pose Estimation

author.name: John Church, Vazghen Nikolian

entry.summary: The paper reports the lowest published mean rotation errors known on the SPEED+ lightbox and sunlamp test sets for known, non-cooperative spacecraft pose estimation, by adapting the DINOv3 self-supervised ViT foundation model within a heatmap-based architecture trained only on synthetic data. They also show the 840M-parameter model runs in about 134 ms per crop at 32 W on a Jetson Orin NX, demonstrating embedded feasibility.

entry.title: Empirical Auditing of Edge-Private Graph Generators

author.name: Anum Fatima, Stratis Limnios, James Adams, Lukasz Szpruch, Carsten Maple, Gesine Reinert, Andrew Elliott

entry.summary: This paper empirically audits privacy leakage in edge-private graph generators by testing whether outputs from edge-neighbouring inputs remain distinguishable, using statistically valid lower bounds on privacy loss. Comparing direct-edge, local-structural, and GNN-based attacks across two generators and two networks, it finds leakage is both mechanism- and network-dependent, with learned representations exposing information conventional local statistics miss.

entry.title: LexLattice: Multilingual Extractive Summarization via Neural Cellular Automata on Document Hierarchies

author.name: Sujay Uday Rittikar, Sheela Ramanna

entry.summary: LexLattice represents a legal act's hierarchy as a 2D semantic lattice and applies masked 2D neural cellular automata to consolidate distributed evidence before extractive selection. It achieves state-of-the-art ROUGE across all 24 EUR-Lex-Sum languages in multilingual and cross-lingual settings, beating instruction-tuned baselines while preserving verbatim traceability.

entry.title: Evolving Inspectable O-RAN Slicing xApps with LLMs

author.name: Faezeh Dehghan Tarzjani, Bhaskar Krishnamachari

entry.summary: The paper uses LLMs to evolve O-RAN slicing controllers as compact, human-readable Python programs, scored offline in a calibrated simulator and deployed unchanged in the O-RAN control loop. This retains adaptability while making decision logic inspectable and editable by network operators, unlike opaque deep RL policies.

entry.title: Task-Induced Riemannian Metrics for Vision Transformer Feature Spaces

author.name: Andrew Bond, Ege Erdem \"Ozl\"u, Tuna \c{C}imen, Ilkin Umut Melanlioglu, Tolga Birdal, Erkut Erdem, Aykut Erdem

entry.summary: Proposes replacing Euclidean or cosine distances in ViT feature spaces with task-induced pullback metrics derived from the task-specific decoder Jacobian, characterizing when low-rank approximation of the metric is learnable via a matrix factorization analysis. The work grounds representation geometry in the actual downstream task.

entry.title: Nonequilibrium Phases of Repulsive Self-Attention: Chaos, Attention Condensation, and Emergent Locality

author.name: Qucheng Gao, Zuyi Yang, Xiao Chen

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes the nonequilibrium dynamics of a minimal recurrent transformer with normalized tokens and a negative value map, showing bifurcations from regular polygon fixed points to period-two motion, chaos, and cluster states as attention feedback strength increases. Despite temporal complexity, attention remains diffuse as N grows at finite temperature, with connections to attention condensation and emergent locality.

entry.title: Meet, Compare, or Abstain: LatWeave for Deterministic Multi-Hop Question Answering on Knowledge Lattices

author.name: Yuze Ren, Shaoheng Fan, Tao Wang, Yabo Yan, Han Han

entry.summary: LatWeave organizes knowledge into a multidimensional lattice and compiles multi-hop QA into three deterministic operators (meet, compare, abstain), confining LLMs to extraction and query planning while answer generation becomes auditable and hallucination-resistant. The design separates what is known from how to reason, enabling structural abstention.

entry.title: A Native-Reference Coordinate Geometry for L2 Pronunciation Deviation Using Self-Supervised Speech Models

author.name: Tina Raissi, Nhan Phan, Mikko Kurimo

entry.summary: The paper proposes evaluating second-language pronunciation by measuring distance of L2 speech to a low-dimensional reference subspace defined by native phone-class averages from self-supervised speech model representations. Unlike prior distance-based approaches, it requires no parallel recordings with matched content or dedicated pronunciation labels, and achieves strong negative Spearman correlations with human ratings.

entry.title: High Dynamic Range Video Reconstruction from Single-Exposure Raw Sequences

author.name: Tao Zhang, Peixian Su, Xingyu Gao, Yunhao Zou, Yu Lu, Zunjie Zhu, Bolun Zheng, Ying Fu, Chenggang Yan

entry.summary: RawHDRV is an end-to-end framework for HDR video reconstruction from single-exposure raw sequences, exploiting the linear response and channel-specific characteristics of Bayer data with channel-decomposition temporal alignment and fusion. It avoids the frame-rate and motion-alignment problems of alternating-exposure capture.

entry.title: Track2Art: Motion-Centric Articulated Object Model Recovery from 2D Point Trackers

author.name: Xiaotong Li, Yixiong Jing, Junsheng Ding, Weihang Li, Benjamin Busam, Guangming Wang, Brian Sheil

entry.summary: Presents Track2Art, a motion-centric framework that recovers articulated object models from RGB-D interaction videos by lifting tracked 2D points into persistent 3D trajectories, exploiting the hypothesis that coherent motion reveals rigid parts and relative motion reveals kinematic constraints. Aims at enabling robotic interaction with articulated objects.

entry.title: AstraLOD3: Zero-shot multimodal agentic reconstruction of LOD3 building models

author.name: Bryan G. Pantoja-Rosero

entry.summary: AstraLOD3 investigates whether a general-purpose multimodal foundation model can zero-shot reconstruct LOD3 building models via an agentic framework that dynamically selects and executes Python and Blender procedures under bounded autonomy, using multi-view images, calibrated cameras, and sparse SfM point clouds. Across 35 runs on benchmark buildings it reports mean FRDS results. This tests agentic, tool-using foundation models against purpose-built geometric pipelines in a structured 3D task.

entry.title: Learning from Humans for Proactive Assistance in Human-Robot Collaborative Transport

author.name: Elvin Yang, Christoforos Mavrogiannis

entry.summary: Studies collaborative human-robot transport of large or heavy objects, combining learned predictions of human collaborative behavior with compliant robot control so the robot both contributes efficiently and stays physically responsive. The approach learns from human-human transport data to balance efficiency and accommodation, unlike prior work that handles these separately.

entry.title: MedVLA: A Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Framework for Closed-Loop Precision Medical Robot Manipulation

author.name: Junjie Xie, Chuxuan He, Angen Ye, Yujia Song, Dapeng Zhang

entry.summary: MedVLA couples high-level multimodal reasoning with low-level function-constrained execution for precision medical robotics, replacing continuous action generation with structured function calls suited to strict safety and interpretability requirements.
