It includes a scalable multi-agent pipeline generating skill-oriented chain-of-thought training data and builds on multiple multimodal backbones.

entry.title: Generalizing Manipulation Skills with a Local Coding Agent

author.name: Raman Talwar, Elias Nijs, Andreas Verleysen, Francis wyffels

entry.summary: Investigates whether a local open-weight VLM, Qwen3.8-27B, driving a UR3e arm through a coding-agent harness can one-shot generalize to new task variations without additional programming or training, by writing and executing its own code over services implementing kinematics, safety limits, and classical computer vision. This tests open-weight models as a path away from fixed action interfaces in language-driven robotics.

entry.title: Lean Pool: An AI-Maintained Archive of Formalized Mathematics

author.name: Vasily Ilin

entry.summary: Lean Pool is a repository of formalized mathematics in the Lean proof assistant that is grown, maintained, and optimized by AI agents rather than human contributors. The paper describes infrastructure for an autonomous, continuously expanding library of machine-formalized mathematical knowledge.

entry.title: Robust Failure, Conservative Repair: Textual Knowledge Distillation from Cross-Model Failures

author.name: Andrew Ren, Haokun Liu, Chenhao Tan

entry.summary: This paper studies the instability of failure-based textual knowledge distillation, where task errors are distilled into rule atoms injected at inference time as cheat sheets. It defines rule atoms and characterizes how transferable knowledge can degrade into model-specific patches or be misapplied to unrelated cases, causing incorrect answer flips, and develops a more conservative repair pipeline.

entry.title: Transformer Heads Looking for Order

author.name: Jasper van Doornmalen, Alexander Kozachinskiy, Corinna Mathwieser, Tomasz Steifer, Felipe Urrutia, Jos\'{e} Verschae, Przemys{\l}aw Andrzej Wa{\l}\c{e}ga

entry.summary: A theory note proving that checking whether a bit sequence is ordered cannot be done by a 1-head 1-layer transformer but can be done with 2 heads, under a transformer model that includes an output MLP. This refines prior expressivity separations by relaxing architectural assumptions.

entry.title: When Are Aggregate Agent Traces Diagnosable? Traffic-Governed Interpretation and Calibrated Abstention

author.name: Peiying Zhu, Sidi Chang

entry.summary: This paper addresses the problem of diagnosing faults in closed-loop agent policies from runtime traces, noting that a fault may be invisible in aggregate traces if the policy rarely visits affected states. Using a simulated hotel-pricing agent, the authors propose gated diagnosability decisions with calibrated false-admission control on a clean stream before any signal analysis is performed.

entry.title: FairMon: A Tool for Monitoring and Visualizing Algorithmic Fairness

author.name: Jan Baumeister, Bernd Finkbeiner, Vladimir Krsmanovic, Frederik Scheerer, Julian Siber, Tobias Wagenpfeil

entry.summary: FairMon is a runtime monitoring tool for algorithmic fairness in high-stakes autonomous decision systems (credit, hiring, criminal justice), built on the RTLola specification language to support the human-oversight requirements of the EU AI Act. It addresses shortcomings of prior monitoring tools that were not designed for fairness oversight in critical scenarios.

entry.title: TREND-10K: A Comprehensive Dataset for Next-Generation Video Quality Assessment Based on Preference-Driven Media

author.name: Ziheng Jia, Zicheng Zhang, Junqi Zhang, Jiaying Qian, Jiarui Wang, Yushuo Zheng, Xiongkuo Min

entry.summary: TREND-10K is a 10,000-video dataset for video quality assessment targeting modern media such as professional short dramas and AI-generated content, with a trend-driven part and a static part. It aims to provide a unified evaluation framework reflecting how user-consumed video content is shifting away from traditional UGC.

entry.title: FISSION: Label Augmentation for Bot Detection

author.name: Sen Yang, Ignacy Nieweglowski, Aviv Yaish

entry.summary: This paper addresses the scarcity of reliable ground-truth labels for detecting bot accounts and coordinated influence operations. FISSION generates supervision automatically by splitting each account's activity into positively labeled sub-accounts, then trains embedding-based detection models that capture recurring behavioral regularities. The authors report that FISSION outperforms prior methods on Wikipedia sockpuppet detection and Twitter/X bot detection benchmarks.

entry.title: REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents

author.name: Tiantong Wu, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: REFLEX is an agent architecture using Jev as a fast typed decision layer that escalates to a strong LLM only on low confidence or generation needs. On a frozen 100-task benchmark it achieves 95% success with 72.7% fewer strong-model calls, though external BFCL and tau-style evaluations show limited advantage over a cheap generative cascade in some conditions.

entry.title: The Probabilistic Structure of Large Language Models

author.name: Adnan Aboulala\^a

entry.summary: Offers a self-contained probabilistic treatment of LLMs, describing them via probability measures on token sequences through autoregressive conditionals, formulating training as maximum-likelihood estimation, and viewing generation as sequential simulation of a stochastic process. It connects KL-divergence asymmetry to characteristic phenomena such as hallucination and mode collapse.

entry.title: Geometric and Semantic Coupling for Interaction Understanding in 3D Scenes

author.name: Hanyang Kong, Xingyi Yang

entry.summary: Introduces Segment-Snap, a method coupling part segmentation, handle detection, and articulation motion in 3D scenes by exploiting the physical relationship between parts and handles, using planar and upright priors to constrain motion without training a dedicated motion regressor. Information transfers between predictors are applied once without iterative feedback, evaluated on Articulate3D.

entry.title: Transformer-Informed Trajectory Optimization for Relative Motion in Cislunar Orbits

author.name: Walter J. Manuel, Yuji Takubo, Simone D'Amico

entry.summary: Extends the Autonomous Rendezvous Transformer (ART) to cislunar rendezvous, proximity operations, and docking for the first time, using transformer-generated warm starts to accelerate non-convex trajectory optimization in severely nonlinear and chaotic cislunar dynamics, especially near perilune.

entry.title: DefaultGNN: A Dual-Perspective GNN Framework for Predicting Corporate Default from Buyer-Seller Transaction Networks

author.name: Junghoon Kim, Hyunsung Kim, Seungyoon Choi, KyoungYong Park, Jihun Lee, YongGu Ji, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: Conducts a large-scale empirical study on six years of real-world electronic tax-invoice data linking transaction histories with default events, showing transaction-driven default risk is role-dependent and scale-dependent. It proposes DefaultGNN, a dual-perspective GNN over multiplex buyer-view and seller-view transaction networks for corporate default prediction.

entry.title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Panagiotis Michael, Moysis Symeonides, Demetris Trihinas

entry.summary: Benchmarks six time series foundation models against statistical baselines and supervised deep learning on energy, traffic, and financial data, examining the trade-off between point accuracy and probabilistic calibration. Finds TSFMs generally outperform baselines but exhibit a fundamental accuracy-versus-calibration trade-off, with xLSTM architectures calibrating better and patch-based transformers excelling at point accuracy.

entry.title: In-Context Guidance: Learning Inter-Task Synergies via Numerical Foundational Models for Few-Shot Multitask Optimization

author.name: Tingyang Wei, Haofeng Wu, Jiao Liu, Zhao Wei, Puay Siew Tan, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: Introduces ICG-MTO, a framework that uses frozen numerical foundation models (e.g., time-series pretrained models) via in-context learning to infer inter-task relationships in few-shot multitask optimization, reducing negative transfer under limited evaluation budgets. The three-stage pipeline constructs in-context queries from evaluated solutions and uses the model's predictions as auxiliary guidance.

entry.title: BAS-OPD: Budget-Aware Selective On-Policy Self-Distillation for Fine-Grained Multimodal Perception

author.name: Zihan Chen, Hengguang Zhou, Yuan Kang, Yiming Zhang, Wenhui Fang, Zenghui Ding, Yining Sun, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: The paper targets a weakness of multimodal LLMs: fine-grained visual perception where critical evidence appears only in small image regions. On-policy self-distillation can transfer privileged visual knowledge from informative views to full-image policies, but querying the teacher for every rollout is costly. BAS-OPD allocates teacher supervision under a limited query budget by selecting informative rollouts via random, uncertainty-based, or learned utility-based strategies while maintaining full-batch student generation.

entry.title: ABAI at COLIEE 2026 Task 1: Multi-Stage Retrieval with GraphRAG-Enhanced Meta-Learning, and a Post-Hoc Study of the Cross-Validation-to-Test Gap

author.name: Minhan Cho, Soyoung Park, Daejin Choi, Jinyoung Han

entry.summary: This system report presents a four-stage legal case retrieval pipeline (multi-view BM25 with reciprocal rank fusion, neural reranking, graph attention features over entity communities, and a LightGBM meta-learner) for COLIEE 2026 Task 1, plus an unusually honest post-hoc analysis of why test F1 (0.177) fell well below cross-validated F1 (0.311). The authors attribute the gap to a recall ceiling from suppressed cited passages, temporal distribution shift, and threshold miscalibration, and report ablations testing these hypotheses.

entry.title: AIGC Video Detection based on the fusion of spatial-frequency-optical flow multimodal features

author.name: S. Hong, X. Q. Wang, C. Zhang, J. C. Wang, P. X. Duan, Y. W. Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CrossAtt-VFD, a dual-branch detector for AI-generated video forgery that jointly analyzes spatial-frequency features and optical flow, exploiting the observation that generative models struggle to maintain cross-modal consistency between appearance and motion. Addresses the growing need for detectors that generalize across evolving synthesis techniques like Sora-class video generators.

entry.title: MAVP: Map-Aware Visuomotor Policies for Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Jinhe Tang, Ruixiao Dai, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: Presents MAVP, a framework improving mobile manipulation reliability by predicting explicit base-pose targets from a static map reconstructed from teleoperated demonstrations and tracking them with localization feedback. This provides consistent spatial supervision across demonstrations and reduces spatial misalignment failures during execution.

entry.title: Topology-Stratified Materials Discovery with A Flow-Based Generative Model

author.name: Jingyi Zhou, Oyshee Chowdhury, Noah Oyeniran, Chongze Hu

entry.summary: Develops UFO-MGen, a flow-based generative model that learns topological features of Wyckoff representations to generate crystal structures across wide structural and chemical spaces, targeting extreme-environment materials for aerospace and fusion applications. It reports the highest crystal generation success among compared state-of-the-art generative models.

entry.title: Measuring the Serving Stack Instead of the Model: Hidden Confounds in Local Tool-Use Evaluation

author.name: Lijuan Tang, Yuemeng Zheng

entry.summary: The paper shows that local LLM serving stacks confound tool-use evaluations: Ollama's static template flags reject some models' tool requests before inference, and harness failure metadata is lost, causing model non-calls to be misclassified. The authors quantify how measured tool-calling fidelity reflects serving-layer artifacts rather than model capability alone.

entry.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue

author.name: Haobo Zheng, Tan Tang, Yan Chen, Weijie Wang, Yingcai Wu

entry.summary: SpeakerMem-R1 proposes a speaker-centered dual-track memory architecture for long-term multi-party dialogue that handles message attribution, relational understanding, and state reconstruction from interleaved histories. It targets known failures of general-purpose LLM memory systems on multi-party benchmarks, where person and group relations are lost.

entry.title: CORE-STACK+: Meta-Learning for Deep Stacked Generalization

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad

entry.summary: This paper identifies two coupled failure modes in stacking heterogeneous vision backbones: ill-conditioning of the meta-learner due to prediction-space multicollinearity, and calibration collapse from naive linear stacking. CORE-STACK+ is a preconditioning pipeline that jointly targets conditioning and calibration, addressing gaps left by ridge regularization, greedy selection, model soups, and SWAG. It matters because ensembling is a dominant accuracy recipe and jointly handling both pathologies could yield more robust deployed ensembles.

entry.title: A Systematic Benchmark of Explainable Methods for Temporal Attribution in Sequential Recommendation Systems

author.name: Akash Pandey, Kanisha Shah, Addrish Roy, Dwipam Katariya, Hongyangyang Shi, Amanda Ding, Kalanand Mishra, Pranab Mohanty

entry.summary: This paper systematically benchmarks gradient-based, perturbation-based, and attention-based explainability methods for temporal attribution in deep sequential recommender systems built on CNN and Transformer architectures. It evaluates which past interactions drive recommendations, supporting developer audits and user-facing rationales. The work brings much-needed systematic comparison to explainable sequential recommendation.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Models via Evolving Variational Autoregressive Networks

author.name: Kewen Pan, Ying Tang

entry.summary: This work introduces a discrete diffusion model parameterized by variational autoregressive networks, yielding normalized probability distributions that support both sampling and direct likelihood evaluation, with explicit Markov jump operators governing forward and reverse dynamics. The framework extends normalized discrete diffusion to spin systems on higher-dimensional lattices, demonstrated on two- and three-dimensional Ising models including ordered, critical, and disordered regimes. It bridges diffusion modeling and statistical physics with tractable likelihoods.

entry.title: Learning Local Heterogeneity and Cross-Region Context for Large-Scale Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Qi Feng, Zidong Wang, Bo Li, Xiaoguang Gao, Jiayu Zhang, Chenfeng Wang, Kaifang Wan

entry.summary: Proposes LoReST, a local-region spatial-temporal network for large-scale traffic forecasting that models spatial dependencies at two granularities: fine-grained node-level relations capturing road identity and direction heterogeneity, plus efficient cross-region context to avoid costly all-pairs interactions. This targets the persistent trade-off between local detail and long-range information in intelligent transportation systems.

entry.title: NS-ATTENTION: Newton-Schulz Transformations of Attention Outputs in Vision Transformers

author.name: Xiaohe Jiang (University of Exeter), Guoqiang Zhang (University of Exeter), Tianjin Huang (University of Exeter), Ronghui Mu (University of Exeter)

entry.summary: Introduces NS-Attn, a parameter-free transformation applying Newton-Schulz iterations to attention head outputs in vision transformers to reduce spectral concentration and increase effective rank before head merging. Motivated by the Muon optimizer's spectral effects, it shows improvements on ViT and Swin models on CIFAR-10/100.

entry.title: Quality over Quantity: Semi-Supervised Detection of Illicit Bitcoin Flows via Feature Engineering

author.name: Yekaterina Smolenkova, Nickolay Larionov, Nikolay Ivanov, Yury Yanovich

entry.summary: Builds a semi-supervised framework for detecting illicit Bitcoin flows in Shared Send Mixer transactions over a 163-million-transaction historical dataset, showing that SSL success depends on feature quality rather than data volume. High-fidelity features such as KeyLinker address clustering and Shared Send Untangling complexity metrics drive strong F1 performance despite extreme class imbalance and label scarcity.

entry.title: Learning from Failures: Heterogeneous Graph Memory for Small Language Model Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Jiaxing Li, Lei Song, Rui Dong, Youyong Kong

entry.summary: This paper proposes a heterogeneous graph memory that lets small language model tool-using agents learn from failed tool calls while preserving their causal context and safety conditions. The approach targets structural errors like premature writes and repeated failed calls in long-horizon stateful environments without expensive fine-tuning.

entry.title: Geospatial embeddings detect old-growth forests but buffered spatial validation narrows their advantage over Sentinel features

author.name: Thomas Ratsakatika (Department of Geography, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK), Mihai Zotta (Fundatia Conservation Carpathia, Brasov, Romania), Srinivasan Keshav (Department of Computer Science and Technology, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK), Emily R. Lines (Department of Geography, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK)

entry.summary: This study maps old-growth forests across 211,893 hectares of Romania's Southern Carpathians using geospatial foundation model embeddings (AlphaEarth, TESSERA v2) versus Sentinel-1/2 features, finding that buffered spatial validation narrows the apparent advantage of GFMs over simpler satellite features. It provides expert-informed reference labels and a rigorous spatial evaluation protocol.

entry.title: Small Cues, Big Consequences: Learning Pivotal Cues for Multimodal Meme Classification

author.name: Akshit Sharma, Prashant W. Patil

entry.summary: Introduces MemeCF, a 9,895-meme benchmark with annotations of pivotal visual, textual, or cross-modal evidence for harm, hate, and sarcasm, plus MemePIVOT, an architecture using frozen CLIP features, unbalanced optimal transport for word-patch alignment, and evidential fusion. The approach targets small decisive cues that global multimodal representations miss.

entry.title: Sharp Convergence of Wasserstein Gradient Flows for Spectrally Nonnegative Interaction Energies

author.name: Zhengjiang Lin, Philippe Rigollet

entry.summary: Proves sharp long-time convergence results for Wasserstein gradient flows of interaction energies on closed manifolds when kernels have nonnegative Laplace-eigenbasis coefficients, deriving a differential inequality between relative entropy and energy gap. It establishes energy-gap decay of order t^-1 and weak convergence to the constant measure even without geodesic convexity.

entry.title: Feed the Panel Dimensions, Not Verdicts: Rubric-Decomposed Fusion of Vision-Language Aesthetic Judges

author.name: Amit Jadhav, Shaurya Beriwala, Beomjin Kim

entry.summary: Empirical study showing that panels of vision-language models used as zero-shot aesthetic judges never significantly outperform their best single member when verdicts are averaged or naively fused. The authors instead decompose judgments across a human-written five-dimension rubric and fuse dimension-level scores with an out-of-fold combiner on the EVA and PARA datasets.

entry.title: Physiologically Informed Digital Auscultation for Pneumonia Detection in Long-term Care Residents

author.name: Nicholas Rasmussen, Oleg Zaslavsky, Zih-Ling Wang, Hongyu Yu, Joelle Fathi, Kaibao Nie, Amil Khanzada, Tomoko Ito

entry.summary: The authors train models on multi-channel digital stethoscope recordings from 185 long-term care residents, comparing radiologist-confirmed X-ray supervision against clinician diagnosis supervision. X-ray-supervised models outperform (F1 0.729 vs 0.637), and interpretability via time-domain Grad-CAM supports clinical use.

entry.title: Dirichlet Process Mixtures of Trees with Gaussian Process Splits: A Bayesian Nonparametric Framework with Posterior Contraction Rate

author.name: Subhasish Basak, Anik Roy, Sourabh Bhattacharya

entry.summary: Proposes a Bayesian nonparametric mixture of regression trees with a Dirichlet process prior over tree-parameter pairs, unifying CART, BART, random forests, and boosting with data-driven ensemble size. A GP-driven splitting rule yields smooth boundaries with exact cancellation in the Metropolis-Hastings ratio, plus posterior contraction theory and an MPI-parallel sampler.

entry.title: Distillation for Efficient Multitask Manipulation Policies via Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Shreya Deshmukh, Imen Mahdi, Nick Heppert, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: This work studies multi-task robot manipulation policy learning with conditional flow matching, proposing to distill knowledge from single-task expert policies into a single multi-task model to avoid the capacity and performance costs of naive dataset concatenation. It targets efficient generative policy learning for manipulation benchmarks.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning LLMs for Translation: General Forgetting Mitigation Does Not Preserve MT-Specific Instruction Following

author.name: Niklas Scholz, David Thulke, Abdallah Nasir, Will Allred, Evgeny Matusov, Hermann Ney

entry.summary: This study examines whether catastrophic forgetting mitigation methods, typically evaluated on general benchmarks, transfer to MT-specific instruction following (formality, gender, length control) when fine-tuning LLMs like Llama 3.1 8B Instruct on Arabic-English and Spanish-English data. It finds Elastic Weight Consolidation preserves general capabilities best, but general forgetting mitigation does not preserve MT-specific instruction following.

entry.title: When Learned Context Planning Fails to Beat Strong Retrieval: A Controlled Study of Planning, Routing, and Reranking for Long-Context QA

author.name: Yingrui Li, Han Chen

entry.summary: This controlled study tests whether learned context planning improves long-context multiple-choice QA once strong retrieval, routing, budgeted selectors, and reranking baselines are in place. Anchored hybrid retrieval (36.18%) edges out the best planner-guided method (34.19%), suggesting learned planners add little beyond strong classical retrieval.

entry.title: Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Yunhao Liang, QingHao Zhang, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: WebMRE is an offline benchmark of 541 WebArena-derived tasks with deterministic scoring, enabling reproducible studies of web agents without live environments. It documents a mutual reinforcement effect between human-oriented guide sentences and grounded actions across decoding orders and model scales.

entry.title: Can Jev Judge Radiology Reports? Evaluating a System One Model for Clinical Factuality

author.name: Jiaju Huang, Hao Yang, Xinyu Ma, Xinglong Liang, Kunyan Cai, Junqiang Ma, Shaobin Chen, Yue Sun, Tao Tan

entry.summary: This work evaluates Jev, a low-cost System One decision model, as a bidirectional factual-agreement judge for AI-generated radiology reports, checking for supported statements, unsupported claims, and omissions. A single-question configuration achieves Kendall correlations of 0.573 on RadEvalX and 0.398 on RadEvalExpert with expert error counts, outperforming an open NLI judge under matched decomposition.

entry.title: Scaling Attention Head Analysis via Gradient-Based Attribution in Context-Aware Machine Translation

author.name: Pawe{\l} M\k{a}ka, Yusuf Can Semerci, Jan Scholtes, Gerasimos Spanakis

entry.summary: The authors propose a gradient-based attention head attribution method that backpropagates a Token-level Max-Margin loss to attention maps, enabling large-scale causal analysis of individual heads in LLMs. Applied to disambiguation in context-aware machine translation across 50 phenomena, 4 models, and 4 language directions, the analysis identifies general-purpose attention heads whose amplification improves model performance.

entry.title: Quieter Than the Room: Representation Drift and Task Robustness in Speech Encoders

author.name: Vsevolod Kovalev, Pranay Manocha

entry.summary: This paper tests eight frozen speech encoders across four tasks under various types of non-speech sound interference, finding that embedding drift and task loss diverge depending on whether noise is placed over speech or in pauses. The results show that representation-level measures do not reliably predict task robustness, with placement effects varying by task such as intent recognition versus emotion recognition.

entry.title: AgroBench: A Reproducible Multimodal Benchmark for Weakly Supervised Crop Yield Learning from County Statistics and Pixel Observations

author.name: Udaiveer Singh, Rajiv Ranjan, Shashank Tamaskar, Dharmendra Saraswat

entry.summary: AgroBench converts public US county-level crop yield statistics into weakly supervised pixel-level crop time series from Earth observation data, bridging the gap between coarse administrative reporting and pixel-level geospatial machine learning needs. It provides a reproducible pipeline pairing satellite pixel sequences with county yield labels.

entry.title: Temporally Ordered Region-Token Mamba with Logit-Space Diffusion for Remote Sensing Change Detection

author.name: Anuvab Sen, Maneet Chatterjee, Aparup Ghosh, Udayon Sen, Arnav Aditya, Yixin Zhang

entry.summary: BMD-CD combines temporally structured state-space modeling with logit-space diffusion refinement for remote sensing change detection, converting bitemporal features into region tokens with explicit temporal partitions processed by a bidirectional Mamba operator. It targets efficient long-range reasoning over high-resolution imagery without dense attention.

entry.title: Geometry-Conditioned Visual Place Recognition in Natural Environments

author.name: Walter Nedov, Saimunur Rahman, Kavindie Katuwandeniya, David Hall, Kaushik Roy, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: Introduces Depth-Aware Distillation, which conditions token representations of a pretrained vision foundation model on geometry from a geometric foundation model to improve visual place recognition in natural environments with repetitive vegetation and large appearance changes. Notably requires no depth sensor, distilling geometric consistency into the visual representation.

entry.title: NeuralSRNF: Neural Square Root Normal Fields for the Statistical Shape Analysis and Generation of Nonrigid 3D and 4D Objects

author.name: Awais Nizamani, Hamid Laga, Guanjin Wang, Farid Boussaid, Mohammed Bennamoun, Anuj Srivastava

entry.summary: Introduces NeuralSRNF, a neural framework for statistical shape analysis and generation of nonrigid genus-zero 3D/4D objects that makes elastic shape analysis practical by learning the computationally expensive inverse mapping from Square Root Normal Fields back to surfaces. Enables efficient geodesic computation, summary statistics, and generation for deformable shapes.

entry.title: Fusion-Aware Direct 3D Gaussian Generation with Structured Patch Latent Flows

author.name: Yizhao Wang, Jingbo Wang, Guantao Zhang

entry.summary: This companion work proposes a fusion-aware hierarchical Gaussian patch representation for direct class-guided 3DGS generation with structured patch latent flows, modeling the intrinsic structural distribution of Gaussian objects rather than fusing observed views. It targets content creation, virtual environments, and digital asset design. Together with the previous paper it advances native generative modeling over Gaussian primitives.

entry.title: Evaluating ADC-only deep learning pipelines for breast cancer detection and segmentation using standalone diffusion-weighted MRI

author.name: Pablo Garc\'ia Marcos, Paula Puerta Gonz\'lez, Guillermo Lorenzo, H\'ector G\'omez, Covadonga del Camino, Angel Rio-Alvarez, V\'ictor M. Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: This study evaluates deep learning detection and segmentation of breast cancer using standalone diffusion-weighted MRI and ADC maps, avoiding the long acquisition times and contrast-agent risks of DCE-MRI. It fills a gap since most deep learning work has focused on contrast-enhanced imaging. If ADC-only pipelines perform adequately, they could enable cheaper, faster, safer breast MRI screening.

entry.title: From Change Captions to Change Detection: Semantic-Appearance Agreement Framework for Remote Sensing Change Detection

author.name: Yuan Qian, Jie Ma

entry.summary: The authors propose using change captions as the sole task-specific supervision for remote sensing change detection, replacing costly pixel-level change masks. Captions naturally encode what changed, what it became, and where, enabling weakly supervised learning of change masks. This significantly lowers annotation cost for an operationally important remote sensing task.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Semantic Segmentation from High-Resolution Depth and Ultra-Low-Resolution RGB

author.name: Xuying Huang, Swithinraj Moses Daniel, Sicong Pan, Sebastian Houben, Maren Bennewitz

entry.summary: The authors introduce an asymmetric sensing setting combining high-resolution depth with ultra-low-resolution RGB to mitigate privacy risks from robot-mounted cameras while preserving geometric understanding. They propose a joint 2D framework using HR geometry to guide semantic-oriented RGB reconstruction and RGB-D segmentation despite severe information imbalance. This addresses growing privacy concerns for robots in everyday environments.

entry.title: Automotive mmWave Spinning Radar Place Recognition with Spatially Gated Feature-Correlation Representation

author.name: Saimunur Rahman, Sagun Singh Shrestha, Abdelwahed Khamis, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: Proposes SGCA-Net, a place recognition framework for automotive spinning FMCW radar that handles rotation-induced circular shifts in polar radar images and uses Spatially Gated Correlation Aggregation to weight spatial relationships among radar returns. This matters for autonomous navigation in conditions where cameras and lidar degrade, such as rain, fog, and darkness.

entry.title: Beyond the Flat Seafloor: A Closed-Form Two-View Constraint to Aid Sidescan Sonar Reconstruction

author.name: Kalin Norman, Joshua G. Mangelson

entry.summary: Derives a closed-form two-view geometric constraint for sidescan sonar showing that a shared feature must lie within the intersection of a sphere and a plane, relaxing the long-standing flat-seafloor approximation. Monte Carlo simulations grounded in real sonar aperture and mounting geometry characterize the size of the residual ambiguity locus.

entry.title: Recording Hand-Held Laparoscopic Instrument Motion in the Operating Room: Magnetometer-Free Fusion of Inertial, Range and Visual Sensing

author.name: Jiyul Lee, Dongho Yee, Juahn Oh, Jinseok Lee, Yechan Seo, Seong Jeong, Minsung Kim, Seonho Shim, Younghoon Noh, Hyuk Choi, Youngbin Kong, Hyoun-Joong Kong

entry.summary: The authors present a clip-on surgical instrument-state logger that fuses a six-axis IMU, time-of-flight rangefinder, and markerless camera in an error-state Kalman filter, explicitly avoiding the magnetometer whose field varies with tool pose and session. The system recovers laparoscopic instrument motion in the operating room that is otherwise lost, supporting skill assessment and robot learning.

entry.title: DynaForge: Planning-Guided Residual Learning for Dynamic Manipulation Demonstration Generation

author.name: Yiyang Jin, Yu Zheng, Xiao He, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: DynaForge generates high-quality demonstrations for dynamic object manipulation by combining low-frequency global planning with high-frequency object-centric inverse kinematics and a learned residual policy that corrects actions near contact. It addresses limitations of planning-based methods and replay-style demonstration generators in dynamic settings.

entry.title: AgriGen: Large-Scale Scene Generation Framework for Photorealistic Agricultural Robotics Simulation

author.name: Utkarsh Bajpai, Serge Tleiji, C\'{e}dric Pradalier, St\'{e}phanie Aravecchia

entry.summary: AgriGen is a ROS-integrated framework built on Isaac Sim for procedural generation of large-scale, photorealistic agricultural environments with physics simulation and domain randomization. It addresses the difficulty of acquiring diverse agricultural robot datasets due to field access constraints and seasonal cycles.

entry.title: What is the Better Curriculum: Controller-Shaped Grasping Behavior for Contact Force-Sensitive Manipulation

author.name: Ziyan Feng, Zizhao Yuan, Yulong Fu, Yuxin He, Zhiyuan Zhang, Zhengjie Zhang, Jinni Zhou, Renjing Xu, Qiang Nie

entry.summary: For manipulating fragile objects where sub-Newton forces matter, the authors use a deterministic 25 Hz tactile reflex controller as a collection-time teacher to produce demonstrations with controller-shaped grasping behavior, then train tactile-free ACT policies on those demonstrations. This sidesteps the problem that human teleoperation is too coarse for narrow force windows.

entry.title: Safety-Constrained Model Predictive Control for an Omnidirectional Walking Assistive Robot Using Control Barrier Function

author.name: Andrea Fortuna, Marta Lorenzini, Elisa Motta, Alberto Ranavolo, Elena De Momi, Arash Ajoudani

entry.summary: Presents I-WANDER, an omnidirectional walking assistive robot whose control framework integrates Control Barrier Functions into Model Predictive Control to enforce collision-avoidance constraints while optimizing energy efficiency and human-robot collaboration smoothness. The system was experimentally validated with 12 healthy participants, providing real hardware evidence beyond simulation.

entry.title: ArborSplat: Online Semantic Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Orchards

author.name: Alessandro Masini, Matteo Frosi, Mirko Usuelli, Matteo Matteucci

entry.summary: Presents ArborSplat, an online semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system for orchard robots that tracks with LiDAR odometry and optimizes semantics directly on the Gaussian map, using class-specific height bands and multi-view evidence fusion to preserve thin structures like trunks, trellises, and fruit that appearance-driven 3DGS SLAM loses. The system rejects labels inconsistent with local geometry.

entry.title: Underwater Navigation in Unsteady Flows Using Measurement Histories from a Single Sensing Unit

author.name: Linhao Jin, Qimin Feng, Peter Gunnarson, Qiang Zhong

entry.summary: This work shows a causal observer can estimate lateral flow velocities from a finite history of measurements from a single sensing unit, replacing distributed spatial sensing for underwater navigation in unsteady flows. Trained only in a cylinder wake at Re=100, the observer achieves 80-84% navigation success at higher Reynolds numbers without retraining, only modestly below direct spatial sensing.

entry.title: Penalized Nonreversible Langevin for Constrained Sampling

author.name: Pervez Ali, Weihao Dong, Xiaoyu Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose penalized nonreversible Langevin algorithms for sampling from distributions restricted to compact convex sets, combining a squared distance penalty with skew-symmetric perturbations that preserve the penalized Gibbs distribution. They derive non-asymptotic total variation bounds under log-Sobolev inequalities and 2-Wasserstein bounds under contraction conditions on the drift.

entry.title: Scalable Minimum-Volume Simplex Estimation with Non-asymptotic Analysis

author.name: Jun LI, Yanlong Guo, Zhaozhao Zeng

entry.summary: DeepMVSA reformulates minimum-volume simplex estimation in neural implicit form, using a lightweight coordinate network for mixing weights and an LU-type triangular parameterization for the dual simplex matrix, reducing memory to O(K^2) independent of sample count and per-pass cost to O(NK^2). This makes the problem tractable at millions to hundreds of millions of samples, with a non-asymptotic sample-complexity bound matching the polynomial-time benchmark order.

entry.title: On the Gradient Heterogeneity Dynamics of Adversarially Robust Federated Regression

author.name: Leonardo F. Toso, James Anderson, Nirupam Gupta, Rafael Pinot

entry.summary: The paper derives gradient heterogeneity bounds for federated regression from the statistical model itself, with fresh data each round, rather than imposing a priori gradient-dissimilarity conditions. The resulting bounds separate heterogeneity among honest clients' true model parameters from finite-sample and adversarial effects, yielding tighter guarantees for robust federated linear and nonlinear regression.

entry.title: A Decentralized Partially Observable Team Decision Methodology with Delayed Information Sharing

author.name: Xiaoxing Ren, Thomas Parisini, Andreas A. Malikopoulos

entry.summary: This work addresses decentralized team decision-making in partially observable Markov decision processes with low-rank latent dynamics and unknown transition models, where members act on private information plus delayed shared common information. Each member learns an approximate low-rank MDP and applies least-squares value iteration, yielding a fully decentralized algorithm without centralized coordination or a known model.

entry.title: Learned Enterprise Data Comprehension: Compression and Routing for Data Agents

author.name: Ethan Torres, Eric Mills

entry.summary: This paper introduces latent equivalence learning, a framework that divides labor between agentic semantic reasoning and learned components that predict and organize recurring structure in enterprise data environments. It separates persistent task-relevant identities from transient context, enabling compression and routing of schema, relationship, and policy information for structured-data agents.

entry.title: Unanimity Without Persuasion: A Single Round of Debate Erases the Disagreement That Verification Needs

author.name: Yang Shu

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that a single debate round can make a 7-judge verification panel nearly unanimous (39.5% to 95.2% on 600 code-correctness candidates) without improving accuracy, with 96.3% of verdict flips following the displayed peer majority — i.e., conformity rather than persuasion. This erodes disagreement as a targeting signal for downstream verification safeguards.

entry.title: Exposing Blind Spots in Deep Imbalanced Regression Evaluation

author.name: Noah C. Puetz, Jens U. Brandt, Marc Hilbert, Elena Raponi, Thomas B\"ack, Thomas Bartz-Beielstein

entry.summary: Revisits evaluation in deep imbalanced regression along three blind spots: over-reliance on image benchmarks, a diagnostic-but-not-decision-complete many/medium/few-shot protocol, and unexamined tail-region stability across seeds. It introduces a multimodal virtual sensing benchmark (MuViS) and systematically re-evaluates DIR methods along these axes.

entry.title: A JEPA Recipe for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Mingyu Jeon, Suwan Cho, Jae Young Suh

entry.summary: Reports a recipe under which the latent objective of a joint-embedding predictive architecture survives convergence on top of a tabular foundation model, where earlier runs collapsed to a constant map. Key ingredients include having the value head read the encoder field, using an EMA-difference target, and plateau-based stopping instead of fixed budgets.

entry.title: Destination Support Restoration for Finite-Set Multimodal Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Fengrui Liu, Jiajun Peng, Duo Peng, Feng Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Destination Support Restoration (DSR), a causal post-selection operator that repairs underrepresented destinations in finite-set multimodal trajectory predictions for robots operating around pedestrians, without retraining or enlarging the prediction set. It builds a temporary destination-stratified candidate bank, converts evidence into integer counts, and protects representatives of active modes for downstream decision-making.

entry.title: FeatLens: Feature-Guided Dynamic Code Graph Construction and Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Generation

author.name: Xutian Li, Bo Xiong, Yifeng Zhu, Kunze Li, Xianlin Zhao, Runbang Yan, Yanzhen Zou, Lu Zhang, Bing Xie

entry.summary: Introduces FeatLens, a feature-oriented framework for repository-level code generation that constructs dynamic code graphs for retrieving reusable dependencies (functions, APIs, cross-file definitions). It aims to reduce the high graph construction, reasoning, and token costs of similarity-search, persistent-graph, and LLM-exploration retrieval baselines.

entry.title: Signal2Symbol: Neuro-Symbolic Temporal Reasoning for Explainable Physiological Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Naser Mansour, Sidahmed Benabderrahmane, Ameer Rahwan

entry.summary: Signal2Symbol is a neuro-symbolic framework for explainable ECG/EEG anomaly detection that converts signals into symbolic sequences via a learned VQ-VAE codebook or SAX baseline, then applies temporal reasoning over the symbolic representation. It aims to explain why a segment is anomalous and whether it belongs to a recurring broader pattern.

entry.title: Local Evidence and Geometric Readout Repair in Trained GNNs

author.name: Nadi Tomeh, Hugo Attali

entry.summary: The paper disentangles two causes of node-classification errors in GNNs — poor mixture weights versus a poorly positioned reachable logit set — using an exact-mass linear program and two learned post-hoc repairs. Across eight datasets, eight backbones, and ten splits, accuracy rises from 62.6 percent frozen to 65.3 percent with set-conditioned translation, with most gains explained by logit translation. It offers a diagnostic lens on how GNN readout geometry limits frozen models.

entry.title: Probabilistic and Geometry Aware Neural Surrogate of Scrape Off Layer Plasma Simulations

author.name: Gabriele Gianuzzo, Stefan Dasbach, Fleur Hendriks, Sven Wiesen, Vlado Menkovski

entry.summary: This work builds a probabilistic neural surrogate for tokamak boundary-plasma simulation, unrolling the curvilinear SOLPS-ITER mesh into image tensors that preserve cell adjacency, and using conditional flow matching to capture multi-modal plasma states near the divertor detachment transition. It provides calibrated uncertainty rather than single point estimates.

entry.title: Memory Attention

author.name: Jiale Kang

entry.summary: Memory Attention (MA) replaces the dedicated value projection in transformers with a token-indexed memory table combined with contextual keys, allowing normalization folding and value construction by lookup and addition at inference. It also enables CPU offloading with prefetching to reduce GPU parameter storage under matched training token budgets.

entry.title: The Computational Value of Sensory-Aligned Receptive Fields Depends on Neuronal Expressivity

author.name: Agnese Adorante, Aaron Spieler, Anna Levina

entry.summary: Uses recurrent networks of Expressive Leaky Memory neurons to independently vary neuronal complexity and receptive-field organization, asking when structured, sensory-aligned receptive fields give computational advantage. The findings indicate the benefit of structured receptive fields depends on neuronal expressivity, informing theories of efficient coding in biological neural systems.

entry.title: Six Layers Less: Encoder Pruning for Whisper with Label-Free Recovery

author.name: Rasmus Aagaard, Nicki Skafte Detlefsen

entry.summary: Presents a label-free encoder pruning method for Whisper ASR models that ranks encoder layers by leave-one-layer-out WER change, removing the six least impactful layers with a recovery procedure. This complements prior decoder-only pruning (e.g., whisper-large-v3-turbo and Distill-Whisper) with custom-inference-free encoder compression.

entry.title: RAMP: Robust Adaptive Mixed-Precision Quantization for Edge CPU Vision Models

author.name: David Poblaci\'on-Criado, Dario Garcia-Gasulla, Eduardo Quinones

entry.summary: RAMP addresses mixed-precision quantization for edge CPU deployment by systematically studying why widely used layer sensitivity metrics fail on modern architectures, then building a robust adaptive quantization method that better identifies layer-wise accuracy-latency tradeoffs. The work targets substantial inference savings without unacceptable task degradation.

entry.title: MORSE: Multi-Context Ordering via Reverse Scoring for Evidence-Preserving Compression

author.name: Ke Wan, Yifan Wang, Liheng Lai, Chen Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies information preemption as the cause of order sensitivity in likelihood-based context compression: earlier partially relevant contexts absorb credit for shared information, causing stronger later evidence to be dropped. MORSE addresses this via reverse scoring to make evidence retention robust to context ordering, supported by controlled pair-swap interventions.

entry.title: Same Scores, Different Decisions: Evaluating JEV and Language Models for Legal Document Understanding

author.name: Fan Zhang, Yankai Chen, Zhuohan Xie, Yixi Zhou, Sijia Peng, Lei Fan, Xinhua Ji, Cunyuan Zheng, Huangyong Shan, Philip S. Yu, Xue Liu, Yu Chen, Preslav Nakov, Songwei He

entry.summary: The paper compares Jev with nine LLMs on ContractNLI across cost, latency, and per-decision correctness under varied hypothesis visibility and output ordering, showing that aggregate accuracy rankings conceal decision-level differences. Jev offers the lowest cost and fastest responses while hosted LLMs achieve higher baseline accuracy, and repeated-request correctness reveals consistency patterns hidden by aggregate scores.

entry.title: SGDet3D++: Geometry-Grounded Semantics for 4D Radar and Camera 3D Object Detection

author.name: Xiaokai Bai, Zhenyu Fan, Lianqing Zheng, Songkai Wang, Si-Yuan Cao, Hui-liang Shen

entry.summary: Formulates hypothesis-conditioned evidence grounding for radar-camera 3D detection, filtering semantic, geometric, and temporal evidence by the evolving 3D object state before updating queries, thus separating candidate access from evidence use. SGDet3D++ instantiates this with anchor-grounded semantic reasoning for 4D radar and camera fusion.

entry.title: Geometry-anchored PET-aware multimodal pseudo-CT synthesis for whole-body attenuation correction: the BIC-MAC Challenge

author.name: Xuan Loc Nguyen, Hoang-Loc Cao, Truong Thanh Hung Nguyen, Phuc Ho, Phuc Truong Loc Nguyen, Nguyen Truong Toan To, Hung Cao

entry.summary: GeoPACT addresses CT-less PET attenuation correction by synthesizing whole-body pseudo-CT from non-attenuation-corrected PET, Dixon MRI, and a 2D topogram, using NAC-PET as the spatial anchor with gated residual fusion and differentiable PET-response surrogate losses. It was developed for the BIC-MAC challenge and supports label-free sliding-window inference. Accurate attenuation correction without CT can broaden PET imaging access.

entry.title: Diff-RF: Mutually Reinforced Image Registration and Fusion via Degradation-Aware Learning

author.name: Xunpeng Yi, Zaixi Du, Qinglong Yan, Yibing Zhang, Han Xu, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: Diff-RF is a diffusion-based framework that jointly performs image registration and fusion of misaligned, degraded multi-modal images, exploring the coupling between registration-fusion and information restoration. By making the two processes mutually reinforcing under a degradation-aware formulation, it enables high-quality fusion in challenging real-world conditions such as low illumination and noise. This targets a practical gap where prior methods assume relatively clean, roughly aligned inputs.

entry.title: Recursive Uncertainty-Gated Image Registration for Learning-based Algorithms

author.name: Clara Rodrigo Gonz\'alez, Oscar Bates, Fu Siong Ng, Meng-Xing Tang

entry.summary: Proposes RUGI, a recursive refinement scheme for learning-based image registration in which each iteration predicts an incremental deformation gated by a map that concentrates updates in hard-to-register regions, using either learned uncertainty or image residuals. Evaluation on cardiac data suggests improved robustness on out-of-domain samples while retaining fast inference.

entry.title: Control Barrier Functions for Safe Free-Flying Robotic Spacecraft Operations in Tumbling Target Capture

author.name: Alexander Meinert, Peter Stadler, Niklas Baldauf, Alen Turnwald

entry.summary: The paper presents a modular control barrier function framework for safe free-flying spacecraft capture of tumbling targets, decomposing a 13-DoF system into translational, attitude, and robotic subsystems, each with a QP-based safety filter. It translates ESA proximity-operations guidelines into CBFs covering approach corridors, collision avoidance, pointing, joint limits, and actuator constraints.

entry.title: Hierarchical Floorplan-Guided Vision-Language Exploration for Embodied Question Answering

author.name: Albert Gassol Puigjaner, Kostas Alexis

entry.summary: Proposes HFLEX-EQA, a hierarchical embodied question answering framework that combines incremental hierarchical scene graph construction, VLM-based planning, semantic frontier exploration, and architectural floorplan priors, using RGB-D observations to build open-vocabulary occupancy maps. Structural priors about environments are exploited, which most VLM-driven EQA approaches ignore.

entry.title: Wheel-loader V-Cycle Automation with Deep Koopman MPC

author.name: Armin Abdolmohammadi, Navid Mojahed, Dinesh Kumar, Bahram Ravani, Shima Nazari

entry.summary: A hierarchical autonomy framework for wheel-loaders in earthmoving that combines geometric long-horizon planning of forward-reverse maneuvers with data-driven deep bilinear Koopman models used within model predictive control to capture nonlinear articulated-vehicle and terrain dynamics. The forward and reverse trajectories are jointly optimized through a shared intermediate state.

entry.title: RankCert: When Can Simulated Learners Safely Select an AI Tutor? Robust Decision Certification Under Structural Uncertainty

author.name: Nizam Kadir

entry.summary: RankCert is a certification scheme for selecting among eight equal-budget tutoring policies that abstains unless multiple criteria — model-averaged utility, posterior regret, cross-domain ranks, and leave-one-domain/family-out averages — agree on the same candidate. It was evaluated over 1,280 frozen held-out settings across five oracle families using a licensed EdNet-KT1 derivative with 5,000 learners and about 590,000 responses.

entry.title: GitScholar: A Dataset for Predicting AI Research Impact from GitHub Engagement

author.name: Emilien Guandalino, Lorenz K. M\"uller, Beatrice Alessandra Motetti, Konstantin Berestizshevsky, Lukas Cavigelli

entry.summary: Introduces GitScholar, a dataset linking GitHub activity from 444,000 repositories to over 558,000 AI arXiv papers, and demonstrates that GitHub engagement is a timely and accurate signal for predicting AI research impact. It supports automated identification of impactful work amid hundreds of daily publications.

entry.title: A Leakage-Aware Multimodal Evaluation Framework for Early Intraoperative Acute Kidney Injury Prediction

author.name: Quang Minh Nguyen, Duc Minh Le, Ho Nhat Minh Nguyen, Thuy Quynh Nguyen, Trong Nghia Nguyen

entry.summary: This retrospective cohort study proposes SynerT, a waveform-only hybrid temporal backbone (causal dilated TCN with dilated recurrent hierarchy) for predicting postoperative acute kidney injury from early intraoperative physiologic trajectories, plus multimodal and leakage-safe stacked-ensemble variants. The work emphasizes leakage-aware evaluation for clinical deployment credibility.

entry.title: Scalable Subgraph Sampling via Resistance Curvature

author.name: Chaoqun Fei, Tinglve Zhou, Tianyong Hao, Yangyang Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes ERC-LG, a curvature approximation method for large-scale graphs combining Johnson-Lindenstrauss projections with regularized multi-GPU batched conjugate-gradient solvers, avoiding explicit Laplacian pseudoinverse computation. The resulting resistance curvature guides node- and edge-sampling probabilities for GNN training subgraphs. It achieves numerical agreement with pseudoinverse-based curvature at reduced runtime and competitive downstream accuracy.

entry.title: LAYERSCOPE: A Layerwise Characterization of Video and Multimodal Learned Representations

author.name: Sandra Arcos-Holzinger, Debashish Chakraborty, Rohita Mocharla, Will Walden, Andrew Yates, Reno Kriz, Sarah M. Erfani, James Bailey, Vishal M. Patel, Sanjeev Khudanpur

entry.summary: LAYERSCOPE is a label-free framework for characterizing learned representations layer by layer in video and multimodal models, using local, global, distributional, and correspondence-based geometric metrics instead of costly task-specific labeled evaluations. It evaluates seven architecturally diverse models on MVEB/MVEB+ tasks.

entry.title: Support-Compiled Feature Folding: More Evidence at Lower Memory Across Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Tian Zhou, Beverly Jin, Xue Wang, Linxiao Yang, Wenwei Wang, Bingqing Peng, Mengni Ye, Jinjie Gu, Liang Sun

entry.summary: SCFF is a training-free inference framework for tabular foundation models that routes support-ranked features through bounded leaves of the native encoder, converting quadratic feature-interaction work into linear-in-width work without changing the frozen backbone or ensembling. It resolves the trade-off between full-width pairwise mixing and feature selection.

entry.title: NeuroRule: Making Black-Box Neural Networks Explainable through Rule-set Evolution

author.name: Tapaswini Kodavanti, Hormoz Shahrzad, Risto Miikkulainen

entry.summary: Adapts the EVOTER rule-set evolution framework to distill high-capacity neural network classifiers into concise propositional logic rule-sets. The NeuroRule framework addresses the performance-explainability trade-off by evolving interpretable rule sets against neural network targets, with contributions including an evolutionary metaheuristic design.

entry.title: A Hybrid Iterative Deep Ritz Method for Elliptic Interface Problems

author.name: Tianhao Hu, Bangti Jin, Fengru Wang, Yifeng Xu

entry.summary: H-IDRM solves elliptic interface problems via a new mixed formulation and a sequence of convex minimizations using a level-set neural network representation. It avoids explicit interface sampling and includes error analysis covering neural approximation, Monte Carlo, and discretization errors.

entry.title: Predicting Quantization Price for Selecting PTQ Configurations Before Deployment

author.name: Junbin Qiu, Jian Mu, Weitong Zhang, Yao Shu

entry.summary: This paper formulates post-training quantization as a pre-deployment configuration selection problem, treating each layer configuration as an error generator with a deployment cost and inducing a layer-output error covariance. It predicts quantization-induced output-distribution drift before the quantized model is built, jointly covering formats, granularities, quantizer families, and bit widths.

entry.title: Can One Adapted Model Do It All? Fine-Tuning Strategy Selection for Customer Support LLMs

author.name: Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Xue-Yong Fu, Shashi Bhushan TN

entry.summary: This study compares separate task-specialist models versus multi-task training, sequential updates, and model merging for customer-support LLMs, using thirteen models from five families (0.6B-32B) across eight datasets and 200+ checkpoints under a fixed protocol. It provides practical guidance on which fine-tuning strategy suits which deployment constraint.

entry.title: Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Dingyi Rong, Zijian Chen, Zicheng Zhang, Xiongkuo Min, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: Proposes MVCAP, a motion-based CAPTCHA framework where target semantics exist only as motion-defined structures recoverable through temporal segregation from an evolving background, designed to resist multimodal LLMs and GUI agents that can solve static CAPTCHAs. Instantiated at three perceptually progressive difficulty levels.

entry.title: TopoGS: Topology-Aware Anchor Feature Aggregation for Large-Scale 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Wei Zhang, Shiqiang Gong, Shengkai Yu, Zeyu Wang, Clement Mallet, Zhitong Xiong, Qi Wang

entry.summary: TopoGS improves octree-based 3DGS for large-scale scenes by exploiting the octree topology during feature learning, introducing Hierarchical Anchor Coupling for bidirectional cross-level gradient pathways and Structure-Aware Containment Aggregation for selective information flow between levels. This addresses the underuse of hierarchical structure when levels are optimized independently. It enables better level-of-detail rendering for large environments.

entry.title: HaRP: High Dynamic Range Photosequencing through Dual Reversed Shutter Scanning

author.name: Xiang Ji, Guixu Lin, Jiancheng Zhao, Zhengwei Yin, Yinqiang Zheng

entry.summary: HaRP proposes a dual reversed scanning setup that combines rolling shutter with global reset (RSGR) and inverted RSGR views to handle the RSGR mode's reduced capture speed and compressed dynamic range. Synchronizing complementary exposures balances dynamic range across frames and enables HDR photosequencing in highly dynamic scenes. This is a novel hardware-plus-algorithm contribution for mobile imaging.

entry.title: Learning to Plan in Human-Robot Collaboration: Multimodal Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Interaction

author.name: Afagh Mehri Shervedani, Siyu Li, Natawut Monaikul, Bahareh Abbasi, Barbara Di Eugenio, Milo\v{s} \v{Z}efran

entry.summary: Proposes a reinforcement learning approach to learn multimodal interaction-management policies for assistive robots that help users, such as older adults, locate objects at home, replacing hand-crafted policies that do not scale with interaction complexity. The system integrates task observation, human state, and intent inference to select robot actions.

entry.title: Induced Riemannian Metrics for Motion Planning with Constraints

author.name: Phone Thiha Kyaw, Thomas Cohn, Miguel Angel Rogel Garcia, Jonathan Kelly

entry.summary: This work examines how the choice of metric affects constrained motion planning, where task constraints restrict motion to a lower-dimensional submanifold of configuration space. The authors derive induced Riemannian metrics that give consistent path-cost semantics for both implicit (constraint level-set) and explicit (parameterized) submanifold representations.

entry.title: SparseNav: Instruction-conditioned Sparse Semantic Perception for Training-Free Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Quanhua Chen, Juhan Kang, Runfeng Lin, ZiFei Zhang, Enquang Feng, Chunran Zheng, Xiwang Dong, Jiarong Lin

entry.summary: Presents SparseNav, a training-free vision-language navigation framework following a less-is-more principle: it maintains a lightweight geometric BEV map and sparse landmark memory, acquiring semantics on demand conditioned on the current instruction rather than exhaustively annotating the scene. This reduces perception cost and representation clutter for the VLM planner.

entry.title: The AI Neuroscientist: An Interactive Agentic Interface for Neuroimaging Analysis

author.name: Aakash Patel, Panos Ketonis, Shreya Saxena, Smita Krishnaswamy, David van Dijk

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-based agent that lets neuroscientists perform quality control, modeling, and visualization of neuroimaging data through natural language, demonstrated on functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data. It includes a custom fNIRS benchmark for evaluating the agent, positioning it as a transparent, interactive alternative to scripted analysis pipelines for small-scale data exploration.

entry.title: ZeroGate: Trust-Preserving Fast Paths for Governed AI Agent Runtimes

author.name: Zexun Wang

entry.summary: ZeroGate separates exact-action approval from durable local admission in governed agent runtimes: an issuer signs a short-lived ActionPass, and a trusted runtime adapter reconstructs the final action for a local gate that checks binding and consumes a nonce within a SQLite transaction coupled to quotas and admission receipts. The paper states a conditional decision-preservation proposition linking local admission to what a synchronous policy would authorize.

entry.title: CQ4OE: A benchmark for assessing LLM-assisted ontology generation from competency questions

author.name: Jiayi Li, Ziyuan Wang, Daniel Garijo, Mar\'ia Poveda-Villal\'on

entry.summary: CQ4OE is a benchmark for reproducible evaluation of LLM-based ontology generation from competency questions, providing gold OWL ontologies with explicit provenance linking each competency question to ontology elements. It addresses fragmented task formulations, weak provenance, and metrics that conflate lexical overlap with structural and logical adequacy.

entry.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy response prediction using pretreatment diffusion and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging with clinical variables

author.name: Pablo Garc\'ia Marcos, Paula Puerta Gonz\'alez, Guillermo Lorenzo, H\'ector G\'omez, Covadonga del Camino, Ad\'an Rodr\'iguez, Ignacio Pel\'aez, Angel Rio-Alvarez, V\'ictor M. Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: This study develops a deep-learning model predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer using only pretreatment ADC maps, DCE-MRI, and clinical variables, on the public multicenter ACRIN 6698/I-SPY2 dataset. It uses pretrained EfficientNet-B0 encoders with late fusion of clinical data, finding that only HR/HER2 subtype improved average AUC among evaluated clinical variables.

entry.title: Early Prediction of Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Using Temporal Deep Learning on DWI

author.name: Pablo Garc\'ia Marcos, Md. Tarequl Islam, Paula Puerta Gonz\'alez, Guillermo Lorenzo, H\'ector G\'omez, Covadonga del Camino, Angel Rio-Alvarez, V\'ictor M. Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: A companion study predicting pathological complete response early in neoadjuvant chemotherapy using only diffusion-weighted MRI at baseline and after the first cycle, feeding tumor-centered patches to an EfficientNet-based temporal model without explicit radiomic feature engineering. This targets early identification of non-responders where multiparametric MRI and late time points limit existing models.

entry.title: Improved Multiplayer Bandit Algorithm for Bernoulli Rewards

author.name: Khang Nguyen, Ricardo Parada, William Chang

entry.summary: The paper studies multiplayer multi-armed bandits with information asymmetry under Bernoulli rewards across three information structures. By replacing Hoeffding-style confidence bounds with KL-divergence-based bounds in algorithms mKL-UCB, mKL-UCB-Intervals, and mKL-DSEE, it achieves strictly tighter regret guarantees, at least a factor of two improvement by Pinsker's inequality.

entry.title: The Delegation Blind Spot: Auditing Product Decisions from Agent Choices

author.name: Shivam Gupta

entry.summary: This paper presents a decision-specific audit workflow for inferring which future product improvements a user would value from agent execution choices. In a frozen experiment with 4,800 requests to two pinned model snapshots, all 36 conservative intervals remained unresolved, and an exploratory follow-up resolved only three of nine comparisons, highlighting limits of inferring preferences from agent behavior.

entry.title: You've Seen Enough: Quality-Constrained Image Coding for Machines

author.name: Khoa Pham-Dinh, Sanaz Nami, Hamed Rezazadegan Tavakoli, Moncef Gabbouj, Farhad Pakdaman

entry.summary: Recasts joint compression-segmentation training as constrained optimization for Image Coding for Machines: cap human-observed quality at a just-acceptable level (inspired by just-noticeable distortion) and spend the remaining coding capacity on machine-task performance. This reallocates bits between human validation and machine consumption of visual data.

entry.title: How Children Design and Reason about Trustworthy AI Chatbots

author.name: Deniz Ozturk, Jiayu Li, Daksh Pratap Singh, Yasitha Rajapaksha, Fasika Melese, Bahare Riahi, Shiyan Jiang, Qiao Jin, Joey Huang, Veronica Catet\'e, Tiffany Barnes, Xiaoyi Tian

entry.summary: Presents a mixed-methods study of 115 learners aged 8-18 who built 119 chatbots in a construction environment with adjustable trust-relevant traits such as confidence, transparency, and assertiveness. Findings include age differences in trust calibration, with younger children setting higher confidence levels, examined through a designer rather than user perspective.

entry.title: Compressing Long Context into Answer-Aligned Memory Embeddings for LLM Inference

author.name: Md Mostafizer Rahman, Md Faizul Ibne Amin, Md Shahajada Mia, Yutaka Watanobe, Fang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes CMC, a framework that compresses long input contexts into compact Context Memory Embeddings aligned to a frozen decoder's embedding space, with a two-tier KV cache combining question-guided selection and answer-targeted supervision, reducing inference cost without modifying decoder weights.

entry.title: Syndrome, Synergy, and Safety: Structured Reasoning and Knowledge-Driven Alignment for TCM Prescription Generation

author.name: Zheng Chen, ZhiCheng Du, Haoxuan Li, Peiwu Qin

entry.summary: The authors identify three clinically critical gaps when LLMs generate Traditional Chinese Medicine prescriptions: lack of auditable reasoning under the li-fa-fang-yao paradigm, no longitudinal follow-up adjustment via sui zheng jia jian, and failure to enforce absolute contraindication rules such as Shi Ba Fan. They propose a progressive four-stage training framework (SFT, PG-CoT, Dynamic SFT, and knowledge-driven RL) that produces auditable diagnostic chains, models patient trajectories, and encodes deterministic safety rules. The work demonstrates how domain-specific reasoning structure and hard safety constraints can be injected into LLM alignment pipelines.

entry.title: Toward Responsible AI-Augmented Cyber Defense: Pattern Recognition, Defense-in-Depth, and the Case for Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Mustafa S. Aljumaily, Hayder Kareem Abed, Nawar S. Alseelawi

entry.summary: Develops a formal, falsifiable model connecting Defense-in-Depth Theory, the AI Theory of Pattern Recognition, and human-AI collaboration in security operations, formalizing layered defense as a Bernoulli detection cascade with AI augmentation entering multiplicatively and per-layer recognition as Neyman-Pearson style decisions. Aims to ground qualitative concerns about over-automation and analyst-skill erosion in formal structure.

entry.title: Compiling Sufficient Governance Context from Declared Losses and Reachable States: Exact Observation-Contract Synthesis with Cardinality and Cost Objectives

author.name: Gaston Besanson

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a minimal sufficient governance context: given a finite reachable-state model, a declared verdict, and candidate observable attributes, it synthesizes observation contracts (attribute sets that determine the verdict on all reachable states) and distinguishes individually indispensable attributes from jointly sufficient contracts. It provides exact synthesis under cardinality or cost objectives, with exhaustive enumeration where affordable, and binds selected contracts to gate schemas for governance.

entry.title: TransBERT: A Framework for Synthetic Translation in Domain-Specific Language Modeling

author.name: Julien Knafou, Luc Mottin, Ana\"is Mottaz, Alexandre Flament, Patrick Ruch

entry.summary: Introduces TransBERT, a framework for pre-training domain-specific language models exclusively on synthetically translated text, plus TransCorpus, a scalable translation toolkit. Focusing on French life sciences, it shows SOTA downstream performance is achievable with synthetic data alone, releasing a 36.4GB corpus, pretrained model, and code.

entry.title: The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Military Operations

author.name: Nicolas Drapier, Florian Mauberger, Aladine Chetouani, Aurelien Chateigner

entry.summary: Argues that the ethical challenge of AI in military operations is fundamentally epistemic: opaque, gameable deep learning systems fracture accountability in ways that International Humanitarian Law, presupposing human judgment capacities, cannot accommodate. The paper maps a concrete accountability gap across designers, operators, and policymakers.

entry.title: LWCal: Loss-Weighted Calibration for Tabular Classifiers with Noisy Calibration Labels

author.name: Zeming Liu, Hang Lyu, Jingtao Zhang, Yuan Xie

entry.summary: LWCal is a CPU-only post-hoc calibration method for tabular classifiers that down-weights calibration examples whose noisy labels are contradicted by the base model's held-out probabilities, requiring no clean labels, noise-rate estimates, or retraining. A gated variant adds a conservative disagreement gate with fallback behavior.

entry.title: Resource-Efficient Distributed Recursive Gaussian Processes

author.name: Josephine King, Ali Emre Balci, Raj Thilak Rajan

entry.summary: The authors develop two distributed recursive Gaussian process algorithms, ADMM-RGP and PDMM-RGP, for multi-output GP regression across multi-agent systems without centralized processing. They provide stability and convergence analysis and parameter-selection strategies that reduce communication requirements. This extends principled uncertainty-aware regression to decentralized settings.

entry.title: TNLearn: An Open Source Python Package for Task-based Neurons

author.name: Meng Wang, Tieyun Li, Juntong Fan, Hanyu Pei, Jing-Xiao Liao, Yaodong Yang, Jianwei Ma, Fenglei Fan

entry.summary: TNLearn is an open-source Python package for constructing and training task-based neurons, embodying the idea that customized neuron units, not just architectures, should be designed per task to capture task-specific prior knowledge. It provides automated neuron and network construction, documentation, API references, and examples. The package lowers the barrier to a neuron-level design paradigm in scientific and industrial applications.

entry.title: Riemannian Structure and Optimization for a Class of Low-Parametric Orthogonal Matrices

author.name: Ali Aliev, Maxim Rakhuba

entry.summary: The paper develops Riemannian geometric machinery for structured matrices formed by block-diagonal factors interleaved with fixed permutations, which appear in efficient deep learning architectures. For orthogonal two-factor matrices, it derives manifold structure and efficient automatic-differentiation-based optimization algorithms.

entry.title: Confidence Falls Short: Asymmetric Certainty Gains from Optimization Hinder Multimodal Classification

author.name: Longfei Huang, Xiangyu Wu, Yang Yang

entry.summary: The paper identifies that modality imbalance in multimodal learning stems partly from asymmetric gains in predictive certainty, where the strong modality becomes disproportionately confident during optimization. It proposes a multimodal Max Confidence Regularization with positive cross-modal intervention to correct this confidence discrepancy.

entry.title: Context-Continuous Preference Learning for Exoskeleton Personalization

author.name: Sunin Baek, Sungwoo Park, Daekyum Kim

entry.summary: Proposes Context-Continuous Preference Learning (CCPL), a Gaussian-process preference model that shares user feedback across nearby operating conditions to personalize exoskeleton assistance. Simulations and retrospective ankle/elbow exoskeleton data from nine adults show improved reconstruction and preference-based Bayesian optimization over independent per-context models.

entry.title: Untangling the Geometry and Speed for RF Sensing Spectrograms

author.name: Mert Torun, Darius Cuenca, Yasamin Mostofi

entry.summary: Develops a physically interpretable foundation for WiFi RF sensing that disentangles target motion from sensing geometry, jointly recovering speed, geometry factor, amplitude, and width of dominant Doppler ridges. A compact parametric representation validated via computer-vision analysis of a large human-activity dataset enables tractable learning-based sensing.

entry.title: Reliable Federated TinyML Deployment for IoT Security

author.name: Younsoo Park, Seokhyoen Bae, Shasi Kumar Ramachandran Prabhu, Suman Saha, Peilong Li

entry.summary: The paper combines federated learning with TinyML model compression (knowledge distillation, structured pruning, quantization) for privacy-preserving intrusion detection on microcontroller-class IoT devices. It evaluates reliability and stability of these compact federated models under resource constraints.

entry.title: Multitask Regression with Pairwise Fusion

author.name: Xiaodong Li, Zhentao Li

entry.summary: The paper studies multitask regression where coefficient sharing varies by predictor, formalizing structure via the number of active predictors and the number of task coefficients deviating from the majority value. It estimates coefficients via pairwise-difference penalties with matching upper and lower bounds.

entry.title: FFM-CP: Cross-Backbone Fusion of Vision-Language Foundation Models for Few-Shot Computational Pathology

author.name: Anh-Tien Nguyen, Trung DQ. Dang, Nghiem Tuong Diep, Bui Ngoc Han Nguyen, Tan-Ha Mai, Miriam Cindy Maurer, Phuong Hoa Nguyen, Thi Thuy Uyen Nguyen, Youngjun Park, Daniel Sonntag, Duy Minh Ho Nguyen, Anne-Christin Hauschild

entry.summary: Proposes FFM-CP, a framework that fuses multiple pathology vision-language foundation models in few-shot settings by aligning heterogeneous representations with a closed-form Orthogonal Procrustes transformation before learning an effective fusion. It addresses the fact that no single pathology VLM dominates across diseases and annotation is costly.

entry.title: Type-II Error Bounds for Test Supermartingales from Lower-Tail Hypotheses

author.name: Patrick Forr\'e

entry.summary: A companion to the authors work on safe sequential testing, deriving type-II error bounds for test supermartingales under various hypotheses on the lower-tail probabilities of log-increments, unified through a single master inequality. It addresses the catastrophic-bet failure mode where rare large losses erase accumulated evidence.

entry.title: NPBoost: Neural Processes with Gradient-Boosted Fixed Effects

author.name: Andrea Nava, Ken R\"olli, Armin Begic, Fabio Sigrist

entry.summary: NPBoost decomposes structured response variability into tree-boosted fixed effects shared across tasks and neural process random effects capturing task-to-task stochastic variation, training the two jointly with a boosting algorithm. The method is motivated by the connection between meta-learning and mixed-effects models.

entry.title: Classifying Interpretive Canons at the Sentence Level: A Benchmark from the German Federal Constitutional Court

author.name: Felix Ringe

entry.summary: The authors build a sentence-level benchmark for classifying interpretive canons from German legal theory (Larenz/Savigny tradition), using annotated decisions of the German Federal Constitutional Court. Baselines with four LLMs, including GEPA-optimized prompts, reach mean F1 between 70.4 and 79.2 across seven binary subtasks.

entry.title: Count Evidence, Not Sentences: Tempered Evidence Fusion of LLM Judgments for Long-Text Value Measurement

author.name: Yuhe Wu, Rui Qian, Guangyu Wang, Yuran Chen, Yuanchao Zhu, Junjie Yang, Zhengheng Li, Jiulin Cai, Tianyi Zhang, Zihan Dong, Jiaxin Liu, Yujie Chen, Guang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Tempered Evidence Fusion (TEF), a training-free rule that weights each sentence's log-odds by normalized information gain from a generalized Bayesian posterior, for measuring value orientations in long social media posts. This avoids the overconfidence of document-level prediction and the naive averaging of sentence-level voting.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Legal QA for Vietnamese Labour Law: Retrieval, Translation, and Verifier-Guided Correction

author.name: Nguyen Minh Chi, Mo El-Haj, Nguyen Ha Thanh, Dawn Knight, Paul Rayson

entry.summary: The paper introduces a bilingual Vietnamese-English legal QA suite (231 pairs, 75 annotated for five reasoning phenomena) and a verifier-guided pipeline that decomposes answers into claims, checks citation reachability and entailment, and corrects failures. It also proposes six automatic faithfulness diagnostics, finding learned-sparse retrieval performs poorly for English queries.

entry.title: ThaiTrees: Thai Syntactic Dependency Trees Across Domains

author.name: Attapol T. Rutherford, Papatchol Thientong

entry.summary: ThaiTrees is a 342M-token automatically parsed Thai corpus spanning news, Wikipedia, spoken transcripts, and social media, built with a reproducible cleaning and Universal Dependencies parsing pipeline. The resource makes Thai grammatical relations searchable and includes a released frequency lexicon and CoNLL-U parses, enabling quantitative syntactic research for a lower-resourced language.

entry.title: Controlled Attribute-Specific Summarization of Interrogative Dialogues

author.name: A Aditya Bhardwaj, Arjit Singh Arora, Md Shad Akhtar

entry.summary: The paper introduces CASPER, a chain-of-thought attribute-specific prompting framework with hierarchical multi-role evaluation (RoleEval) for summarizing interrogator-witness dialogues in forensic settings, plus MINDSum, a dataset of 6,000 annotated utterance pairs with event details, factual statements, character descriptions, and fillers. The combination targets high factual accuracy and attribute-specific relevance.

entry.title: A Decade of Climate Polarization on Brazilian YouTube using Language Models

author.name: Daniel Morais, Diego H. M. Magalhaes, Gabriel H. Silva, Andrea Failla, Valeria de C. Santos, Helen C. S. C. Lima, Carlos H. G. Ferreira

entry.summary: The authors collect over 240,000 Portuguese-language YouTube comments from 2014-2024 retrieved via Brazil-oriented climate searches and formulate stance detection as three-way classification (Believer, Denier, Inconclusive) in a noisy, low-resource setting. The work provides the first longitudinal characterization of climate stance polarization in Portuguese-language online discourse.

entry.title: From greenhouse climate to individual leaves: an organ-resolved model of lettuce growth

author.name: Md Hasibur Rahman, Faraz Ahmed, Hafiz Muhammad Bilal, Daniel Wells, Dylan Tobin, Tanzeel U. Rehman

entry.summary: The authors build an organ-resolved lettuce digital twin that simulates per-leaf photosynthesis, carbon allocation by age, size, and local canopy environment, and renders the evolving plant in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. It supports greenhouse climate decision-making by predicting crop response before conditions change.
