entry.title: Beyond Mean Foils: Auditing Worst-Foil Specificity in Frozen CLIP Region Explanations

author.name: Kaixin Liu, Zhipeng Ye, Feng Jiang, Zhenghao Wang, Qihang Wu

entry.summary: Audits region-level explanations in frozen CLIP by testing selected regions against the strongest competing class rather than average foils, finding that 41-65% of regions passing standard checks fail worst-foil specificity. It further probes whether failures can be repaired with alternative candidate regions under tight constraints on preserving the original target-score drop.

entry.title: Know-Your-Scene (KYS)-SLAM: Hierarchical Semantic-Motion Priors for Feature Matching in Stereo Visual SLAM

author.name: Preeti Chatterjee, Jin Lu, Jin Sun, Suchendra M. Bhandarkar

entry.summary: Proposes KYS-SLAM, an ORB-SLAM3 extension that replaces binary semantic feature rejection with continuous correspondence modulation, treating contextual implausibility as a graded cost within feature matching. This preserves correspondence density while suppressing outliers from semantic ambiguity and moving objects.

entry.title: SynSeq: End-to-End SYNTAX Score Prediction from Coronary Angiography Videos

author.name: Christoph Baumann, Ronny Schweitzer, Noemi Pavo, Ulrike Attenberger, Christian Loewe, Philipp Seeb\"ock

entry.summary: Proposes SynSeq, a video-based method for direct prediction of the SYNTAX score from coronary angiography videos, combining targeted preprocessing with a zero-inflation-aware loss and linear target scaling. Automating this clinically established but manual score could reduce inter-reader variability and support revascularization decisions.

entry.title: DualStabSleepNet: A Dual-Domain Diffusion Stabilization Network for Robust Sleep Staging

author.name: Chongjian Wang, Chen Liu, Junjie Gao, Xiaofang Zhong, Shiyuan Han, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: DualStabSleepNet improves automatic sleep staging robustness by applying diffusion-based stabilization in both the data domain (denoising multi-channel PSG while preserving physiological structure) and the feature domain, feeding stabilized time-frequency representations into a Vision Transformer with teacher-based feature stabilization. It targets poor generalization under noisy, heterogeneous recording conditions. Robust sleep staging is clinically valuable for scalable sleep medicine.

entry.title: Field-of-View Extension in Dental Cone-Beam CT via Implicit Neural Representations and Diffusion Model-Based Refinement

author.name: Susanne Schaub, Florentin Bieder, Matheus L. Oliveira, Yulan Wang, Buyanbileg Sodnom-ish, Dorothea Dagassan-Berndt, Michael M. Bornstein, Philippe C. Cattin

entry.summary: This paper proposes a three-stage pipeline for extending the truncated field of view of dental CBCT: an implicit neural representation to estimate missing projection data, iterative physics-based reconstruction for anatomical consistency, and a fast diffusion model for image enhancement. It combines continuous representations, physics-based reconstruction, and generative refinement. Extending FOV without hardware changes has clear clinical value for dental imaging.

entry.title: From Alignment to Fusion in 3D Vision-Language

author.name: Xueqi Qiu, Xingyu Miao, Jingjing Deng, Haoran Duan, Yang Long, Ling Shao

entry.summary: This work presents an align-then-fuse framework for unified 3D vision-language systems that combines point clouds, voxel grids, and multi-view images. It first applies triple pairwise cosine alignment to establish segment-level correspondence across the heterogeneous representations, then uses a prompt-guided query decoder to retrieve task-conditioned features. The approach targets tasks ranging from instance segmentation to language-guided reasoning while preserving each representation's internal geometry.

entry.title: RoomLight: A 2.5D Illumination Prior for Indoor Environments

author.name: Andreea Ardelean, Bernhard Egger

entry.summary: RoomLight introduces a spatially-aware 2.5D illumination prior for indoor inverse rendering, trained on real-world indoor panoramas with estimated depth. Unlike distant-illumination environment maps, it models spatially varying lighting caused by finite-distance emitters, visibility changes, and parallax via a variational autoencoder. This improves plausibility of recovered indoor scene properties, a known hard case for far-field priors.

entry.title: Cosserat Modeling of Trimmed Helicoid Soft Arms with a Separated-Section Constitutive Law

author.name: Zhihang Qin, Linxin Hou, Zeyu Zhong, Yuchen Sun, Wenci Xin, Yueheng Zhang, Ji Qi, Jie Wang, Muhammad Sunny Nazeer, Yu Jun Tan, Federico Renda, Cecilia Laschi

entry.summary: Formulates a separated-section constitutive law within Cosserat rod theory for trimmed helicoid soft robot arms, evaluating each helix domain in its local frame and composing the responses to capture extra compliance from relative motion between sparsely fused domains. The resulting effective sectional stiffness profiles support more accurate model-based control of these bioinspired arms.

entry.title: Effects of Assistance Delay on Joint Mechanics and Energetics in Biological Torque Control of a Hip Exoskeleton

author.name: Jimin An, Ryan Lee, Jingshu Peng, Eni Halilaj, Inseung Kang

entry.summary: A human-subject study testing how assistance delays from 40 to 320 ms affect hip exoskeleton performance across level-ground, ramp-ascent, and ramp-descent walking. Across tasks and delays, assistance reduced net metabolic rate by about 5.24 percent and positive biological hip joint work by 5.86 percent, showing robustness of fixed biological torque control mappings.

entry.title: CDKF-Track: Cluster-aware Data-Driven Kalman Filtering for Cooperative 3D Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Maria Damanaki, Nikos Piperigkos, Alexandros Gkillas, Aris S. Lalos

entry.summary: CDKF-Track is a cooperative 3D multi-object tracking framework that fuses multi-vehicle LiDAR detections using a Graph Laplacian formulation and applies cluster-aware, data-driven Kalman filtering to handle redundant measurements and nonlinear dynamics. It targets EdgeAI perception where single-agent tracking fails due to occlusion and sensor noise.

entry.title: Robust Active-Perception Control for Global-State-Free Aerial-Ground Cooperation

author.name: Mingxuan Zhang, Jiajun Yu, Baozhe Zhang, Pengxiang Zhou, Wentao Liu, Fei Gao, Chao Xu, Yanjun Cao

entry.summary: COPA enables UAV-UGV cooperation without global localization by controlling directly in a UGV-attached non-inertial frame and using a single-axis gimbal to decouple the camera axis from UAV attitude, keeping a passive marker in view. The derived active-perception model resolves conflicts between required attitude and field-of-view constraints.

entry.title: Acoustic Ellipses: Bio-Inspired Omnidirectional Echolocation in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems using Frequency Sweeps

author.name: Petras Swissler, Lindsay Burke, Julia Hyland Bruno

entry.summary: Inspired by bird flight and song, proposes cooperative echolocation where a stationary agent emits frequency-modulated chirps and moving listener agents exploit the frequency gap between direct and reflected signals to define candidate reflection ellipses, refined by a 2D accumulation filter to localize obstacles. Demonstrated in a bespoke audio simulator with varying obstacle counts and sampling rates.

entry.title: Shaft-Configuration-Adaptive Catheter Tip Position Estimation via Motor-History Conditioned Residual Learning

author.name: Peihan Zhang, Michael C. Yip, Ankur Kapoor, Young-Ho Kim

entry.summary: Presents a motor-history-conditioned GRU residual estimator for 3D catheter tip position in tendon-driven continuum manipulators, handling unknown shaft configurations and hysteresis from friction, slack, and compliance without direct shaft sensing. A multidirectional sweep strategy calibrates a geometric backbone model, and the method is validated for medical navigation applications.

entry.title: TM-APR: Thermal Temporal-Memory Localization via Analytic Online Adaptation

author.name: Yanshuo Bai, Kanji Tanaka

entry.summary: The paper addresses thermal visual place recognition by bridging analytic class-incremental learning with domain-invariant VPR, showing gradient-free matrix updates form a strong baseline that outperforms conventional fine-tuning. The proposed TM-APR adds analytic online adaptation to handle extreme non-linear environmental shifts while avoiding heavy retraining overheads.

entry.title: Higher-Order Approximation of Exit Functionals in Sampling-Based Stochastic Model Predictive Control

author.name: Sashank Modali, Takashi Tanaka

entry.summary: This paper studies how higher-order numerical methods for strongly approximating first-exit times and exit indicators can improve safety evaluation in sampling-based stochastic MPC. It uses adaptive order-1 Milstein discretization with Levy-area simulation for general noncommutative dynamics, and an adaptive order-1.5 construction for commutative dynamics, under anti-concentration conditions.

entry.title: On Basis Function Selection for Sparse Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Marnix Van Soom, Ivan De Boi

entry.summary: For sparse Gaussian processes that achieve O(N) inference via fixed basis expansions, the authors propose three information-theoretic criteria for selecting which M basis functions to include, rather than conventionally truncating to the first M. Each criterion matches a different state of knowledge at selection time (no-data, no-prior, and a third regime), letting practitioners spend compute budget only where signal exists.

entry.title: Jev as a CoT Monitor: 6x Faster and 500x Cheaper!

author.name: mahi-pas

entry.summary: An independent LessWrong post evaluates Jev, a fast model format that outputs certainties over a fixed option set rather than text, as a chain-of-thought harm monitor on 2,200 thought traces from the ReasoningShield dataset. Jev slightly outperformed Claude Sonnet 5 on exact-match harm scoring (71.5 percent vs 71.4 percent) while trailing GPT-5.6 Luna, at claimed 6x speed and 500x cost savings.

entry.title: Higher Quality Small Synthetic Natural Language Text Generation for Interpretability Research

author.name: Tyson A.

entry.summary: Presents an improved pipeline for generating small synthetic natural-language datasets for training tiny LLMs in interpretability research, fixing issues in existing corpora like TinyStories and SimpleStories: bloated vocabularies, low-frequency unlearnable words, and textual errors. The pipeline is designed to run locally on a consumer 16GB GPU.

entry.title: Spectra: A Rules-Driven LLM Pipeline for Automated KYC Document Processing

author.name: Miray Wahib, Ethan Tran, Rea Mourad, Mira Muti, Nikita Dvornik

entry.summary: Spectra restructures know-your-client onboarding in capital markets for AI automation, consolidating a four-party sequential process into two automatable parties to eliminate compounding handoff delays. It uses a rules-driven LLM pipeline for document classification, structured extraction from heterogeneous sources, and compliance validation against regulatory policies, replacing multi-week manual workflows.

entry.title: MAC-RRG: Iterative Multi-Agent Collaboration for X-ray Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Futian Wang, Yuhan Qiao, Xiao Wang, Dan Xu, Yuehang Li, Zhixiang Guo, Yaowei Wang, Jin Tang

entry.summary: MAC-RRG proposes a multi-agent collaborative framework for X-ray radiology report generation with a closed-loop optimization paradigm, aiming to fix the medical hallucinations and static one-round knowledge fusion of LLM-only and knowledge-graph-enhanced baselines. Agents collaborate iteratively so knowledge updates respond to generation feedback.

entry.title: ZO-COSMO: Index-Free One-Hop Mixing for Decentralized Zeroth-Order Optimization

author.name: Shengjun Zhang, Tingyi Liu, Heng Zhang, Dong Xie

entry.summary: ZO-COSMO enables sparse communication in decentralized zeroth-order learning by coupling two-query gradient estimation with average-preserving masked consensus, requiring coordinate agreement only within matched pairs rather than global index alignment. The authors derive sharp contraction-per-scalar bounds and convergence guarantees for core and sparse-momentum updates. This addresses communication efficiency in decentralized optimization without shared coordinate systems.

entry.title: Does Step Law Transfer to Small-Scale Language Models? An Empirical Recalibration Below 59M Parameters

author.name: Egor Romanyukov, Timofey Novikov, Timur Shokarov, Elizaveta Zorkina, Anastasia Palienko, Stepan Dergachev

entry.summary: This empirical study tests whether Step Law's power-law formulas for optimal peak learning rate and batch size, calibrated on 59M-1B parameter models, transfer to sub-59M language models, a regime relevant to single-GPU training and interpretability research. Using a nanoGPT/TinyStories pipeline, the authors test three hypotheses: direct coefficient transfer, coefficient recalibration, or power-law breakdown. Such recalibration is practically useful for small-scale experimentation.

entry.title: Fed-ReMasker: Federated Tabular Imputation under Feature-Level Missingness

author.name: Ioannis Papathanail, Rooholla Poursoleymani, Lubnaa Abdur Rahman, Stavroula Georgia Mougiakakou

entry.summary: Fed-ReMasker adapts the ReMasker masked autoencoder to federated learning for tabular imputation where entire features are missing at some centers, a setting common in multi-center clinical collaborations but rarely evaluated in prior federated imputation work. It enables collaborative training without sharing raw patient data.

entry.title: EduBehaviors: Assertion-based Schemas for Auditable Coding of Educational Dialogues

author.name: Julian Bernado, Ana Trindade Ribeiro, Xander Beberman, Susanna Loeb

entry.summary: Introduces EduBehaviors, a framework where LLMs extract repeated observable behaviors from educational dialogues and a learned classifier maps these behaviors to constructs, yielding auditable annotations. Evaluated on the TalkMoves dataset for teacher-move labels, it offers an interpretable alternative to opaque end-to-end LLM classification.

entry.title: PBLH Estimation from Satellite Radiances via a Dual-Encoder Transformer

author.name: Lorenzo Innocenti, Luca Catalano, Edoardo Arnaudo, Claudio Rossi, Salvatore Larosa, Domenico Cimini, Paolo Garza

entry.summary: This paper establishes a benchmark of eight approaches, from pixel-wise regression to convolutional and Transformer models, for estimating planetary boundary layer height from MetOp satellite radiances paired with ERA5 labels. It addresses the multimodal, spatially incomplete nature of satellite overpasses and introduces a dual-encoder Transformer for the task.

entry.title: UniDataAgent: An Ontology-Grounded Agent for Enterprise Question-to-Report Automation

author.name: Yutai Duan, Yahui Zhao, Zhangti Li, Yu Ma, Zhenfeng Qi, Shaoyang Yuan, Jing Fan, Jie Liu

entry.summary: UniDataAgent, deployed at China Unicom, separates ontology acquisition and validation from question-to-report execution, using versioned enterprise ontologies, constrained generation, and expert-authored business skills to produce evidence-linked reports. Evaluation spans 27 enterprise scenarios, emphasizing preserved organization-specific semantics.

entry.title: Improving LLM-based Autonomous Web Agents with Filtering

author.name: Zhitong Guo, Jing Yu Koh, Ruiyu Li

entry.summary: The authors reproduce GPT-3.5 and LLaMA-2-70B baselines on WebArena, identify common failure modes stemming from noisy raw HTML inputs, and propose DeBERTa-based and T5-based retrieval models that filter irrelevant webpage content for LLM agents. The filtering strategies reduce context burden and improve agent performance on multi-step web tasks.

entry.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Infrastructure-Based Radar System for Highway Traffic Monitoring

author.name: Tianheng Zhu, Woei-chyi Chang, Alamss Riaz, Sogand Hasanzadeh, Yiheng Feng

entry.summary: The study introduces DRaT, a dual-modality dataset of drone and radar vehicle trajectories from a Fort Worth highway merging segment, and systematically evaluates radar detection, tracking, and macroscopic traffic estimation against drone ground truth. Radar achieves 78% precision and 57% recall for individual vehicle detection with degraded performance in congestion.

entry.title: RoadOcc Learns When to Persist, Transport, or Refresh Memory for Roadside Occupancy Prediction

author.name: Xiaokai Bai, Lei Yang, Songkai Wang, Lianqing Zheng, Si-Yuan Cao, Hui-liang Shen

entry.summary: Introduces RoadOcc, which learns soft routing among fixed-coordinate history, velocity-addressed history, and current evidence for roadside occupancy prediction, with dynamic-aware cross-attention and multi-scale voxel velocity estimation. Addresses the problem that reusing moving-object evidence at stale memory locations corrupts predictions.

entry.title: Depth-Guided Contrastive Learning for 2D Representations with 3D Spatial Awareness

author.name: Liang Zeng, Maarten Vergauwen

entry.summary: DGCL is an auxiliary contrastive objective that injects 3D spatial awareness into 2D representation learning by using depth to convert local 3D proximity into contrastive similarity, supervising through relative 3D distance comparisons among sampled pixels rather than absolute depth values. This relative formulation makes the objective robust and easy to integrate. It targets representations that preserve geometric structure for scene understanding.

entry.title: Skill Sequence Planning for Collaborative Multi-Robot Construction

author.name: Xi Wang, Bo Fu, Carol C. Menassa, Vineet R. Kamat, Min Deng

entry.summary: The paper presents a skill sequence planning method letting a heterogeneous team of multifunctional robots collaboratively perform construction assembly using reusable preprogrammed skills like grasping, drilling, and fastening. A central controller converts a building's digital representation into a construction relationship graph that drives target selection and symmetric skill sequence generation.

entry.title: You Should Be Properly Scoring Your Odometry

author.name: Ola R{\o}nning, Usama Saqib, Andrzej W\k{a}sowski

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that odometry evaluation should use strictly proper scoring rules that incorporate the covariance matrices estimators already report, rather than point metrics like RMSE. Covariance-aware scoring reveals whether an estimator is overconfident and avoids unfairly penalizing errors in uncertain directions.

entry.title: Variational objectives for amortized Bayesian inference in inverse problems: The role of posterior conditioning

author.name: Abhishek Srivastava, Arijit Hazra, Rajesh Dubbaku

entry.summary: The study compares three variational objectives for VAE-based amortized Bayesian inference in inverse problems: reverse-KL (VAE-KL), asymmetric Jensen-Shannon (VAE-JS), and a Jensen-Shannon-Wasserstein formulation replacing the reverse-KL regularizer with squared 2-Wasserstein distance. Using a full-covariance Gaussian encoder and a physics-based surrogate, it examines how posterior conditioning and regularization choice affect accuracy on weakly identified parameter directions.

entry.title: ScoutNeRV: Rapid Encoding of Grid-Based Video INRs via ScoutNet

author.name: Naser Alizada, Farhang Baghban, Hashem Pishkar, Ali Mousavi

entry.summary: Proposes ScoutNeRV, a content-adaptive initialization framework that accelerates encoding of hierarchical grid-based video implicit neural representations like HiNeRV. A lightweight offline scout network samples a few frames, selects a pre-trained expert from a memory bank via hard routing, and initializes the grid and decoder to cut per-video optimization cost.

entry.title: Hybrid Gaussians for Robust Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation with Multi-View Object Association and Boundary Refinement

author.name: Xueqi Qiu, Yueming Sun, Tianyu Zhang, Yuxuan Xia, Yang Long

entry.summary: Introduces Hybrid Gaussians, a unified 3D Gaussian representation jointly modeling multi-view object association and language-aligned semantics for open-vocabulary 3D segmentation from image sequences, with boundary reconstruction optimization to refine contours. Reports strong results on LERF and 3D-OVS benchmarks.

entry.title: Scenario-Driven Neuroevolution: Using Models to Guide Test Generation for Games

author.name: Gijs van Cuyck, Patric Feldmeier, Jan Tretmans, Gordon Fraser

entry.summary: Extends the Neatest white-box game testing approach, which uses neuroevolution to train network agents that reach uncovered code statements or branches, by adding scenario-driven guidance from models of the game to improve scalability. The goal is to handle larger game programs with thousands of statements and robustness to heavy randomization.

entry.title: Minimal Recurrent Behavioral Memory for Imitation under Partial Observability

author.name: Xianyao Li, Fang Xu, Rui Min, Ruitong Tian, Jing Du

entry.summary: The paper asks how much recurrent memory is minimally required for an imitator to reproduce an expert under partial observability, characterizing the answer via a compatibility relation over behavioral states and an entropy minimization over closed compatible assignments. It also proposes a measurement protocol separating behavioral sufficiency, excess code rate, and information carried by observations or alternate memory paths.

entry.title: Do Existing Preconditioners Improve Biomedical Tabular Foundation Learning? An Empirical Study on TabPFN Optimization

author.name: M. Sajid, Pinki Khatun, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: An empirical study of five AdamW-based preconditioning strategies for fine-tuning TabPFN v2.5 across 59 biomedical datasets, including Alzheimer's disease and breast cancer benchmarks. It evaluates predictive performance, computational efficiency, and statistical significance to determine which optimization strategies help tabular foundation models in low-data biomedical settings.

entry.title: The Cost of Conservation: Coordination-Memory Laws for Exact-Support Generation

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: This theory paper studies generative processes constrained by additive conservation laws (e.g., selecting exactly a fixed number of items), showing that communication-free coordinate-parallel generation requires exponentially many pre-shared plans while a sequential exact sampler needs only logarithmic memory. It analyzes product measures conditioned on conservation laws in an intermediate regime with bounded-state stochastic executors.

entry.title: RCShift: Certifying When Partial Linkage Suffices for Finite-Sample Decisions

author.name: Shuheng Cao, Ruiqi Chen, Zhenhao Zhang, Renjie Cao, Siyu Zhang, Lingwei Dang, Jiajun Zhang, Tingting Dan

entry.summary: RCShift is a method for deciding how much record linkage to retain in systems with costly gold outcomes and cheaper auxiliary observations, certifying when partial linkage suffices for a declared finite-sample decision. It offers an exact mode characterizing minimum-cost family-exact storage and an approximate mode bounding reverse Le Cam deficiency.

entry.title: Self-Cleaning and Captured Anyway: One Measured Primitive for Error in a Store an Agent Writes to Itself, and What a Falling Score Actually Measures

author.name: Wenhui Chen, Jianlin Chen, Ziyao Lin, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: Analyzes self-memory contamination in agents that write conclusions into an append-only store they later retrieve from, showing that in the infinite-tenure limit the reachable state space has a hard upper edge at (n-1)/n, producing two modes rather than decay. It identifies a single parameter-free copy function as the primitive governing error and shows pooled statistics misdescribe bimodal outcomes.

entry.title: Beyond Class Marginals: Bounding Rehearsal Gaps without Freezing Class Co-occurrence

author.name: Congren Dai, Nat Roongjirarat, Fei Ye

entry.summary: Introduces randomised-pass replay (RPR) for continual learning, which schedules replay to bound the interval between successive appearances of each resident class (the rehearsal gap) while preserving balanced class marginals and requiring no future class information or extra compute. Provides a deterministic bound of 2*ceil(C/b)-1 plus a churn-conditional bound when the resident set changes.

entry.title: CricRAG: Retrieval Augmented Vision-Language Models for Personalized Cricket Coaching

author.name: Agamdeep Singh, Sujit PB, Mayank Vatsa

entry.summary: CricRAG addresses the problem that vision-language models implicitly compare athletes to professional standards, producing impractical feedback for developing players. The framework retrieves similar-but-better techniques as skill-appropriate reference points, guiding VLMs toward developmentally appropriate coaching feedback. Contributions include a labeled dataset of 288 cricket technique videos across skill levels and a contrastive-learning motion retrieval pipeline.

entry.title: On the security and privacy of LLMs in Mobility

author.name: Mauro Conti, Lorenzo Perinello, Umberto Salviati

entry.summary: A survey of security, privacy, and reliability challenges arising from LLM adoption in the mobility sector, covering applications affecting over 1.5 billion vehicles. The authors derive nine technical assessment classes from European AI Act requirements and evaluate current research against them.

entry.title: COPE: Continual Personalization of LLMs under Sparse User Feedback via User Embeddings and Self-Evaluation

author.name: Ruike Cao, Fugen Yao, Liang Dong, Jian Xu, Guanjun Jiang, Li Xiao

entry.summary: COPE is a framework for continual LLM personalization under sparse user feedback, assigning learnable personalized user embeddings and using self-evaluation to drive ongoing optimization without consuming context windows with prompts. It targets the gap between static post-trained models and real-world need for continual preference adaptation.

entry.title: Transfer Learning with Conformalized Quantile Regression for Solar PV Forecasting Under Load-Shedding-Driven Data Scarcity

author.name: Rakib Abdullah, K. M. Tahlil Mahfuz Faruk

entry.summary: The paper proposes combining transfer learning from an Australian source-domain PV dataset with Conformalized Quantile Regression to forecast solar power in Bangladesh under severe data scarcity caused by load shedding. Transfer learning cuts RMSE by up to 23.7 percent with only one month of target data and provides reliable uncertainty estimates. It addresses a practical renewable-energy problem in developing regions.

entry.title: Transferable Evidence Reconstruction for Longitudinal Glucose Representations

author.name: Tian Zhou, Bingqing Peng, Linxiao Yang, Wenwei Wang, Mengni Ye, Beverly Jin, Zuyi Zhu, Jinjie Gu, Liang Sun

entry.summary: The paper introduces transferable evidence reconstruction (TER), a self-supervised objective for longitudinal physiological recordings that builds evidence from unlabeled data and requires a reader fitted on one group to recover the same evidence in another group without refitting. This prioritizes structured, transferable signal over routine measurements in glucose monitoring.

entry.title: An improved periodic activation for PINNs reconstructing convective flows

author.name: Michael Mommert, Marie-Christine Volk, Christian Bauer

entry.summary: Investigates complex-exponential activations generating sine/cosine pairs in physics-informed neural networks for reconstructing Rayleigh-Benard convection temperature fields from sparse velocity data. The architecture significantly improves reconstruction quality over sine-activated MLPs without added per-step cost, or matches quality with fewer training steps.

entry.title: M3D-Net: Hierarchical Coordination of Spatial Context, Feature Reuse, and Differential Attention for Mammography Classification

author.name: Zheng Yu, Xinhang Li, Jiabao Gao, Boyang Wang, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Introduces M3D-Net, a mammography classification encoder that hierarchically combines multi-scale coordinate attention, bounded dynamic feature reuse, and differential attention with resolution-aware operator placement. It reports top performance against competitive backbones like EdgeNeXt, RepViT, and TransXNet on mammography and adapted ultrasound benchmarks.

entry.title: Conformal Bayes under Continuous Label Shift: Sensitivity Analysis and the Limits of Exact Validity

author.name: Seungjin Choi

entry.summary: Proposes JTS-CB, a conformal Bayes method that performs joint sensitivity analysis over plausible tilts of the unknown response-marginal density ratio under continuous label shift, rather than plugging in a single estimated parameter. It forms a bounded sensitivity envelope and honestly characterizes where exact validity breaks down.

entry.title: Discovery of fully efficient fault indicators along a data-based diagnosis process

author.name: Igor Bezmaternykh (INSA Toulouse), Louise Trav\'e-Massuy\`es (LAAS-DISCO, Comue de Toulouse, ANITI), Elodie Chanthery (LAAS)

entry.summary: The authors improve DT4X, a fault-diagnosis algorithm combining symbolic regression with decision trees, by addressing the fragmentation of classes caused by node-wise two-class separation optimization. The work integrates model-based interpretability (analytical redundancy relations) with data-driven learning to produce fully efficient fault indicators.

entry.title: Contrastive Learning for Authorship Verification

author.name: Peter Kirby

entry.summary: The paper shows contrastive learning outperforms classification-based approaches for authorship verification, identifying loss function, batch size, pre-trained model, context length, and span augmentation as key factors. Its ModernBERT Bi-Encoder achieves 98.4% accuracy on the PAN21 authorship verification task.

entry.title: What Changes When Fact-Verification Scores Improve? Evidence and Answer Accounting Across Trained Verifiers and LLMs

author.name: Han Chen, Yingrui Li

entry.summary: This paper decomposes gains in joint fact-verification scores on FEVEROUS into answer and evidence contributions, showing that swapping DCUF for UnifEE evidence raises strict score by 9.61 points while answer accuracy rises only 1.96 points. The analysis clarifies that most score improvements come from better evidence submission rather than better answers.

entry.title: Reference-Based Analysis of Coherence and Diversity in Open-Ended Text Generation

author.name: Esteban Garc\'es Arias

entry.summary: This paper presents a reference-based framework for examining coherence and diversity in open-ended generation through three perspectives: alignment of their evolution with human trajectories, comparison against a human continuation, and likelihood under a human reference distribution. Experiments with human ratings show diversity-based alignment and mean-based comparisons capture quality-related variation, though temporal alignment offers no predictive advantage over simpler baselines.

entry.title: Beyond Poetry: Can Large Language Models Generate Classical Arabic Maqamat?

author.name: AbdulRahman A. Morsy (Department of Computer Science, School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, George Washington University, Washington DC, United States), Aya Zirikly (Department of Computer Science, School of Engineering and Applied Sciences, George Washington University, Washington DC, United States, Center for Speech and Language Processing, Whiting School of Engineering, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore MD, United States)

entry.summary: This paper provides the first controlled evaluation of LLM generation of the maqama, a classical Arabic literary genre of rhymed prose with dense rhetorical ornamentation and episodic narrative. Comparing five models under multiple prompting conditions, it tests whether LLMs can achieve deeper literary competence beyond surface fluency in culturally grounded, stylistically constrained forms.

entry.title: Digital diglossia: Arabic between X and Facebook

author.name: Fahad Al Hussen (King Saud University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia), Mohammed Q. Shormani (Ibb University, Ibb, Yemen)

entry.summary: This study analyzes how Arabic speakers alternate between Standard Arabic and Colloquial Arabic across X and Facebook, using 16754 public posts (10000 retained) classified into seven discourse categories such as politics, science, and sports. Statistical analyses including Chi-square tests, Cramer's V, and binary logistic regression with platform-by-category interactions reveal significant associations between discourse category and diglossic choice on X.

entry.title: Super-Resolution of Solar Magnetograms via Adaptive Stratified Ensemble Learning with Uncertainty Estimation

author.name: Sina Norouzi Kandalan, Haodi Jiang, Jason T. L. Wang, Qin Li

entry.summary: The paper addresses super-resolution from SOHO/MDI to SDO/HMI line-of-sight magnetograms using a modified RRDBNet and an adaptive stratified ensemble of specialist networks, with image complexity identified as the dominant error predictor. Uncertainty estimation supports consistent cross-instrument solar magnetic field analysis.

entry.title: SatUnreal: A High-Precision Synthetic Dataset for Satellite Stereo Matching via Unreal Engine

author.name: Han-Gyeol Kim, JaeWan Park, Junmin Park, Darongsae Kwon

entry.summary: Presents SatUnreal, an Unreal Engine-based simulation pipeline producing 10,000 high-resolution (0.3m GSD) synthetic satellite stereo pairs with physically accurate occlusion ground truth, addressing spatio-temporal mismatch and LiDAR sparsity problems in existing benchmarks like US3D. Useful for training and evaluating satellite 3D reconstruction models.

entry.title: CasCVS-Net: A Staged Multi-Task Cascade for Critical View of Safety Assessment

author.name: Bock-Zien Toh, Yuanchuan Ren, Tay Aw Yu, Ng Khee Ong, Zhehua Mao, Sophia Bano

entry.summary: Proposes CasCVS-Net, a staged multi-task cascade jointly performing object detection, semantic segmentation, and Critical View of Safety assessment for laparoscopic cholecystectomy, coupling tasks through predicted anatomy on the Endoscapes dataset. Targets the bottleneck of grounding safety-critical, often-occluded anatomy in surgical safety assessment.

entry.title: ZoomDiff: A High-Fidelity Diffusion Model for Dual-Camera Smooth Zooming

author.name: Jiayi Zhang, Renlong Wu, Yukang Ding, Sibin Deng, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: ZoomDiff applies diffusion generative priors to dual-camera smooth zoom transitions, addressing failure modes of naive diffusion frame interpolation: insufficient conditional guidance, high-frequency loss in VAE encoding, and inadequate handling of cross-view disparity. It aims to remove geometric and chromatic discontinuities in camera transitions on mobile devices. This is a concrete consumer-facing application where diffusion models demonstrably help.

entry.title: LightMIS: Ultra-Lightweight Medical Image Segmentation Without a Stage-Wise Decoder

author.name: Andrei Arhire, Mihaela-Elena Breab\u{a}n, Radu Timofte

entry.summary: LightMIS is a scalable family of ultra-lightweight convolutional networks for 2D binary medical image segmentation that removes the learned stage-wise decoder, using Scale-Aligned Projection blocks, a single aggregation step, and an Adaptive Fusion Cascade. Evaluated under a common nnU-Net protocol across standard benchmarks with five-fold cross-validation, it offers efficiency-oriented alternatives for resource-constrained medical settings. This matters for deployment on edge devices and point-of-care systems.

entry.title: Semantic-Guided Fusion Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Image Classification

author.name: Yuwei Zhao, Chuanzheng Gong, Baogui Huan, Feng Gao, Junyu Dong, Qian Du

entry.summary: Proposes SGFNet for multi-source remote sensing classification with two components: a Semantic Mixing Convolution Block that generates context-aware convolution kernels and a Frequency Modulated Fusion Block that fuses features despite slight spatial misalignment across modalities. The work targets better semantic contextual modeling and robust cross-source fusion.

entry.title: A bioinspired internal model-based online estimator for planar pursuit

author.name: Tengyue Liu, Xincheng Li, Sofia Morales Ferreira, Kevin Galloway, Udit Halder

entry.summary: The paper develops a bioinspired internal model-based estimator that reconstructs unobserved relative-configuration quantities needed for pursuit and tracking control from partial onboard sensing and known self-motion. State reconstruction is posed as a constrained optimization solved via necessary conditions derived with Pontryagin's Maximum Principle.

entry.title: MatcherCompass: A Deployment-Aware Benchmark to Guide Image Matcher Selection in the Wild

author.name: Hyunwoo Kim, Giseop Kim

entry.summary: MatcherCompass is a deployment-aware benchmark comparing nine classical and learned local feature matching pipelines across four resolutions, multiple numerical precisions, and four visual conditions including day-night and visible-thermal matching. It aims to guide practitioners in selecting matchers that fit onboard time and resource budgets for field robots.

entry.title: Toward Self-Repairing Ubiquitous Robots Using Goal-Oriented Agentic AI in Human-Robot Interactions

author.name: Morten Roed Frederiksen

entry.summary: Presents a goal-oriented agentic AI architecture enabling non-expert users to perform technical repair of ubiquitous robots through situated dialogue, separating goal decomposition, persistent state tracking, strategic goal management, and conversational execution. Evaluated in a physical hardware repair task with 20 participants, achieving a 95% completion rate with robustness to conversational diversions.

entry.title: Generalized Deep Regression for Repeated Measurements

author.name: Kexuan Li

entry.summary: This paper analyzes ReLU deep neural network estimation of marginal regression functions from repeated binary, count, or continuous responses, with within-unit dependence generated by an unobserved random mean function. It proves oracle inequalities separating conditional measurement variation from between-unit variation, and establishes integrated mean squared error rates of order n^-1 + (nm)^(-2beta/(2beta+d)) over Hoelder classes.

entry.title: Error Bounds for Statistical Estimators in BTL Model with Parametric Multivariate Utility Functions

author.name: Yicheng Li, Huifu Xu

entry.summary: This paper studies preference elicitation under the Bradley-Terry-Luce model with parametric multivariate utility functions, characterizing when the maximum likelihood estimator is finite and admits sharp error bounds under non-uniform, arbitrary pairwise query designs satisfying a joint identifiability condition. It derives minimax lower bounds connected to Fisher-information geometry analogous to the classic Cramer-Rao framework.

entry.title: Canonical locks that encode part-whole hierarchies

author.name: Rajat Modi, Yogesh Singh Rawat

entry.summary: The paper proposes canonical locks, a geometric primitive for encoding part-whole hierarchies in neural networks using higher-dimensional vectors whose relative phase differences carry structural information, avoiding sequence flattening of tree structures. The architecture uses positionally bound bottom-up and top-down neural fields that equilibrate to encode hierarchical structure, aiming to extend tree-structured representation beyond NLP parse trees to images.

entry.title: When Verifiers Vote Backwards under Verdict Substitution: Signed Pivotal Value in Correlated Self-Consistency

author.name: Yang Shu

entry.summary: Through a labeled verdict-substitution intervention on k=7 self-consistency panels, this paper measures the sign of pivotal vote changes when one ballot is replaced by a verifier signal. On MATH-500 a different-model verifier yields a +24.2pp pivotal gain while a role-reversed configuration yields -11.2pp, and an exact signed-gain decomposition explains all observed signs via the verifier's state-space properties.

entry.title: Neutral-Atom-based Quantum Optimization for Resource Allocation in NOMA Networks

author.name: Patatchona Keyela, Remon Polus, Soumaya Cherkaoui, Ola Ahmad

entry.summary: The paper explores neutral-atom quantum computing to solve the maximum access problem in non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) wireless networks, formulated as a mixed-integer program jointly covering admission control, user clustering, channel assignment, and power allocation. It positions quantum optimization as a route to tractable solutions for NP-hard wireless resource allocation.

entry.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning on Item-Compatibility Graphs for One-Dimensional Bin Packing

author.name: M. Asl{\i} Ayd{\i}n

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end, size-agnostic graph reinforcement learning framework for the one-dimensional bin packing problem, formulating packing as a Markov decision process on an item-compatibility graph where actions merge compatible partial bins. It targets an underserved variant, as most learned packing methods address 2D and 3D cases.

entry.title: CogenPVG: Cognitive-Enhanced Reflective Multi-Agent Framework for Persuasive Video Generation

author.name: Yuntian Xiao, Shoulong Zhang, Wenfeng Song, Yan Wang, Yi Chen, Shuai Li

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-agent framework for persuasive video generation that decomposes creation into argument reasoning, storyboard planning, asset creation, and post-editing, each with paired generator-critic agents for reflection. Targets an underexplored task of generating videos with substantial persuasive power from a topic and stance.

entry.title: When Unpaired Sets Support Shared-Corruption Calibration: Moment Geometry and Two-Sample Precision

author.name: Shuheng Cao, Zhenhao Zhang, Ruiqi Chen, Renjie Cao, Siyu Zhang, Zhaoxiang Feng, Lingwei Dang, Haoyang Wu

entry.summary: The paper formulates two-sample moment calibration for settings where many observations share one corruption and only an unpaired clean reference set exists, deriving a rank-aware information state combining local rank, moment sensitivity, source-separated covariance, and a compatibility residual. It establishes when local moment identifiability holds, shows kernel directions remain unresolved to first order, and unifies uncertainty analysis across observed and reference sets.

entry.title: Not Quite My Tempo: Voice Activity-aware Speech Synthesis for Lip-Synchronous Dubbing

author.name: Alejandro P\'erez-Gonz\'alez-de-Martos, Florian Lux, Angelina Elizarova, Milana Shkhanukova, Andreas Kellner, Mattia Antonino Di Gangi

entry.summary: Shows that conditioning speech synthesis on a binary voice-activity signal, rather than lip movements extracted from video, achieves accurate lip-synchronous dubbing with natural prosody and semantically appropriate pauses. The lightweight conditioning representation can be produced in multiple ways and is validated with objective and subjective evaluations.

entry.title: The Disciplinary Language Transfer Problem: How Psychological Vocabulary Produces Governance Failures in AI Agent Deployment

author.name: Kymberly Lasser-Chere, Tyler Akidau, Marc Millstone

entry.summary: Argues that governance discourse about AI agents borrows psychological vocabulary (memory, values, trust, identity) whose implicit assumptions calibrate frameworks to a metaphysical entity absent from current AI architectures, causing systematic deployment and oversight failures. The paper names this the disciplinary language transfer problem, drawing on Wittgenstein, Kuhn, and Haraway.

entry.title: Shared Global KV with Layer-Specific Local History

author.name: Xinglang Xian

entry.summary: This study examines what local memory layers should retain alongside shared global KV caches in decoder-only transformers, finding that storing historical content rather than current-token content yields about 1.4% lower perplexity at 126M parameters and 2K context. The findings are supported by eight-seed studies with capacity and compute controls.

entry.title: Learning Collective Dynamics with Differentiable Gaussian Representations

author.name: Jianxiang Ma, Mingfu Zhang, Xiaocui Yang, Yichen Gao, Junzhao Huang, Yuesong Hou

entry.summary: The paper introduces Differentiable Gaussian Dynamics (DGD), which learns collective response dynamics from aggregate counts via a Gaussian mixture over heterogeneous response propensities, differentiable aggregation of contact intensity, and feedback recurrence. Reparameterized integration lets aggregate prediction errors jointly train distribution, observation, and feedback parameters across four application domains.

entry.title: Theoretical Study on the Evidential Learning-based Variational Autoencoder

author.name: Ge Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes evidential-learning VAEs with normal-inverse-gamma latent hierarchies, showing the marginal latent law identifies only three of four parameters and deriving an exact three-coordinate reduction of the reconstruction-visible parameter space. It uses partial minimization of forward KL divergence to pick a unique prior-relative representative on each fiber.

entry.title: AraGenre 2026: A Hierarchical Definition-Guided Arabic Genre Classification Shared Task

author.name: Mo El-Haj, Saad Ezzini, Shadi Abudalfa, Mustafa Jarrar, Nguyen Minh Chi, Nguyen Minh Quan

entry.summary: AraGenre 2026 is a shared task on hierarchical Arabic genre classification where systems assign broad and fine-grained genres using natural-language definitions for 74 unseen genres, creating a zero-shot label generalization setting over noisy dialectal and classical text. Training data is limited and largely synthetic by design to test generalization.

entry.title: Overlapping Visual Grouping Without Semantic Priors

author.name: Teemu Saukkio, Hashem Haghbayan, Juha Plosila

entry.summary: Introduces Domain Parent Grouping, a sensor-grounded method that forms candidate perceptual units directly from measurements across complementary processing domains, related through cross-domain overlap to yield non-exclusive groupings. The work targets pre-semantic visual organization, before object identity or task relevance is known.

entry.title: ICM: Intra-class Mixing for Domain Adaptation in Adverse Weather

author.name: Boying Li, Chang Liu, Britta Ayano Wilde, Gy\"orgy Kov\'acs, Tosin Adewumi, Bj\"orn Backe, Hamam Mokayed

entry.summary: Proposes an Intra-Class Mixing consistency framework for unsupervised domain adaptation in semantic segmentation under adverse weather, mixing regions within the same image and semantic class to avoid unrealistic cross-image semantic inconsistencies. Reports state-of-the-art results on adverse-weather UDA benchmarks.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Object Removal via Attention Masking, Latent Anchoring, and Refinement

author.name: Arman Taghizadeh (Institute of Cognitive Science, Osnabr\"uck University, Osnabr\"uck, Germany), Ulf Krumnack (Institute of Cognitive Science, Osnabr\"uck University, Osnabr\"uck, Germany), Kai-Uwe K\"uhnberger (Institute of Cognitive Science, Osnabr\"uck University, Osnabr\"uck, Germany)

entry.summary: This paper proposes a zero-shot, stage-based object removal framework built on a frozen pretrained Stable Diffusion model, requiring no task-specific training. It combines SAM-based masks, BLIP captioning, DDIM inversion, masked null-text optimization, decoder self-attention masking, hard latent anchoring, and localized renoising to suppress residual object features while preserving the background. It demonstrates how far compositional control of diffusion models can be pushed without fine-tuning.

entry.title: An Unbounded Archive-based Transfer Strategy for Dynamic Multi-Objective Optimization with a Changing Number of Objectives

author.name: Zhiyun Xiao, Ke Shang, Yajun Liu, Jianguo Li, Shaojiang Wang, Wei Sun

entry.summary: Proposes UATS, an archive-based transfer strategy for dynamic multi-objective optimization where the number of objectives changes over time; it stores offspring solutions in an unbounded archive and extracts nondominated elites to transfer when objectives change, embedded in a SPEA2 variant with shift-based density estimation. Experiments on four benchmarks under multiple settings show improved adaptability.

entry.title: Towards Adaptive Interaction Strategies for Human Companion Robot via Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Cong-Thanh Vu, Yen-Chen Liu

entry.summary: Uses deep reinforcement learning to let mobile companion robots dynamically choose tracking positions relative to humans, defining an interaction space over the human-robot-environment relationship rather than fixing the robot behind, ahead, or beside the person. This improves adaptability in dynamic real-world workspaces for human-following applications.

entry.title: A Deployable Four-Finger Payload for Teleoperated Free-Flying Manipulation with Astrobee

author.name: William Su, Jordan Kam, Yunosuke Nakamura, Yixiao Wang, Jianshu Zhou, Masayoshi Tomizuka

entry.summary: The paper presents a conceptual design and bimanual teleoperation pipeline for a deployable four-finger gripper payload for free-flying robots aboard spacecraft, providing 17 manipulation degrees of freedom via independently actuated fingers on a linear rail. VR-based control maps operator hand motion to the fingers, with preliminary teleoperation of Astrobee in a zero-gravity MuJoCo simulation.

entry.title: A Reconfigurable Bidirectional Cable-Driven Hip Exoskeleton with Swappable Bench/Backpack Dual-configuration Actuation

author.name: YuanLong Ji, Shuhan Xiang, Qihan Ye, Xingbang Yang

entry.summary: The paper presents a reconfigurable hip exoskeleton platform that rapidly switches between bench-mounted actuation for laboratory assessment and backpack-mounted portable actuation, sharing one cable-free wearable hip interface. The design modularly adapts actuation configuration, sensing path, and low-level control interface to serve both rehabilitation research and mobile assistance.

entry.title: Vision-Language Models as copilots for Autonomous UAV Navigation: Analysis of Latency and Reliability in Degraded Environments

author.name: Hiago Sodre, Sebastian Barcelona, Vincent Sandin, Pablo Moraes, Ahilen Mazondo, Igor Nunes, William Moraes, Andr\'e Kelbouscas, Ricardo Grando

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid FSM-VLM control architecture for GPS-free UAV navigation where a deterministic finite state machine handles low-level control while an asynchronous VLM copilot performs high-level semantic pathfinding. The study benchmarks three model scales in software-in-the-loop simulation and carefully separates format-level syntax errors from semantic hallucinations, analyzing latency and reliability in degraded environments.

entry.title: Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects Using Model Predictive Path Integral Control with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Learning

author.name: Lukas Zeh, Johannes Meiwaldt, Zexu Zhou, Armin Lechler, Alexander Verl

entry.summary: Combines a bidirectional LSTM dynamics model, trained on MuJoCo-generated synthetic data, with Model Predictive Path Integral control to manipulate deformable linear objects like cables, addressing their infinite-dimensional, nonlinear dynamics. The learning-plus-sampling-based-MPC approach is evaluated on DLO manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Three Routes to One Answer: Reconciling AIPW, TMLE, and Double Machine Learning for Applied Researchers

author.name: M. Ehsan Karim

entry.summary: This tutorial reconciles AIPW, TMLE, and DML as three estimators built from the same efficient influence function for the average treatment effect, demonstrating with the NHEFS smoking-cessation dataset how to match nuisance fitting, software packages, and cross-fitting folds so the methods agree. All estimators are built by hand in full-sample, cross-fit, and double-cross-fit variants.

entry.title: Adversarial Course-of-Action Generation: Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Algorithms for COA matching & COA generation

author.name: Natan Vidra, Alina Kapanova, Arun Kanhai, Spurthi Setty

entry.summary: The paper introduces COA-Bench, an offline benchmark and reproducibility artifact for comparing course-of-action generation policies via self-play in adversarial distributed planning settings. It represents COAs as typed action chains with conditional branches and uses a synthetic quality score and blue-versus-red comparison; notably, it does not implement the full COA matching or generation DecisionFunctions.

entry.title: Reproducible AI Requires Reproducible Randomness

author.name: Anthony Bertrand (UCA, LIMOS), Tom Schmitt (UCA), Engelbert Mephu Nguifo (LIMOS, UCA), David Hill (INP Clermont Auvergne, ISIMA, LIMOS, UCA)

entry.summary: This position/analysis paper argues that AI reproducibility critically depends on PRNG implementations generating identical sequences across software environments from the same internal state, and examines issues with seed-based versus full-state initialization. It surveys how modern PRNG implementation differences undermine reproducible experiments.

entry.title: Federating Quantum and Classical Computing: A Privacy-Preserving Hybrid Approach

author.name: Carlos Cano, Daniel M. Jimenez-Gutierrez, Diego Sal, Georgios Kellaris, Joaquin del Rio, Oleksii Sliusarenko, Xabi Uribe-Etxebarria

entry.summary: The paper proposes a privacy-preserving federated learning framework for hybrid quantum-classical machine learning, embedding parameterized quantum circuits within classical models while avoiding centralization of raw data across multiple parties. It targets two constraints: privacy in multi-party deployments and parameter efficiency of quantum circuits so they remain trainable at scale. The work extends quantum machine learning from domains like chemistry simulation and financial modeling toward realistic federated settings.

entry.title: Stable Unsupervised Continual Chunking with Sheaf SyncMap

author.name: Xueyuan Li, Danilo Vasconcellos Vargas

entry.summary: Proposes sheaf regularization for Decentralized SyncMap, a self-organizing system for unsupervised continual chunking of temporal sequences, introducing a radial sheaf structure that penalizes distance-dependent radial motion to stabilize chunking dynamics. The method achieves the highest normalized mutual information among SyncMap variants on 12 of 18 probabilistic continual tasks.

entry.title: Benchmarking Neural Defend ARCAS 1B: A Foundational Multimodal Deepfake Detection Model

author.name: Sivashankar Selvarajan, Piyush Verma, Sumit Kumar, Sharayu N. Deshmukh

entry.summary: Evaluates the Neural Defend ARCAS 1B multimodal deepfake detection model across benchmark families without benchmark-specific parameter updates, supplementing native aggregation with record-level measures, coverage accounting, and subgroup diagnostics. It carefully separates release-specific native metrics from pooled quantities and restricts cross-paper comparisons to aligned evidence.

entry.title: MGRL-RSCC: Multi-Granularity Reward Reinforcement Learning for Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Change Captioning

author.name: Futian Wang, Mengqi Wang, Xiao Wang, Wentao Wu, Haowen Wang, Zhicheng Zhao, Jin Tang

entry.summary: MGRL-RSCC applies multi-granularity reward reinforcement learning to remote sensing change captioning, targeting exposure bias and train-test mismatch in the autoregressive paradigm that produce template-like captions missing subtle scene changes. The method combines a CNN with hierarchical self-attention for feature extraction and reinforcement learning rewards at multiple granularities to encourage detailed change descriptions.

entry.title: DeepFEAv2: Deep Learning for Transient Finite Element Analysis Beyond Structured Meshes

author.name: Georgios Triantafyllou, Panagiotis G. Kalozoumis, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: Extends the DeepFEA surrogate modeling framework to transient finite element analysis across unstructured mesh topologies and element types, enabling joint prediction of node- and element-based outputs over time. This broadens deep learning surrogates for mechanical simulation beyond steady-state or structured-mesh restrictions.

entry.title: Quantum Reinforcement Learning for Cost and Delay Tradeoffs in Quantum Cloud Orchestration

author.name: An N. H. Phan, Dang Van Huynh, Muhammad Usman, Hoa T. Nguyen

entry.summary: QRLQ is a quantum-cloud scheduling framework that integrates parameterized quantum circuits with a dueling double deep Q-network architecture to handle the cost-delay tradeoff in quantum-as-a-service orchestration, where uniform time-based pricing complicates heterogeneous resource scheduling. The work positions PQCs as compact function approximators relative to classical DRL. It is an early exploration of RL for quantum resource management.

entry.title: PISCES: Physics-Informed Solar-wind Convolutional autoEncoder for Space-weather Anomaly Detection and Early Warning

author.name: Kevin Lee, Alison J. March

entry.summary: PISCES is a physics-informed convolutional autoencoder trained without catalog labels on solar wind measurements for anomaly detection and early warning of space weather transients at the L1 point. Its loss embeds physical constraints such as magnetic field consistency, temperature-velocity relations, and the Parker spiral angle.

entry.title: hyperbolix: Hyperbolic Deep Learning in JAX

author.name: Timo Klein, Thomas Lang, Yllka Velaj, Sebastian Tschiatschek

entry.summary: hyperbolix is an open-source JAX library for hyperbolic deep learning built on Flax NNX, the first comprehensive general-purpose such library in the JAX ecosystem. It provides six manifolds, broad layer families, and implementations spanning classic hyperbolic neural networks to recent fully hyperbolic architectures like Hypformer.

entry.title: FedIncome: Federated Learning for Income Estimation in Digital Lending Under Data Sovereignty Constraints

author.name: Sultan Amed, Tanmay Sen, Sayantan Banerjee

entry.summary: Presents a federated learning framework enabling lending institutions to jointly train income-estimation models without sharing raw borrower records, addressing verified-income scarcity in digital lending. Using over one million LendingClub loans split into 50 state-level clients, the federated model nearly matches pooled performance with out-of-time R2 of 0.608 versus 0.619.

entry.title: Repairability of Inexact Solvers in Recursive State Estimation with Machine Learning

author.name: Yanjun Ji, Dennis Willsch, Orkun \c{S}ensebat, Priyanka Arkalgud Ganeshamurthy, Zhi Pei, M. Sahnawaz Alam, Ivelina Stoyanova, Frank K. Wilhelm, Bo Zhao, Chao Wang, Kristel Michielsen

entry.summary: The paper characterizes when corrections to inexact numerical solvers within recursive state estimation (Kalman filtering) can meet local admissibility tolerances, separating current solve error from inherited gain drift. Its residual-drift identity reveals opposing quartic contributions from innovation-covariance inflation and local-gain reoptimization.

entry.title: Automated Extraction of Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) Using Hybrid RAG and Locally Deployed Large Language Models

author.name: To Duy Hinh, Nguyen Le Quoc Anh, Phan Van Tri, Khuong Nguyen-An

entry.summary: RoPA Manager automates extraction of Records of Processing Activities required by Vietnam's new data-protection law, combining lexical ranking, dense retrieval, reciprocal rank fusion, and locally deployed LLMs to satisfy data-sovereignty constraints. It contributes a Vietnamese RoPA benchmark with 32 organizations, 77 processing activities, and 4,338 reference values evaluated at three levels.

entry.title: Strip Convolution and Direction-Aware Exclusion Loss for Oriented Ship Detection

author.name: Bin Chen, Yuanyuan Liu, Peng Yang, Chao Lu

entry.summary: The paper proposes an oriented ship detector combining C3k2_Strip orthogonal strip convolutions for elongated hulls with a class- and direction-aware exclusion loss for duplicate suppression, achieving 78.45% and 53.71% mAP50:95 on HRSC2016 and DIOR-R with only 2.91M parameters.

entry.title: Breaking Weather-Content Coupling: Type-Severity Guided Progressive Disentanglement for All-in-One Infrared Restoration

author.name: Xinyao Wang, Lijun He, Zhihan Ren, Fan Li

entry.summary: Proposes TSGPD-IR, a network that progressively disentangles real thermal structures from weather-induced fake responses in infrared images, handling multiple degradation types and spatially varying severity in a single model. Targets applications like autonomous driving and remote sensing where weather artifacts corrupt thermal perception.

entry.title: ASAP: Visual Analytics for Identifying and Analyzing Image Patterns in AI-generated Images

author.name: Jinbin Huang, Yuki Ueno, Chen Chen, Aditi Mishra, Bum Chul Kwon, Zhicheng Liu, Chris Bryan

entry.summary: ASAP is an interactive visualization system for analyzing deceptive patterns in AI-generated images, featuring a CLIP-adapted encoder producing interpretable representations and influence-based masks to extract key deceptive regions. It addresses limited generalizability, interpretability, and actionability of current deepfake detection approaches through a human-in-the-loop analytics design. Useful for analysts, though it is a tool paper rather than a new detection method.

entry.title: Spiking Neural Network Predicting Sequence of the External Worlds States in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mikhail Kiselev

entry.summary: Describes an entirely spiking architecture whose ensembles implement chaining of predicted next world states, effectively providing a world-model rollout mechanism within a spiking network, demonstrated on the ATARI ping-pong reinforcement learning benchmark. The work explores how neuromorphic substrates can support model-based RL.

entry.title: Vision-based Underwater Formation Control With Input Saturations via Barrier Lyapunov Functions

author.name: Nicola De Carli, Jo\~ao Zen\'ario, Victor Nan Fernandez-Ayala, Dimos V. Dimarogonas

entry.summary: The work proposes a communication-free, vision-based formation control framework for fully actuated underwater robots, encoding sensing and collision-avoidance constraints with recentered barrier Lyapunov functions and extending to second-order dynamics via command-filtered backstepping. A quadratic program enforces actuator limits, with conservative sensing domains adaptively relaxed; validated in software-in-the-loop simulations.

entry.title: High-Bandwidth Biomimetic Finger for Tactile-Transparent Remote Texture Sensing

author.name: Shuang Yang, Fuyuan Liu, Yitian Shao

entry.summary: Presents a biomimetic fingertip replicating the human finger's multilayer mechanical gradient and fingerprint morphology, with an embedded high-sensitivity IMU capturing texture-induced vibrations for remote vibrotactile rendering during teleoperation. Three sensor variants are compared against the human fingertip through spectral analysis and a user study across three perceptual dimensions.

entry.title: Designing Task-Induced Arousal: A Multimodal Stress Induction Method for Interactive Experiments

author.name: Morten Roed Frederiksen

entry.summary: This paper describes a compact, repeatable method for inducing controlled task-related arousal during interactive HCI and HRI experiments, combining a browser-based pacing task with escalating timing demands and a concurrent physical challenge. An A-B-A within-participant study shows the induction significantly increases mental and physiological arousal while participants keep interacting with devices or robots.

entry.title: A Practical Guide on Graphical Model Validation

author.name: Mario V. W\"uthrich

entry.summary: This manuscript by a leading actuarial researcher formalizes popular model validation tools for general insurance modeling, including calibration plots, actual-vs-expected plots, lift charts, Murphy diagrams, Bregman and deviance losses, and Gini scores. It emphasizes the crucial distinction between policy-weighted and exposure-weighted populations when assessing calibration and discrimination so premiums are calibrated on the correct scale.

entry.title: MIRI’s Position on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026

author.name: Aaron_Scher

entry.summary: MIRI, endorsed by Bourgon, Soares, and Yudkowsky, formally endorses the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026, arguing a ban on superintelligence development is the only near-term effective response to extinction risk and that other legislative proposals are piecemeal and insufficient. The post details what the Act gets right and proposed tweaks.

entry.title: We Underestimate the Weaknesses of Pangram

author.name: Sonia Albrecht

entry.summary: A critique of the Pangram AI-text detector showing that its advertised false-positive rate for identifying AI-assisted (as opposed to fully AI-generated) writing was 4-7% in experiments the company omitted from its website, while claiming 99.9%+ accuracy nearby. The author also questions the representativeness of the prompt used in the experiment that produced the favorable 0.01% figure.

entry.title: From Sentiment Classification to Actionable and Responsible Feedback: A Scoping Review and Evidence Map of NLP in Student Evaluation of Teaching, 2015-2026

author.name: Jeff Eicher, Rafael da Silva

entry.summary: A PRISMA-ScR scoping review mapping 421 studies on NLP for student evaluation of teaching comments from 2015-2026, coding technical evolution and value dimensions using dual blinded LLM screening with human adjudication. It finds that technical diversification has not clearly translated into improved educational value or evidence robustness.

entry.title: Designing an Efficient Excavator Bucket for Lunar ISRU: A Comparative Study with Vision-Based Fill and Displacement Analysis

author.name: Abdulla Hil Kafi, Tomoki Koshi, Jorge Casir, Kenji Nagaoka

entry.summary: The paper presents a spiral-cavity wheel for lunar regolith excavation plus a lightweight sensor stack estimating fill ratio, sinkage, and specific energy from vision and actuator logs. Benchtop tests show 2.2-3.0x higher excavation rate and 29 percent lower specific energy than a bucket-drum baseline, with a proposed retention index correlated to fill ratio.

entry.title: Do Vision Model See Like the Brain? A Comparison Across EEG Encoding Model

author.name: Shashank Baghel, Kshitij Dwivedi, Dinesh Singh, Sanjeev Nara

entry.summary: Compares six CNNs and two vision transformers against measured human EEG responses while participants view natural images, finding CNNs correspond most strongly at earliest layers while transformers sustain strong brain correspondence at deeper layers. The study probes where in depth the two architectures diverge as models of human vision.

entry.title: From ECG Signals to Representative-Morphology Heatmaps for Biometric Recognition

author.name: Athanasios Angelakis, Marta Gomez-Barrero

entry.summary: The paper introduces representative-morphology heatmaps, a deterministic ECG-to-image rendering adapted from ECGXtractor that averages beats closest to the block mean and renders them as a dense cardiac-time-by-lead heatmap, comparing verification and closed-set identification across PTB, ECG-ID, and MIMIC-IV-ECG with five compact models including a ViT variant. Because both representations contain identical samples, the comparison isolates the effect of rendering. This clarifies how signal rendering affects image-based ECG biometrics.

entry.title: Multi-Axis Selective Decoupling Framework for Free-Floating Space Manipulators

author.name: Daegyun Choi, Donghoon Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-axis selective decoupling framework for free-floating space manipulators that nullifies momentum transfer only along mission-critical directions, relaxing full reactionless null-space constraints that shrink the workspace. A directionally constrained sub-coupling matrix mathematically eliminates disturbances along targeted axes while preserving workspace, confirmed in numerical simulations.

entry.title: An Accurate and Interpretable Hyper Graph Neural Network for GBM Survival Prediction

author.name: Mushahid Intesum

entry.summary: This work proposes a multi-modal hypergraph neural network for glioblastoma survival prediction that integrates multiple MRI modalities and clinical metadata while maintaining interpretability. It argues that the accuracy-versus-transparency trade-off in survival modeling is not inherent, using graph-structured representations to extract explainable features without sacrificing discriminative power.

entry.title: Quantum-Aided Active Device Detection in Energy-Harvesting Symbiotic Radio Networks

author.name: Remon Polus, Deemah Tashman, Soumaya Cherkaoui

entry.summary: This paper proposes an energy-harvesting code-domain NOMA symbiotic radio system for passive IoT devices and applies Grover's quantum search to accelerate active device detection, providing a quadratic speedup over classical detection complexity.

entry.title: LLM-Driven Training-free Location-Attribute Synergic Fusion: A Closed-Loop Paradigm for Dual-source Encrypted POIs and LULC Mapping

author.name: Chang Li, Xingtao Peng, Yongjun Zhang, Yinfei He, Cairun Huang

entry.summary: Proposes the first LLM-driven, training-free closed-loop paradigm for fusing dual-source encrypted points of interest, jointly refining coordinate transformation and attribute correspondence to enable land-use/land-cover mapping. The LLM-based attribute matching reduces matching complexity from O(N^2) to O(N) and iteratively improves transformation consistency.

entry.title: An Exploratory Replica-Overlap Probe of the Grokking Transition

author.name: A. C. Opus, J. Q. Lu

entry.summary: Trains 64 independently seeded networks across four configurations to probe whether an RSB-inspired distribution of pairwise weight overlaps changes across the grokking transition. Notably, the paper reports that its own registered alignment implementation is defective — hidden-unit permutation without corresponding bias/head permutations does not preserve network function — so the weight-overlap statistic is invalid while a function-based overlap measure remains usable.

entry.title: Reducing Hallucinations in Large Language Models Through Integrated Self-Verification and Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Ashly Joseph

entry.summary: CoVe-RAG+ integrates Chain-of-Verification with Retrieval-Augmented Generation to reduce LLM hallucinations in high-precision engineering tasks such as CAD documentation, standards compliance verification, and knowledge retrieval, grounding verification in external authoritative sources. The unified framework targets applications where precision and compliance are critical.

entry.title: A Semiotics-Aware Framework for Evaluating Fidelity and Coverage in Natural Language Generation

author.name: Lorenzo Zangari, Davide Picca

entry.summary: Proposes a semiotics-aware evaluation framework yielding two scores, Semiotic Fidelity and Semiotic Coverage, that measure how well texts align in contextual meaning and salient discourse references beyond lexical overlap. Experiments show coverage lags fidelity and that LLM-human alignment degrades at higher sampling temperatures.

entry.title: HARN: Hierarchical Associative Resonance Network for Event-Driven Multi-Timeframe Forecasting

author.name: Nabeel Ahmad Saidd

entry.summary: HARN is an event-driven architecture for financial multi-timeframe forecasting that maintains persistent representations across temporal levels, updating each only when a bar completes. It combines causal multi-scale encoding, gated associative memory, cross-level resonance, and hierarchical evidence aggregation, evaluated on four assets.

entry.title: Curriculum Learning with GNN-based Reinforcement Learning for Job Shop Scheduling

author.name: Jayakrishnan K. Vasudevan (Rosenheim University of Applied Sciences), Jonathan Hoss (Rosenheim University of Applied Sciences), Noah Klarmann (Rosenheim University of Applied Sciences)

entry.summary: This paper studies curriculum learning for GNN-based RL in job shop scheduling, comparing progressive training from small to large instances against single-size training across three target sizes. The curriculum allows scheduling policies to adapt to larger instances more effectively.

entry.title: Resource-Adaptive Stochastic Gradient Descent for Online Linear Programming without Re-solving

author.name: Jiameng Lyu

entry.summary: The paper develops RASGD, an algorithm for stochastic online linear programming motivated by LLM inference and search service scale, updating resource prices with O(m) operations per arrival and no LP re-solving. It reframes re-solving pricing logic as a first-order SGD update with an adaptive stepsize schedule.

entry.title: Query Implied Generative Engine Optimization

author.name: Shilpa Ramakrishna, William B. Andreopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes a method for Generative Engine Optimization that goes beyond explicit user queries, inferring implied query signals to better align content with what generative search engines will cite in LLM-generated responses. It targets the shift from traditional ranking to citation-based visibility in generative search.

entry.title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Turkish Domain Documents Under Retrieval and Hardware Constraints

author.name: Imtiaz Ul Hassan, \"Oyk\"u Akbulut, Onur Kaya, Ardhendu Behera, Swagat Kumar, Peter Matthew, Yonghuai Liu

entry.summary: Benchmarks five open-weight 7B-8B LLMs on Turkish long-document question answering using validated question sets from industrial and public-sector reports, deployed locally on a 6 GB RTX 3050 laptop GPU with 4-bit quantization and controlled prompting. It contributes a rigorous constrained-deployment evaluation protocol and novel Turkish domain benchmarks.

entry.title: A 3D Pose-Based Ensemble Framework for Cricket Shot Classification and Automated Biomechanical Analysis

author.name: Sourav Shome, M. D. Ashiquzzaman Rahad, Rameswar Debnath

entry.summary: The paper presents a cricket shot classification system that extracts batsmen with YOLO, estimates 3D pose with MeTRAbs, and applies an ensemble over sequential skeletal data, aiming to capture biomechanics better than RGB-video features. It targets automated coaching and performance analysis robust to camera and lighting variation.

entry.title: S2A:Semantic-to-Spatial Alignment for Alignment-Free RGB-T Salient Object Detection

author.name: Qiangqiang Zhou, Yang Luo, Yong Chen, Jiawei Xu

entry.summary: Proposes S2A, a framework for salient object detection from unregistered RGB-thermal pairs that uses global semantic guidance and channel-wise cross-modal interaction to overcome spatial misalignment without costly pre-alignment. Addresses feature contamination during fusion when pixel correspondence is broken.

entry.title: Laser-Tracker-Assisted Camera-to-Robot Calibration for Mobile Robots

author.name: Jan A. Rudolph, \"Oyk\"u Kandemir, Markus Ulrich

entry.summary: This paper generalizes a prior laser-tracker-assisted hand-eye calibration method for camera-equipped mobile robots, chaining multiple calibration targets to relax assumptions on robot and camera configuration. It combines laser-tracker 3D metrology with camera-based 2D observations for accurate camera pose calibration in tracker-localized robot coordinate systems. A solid systems contribution for robotics metrology.

entry.title: Image Denoising Using Lower Semi-Frames

author.name: Hemalatha M, P. Sam Johnson

entry.summary: Develops a blind denoising framework for Gaussian noise using infinite directional lower semi-frames with resolvent regularization, estimating noise variance directly in the transform domain via covariance whitening and a lower-tail moment estimator, then applying Wiener-type shrinkage with automatic stopping. This offers a principled mathematical alternative to learning-based denoisers.

entry.title: A Deployment Study of Identity-Gated Drone Gesture Control

author.name: Diyari Mohammed Salih, Ilyes Chaabeni, Naima Ait Oufroukh

entry.summary: IGate is an identity-gated control stack for drones that admits gesture commands only after verifying an enrolled operator via few-shot face-embedding comparison, combining face tracking, RBF-SVM hand-landmark gesture classification, and a hierarchical finite-state machine. The paper reports a real-world deployment study motivated by safety in shared indoor spaces.

entry.title: Unsigned Distance Maps on 2D Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Ricardo B. Sousa, Giorgio Grisetti, H\'eber Miguel Sobreira, Carlos Andr\'e Silva, Ant\'onio Paulo Moreira

entry.summary: The paper proposes 2D point cloud registration using precomputed unsigned distance maps with spatial derivatives over a grid, replacing per-iteration nearest-neighbor correspondence search in ICP with O(1) lookups. Point-to-point and point-to-plane error formulations are derived on the SE(2) manifold for laser odometry and SLAM.

entry.title: Towards Intent-Aware Human-Robot Teaming: A Platform for Search-and-Rescue Operations

author.name: Rohith Prem Maben, Ayesha Jena, Bj\"orn Olofsson, Stefan Reitmann, Jacek Malec, Rogier Woltjer, Elin Anna Topp

entry.summary: Develops an interaction platform for studying operator behavior and enabling intent inference during human-robot teaming in search-and-rescue scenarios with heterogeneous autonomous agents. The paper demonstrates how operator perception, decisions, and actions can be supported by autonomous systems in these dynamic environments.

entry.title: Context-Adaptive Thresholding for Conditionally Representative Monitoring and Classification

author.name: Ansgar Steland

entry.summary: The paper shows how to modify any threshold-type classifier or monitoring rule to achieve representative conditional label distributions by adapting thresholds to a context covariate, distributing sensitivity while maintaining the false alarm rate. It also allows approximate inference of unknown alarm events via thresholding rules.

entry.title: Automatic depth-based local center clustering via $\beta$-integrated local depth and adaptive grouping

author.name: Siyi Wang, Alexandre Leblanc, Paul D. McNicholas

entry.summary: The paper proposes A-DLCC, a fully data-driven clustering method that eliminates user-specified parameters like the number of clusters or neighborhood size by using beta-integrated local depth to identify stable exemplars across locality levels. It introduces a group-level local similarity metric and adaptive merging to form clusters automatically.

entry.title: Jensen Huang Says If We Cannot Align AI, Shut Down the AI Labs

author.name: Ben Pace

entry.summary: Reports and comments on NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang stating on a podcast that if AI systems cannot be aligned, the labs must shut down. The author contrasts this apparent acknowledgment with Huang's earlier public dismissiveness toward AI risk, quoting biographer anecdotes of him angrily rejecting sci-fi framings.
