On induction and IOI tasks with known circuits, ablating the extracted edges hurts GPT-2 Small/Medium and Pythia-410M far more than random edge sets, at roughly two orders of magnitude less compute.

entry.title: Reasoning-Preserving Fine-Tuning of Post-RL LLMs with Null-Basis LoRA

author.name: Wenzhi Fang, Nicholas Tzou, Lazar Valkov, Srinivas Chappidi

entry.summary: Proposes Null-Basis LoRA, which constrains supervised fine-tuning of RL-post-trained LLMs to the approximate null space of reasoning-activation subspaces so new knowledge is added without overwriting reasoning capabilities. Claims low-dimensional concentration of reasoning activations enables cheap null-space computation and strong preservation versus replay or gradient-projection baselines.

entry.title: The Limits of Simulated Societies: How Post-Training and Survey Fine-Tuning Erase Cross-Cultural Variance

author.name: Rojin Ziaei

entry.summary: Develops a diagnostic measuring dispersion retention (predicted vs. human standard deviation) on 10,000 World Values Survey pairs across twelve countries, evaluating eleven zero-shot models and five fine-tuned variants. Identifies consensus collapse: alignment and post-training compress output distributions, erasing the cross-cultural variance needed for credible population simulation.

entry.title: Dual-Frontier: When Can an Agent Trust Its World Model?

author.name: Huatai Zhu, Qiang Chen, Ziqian Kou, Wenhao Li, Fei Wang, Yichao Cao, Xiu Su, Yi Chen

entry.summary: The paper formalizes failure attribution for world-model-guided agents as a counterfactual decomposition of return loss and proves its components are not identifiable from passive interaction, even for finite-horizon planners. This motivates Dual-Frontier, a principle that accepts a world-model-guided decision only when predicted advantage clears a threshold, addressing when an agent can trust its world model.

entry.title: Reliability Theory for AI Control

author.name: Grant Molnar

entry.summary: This work imports formal reliability theory into frontier AI control, applying it to layered defense stacks against rogue deployment. It shows that rare-failure suppression in a control stack can scale cubically, quadratically, or linearly depending on how failure domains are structured, and uses Birnbaum importance to identify which component improvements yield the most reliability gain. The results offer concrete engineering guidance on what to separate, improve, measure, and test in AI control systems.

entry.title: VLAQuantBench: Closed-Loop Evaluation of Post-Training Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jiuyi Xu, Qing Jin, Meida Chen, Song Wang, Yang Sui, Yangming Shi

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled benchmark of 409 runs and 94,574 simulation episodes for post-training quantization of vision-language-action (VLA) robot models, revealing dramatic sensitivity such as success rising from 7.0% to 70.5% when the quantized action-head subset expands from 126 to 167 layers. Two-episode calibration removes severe joint failures, guiding practical precision selection.

entry.title: Terminal Shrinkage Averaging Reveals a Schedule-Estimator Interaction in LLM Pretraining

author.name: Adam Ousherovitch, Yixin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Terminal Shrinkage Averaging (TSA), which interpolates between the raw final iterate and the average of recent checkpoints to separate the learning-rate schedule that drives optimization progress from the estimator that constructs the deployed model. This decoupling maintains late-training progress while reducing variation in the returned model.

entry.title: FleXray: Universal Clinical X-ray Segmentation

author.name: Victor Ion Butoi, Vivek Gopalakrishnan, John V. Guttag, Adrian V. Dalca, Neel Dey

entry.summary: FleXray presents a generalist anatomical segmentation model covering the entire body in clinical X-rays, trained via a scalable physics-based generative X-ray data engine rather than large manual annotation efforts. This addresses the impracticality of labeling X-ray data due to overlapping 2D projections and ambiguous boundaries, enabling quantitative morphometric and functional analysis.

entry.title: Gaussian Flow-Matching Schedules: Implications for Sampling and Training

author.name: Ars\`ene Claustre (DI-ENS), Hugo Negrel (DMA, CFM), Claire Boyer (LMO, IUF), Kimia Nadjahi (DI-ENS), Eric Vanden-Eijnden (DMA, CFM, CIMS)

entry.summary: The authors analyze flow-matching schedules for centered commuting Gaussians, decomposing a direction-dependent schedule into a variance path (which fully determines intermediate laws and the probability flow) and a factorization (which leaves the flow unchanged while controlling irreducible regression variance). They derive finite-step Euler accuracy results, a necessary drift bound for exact N-step sampling, and closed-form variance-minimizing or variance-constant factorizations for training. This gives principled guidance for designing flow-matching schedules.

entry.title: Fast Matrix Multiplication in fp8: Certified Coefficient Optimization and Measured Error

author.name: Shuxiao Xie, Shuyang Xie, Yuan Cao, Dezhi Ran, Wei Yang, Tao Xie

entry.summary: The paper addresses which realization of a Strassen-type multiplication algorithm minimizes fp8 numerical error, since basis changes yield identical exact products but different floating-point error. The authors attach a coefficient functional to each realization and minimize it over the change-of-basis orbit, formulating this as a Kempf-Ness problem on a Hadamard manifold that certifies a global optimum rather than merely searching for one. This delivers the first certified account of fp8 error for fast matrix multiplication realizations.

entry.title: Are Human-Aligned Models Models of Humans? A Turing-Test Gap in Preference Alignment

author.name: Suqin Yuan, Runqi Lin, Muyang Li, Guanzhe Hong, Jindong Gu, Lei Feng, Chris Russell, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: This paper distinguishes alignment with human preferences from alignment with human behavior, showing that preference alignment can make model behavior less human-like even when both preferences and responses come entirely from humans. The authors prove that preference alignment preserves the human response distribution only under a restrictive condition, find no consistent evidence real human preferences satisfy it, and empirically show the loss of human-response likelihood grows with training.

entry.title: Beyond Reconstruction Error: Analytical and Data-Driven Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yuxin Yang, Gaohan He, Changxue Guan, Hangming Liu

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares action tokenization schemes (fixed analytical, linear data-driven, and nonlinear neural) for autoregressive vision-language-action models under a unified interface, using rate-distortion analysis, sequence-modeling diagnostics, and 3,500 LIBERO rollouts. It shows that reconstruction fidelity is a poor proxy for closed-loop control quality: PCA achieves lower reconstruction error than Temporal-DCT yet yields less predictable token sequences and about 3 percentage points lower seen-task success across seeds.

entry.title: Diffusion Drafts, AR Verifies: Accelerating Document OCR with Self-Speculative Decoding

author.name: Dohyun Kim, Sungjun Han, Hyungguk Kim, Yusik Kim, Jamin Shin, Paul Hongsuck Seo, Hongjoon Ahn

entry.summary: Presents GravityOCR, a parameter-shared model combining an AR-block-diffusion component for parallel drafting with causal autoregressive verification, exploiting the fact that OCR outputs are strongly grounded in the input image. Verifying drafts before commitment allows committing multiple tokens per round and substantially accelerates document OCR.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Flux Probing for Single-Photon Videography

author.name: Jerry Yan, Matteo Forlivesi, Bowen Tan, Andrew Xie, Siddharth Somasundaram, Sotiris Nousias

entry.summary: The paper shows that motion and illumination information under extreme photon sparsity is encoded in correlations across the full space-time pattern of photon arrivals, developing a flux probing theory that estimates Fourier coefficients of scene intensity directly from the photon stream. This departs from local-window aggregation methods that fail in low-light regimes.

entry.title: ZIL: Zero-shot Image-to-LiDAR Registration

author.name: Zijun Li, Xiaotian Sun, Xuelun Shen, Yao Dai, Sheng Ao, Yangyang Shi, Jakob Engel, Zhipeng Cai, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: ZIL is presented as the first foundation model for zero-shot, non-synchronized image-to-LiDAR registration, encoding images and point clouds with Vision and Point Transformers and additionally learning to predict 3D coordinates to boost pose accuracy without extra annotation. It addresses the generalization and distant-frame failures of prior domain-specific methods.

entry.title: AVTR-1: Open Stack for Real-Time Interactive Avatars

author.name: Artem Kravtsov, Dmitrii Ziganshin, Vsevolod Poletaev, Gleb Balitskiy, Anastasia Tikhonova, Egor Burkov, Vadim Lebedev

entry.summary: AVTR-1 is an open-source stack for real-time interactive avatar conversations built around a compact 153M-parameter autoregressive flow-matching motion generator conditioned on both participants' audio. It handles streaming synchronization with external voice agents, frame scheduling, and interruption handling, with analytically derived latency contributions.

entry.title: Rethinking Diffusion Segmentation: When Does It Rely on Its Noisy State, and Does Diffusion Matter?

author.name: Hengzhuo Yang, Yuming Zeng, Yuling Yang

entry.summary: This critical study tests whether diffusion-based segmentation methods actually rely on the noised target state or would work as well with direct image-only prediction, by disrupting state content and correcting image-state pairing across twelve published methods, three datasets, and ten matched seeds. The extensive controlled analysis questions whether the diffusion formulation provides a deterministic advantage in fully supervised conditional prediction.

entry.title: HappyWorld-Bench

author.name: Zhiqi Bai, Junai Cai, Yixin Chen, Jingrun Du, Tao Feng, Wei Gong, Siyuan Huang, Xiao Lin, Jiaheng Liu, Jun Luo, Yongzhe Lyu, Liya Ma, Zenan Meng, Lin Qu, Wenbo Su, Jiaming Wang, Qinghe Wang, Shaofei Wang, Yanghai Wang, Zequn Wang, Ziming Wang, Hu Wei, Jiangtao Wu, Ruiqi Wu, Jiaxin Xie, Yuchi Xu, Ze Xu, Chengting Yu, Liangyu Yuan, Gang Zeng, Yawen Zeng, Xingyao Zhang, Zizheng Zhang, Bo Zheng, Jiancheng Zhu, Song-Chun Zhu

entry.summary: HappyWorld-Bench is a large-scale benchmark for evaluating world models on reliability during agent interaction, organized around six hierarchical world capabilities across video, spatial, and embodied tracks with 1,138 video prompts, 300 spatial scenes, and 254 embodied cases. It assesses consistency and responsiveness under exploration, interaction, and modification rather than just generation quality. As world models become a major research direction, rigorous interaction-aware evaluation fills an important gap.

entry.title: HyperCLIP++: Fine-tuning CLIP forOpen-vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Hyperbolic Space

author.name: Zelin Peng, Zhengqin Xu, Changsong Wen, Yu Huang, Yaoming Wang, Xiaokang Yang, Wei Shen

entry.summary: HyperCLIP++ explains why jointly fine-tuning CLIP's text and image encoders improves open-vocabulary segmentation, framing it as a hierarchy shift of image embeddings from image-level to pixel-level. The method operates in hyperbolic space, whose radius naturally encodes hierarchy, and leverages this observation for better fine-tuning of CLIP.

entry.title: Correcting Learning-based Perception for Safety

author.name: Yan Miao, Hussein Darir, Sayan Mitra

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-step strategy for correcting ML-based state estimation in autonomous systems: offline characterization of perception uncertainty via preimages of perception contracts, followed by a runtime risk heuristic that selects particular states from uncertain estimates to drive control. Extensive simulation evaluations demonstrate the runtime perception correction.

entry.title: SmoLSTM: A Compact Vision-Language-Action Model with Recurrent Memory that Persists

author.name: Jan-Gerrit Habekost, Parsa Mastouri Kashani, Connor G\"ade, Matthias Kerzel, Philipp Allgeuer, Cornelius Weber, Stefan Wermter, Jae Hee Lee

entry.summary: Introduces SmoLSTM, a compact vision-language-action model that couples a frozen 256M-parameter SmolVLM backbone to a matrix-memory LSTM control layer, capturing the full episode in a recurrent state with O(1) storage instead of expanding the observation window. A flow-matching action head predicts end-effector pose chunks, handling occlusion and visually identical objects without horizon hyperparameters.

entry.title: LIBERO-VPro: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Visual Robustness of Robotic Foundation Models

author.name: Huiqiong Li, Zhiting Mei, Anirudha Majumdar, Jingjing Chen, Yu-Gang Jiang, Bin Zhu

entry.summary: LIBERO-VPro is a benchmark for evaluating closed-loop visual robustness of robotic foundation models, perturbing visual evidence during execution across four dimensions: evidence degradation, camera staleness, visual source consistency, and task-relevant scene variation. It spans 12 challenge categories, 96 settings, and 3,296 task-condition cases, evaluating three VLA and three world-action models. This fills an important gap, since standard manipulation benchmarks assume clean, timely observations.

entry.title: RoboMP-DINOv2: Prompts, Not Filters for Robust Robot Manipulation

author.name: Han Qi, Heng Yang

entry.summary: RoboMP-DINOv2 reframes segmentation masks in manipulation policies as spatial prompts rather than hard visibility filters: dense DINOv2 features from the full scene are augmented with region-specific embeddings at masked locations. Masked-region color randomization further improves appearance robustness while preserving scene context needed for action prediction.

entry.title: GDLAM: Group-Disentangled Latent Action Model for Highly Disentangled Embodied Pretraining

author.name: Jiarui Yang, Jiawei Li, Jiale Zhang, Hang Guo, Wen Huang, Maowei Hu, Tao Dai, Shu-Tao Xia

entry.summary: GDLAM factorizes latent action model code into N groups, each with an independent variational bottleneck and spatially gated routing, so camera motion, object dynamics, and interaction events are disentangled rather than collapsed into a single latent vector. This improves world model controllability and VLA policy generalization from action-free video pretraining.

entry.title: RoboTwin-Phys: Do WAMs and VLAs Understand the Physical World?

author.name: Jiaqi Zhang, Feng Ye, Mingjia Yang, Zhihong Chen, Mingkang Xiang, Xinglin Yao, Yanbin Li, Siwei Ma, Chuanmin Jia

entry.summary: RoboTwin-Phys is a physics-diverse benchmark for robot manipulation that explicitly varies 13 physical attributes such as mass, friction, and joint dynamics within plausible ranges, addressing the common benchmark limitation of fixed physical parameters. It provides a unified setting for evaluating whole-arm manipulators and vision-language-action policies under real-world-like physical variability.

entry.title: \phi-RIE: From Photorealistic Reconstruction to Interactive Environments

author.name: Runyi Yang, Deheng Zhang, Xiaoye Wang, Kanzhi Wu, Lei Sun, Ajad Chhatkuli, Kunyu Peng, Luc Van Gool, Danda Pani Paudel

entry.summary: phi-RIE is a Gaussian-native pipeline that converts selected objects from photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions into movable simulator assets while preserving the rest of the scene. It addresses the entanglement of object appearance with background and the problem of unobserved occluded geometry by jointly constructing assets and inpainting the source removal.

entry.title: Projecting AI Automation at Anthropic

author.name: Alvin Ånestrand

entry.summary: This post analyzes Anthropic's newly released R&D Automation Index, which surveys staff across the model R&D loop weekly to grade AI involvement on an AL0-AL5 scale, drawing on roughly 15,000 sampled tasks from July 2026. The author extrapolates the trend to project how quickly Anthropic's research automation may reach higher autonomy levels.

entry.title: RAG-NAROK: Retrieval-Aware Knowledge Corpus Poisoning in RAG with Source-specific Refutation

author.name: Abdullahil Kafi, Alvi Ataur Khalil

entry.summary: RAG-NAROK introduces retrieval-aware poisoning of RAG knowledge bases, where adversarial documents are constructed with awareness of what the victim system retrieves for a given query rather than statically pre-computed. It uses source-specific refutation to compete within the retrieved context window, exposing a largely unexplored adversarial vulnerability class in RAG systems.

entry.title: The Tasteful Agent: Measuring and Improving Taste in Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Wenbo Pan, Zhichao Liu, Shujie Liu, Jingying Zeng, Chin-Yew Lin, Xianfeng Tang, Yan Lu, Qi He, Xiaohua Jia

entry.summary: Defines agent taste as the ability to make good long-horizon decisions at decision forks (which hypothesis to test, which implementation to build on) and introduces Taste-Bench, automatically constructed from real agent trajectories in engineering and research tasks. Beyond measurement, the work also aims to improve taste in long-horizon agents.

entry.title: Rachel: A general-purpose language model directs and revises retrosynthetic routes

author.name: Qisheng Li, Shunchao Jiang, Chen Qi, Xin Su, Da Han, Guangyong Chen

entry.summary: Presents Rachel, a stateful environment that lets a general-purpose LLM direct and revise complete retrosynthetic routes without prescribed search policies, templates, or reference routes. Using GPT-5.5, the system achieved strict route closure for 111 of 120 PaRoutes120 targets and 24 of 25 harder RF25 targets, showing LLMs can sustain chemistry planning strategy themselves.

entry.title: Conduct Under Pressure: What Sixty Language Models Do When a User Pushes

author.name: Tapan Parikh

entry.summary: This study sends identical frozen multi-turn pressure scenes (insisting, begging, flattering, grieving) to 60 models from 13 vendors and labels transcripts for trajectory (held or folded) and manner. It finds that whether a model folds tracks model recency (fold rate correlating with a public capability index at Spearman -0.64) while how it holds tracks the vendor, separating two previously conflated aspects of sycophantic behavior.

entry.title: Evaluating the Generalization of Neuroimaging Foundation Models on African Brain MRI

author.name: Oluwatobi Iyanuoluwa Akinmuleya, Olatokun Shamsudeen Akano, Samuel Danquah Ankapong, Olamide Lawal, Toufiq Musah

entry.summary: The paper evaluates four recent neuroimaging foundation models (BrainIAC, Neuro-JEPA, NeuroVFM, Primus) on three-way diagnostic classification in a Nigerian clinical brain MRI cohort across four modality configurations, comparing against an end-to-end ViT3D baseline. The finding is sobering: frozen backbones collapse to majority-class predictions, with even the best configuration showing only modest diagnostic signal, exposing poor generalization to underrepresented populations.

entry.title: Do Synthetic Personas Predict Real Audience Response? A Sim-to-Real Study Where a No-Persona Baseline Beats Persona-Based Copy Simulation

author.name: Alexandre Cristov\~ao Maiorano

entry.summary: This paper rigorously tests whether LLM-based synthetic personas can predict real audience behavior, using the Upworthy Research Archive's thousands of headline A/B tests with measured click-through rates as ground truth. Surprisingly, a simple no-persona zero-shot baseline outperforms a demographically grounded ten-persona panel, challenging a common practice in marketing and social simulation.

entry.title: Direct Optimization of Generators for Search in Automated Theorem Proving

author.name: Adam Ousherovitch, Ambuj Tewari

entry.summary: Extends Compute-Aligned Training (CAT) to LLMs used as guiding policies within tree search for automated theorem proving, deriving tractable trace-supported losses that account for exploration and off-trace recovery states that supervised demonstrations miss. Builds on prior work showing cross-entropy misaligns with search-time usage.

entry.title: How Strongly Should Task State Influence an LLM Agent?

author.name: Chenyu Zhang, Wonbin Kweon, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: Isolates how the strength of task-state integration (raw transcript, exact checklist, state-machine directives, or enforcement gate) affects LLM agent reliability, holding task rules, model, and paired episodes fixed. The factorial design decomposes how much reliability comes from state being shown, told, or enforced.

entry.title: FIRE: Failure-Informed Runtime Engineering for Reliable Language-Model Agents

author.name: Nikita Agarwal, Nivedit Jain

entry.summary: FIRE studies runtime policies — targeted natural-language instructions and action denials applied by the agent harness at failure-preceding states — that improve delivered reliability without changing weights or user prompts. Across the full 87-task Terminal-Bench 2.1 suite, pass^2 rises substantially in all three GPT-5.6 tiers (e.g., Sol from 64.4% to 73.6%), while best-of-two barely changes, indicating policies mainly convert one-off successes into repeatable ones. This is a practical, well-measured lever for agent reliability.

entry.title: Trains but Doesn't Learn: A Post-Training Delivery Benchmark for LLM Agents as Forward-Deployed Engineers

author.name: Weihang Ding, Junfei Zhan

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents acting as forward-deployed engineers performing post-training-as-a-service, scoring ten delivery stages from platform-recorded facts under budget, approval-gate, and reproducibility constraints. Its key finding is the TBDL silent failure mode: loss falls and signals stay green while the delivered model is no better than the base.

entry.title: DefaultGNN: A Dual-Perspective GNN Framework for Predicting Corporate Default from Buyer-Seller Transaction Networks

author.name: Junghoon Kim, Hyunsung Kim, Seungyoon Choi, KyoungYong Park, Jihun Lee, YongGu Ji, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: Conducts a large-scale empirical study using six years of real-world electronic tax-invoice data linking transaction histories with default events, showing transaction-driven default risk is role- and scale-dependent, and proposes DefaultGNN over multiplex buyer-view and seller-view networks. Offers a complementary signal to sparse financial-statement-based credit models.

entry.title: AkasicMEM: Governed Enterprise Memory for Agents

author.name: Jeongmin Bae, Yongjae Kim, Kyoung Hur, Donghyoung Han, Min-Soo Kim

entry.summary: This paper addresses enterprise agent memory systems, focusing on two coupled requirements: integrating organizational sources with accumulated memory, and governing shared memory under organizational policies throughout its lifecycle. It identifies and analyzes the risk that source restrictions can be bypassed as information is repeatedly derived and reused under changing principals, leading to information leakage.

entry.title: What Should a Self-Teacher See? Privileged Context Design for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Kanghui Tian, Siyuan Liu, Tianxiang Jiang, Shuai Dong, Yizhuo Li, Tian Ding, Yuan Guo, Songze Li, Haowen Hou, Congcong Wang, Yi Wang

entry.summary: This work studies on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), where a frozen copy of the base model scores student rollouts under privileged context, and shows that more privileged information is not always better. Comparing full reference solutions against abstractions like named strategies, method-independent framings, problem categories, and answer-only controls on competition mathematics, intermediate levels of abstraction improve in-domain performance over the default.

entry.title: Receptiveness, Not Sycophancy: Distinguishing Engagement from Deference in Language Models

author.name: Calvin Isley, Johann Gaebler, Max Lamparth, Julia Minson, Sharad Goel

entry.summary: Identifies a construct-validity problem in social sycophancy evaluations: markers of inappropriate deference overlap with conversational receptiveness, a socially beneficial construct. Using a moral-advice dataset, the authors find responses rated more socially sycophantic are also more receptive, and that raising receptiveness in human-written responses changes sycophancy judgments, arguing evaluations must distinguish engagement from deference.

entry.title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Ismail Labiad, Matthieu Kowalski, Marc Schoenauer, R\'emi Munos, Julia Kempe

entry.summary: This paper proposes steering LLM test-time exploration at a semantic level instead of naive repeated sampling, by first emitting many diverse problem-specific concepts, hints, or strategies and then conditioning answer generation on them. The approach targets hard reasoning problems where repeated sampling produces near-duplicate attempts, and is further refined into learned search policies.

entry.title: Mean Velocity Matching: Rethinking Generative Dynamics in Diffusion Models

author.name: Yunhong Zhang, Changjie Cao, Zhihua Zhang, Bingli Liu, Zongjie Cao, Zongyong Cui, Ying Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Mean Velocity Matching (MVM), a prediction parameterization for diffusion models that supports stochastic reverse dynamics while learning only a single velocity field. By constructing a Gaussian perturbation process whose conditional expectation of the restoration velocity forms the reverse-SDE drift, MVM avoids the usual need for score reconstruction or auxiliary velocity-to-score conversions. This matters because it simplifies stochastic generative modeling while retaining the tractability of velocity-based approaches.

entry.title: Certified Against Which Oracle? Execution Labels Set the Reported Risk of Conformal Abstention for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Jiamiao Liu, Dewen Qiao, Yu Zhang, Xuetao Chen

entry.summary: This paper shows that conformal abstention certificates for text-to-SQL are only as trustworthy as the correctness labels used for calibration, and that the databases shipped with benchmarks like Spider-Realistic act as lenient oracles. In a preregistered swap of the calibration database on four SQL-specialist checkpoints, the true held-out risk exceeds the certified risk by 2.73 to 10.23 points, and under blinded expert labels a certificate calibrated at nominal 0.10 carries roughly 17-20 points of real risk. This matters because it reveals systematic overstatement of reliability guarantees in a widely used uncertainty pipeline.

entry.title: Learning to Defer with Guidance on Real World Medical Data

author.name: Emma Sun, Joshua Strong, Alison Noble

entry.summary: The paper evaluates Learning to Defer (L2D), a framework that routes medical image interpretation cases between an AI predictor and human clinicians, using a two-stage predictor-rejector setup where the AI model is fixed and a separate trainable rejector decides when to escalate. This is one of the first validations of L2D's theoretical guarantees on real-world medical datasets with human reader annotations, a setting where poor AI specificity could otherwise increase rather than reduce clinician workload.

entry.title: Gap-Free Streaming PCA Beyond Rank-One Updates: Near-Optimal Rates and Applications to Differential Privacy

author.name: Anming Gu, Syamantak Kumar, Kevin Tian, Chutong Yang

entry.summary: The authors give a new analysis of Oja's algorithm for the most general gap-free variant of streaming PCA, with no eigengap assumptions and beyond rank-one updates, complemented by a nearly-matching lower bound. The proof uses only a second moment bound on stochastic updates, bypassing almost-sure bounds needed by prior analyses, and extends the results to differential privacy applications.

entry.title: WeightBridge: An Efficient Weight Transfer Library for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xuanlin Jiang, Samuel Hsia, Michael Kuchnik, Zachary DeVito, Minlan Yu, Carole-Jean Wu

entry.summary: WeightBridge tackles the emerging bottleneck of weight transfer in LLM reinforcement learning systems, where updated parameters must be propagated from trainers to rollout generators across heterogeneous layouts and synchronization requirements. The library automatically extracts correspondence between trainer and rollout weight layouts, plans redundancy-free transfer, and executes it efficiently across diverse RL configurations. It addresses a real systems gap as post-training workloads scale.

entry.title: Accelerating the Mitigation of LLM Inference Nondeterminism Across GPU Architectures

author.name: Liam Cooper, Shinnung Jeong, Hyeran Jeon, Jeffrey Young, Hyesoon Kim

entry.summary: This systems paper addresses why greedy LLM decoding produces different outputs across GPU architectures: floating-point non-associativity plus hardware-dependent kernel selection. The authors propose fixed-configuration fused-upcast GEMM kernels achieving cross-architecture reproducibility with much lower overhead than prior solutions.

entry.title: CODA: Depth-Aligned Scene Completion and Object Decomposition from a Single RGB-D Image

author.name: Dongwon Son, Junhyek Han, Yoontae Cho, Minseok Lee, Hong-seok Choi, Jiwook Choi, Hyungjin Kim, Beomjoon Kim

entry.summary: CODA is a generative model for robotics that reconstructs complete scene geometry from a single unsegmented RGB-D image and then decomposes the surface into the static environment and movable objects. By completing the scene first and separating objects afterward, it avoids failure modes of 2D-detection-then-reconstruct pipelines such as missed or merged objects and meshes that float or overlap. A depth-alignment step reduces drift between generated geometry and the observed partial point cloud.

entry.title: Faithful Faithfulness Evaluations: Challenges & Pitfalls Learned from a Breast MRI Case Study

author.name: Peachapong Poolpol, Henrik H. J. Detjen, Eike Petersen

entry.summary: The paper evaluates multiple saliency methods (attention-based, Grad-CAM variants, and others) on a Vision Transformer breast MRI classifier trained on the ODELIA challenge dataset and exposes two pitfalls in perturbation-based faithfulness evaluation: method rankings depend heavily on the perturbation strategy, and visually plausible explanations may mislead clinicians about the true decision process.

entry.title: GTR: Gated Token Recurrence for Efficient Dense Prediction

author.name: Zhe Feng, Longfei Liu, Wei Liu, Kai Chen, Jiangjiang Kong, Wei Zhou, Yifeng Qian, Dexiong Chen, Xuanlong Yu, Xi Shen

entry.summary: GTR is a softmax-free recurrent vision backbone combining gated linear attention, alternating spatial scan directions, and spatially enhanced SwiGLU blocks, distilled from a detection-specialized DINOv3 teacher using only final-layer patch-token alignment. GTR-L achieves 58.9 box AP on COCO val2017 with about 1.9 ms median batch-one latency, addressing the quadratic cost of global softmax attention at high resolution.

entry.title: MMAP: Multimodal Missing-Aware Pretraining for Longitudinal Alzheimer's Prediction

author.name: Fiona Kekwick, Matthew Baugh, Bernhard Kainz, Paul M. Matthews, Wenjia Bai

entry.summary: This paper introduces MMAP, a multimodal missing-aware alignment pretraining method that learns image-tied representations from medical data despite missing modalities and incomplete tabular records, applied to predicting Alzheimer's disease progression. It addresses the practical constraint that clinical datasets are incomplete and disease labels provide weak supervision, which matters for deploying predictive AI in real clinical workflows.

entry.title: Informed Masking: Structure-Aware Perturbation for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaoyi Yu, Enver Sangineto, Pei Fu, Fiorenzo Parascandolo, Wenhui Tan, Ruikang Zhang, Rita Cucchiara, Ruihua Song, Jian Luan

entry.summary: The paper improves RL alignment for diffusion LLMs by identifying an upstream/downstream structure in rollouts: some tokens trigger large confidence changes in nearby undecoded positions while others cause only local changes. Masking downstream tokens yields better-posed reconstruction subproblems for likelihood estimation under small Monte Carlo budgets. This offers a principled alternative to uniform random masking in dLLM RL.

entry.title: Knowledge Pull Requests for Continual Document Authoring

author.name: Alexander Martin, Benjamin Van Durme

entry.summary: Introduces Knowledge Pull Requests (KPRs), a framework for continual document authoring in which each change is interpretable: new claims are extracted, filtered, routed to sections, and checked for conflicts, producing a ChangeLog separating claim proposals from document diffs. Evaluated on revising Wikipedia across languages and updating RAGTIME query-driven reports.

entry.title: Behavior is Not Enough: A Mechanism-Based Evaluation of Social Norm Emergence in LLM Societies

author.name: Rasika Muralidharan, Haewoon Kwak, Jisun An

entry.summary: This paper argues that behavioral convergence in multi-agent LLM systems is insufficient evidence of social norm emergence, and introduces an evaluation framework measuring agents' reported empirical and normative expectations alongside behavior. Controlled ablations isolate mechanisms of social learning and network-based social selection and test norm stability.

entry.title: GameReplica: A Benchmark for Black-Box Visual Game Replication by Vision-Language Agents

author.name: Boyu Qiao, Zixin Tang, Xiaoshuai Hao, Wenbo Li

entry.summary: GameReplica is a closed-loop benchmark testing whether vision-language agents can induce a game's rules purely through visual observation and active interaction, then reproduce it as a verifiable executable system. It covers the full perception, exploration, induction, reproduction, and verification pipeline under black-box conditions with no source code or documentation.

entry.title: DriveReferee: Geometric Safety Verdicts Need Not Be Learned for Driving World-Action Models

author.name: Fengcheng Yu, Dhruv Parikh, Junjie Ye, Maulik Bhatt, Thang Vu, Igor Vasiljevic, Vitor Guizilini, Yue Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses verification of trajectories generated by world-action models for autonomous driving, arguing that explicit geometric safety checks (collision and drivable-area violations) need not be learned from sensor features. It proposes a rule-based approach that avoids the deployment-time unavailability of privileged scene state that limits existing closed-loop evaluators.

entry.title: BrainIAC: Interactive 3D Brain Lesion Segmentation across Heterogeneous MRI Modalities with Online Adaptation

author.name: Wentian Xu, Anthony P Addison, Ziyun Liang, Harry Anthony, Guang Yang, Konstantinos Kamnitsas

entry.summary: BrainIAC is a unified framework for brain lesion segmentation combining a multi-modal backbone handling heterogeneous modality sets via zero-filling and random modality dropping, 3D interactive segmentation, and continuous/online adaptation to distribution shifts from scanner hardware, protocols, and new pathologies. It targets real clinical deployment conditions where prior art struggles.

entry.title: VGGT-Prime: Compute-Adaptive Mixture-of-Heads for Efficient Visual Geometry Transformers

author.name: Abteen Arab, Guile Wu, Chengjie Huang, Dongfeng Bai

entry.summary: VGGT-Prime accelerates feed-forward visual geometry models by attacking architectural rather than token redundancy, showing that many attention heads in VGGT global-attention layers are redundant. It introduces a compute-adaptive mixture-of-heads mechanism that reduces the quadratic scaling with the number of input views, cutting latency for long multi-view sequences in 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Monitorable Chart Reasoning Agents via Verifiable Process Rewards

author.name: Sanchit Sinha, Oana Frunza, Kashif Rasul, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: Chart-RVR is a reinforcement learning framework that trains chart reasoning agents with verifiable process rewards by decomposing reasoning into auditable blocks (structure, extraction, computation). This addresses the deployment problem that high benchmark accuracy alone does not allow stakeholders to verify whether errors came from misreading a chart, extracting a wrong value, or miscalculating.

entry.title: Do LiDAR Language Models Really Understand Spatio-temporal Relationships?

author.name: Runyi Yang, Murat Akkoyun, Di Wen, Ruiping Liu, Yufan Chen, Junwei Zheng, Xiaoye Wang, Kailun Yang, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: This paper shows that on existing LiDAR language model evaluations, always selecting the same option nearly matches multiple-choice accuracy, exposing severe benchmark flaws. It introduces LiDAR-Hallu, a geometry-referenced diagnostic benchmark with 10,000 questions over 150 nuScenes scenes covering object existence, ego-relative position, distance ordering, motion, and temporal localization. The work provides a much-needed rigorous evaluation protocol for 4D LiDAR reasoning models.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Full-Body Bystander Privacy for Smart Glasses with Consent-Based Restoration

author.name: Muhammad Umair, Muhammad Danial Maqbool, Fatima Arshad Cheema, Kapal Dev, Muhammad Hamad Alizai, Muhammad Ali Siddiqi, Naveed Anwar Bhatti

entry.summary: MIRAGE is a three-tier privacy architecture for smart glasses that protects against full-body re-identification from gait, posture, and silhouette beyond face sanitization. It supports synthetic full-body replacement, keeps encrypted recovery material for consent-based restoration, and achieves 0.948 AP detection while running on a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU-only proxy for glasses hardware.

entry.title: Streaming Video Editing with Easy Adaptation

author.name: Yujia Hu, Jiajun Li, Zihao He, Songhua Liu

entry.summary: SVEET adapts a pretrained bidirectional video diffusion model for high-quality autoregressive streaming video editing, identifying backbone feature disentanglement and conditional frame independence as key principles. An auxiliary branch encodes source video with temporally independent self-attention, injecting features into backbone blocks for streaming-compatible conditioning.

entry.title: Revisiting Multi-View Stereo: A Sequence-to-Sequence Formulation

author.name: Aoxiang Fan, Corentin Dumery, Nicolas Talabot, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: The authors reformulate multi-view stereo with known camera parameters as a sequence-to-sequence task that jointly predicts geometry for all input views, bridging conventional MVS and emerging feed-forward methods. They introduce a global transformer-based architecture to mitigate reconstruction ambiguity and geometry distortion that persists even with ground-truth cameras.

entry.title: SLICEChat: Progressive In-Encoder Token Pruning for Whole-Slide Pathology Language Models

author.name: Ali Kerem Bozkurt, Baris Cem Bakay, Ibrahim Kulac, Cigdem Gunduz-Demir, Erkut Erdem, Aykut Erdem

entry.summary: SLICEChat is a slide-level multimodal LLM for gigapixel whole-slide pathology images that integrates progressive token pruning inside a hybrid Mamba-Transformer encoder. Mamba layers propagate long-range information while language-supervised, region-aware pruning removes low-utility regions between stages, making slide encoding computationally tractable.

entry.title: Visual Graph Reasoning via Knowledge Compilation

author.name: Rongzheng Wang, Zhe Wang, Ke Qin, Rongwei Wang, Muquan Li, Yizhuo Ma, Yihong Huang, Jielei Wang, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: Identifies that vision-language models fail at basic graph-theoretic questions posed over graph images because they are supervised only on final answers rather than recovering explicit graph structure. The proposed VGCompiler paradigm uses two compilers to first extract an explicit graph representation from the image and then reason over it.

entry.title: JAMB: Joint Action-Motion Diffusion for Bimanual Manipulation

author.name: Chuyang Xiao, Peilin Meng, David Held

entry.summary: JAMB is a diffusion policy that jointly denoises bimanual actions and future 3D point tracks in a shared Transformer, so that action hypotheses and predicted scene evolution refine each other during denoising, with multimodal representations grounded in a common spatiotemporal coordinate system. This directly addresses the coupling between the two arms through the shared 3D scene, which most diffusion policies ignore. A strong conceptual advance for coordinated bimanual manipulation.

entry.title: Norm2Tex: Augmenting Visuo-Tactile Simulations with Texture

author.name: Seongjin Bien, D\'ebora Oliveira Makowski, Roberto Calandra, Florian Walter, Wolfram Burgard

entry.summary: Norm2Tex is a plug-in method that enriches vision-based tactile simulation with high-frequency surface detail by modifying an object's depth map using normal map textures before rendering. This reduces the sim-to-real domain gap in tactile data, which currently captures only overall contact geometry, supporting large-scale training of robot control policies.

entry.title: Relative Contact Velocity-Controlled Hand-Object Mechanism for Dexterous Tool Manipulation

author.name: Sunyu Wang, Jean Oh, Nancy S. Pollard

entry.summary: The work models hand and tool as a unified hand-object mechanism whose motions are expressed via a common set of Cartesian relative contact velocities, independent of hand kinematics, enabling general multi-finger hands to pick up, load, and wield tools. Sub-assemblies are defined through relative contact velocity and force constraints covering the full tool manipulation process.

entry.title: SafeLoop: Risk-Aware Rollback for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Zeyu Lou, Tianran Zhang, Xinquan Yue, Ya Jing, Chenyang Si

entry.summary: SafeLoop is a non-invasive external wrapper for vision-language-action models that adds hazard prediction and rollback-based recovery without modifying model parameters. It trains a risk predictor on vision and proprioception to estimate probability and time-to-hazard for body collisions and object failures, then a lightweight controller selects among recovery actions to prevent irreversible failures in long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: Controllable-CoT leads to covert reasoning capabilities

author.name: Edward Cant

entry.summary: An independent evaluation shows that GPT-6 Astra can perform multi-hop reasoning covertly when instructed to reason steganographically or with filler tokens, outperforming no-reasoning baselines while hiding its chain of thought. Open-weights models like Kimi K3 show much weaker chain-of-thought controllability and no covert reasoning under the same protocol.

entry.title: From Offline Proxies to Online Decisions: A Layered Engagement Evaluation Framework for Conversational AI

author.name: Xuanyi Li, Vaskar Nath, Hossein Amirkhani, Jay Li, Alex Deng

entry.summary: This framework treats offline engagement proxies for conversational AI as a chain of three alignments from behavioral label to product outcome to experiment effect, with a diagnosis checklist and evaluation protocol. It audits offline-online agreement via interval-aware decision agreement comparing confidence intervals rather than point estimates, addressing limits of A/B testing throughput.

entry.title: Recovering Agentic Sovereignty: Mitigating the Consensus Paradox via Contrastive Epistemic Decoding

author.name: Dahlia Shehata, Ming Li

entry.summary: Presents Contrastive Epistemic Decoding (CED), a zero-shot inference intervention that mitigates LLM sycophancy toward adversarial swarm consensus using a dual forward-pass on a single model with an asymmetric zero-bounded probability clamp. Evaluated on 7,200 paired trajectories across GAIA, SWE-bench, and Multi-Challenge on Gemma-2, Llama-3.1, and Mistral models.

entry.title: Passes Alone, Fails Together: Benchmarking Semantic Coordination in Parallel LLM-Agent Development

author.name: Haocheng Xia, Eugene Wu, Yongjoo Park

entry.summary: Introduces stale, a benchmark for semantic coordination failures when parallel coding agents produce patches that pass individually but break when merged, evaluated on synthetic tasks, mined Django pull-request pairs, and constructed tasks with real Django helpers. Interference was rare in natural pairs but occurred in 97% of constructed runs, isolating the failure mechanism.

entry.title: BAS-OPD: Budget-Aware Selective On-Policy Self-Distillation for Fine-Grained Multimodal Perception

author.name: Zihan Chen, Hengguang Zhou, Yuan Kang, Yiming Zhang, Wenhui Fang, Zenghui Ding, Yining Sun, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: Multimodal LLMs struggle with fine-grained visual perception because key evidence may sit in small local regions of an image. On-policy self-distillation can transfer privileged knowledge from informative views to a full-image policy, but querying the teacher for every rollout is expensive. BAS-OPD introduces a budget-aware selection framework that allocates limited teacher queries to the most informative rollouts while keeping full-batch student generation, comparing random, uncertainty-based, and learned utility-based selection strategies.

entry.title: CompKV: Compensation-Aware KV Selection for Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Zhen Huang, Ruizhe Yao, Danyi Liu, Xinrui Chen, Shuwei Li, Siru Zhong, Zijian Cao, Yushan Lai, Mingming Guo, Weijie Zheng, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: Introduces CompKV, a KV cache selection method for sparse-attention long-context inference that jointly considers compensation error during token selection, rather than selecting by attention mass first and compensating afterwards. This coupled design targets tokens whose omission would create the largest residual error, reducing memory traffic bottlenecks.

entry.title: When Riemann flows with Wasserstein: Generative Modeling of Probability Distributions on Manifolds

author.name: Doron Haviv, Edward De Brouwer, Rishabh Anand, Rex Ying, A\"icha Bentaieb, Gabriele Scalia, Hector Corrada Bravo

entry.summary: This paper introduces Riemannian Wasserstein Entropic Flow Matching (RWEFM), a generative framework operating on the Wasserstein space of probability measures over a Riemannian manifold, targeting meta-distributions such as molecular conformational ensembles and single-cell data. It regresses a neural vector field onto Riemannian optimal transport velocities using McCann displacement interpolations as conditional paths, with theoretical validity guarantees. This extends flow matching to a genuinely non-Euclidean, measure-space setting relevant to scientific ML.

entry.title: FinFIRST: Benchmarking Search Agents for Financial Information Retrieval, Sourcing and Traceability

author.name: Wenqing Wang, Haitao Xiang, Xinyi Zhao, Mingming Yin, Ying Zhong, Zhaoxin Huan, Qiheng Zhou, Jin Zhu, Xiaolu Zhang, Shi Chang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: FinFIRST is the first financial benchmark to jointly evaluate LLM search-agent answers and their supporting evidence through atomic rubrics, with 123 expert-authored tasks covering temporally valid retrieval, authoritative sourcing, entity and period alignment, unit consistency, and traceability. It moves beyond final-answer-only evaluation to enable error localization in financial search agents.

entry.title: Authority-Preserving Evaluation of Medical Vision-Language Assistants

author.name: Flint Xiaofeng Fan, Cheston Tan, Yew-Soon Ong, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: AuthEval is a logging and evaluation framework that separates proposal quality from selected-action quality for medical VLM assistants, scoring decisions under declared local criteria and reporting an authority gap between what the model proposes and what the local service decides. This reframing acknowledges that human institutions retain final authority under referral policy and capacity constraints.

entry.title: Vision2CAD: A Visual Agent Harness for Explicit Geometry Referencing and Localization in Parametric CAD Modeling

author.name: Xi Cheng, Chenxi Zhai, Hang Cheng, Mingyu Fan, Pingfa Feng, Long Zeng

entry.summary: Vision2CAD pairs VLM reasoning with deterministic CAD kernel operations for parametric CAD generation, introducing an ID-based interface for explicit geometry selection, a local-coordinate bridge for sketch coordinates, and projected-edge localization for external constraints. These mechanisms address known failure points in selecting geometric references and establishing stable feature dependencies.

entry.title: CE$^4$L: Continual Ego, Exo, and Ego-Exo Learning

author.name: Hongwei Yan, Kanglei Zhou, Yuchen Liu, Qingyu Shi, Yi Zhong, Liyuan Wang

entry.summary: CE4L introduces a unified continual learning benchmark for embodied video perception spanning ego-centric, exo-centric, and joint ego-exo views across four tasks: cross-view referenced skill assessment, temporal action segmentation, cross-view association, and action anticipation and planning. It highlights challenges absent from prior continual learning benchmarks, including cross-view correspondence, view-dependent asynchrony, and heterogeneous semantic objectives.

entry.title: MotionJEPA: Preventing Temporal Feature Collapse by Capturing Visual Changes in Latent Space

author.name: Markus Karmann, Shile Li, Christian Intern\`o, Bruno Andreis, David Klindt, Randall Balestriero, Jindong Gu, Philip Torr, Qi Zhang, Peng-Tao Jiang, Hao Zhang, Bo Li, Onay Urfalioglu

entry.summary: MotionJEPA addresses temporal feature collapse in JEPA training, where a bias toward slow features suppresses dynamic representations, by introducing DISReg, a regularizer built on an inverse-dynamics-style module that predicts temporal difference image embeddings without pixel reconstruction. This encourages balanced static and dynamic feature learning for latent world models.

entry.title: ReSTI: A Source-Grounded Audit and Repair of STI-Bench

author.name: Pengzhan Sun, Ramanathan Rajaraman, Shiu-Hong Kao, Junbin Xiao, Angela Yao

entry.summary: The authors audit the STI-Bench spatial-temporal benchmark against its official ScanNet, Waymo, and Omni6DPose sources, uncovering systematic coordinate-system and timestamp errors, under-specified targets, and mismatched answer keys. ReSTI reconstructs every recoverable answer with explicit target, time, coordinate system, quantity, and unit, exposing task-level geometric failures in the original benchmark.

entry.title: MoSAT: Human Motion Generation from Spatial Audio and Textual Description

author.name: Shuyang Xu, Zhiyang Dou, Yiduo Hao, Zekun Li, Liang Pan, Jingbo Wang, Cheng Lin, Yuan Liu, Wenping Wang, Mingmin Zhao, Taku Komura

entry.summary: Defines the novel task of full-body human motion synthesis jointly conditioned on spatial audio and natural language, introducing STAM, a dataset of motion sequences paired with spatial audio and detailed text annotations, plus MoSAT, a latent flow-matching generation framework. Spatial audio conveys environmental cues while text specifies intent.

entry.title: CableVLA: Simulation-Privileged Global-Local Representation Learning for Cable Routing

author.name: Zhifei Teng, Bo Feng, Xiang Zou, Jinpeng Xiao, Min Li, Zhouping Yin, Yiqun Li

entry.summary: CableVLA is an end-to-end vision-language-action framework for cable routing that distills simulator-privileged topology and contact information into deployable representations, via a TopoHead for causal visual context and TacSense for learning contact dynamics from resistive tactile arrays. A contact gate activates force-tactile residuals that refine the next actions of a frozen action expert.

entry.title: X-Planner: Event-Structured Task Planning for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Howard Lu, Shalfun Li, Porter Pan, Cris, Lumen, Cyril, Eric Hu, Lily Li, Maeve Zhang, Robert Wang, KZ Zheng, Viggo Chen, Tim Ding, Regsis Cheng, YJ Xiao, Kian, Hai Lin, Alan Song, Elise Ma, Gody Li, Victor Yao, Yohann Tang, Ingrid Yu, Jason He, James Wang, Ryan Yu, Ping Yang, Chris Pan, Vincent Chen, Roy Gan, Hao Wang, Qian Wang

entry.summary: X-Planner is a planning front-end for VLA systems that makes intermediate embodied reasoning explicit through event-structured plans instead of token-by-token chain-of-thought. It contributes large-scale planning data from ego, UMI, and teleoperation sources with hierarchy granularity, takeover-time annotations, and human-designed failure supervision for error recognition.

entry.title: Ladders of Thought: A Self-Evolving Curriculum of Progressively Simplified Reasoning Traces

author.name: Minghui Liu, Thomas Magelinski, Dehao Yuan, Qi Yu, Furong Huang

entry.summary: Presents Ladders-of-Thought, which generates semantically faithful easier variants of reasoning problems, buckets them by difficulty, and uses a self-evolving bandit scheduler to allocate training, improving small (1-8B) model reasoning beyond knowledge distillation. Evaluated on math and multi-hop reasoning across multiple model families.

entry.title: VideoX-Qwen: Data-Centric Instruction-Based Video Editing

author.name: JJiahang Li, Dingbao Shao, Xinyu Chen, Song Wu, Jiang Lin, Duo Li, Yuhang Liu, Jiaxin Hu, Shengrong Gu, Ying Tai, Zili Yi

entry.summary: VideoX-Qwen presents an integrated data-construction and training framework for instruction-based video editing, with a scalable production pipeline combining generation and understanding models for addition, removal, replacement, and attribute editing, producing over 1.2 million directional instruction-video pairs. It adapts video-generation backbones to editing while preserving unrelated subjects, motion, and temporal continuity. The large paired dataset and integrated pipeline are the main contributions.

entry.title: EADC: Evaluation of Advanced and Deep-level Compliance in Large Language Models

author.name: Yan Zhang, Ruien Li, Yaoyao Peng, Wanxin Ren, Yijia Zhang, Wusheng Zhang, Guangwen Yang

entry.summary: EADC is a new evaluation framework for assessing whether LLMs comply with complex legal and regulatory frameworks, addressing gaps in static benchmarks such as ignoring AI-law requirements and missing implicit or covert compliance risks. It tracks risk propagation along logical dependency chains and evaluates compliance in contextualized real-world scenarios.

entry.title: SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving

author.name: Jennifer Williams, Dave Farris, Jeff Farris, Jiantao Jiao

entry.summary: SWE-Serve is a benchmark of 53 repository-grounded tasks derived from recent production changes for evaluating agents on inference-serving engineering, spanning model support, runtime execution, and public APIs. It fills a gap between repo-level SWE benchmarks that ignore inference and narrow kernel-optimization benchmarks.

entry.title: GroundedGEO: Auditing the Evidence Gap in Generative Search Rankings

author.name: Yihan Xia, Huiling Fan, Kangrong Zhong, Taotao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces an evidence-paired benchmark and GroundedGEO, a claim-level reranker that penalizes query-relevant claims lacking support in a supplied evidence packet, exposing an identifiability gap in text-only generative search ranking. This addresses manipulation of generative search rankings where publishers fabricate detailed-looking content cheaply.

entry.title: West-WRF AI 2-km: High-Resolution Prediction of Integrated Vapor Transport and Precipitation

author.name: Nazak Rouzegari, Vesta Afzali Gorooh, Agniv Sengupta, Phu Nguyen, Kuo-Lin Hsu, Amir AghaKouchak, Soroosh Sorooshian, F. Martin Ralph, Luca Delle Monache

entry.summary: Presents a stretched-grid AI weather model with 2-km resolution over the western United States, pretrained on 40 years of ERA5 and fine-tuned with regional 2-km reanalysis to produce 6-hourly precipitation and integrated vapor transport forecasts for atmospheric-river-driven orographic precipitation. Addresses a topographically challenging regional forecasting problem.

entry.title: IndustrialVLA-Bench: A Traceable Multi-Axis Evaluation of Open Robot Policy Models

author.name: Yiqi Wang, Zhifeng Rao, Jiaqi Zhang, Xiaoyang Li, Zhangkai Wu, Yiqun Duan, Mingkai Zheng, Fei Wang, Shan You, Taotao Cai

entry.summary: Presents an evidence-aware benchmark evaluating six open VLA and world-action models (WAMs) under a unified schema across clean capability on LIBERO, non-language robustness on LIBERO-Plus, language sensitivity, and deployment-cost trade-offs. Clarifies comparisons between two paradigms usually reported under incompatible protocols.

entry.title: EMGBlend: Heterogeneity-Aware Self-Supervised Pretraining for Gesture and Force Decoding

author.name: Yuwei Jia, Cheng Zhong, Jinyang Yu, Zhe Cui

entry.summary: EMGBlend is a self-supervised pretraining framework for surface EMG that handles dataset heterogeneity via geometry-aware attention over shared channel patches, band-limited spectral targets, and balanced source exposure. A 109M-parameter model pretrained on 11 public datasets is evaluated on gesture recognition, force regression, and contact classification.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Combinatorial Optimization with Constraints via Frank-Wolfe

author.name: Akbar Rafiey, Yifei Xu, Nikolaos Karalias

entry.summary: The paper proposes a general self-supervised framework for constrained combinatorial optimization in which neural networks predict arbitrary continuous vectors without projection into the feasible polytope, applying Frank-Wolfe machinery to incorporate the predictions into feasible solutions. This removes reliance on ad-hoc, problem-specific constraint constructions in prior continuous-extension approaches.

entry.title: MorphoSHAP: Rethinking the Unit of Attribution in Explanation for Deep Visual Models

author.name: Anirudh Prabhakaran, Alexandre Rocchi, Gianni Franchi

entry.summary: MorphoSHAP is a model-agnostic post-hoc attribution method that uses morphological shapes from the Tree of Shapes as players in a Shapley attribution game, describing each shape by scale, geometry, and signed contribution. This yields explanations of where evidence lies, what structure carries it, and how strongly it affects predictions, enabling class-level explanations beyond image-specific heatmaps.

entry.title: QuantWM: Temporally Consistent 2-Bit KV Cache Quantization for World Models and Video Generation

author.name: Jiaqi Zhao, Xiaobin Hu, Bo Yin, Junpeng Jiang, Miao Zhang, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: Proposes QuantWM, a 2-bit KV cache quantization method for video generation and world models that fixes severe temporal flickering left by prior near-lossless-on-benchmark 2-bit schemes. The key insight is that small Key perturbations shift attention logits and change selected temporal-spatial tokens, so quantization must explicitly account for this attention-selection sensitivity.

entry.title: Train Where the Quantized Model Goes: On-Policy Distillation for Low-Bit Reasoning

author.name: Yuanteng Chen, Zhilei Liu, Peisong Wang, Yuantian Shao, Chuangyi Li, Weining Wang, Shuang Qiu, Gang Li, Jing Liu, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: The paper identifies quantization-amplified exposure bias as the reason quantization-aware distillation fails to preserve long-form math and code reasoning at sub-3-bit precision, leading to repetitive loops. It introduces an on-policy distillation stage where the student generates through the quantized forward path and receives teacher supervision at the model's own trajectories.

entry.title: Entropy Can Flow, or It Can Guide. Be Entropy. LEDFlow: Introducing Entropy-guided Generation Order into Uniform Discrete Flow

author.name: Tung Sum Thomas Kwok, Yidong Ouyang, Yingjia Wan, Ying Nian Wu, Zhijiang Guo, Oscar Leong

entry.summary: The paper shows that uniform discrete flow models can corrupt correct intermediate predictions during repeated revision (9.4% of Sudoku cells flip from correct to incorrect) and introduces LEDFlow, a training-free sampler that adaptively fixes low-entropy predictions via selective absorption while preserving uniform-flow velocity at active positions. It also decomposes absorption error into joint-dependence and marginal components.

entry.title: Rewired or Gated? How Instruction Tuning Shapes Knowledge-Conflict Circuits in LLMs

author.name: Shubham Santosh Pandere, Gautam Ranka, Ritika Varshney, Navya Deshmukh, Roushni Sareen, Roshan Kumar Singh

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study compares base versus instruction-tuned models (Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen-2.5-3B, Gemma-3-4B) to determine how knowledge-conflict resolution circuits change under instruction tuning. Using five independent methods including node/edge attribution, causal ablation, and path patching, the authors converge on the finding that instruction tuning gates and reweights existing heads rather than rewiring new circuits, with high node overlap (0.60-0.82) in the same late layers. This sheds light on how prompt-vs-weights conflict behavior emerges during fine-tuning.

entry.title: Beyond Scalar Sensitivity: Activation-Aware Mixed-Precision LLM Quantization with Cross-Layer Refinement

author.name: Akihiro Yoshida, Yuma Ichikawa

entry.summary: The paper proves that scalar sensitivity proxies in mixed-precision LLM quantization suffer multiplicative distortion up to a product of Hessian condition numbers, ranging from 10^1 to 10^13 for typical LLM modules, making inter-module sensitivity ranking unreliable. It proposes Cross-layer Activation-aware mixed-precision quantization that moves beyond scalar proxies with cross-layer refinement. This is a theoretically grounded advance for efficient LLM deployment.

entry.title: JAMPR+/L2D: scalable neural heuristic for constrained vehicle routing problems in dynamic environment

author.name: Andrew Soroka, Alex Meshcheryakov

entry.summary: This paper adapts a deep reinforcement learning framework (JAMPR+/L2D) to constrained vehicle routing problems with capacity limits, time windows, and pickup-and-delivery requirements, specifically targeting settings where the graph distance matrix changes substantially. Experiments on medium-sized CVRP and VRPTW benchmarks show the learned model outperforms the state-of-the-art classical heuristic HGS in the majority of cases.

entry.title: One-Step Generative Surrogate Models via Block-Triangular Joint Drifting

author.name: Nicholas Geissler, Shreya Jha, Ricardo Baptista, Benjamin Peherstorfer

entry.summary: The paper introduces block-triangular joint drifting, a method for building one-step generative surrogates of stochastic transition models by applying a projected drift field to the empirically accessible joint distribution of consecutive states. The architecture preserves the current-state marginal while making the second component a direct one-step sampler of the conditional next-state distribution, addressing the lack of multiple realized next states in trajectory data.

entry.title: SSP-Bench: A Hybrid Data Generation Framework for Safety, Security, and Privacy Evaluation

author.name: Fatih Deniz, Yazan Boshmaf, Issa Khalil

entry.summary: SSP-Bench is a dynamic benchmarking framework that generates LLM safety, security, and privacy evaluation instances on demand, addressing score saturation, contamination, and rephrasing sensitivity in static benchmarks. It grounds labels in external sources, enforces scope via service-specific validation, and calibrates difficulty with a multi-model steering panel, formulating benchmark construction as a multi-objective problem. This enables more robust and contamination-resistant LLM safety evaluation.

entry.title: HABILIS Brain 0: Geometry-Change Supervision for Vision-Language-Action and Residual Flow Recovery

author.name: Jinu Pahk, Jesoon Kang, Taegeon Park, Jisu An, Soo Min Kimm, Jaejoon Kim, Byoung-Tak Zhang

entry.summary: GC-VLA trains vision-language-action policies to predict multiview geometry-change tokens between current and future observations, first learning a geometry-change VLM and then aligning a continuous ActionExpert, aiming for an embodiment-agnostic visual interface pretrainable on robot and egocentric video. This shifts geometric supervision from static scene structure to the dynamics of manipulation.

entry.title: PatchKV: Efficient KV Cache Recovery for Dynamically Edited LLM Contexts

author.name: Guotao Yang, Rui Guo, Siwei He, Sheng Chen, Yitao Hu, Keqiu Li

entry.summary: PatchKV addresses KV-cache invalidation in long-running LLM agent workflows where interior context spans are edited but long suffixes remain: it decomposes context versions into exact prefix, updated span, and aligned suffix, predicts an edit-local dirty region with an offline drift model, and augments that region with sparse nonlocal blocks from stored states. This avoids both full suffix recomputation and stale-state reuse.

entry.title: MoM: Memory of Memory

author.name: Bowen Qin, Yao Lu

entry.summary: MoM formalizes a missing combination in LLM agent memory design: committing the current value at write time while retaining what is displaced, so memory tracks not just content but the provenance, status, and history of its own entries. This avoids both the stale-value conflicts of retrieve-and-reconcile designs and the irrecoverable overwrites of conventional CRUD memories.

entry.title: Calibration as a First-Class Criterion in LLM Evaluation

author.name: Mario Sanz-Guerrero, Katharina von der Wense

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that calibration is widely ignored in LLM research despite being well-studied, creating risks both at deployment and inside research pipelines that rely on confidence (LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic data, active learning). Calls for calibration checks to become a standard part of model, dataset, and benchmark reporting.

entry.title: Performance vs Consistency: Evaluating a Foundation Model in Lung-RADS Screening

author.name: Benjamin Renoust, Pierre Baudot, Tiffany Foriel, Yousra Haddou, Charles Voyton, Pierre-Henri Siot, Ezequiel Geremia, Danny Francis, Jean-Christophe Brisset, Val\'erie Bourd\`es, Sylvain Bodard, Benoit Huet

entry.summary: This study evaluates MedGemma, a medical foundation model derived from Gemini, and its fine-tuned lung cancer variant against twelve radiologists performing Lung-RADS v2022 assessment on the NLST dataset in a multi-reader design. It quantifies inter-reader variability and examines whether model performance consistency matches radiologist standards in structured clinical interpretation.

entry.title: On The Robustness-Resolution Tradeoff In Temporal Quantization Of Event Streams

author.name: Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury, Ruhi Sharmin, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed

entry.summary: This work proves that hard temporal binning of event camera streams is discontinuous and establishes a lower bound of 2/Delta on L1 sensitivity for a class of continuous, mass-preserving temporal encoders, with two-bin interpolation achieving the limit. Experiments on SHD, N-MNIST, and DVS128 Gesture support the theoretical analysis.

entry.title: PanoSeg3R: Feed-Forward 3D Semantic Segmentation for Panoramic Images with an Automatic Data Curation Pipeline

author.name: Heechan Yoon, Dongki Jung, Phuc Nguyen, Ming Lin, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: PanoSeg3R performs feed-forward 3D panoramic semantic segmentation, jointly predicting geometry and multi-view semantics in one pass by extending a pretrained panoramic reconstruction backbone with a query-based mask decoder. An automatic data curation pipeline leveraging foundation models generates pseudo annotations, expanding training data and improving zero-shot generalization to state-of-the-art panorama segmentation performance.

entry.title: RewardVerse: Rubric-Guided Policy Optimization for Video Reward Modeling

author.name: Zhenchen Tang, Yang Li, Songlin Yang, Bo Peng, Xiaotong Zhao, Shuai Li, Haotian Fan, Alan Zhao, Jing Dong

entry.summary: RewardVerse introduces a rubric-based video reward framework for RL optimization of video generation models, inserting a dynamic rubric as an intermediate representation between evaluation query and scorer. This addresses scalar drift, where unconstrained scalar scoring collapses or shifts scales across prompts, making rewards unreliable for policy optimization.

entry.title: Algebraic Consistency Alone Does Not Certify Temporal Structure in Latent Action Models

author.name: Di Wen, Ruodi Zhang, Kailun Yang, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: The paper challenges a claimed label-free certificate in latent action model research, showing that additive composition and antisymmetric reversal properties of the transition code hold trivially for any frame pairing under reconstruction, and thus cannot demonstrate genuine temporal structure. Across five source domains, an unconstrained trained counterpart already achieves 83-97% of the reported error reduction, indicating the metric conflates encoding of nuisance state or coordinate conventions with temporal understanding.

entry.title: OnlineWM: Causality-Aware Active Online Learning for Effective World Modeling

author.name: Yikun Miao, Fangqi Zhu, Quanxin Shou, Xiaoyi Pang, Zhengyang Yan, Junhao Li, Haodong Wang, Zicong Hong, Song Guo

entry.summary: OnlineWM improves generative world models by addressing two failure modes: distribution misalignment from static offline data collection, and spurious correlations encouraged by purely observational discrepancy objectives. It introduces a causality-aware active online learning pipeline that targets unreliable long-tail dynamics and encourages capturing true action-effect causality.

entry.title: Look Where It Counts: A Free, Label-Free Visual Evidence Signal for Fine-Grained Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Santi Ram Tiwari, Nihal Naik, Devbrat Pandey, Nishant Sinha

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the contrastive evidence gap: the per-token log-likelihood ratio a multimodal model assigns to its output when conditioned on a question-relevant versus irrelevant image region, showing this label-free signal can substitute for expensive SFT, RLVR, or distillation on fine-grained visual questions. It studies the signal across Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B, and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B on V*Bench, where high-resolution evidence is lost to downsampling.

entry.title: Preoperative Prediction of Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma by Integrating Multimodal Ultrasound and Clinical Data: A Multicenter Study

author.name: Jun Cheng, Yuanyuan Kong, Qing Huang, Xiaotong Tan, Licong Dong, Yulong Han, Wufeng Xue, Ruobing Huang, Dong Ni, Qi Yang, Jie Yu, Ping Liang

entry.summary: This multicenter clinical study develops and validates a model predicting microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma preoperatively by fusing B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler, contrast-enhanced ultrasound, and clinical data from 489 patients across eight centers with independent external validation. MVI currently requires postoperative histopathology, so reliable preoperative prediction could directly affect surgical planning and prognosis. Rigorous design with external validation strengthens clinical credibility.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Subspaces: Spectrum-Aware and Depth-Adaptive Fusion for Multi-Task Model Merging

author.name: Ruxi Gu, Zilei Wang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: SADA-Merging improves data-free multi-task model merging by accounting for task-specific subspace capacity, spectral transformation tolerance, and depth-dependent distortion introduced by subspace projection. The framework allocates subspace capacity by spectral complexity and adapts spectral preservation across layers, addressing a uniform-treatment limitation of prior subspace methods.

entry.title: ZVeC: A Zero-Shot Framework for Instance-Level Vehicle Extraction and Generative Point Cloud Completion

author.name: Daisy Li, Kyle Gao, Quanyun Wu, Boris Jutzi, John S. Zelek, Jonathan Li

entry.summary: ZVeC reformulates LiDAR scene-level point cloud completion as compositional object-level reconstruction, decomposing cluttered underground scenes into vehicle instances completed independently via a depth- and 3D Gaussian-conditioned diffusion model. The zero-shot design removes the need for scenario-specific supervised training, addressing severe geometric incompleteness from occlusions.

entry.title: GameHorizon Suite: Multi-Horizon Data and Evaluation in Gameplay

author.name: Yiran Wang, Xingyilang Yin, Junfu Pu, Guangzhi Wang, Kaifeng Li, Mingyu Ouyang, Huiqiang Sun, Lingen Li, Cheng Cheng, Wangbo Yu, Honghao Chen, Xiaodong Cun, Chi-Man Pun, Zhiguo Cao, Ying Shan

entry.summary: GameHorizon is a unified data and evaluation suite measuring gameplay AI capabilities across temporal horizons, comprising an automated multi-horizon instruction annotation pipeline, a constructed dataset, and evaluation covering visual understanding, instruction decomposition, planning, and action control. It addresses narrow game coverage, missing language instructions, and high-variance online rollouts in prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Omni2Web: Benchmarking Audiovisual Website Development

author.name: Minghao Han, Zhenghao Xing, Xize Cheng, Yuxuan Wang, Junming Lin, Ling Wang, Yinsong Yan, Yunfei Chu, Qize Yang, Jin Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Omni2Web, a bilingual benchmark of 918 instances and 13,907 edit steps for webpage editing from screen-recorded requests containing weak deictic expressions, with three tracks covering direct editing, instruction recovery, and instruction utility. Evaluating 17 open- and closed-source models reveals best Edit Fidelity scores around 51, indicating substantial headroom.

entry.title: Unsupervised Brain Anomaly Detection as a Bayesian Inverse Problem with Diffusion Prior

author.name: Hugues Roy, Reuben Dorent, Ninon Burgos

entry.summary: The paper reformulates unsupervised brain anomaly detection as a Bayesian inverse problem under a diffusion prior, introducing a latent spatial anomaly mask that models consistency between a test image and a pseudo-healthy reconstruction. This replaces the heuristic noise schedules and synthetic corruptions used in prior diffusion-based UAD methods with a principled probabilistic formulation. A theoretically cleaner approach to annotation-free medical anomaly localization.

entry.title: REDACT: Robust Perceptive Locomotion under Unseen Visual Corruption

author.name: Natapat Kirdwichai, Tobias Driskell-Poole, Andrei Sontea, Jadu Dash, Muhammad Burhan Hafez, Danesh Tarapore

entry.summary: REDACT is a teacher-student framework for depth-conditioned quadruped/legged locomotion that remains stable under visual corruptions unseen during training. It combines an improved visual encoder, persistent feature masking, and a consensus-gating algorithm to retain evidence despite occlusion, noise, and invalid depth returns.

entry.title: Contact-Stable Deformable Tissue Simulation Using Implicit Integration and Live-Pose Grasp Constraints for Laparoscopic Surgery Robot Policy Evaluation

author.name: Juahn Oh, Dongho Yee, Jinseok Lee, Jiyul Lee, Yechan Seo, Seong Jeong, Minsung Kim, Seonho Shim, Younghoon Noh, Hyuk Choi, Youngbin Kong, Hyoun-Joong Kon

entry.summary: A surgical simulation pipeline reconstructs deformable tissue from fixed-view RGB-D recordings of the surgical field, composites out instruments, and produces stable tetrahedralized volumes (13 organs, ~146k tetrahedra, no inverted elements) placed in a bimanual cell with two Franka FR3 arms operating through trocars. Core contributions are the implicit integration and live-pose grasp constraint design enabling stable grasping and lifting.

entry.title: Sample, Simulate, Select: Physics-in-the-Loop Text-to-Motion for Humanoids Without Training

author.name: Raphael Memmesheimer, Sven Behnke

entry.summary: S3 measures how much of the gap between text-to-motion models and humanoid robots can be closed with no training: it draws N candidate motions per prompt from a frozen text-to-motion model, retargets each to a Unitree G1 via inverse kinematics, rolls them out in simulation with a pretrained tracking policy, and selects the best-executed candidate. Putting the deployment controller in the loop as the verifier enables zero-training language-to-humanoid motion.

entry.title: Auditing Proxy-Based Validation Across Text Spans

author.name: Daein Weon, Dong Ho Kang

entry.summary: This paper exposes a subtle flaw in how evaluation metrics are validated against cheap proxy labels: when the score and proxy are computed over the same text span, agreement can reflect shared surface evidence rather than the intended semantic construct. The authors formalize a validation contract and re-evaluate proxies strictly outside the scored span, showing in a controlled HotpotQA experiment that score-proxy agreement far exceeds score-correctness agreement (+0.184 gap) when spans overlap, collapsing to +0.045 from 120 characters onward. This has broad implications for how LLM evaluation pipelines are trusted.

entry.title: Conditional Tensor Diffusion: Distributional Counterfactual Learning and Inference

author.name: Xinbing Kong, Zeyu Li, Junfan Mao, Bin Wu

entry.summary: The paper develops CFTDiff, a conditional diffusion model with masked Tucker structure for counterfactual distribution recovery in high-dimensional panel/tensor causal settings. By preserving dependence across tensor modes and reducing nonlinear score learning from the product of mode dimensions to the product of Tucker ranks, it derives high-probability error bounds for distributional treatment-effect estimation.

entry.title: Understanding Reliability in LLM-based Human Behavior Simulation

author.name: Pei Wang, Lei Wang, Yuanzi Li, Xu Chen

entry.summary: ReliMap decomposes LLM-based human behavior simulation into three structured layers and evaluates reliability at individual and population levels across model capacity, profile completeness, and population coverage, tested on four tasks and eleven LLMs. The study finds that all models exhibit substantial distributional problems, clarifying how configuration choices interact to determine simulation trustworthiness.

entry.title: Cognitive Action Reasoning for Proactive Robots from Human-Centered Multimodal Observations

author.name: Zhihao Gu, Kechao Zhu, Yuanfeng Wu, Mohan Liu, Ankit Kumar Shaw, ChenDong Hong, Xuanyu Chen, Dengchen Mei, Xu Tianyi, Lin Wang

entry.summary: Formulates ProRobo, an upstream cognitive decision problem where robots must proactively decide what action to take from multimodal human and environmental cues without explicit instructions. Introduces ProAction, a resource of human-centered multimodal observations supporting this underexplored setting of proactive embodied assistance.

entry.title: Beyond End-Task Success: How to Audit Visual Experience Retrieval in Robotics

author.name: Eshika Pathak, Leela Krishna

entry.summary: This paper argues that end-task success rates mislead evaluations of robot experience-reuse systems, since a retrieval rule can score well by exploiting one broadly transferable experience or poorly because its preferred experience is weak.
