entry.title: How to Estimate Whether You Have Found Several Needles in a Haystack: Measuring Calibration in Multi-Label Text Classification

author.name: Sophie Henning, Georg Hofmann, Alexander Schulte, Alexander Fraser, Annemarie Friedrich

entry.summary: Shows that existing binning schemes for label-wise expected calibration error are unreliable on multi-label tasks dominated by negatives, either underestimating error or reflecting label frequency. Proposes improved calibration measurement for trustworthy label-wise confidence estimation in tasks like medical coding.

entry.title: DOA-SORT: Directional Occlusion-Aware Multi-Object Tracking with Distributional Observations

author.name: Hao Wang

entry.summary: DOA-SORT is an online, training-free multi-object tracker that models occlusion directionally rather than as a scalar penalty, inferring soft front-back ordering, estimating directional occlusion coverage and depth, and constructing a mixture of clean and four directional occlusion distributions. This explicitly captures how left, right, top, and bottom occlusions distort detections differently.

entry.title: An Evolutionary Agentic Approach for Open-ended Image Quality Perception

author.name: Zhenchen Tang, Bo Peng, Zichuan Wang, Songlin Yang, Leilei Cao, Fengjie Zhu, Jing Dong

entry.summary: PACE is a training-free multi-agent framework that formulates open-ended image quality assessment as explicit protocol construction, using collaborative agents to evolve scoring protocols for novel perceptual dimensions like physical plausibility and text-rendering correctness. It identifies holistic bias, where models reuse generic quality priors on unseen dimensions, causing rank inversion.

entry.title: UltraTex: Unleashing 2K Multi-View Diffusion for 3D Texturing

author.name: Yibo Zhang, Ze Yuan, Nan Cao, Li Zhang, Yan-Pei Cao, Yuan-Chen Guo, Rui Ma

entry.summary: UltraTex is an efficient framework for high-resolution (2048) multi-view diffusion-based 3D texturing, overcoming the prohibitive cost of unified multi-view sequences exceeding 212K tokens. It exploits the observation that object-centric multi-view renderings contain distinct structural properties to preserve high-frequency details from reference images in production-quality 3D assets.

entry.title: An Efficient and Effective Watermarking Scheme for the Protection of the Intellectual Property Rights of Video Generative Models

author.name: Wenhong Huang, Jianwei Fei, Benedetta Tondi, Bin Ma, Fangjun Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes an in-generation watermarking scheme for video generative models addressing two forensic tasks: verifying whether a video came from a protected model and verifying whether a suspect model is an unauthorized copy. It presents VidMark, a watermarking network using two-scale discrete wavelet transform decomposition and global modeling for robust, efficient embedding in generated videos.

entry.title: All-in-One Multilingual Scene Text Recognition with Script-aware Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Xingsong Ye, Yongkun Du, Jiaxin Zhang, Zhixian Li, Chong Sun, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Lianwen Jin, Zhineng Chen

entry.summary: This work builds an all-in-one multilingual scene text recognizer positioned between costly per-language experts and expensive VLMs, introducing TextMuSS-10M, a large-scale synthetic dataset spanning 10 scripts and 229 languages, plus a script-aware mixture-of-experts architecture. The goal is a single model that is simpler, lighter, and more accurate than existing alternatives across low-resource scripts.

entry.title: Dissecting Agentic Forensics: The Role of Triage, Prompting, and Evidence Arbitration in Open-World Fake Image Detection

author.name: Xianlong Li (IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca, Italy), Pietro Bongini (University of Siena, Italy), Niccol\'o Pancino (University of Siena, Italy), Marco Blanchini (IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca, Italy), Benedetta Tondi (University of Siena, Italy), Mauro Barni (University of Siena, Italy)

entry.summary: This paper empirically dissects which components of training-free agentic image forensics systems drive performance, studying specialist detectors, per-detector triage, and conflict-aware evidence arbitration across six configurations. It questions whether agentic benefits persist under distribution shift, an important robustness check for an emerging paradigm. The work matters for understanding how to detect diverse manipulations from synthesis to splicing in an open-world setting.

entry.title: INTCORT: Training-Free Spatial Reasoning Enhancement for Vision-Language Models via Input Transformations and Confidence Routing

author.name: Haoran Sun, Jingqi Xu, Yanhui Li, Enci Liu, Kaidi Xu, Yanwei Liu

entry.summary: INTCORT is a training-free framework that improves VLM spatial reasoning by verifying two hypotheses (geometric image transformations and query-reversal can recover wrong predictions; correct predictions show higher relation-token confidence), then routing among multiple transformed inputs via confidence. It avoids catastrophic forgetting and internal interference that plague training-based or other training-free methods.

entry.title: Correlation-Guided Flow Matching with Annealed Masking for Spatial Transcriptomics Generation

author.name: Yupei Zhang, Hao Chen, Li Pan, Chao Li, Xiaohan Xing

entry.summary: The paper generates spatial transcriptomics gene expression from histology images using flow matching with correlation-guided modeling of gene-gene interactions and annealed masking, arguing that preserving co-expression patterns shared across pathways is essential for biologically meaningful predictions. This departs from treating genes as independent targets.

entry.title: If You Hear It, Help Find It: Orthogonal Knowledge Distillation for Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization

author.name: Yi Xu, Cheng Chen, Wenzhuo Lei

entry.summary: Formulates open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization as a supervision placement problem, determining which teacher signals should shape the localization decision and which should remain auxiliary, based on observed differences in temporal-boundary reliability between audio and visual teachers. Proposes OV-OrthKD, a reliability-aware asymmetric orthogonal knowledge distillation method.

entry.title: History-Conditioned Flow Matching for Probabilistic Dynamics of Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots

author.name: Hang Yang, Tingcong Liu, Junjie Xiong, Fangju Yang, Ke Wu

entry.summary: The paper develops a history-conditioned, physics-informed flow-matching framework that predicts probability distributions of next joint configurations for tendon-driven continuum robots, where deterministic dynamics fail due to friction, transmission, and contact uncertainties. Recursive sampling yields distributions of future whole-body motions under prescribed commands.

entry.title: Benchmarking Robots for Everyday Environments: From Lab Experiments to Real-World Operations

author.name: Raphael Memmesheimer, Martina Overbeck, Dominik Beyer, Bj\"orn Kral, Sabine Bellmann, Sven Schneider, Jan Zimmermann, Anna-Maria Meer, Medina Klicic, Simone Roth, Carolin Stra{\ss}mann, Alexander Arntz, Marlene Wessels, Johannes Kraus, Paul Schweidler, Tristan Schnell, Christoph Zimmermann, Benedikt Pulver, Wilhelm Stork, Martin Gersch, Sven Behnke, Arne R\"onnau

entry.summary: This interdisciplinary study introduces a framework for benchmarking robots deployed in public environments, evaluating three robots across park cleaning, underpass cleaning, and library assistance over a three-year effort with seven benchmarking events and six on-site evaluations. It assesses not only technical performance but broader deployment implications in unstructured human environments, bridging lab metrics and real-world operations.

entry.title: MATES: Learning Multi-Agent Interactions by Transforming Observations for Frozen Single-Agent Policies

author.name: Elie Abboud, Oren Gal

entry.summary: MATES is an input-side adaptation framework for multi-agent reinforcement learning that trains a small observation-adapter to map multi-agent observations into the format expected by a frozen single-agent policy. This avoids training decentralized policies from scratch, exploiting the fact that many multi-agent tasks have learnable single-agent counterparts.

entry.title: 4DGS-JEPA: Temporally Compositional Joint-Embedding Prediction for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yongchao Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes 4DGS-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture over dynamic Gaussian splatting scenes for causal multi-horizon prediction of evolving 3D environments. It uses hierarchical scene, motion-group, and Gaussian-level representations with a horizon-conditioned transition operator enforcing temporal composition, supporting both direct prediction and recursive rollout.

entry.title: ArticleMiner: Ontology-Guided Knowledge Graph Construction from Scientific Publications

author.name: Md Abrar Jahin, Craig A. Knoblock, Jay Pujara

entry.summary: Presents ArticleMiner, a system that extracts quantitative scientific facts from papers and supplementary files by gathering evidence from multiple parsers and a language model, reconciling it and mapping to ontologies rather than merely recovering table structure. Addresses the gap between clean-table semantic interpretation and publication-level extraction.

entry.title: LatentPort: Beyond KV Cache - Cross-Model Transfer of Recurrent Memory in Hybrid Language Models: A 4B-to-9B Hybrid-State Handoff Without Target Prefix Replay

author.name: Simon P. Villani

entry.summary: Demonstrates the first cross-model handoff of persistent recurrent inference state between differently sized hybrid language models (a Qwen3.5 4B-to-9B pair) without the receiver rereading the context. Transferring the Gated DeltaNet persistent-state package alongside attention KV lowers teacher-forced negative log-likelihood by 0.747 nats/token across all 64 PG19 test documents.

entry.title: Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems

author.name: Sanjay Surendranath Girija, Aniruddh Nath, Li Wei, Yanhao Jiang, Shawn Andrews, Lukasz Heldt, Yi Wu, Aditya Mahajan, Mohit Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces the Light Heads framework for dynamically injecting new prediction tasks into existing multi-task ranking models in production recommenders, avoiding costly backbone retraining and cold-starting during continuous online learning. Aimed at accelerating experimentation velocity at industrial scale.

entry.title: RootQuantV2: Adapting a Vision Foundation Model for Root-Trait Regression from Minirhizotron Imagery

author.name: Kinjalk Parth, Sebastian Varela, Andrew D. B. Leakey

entry.summary: RootQuantV2 adapts a vision foundation model to regress root traits (length, surface area) directly from minirhizotron field images, bypassing the need for scarce, proprietary, manually traced annotations. This enables high-throughput below-ground crop phenotyping, a long-standing bottleneck in plant science.

entry.title: TSS: Target-Side Sparsification for Speculative Decoding in Domain-Specific Large Language Models

author.name: Haibo Hu, Lianming Huang, Qiao Li, Nan Guan, Chun Jason Xue

entry.summary: TSS challenges the assumption that the target model in speculative decoding must remain dense: the authors show that in domain-specific inference, skipping selected target layers can reduce verification cost while increasing draft acceptance and preserving or improving task performance. They propose an acceptance- and metric-aware breadth search over multi-layer sparsification configurations. This shifts optimization attention from the draft side to the target side of speculative decoding.

entry.title: MAVP: Map-Aware Visuomotor Policies for Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Jinhe Tang, Ruixiao Dai, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: Presents MAVP, a framework for mobile manipulation that predicts explicit base-pose targets and tracks them with localization feedback, reconstructing a static map from teleoperated demonstrations to give consistent spatial supervision. This improves execution reliability where demonstration-trained policies otherwise produce spatial misalignment and manipulation failures.

entry.title: Neural Approximation by Function Composition: Rigidity and Doubly Exponential Convergence

author.name: Wentao Huang, Haizhang Zhang

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies a core mechanism of deep network approximation power: geometrically weighted sums of iterates of a single scalar generator function, underlying tent-map and Yarotsky-style constructions. It establishes a rigidity theorem showing that continuous piecewise linear generators with finitely many segments can only represent at most quadratic C^3 functions in this way, while non-affine quadratic generators achieve doubly exponential convergence. These are fundamental results about what composition itself contributes to approximation.

entry.title: Statistical Rates for Entropic Optimal Transport in the Discrete to SubGaussian Regime

author.name: Tomas Gonzalez, Gonzalo Mena

entry.summary: This work establishes parametric convergence rates for empirical dual potentials in entropic optimal transport when one measure is finitely supported and the other is sub-Gaussian, with no dimension dependence in the leading term. As a consequence, the empirical barycentric projection achieves a fast squared-error rate of n^-1, improving on previously known rates.

entry.title: SpecialEduBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Knowledge, Skill, and Attitude in Language Intervention for Autistic Children

author.name: Jihoi Na, Taeyeong Kim, Sungjune Kong, Jaemin Jung, Min Joung Park, Kyungtae Joo, Ahhyun Kim, Shim Jaechang, Sooyoung Joo, Dongjin Ka, SeJoong Kim, Jimin Kim, HyunJin Jung, Unggi Lee

entry.summary: SpecialEduBench benchmarks vision-language models on language intervention for autistic children, emphasizing situated skills and attitudes rather than static knowledge, and requiring visual evidence such as wait time and gaze that transcripts miss. Because good teaching depends on the child's just-observed behavior, the benchmark uses paired contextualized judgments rather than a fixed answer key. It opens a new, socially significant evaluation area for VLMs.

entry.title: MarsRecon: Self-Supervised and Multimodal Surface Representations for Mars

author.name: Akshay Naik, Marius F. R. Juston, Jay Mahajan

entry.summary: MarsRecon is a geospatially aware pipeline that trains a masked autoencoder on unlabeled HiRISE imagery of Olympus Mons, then aligns the frozen visual encoder with observation text, coordinates, and local-global context. Improving resolution and token filtering reduced held-out reconstruction loss from 0.1751 to 0.1342.

entry.title: Planning and Rendering in Concert: DeepFusion of Autoregressive Layouts and Diffusion for Visual Text Generation

author.name: Guanqiao Chen, Jingru Tan, Dongxing Mao, Catherine Chen, Zijian Du, Libo Qin, Hu Jian Guo, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: DuetGen is an autonomous visual text generator that jointly learns autoregressive layout planning and diffusion rendering via DeepFusion, conditioning a diffusion transformer on the planner's prompt and bounding-box representations. It addresses the limitation of prior AR-diffusion systems that optimize planning and rendering separately, preventing joint adaptation.

entry.title: Modeling Clinical Workflow for SYNTAX Scoring from Coronary Angiography Videos

author.name: Suzhong Fu, Jingqi Dong, Xuan Ding, Rui Sun, Yiming Yang, Shuguang Cui, Zhen Li

entry.summary: This work reformulates automated SYNTAX scoring for coronary artery disease as a vessel segment identity-preserving anatomical reasoning problem rather than direct video-to-score regression. The hierarchical framework maintains vessel segment identity across frames and views, estimates stenosis severity at the segment level, and aggregates evidence according to coronary anatomy, while addressing data scarcity.

entry.title: LegendBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Legend Understanding with Counterfactual Interventions

author.name: Xinnuo Zhang, Zhike Tang, Jing Xu, Haoyuan Zhao, Weikai Yang

entry.summary: LegendBench is a parametric benchmark and generation pipeline producing targeted legend-centric test cases for chart understanding, with a capability-task taxonomy spanning legend parsing, grounding, conditioned reasoning, and abstention. It uses counterfactual interventions to isolate legend-specific errors that aggregate accuracy conflates with other reasoning failures.

entry.title: Topographic Training Concentrates Causal Circuits Without Improving Neuron Monosemanticity

author.name: Gautam Ranka, Shubham Santosh Pandere, Aiden Dsouza

entry.summary: The paper tests whether a spatial-locality training loss (TopoLoss) improves interpretability of vision transformers, measuring causal sufficiency of topographic clusters via activation patching and feature geometry via sparse autoencoders on ImageNet-100. The headline finding is that topographic training concentrates causal circuits without improving neuron monosemanticity. This offers a nuanced picture of how training-time priors interact with mechanistic interpretability tools.

entry.title: Ev-YOLO: Uncertainty-Aware Object Detection via a Unified Evidential Formulation

author.name: Simon Barbarit-Gaboriau (LITIS - STI, INSA Rouen Normandie), Hind Laghmara (LITIS - STI), R\'emi Boutteau (LITIS - STI), Samia Ainouz (LITIS, LITIS - STI)

entry.summary: Ev-YOLO reformulates both classification and bounding-box regression of YOLOv8 within a single evidential deep learning framework, unifying uncertainty estimation under subjective logic rather than mixing evidential classification with ad-hoc regression uncertainty models. It leverages YOLOv8's distribution-based box representation for a principled uncertainty-aware detector.

entry.title: Active Spatial Inspection for Effective and Efficient Embodied Exploration

author.name: Wenbin Wang, Xiang Bai, Yizhao Wang, Hang Sun, Dong Ren, Jie Qin, Qingquan Li, Bing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes the ACE framework for embodied exploration that replaces coarse, indirect cue-based guidance with a spatially explicit decision paradigm, coupling evidence-grounded perception with exposure-informed movement. This helps agents judge whether cues are sufficient, avoiding premature termination or excessive continuation.

entry.title: Not All Task Vectors Need Equal Rank: Energy-Proportional Allocation for Model Merging

author.name: Hyunjoong Cho, Jinhyeok Jang

entry.summary: SERA addresses spectral model merging methods that assign identical rank capacity to every task vector, proposing instead to allocate ranks proportionally to each task vector's singular-value energy structure. Tasks with richer spectral complexity receive more capacity in the shared merging space. A simple, well-motivated improvement over uniform-rank spectral merging for combining fine-tuned models without joint training.

entry.title: Recording Hand-Held Laparoscopic Instrument Motion in the Operating Room: Magnetometer-Free Fusion of Inertial, Range and Visual Sensing

author.name: Jiyul Lee, Dongho Yee, Juahn Oh, Jinseok Lee, Yechan Seo, Seong Jeong, Minsung Kim, Seonho Shim, Younghoon Noh, Hyuk Choi, Youngbin Kong, Hyoun-Joong Kong

entry.summary: The authors present a clip-on instrument-state logger that fuses a six-axis IMU, time-of-flight rangefinder, and markerless camera in an error-state Kalman filter to recover hand-held laparoscopic instrument motion in the OR, avoiding unreliable magnetometer readings. This preserves the surgical skill signal normally lost when only endoscopic video is retained.

entry.title: PLAT: Sparse Timed Keyframe Motion Tracking for Humanoid Control via Privileged Latent Transition Learning

author.name: Zepeng Wang, Jiangxing Wang, Chao Ma, Xiaochuan Shi, Zongqing Lu

entry.summary: PLAT addresses sparse timed keyframe motion tracking for humanoids, where the policy receives only sparse future keyframes with arrival times instead of dense frame-by-frame references. A three-stage framework uses dense motion tracking as privileged supervision during training via latent transition learning, then requires only sparse goals at deployment. This bridges dense motion tracking and sparse goal-conditioned control, making humanoid policies usable as high-level motion controllers for planning and generation.

entry.title: Shaft-Configuration-Adaptive Catheter Tip Position Estimation via Motor-History Conditioned Residual Learning

author.name: Peihan Zhang, Michael C. Yip, Ankur Kapoor, Young-Ho Kim

entry.summary: The paper presents a motor-history-conditioned GRU residual estimator for 3D catheter tip position in tendon-driven continuum robots, handling unknown shaft configurations, friction, slack, and hysteresis without direct shaft-configuration sensing. A multidirectional sweep calibrates a geometric model backbone while encoding motor-angle and torque responses into configuration estimates.

entry.title: Autonomous Evidence Factories: Safe and Useful Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Adam Chlipala

entry.summary: Adam Chlipala proposes an oracle-AI variant for safe recursive self-improvement: constrain the AI's reward function and world model to mathematically precise semantics so its only external effect is producing formally verified solutions to well-specified problems, with no representation of humans as goal-relevant objects. The design aims to harvest intelligence-exploding capability gains while forgoing real-world agency.

entry.title: Efficient Iterative Retrieval with Heterogeneous Batching

author.name: Dohyun Park, Hubertus Franke, Daniel G. Waddington, Swaminathan Sundararaman, Yongjoo Park

entry.summary: Orthrus is a serving system that unifies embedding and generative workloads in a single heterogeneous batching loop to improve throughput and GPU utilization for iterative retrieval systems. It tackles computational bubbles from coarse GPU partitioning using chunked embedding with dynamic batch composition.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Quantum Error Mitigation

author.name: Seyed Mohamad Ali Tousi, G. N. DeSouza

entry.summary: Proposes weakly supervised quantum error mitigation that replaces exponentially costly ideal-output labels with sixteen cheap heuristic labeling functions (stabilizer constraints, calibration data, circuit structure) reconciled via a probabilistic label model. This targets the regime where supervised mitigation is unavailable because noiseless simulation is infeasible.

entry.title: Prediction Is Not Detection: Evaluating Pre-Recognition Claims in Longitudinal Clinical AI

author.name: Jing Yang, Long R. Jiao, Xiujun Cai, Zongjiu Zhang

entry.summary: The authors argue that longitudinal clinical AI evaluations often conflate recognition-mediated care-process signals with genuine pre-recognition early detection, inflating apparent lead time and performance. They define an interval-censored pre-recognition transition, an independent as-of reference standard, and a prespecified recognition proxy to make early-detection claims testable. This is an important methodological correction for clinical AI evaluation broadly.

entry.title: The Architect, the Adversary, and the Judge: Closed-Loop Generation of Standards-Aligned Assessment Items at Scale

author.name: Wenhui Chen, Ziyao Lin, Jianlin Chen, Peiji Long, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: CLAIM is a production pipeline for K-12 assessment-item generation using a generate-then-attack protocol, bidirectional few-shot conditioning on accepted and rejected items with evaluator diagnoses, and a 44,844-rule mined knowledge dictionary. Across 43,227 scored items over 755 Common Core ELA standards and ten LLMs, it achieves a 97.8% expert pass rate on a 9,074-item production run, and the paper critically examines what that rate certifies. The scale, closed-loop design, and self-critical evaluation make it a strong applied contribution.

entry.title: Toward User-Mediated Self-Repair in Ubiquitous Robots Through Goal-Oriented Agentic AI

author.name: Morten Roed Frederiksen

entry.summary: This paper presents a goal-oriented agentic AI architecture that lets non-expert users repair ubiquitous robots through natural language dialogue, decoupling high-level planning from reactive conversation. A 20-participant study on a physical hardware testbed achieved a 95% task completion rate with positive reported self-efficacy.

entry.title: FISSION: Label Augmentation for Bot Detection

author.name: Sen Yang, Ignacy Nieweglowski, Aviv Yaish

entry.summary: This paper addresses the scarcity of reliable ground-truth labels for detecting bot accounts and coordinated influence operations, which are typically discovered through heuristics. FISSION generates augmented training labels by splitting each account's activity into positively labeled sub-accounts, then trains embedding models that group bots and accounts from the same coordinated operation. The method outperforms prior approaches on Wikipedia sockpuppet and Twitter/X bot detection benchmarks.

entry.title: Type-Safe Is Not Error-Free: A Constrained Decision Head Follows the Option Name, Not the Rubric Bound to It

author.name: Yu Sun, Junhao Xu

entry.summary: The paper studies typed decision models including Jev and two open-weight Jev-like models, showing that when option-name-to-rubric assignments are permuted while rubrics and option sets stay fixed, models follow the option name rather than the textual rubric that defines it. On 1,200 workflow decisions, schema conformance does not guarantee intended semantic interpretation.

entry.title: Not All 4-bit Quantizers Are Equal: Deployment-Time Mitigation of PII Leakage in Fine-Tuned Small Language Models

author.name: Cristhian Kapelinski, Diego Kreutz

entry.summary: Shows that 4-bit quantization method choice affects privacy leakage of fine-tuned small language models: calibration-based methods (AWQ, GPTQ) reproduced no planted records while calibration-free GGUF Q4_K_M leaked 5.3%. The paper traces the difference to calibration corpus use rather than bit width, across five open 0.5-7B models.

entry.title: Impact Is Not Invalidation: Ask About the Claim, Not the Diff

author.name: Atul Anand

entry.summary: Examines how coding-agent memory systems should invalidate stored claims when repositories change, showing that semantic-equivalence classification of diffs is a poor signal: five models spanning a 40x price range fire on 59-72% of real commits with precisions near the 0.25 base rate. Reframing the question to whether a specific stored claim still holds raises precision dramatically (0.705-0.974), a framing effect rather than a capability limit.

entry.title: Multi-Term Fourier Graph Neural Network with Sample Relationship Learning for Enhanced Remaining Useful Life Prediction

author.name: Ya Song, Laurens Bliek, Yaoxin Wu, Yingqian Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a Fourier-enhanced spatio-temporal graph neural network for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction that learns graph structure automatically and removes the fixed lookback-window restriction of prior ST-GNNs, capturing both short- and long-term temporal dependencies. This matters for predictive maintenance in industrial settings where hand-designed graph structures and fixed windows limit applicability.

entry.title: Beyond Class Marginals: Bounding Rehearsal Gaps without Freezing Class Co-occurrence

author.name: Congren Dai, Nat Roongjirarat, Fei Ye

entry.summary: The paper separates the rehearsal gap (interval between replay appearances of a class) from class marginals and co-occurrence in continual learning, introducing randomized-pass replay (RPR), which visits each resident class once per shuffled pass. RPR preserves balanced time-averaged class marginals, bounds every gap by 2*ceil(C/b)-1, and requires no future class information, extra examples, or extra forward passes.

entry.title: Syndrome, Synergy, and Safety: Structured Reasoning and Knowledge-Driven Alignment for TCM Prescription Generation

author.name: Zheng Chen, ZhiCheng Du, Haoxuan Li, Peiwu Qin

entry.summary: This paper identifies three clinical gaps when applying large language models to Traditional Chinese Medicine prescription generation: lack of auditable reasoning under the li-fa-fang-yao paradigm, no longitudinal adjustment across patient encounters, and failure to enforce absolute contraindication rules such as Shi Ba Fan. The authors propose a progressive four-stage training framework combining SFT, paradigm-constrained chain-of-thought distillation, dynamic patient-trajectory modeling, and knowledge-driven reinforcement learning. It matters because it shows how domain-specific structured reasoning and hard safety constraints can be injected into LLMs for specialized medical domains.

entry.title: In-Context Guidance: Learning Inter-Task Synergies via Numerical Foundational Models for Few-Shot Multitask Optimization

author.name: Tingyang Wei, Haofeng Wu, Jiao Liu, Zhao Wei, Puay Siew Tan, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: ICG-MTO leverages frozen numerical foundation models to infer auxiliary inter-task guidance through in-context learning, improving inter-task coupling estimation in few-shot multitask optimization and mitigating negative transfer. The framework constructs algorithm-specific in-context queries from evaluated solutions and uses the foundation model's predictions to guide optimization.

entry.title: Toward Responsible AI-Augmented Cyber Defense: Pattern Recognition, Defense-in-Depth, and the Case for Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Mustafa S. Aljumaily, Hayder Kareem Abed, Nawar S. Alseelawi

entry.summary: The paper develops a formal, falsifiable model connecting Defense-in-Depth Theory, the AI Theory of Pattern Recognition, and human-AI collaboration in security operations. It formalizes layered defense as a Bernoulli detection cascade with AI entering multiplicatively across layers and each layer's pattern-recognition behavior via a Neyman-Pearson style formulation, while addressing over-automation and analyst-skill-erosion concerns.

entry.title: SE-MSB: End-to-End Unpaired Speech Enhancement using Mamba Schr\"odinger Bridges

author.name: Andreas Bagge, Andreas Nymand, Michael Riis Andersen, Bj{\o}rn Sand Jensen

entry.summary: The authors propose a speech enhancement framework that works without paired clean/degraded training data by learning a stochastic transport between clean and degraded speech distributions via Diffusion Schrodinger Bridges. To reduce the computational burden of simulating differential equations during training, they pair DSB with an efficient Mamba-based diffusion backbone for end-to-end waveform processing. This targets real-world scenarios where acoustic conditions are unknown.

entry.title: EMERGE: Resolution-Agnostic Point Cloud Generation with Equivariant Graph-Based Diffusion

author.name: Ilias Mitsouras, Nikolaos Chaidos, Giorgos Stamou, Athanasios Voulodimos

entry.summary: EMERGE introduces what the authors describe as the first fully SE(3)-equivariant graph-based diffusion backbone for 3D point cloud generation, addressing the neglect of continuous, non-grid 3D topologies by Transformer- and VAE-based generators. The architecture is multi-scale and resolution-agnostic. This brings geometric deep learning benefits from discriminative vision into 3D generative modeling.

entry.title: AIGC Video Detection based on the fusion of spatial-frequency-optical flow multimodal features

author.name: S. Hong, X. Q. Wang, C. Zhang, J. C. Wang, P. X. Duan, Y. W. Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CrossAtt-VFD, a dual-branch detector for AI-generated video forgeries that jointly analyzes spatial-frequency features and optical-flow motion features, exploiting the observation that generative models struggle to keep appearance and motion cross-modally consistent. This addresses growing needs to detect synthetic video from tools like Sora-style generators.

entry.title: Topology-Stratified Materials Discovery with A Flow-Based Generative Model

author.name: Jingyi Zhou, Oyshee Chowdhury, Noah Oyeniran, Chongze Hu

entry.summary: Develops UFO-MGen, a universal flow-based generative model for crystal structure generation that learns topological features of Wyckoff representations to generate crystals across broad structural and chemical spaces, targeting extreme-environment materials for aerospace and fusion applications. It reports the highest crystal generation success among compared state-of-the-art generative models.

entry.title: Towards Hierarchical GNNs for multi-grid power flow: generalization across operating scenarios

author.name: Carmine Delle Femine, Leire Garin Atxaga, Asier Diaz-Iglesias, Juan Pablo Maroto Herrera, Ane Miren Florez-Tapia, Marco Quartulli. Izaro Goienetxea Urziku

entry.summary: This paper applies hierarchical latent communication to graph neural networks for power-flow prediction across multiple grid topologies, comparing Kron-derived transports, a Quotient construction, and a flat backbone. On three grid topologies, the Kron approach reduces macro family-balanced voltage error by 85% relative to the flat model and 31% relative to Quotient, showing improved generalization to new operating scenarios.

entry.title: SpeakerMem-R1: Speaker-Centered Dual-Track Memory for Multi-Party Dialogue

author.name: Haobo Zheng, Tan Tang, Yan Chen, Weijie Wang, Yingcai Wu

entry.summary: SpeakerMem-R1 proposes a dual-track memory architecture for long-term multi-party dialogue that explicitly handles message attribution, person and group relations, and state reconstruction from interleaved conversation histories. It targets documented failures of general-purpose LLM memory systems in multi-party benchmarks, where who-said-what and relational state are lost.

entry.title: Concept Drift from a Causal Perspective

author.name: Eduardo V. L. Barboza, Jean Paul Barddal, Robert Sabourin, Rafael M. O. Cruz

entry.summary: This paper introduces a causal taxonomy of concept drift in data streams using structural causal models, categorizing drift by origin (exogenous variables, endogenous mechanisms, confounders, target-generating processes). It also provides an SCM-based data stream generator simulating controlled mechanism-level changes and studies detection approaches.

entry.title: Efficient Cost-Aware LLM Evaluation via Bayesian Bandit Gittins Indices

author.name: Qian Xie, Yueli He, Nairen Cao

entry.summary: GittinsEval formulates LLM configuration selection across benchmarks as a cost-aware Bayesian bandit problem and applies the Gittins index policy to decide which configuration to evaluate next and when to stop. It adds an anytime recommendation rule with LCB-style uncertainty accounting and needs only lightweight online updates after offline precomputation. Experiments on GSM8K, PIQA, AlpacaEval, and MMLU show consistent competitiveness with substantial cost savings.

entry.title: Exploring Solver-Level Warmstarting for Neural Network Verification

author.name: Annelot Bosman, Minghao Liu, Marta Kwiatkowska, Holger Hoos, Jan van Rijn

entry.summary: The authors investigate whether solver-level warmstarting, reusing information from previously solved neural network verification problems, can cut verification runtimes for adversarial robustness properties. They systematically study how changing perturbation radii, input data, and network weights affects warmstart gains using a pipeline designed to be adaptable to state-of-the-art verifiers. Warmstarting significantly reduces verification time, which is valuable given that robustness verification is NP-complete in general.

entry.title: CoEvo: Oracle-Grounded Self-Evolution of a Single Model for Multi-Step Causal Reasoning

author.name: Jian Zhang, Bingyi Wang, Yizhi Liu

entry.summary: CoEvo tackles multi-step causal reasoning via single-model self-evolution grounded in a deterministic, queryable oracle that verifies individual reasoning steps rather than final answers, exploiting the asymmetry that generating correct chains is hard while verifying a single step is easy. This guards against outcome-only reward hacking, distributional shortcuts, and the collapse of naive self-evolution when teacher LLMs err or cloud distillation is restricted. It is relevant for high-stakes domains needing adaptation without external teachers.

entry.title: Beyond Imitation: Auditing the Recoverability of Reasoning in Distilled Models

author.name: Ruitong Li, Binjie Guo, Aisheng Mo, Guowei Su, Han Wang, Jie Li, Ru Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces prefix recovery as an audit metric for distillation: reveal 25-75% of a verified teacher solution and test whether the student can complete it, connecting recovery to the cosine conflict between cross-entropy and reverse-KL gradients. Across Qwen3 teacher-student pairs from 0.6B to 8B, prefix recovery rises from 71.0% to 91.9% as student size grows from 0.6B to 4B, and reverse-KL distillation most consistently improves students below 2B parameters. This gives a finer-grained lens on which students actually absorb teacher reasoning rather than imitating surface outputs.

entry.title: Empirical Auditing of Edge-Private Graph Generators

author.name: Anum Fatima, Stratis Limnios, James Adams, Lukasz Szpruch, Carsten Maple, Gesine Reinert, Andrew Elliott

entry.summary: The authors audit privacy leakage in differentially private graph generators by testing whether outputs from edge-neighbouring inputs are distinguishable, using statistically valid lower bounds on witnessed privacy loss. They compare direct-edge, local-structural, and GNN-based attacks across two generators and two networks. Findings show leakage is both mechanism- and network-dependent, with learned GNN representations exposing information missed by conventional local statistics.

entry.title: FAST-ML: A Hybrid Physics-Machine Learning Framework for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Forecasting

author.name: Shijie Xiao, Jonathan Lin, Thomas Ehrmann, Ali Sarhadi

entry.summary: FAST-ML is a hybrid physics-ML framework for tropical cyclone rapid intensification forecasting that uses a physically informed dual-stream network on 3D ERA5 fields to diagnose ventilation controls, optimized end-to-end through a differentiable intensity model. It balances the interpretability and physical grounding of numerical weather prediction with the efficiency of data-driven methods.

entry.title: Differentiable Policy Transport over Multi-Layer Network Feasibility Geometry

author.name: Zuyuan Zhang, Zeyu Fang, Mahdi Imani, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Tian Lan

entry.summary: NFG-RL models coupled cross-layer network constraints (interference, power-rate coupling, flow conservation, latency, reliability) via transport theory, defining the executed policy as the pushforward of a proto-policy through a feasibility-transport map. This makes constraint satisfaction explicit and differentiable rather than relying on reward penalties, Lagrange multipliers, or post-hoc repair.

entry.title: Error Bounds for Statistical Estimators in BTL Model with Parametric Multivariate Utility Functions

author.name: Yicheng Li, Huifu Xu

entry.summary: The paper studies preference elicitation under the Bradley-Terry-Luce model with unknown partworth parameters, deriving minimax lower bounds and sharp finite-sample error bounds for the maximum likelihood estimator under non-uniform, deterministic query designs, without compactness constraints or external regularizers. It connects the analysis to classic Fisher-information geometry.

entry.title: A Decentralized Partially Observable Team Decision Methodology with Delayed Information Sharing

author.name: Xiaoxing Ren, Thomas Parisini, Andreas A. Malikopoulos

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully decentralized learning and planning algorithm for cooperative decision-making in partially observable MDPs with unknown transition models, low-rank latent dynamics, and delayed information sharing among team members. Each agent learns an approximate low-rank MDP from local and delayed common information and applies least-squares value iteration, with no centralized coordinator.

entry.title: ChainDoRA: Tensor-Train Factorized Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Ashfak Yeafi, Mehedi Hasan, Md Khairul Islam

entry.summary: ChainDoRA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that builds DoRA's directional low-rank branch from a connected Tensor-Train chain, with adapter rank as the boundary rank and an independent TT rank controlling capacity and cost. The abstract indicates evaluation under a controlled setup comparing against LoRA-style baselines.

entry.title: From Utterances to Networks: Modelling Slang Adoption and Diffusion Across Subreddits

author.name: Xiaoning Wang, Ted Underwood, Zhewei Sun

entry.summary: This paper studies how neologisms and internet slang spread across Reddit communities, combining social-network and linguistic perspectives that prior work treated separately. It leverages LLMs to reduce the cost of annotating slang usage at scale, enabling network-level diffusion modeling. The work matters for computational sociolinguistics and for understanding cultural transmission online.

entry.title: Same Chart, Different Story: Bias in Vision-Language Chart Interpretation

author.name: Mizanur Rahman, Huan Wu, Arash Asgari, Enamul Hoque Prince, Laleh Seyyed-Kalantari

entry.summary: ChartBias is the first benchmark auditing bias in VLM chart interpretation, containing 820 curated real-world charts across six social attributes yielding paired generations. It tests whether models produce different narratives for identical charts when only the referenced social group changes, a mechanism that can reinforce stereotypes. The work targets a socially consequential failure mode of multimodal models.

entry.title: Enriching Speech Emotion Representations with Conversational Context

author.name: Arthur Peuvot, Romaric Besan\c{c}on, Ga\"el de Chalendar, Bianca Vieru, Ioana Vasilescu

entry.summary: Introduces ACERT, a module that integrates a flexible-length window of conversational context into Speech Emotion Recognition to capture emotional evolution and speaker interactions across an entire dialogue rather than per-utterance. Evaluated across datasets with diverse emotional expressive styles, addressing a common limitation of utterance-level SER.

entry.title: Did You Steal My Shot? Pioneering Camera Motion Plagiarism Detection in Generative Videos

author.name: Chengguo Zhang, Ping Ping

entry.summary: The paper builds the first benchmark for camera motion analysis in generative videos, with a dataset spanning 11 motion styles and evaluation protocols, and proposes a motion representation augmenting optical flow to disentangle camera motion from visual content. This enables detection of camera-motion plagiarism by generative video models, an emerging IP concern.

entry.title: Beyond the Survey: A Systematic Empirical Study of Detection and Association in Visual MOT

author.name: Linh Van Ma, Juhua Hu, Wei Cheng, Unse Fatima, Moongu Jeon

entry.summary: This paper provides a large-scale empirical evaluation of state-of-the-art multi-object tracking algorithms, decomposing tracking performance into detection and association contributions using publicly available implementations. It introduces a unified pipeline covering tracking-by-detection and end-to-end branches, offering practical guidance for method selection that existing taxonomic surveys lack.

entry.title: Event-Frame Fusion for Inter-Frame Segmentation via Event-Guided Motion

author.name: Dalia Hareb, Jean Martinet, Benoit Miramond, Elisabetta Chicca

entry.summary: This work proposes a hybrid architecture combining standard frame cameras with event cameras for autonomous navigation segmentation, using event-guided motion to recover information lost between frames due to blur, glare, and low temporal resolution. The design aims to combine frame-based accuracy with event-based high temporal resolution and dynamic range.

entry.title: General Collaborative Intelligence: Architecting Cognition for Resilient Multi-Agent Ecosystems

author.name: Lei Zhang, Chun Ye, Le Yang, Zhaozhong Wang, Deng-Ping Fan, Hang Dai, Binglu Wang

entry.summary: This is a survey of collaborative intelligence for multi-agent unmanned systems, offering a unified synthesis through a five-dimensional taxonomy (collaboration stage, communication paradigm, fusion architecture, learning strategy, application domain) and cross-dimensional analyses that prior isolated surveys miss. It covers how distributed agents exchange compact features to overcome occlusion, limited range, and environmental degradation.

entry.title: MixiMotion: One-Step Text-to-Motion Generation via Asymmetric Set Distillation

author.name: Hung Dinh, Binh Mai, Tran Quoc Bao Le, Lam Nguyen, Cong Tran

entry.summary: MixiMotion achieves strict one-step text-to-motion generation via offline set distillation, aligning teacher and student sample sets through asymmetric bidirectional matching: teacher-to-student matching promotes coverage of diverse motions while student-to-teacher matching suppresses unsupported generations. It also adds differentiable decoded-space kinematic components.

entry.title: LD-RSVIS: A Large-Scale and Diverse Benchmark for Referring Surgical Video Instrument Segmentation

author.name: Zan Wang, Yunhe Feng, Dong Nie, Oluwatosin Oluwadare, Kewei Sha, Yan Huang, Heng Fan

entry.summary: This paper introduces LD-RSVIS, a large-scale benchmark for referring surgical video instrument segmentation containing 3,536 surgical videos with 1.09 million frames. Unlike prior small benchmarks limited to single-target expressions, it supports multi-target and no-target referring expressions, enabling more practical and generalizable text-guided surgical video segmentation.

entry.title: HOIBlender: Blending Lightweight Detection with Vision-Language Priors for Efficient Human-Object Interaction Detection

author.name: Junwen Chen, Keiji Yanai

entry.summary: This paper introduces HOIBlender, an efficient human-object interaction (HOI) detector that blends detector-grounded visual tokens, spatial subject-object reasoning, and BLIP-2 semantic priors within a single lightweight decoding pipeline built on an RF-DETR/LW-DETR-style foundation with a DINOv2 backbone. It targets the common problem that prior HOI methods stack heavy transformer encoders, denoising schedules, and post-hoc calibration on top of detectors, and addresses long-tailed verb supervision.

entry.title: StyleAT: Defending Face Recognition Against Semantic Attacks

author.name: Ben Shapira, Roi Cohen, Shang-Tse Chen, Mahmood Sharif

entry.summary: This paper addresses the vulnerability of face recognition models to semantic adversarial edits such as subtle aging or pose changes that cause misclassifications. The authors introduce BoundStyle, an efficient semantic attack operating in StyleGAN's latent space that achieves high attack success rates while being roughly 9.5 times faster than existing methods, making it practical for use in adversarial training to build defenses. This matters because face recognition is widely deployed in authentication and surveillance, and scalable attacks are a prerequisite for developing robust defenses.

entry.title: Which Terrain Is Better? Preference Learning with VLM Prototypes for Off-Road Traversability Ranking

author.name: Ji-Hoon Hwang, Jisung Bae, E-In Son, Dong-Wook Kim, Jung-Taak Kim, Seung-Woo Seo

entry.summary: TravPro reframes off-road navigation perception as visual traversability ranking, learning a preference ordering over visible terrain rather than assigning absolute scores, since no universal ground-truth traversability score exists. It leverages standard annotations that implicitly encode preference direction and uses VLM prototypes to supervise comparisons between regions.

entry.title: Patch-to-Global: Random Patch Diffusion for Globally Consistent Megapixel Artifact Inpainting in Whole Slide Images

author.name: Hyeseong Lee, Eunsu Kim, D M Bappy, Ho Heon Kim, Youngsuk Lee, Se Young Chun, Jang-Hwan Choi, Sung Hak Lee, Sangjeong Ahn

entry.summary: RestorePath performs globally consistent megapixel-scale inpainting of tissue artifacts (bubbles, folds) in whole slide pathology images using a latent diffusion model conditioned on pathology foundation model embeddings with large kernel attention. The goal is to prevent silent, high-confidence diagnostic failures caused by artifacts concealing critical morphology.

entry.title: ChartJudgeBench: Evaluating LMM Judges for Chart-to-Code Generation

author.name: Lijian Wu, Henry Hengyuan Zhao, Zijian Zhang, Jiahao Tang, Jiajun Wu, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: ChartJudgeBench is a diagnostic benchmark assessing the reliability of large multimodal model judges used as visual critics and reward models in chart-to-code workflows, with 1,003 pairwise chart comparison instances and 650 binary accept/reject reasoning judgments. It targets the critical dependence of RL-based chart-to-code systems on reward signal quality.

entry.title: LiAuto-MindViT: A Hybrid Vision Backbone with Adaptive Bidirectional Mamba

author.name: Lifu Mu, Shuai Chen, Wen Zheng, Haoyi Sun, Xueyang Fu, Pengfei Yu, Ning Mao, Tao Wei, Zhou Pan, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: LiAuto-MindViT is a hybrid CNN-Mamba-Transformer vision backbone whose core is Adaptive Bidirectional Mamba, which removes directional bias of unidirectional SSMs via bidirectional selective scanning with learnable alpha blending. It also includes a reparameterizable design for deployment-friendly inference, evidently aimed at automotive applications from Li Auto. It contributes to the growing effort to adapt state-space models to vision.

entry.title: FedMust: Semi-supervised Multi-task Student-Teacher Federated Learning for Multi-organ CT Segmentation

author.name: Ashkan Moradi, Bendik Skarre Abrahamsen, Mattijs Elschot

entry.summary: FedMust is a semi-supervised federated learning framework for multi-organ CT segmentation that leverages both labeled and unlabeled data across institutions via a student-teacher multi-task design. It addresses the realistic clinical constraints of privacy, heterogeneous sites, and partial labeling where most local data is unlabeled.

entry.title: RS-Claw-Evolution: Environment-Feedback-Driven Evolution for Lightweight Remote Sensing Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Kai Ouyang, Dongyang Hou, Liangtian Liu, Zeyuan Wang, Ziyu Li, Chengfu Liu, Zichao Tang, Xuezhi Cui, Shengwu Ouyang, Wentao Yang, Hanwen Yu, Haifeng Li

entry.summary: RS-Claw-Evolution progressively improves lightweight LLM-driven remote sensing agents through three stages: interaction evolution using executable code to control observations and maintain state, experience evolution with failure-aware trajectory generation and error-turn masking, and a third stage building on environment feedback to overcome long-horizon state loss and sparse optimization signals.

entry.title: Knowing When to Trust Images: Reliability-Aware Multi-modal Entity Alignment

author.name: Chenxiao Li, Yunhe Feng, Dongfang Liu, Dong Nie, Yan Huang, Heng Fan

entry.summary: Proposes RA-MMEA, a reliability-aware framework for multi-modal entity alignment that predicts visual reliability and adaptively improves unreliable image representations rather than naively fusing all modalities. Two modules, dependency-aware visual reliability prediction and stability-regularized visual embedding generation, drive the improvement.

entry.title: StenoVLA-3D: 3D-Aware Reasoning VLA for Navigation Through Gastrointestinal Stenoses

author.name: Tamima Tabassum, Yiming Huang, Tianchun Wu, Changjing Liu, Zhiqing Tang, Chikit Ng, Beilei Cui, Liangjing Shao, Jiewen Lai, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: StenoVLA-3D is a vision-language-action model for autonomous endoscopic navigation through narrowed gastrointestinal regions, integrating 3D point-maps into the Cosmos-Reason 2 backbone via geometry-gated fusion plus a temporal state branch for traversal progress. It addresses texture-poor monocular observations and retention of lesion evidence beyond the field of view. An interesting domain-specific application of VLA and world-model backbones to medical robotics.

entry.title: PAKT: Physically-Aligned Kinesthetic Teaching for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lars Johannsmeier, Yashraj Narang

entry.summary: This paper introduces PAKT, a framework for kinesthetic teaching in real-world reinforcement learning for contact-rich industrial manipulation, where robots must achieve micrometer-level precision, very high success rates, and human-level cycle times. Instead of teleoperation, PAKT uses physically-aligned kinesthetic guidance — an approach already common in industry — to let operators provide demonstrations and interventions while respecting the constraints of both the physical robot and the policy. The work addresses a practical bottleneck: the lack of an intuitive, physically safe interface for collecting human guidance data in real-world RL.

entry.title: DynaForge: Planning-Guided Residual Learning for Dynamic Manipulation Demonstration Generation

author.name: Yiyang Jin, Yu Zheng, Xiao He, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: DynaForge generates high-quality demonstrations for dynamic object manipulation by combining low-frequency global planning with high-frequency object-centric inverse kinematics, plus a residual policy correcting actions near contact. It overcomes failure modes of purely planning-based generators and simplifying replay approaches like DOMINO.

entry.title: SG-CPG: Severity-Gated Central Pattern Generators for Adaptive Quadruped Locomotion under Continuous Actuator Degradation

author.name: Adarsh Kumar Kosta, Kaushik Roy

entry.summary: Inspired by how injured animals gradually unload a weakened limb rather than switching gaits discretely, this work proposes a central pattern generator framework for quadruped locomotion that adapts to continuous actuator degradation. It freezes a healthy locomotion policy and adds two severity-driven gates: one that re-coordinates all four legs and one that progressively shortens the weakened leg's stride. This offers a graded fault-tolerance mechanism between fully healthy and fully failed actuator states.

entry.title: Sometimes You Gotta Run Before You Can Walk: Run-then-Walk Scheduling Strategy for VLM Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuqi Ye, Shangkun Sun, Junhong Lin, Jiayi Zhao, Changhao Peng, Wei Zheng, Guoqing Liu, Tiesong Zhao, Wei Gao

entry.summary: The paper identifies two distinct RL regimes in GRPO-based training of VLM driving planners: a progress regime that aggressively explores high progress but risks unsafety, and a safety regime that restores safety under stable progress. It proposes a two-stage Run-then-Walk reward scheduling strategy that first runs then walks, achieving better performance and faster convergence than either fixed recipe. This offers a simple, broadly applicable insight about GRPO reward scheduling.

entry.title: Manipulation with Stability Guarantees: Linear Deformable Objects with Non-negligible Physical Response Grasped at Multiple Location

author.name: Daniel Feliu-Talegon, Cosimo Della Santina

entry.summary: This work moves beyond quasi-static assumptions in deformable object manipulation by addressing linear deformable objects such as hoses, pipes, and wiring harnesses whose dynamics cannot be ignored. It introduces a closed-loop control architecture recasting manipulation as shape regulation via forces and torques at multiple fixed grasp points, built on a fully dynamic model of linear deformable objects with stability guarantees. This targets a practically important but underexplored class of objects.

entry.title: Towards Intent-Aware Human-Robot Teaming: A Platform for Search-and-Rescue Operations

author.name: Rohith Prem Maben, Ayesha Jena, Bj\"orn Olofsson, Stefan Reitmann, Jacek Malec, Rogier Woltjer, Elin Anna Topp

entry.summary: This paper presents an interaction platform for studying human-robot collaboration between operators and heterogeneous autonomous agents in search-and-rescue scenarios. It supports intent inference and decision-making and demonstrates how operator perception and decisions can be augmented by autonomous systems in dynamic environments.

entry.title: Vision-Language Models as copilots for Autonomous UAV Navigation: Analysis of Latency and Reliability in Degraded Environments

author.name: Hiago Sodre, Sebastian Barcelona, Vincent Sandin, Pablo Moraes, Ahilen Mazondo, Igor Nunes, William Moraes, Andr\'e Kelbouscas, Ricardo Grando

entry.summary: This work evaluates a hybrid FSM-VLM architecture for GPS-free UAV navigation, pairing a deterministic finite state machine for low-level control with an asynchronous VLM copilot for semantic pathfinding. It measures latency, format-level syntax errors, and semantic hallucinations across three VLMs of different scales in software-in-the-loop simulation.

entry.title: Toward Self-Repairing Ubiquitous Robots Using Goal-Oriented Agentic AI in Human-Robot Interactions

author.name: Morten Roed Frederiksen

entry.summary: The paper introduces a goal-oriented agentic AI architecture that lets non-expert users complete robot repair tasks through situated natural-language dialogue, with separated stages for goal decomposition, state tracking, and conversational execution. Evaluation on a physical hardware repair task with twenty participants achieved a 95% completion rate with robustness to conversational diversions.

entry.title: ArborSplat: Online Semantic Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Orchards

author.name: Alessandro Masini, Matteo Frosi, Mirko Usuelli, Matteo Matteucci

entry.summary: This paper introduces ArborSplat, an online semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system designed for orchard robotics, combining LiDAR odometry for tracking with direct semantic optimization on the Gaussian map. It uses class-specific height bands above a per-keyframe fitted ground plane to reliably segment thin structures like trunks, trellises, and fruit, fusing multi-view evidence into a semantic point cloud in real time. The work addresses a real gap where appearance-driven 3DGS optimization fails to capture small but agriculturally critical structures.

entry.title: Hierarchical Floorplan-Guided Vision-Language Exploration for Embodied Question Answering

author.name: Albert Gassol Puigjaner, Kostas Alexis

entry.summary: HFLEX-EQA is a hierarchical embodied question answering framework combining online scene graph construction, VLM-based planning, semantic frontier exploration, and floorplan priors. It builds a hierarchical scene graph and open-vocabulary occupancy map from RGB-D input, letting a VLM reason jointly over structure and language to guide exploration of unseen environments.

entry.title: Wheel-loader V-Cycle Automation with Deep Koopman MPC

author.name: Armin Abdolmohammadi, Navid Mojahed, Dinesh Kumar, Bahram Ravani, Shima Nazari

entry.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical framework for autonomous wheel-loader operation combining long-horizon geometric planning of forward-reverse maneuvers with data-driven predictive control based on deep bilinear Koopman models of vehicle dynamics. It addresses the nonlinear articulated-vehicle dynamics and vehicle-terrain interactions that limit conventional model-based approaches for earthmoving automation.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Coordination Lets Us Pour More Compute Into Post-Training

author.name: nwyin

entry.summary: The author argues, building on Noam Brown's recent podcast remarks, that training models to coordinate across many agents offers a way to convert dramatically more post-training compute into capability, extending single-agent parallel thinking to multi-agent settings. The post discusses how multi-agent credit for a recent Millennium Prize Problem result was small but why coordination could still open new compute scaling axes.

entry.title: Testing-Driven Reliability Audit of Trajectory-Based Early Outcome Prediction for LLM Agents: Target-Specific Calibration Transfer Persists Within a Single Benchmark

author.name: YanZe Cao

entry.summary: Audits calibration of early-outcome predictors used to cut short expensive LLM agent evaluations, using leave-one-agent-out analyses on SWE-bench Verified trajectories. Finds calibration transfer failures are target-specific, persisting within a single benchmark between agent and predictor-head combinations.

entry.title: Metrics Failure in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Repair: An Empirical Study and a Change-Aware Screen

author.name: Om Nepal, Sushant Aryal, Oluseyi Olukola, Nick Rahimi

entry.summary: This empirical study argues that compile rate is an unreliable proxy metric for LLM-based C/C++ vulnerability repair, showing via five controlled experiments over 203 Big-Vul functions and three small code LLMs that about 64% of compile failures are attributable to evaluation-harness and dataset artifacts rather than model quality. It proposes a change-aware screening approach as a better evaluation method.

entry.title: Learning Defensive Policies against Diverse Inference Attacks for Smart Meter Privacy

author.name: Ruichang Zhang, Mustafa A. Mustafa

entry.summary: The authors frame smart meter privacy as a black-box defense problem against non-intrusive load monitoring attacks and propose a proxy-guided hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that learns battery-based load-shaping policies. The policies inject realistic but misleading consumption signals to degrade appliance-level inference while generalizing to unseen attacker models. This is a concrete RL application to a high-stakes energy privacy problem with practical deployment relevance.

entry.title: HYDRA: Proactive Android Malware Drift Adaptation via Hierarchical Graph Contrastive Learning

author.name: Han Chen, Hanchen Wang, Hongmei Chen, Lu Qin, Wenjie Zhang, Ying Zhang

entry.summary: HYDRA is a proactive framework for adapting Android malware detectors to concept drift, learning drift-invariant representations from hybrid graph structures combining fine-grained control-flow graphs and coarse-grained function call graphs. It aims to avoid both reactive retraining with heavy annotation burden and unstable adversarial approaches.

entry.title: A Computational Approach to Measuring Semantic Change in Sanskrit Literature

author.name: Tanay Agrawal

entry.summary: This paper tests whether diachronic word-embedding methodology transfers to Sanskrit, an ancient low-resource language with sandhi fusion, rich inflection, and compounding. The author assembles a 2.7M-token corpus across four canonical periods, builds a neural sandhi splitter and lemmatizer, and recovers 19 of 21 testable historically documented semantic shifts using anchor-displacement evaluation.

entry.title: CoVeR: Coverage-Based Routing of Verifier Calls in Agentic Retrieval

author.name: Daeyoung Roh, Donghee Han

entry.summary: CoVeR reduces the cost of LLM-verifier-stopped agentic retrieval by gating verifier calls with a threshold on a frozen sentence-embedding coverage margin: calls are skipped when evidence is plainly incomplete and reserved for ambiguous states. Across three multi-hop QA benchmarks it skips most verifier calls without materially changing accuracy. This is a practical efficiency contribution for agentic retrieval systems.

entry.title: PERSONAWEAVER: Controllable Diversity Beyond Conventional Archetypes in Procedural Character Generation

author.name: Maan Qraitem, Kate Saenko, Bryan A. Plummer

entry.summary: Identifies behavioral homogenization in LLM-based procedural character generation, where generated populations overwhelmingly conform to positive moral norms and assistant-like helpfulness. PersonaWeaver disentangles world building from behavioral specification and models setting-general and divergent behaviors to produce diverse, controllable characters for games and simulations.

entry.title: Enabling Vision and Cross-Modal Learning for Multimodal Stroke Recurrence Prediction: An Interpretable Two-Step Framework

author.name: Christian Gapp, Elias Tappeiner, Martin Welk, Karl Fritscher, Stephanie Mangesius, Constantin Eisenschink, Philipp Deisl, Michael Knoflach, Astrid E. Grams, Elke R. Gizewski, Rainer Schubert

entry.summary: This medical imaging study investigates whether self-supervised pretraining on 3D CTA scans reduces modality imbalance and improves cross-modal integration for stroke recurrence prediction, a clinically critical task. The interpretable two-step framework analyzes how pretraining and selective parameter freezing affect modality contributions.

entry.title: Retrieval Geometry Shapes Cache-Based Clip Adaptation

author.name: Mahir Shahriar Tamim, Md. Samiul Alim, Azmine Toushik Wasi, Shahriyar Zaman Ridoy, Meharun Nesa, Mohammad Abu Yousuf, Alex Lamb, Mohammad Ali Moni

entry.summary: This paper shows that cache-based test-time adaptation of CLIP depends heavily on the retrieval feature space: with a fixed memory, changing only the retrieval encoder swings ImageNet-A cache gains from +0.44 to +19.7 across sixteen retrieval spaces, with label-free retrieval-space selection retaining 98% of oracle gain. This reveals that adaptation quality depends on retrieval geometry, not just memory contents.

entry.title: Benchmarking Off-the-Shelf Multimodal AI Models Against Dermatologists on Patient-Captured Skin Images

author.name: Rian Dolphin, Laura Knowles

entry.summary: The paper evaluates three low-to-mid priced multimodal models on diagnosing dermatological conditions from patient-submitted images, comparing against grades from a panel of three certified dermatologists. The authors report four findings, framing these models as a floor rather than a ceiling on current capability in this clinically relevant task.

entry.title: Anatomically Faithful Artifact Suppression in SENSE Accelerated Brain MRI

author.name: Changjing Chai, Bin Huang, Libo Xu, Jian Zhou, Boyang Pan, Kristen W Yeom, Qiyong Gong, Nan-Jie Gong

entry.summary: Develops ART-Net, an Anatomy-aware Residual Attention Network that refines 4x-accelerated SENSE brain MRI reconstructions to suppress noise and aliasing while preserving anatomical information for quantitative measurements. Evaluated in a prospective paired study of 80 participants with fully sampled and accelerated acquisitions.

entry.title: Capability-Aware Arbitration for Semantic Intent-Based Shared Control

author.name: Zhaoda Du, Michael Bowman, Xiaoli Zhang

entry.summary: This shared-control framework combines a VLM that infers human intent with semantic-intent confidence and a VLA policy whose capability confidence is estimated online from the dispersion and instability of stochastic action trajectories; a nonlinear Bayesian-filtered arbitration policy adapts robot authority to avoid over-helping when autonomous execution is unreliable. A thoughtful fix to a real failure mode of intent-confidence-based shared autonomy.

entry.title: Leveraging Vision-Based Point Cloud Map Priors for Camera-Based 3D Object Detection and Online Vectorized HD Mapping

author.name: Markus K\"appeler, Rohit Mohan, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: The authors propose constructing a static point cloud prior map from previous camera traversals (avoiding expensive LiDAR) and augmenting points with DINOv3 features, retrieving local prior patches at runtime to aid camera-based 3D detection and online vectorized HD mapping. This exploits long-term deployment observations to mitigate depth ambiguity in vision-only perception.

entry.title: MedGate-Fusion: Integrating First-Encounter Semantic Narratives and Physiological Biomarkers for Prospective Stroke Risk Stratification

author.name: Hemn Khdr, Mohammad Noaeen, Karim Keshavjee, Aziz Guergachi, Zahra Shakeri

entry.summary: MedGate-Fusion is a multi-modal gated architecture combining transformer embeddings of first-encounter clinical narratives with ten routine risk markers for five-year prospective stroke risk stratification in primary care. Built on roughly 800,000 CPCSSN encounter observations yielding over 100,000 patient records, it also addresses target leakage from diagnostic mentions in notes.

entry.title: Gaze responses to false-positive computer-aided detection prompts during colonoscopy: a paired-video and real-time eye-tracking study

author.name: Te Luo, Yan Zhu, Peiyao Fu, Ruijie Yang, Xian Yang, Quanlin Li, Pinghong Zhou, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: Uses event-locked eye tracking in retrospective paired-video and prospective real-time studies to quantify how false-positive CADe prompts divert endoscopists' attention during colonoscopy, finding false positives attracted gaze in roughly half of observed cases. Results inform the human factors costs of AI assistance in clinical practice.

entry.title: OmniFysics-Nano-V2 Technical Report: Understanding the Physical World Across Modalities

author.name: Yizhou Liu, Jinghang Han, Kaixiang Qiu, Qi He, Minghao Han, Yue Jiang, Xujia Chen, Wei Zou, Shunli Wang, Lihua Zhang, Dingkang Yang

entry.summary: Presents OmniFysics-Nano-V2, a compact omni-modal model accepting image, video, audio, speech, and text within a shared reasoning framework, trained with objectives targeting physical attributes, interaction states, and causal mechanisms rather than just semantic descriptions. Includes text and speech generation for physical-world perception tasks.

entry.title: Selection-Invariant Communication Compilers for Privacy-Aware Multi-Agent LLM Workflows

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu

entry.summary: The paper identifies selection-channel leakage in multi-agent LLM workflows: even after authorization, choosing among semantically valid message realizations can leak private state. It introduces a selection-invariant communication compiler with a compositional communication-layer guarantee combining authorization, public randomization, and canonical forms. This is a principled, provable contribution to privacy in agentic systems.

entry.title: FusionMMT: A Unified Multimodal and Multitask Learning Framework for Nuclear Fusion

author.name: Qiang Chen, Xiao Wang, Qingquan Yang, Hao Si, Zikang Yan, Meiwen Chen, Guosheng Xu, Jin Tang

entry.summary: FusionMMT presents a unified multimodal multitask learning framework for tokamak diagnostics, releasing EAST-VTD640, a dataset spanning vision and time-series signals from 640 EAST shots for disruption prediction, ELM recognition, and H98-related performance tasks. Prior fusion ML work has been limited to unimodal multitask or multimodal single-task setups. The dataset and unified framework could accelerate ML for fusion control and monitoring.

entry.title: Decoupling Is Not Identification: Supervised Evidential Learning in Next-Token Prediction

author.name: Ge Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes an Evidential Next-Token Prediction (ENTOP) framework to audit whether Dirichlet-head concentration parameters actually carry evidence signal, using exact 8-gram counts on character-level Moby-Dick as a reproducible support label. It finds implicit evidential training carries essentially no count signal beyond confidence (rho near 0.001), while explicit supervision generalizes (rho about 0.201).

entry.title: Prompt Breadth and Rollout Refresh Interact in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Lingxiang Hu, Tianle Xia, Ming Xu, Yiding Sun, Linfang Shang

entry.summary: Jointly studies prompt breadth and rollout refresh in on-policy distillation using a 3x3 controlled experiment on mathematical reasoning. It finds a strong interaction: breadth helps substantially only when responses are refreshed from recent policy snapshots, with 8 prompts approaching the accuracy of 14,080 under sufficient refresh.

entry.title: Geometric and Semantic Coupling for Interaction Understanding in 3D Scenes

author.name: Hanyang Kong, Xingyi Yang

entry.summary: Presents Segment-Snap, a method coupling part segmentation, handle detection, and motion estimation for articulated 3D objects using planar/upright priors to select hinge lines without training a motion regressor, with one-shot bidirectional information transfer between predictors. Evaluated on Articulate3D validation data.

entry.title: Destination Support Restoration for Finite-Set Multimodal Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Fengrui Liu, Jiajun Peng, Duo Peng, Feng Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Destination Support Restoration (DSR), a causal post-selection operator that repairs the support of multimodal pedestrian trajectory predictions so plausible alternative destinations are not lost during repeated online updates, without retraining the predictor or enlarging the prediction set. This preserves the diversity of futures available to downstream robot decision-making.

entry.title: Skytopia: Monocular Drone Navigation with Action-Conditioned Latent World Models

author.name: Yuhang Zhang, Rangya Zhang, Yujing Shang, Zhuoyuan Yu, Weiying Wang, Steven Yang, Qingsong Yan, Chao Yan, Mir Feroskhan

entry.summary: This work tackles monocular drone navigation in unseen environments by rethinking what a policy needs from a world model: not the prediction itself, but the latent representation needed to produce it. The authors observe that in flight, actions explain nearly all inter-frame change, so prediction reduces to reprojecting a static scene under known displacement. They build a policy on an action-conditioned latent world model that exploits this insight.

entry.title: REVE: Efficient Hallucination Correction for Large Audio-Language Models via Reused Encoder States

author.name: Hongjin Song, Jiasheng Kuang, Xinyu Yang, Qiuyu Fang, Ziyu Wu, Guowu Tan, Xiang Xie

entry.summary: REVE targets hallucinated acoustic-event mentions in large audio-language models by verifying them without a second audio encoder or forward pass. It reuses encoder states already computed by the target model, using readout heads for class scores and pooled frame-interval states, with class-aware score fusion. On AudioSet it removes 92.9% of label-unsupported mentions under a faithful-mention recall constraint with few added parameters.

entry.title: StepTrigger: Contact-State-Triggered Backdoor Attacks on VLM-Powered Legged Robots

author.name: Jiageng Zhang, Doniyorkhon Obidov, Kaichen Yang

entry.summary: StepTrigger demonstrates a new backdoor attack surface for VLM-powered legged robots in which the trigger is not a prompt token or visible marker but a physical pressure and foot-ground contact pattern. A compromised planner behaves normally in most runs yet changes target selection when the hidden contact-state trigger occurs. This extends embodied-agent security beyond language and visual triggers.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Hyperbolic Residual Quantization

author.name: Alessio Colombo, Melika Ayoughi

entry.summary: Proposes a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual vector quantization method that fixes inconsistencies of naive hyperbolic extensions, such as non-associative hyperbolic addition and geometry-blind straight-through gradients, in both forward and backward passes. This embeds the coarse-to-fine hierarchy of quantized codes in hyperbolic space where it is a natural fit.

entry.title: GitScholar: A Dataset for Predicting AI Research Impact from GitHub Engagement

author.name: Emilien Guandalino, Lorenz K. M\"uller, Beatrice Alessandra Motetti, Konstantin Berestizshevsky, Lukas Cavigelli

entry.summary: Introduces GitScholar, a dataset linking GitHub activity from 444,000 repositories to over 558,000 AI arXiv papers, enabling research impact prediction from code engagement signals. The authors show GitHub engagement is a timely and accurate complement to content- and citation-based impact prediction, helping researchers triage the flood of daily publications.

entry.title: TraceVIC: Causal Reasoning over Code Evolution for Identifying Vulnerability-Inducing Commits

author.name: Fnu Tanish, Samiha Shimmi, Samikshya Chapagain, Hamed Okhravi, Mona Rahimi, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: TraceVIC reframes vulnerability-inducing commit identification as causal reasoning over how vulnerability-relevant code evolves across revisions, rather than relying on git blame and positional heuristics. The approach traces code evolution across multiple commits to locate where the underlying vulnerable condition was introduced.

entry.title: Does AI Save Time on Product Design? A Randomized Controlled Experiment of AI Prompt-to-Design Workflows

author.name: Remy Stewart, Olabode Anise, Andrew Hogan, Augustus Griffin

entry.summary: A randomized controlled trial with 50 product designers and 50 product managers evaluated whether Figma Make's prompt-to-design workflows save time on standardized design tasks. Among completers, access to the tool was associated with roughly 20% shorter completion times, providing rare experimental evidence on AI productivity in design work.

entry.title: Signed Graph Pre-Training and Prompt Learning

author.name: Zihan Mei, Rong Pan, Yuzhou Chen, Yixuan He

entry.summary: TopoSIGN is a pre-training and prompt-learning framework for signed graphs, combining a magnetic signed Laplacian structural encoder with a persistent-homology branch that encodes signed topology via Dowker-complex persistence images. The fused embeddings transfer to downstream tasks through prompt learning, addressing the underdeveloped area of transfer learning on signed graphs (trust networks, financial correlations, biological interactions). Experimental results demonstrate effectiveness across signed graph tasks.

entry.title: BOBA: Dynamic Bayesian Optimization through Bayesian Active Inference

author.name: Merlin Angel Kelly, Rishan Patel, Alexander Thomas, Ziyue Zhu, Zikun Quan, Tom Carlson, Youngjun Cho

entry.summary: BOBA proposes a new acquisition function for dynamic Bayesian optimization, where the objective drifts over time, derived from the free energy principle of active inference. Unlike standard UCB-style acquisitions, it explicitly minimizes predictive uncertainty about future states to better track moving optima. This addresses a known weakness of existing dynamic BO methods that ignore temporal variation in sample allocation.

entry.title: FuncCode: Compressing Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks in Function Space with Hardware-Aware Quantization

author.name: Kazi Ahmed Asif Fuad, Lizhong Chen

entry.summary: FuncCode compresses Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks by building shared codebooks from sampled edge responses in function space rather than compressing spline coefficients, then exporting quantized, bit-packed codebooks and per-edge indices. The authors show edge responses have 13-35% lower effective rank than coefficient representations and provide replicated controls showing function-space clustering is statistically tied with coefficient-space alternatives. This is the first systematic hardware-aware compression study for KANs.

entry.title: From Risk Scoring to Risk Allocation: A Density-Driven Framework for Diverse Monitoring in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhaohui Wang
