entry.summary: This paper identifies a Crowding Paradox in multi-agent risk monitoring: risk correlates with state density, not anomaly scores, so scoring states independently selects redundant, correlated alerts (herding in monitoring). It reframes monitoring as risk allocation rather than risk scoring, showing density-based scoring reaches AUROC >= 0.94 on financial crash horizons while five anomaly baselines stay below 0.80, and proposing diversity-aware allocation of monitoring effort. The reframing is applicable to LLM multi-agent systems and finance alike.

entry.title: Can You Delete a Year of Market Data? Machine Unlearning Against Exact Retraining Oracles

author.name: Junyi Ye

entry.summary: This work benchmarks temporal machine unlearning on an S&P 500 volatility panel using 3,200 paired references, comparing deployable unlearned models against exact retraining oracles across five architectures, four rolling folds, five deletable years, and three deletion levels. Removing the 2020 COVID crisis year produces the largest memorization gap, and its removal improves all deployable models in every fold, while non-deployable models respond inconsistently. The study grounds data-license-driven deletion obligations in a concrete financial forecasting setting.

entry.title: Quantifying Protocol-Induced Uncertainty in Comparative Predictive-Model Evaluation: Evidence from Large-Scale Daily PM10 Forecasting

author.name: Rafael da Silva, Kiersten Monahan

entry.summary: This work formalizes how rankings of predictive models depend on evaluation protocols, introducing a framework that measures ranking displacement when switching between protocols, quantified via a Protocol Sensitivity Score and a full-refit reference. It validates the approach on daily PM10 forecasting across 425 European background stations and 365 US EPA monitors, comparing static-split and rolling-origin evaluation.

entry.title: FREESIA: Covariance-Aware Posterior Transport for Expressive and Scalable Data Assimilation

author.name: Shiwei Ni, Yangwen Zhang, Hang Qi, Xiaofei Guan, Lili Ju

entry.summary: FREESIA is a training-free, asymptotically exact posterior transport method for data assimilation that addresses multimodal posteriors induced by nonlinear or non-injective observation operators under high-dimensional sparse observations. It designs a covariance-aware posterior transport scheme that scales like ensemble filters while avoiding the restrictive distributional assumptions of ensemble methods and the structural errors of training-free generative filters such as EnSF and EnFF.

entry.title: Variational objectives for amortized Bayesian inference in inverse problems: The role of posterior conditioning

author.name: Abhishek Srivastava, Arijit Hazra, Rajesh Dubbaku

entry.summary: This paper compares three variational objectives for VAE-based amortized Bayesian inference in inverse problems: reverse-KL, asymmetric Jensen-Shannon, and a Jensen-Shannon-Wasserstein hybrid that replaces the reverse-KL regularizer with a squared 2-Wasserstein distance. Using full-covariance Gaussian encoders and a physics-based pre-trained surrogate, it examines how each objective handles weakly identified parameter directions. The results inform objective choice when posterior accuracy is sensitive to regularization.

entry.title: Scalable Minimum-Volume Simplex Estimation with Non-asymptotic Analysis

author.name: Jun LI, Yanlong Guo, Zhaozhao Zeng

entry.summary: DeepMVSA reformulates minimum-volume simplex estimation in neural implicit form, using a coordinate network and LU-type triangular parameterization to reduce memory to O(K^2) independent of sample size and per-pass cost to O(NK^2), enabling application to N of 10^6-10^8. The paper also provides non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantees matching polynomial-time benchmarks.

entry.title: Sample-Smooth Spaces: A Convenient Category for Differentiable Probabilistic Programming

author.name: Patrick Forr\'e

entry.summary: The paper introduces a category of sample-smooth spaces over a mixed site, combining Cartesian spaces with the universal Hilbert cube carrying all universally measurable sets, so that smoothness and measurability become a single structure over one site rather than two structures glued by axioms. This yields a clean categorical foundation for differentiable probabilistic programming in which measurability of smooth families is derived rather than assumed.

entry.title: PROSWIN: Probabilistic Solar Wind Speed Forecasting Using Deep Distributional Regression From Solar Images

author.name: Daniel Collin, Yuri Shprits, Luca Chiarabini, Stefan J. Hofmeister, Nadja Klein, Guillermo Gallego

entry.summary: PROSWIN is a probabilistic model forecasting hourly solar wind speed at Earth with a four-day lead time, combining solar images and magnetograms via a deep neural network coupled to distributional regression. It also introduces a prediction score metric that better emphasizes high-speed solar wind stream peaks, which threaten technological infrastructure.

entry.title: TelecomGPT-R1: Unified Post-Training for Reasoning Across Heterogeneous Telecom Tasks

author.name: Bohao Wang, Chenwei Wu, Hang Zou, Yu Tian, Lina Bariah, Li Wei, Chongwen Huang, Yongliang Shen, Zhaoyang Zhang, Merouane Debbah

entry.summary: TelecomGPT-R1 is a family of open-source telecom reasoning models organized around four axes (protocol, knowledge, modeling, and fault), built with an axis-aware data pipeline and unified post-training to reason across standards, network configurations, math models, code, and logs. It targets the gap between general LLMs lacking telecom grounding and narrow telecom-specialized models.

entry.title: ClusterFewshot: Improving Few-shot Optimization for LLMs workflow

author.name: Omri Bar Haim, Shahar Katz, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: ClusterFewshot improves in-context demonstration selection for LLM workflow optimization by combining semantic clustering with utility-aware scoring, rather than random sampling or metric ranking. Evaluated in DSPy-based pipelines, it reduces optimization cost while consistently improving accuracy over prior bootstrap-style methods. It is a practical advance for prompt/program optimization.

entry.title: Moonworks Lunara: Modeling Artistic Intelligence

author.name: Yan Wang, Yanzu Wang, Maitreyee Joshi, Samiha Sadeka, Partho Hassan, Reza Jarral, Sayeef Abdullah, Sabit Hassan

entry.summary: The paper formulates Artistic Intelligence as exploration-driven world realization and implements it in Lunara, a text-to-image model built on a novel Diffusion Mixture Transformer architecture with a training algorithm that iteratively injects human-created art via informative sample acquisition. Benchmarked against seven image generation models including FLUX.2-Klein-4B and Qwen-Image, Lunara ranks first in aesthetic quality using GPT-5.6 Sol as evaluator.

entry.title: Style as Cover: Deep Image Steganography via Stylized Transmission

author.name: Qi Li, Jidong Yang, Huaike Yu, Chunpeng Wang, Suo Gao, Herbert Ho-Ching Iu, Yuantian Miao, Bin Ma, Xiao Chen

entry.summary: StyleStegaNet replaces cover-preserving steganography with style-concealment transmission, generating stylized stego images conditioned on public style references so hidden content camouflages as ordinary stylization behavior. The work redefines invisibility from matching a specific cover to behavior-level camouflage and tackles the resulting secret-recovery challenges.

entry.title: Image Frame Dynamic Object Segmentation and Ego Motion Estimation using Radar Image Fusion

author.name: Astik Srivastava, Suhani Grover, Avinash Sharma, Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: Radar-Dot is a radar-RGB framework that uses Doppler measurements to jointly solve dynamic object segmentation and ego-motion estimation, two tightly coupled problems in autonomous driving. It estimates ego velocity from a linear Doppler constraint, performs residual-based static/dynamic segmentation, and flags image regions whose motion is inconsistent with the rigid scene.

entry.title: Compressing 3D Gaussian Splatting via Cross-Representation Priors

author.name: Yezheng Zhang, Huanxiong Liang, Chuqin Zhou, Guo Lu, Wenjun Zhang

entry.summary: CRP-GS is a rate-distortion optimized compression framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting that exploits cross-representation priors for anchor-level entropy modeling. It organizes anchors by feature correspondence rather than spatial proximity, building root-leaf dependencies so selected anchors conditionally encode others, reducing the high storage and transmission costs of dense Gaussian primitives.

entry.title: An Eternal Irradiance Camera

author.name: Jeremy Klotz, Shree K. Nayar

entry.summary: This optics/computer-vision paper proposes an omnidirectional irradiance camera that measures illumination incident on every point of a sphere rather than per-pixel radiance. Because the irradiance function is bandlimited and approximable by the first seven spherical harmonic degrees, it can be reconstructed from only a handful of measurements, enabling cameras with drastically fewer detectors.

entry.title: GrapeSplat: Geometry-Grounded Reconstruction via Amalgamated Pose-Free Encoding for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Si-Yu Lu, Yung-Yao Chen, Yi Jan Chen, Shang-Lin Li, Ching-Chan Liao, Wen-Huang Cheng

entry.summary: GrapeSplat improves feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting from unposed, uncalibrated images by amalgamating multi-view cues into a voxel-aligned scene representation and decoding Gaussians directly from a learned grid without per-scene optimization. Components include an Atlas Encoder producing pixel-wise geometry-and-appearance features anchored at predicted 3D points and PEACH-Vox, which maps unbounded scenes into a bounded sparse grid with a closed-form inverse.

entry.title: AniPrO: Interpretable Anime Image Provenance Detection via Multi-Dimensional Semantic Reasoning

author.name: Yan Liu, Baoxiang Huang, Zi'an Wang, Wenbo Xie

entry.summary: AniPrO addresses the growing problem of distinguishing human-drawn, AI-inpainted, and text-to-image generated anime-style images, which matters for copyright attribution and content governance. The framework uses multi-dimensional structured descriptions (five dimensions) and is built on a new dataset, AnimeDL-2M, with 15,000 balanced samples across Real, Inpainting, and Text2Image categories. Its emphasis on interpretability and anime-specific cues (flat coloring, line control) fills a gap left by detectors focused on photographic images.

entry.title: PhysReflect: Geometry and Perception Guided Diffusion for Physically-Plausible Mirror Reflections

author.name: Shuheng Ge, Hongwei Ren, Li Zhang, Xiangqian Wu

entry.summary: PhysReflect is a geometry- and perception-guided diffusion framework that corrects physically implausible mirror reflections in generated images, such as positional offsets, directional misalignment, and structural distortion. The paper argues that prior fixes based on synthetic data scaling or depth conditioning rely only on implicit latent-space supervision, and instead enforces reflection-specific geometric and perceptual constraints directly.

entry.title: G6D: Geometric Learning-Free RGB-D 6D Pose Solver for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yixuan Liang (Tsinghua University), William Chen (Sapient Intelligence), Yunan Wang (Tsinghua University), Jizhou Yan (Tsinghua University), Zhao Jin (Tsinghua University), Changling Liu (Sapient Intelligence), Chuxiong Hu (Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: G6D is a learning-free, geometry-driven RGB-D 6D pose solver that, given an RGB-D observation, an object mask, camera intrinsics, and a CAD model, generates and refines pose hypotheses without large pretrained networks. It targets zero-shot generalization to unseen objects while fitting the limited compute budget of robots where perception, planning, and control share resources.

entry.title: Confidence-Aware Teacher-Student Distillation for 3D Medical Segmentation

author.name: Georgios Triantafyllou, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: This work proposes an annotation-efficient student-teacher framework for 3D medical segmentation requiring only point prompts on a single 2D slice per volume. A foundation-model teacher generates full-volume pseudo-annotations with spatial confidence scores, and the student training mitigates error propagation from noisy pseudo-labels.

entry.title: STAR: Scene- and Task-Aware 4D Radar Preprocessing Towards End-to-End Cognitive Radar

author.name: Seung-Hyun Song, Dong-Hee Paek, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: STAR makes 4D radar preprocessing scene- and task-aware, moving beyond signal-level CFAR detection that can discard information valuable for downstream perception. It connects radar point cloud generation directly to perception task objectives, moving toward end-to-end cognitive radar pipelines.

entry.title: IMPLICIT-Bench: Measuring Implicit Bias in Text-to-Image Models under Neutral Prompts

author.name: Yue Dai, Ziyang Liu, Marc Cheong, Caren Han

entry.summary: IMPLICIT-Bench measures implicit bias in text-to-image models under neutral natural prompts where stereotype-relevant attributes are unspecified, using knowledge-graph-constructed triplets of neutral, stereotype, and anti-stereotype prompts differing along a single bias dimension. This moves beyond slot-based templates that probe only explicit demographic attributes in isolation.

entry.title: MECAIL: Communication-Aware Incremental Learning for Object Detection with 14.6 KB Spatiotemporal Experts

author.name: Matthias Neuwirth-Trapp, Maarten Bieshaar, Danda Paudel, Konrad Schindler, Luc Van Gool, Christos Sakaridis

entry.summary: MECAIL addresses incremental learning for object detection on resource-limited edge devices in intelligent transportation, transmitting tiny (14.6 KB) specialized spatiotemporal expert modules from servers over constrained V2X, Wi-Fi, and cellular links. The strict size budget is designed to fit within the first TCP window and minimize fragmentation. It combines systems constraints with continual learning in a realistic deployment scenario.

entry.title: What Survives on Real Drawings: Active Sampling, Connectome Wiring, and Matched Baselines in Architectural Document Vision

author.name: Dmitry Kuklev

entry.summary: A single-author study uses a connectome-constrained model of the fly visual system as a frozen texture representation for architectural document analysis, compared against information-matched CNN baselines on 721 photoreceptor samples. Trained networks win on clean data but the frozen connectome pipeline is far more noise-robust, degrading only 0.030 versus up to 0.188 for trained networks.

entry.title: GraphSVR: q-Space--Aware Graph-Based Slice-to-Volume Registration for Diffusion MRI

author.name: Noga Kertes, Daphna Link Sourani, Alex M. Bronstein, Moti Freiman

entry.summary: GraphSVR frames 4D slice-to-volume registration in diffusion MRI as a q-space-aware graph problem, representing slice groups so that diffusion-direction-dependent contrast and dozens of measurements share a common reference frame. It improves robustness under sparse gradient sampling and severe motion compared to sequential or pairwise-similarity approaches.

entry.title: DTKDP: A Dual Teacher Knowledge Distillation and Pruning Framework for Lightweight Oriented SAR Ship Detection

author.name: Yuming Li, Fan Zhang, Alin M. Achim

entry.summary: DTKDP distills two-stage oriented SAR ship detectors into lightweight one-stage students using dual-teacher knowledge distillation with learnable gates for pruning channels and RoI-head neurons. A rotated proposal alignment mechanism preserves the proposal-level refinement that one-stage lightweight detectors typically lack.

entry.title: SolarFlowRefiner: Refinement-Aware Flow Matching for Surface Solar Radiation Downscaling

author.name: Udbhav Srivastava, Antonita Racheal, Yiheng Chen, Runlong Yu, Xinyue Ye

entry.summary: SolarFlowRefiner performs multiscale downscaling of surface solar radiation from coarse ERA5 reanalysis plus satellite channels using refinement-aware flow matching, addressing the spatially sharp and ambiguous corrections caused by mixed sunlit and cloud-shadowed regions within a single grid cell. It avoids oversmoothing of one-stage predictors and the stage-wise mismatch of post-hoc refinement.

entry.title: SomaNet: Weakly Supervised Learning for Instance Soma Segmentation in 3D Electron Microscopy with Partial Annotations

author.name: Mohammad Khateri, Morteza Ghahremani, Jussi Tohka, Alejandra Sierra

entry.summary: Proposes SomaNet, a teacher-student framework for instance soma segmentation in 3D electron microscopy under partial annotations, where a teacher trained on partial data generates pseudo-labels to supervise the student. It targets the prohibitive cost of dense instance-level manual annotation in connectomics.

entry.title: Rethinking Pairwise Token Interaction in Spiking Transformers

author.name: Sicheng Shen, Dongcheng Zhao, Zhiyuan Li, Jinyan Yu, Qian Zhang, Dengpeng Xing, Zhitong Zhang, Tielin Zhang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why inherited Transformer token-interaction mechanisms fit poorly with sparse binary spike representations and proposes Gated Spike Axial Propagation (GSAP), a spike-native mechanism that decouples long-range information propagation from context selection rather than relying on pairwise spike coincidence. An architectural rethinking for energy-efficient spiking Transformers.

entry.title: Effects of Assistance Delay on Joint Mechanics and Energetics in Biological Torque Control of a Hip Exoskeleton

author.name: Jimin An, Ryan Lee, Jingshu Peng, Eni Halilaj, Inseung Kang

entry.summary: A human-subject study testing how assistance delay (40-320 ms) affects hip exoskeleton performance during level-ground, ramp-ascent, and ramp-descent walking under biological torque control. Assistance consistently reduced metabolic cost and joint work across tasks, providing evidence that a fixed state-to-torque mapping remains effective over biomechanically distinct activities.

entry.title: MotionForge: A Data Generation Pipeline and Large-Scale Benchmark for Long-Horizon Manipulation of Dynamic Objects with Domain Shifts

author.name: Mohan Liu, Dengchen Mei, Haotian Xian, Ruyang Han, Jiayi Sun, Xuanyu Chen, Haitian Zhang, Luxi Li, Kaimin Mao, Lin Wang

entry.summary: MotionForge is claimed to be the first large-scale simulation benchmark and data-generation pipeline for long-horizon manipulation of dynamic objects, jointly evaluating domain shifts and extended interactions rather than short reactive tasks. It includes model-agnostic real-time execution protocols, addressing gaps in existing dynamic simulation benchmarks. The work responds to the fact that most learned manipulation policies are still evaluated in static environments.

entry.title: Fisheye-VLA: Decoupling Coverage and Acuity for Manipulation with a Single Fisheye Camera

author.name: Ziang Ren, Zike Yan, Raymond Zhang, Xuguo He, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: Fisheye-VLA shows that a single passive fisheye camera can serve manipulation policies needing both wide workspace awareness and fine local detail, using perspective crops rendered from the fisheye view. A controlled re-rendering study compares crop directions and finds end-effector-centered views capture most of the benefit of a much larger candidate pool. This simplifies vision-language-action robot setups by removing separate front and wrist cameras.

entry.title: Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects Using Model Predictive Path Integral Control with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Learning

author.name: Lukas Zeh, Johannes Meiwaldt, Zexu Zhou, Armin Lechler, Alexander Verl

entry.summary: This work tackles cable-like deformable linear object (DLO) manipulation by learning DLO dynamics with a bidirectional LSTM trained on MuJoCo synthetic data, then using Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control for manipulation. The learning-based modeling plus sampling-based control combination addresses the infinite-dimensional, nonlinear nature of DLOs.

entry.title: TM-APR: Thermal Temporal-Memory Localization via Analytic Online Adaptation

author.name: Yanshuo Bai, Kanji Tanaka

entry.summary: This paper tackles thermal visual place recognition by bridging Analytic Class-Incremental Learning with domain-invariant VPR, showing that gradient-free matrix updates form a strong baseline that outperforms conventional fine-tuning while avoiding heavy online retraining. It also identifies and addresses a vulnerability of standard ACIL to extreme non-linear domain shifts.

entry.title: Announcing B-Side Labs: Measuring Character (Seeking Collaborators and Testers)

author.name: jacklchang

entry.summary: This post announces B-Side Labs, an independent research initiative studying AI character instability: the degree to which a model's stated values or persona shift under social pressure rather than in response to evidence. It describes plans for discriminative evaluations, real-time drift detection, and interventions, and introduces a first tool called Virtue Council with pilot results.

entry.title: Modular Norm RandOpt: Population-Efficient Ensembling through Architecture-Aware Perturbations

author.name: Kirato Yoshihara, Hiroaki Hamade

entry.summary: This work improves RandOpt, a weight-perturbation sampling and plurality-voting ensembling method for LLMs, by replacing a single global perturbation scale with module-wise natural norms that respect heterogeneous architecture geometry. The result matches or exceeds RandOpt accuracy using 3-12x fewer candidate samples on Countdown, GSM8K, and MATH-500 across Qwen 0.5B-3B, Llama 3.2 3B, and Gemma 3 4B scales. The efficiency gains make architecture-aware randomization more practical.

entry.title: UniK: Universal Knowledge Perception for Digital and Physical AI

author.name: Nirmit Desai, Kunal Sawarkar, Aditya Mahakali, Dongkon Lee, Kevin Park, Eric Song

entry.summary: Proposes UniK, a common platform for digital AI (chatbots, agent workflows) and physical AI (robotics, autonomous systems) that spans the full knowledge lifecycle from ingestion and enrichment to indexing, retrieval, and continuous evaluation across heterogeneous modalities. It targets raw knowledge locked in private corpora that existing infrastructure cannot reliably access.

entry.title: Vision Foundation Models with Synthetic-Only Training for Monocular Spacecraft Pose Estimation

author.name: John Church, Vazghen Nikolian

entry.summary: This paper reports state-of-the-art mean rotation errors on the SPEED+ spacecraft pose estimation benchmarks by swapping DINOv3 into a heatmap-based pose architecture, training purely on synthetic data, and scaling from 300M to 840M parameters without saturation. It also demonstrates embedded feasibility with latency and power measurements on a Jetson Orin NX.

entry.title: Learned Enterprise Data Comprehension: Compression and Routing for Data Agents

author.name: Ethan Torres, Eric Mills

entry.summary: The paper introduces latent equivalence learning, a framework that separates persistent task-relevant identities in enterprise data environments, letting learned systems predict and organize recurring structure while agents handle semantic reasoning. It targets compression and routing of complex schema, relationship, and policy information for structured-data agents.

entry.title: Transformer Heads Looking for Order

author.name: Jasper van Doornmalen, Alexander Kozachinskiy, Corinna Mathwieser, Tomasz Steifer, Felipe Urrutia, Jos\'{e} Verschae, Przemys{\l}aw Andrzej Wa{\l}\c{e}ga

entry.summary: A theory note proving that checking whether a bit sequence is ordered cannot be done by a 1-head 1-layer transformer but can be done with 2 heads, under a model that includes an output MLP. This sharpens prior expressivity results by removing assumptions about output-layer limitations.

entry.title: CausalLoss-Fin: Attributing Financial-Agent Loss to Decisions and Infrastructure Faults

author.name: Abhishek Sharma

entry.summary: This paper introduces a causal attribution method for financial agents that intervenes on both agent decisions and infrastructure faults (such as dropped settlement messages), rather than charging all loss to agent actions. It derives a telescoping identity that exactly splits policy loss into infrastructure effect, policy differential, and other components on a replayable fault benchmark. The work highlights a real blind spot in agent-step attribution methods.

entry.title: Canonical locks that encode part-whole hierarchies

author.name: Rajat Modi, Yogesh Singh Rawat

entry.summary: The paper proposes canonical locks, a geometric primitive for encoding part-whole hierarchies in neural networks using higher-dimensional vectors whose relative phase differences carry information, with positionally-bound bottom-up and top-down fields driving each other to equilibrium. This departs from flattening tree structures into sequences for autoregressive modeling. It is an ambitious attempt at structured representation learning, particularly for images.

entry.title: ChainUQ: Reasoning Consistency-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models

author.name: Dahai Yu, Rongchao Xu, Lin Jiang, Ximiao Li, Guang Wang

entry.summary: ChainUQ is an uncertainty quantification framework for LLM reasoning that captures logical inconsistencies between intermediate claims and final conclusions, going beyond token-level probabilities. It dynamically calibrates confidence using the structural logic of the generated reasoning chain. The approach addresses a known weakness of probability-based confidence in chain-of-thought settings.

entry.title: VACS: Value-Aligned Compositional Shielding for Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Yiyao Zhang, Diksha Goel, Hussain Ahmad, Shixun Huang, Jun Shen

entry.summary: VACS is a four-layer framework for multi-agent systems in high-stakes domains that infers each agent's implicit values from behavior (Bradley-Terry rewards plus deep MaxEnt IRL), provides compositional formal safety shields without full online communication, and performs value-aware conflict resolution with faithful explanations. It jointly addresses value inference, safety guarantees, and conflict resolution, which prior methods handled separately. This is a substantive safety architecture for heterogeneous multi-agent systems.

entry.title: The Delegation Blind Spot: Auditing Product Decisions from Agent Choices

author.name: Shivam Gupta

entry.summary: The paper presents a decision-specific audit mapping an agent's declared observation channel and product-value contrasts to compatible intervals and witness populations, testing whether successful execution reveals which product improvement a user would value. A controlled 4,800-request study found all 36 primary intervals unresolved despite differing execution accuracy, a largely negative result about inferring user value from agent choices.

entry.title: "As a Language Model...": Chat Template Switches LLM Self-Referential Voice and Activation Steering Reproduces It

author.name: J\k{e}drzej Maczan

entry.summary: Demonstrates that the chat template acts as a switch governing LLM self-referential voice: with it, disclaimer voice ('I'm just an AI') increases and experiential voice decreases, and vice versa, across 8 open instruct models. The authors locate a directional mechanism in model activations and reproduce the effect via activation steering.

entry.title: Brain-Inspired Hierarchical Modularity for General Continual Learning

author.name: Hongwei Yan, Kanglei Zhou, Qi Cheng, Weiyi Dong, Chunyan Lan, Guanglong Sun, Jun Zhou, Qian Li, Yi Zhong, Liyuan Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a hierarchical modular principle, inspired by the Drosophila learning and memory system, that separates conflicting experience to reduce interference while integrating compatible experience for generalization in online, uncertain data streams. This targets the underexplored general continual learning regime beyond offline task-boundary settings.

entry.title: How Children Design and Reason about Trustworthy AI Chatbots

author.name: Deniz Ozturk (Georgie), Jiayu Li (Georgie), Daksh Pratap Singh (Georgie), Yasitha Rajapaksha (Georgie), Fasika Melese (Georgie), Bahare Riahi (Georgie), Shiyan Jiang (Georgie), Qiao (Georgie), Jin, Joey Huang, Veronica Catet\'e, Tiffany Barnes, Xiaoyi Tian

entry.summary: A mixed-methods study of 115 learners aged 8-18 building their own chatbots in an environment with adjustable trust-relevant traits, examining how children configure and reason about trustworthiness and whether behavior matches designs. It shifts AI-literacy research from children as evaluators to children as designers.

entry.title: When Quantum Meets AI: Quantum Methods for Machine Learning and Machine Learning Methods for Quantum Systems

author.name: Tak Hur

entry.summary: This thesis explores both directions of the quantum-AI interface: Neural Quantum Embedding for improving classification on noisy quantum hardware, an objective based on Hilbert-Schmidt inner products demonstrated on an NMR quantum processor, and margin-based generalization analysis for quantum neural networks, plus ML methods for quantum systems. It connects quantum neural network performance to quantum statistical bounds.

entry.title: CogenPVG: Cognitive-Enhanced Reflective Multi-Agent Framework for Persuasive Video Generation

author.name: Yuntian Xiao, Shoulong Zhang, Wenfeng Song, Yan Wang, Yi Chen, Shuai Li

entry.summary: CogenPVG is a multi-agent framework for persuasive video generation that decomposes the task into argument reasoning, storyboard planning, asset creation, and post-editing, each with paired generator-critic agents for reflective refinement. It imitates human video producer workflows to create stance-driven, persuasive video content from a topic and stance supplied by the user.

entry.title: xWhyL: Causal Interactive Learning

author.name: Nicholas Tagliapietra, Florian Peter Busch, Moritz Willig, Matej Ze\v{c}evi\'c, Lavdim Halilaj, Juergen Luettin, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: The paper proposes xWhyL, a formal framework that reverses the usual XAI direction: instead of using causal models to produce explanations, it learns causal models from explanations. The authors develop a mathematical theory translating abductive explanations into a learning signal complementary to observational data. This enables overcoming limitations of purely observational causal discovery.

entry.title: Policy-Backed Selective Regeneration under Tainted Inter-Agent Communication

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces ESC-CR, a framework for secure inter-agent code generation that separates message claims from authorization and enforces executable semantic commitments at an external release boundary. When a violation occurs, the framework taints the responsible message and rejected artifacts, enabling clean-room recovery rather than discarding useful content wholesale. It addresses prompt-injection-style threats in multi-agent LLM systems without relying on prompt-based defenses.

entry.title: Silent Sabotage: Internal State Triggered Backdoor Attacks on LLM-Powered Robotic Systems

author.name: Doniyorkhon Obidov, Shivayogi Akki, Tan Chen, Kaichen Yang

entry.summary: This paper presents the first comprehensive study of history-based backdoor attacks on LLM-powered robotic systems, where the trigger is embedded in the agent's own operational logic rather than external stimuli like words or visual objects. Attackers can hide triggers in interaction history that cause harmful behavior when internal conditions recur. This exposes a more insidious vulnerability class for LLM-controlled agents.

entry.title: TransBERT: A Framework for Synthetic Translation in Domain-Specific Language Modeling

author.name: Julien Knafou, Luc Mottin, Ana\"is Mottaz, Alexandre Flament, Patrick Ruch

entry.summary: Introduces TransBERT, a framework for pre-training language models entirely on synthetically translated text in specialized domains, plus TransCorpus, a scalable translation toolkit. Focusing on French life sciences, it shows SOTA downstream performance is achievable using only synthetic translation, releasing a 36.4GB corpus, models, and code.

entry.title: FairMean: Promoting Fairness in Distributed Learning under Label Poisoning Attacks

author.name: Huigan Zheng, Jiaojiao Zhang, Yongxiang Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies a conflict between fairness-aware distributed learning and robustness to label poisoning: fairness mechanisms upweight clients with large losses, but poisoned clients also exhibit large losses, so fairness weighting can amplify malicious gradients. The proposed FairMean method weights client gradients using a bounded, nondecreasing function of local loss, prioritizing high-loss clients while capping amplification of poisoned-client gradients. The authors prove that in the unpoisoned setting FairMean yields fairer solutions than standard average-loss minimization and derive an average-stationarity bound under label poisoning.

entry.title: The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Military Operations

author.name: Nicolas Drapier, Florian Mauberger, Aladine Chetouani, Aurelien Chateigner

entry.summary: Argues that the ethical challenge of AI in military operations is fundamentally epistemic: delegating force decisions to opaque, gameable systems undermines the conditions for responsible human judgment, creating an accountability gap in which responsibility diffuses across designers, operators, and policymakers. The paper analyzes how this gap conflicts with International Humanitarian Law's presuppositions about judgment.

entry.title: From Alignment to Access Control: A Framework for GenAI Policy Enforcement

author.name: Nathalie Baracaldo

entry.summary: This position-style paper surveys the state of policy enforcement for generative AI applications, arguing that inconsistent definitions of policy across practitioners lead to siloed, compliance-inadequate solutions. It frames policy as a cornerstone of secure and compliant GenAI systems and outlines a unified framework spanning alignment and access control.

entry.title: Correcting Within-Group Self-Selection Bias in Prioritized Replay

author.name: Oscar Mir\'o L\'opez-Feliu, Herke van Hoof

entry.summary: The paper identifies within-group self-selection bias in prioritized experience replay: in stochastic environments, replaying by absolute TD error distorts the distribution of realized outcomes for the same state-action pair. It decomposes PER into between-group allocation and sibling selection and derives fixed-buffer corrections (SAMPLE, AVG, MODEL) that preserve group-level priority mass.

entry.title: SambaGraph: Action-Reaction Spatio-Temporal Graphs for Soccer Tactical Response Modeling

author.name: Abel A. Reyes-Angulo, Henry O. Velesaca, Steven Araujo

entry.summary: SambaGraph introduces a dataset and benchmark for modeling tactical responses in soccer, built from tracking and event data across all 64 matches of the 2022 FIFA World Cup, with 4,070 action-centered episodes as spatio-temporal player-ball graphs. It defines tasks including classifying defensive responses from attack episodes and retrieving successful defenses for a query attack. The resource is valuable for multi-agent spatio-temporal modeling research beyond soccer.

entry.title: CacheDyG: Decoupling Temporal Propagation for Efficient Dynamic Graph Learning

author.name: PinHeng Zong, Ye Yuan

entry.summary: CacheDyG is a cache-refine framework for dynamic graph neural networks that decouples temporal propagation from routine parameter updates by caching largely unchanged historical structures instead of recomputing them each epoch. This reduces substantial training and parameter overhead from maintaining node-time representations. It is an efficiency contribution for a widely used modeling class.

entry.title: The Dynamics of Quasiregular Neural Learning

author.name: Matthia Sabatelli

entry.summary: Motivated by U-shaped learning in child language acquisition, this controlled study examines how neural networks learn mixtures of dominant regularities and systematic exceptions in quasiregular regression tasks. Networks first partially acquire exceptions, then overregularize back toward the dominant pattern, and finally recover exceptions again, with overregularization strongest when exceptions are rare. The results isolate a simple competition between regularity and exception learning during neural training.

entry.title: Activation-Energy Pruning for Spiking Neural Networks: Unsupervised Personalization via Spike-Count Saliency

author.name: Joseph Bingham

entry.summary: This paper extends activation-energy pruning to spiking neural networks, where removing weights below a magnitude-times-cumulative-spike-count threshold corresponds to literal synaptic metabolic cost. Surprisingly, gradient-based pruning methods that work well on conventional networks (SNIP, GraSP, magnitude pruning) collapse to near-chance accuracy on SNNs, while the physically grounded criterion succeeds. The work supports unsupervised on-device personalization for neuromorphic systems.

entry.title: Partially Observed Sparse Graphs: The Unknown Sampling Rate is a Tail Index

author.name: Jian Xu, Delu Zeng, John Paisley, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: For large graphs observed only through a partial sample of unknown sampling fraction, the paper proves that under sparse exchangeable graphex models the expected non-isolated fraction scales as s^(1+sigma), so estimating the sampling rate reduces to estimating the tail index sigma. Substituting back yields a global edge count estimator identical to the design-based one with the design quantity inferred. This cleanly reframes graph cardinality estimation under unknown sampling as tail-index estimation.

entry.title: Can We Predict Anomaly Detection Performance from Embedding-Space Geometry?

author.name: Kevin Wilkinghoff, Zheng-Hua Tan

entry.summary: This paper studies whether anomaly detection performance can be predicted without access to labeled anomalies, deriving a lower bound on the AUC for kNN-based detectors that relates detection performance to inlier-outlier score separation and their variances. Under a local scaling model it characterizes how density variation, intrinsic-dimensional heterogeneity, and cross-domain mismatch contribute to score variability, and examines anomaly-free model selection.

entry.title: When Residualization Helps an Audit: Format Effects, Slice Gains, and Their Limits

author.name: Daein Weon, Dong Ho Kang

entry.summary: This work audits surface-form effects in LLM evaluation components such as reward models, rerankers, and LLM judges, showing a public preference reward model selects a terse correct solution over a commented buggy one no better than chance on MBPP problems. It formalizes why subtracting a predictable surface component does not by itself yield more valid measurement, since the removed component may carry construct-relevant signal, and uses unit-test-labeled interventions to quantify what residualization actually fixes.

entry.title: What Does Chain-of-Thought Entropy Measure? A Channel Audit of Scaffolding, Routing, and Content

author.name: Marios Papamichalis, Regina Ruane

entry.summary: This paper decomposes entropy over chain-of-thought tokens, which governs which tokens receive policy gradient, which get pruned, and whether a run has collapsed, into three mixed choices: whether to emit connective scaffolding, which connective, and what the substantive continuation is. The authors prove raw and content conventions can disagree about which position is the larger fork and bound answer diversity by the content channel plus a leakage term, validating across twenty-three configurations.

entry.title: SPARC: SuperPixel-Aware Region Contrastive Learning for Self-Supervised Dense Prediction

author.name: David Szczecina, Yuanpei Xiang, Jitao Hu, David Clausi, Yuhao Chen, Jason Deglint, Paul Fieguth

entry.summary: SPARC is a region-level contrastive self-supervised learning framework that leverages superpixels to establish explicit correspondence between augmented image views, introducing a region contrastive branch that performs superpixel-based feature pooling. It optimizes a region-level objective jointly with a global image-level objective, targeting dense prediction tasks where image- or pixel-level contrastive methods are insufficient.

entry.title: Calibration Count Reuse: Validity Does Not Determine Efficiency

author.name: Rudra Chopra

entry.summary: This conformal prediction paper establishes a validity criterion for count-dependent nonconformity scores when calibration counts are reused across classes, proving it via a leave-self-out full conformal reference. It shows that validity conditions (monotonicity in the count under certain transformations) do not imply any parallel ordering of efficiency, separating two properties often conflated. This clarifies when calibration data sharing is theoretically sound for multi-class conformal methods.

entry.title: Synthesis and editing of multi-instrument audio mixtures using scalar-quantised latents with MIDI Span conditioning

author.name: Sungkyun Chang, Keshav Bhandari, Simon Dixon, Emmanouil Benetos

entry.summary: SpanSynth-Edit is a flow-matching model for MIDI-guided synthesis and editing of multi-instrument audio mixtures, encoding instrument-labelled note lifecycles as compact per-frame conditioning vectors over scalar-quantised latents. It supports local editing by resynthesizing only revised regions while retaining context, with competitive benchmark results.

entry.title: On the Gradient Heterogeneity Dynamics of Adversarially Robust Federated Regression

author.name: Leonardo F. Toso, James Anderson, Nirupam Gupta, Rafael Pinot

entry.summary: This paper derives gradient heterogeneity bounds for federated regression from the underlying statistical model with fresh samples per round, rather than imposing a priori gradient-dissimilarity assumptions, yielding less conservative guarantees under adversarial clients. The bounds separate honest-client heterogeneity, finite-sample effects, and adversarial influence.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Restricted Boltzmann Machine Neural Quantum State

author.name: H. L. Dao

entry.summary: The author constructs the first non-Euclidean, non-autoregressive neural quantum state, a hyperbolic Restricted Boltzmann Machine, studied via variational Monte Carlo on the Quantum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model whose ground state has volume-law entanglement. Across a 512-fold increase in Hilbert space dimension (N=14 to N=24), the hyperbolic variant beats the Euclidean RBM on ground-state energy optimization and entanglement entropy reconstruction errors.

entry.title: TailSpec-EASE: Knowledge-Graph-Regularized Linear Recommendation for Web Long-Tail Discovery

author.name: Jianru Shen

entry.summary: TailSpec-EASE injects a relation-aware spectral knowledge-graph prior into a local closed-form EASE-style reconstruction objective for recommendation, with prior strength adapting to item popularity so long-tail items receive stronger semantic guidance. It evaluates across four datasets against graph-neural KG-aware recommenders.

entry.title: A Practical Guide on Graphical Model Validation

author.name: Mario V. W\"uthrich

entry.summary: The manuscript formalizes the most popular model-validation tools used in insurance actuarial modeling, including calibration plots, actual-vs-expected plots, lift charts, Murphy diagrams, Bregman and deviance losses, Murphy decomposition, and Gini scores. It emphasizes whether calibration and discrimination are assessed under policy-weighted or exposure-weighted population measures, which is crucial for correctly scaled premium schemes.

entry.title: Discovery-Driven Integration of Disjoint Tables via Text

author.name: Md Ataur Rahman, Dimitris Sacharidis, Oscar Romero, Sergi Nadal

entry.summary: This paper addresses data lake integration for semantically related tables that cannot be joined directly due to missing explicit attributes, formalizing a new task called Text-Mediated Join Path Discovery where unstructured text provides the evidence linking individual rows across tables. The authors propose LOKI, a horizontal bidirectional cross-attention architecture for discovering these fine-grained row-level connections. This matters because it tackles a practical bottleneck in enterprise data integration where the relational structure itself must be discovered before integration can occur.

entry.title: Diffusion-Induced Spatial Attention Overlapping Community Detection

author.name: Kosti Koistinen, Vesa Kuikka, Joni Herttuainen, Matthew Hendren, Brian Holt, Kimmo K. Kaski

entry.summary: DISCO is a deep-learning framework for overlapping community detection that combines a structural prior from influence-spreading dynamics, sparse multi-head attention, and non-negative community-affiliation learning. The prior lets attention reach beyond immediate graph neighbors, mitigating the boundary-smoothing problem of local message-passing GNNs.

entry.title: ICDAR2026 Competition on Multimodal Reasoning over Documents in Multiple Domains

author.name: Artemis Llabr\'es, Marc Serra Ortega, Tom\`as Ockier, Samuel Ortega Cuadra, Amritpal Singh, Christos Georgakilas, Andrey Barsky, Ernest Valveny, Dimosthenis Karatzas

entry.summary: This report presents results of the ICDAR2026 competition on multimodal reasoning over documents, a VQA benchmark spanning eight domains including business reports, scientific papers, maps, comics, and engineering drawings. Twenty valid submissions from eight teams covered zero-shot VLMs, OCR-augmented pipelines, agentic retrieval, multi-agent ensembles, and fine-tuned multimodal models.

entry.title: ARAFA: An LLM-Generated Arabic Fact-Checking Dataset

author.name: Christophe Khalil, Shady Elbassuoni, Rida Assaf

entry.summary: Arafa is a large-scale fact-checking dataset for Modern Standard Arabic built with an automated LLM pipeline: generating claims from Arabic Wikipedia with supporting evidence, mutating claims into counterfactuals with refuting evidence, and validating label correctness automatically. It addresses the scarcity of Arabic fact-checking resources and enables training and evaluating verification models in a low-resource language setting.

entry.title: Beyond Static Charts: Can Language and Vision Language Models Generate Interactive Data Visualization Interfaces?

author.name: Mizanur Rahman, Aaryaman Kartha, Enamul Hoque Prince

entry.summary: VIS-GEN is a benchmark of 3,042 samples evaluating whether LLMs and VLMs can generate interactive visualization interfaces from natural language, covering filtering, temporal analysis, and visualization editing. It fills a gap left by static-chart benchmarks and provides a systematic measure of an underexplored capability. Results are expected to inform the design of language-driven analytics tools.

entry.title: A retrospective analysis on the use of LLMs to study infant syntax learning

author.name: H\'elie Bazin (SCAI, SND, ISIR), Anouk Barberousse (SND), Fran\c{c}ois Yvon (MLIA)

entry.summary: An epistemological assessment of the BabyLM challenge and related studies that use LLMs to model infant syntax acquisition, examining dataset construction, model training, and syntactic evaluation. The authors find significant methodological assumptions that weaken the theoretical conclusions drawn from these modeling efforts.

entry.title: Semantic Abstraction for Natural Language Inference: a Methodological Framework for Discovering and Compensating Semantic Knowledge and Reasoning Gaps in Large Language Models

author.name: David Torres-Moreno, Jorge Hermosillo-Valadez

entry.summary: This paper proposes a methodological framework for probing how large language models use abstract semantic knowledge in natural language inference, defining semantic compatibility and incompatibility relations between premises and hypotheses. The framework aims to systematically discover and compensate for semantic reasoning gaps in LLMs.

entry.title: ALPINE: Adaptive Localization for Parameter- and Sample-Efficient Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Neeraj Yadav

entry.summary: ALPINE is an ultra-lightweight few-shot image classification architecture of only 22,249 to 34,917 parameters combining fixed Gabor edge-energy guidance with a content-adaptive windowed patch locator. Under a strictly matched episode-budget protocol it outperforms Prototypical Networks, Relation Networks, and MAML on CIFAR-FS with consistent gains across five seeds.

entry.title: LINGO: Latent Initialization and Gradient Optimization for Sparse-view X-ray Novel View Synthesis and CT Reconstruction with 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Lifeng Xing, Dequan Jin, Kunpeng Bu, Peigeng He, Shihui Ying

entry.summary: LINGO improves sparse-view X-ray novel view synthesis and CT reconstruction with 3D Gaussian Splatting by combining latent mask-space initialization with dynamic gradient optimization. It addresses noisy initialization, positional insensitivity, and weak gradients in low-density regions, improving structural completeness while accelerating training.

entry.title: ScaleBlind: Point Cloud Completion under Unknown Scale

author.name: Shenghui Wu, Chen Wang, Yuan Feng, Guangshun Wei, Yuanfeng Zhou, Changjian Li

entry.summary: ScaleBlind removes the hidden ground-truth-scale assumption in learning-based point cloud completion, which causes artifacts like over/under-completion and nested shells when the oracle scale is unavailable in real inference. The method leverages foundation image generation models' understanding of shape scale to complete partial point clouds without GT-scale access.

entry.title: GARO: Geometry-Aware Redundancy Optimization for Real-Time and High-Fidelity Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Huiwen Xue (School of Software, Northwestern Polytechnical University), Kaixing Zhao (School of Software, Northwestern Polytechnical University), Zuheng Ming (L2TI, Universit\'e Sorbonne Paris Nord, EmboMind Research), Tingcheng Li (School of Electronic Information, Engineering, Suzhou University of Science, Technology)

entry.summary: GARO introduces a unified redundancy measurement framework for the adaptive density control stage of dynamic Gaussian Splatting, selecting low-gradient candidates via an optimization activity assessment and evaluating geometric complexity through low curvature analysis. The goal is to cut the large number of redundant Gaussians that inflate memory and hurt rendering speed in dynamic scene reconstruction for applications like VR.

entry.title: PosEviLoc: Position-Conditioned Spatial Evidence for Language-Based 3D Localization

author.name: Tianyi Shang, Yike Shi, Zhenyu Li

entry.summary: PosEviLoc addresses coarse text-to-point-cloud localization by evaluating candidate submaps using explicit semantic and spatial evidence rather than compressing queries and submaps into global descriptors. It models direction as a relation jointly determined by an object position and a hypothetical query position, producing query-position-aware spatial evidence for matching descriptions of nearby objects.

entry.title: Training-Free Spectral Transductive Refinement for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Classification

author.name: Fahim Rahman, S. M. Tanjeeb Meheran Rohan, Md. Taimum Ibne Sayed, Asaduzzaman Herok, Md. Bakhtiar Hasan

entry.summary: STR is a training-free transductive inference rule for cross-domain few-shot classification that builds a joint k-nearest-neighbour graph over support and query embeddings, maps episodes into a normalized-Laplacian spectral coordinate system, and iteratively refines class representatives using pseudo-labelled queries. It requires no encoder retraining or source augmentation, targeting fragility under domain shift and one-shot supervision.

entry.title: DFD-Lab: A Modular Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection Pipeline

author.name: Jan Rybarczyk, Mateusz Roszkowski, Jacek Komorowski

entry.summary: DFD-Lab is a modular open pipeline for comparing audio-visual deepfake detectors, integrating Xception-based maximum-logit fusion, ResNet-LSTM fusion, and an AVFF reimplementation under shared training and evaluation workflows. Notably, its experiments show detectors trained on FakeAVCeleb nearly fail on the in-the-wild Deepfake-Eval-2024 subset (AUROCs near 0.5), with degradation-aware augmentation providing only partial recovery.

entry.title: The Visual Target Matters: Learning across the Visual Hierarchy for Brain-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Ye Wang, HaoKun Ren, Hong Yu, Ruirui Li, Xiao Li, Ke Liu, Wei Wu

entry.summary: NeuroGlyph learns a trial-independent visual target for brain-to-image retrieval by aggregating representations across multiple depths of a frozen vision model, instead of training against a fixed final-layer target. This lets the visual hierarchy directly shape the retrieval objective for non-invasive neural responses.

entry.title: SAFe: Segment-guided Aggregation of Feature Densities for Anomaly-aware Segmentation

author.name: Anja Deli\'c, Jurica Runtas, Marin Or\v{s}i\'c, Ivan Markovi\'c, Ivan Petrovi\'c

entry.summary: SAFe is a generative method for anomaly-aware segmentation that trains lightweight normalizing flows for class-conditional density estimation over self-supervised foundation-model representations, with segment-guided aggregation for spatial consistency. It targets reliable detection of out-of-distribution objects during real-world deployment of segmentation systems.

entry.title: AlignMorph: Tuning-Free Diffusion Image Morphing via Explicit Semantic Transport

author.name: Wuyi Liu, Xu Han, Yuren Chen, Yige Mao, Zishuo Peng, Xianzhi Li

entry.summary: AlignMorph is a tuning-free diffusion-based image morphing framework that decouples geometric alignment from generative denoising using a transport-then-denoise principle. It employs entropic optimal transport for semantic alignment with reliability-aware latent warping, plus a coordinate component, avoiding expensive per-pair optimization. It addresses a real failure mode of prior methods under large layout discrepancies.

entry.title: TReViS: Temporal Repetition Structure Aware Video Synthesis for Self-supervised Repetitive Action Counting

author.name: Fanqi Yu, Shengming Ma, Stefano Fiorini, Vito Paolo Pastore, Xuan Qi, Vittorio Murino, Cigdem Beyan

entry.summary: TReViS enables self-supervised repetitive action counting by estimating temporal repetition structure via a Temporal Self-Similarity Matrix, inferring cycle statistics, and synthesizing training videos with controlled variability paired with pseudo-labels. This removes the need for costly dense temporal annotations. It consistently improves over baselines across datasets and backbones.

entry.title: Evaluating Transformation Models for pCLE Mosaic Registration

author.name: Ahmed Aboelela, Johannes Barcsay, Jana Friedhof, Miguel Gon\c{c}alves, Alexander Hann, Katharina Breininger

entry.summary: The paper builds a manually annotated landmark dataset of 132 frame pairs from 14 probe-based Confocal Laser Endomicroscopy sequences to evaluate non-linear transformation models for image mosaicing. It demonstrates that appearance-based metrics like NCC can improve without genuine geometric accuracy gains, providing Target Registration Error-based benchmarks for the field.

entry.title: Ananke: Contractive Torus Attractor Networks

author.name: Zhongping Ji

entry.summary: Ananke introduces a representation-learning framework scaffolding latent representations on a product-torus prior, with CTAN as a visual backbone that factors latent spaces into orthogonal 2D phase planes. It uses decoupled dual-phase continuous flow: skew-symmetric Hamiltonian transport preserves semantic phase invariants while signed gradient dissipation contracts perturbations toward invariant manifolds.

entry.title: CIG-MAE: Cross-Modal Information-Guided Masked Autoencoder for Self-Supervised WiFi Sensing

author.name: Gang Liu, Yanling Hao, Yixuan Zou

entry.summary: CIG-MAE is a cross-modal information-guided masked autoencoder for self-supervised human action recognition from WiFi channel state information, avoiding contrastive augmentations that conflict with the physical semantics of radio signals and the need for large-batch training. It targets the annotation cost and limited dataset scale that constrain supervised CSI approaches.

entry.title: Task-Aware Hybrid QUBO Optimization for Structured Neural Network Pruning

author.name: Osama Orabi, Artur Zagitov, Hadi Salloum, Viktor A. Lobachev, Yaroslav Kholodov

entry.summary: The paper casts structured filter pruning as a hybrid QUBO combinatorial optimization problem, incorporating Taylor and Weight-Fisher sensitivity into the linear objective and activation similarity into quadratic filter interactions, with a binary-search-based cardinality control avoiding explicit penalty terms.

entry.title: An Affordable AI-Integrated Smart Cane for Multimodal Mobility Assistance of Visually Impaired Users

author.name: Ali Akarma, Adeel Ahmad, Toqeer Ali Syed

entry.summary: Presents an $88 fully offline smart cane for visually impaired users built on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W, fusing RGB vision with Time-of-Flight distance sensing and an INT8-quantized SSD MobileNet V1 model to deliver vibrotactile and audio alerts. It addresses a real accessibility gap since conventional canes cannot detect elevated hazards or provide semantic context.

entry.title: OpenFlyScan: A Quality-Guided Aerial Reconstruction System for Consumer Drones

author.name: Zhongrui You, Zhen Li, Junli Liu, Zhigang Wang, Bin Zhao

entry.summary: OpenFlyScan is an integrated system for consumer-drone aerial reconstruction using 3D Gaussian Splatting, combining a learned quality model that predicts regional reconstruction quality from GS rendering errors, a reacquisition planner that generates complementary flight strips, and a mobile app. It closes the quality-feedback loop that usually requires costly equipment and post-hoc defect discovery. Practical for large-scale embodied simulation asset creation.

entry.title: HOTICE: Whole-Body Humanoid Object Transportation in Cluttered Environments

author.name: Toan Nguyen, Weiduo Yuan, Siheng Zhao, Yue Wang, Daniel Seita

entry.summary: HOTICE presents a whole-body humanoid framework for transporting objects through clutter: humanoid-object decoupled potential fields jointly encode collision avoidance for robot and payload, and a dual-agent RL architecture decouples upper- and lower-body control to handle the large action space of loco-manipulation. A practical systems contribution for a fundamental humanoid capability.

entry.title: The Cartesian Hand: In-Hand Manipulation with All-Linear Fingers

author.name: Boxi Xia, Bokuan Li, Ryan Shin, Zijiang Yang, Jiaxun Liu, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: The Cartesian Hand is a 7-DoF end-effector that combines independent grasping and relative in-hand manipulation using only linear finger motions, avoiding the mechanical and control complexity of highly articulated dexterous hands while exceeding parallel grippers. It targets articulated-object tasks like threaded containers and instruments that usually require a second gripper or external fixture. This is a novel hardware-plus-control design point in the manipulation design space.

entry.title: Situation Aware Locomotion for Dual Mobile Cobots in Shared Environments

author.name: William Moraes, Igor Nunes, Ahilen Mazondo, Sebastian Barcelona, Hiago Sodre, Pablo Moraes, Ricardo B. Grando

entry.summary: The authors propose a situation-aware locomotion framework for two mobile collaborative robots sharing an industrial workspace, modeling perception, comprehension, and projection to choose safe navigation actions. Evaluated in simulation against two baselines, the method achieved 100% task success across randomized trials.

entry.title: High-Bandwidth Biomimetic Finger for Tactile-Transparent Remote Texture Sensing

author.name: Shuang Yang, Fuyuan Liu, Yitian Shao

entry.summary: The authors build a biomimetic fingertip replicating the human finger's multilayer mechanical gradient and fingerprint morphology, with an embedded high-sensitivity IMU capturing texture-induced vibrations for remote vibrotactile rendering. Three sensor variants are compared against the human fingertip via spectral analysis and a user study across perceptual dimensions.

entry.title: Learning Air-Ground Motion Control with Temporal Mode Switching and Cross-Terrain Tracking

author.name: Ruitian Pang, Mingrui Li, Xuanting Liu, Tiancheng Lai, Juncheng Chen, Xiangyu Li, Ruibin Zhang, Qishao Wang, Jin Yu, Haiyin Piao, Fei Gao, Chao Xu, Yanjun Cao

entry.summary: This work proposes a learning-based control framework for passive-wheeled terrestrial-aerial bimodal vehicles, featuring a learned mode selector that uses single-point ToF measurements, robot states, and future reference information for autonomous air-ground switching, plus an RL policy for cross-terrain trajectory tracking. The design targets real-world deployment with limited onboard perception.

entry.title: Underwater Navigation in Unsteady Flows Using Measurement Histories from a Single Sensing Unit

author.name: Linhao Jin, Qimin Feng, Peter Gunnarson, Qiang Zhong

entry.summary: The paper shows that a causal observer can estimate current lateral velocities from a finite history of measurements from a single sensing unit, enabling underwater navigation in unsteady flows without distributed sensing. Trained only in a cylinder wake at Re=100, the observer generalizes to held-out Reynolds numbers with modest performance loss relative to full spatial sensing.

entry.title: AI: artificial immigrants

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A conceptual essay arguing that advanced AI closely mirrors the conservative framing of immigration as a societal risk: new agents entering the economy with alien values, undercutting wages with cheap labor, and gradually accumulating power over the original population, but in more extreme form. The author uses this analogy to argue AI-driven labor and power displacement deserves more serious attention.

entry.title: When talked into harm, a model blames the answer, not itself (an interpretability study of guilt vs shame)

author.name: star2vec

entry.summary: An interpretability study building on emergent misalignment: across 192 persuasion chains, a safety-trained model committed a harmful act in 109 cases, and whether a chain broke was predictable from the model's internal state at the first turn. The work explores how blame framed toward the act versus the model itself changes self-representations and subsequent behavior, with a released codebase.

entry.title: DeepFEAv2: Deep Learning for Transient Finite Element Analysis Beyond Structured Meshes

author.name: Georgios Triantafyllou, Panagiotis G. Kalozoumis, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: Extends the DeepFEA surrogate framework to transient finite element analysis over arbitrary mesh topologies and element types, enabling joint prediction of node- and element-based outputs over time where prior surrogates were limited to structured meshes or steady states. This targets real-time, high-resolution mechanical simulation at a fraction of FEA cost.

entry.title: Topological Signal Processing With Unoriented Operators

author.name: Andrea Cavallo, Varun Sarathchandran, Geert Leus, Elvin Isufi

entry.summary: The paper develops an unoriented topological signal processing (UTSP) framework that replaces oriented boundary operators with unoriented incidence matrices, appropriate for higher-order signals lacking a natural orientation. It shows these matrices admit graph-like spectral properties and introduces an unoriented alternative to the Hodge decomposition.

entry.title: Graph Domain Adaptation Does Not End with Representation Learning

author.name: Ziqian Liu, Yongxue Xu, Enze Zhang, Jiaqi Zhang, Hao Wang, Maolin Wang

entry.summary: The paper argues that existing graph domain adaptation methods stop at adapting representations via a single graph-propagating prediction path, leaving predictive evidence in the target domain unexploited. It proposes EviGDA, an evidence-augmented framework that complements graph-aware experts with graph-free local experts to handle differing failure modes under topological shifts. This reframing could improve robustness of graph transfer under combined attribute and structure shifts.

entry.title: Bridging the Data Gap: Digital Twin as a New Paradigm for AI-based Radio Sensing

author.name: \'Eloi Sainte-Beuve (Orange Research), Guillaume Larue (Orange Research), Louis-Adrien Dufr\`ene (Orange Research), Quentin Lampin (Orange Research), Ali Al Khansa (Orange Research)

entry.summary: Researchers at Orange propose using a 3D digital twin of the environment as a world model feeding a ray-tracing engine that generates large volumes of time-indexed channel impulse responses under varied scenes, weather, and layouts, from which a sequential network learns device-free localization from CIR time series. The framing treats radio sensing as an environment-conditioned learning problem rather than seeking universal models. This is a synthetic-data paradigm for scaling wireless sensing where real labeled data is scarce.

entry.title: MSA-CITE: A Co-Adapted LoRA Specialist Ecology for Fixed-Budget Small-Model Inference

author.name: Ruitong Li, Binjie Guo, Aisheng Mo, Guowei Su, Jie Li, Ru Zhang

entry.summary: MSA-CITE treats multiple discarded post-training checkpoints from a single Qwen3-4B backbone as composable assets: four frozen LoRA specialist branches each contribute one sampled completion within a fixed four-generation budget, and answers are grouped into equivalence classes scored via calibration-derived evidence. This challenges the default practice of repeatedly sampling one post-trained checkpoint. The work offers a deployment strategy for small models under fixed compute budgets.

entry.title: Penalized Nonreversible Langevin for Constrained Sampling

author.name: Pervez Ali, Weihao Dong, Xiaoyu Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Langevin sampling algorithms with squared-distance penalties and skew-symmetric drift perturbations to sample from distributions restricted to compact convex sets while preserving the penalized Gibbs distribution. It derives nonasymptotic total variation bounds under a log-Sobolev inequality and 2-Wasserstein bounds for stochastic-gradient variants. This extends constrained MCMC theory to smooth, possibly nonconvex targets.

entry.title: Optimal Tradeoffs Between Network Size and Parameter Magnitude in Neural Approximation and Minimax Regression

author.name: Baicheng Li, Zuowei Shen, Haizhao Yang, Shijun Zhang

entry.summary: Using a bounded 1-Lipschitz dyadic-triangular activation, the authors establish a sharp width-magnitude tradeoff for approximating Hoelder functions, with matching upper and lower bounds showing optimal error scales as [N^2 log(eNT)]^(-beta/d) as a function of width N and parameter bound T. The results extend to minimax regression, quantifying parameter magnitude as a complexity resource alongside network size.

entry.title: ufakzeka-1: Building and Evaluating a 151M-Parameter Turkish Language Model from Scratch

author.name: Sait Furkan Teke (ufak AI)

entry.summary: ufakzeka-1 is a 151M-parameter decoder-only Turkish language model pretrained from scratch on 13.5B openly licensed tokens and instruction-tuned for chat, at a total cost of about 286 dollars. The stated contribution is the documented process: a Turkish byte-level tokenizer, a three-stage pretraining schedule, and a release-gated evaluation battery with held-out prompts.

entry.title: Detecting GPT-Assisted Writing Using Interpretable Stylometric Features

author.name: Rajesh Kumar, Nabeel Siddiqui, Alexander Fuchsberger

entry.summary: Evaluates interpretable stylometric features for distinguishing GPT-assisted from independently authored student writing using data from 90 participants who wrote both ways, with participant-grouped validation. Random Forest reaches ROC-AUC 0.87 and F1 0.84, with SHAP analysis showing lexical and grammatical features drive predictions.

entry.title: Complementary rPPG-Derived and Lip-Region Frequency Cues for Talking-Face Deepfake Detection

author.name: Othmane Harraq, Tamer Aldwairi

entry.summary: This work studies two lightweight visual-only cues for talking-face deepfake detection: rPPG-derived waveforms from RhythmFormer and lip-region DCT coefficients, evaluated on seven generators in Celeb-DF++ under subject-independent and leave-one-generator-out protocols. Concat fusion reaches AUC 0.891 in-domain, and the cues show complementary cross-generator transfer behavior.

entry.title: Math2Visual-X: A Modular Framework for Pedagogically Aligned Lower-Primary Math Visuals Generation

author.name: H. D. E. Maduranga, S. K. Munasinghe, K. P. T. I. Weerasekara, Surangika Ranathunga, Nisansa de Silva

entry.summary: Math2Visual-X is a symbolic visual generation framework for lower-primary math word problems with an LLM-based routing layer, three worksheet-oriented generation modules, and fallback mechanisms for open-world SVG asset acquisition. Human evaluation found it outperforms Stable Diffusion XL, Nano Banana, and GPT Image on satisfying exact mathematical constraints.

entry.title: D3GS: Depth, DINO, and RGB Diffusion Co-Guided 3D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Reconstruction

author.name: Yunqi Gao, Zhanfeng Liao, Hanzhang Tu, Zhaoqi Su, Guoqing Zheng, Songtao Wang, Hongwen Zhang, Zhou Xue, Leyuan Liu, Yebin Liu

entry.summary: D3GS improves sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting by jointly enhancing geometry and appearance: diffusion-based depth completion with DPT refinement provides robust Gaussian initialization and geometric constraints, while DINO-guided view-consistent learning augments Gaussian attributes with structural features.

entry.title: Adaptive Cortically Constrained EEG-Vision Alignment for Zero-Shot Brain-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Ye Wang, Haokun Ren, Wei Wu, Guoyin Wang, Zhuliang Yu, Hong Yu, Ke Liu

entry.summary: This work reconstructs noisy scalp EEG responses into ROI-level cortical source representations and encodes them with a Neuro-ROI Attention Encoder for zero-shot brain-to-image retrieval. An evidence-based adaptive supervision strategy weights visual targets per response, addressing variability in alignment reliability that fixed visual supervision ignores.

entry.title: MIGA:Shared-Geometry Gaussian Representation with Implicit Amplitude Modeling for Accelerated 3D Multi-Echo MRI

author.name: Jingran Xu, Yuanyuan Liu, Yanjie Zhu

entry.summary: MIGA is a scan-specific framework for reconstructing undersampled 3D multi-echo MRI using shared anisotropic Gaussian geometry across echoes, a coordinate-conditioned multi-output amplitude network, and echo-specific phase variables. It exploits shared anatomy while preserving echo-dependent signal variation with reduced computational and memory demands. This addresses a real clinical bottleneck of long acquisition times.

entry.title: 0.5%>100%: Bidirectional Reciprocal Learning for Referring Image Segmentation

author.name: Xiaoqiang Lu, Licheng Jiao, Lingling Li, Yuting Yang, Long Sun, Wenping Ma, Xu Liu, Fang Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes bidirectional reciprocal learning for referring image segmentation, enabling progressive cross-modal interaction and visual feedback for textual refinement within a parameter-efficient fine-tuning setting for vision foundation models. It avoids full fine-tuning costs and catastrophic forgetting while going beyond unidirectional language-to-vision guidance. The catchy title refers to achieving strong gains with only 0.5% trainable parameters.

entry.title: Multicentre Bi-atrial Segmentation from LGE-MRI for Atrial Fibrillation with a 2D and 3D Framework

author.name: Malitha Gunawardhana, Gregory B. Sands, Mark L. Trew, Jichao Zhao

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage segmentation framework and benchmarking platform for bi-atrial wall and cavity delineation in multicentre late gadolinium enhancement MRI, systematically evaluating ROI localization, encoder design, 2D vs 3D dimensionality, and ensemble fusion. Targets a prerequisite for structural analysis and fibrosis quantification in atrial fibrillation.

entry.title: What is the Better Curriculum: Controller-Shaped Grasping Behavior for Contact Force-Sensitive Manipulation

author.name: Ziyan Feng, Zizhao Yuan, Yulong Fu, Yuxin He, Zhiyuan Zhang, Zhengjie Zhang, Jinni Zhou, Renjing Xu, Qiang Nie

entry.summary: For manipulating fragile objects where sub-Newton forces cause damage, this work argues the bottleneck occurs during data collection, where manual teleoperation is too coarse to stay in narrow force ranges. It uses a deterministic 25 Hz tactile reflex controller as a collection-time teacher, producing controller-shaped demonstrations from which tactile-free policies (on ACT) can be trained. This reframes curriculum design as shaping demonstration quality rather than adding tactile inputs to the policy.

entry.title: MatchFusion: Explicit-Implicit Instance Matching for Spatio-Temporal Multimodal Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Jiajia Fu, Long Shi, Tianyu Du, Ruihang Li, Xian Wu, Lijun Zhao, Yingtao Zhang, Lining Sun, Ruifeng Li

entry.summary: MatchFusion is a learnable instance matching and fusion module for spatio-temporal multimodal autonomous driving that combines attention-based contextual matching with efficient, interpretable matching based on structured object states. It targets reliable instance correspondences across LiDAR-camera and temporal dimensions despite geometric and semantic discrepancies.

entry.title: LingLan: An Advancing Traditional Chinese Medicine Diagnosis LLM with Multimodal Data

author.name: Zheng Chen, Zhicheng Du, Haoxuan Li, Yingshan Liang, Peiwu Qin

entry.summary: Introduces a Unification Framework for Multimodal Data that converts tongue and pulse images into structured clinical descriptions spanning the four TCM diagnostic processes, and builds LingLan-14B, a TCM-specific large language model on this structured data. Aims to bridge subjective holistic diagnostics with standardized AI systems.

entry.title: Not Quite My Tempo: Voice Activity-aware Speech Synthesis for Lip-Synchronous Dubbing

author.name: Alejandro P\'erez-Gonz\'alez-de-Martos, Florian Lux, Angelina Elizarova, Milana Shkhanukova, Andreas Kellner, Mattia Antonino Di Gangi

entry.summary: Conditions speech synthesis for lip-synchronous dubbing on a binary voice-activity signal rather than lip movements extracted from video, generating alternating voice and silence patterns matching the source clip timing. The approach achieves high timing accuracy while preserving natural prosody and appropriate pause placement, validated via objective and subjective evaluation.

entry.title: The Disciplinary Language Transfer Problem: How Psychological Vocabulary Produces Governance Failures in AI Agent Deployment

author.name: Kymberly Lasser-Chere, Tyler Akidau, Marc Millstone

entry.summary: Argues that governance discourse about AI agents borrows psychological vocabulary (memory, values, trust, compliance) that imports an invisible disciplinary grammar, calibrating frameworks to a metaphysical entity absent from current AI architectures, causing systematic deployment and oversight failures. The authors ground the argument in Wittgenstein, Kuhn, and Haraway and name this the disciplinary language transfer problem.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Kronecker Covariance Neural Networks

author.name: Andrea Cavallo, Athanasios Georgoutsos, Elvin Isufi

entry.summary: KVNN is a temporal graph neural network that represents spatiotemporal covariance matrices as sums of Kronecker products, decoupling spatial and temporal dependencies while capturing correlations across time steps. It improves on spatiotemporal PCA and existing covariance-based networks that ignore cross-time correlations.

entry.title: AURA: Angular Update Rate Adaptation for training complex-valued neural networks

author.name: Enrico Ballini, Allan Peter Engsig-Karup, Tito Andriollo

entry.summary: AURA is a per-parameter step-size adaptation method for complex-valued neural networks that exploits angular information in the complex plane, measuring agreement between consecutive updates in length, alignment, and rotation sense. It can be added on top of any first-order optimizer without altering update directions and removed cleanly afterward. This fills a real gap, as CVNNs typically inherit real-valued step-size heuristics that ignore complex geometry.

entry.title: Learnable Classifier-Free Guidance Null Embeddings for Enhanced Controllable Speech Synthesis

author.name: Biel Tura Vecino, Yoach Lacombe, Julian Weber, Zbigniew {\L}atka, Haitong Zhang, Logan Hart, Eren G\"olge

entry.summary: The authors replace the fixed null vector used for unconditional predictions in classifier-free guidance for TTS with a learnable unconditional embedding optimized to represent a meaningful unconditional state. Objective and subjective evaluations show consistent gains in speaker similarity, stability, and expressiveness, plus robustness to larger guidance scales. This is a simple, broadly applicable tweak to CFG-based generative audio systems.

entry.title: Unlocking Cross-Scenario Physical Layer Security: A Mixture-of-Experts Framework with Generative Diffusion Models

author.name: Xiao Tang, Tong Hui, Chao Shen, Yichen Wang, Qinghe Du, Li Sun, Zhu Han

entry.summary: The paper proposes a mixture-of-experts framework for cross-scenario physical-layer security in anticipated 6G networks, training scenario-specific generative diffusion model experts for secure transmission beamforming with adaptive routing among experts. The goal is robust security provisioning across diverse wireless environments without full recomputation per scenario.

entry.title: Retrieved-Span Training for Efficient Query-Focused Meeting Summarization on QMSum

author.name: Edward Xi Yang (Ertas AI)

entry.summary: The paper rescores or generates 15 systems under one implementation to address QMSum's lack of a shared scorer, and shows that a released 406M Fusion-in-Decoder specialist loses 6.30 ROUGE-1 when moved to 2,000-word retrieved spans but recovers with span-regime fine-tuning. The resulting small system statistically ties a 1.2B system while using about one-third the parameters and less than half the peak inference memory.

entry.title: Challenges of Multi-Speaker Extraction for Real Conversational Speech Enhancement

author.name: Robert Sutherland, Stefan Goetze, Jon Barker

entry.summary: This work examines the gap between simulated training conditions and real multi-party conversations for target/multi-speaker extraction, noting that real conversations feature long silences and enrolment samples that differ from target speech. The authors propose a new loss function to better handle these real-world conditions.

entry.title: Combining Foundation Model Confidence and Monocular Depth for Training-Free Out-of-Distribution Segmentation
