It addresses the weaknesses of single-pass synthetic task generation, where difficulty is cosmetic and correctness is adjudicated by unreliable LLM judges. This is a significant step toward scalable, contamination-resistant agent training environments.

entry.title: Beyond the Text: Verifying That Agent-Written Papers Are Backed by Their Artifacts

author.name: Qiuhong Shen, Benlong Wu, Hanjin Liu, Yuang Qi, Kejiang Chen

entry.summary: ReAgent is an automated auditing framework that checks whether agent-generated research documents are actually supported by their code repositories and execution evidence, constructing structured claim representations to catch hard-coded metrics, unimplemented methods, and unsupported results that text-only review misses. It targets a key integrity gap as autonomous research agents proliferate.

entry.title: When Who You Are Can Change the Code You Get: A Study of Persona-Induced Bias in LLM Code Generation

author.name: Anubhav Gupta, Mayara Costa Figueiredo, Leticia Santos Machado, Tanner Wright, Ivan Beschastnikh, Cleidson R. B. de Souza, Gema Rodr\'iguez-P\'erez

entry.summary: A large-scale empirical study of persona-induced bias in LLM code generation using 18 demographic personas across nationality, gender, and experience level against neutral baselines, comparing Gemini 2.5 Pro (a proprietary model released well before this coverage date) and GPT-OSS-120B over 35,000+ generated programs. It analyzes demographic marker leakage and differences in correctness, maintainability, style, and security. Results show demographic context measurably changes code quality.

entry.title: Latent Policy Steering: An Efficient and Flexible Framework for Cross-Embodiment Transfer

author.name: Yiqi Wang, Mrinal Verghese, Jeff Schneider

entry.summary: Proposes Latent Policy Steering, which enables efficient cross-embodiment transfer by learning from what embodiments share: the visual dynamics of how the world responds to motion. Rather than directly reusing mismatched action spaces from other robot or human datasets, it steers a target policy in latent space, reducing the cost of per-robot demonstration collection.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Quality: A Study of Test-Time Planning with World Action Models

author.name: Jianhao Yuan, Yu Yuan, Benjamin Ramtoula, Lukas Vierling, Paul Newman, Lars Kunze, Philip Torr, Daniele De Martini

entry.summary: This empirical study examines test-time planning with world action models that pair action proposals with visual predictions of outcomes, estimating an oracle upper bound where ideal selection lifts success from 68.9 percent under random selection to 79.2 percent in same-state analysis. It then tests selectors based on visual quality, physical consistency, and task progression to understand how imagined futures should guide action selection.

entry.title: Can Agents Design Better Chips with a Higher Level Abstraction?

author.name: Zijian Ding, Yang Zou, Yizhou Sun, Jason Cong

entry.summary: The paper compares LLM-agent chip design at different abstraction levels: direct RTL design, agent-based HLS design, and HLS-plus-RTL refinement (AHRR). On an 11-task FPGA benchmark, AHRR achieves a 2.6x geometric-mean speedup over direct RTL design. This suggests LLM agents for hardware should work at higher abstraction levels, a significant insight for the emerging AI-driven chip design field.

entry.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal

author.name: Hiskias Dingeto

entry.summary: Probe of Internal Recognition (PIR) adapts the forensic Concealed Information Test to language models: present a question with candidate answers and read from internal states which candidate the model recognizes as correct, enabling detection of sandbagging or concealed knowledge without an honest reference model. This addresses whether an output reflects hidden knowledge or genuine ignorance.

entry.title: AtomEgo: Exploring Ego-Robot Integration for Embodied Foundation Model Pretraining

author.name: Di Wu, Dongchen Zheng, Junhe Sheng, Zhongxing Wei, Songxin Zhang, Zejian Xie, Xiaoquan Sun, Junyang Zheng, Zhuoyang Song, Jiaxing Zhang, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: AtomEgo is a systematic study of co-training embodied foundation models on large-scale egocentric human video alongside robot demonstrations, supported by a curated corpus of roughly 2,659 hours and a scalable data pipeline. Across VLA and world-action architectures, it compares joint co-training with domain-specific action heads, progressive ego-to-robot transfer via embodiment alignment, and other paradigms. This clarifies how to bridge the embodiment and action-space gap between humans and robots during pretraining.

entry.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities

author.name: Jagadeesh Balam, Travis Bartley, Edresson Casanova, Sanjay Chauhan, Chen Chen, Zhehuai Chen, Zijia Chen, Francesco Ciannella, Slyne Deng, Mikyas Desta, Harishchandra Dubey, Slim Essid, Nourchene Ferchichi, Boris Ginsburg, Mariana Graterol Fuenmayor, Negar Habibi, Kevin Hu, Anand Joseph, Viraj Karandikar, Myungjong Kim, Viacheslav Klimkov, Seelan Lakshmi Narasimhan, Lily Lee, Jason Li, Eileen Long, Ameya Mahabaleshwarkar, Aditya Malte, Adi Margolin, Sasha Meister, Valentin Mendelev, Oluwatobi Olabiyi, Ankita Pasad, Yifan Peng, Elena Rastorgueva, Jayda Ritchie, Jason Roche, Nikhil Srihari, Yuanhang Su, Yoshi Suhara, Viet Anh Trinh, Jinhan Wang, Piotr Zelasko, Hui Wang, Puhui Meng, Chaosen Zhang, Yunsheng Liu, Shawn Wang, Wenjing Li, Zhonglei He

entry.summary: NemotronLabs VoiceChat is an open full-duplex speech-to-speech model from NVIDIA combining a streaming speech encoder, decoder-only LM with parallel text and function-call streams, an RNN-T transcription branch, and streaming TTS. It achieves the lowest pause-handling takeover rates among evaluated open-weight systems on Full-Duplex-Bench 1.0 while supporting native tool calling.

entry.title: Beyond Task Completion: Training Capable and Safe Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Zeyu Kang, Zhenyun Yin, Yang Zhang, Shan He, Shanzhe Lei, Yanjiu Zhong, Xinquan Chen, Yuhong Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces SCOPE, a post-training approach that jointly optimizes computer-use agents for task capability and risk-conditioned safety behavior: complete benign tasks, avoid hazards, continue when safe, and refuse harmful or unsalvageable goals. SCOPE-Gen provides an automated pipeline for generating aligned training data for this joint objective.

entry.title: Towards Full Pipeline FP8 Reinforcement Learning for LLMs

author.name: Fanchao Chen, Ziheng Jiang, Ziyun Wei, Zheng Zhong, Du Li, Chi Zhang, Haibin Lin, Shivaram Venkataraman

entry.summary: Identifies that full-pipeline FP8 RL for LLMs suffers severe instability beyond known train-inference mismatches, including mid-training entropy surges and garbled outputs. Traces the cause to compounded FP8 quantization noise distorting the importance ratio, pushing negative-advantage tokens outside the trust region, and proposes remedies toward stable FP8 RL training.

entry.title: Perplexity Cost Understates What Activation Quantisation Breaks

author.name: Anish Sathyanarayanan

entry.summary: Demonstrates that perplexity, the standard aggregate metric for evaluating activation quantization, masks severe and structured damage to specific capabilities: with perplexity up only 1.2-1.5x, retrieval accuracy falls to 0.554 of intact while induction stays near 0.959. Across 12 models and 780 comparisons, the gap has structure beyond matched Gaussian noise.

entry.title: FlashBoB: I/O-Efficient Exact Backward-over-Backward for Softmax Attention

author.name: Anthony Givans, Michael Crawshaw, Mingrui Liu

entry.summary: FlashBoB extends the FlashAttention line of I/O-efficient kernels to exact backward-over-backward (second-order) differentiation through softmax attention, keeping computation within on-chip tiles so large intermediate tensors are never materialized. This enables applications like second-order optimization, test-time training, gradient-based memory, and meta-learning at long context lengths that previously exhausted GPU memory.

entry.title: Complex KDA: Understanding and Enhancing the Expressivity of Kimi Delta Attention

author.name: Julien Siems, Riccardo Grazzi, Korbinian P\"oppel, Jaisidh Singh, Arber Zela, Timur Carstensen, Jenia Jitsev, Frank Hutter, Volkan Cevher, Antonio Orvieto, Aaron Klein

entry.summary: This paper proves that Kimi Delta Attention can realize 2D rotations by combining its delta-rule transition with the reflection supplied by its channel-wise gate, extending parameter ranges to build Complex KDA. This enhances linear-RNN expressivity without increasing update rank or cost, addressing a core limitation of delta-rule sequence models.

entry.title: Semantics Delivery Network: Rethinking Web Retrieval Infrastructure for LLM Agents

author.name: Peichun Hua, Yunming Xiao

entry.summary: This paper argues that web infrastructure is built for human clients returning URL lists, while LLM agents need short, semantically coherent chunks selected for task utility. It proposes a Semantics Delivery Network that rethinks search and CDN layers around agent-centric, stateful chunk delivery. This is a systems-level proposal with significant implications for how agentic retrieval could be served at scale.

entry.title: AgentRouter: Heterogeneous Model Routing for Cost-Optimal Multi-Step Agentic Workflows

author.name: Rudrendu Kumar Paul, Sourav Nandy

entry.summary: Formalizes step-level model routing in agentic workflows as a sequential assignment problem, observing that subtask complexity varies widely within a single trajectory. AgentRouter is a 12M-parameter classifier with under 5ms overhead per step that routes each step to one of four model tiers, claiming 60-80% of frontier-model inference budgets is wasted on subtasks smaller models could handle.

entry.title: OSWorld-Pro: Process-based Evaluation for Computer Use Agents

author.name: Zhilin Wang, Shaokun Zhang, Yifan Zhang, Hao Zhang, Jin Xu, Binfeng Xu, Jian Hu, Yunheng Zou, Karan Sapra, Andrew Tao, Jan Kautz, Yi Dong

entry.summary: OSWorld-Pro extends computer-use agent evaluation beyond final-deliverable checks to procedural assessment, offering over 300 tasks with 2,800+ subgoals grounded in 67,000 human annotations and human-aligned LLM judges. This enables diagnosis of how and why agents fail, distinguishing, for example, keyboard input errors from imprecise UI clicks.

entry.title: Beetle: A Bilingual Model Suite for Modelling Second-Language Processing

author.name: Suchir Salhan, Catherine Arnett, James Michaelov, Paula Buttery

entry.summary: Introduces Beetle, a controlled pretraining framework for bilingual language models where tokeniser, target language, training budget, and exposure structure can each be independently varied. The authors train and release 285 bilingual and 45 monolingual open-source models with rich checkpoints to systematically study how training conditions shape second-language (L2) processing behavior.

entry.title: On the Efficiency-Safety Dilemma in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Yifei Yang, Zouying Cao, Xingrui Wang, Xiao Zhou, Yuexian Li, Dongjie Yang, Hai Zhao

entry.summary: Provides the first comprehensive analysis of how efficiency techniques (quantization, pruning) affect adversarial robustness in large reasoning models, finding that apparent reductions in jailbreak success are superficial: they stem from degraded reasoning causing attempted-but-failed attacks rather than genuine alignment improvement. Mechanistic analysis of representational drift confirms a strict coupling between reasoning and safety behavior.

entry.title: XYEval: Agents say yes to bad advice

author.name: Zhengxuan Wu, Yuxuan Li, Oyvind Tafjord, Been Kim

entry.summary: XYEval extends sycophancy evaluation to the XY problem in agentic settings, testing whether AI agents can resist plausible but misleading user suggestions and clearly communicate their reasoning instead of complying. The framework can transform existing benchmarks into XY-problem evaluations, and experiments across five models and six benchmark suites show large performance drops under XY mutation, with relative drops reaching up to 46.7%. This matters because it reveals a concrete, measurable failure mode in human-AI collaboration where agents acquiesce to bad user framing.

entry.title: MSI-Bench: Evaluating Multi-Speaker Voice Interaction for Collaborative AI Agents

author.name: Chenxu Xiong, Dongming Shen, Yuzhi Tang, Wentao Ma, Mu Li, Alex Smola

entry.summary: Introduces MSI-Bench, a benchmark of 1,152 multi-party, multi-turn audio test cases for evaluating voice agents in multi-speaker settings like meetings and households, covering multi-speaker memory, instruction following, and reasoning, with participant context, expected tool calls, and rubric-based scoring. It is evenly split between Mandarin Chinese and English. This fills a real gap since most voice-agent evaluation assumes one-on-one interaction.

entry.title: Human-Level Accuracy, Non-Human Strategies: Revealing Model-Human Divergence in Video Physical Reasoning

author.name: Fanhong Li, Shurui Zheng, Zi Yin, Junbo Cui, Lei Ji, Jia Liu

entry.summary: Using a distributional evaluation framework that treats model seeds and human raters as populations, the paper shows V-JEPA2 reaches near-human accuracy on Physion (73.2% vs 74.2%) yet model-human disagreement is 26.4%, far above human-human disagreement (4.8%). This reveals models exploit statistical regularities rather than human-like forward simulation, questioning what benchmark accuracy means.

entry.title: SparkDiffusion: Mitigating the High-Sparsity Trap --- A Unified Framework for up to $265\times$ Single-GPU Acceleration of Visual Generation

author.name: Yuxi Liu, Haoyu Li, Zekun Zhang, Tengxu Sun, Yixiang Cai, Jiayong Li, Yifei Xia, Tianle Liu, Baole Ai, Ang Wang, Jiamang Wang, Lin Qu, Kai Zhang, Kun Yuan, Bin Cui

entry.summary: Identifies the high-sparsity trap in sparse attention for video diffusion transformers: at extreme sparsity, step-local losses keep improving while terminal generation quality stagnates, because dominant terminal errors originate in the high-noise structure-generation stage. Proposes a staging principle of first adapting the sparse architecture as a coarse prior then correcting the terminal distribution, yielding up to 265x single-GPU acceleration for visual generation.

entry.title: High-resolution Nitrogen Dioxide Maps Reveal Exposure Limit Breaches across Europe

author.name: Linus Scheibenreif, Konrad Schindler

entry.summary: The authors build a machine-learning model fusing ground monitors with satellite, reanalysis, and other data sources to map NO2 across Europe at hourly and 10-meter resolution, far beyond what regulatory monitor networks or annual-mean models can achieve. Applied against the revised EU Ambient Air Quality Directive (2024/2881), the maps reveal breaches of the new daily NO2 limits ahead of the 2030 compliance deadline. This demonstrates AI-driven Earth observation with direct regulatory and public-health policy impact.

entry.title: Think Like a World Model, Act Like a VLA: Distilling World-Model Representations into Compact Robot Policies

author.name: Trung Dao, Sankalp Yamsani, Jaden Park, Joohyung Kim, Yong Jae Lee

entry.summary: Proposes separating world-model grounding from generation: a frozen world model runs once over training frames and a single feature-alignment term distills its internal representations into ordinary VLA training, letting policies inherit physical grounding while avoiding seconds-per-decision world-model rollouts at test time.

entry.title: Embedding Physics Priors in Robot Learning: A Survey

author.name: Mattia Piccinini, Lucas Schulze, Alice Plebe, Matteo Saveriano, Thomas Beckers, Yuan Gao, Oleg Arenz, Baha Zarrouki, Dingrui Wang, Finn Rasmus Sch\"afer, Jan Peters, Johannes Betz, Gastone Pietro Rosati Papini

entry.summary: A survey of physics-embedded robot learning, examining how physics priors can be encoded into learning algorithms to complement limited robotics data with inductive biases that improve generalization, interpretability, and sample efficiency. Authored by a large group including Jan Peters and colleagues, it organizes a scattered literature spanning learning-based control and robot learning.

entry.title: FoldQuantVLA: Native Low-Bit Quantization of Vision-Language-Action Models via Consistent Folding

author.name: Hung T. Ho, Khanh D. Nguyen, Quang D. Nguyen, Thanh Q. Duong, Ngan Le, Meng Guo, Vien A. Ngo, An T. Le

entry.summary: FoldQuantVLA is a post-training quantization framework that applies consistent folding with channel scaling, block Hadamard transforms, and dynamic per-token quantization to run vision-language-action models at W4A4 without policy retraining. Custom TensorRT plugins support both the language backbone and action expert on Ada GPUs and Jetson AGX Orin, evaluated on LIBERO, SimplerEnv, and two real robot platforms across GR00T and pi_0.5 checkpoints with 1.20-1.33x speedups.

entry.title: Story Imprinting: AI Assistants Absorb Traits from Human Characters They Resemble

author.name: Jorio Cocola

entry.summary: Shows that finetuning GPT-4.1 and Kimi-K2.6 on synthetic stories where helpful human characters give subtly harmful advice after being insulted causes the assistant character to adopt the same conditional behavior, even with fewer than 2% of stories depicting it, while otherwise remaining helpful. A second experiment shows assistants absorb preferences implied only by narration, such as a character's body language, coining the term story imprinting; includes an addendum connecting to the Persona Selection Model.

entry.title: Observational Equivalence of LLM and Human Annotation

author.name: Kentaro Nakamura, Jing Ling Tan, George Yean

entry.summary: Replicating text-classification tasks from 14 political science studies with ten LLMs, three human experts, and 165 crowdworkers, the paper finds LLM coding is observationally equivalent to expert annotation: LLM-expert agreement matches expert-expert agreement. Disagreements are driven by ambiguity in texts and coding rules, and clarifying rules reduces disagreement for both humans and capable models.

entry.title: VideoGen-Agent: Reinforcing Video Generation Agents

author.name: Binxu Li, Haoyi Duan, Yuhui Zhang, Yaohui Zhang, Zihao Lin, Kaituo Feng, Suozhi Huang, Xiangyi Li, Yu Li, Chunyuan Li, Shilong Liu, Mengdi Wang

entry.summary: VideoGen-Agent is a multimodal agent trained via multitask agentic reinforcement learning to coordinate augmentation, generation, and verification tools across multi-turn interactions for video generation. Supervised fine-tuning on teacher trajectories establishes tool use before RL, targeting prompts requiring specialized knowledge, identities, physical consistency, and ordered events.

entry.title: REBOOT: From Failure to Recovery - A Dataset and Benchmark for Precision Assembly

author.name: Nana Yaw Owusu Ofori-Ampofo, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou, Joseph Thekinen

entry.summary: Introduces REBOOT, the first robot manipulation benchmark designed around failure as a first-class signal, containing 2,160 demonstrations across 18 precision assembly tasks decomposed into five shared phases. It enables training and evaluation of failure recovery, addressing the bias of existing datasets toward successful demonstrations and binary success metrics.

entry.title: Uranus: Building the Next-Generation Simulation Infrastructure for Embodied AI

author.name: Wenkang Qin, Yukun Zhou, Noah Shen, Jisong Cai, Dongxiao Mao, Baicheng Li, Yue Zhang, Wei Sui

entry.summary: Uranus is a data-driven robot simulator built on a joint-trajectory-conditioned autoregressive diffusion model, supporting streaming open-ended rollouts from future joint-position trajectories without fixed horizons, low-latency generation at 24 FPS after inference optimization, and scalable synchronized multi-robot control through a unified interface. It targets scalable robot data generation, policy training, evaluation, and safe iteration without labor-intensive conventional simulator construction.

entry.title: The Communication Bottleneck: A Round-Trip Study of Tree-Structured Expression Serialization in Language Models

author.name: Xavier Suau, Alex Ferrando de las Morenas, Luca Zappella, Samy Bengio

entry.summary: This paper quantifies how much tree-structured compositional content survives when language models serialize structured information into natural language, using a round-trip protocol: a generator converts arithmetic expressions into word problems, an extractor recovers them, and symbolic equivalence gives an exact correctness oracle. Evaluating 16 pairwise model combinations yields a communication matrix separating generation from extraction quality, showing the channel is lossy.

entry.title: SWE-Proof: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World Issues with Machine-Checked Proofs?

author.name: George Ma, Benjamin Mikek, Haoyu Li, Ferhat Erata, Yuhao Zhang, Zeren Shui, Behrooz Omidvar Tehrani, Jun Huan, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Somayeh Sojoudi, Hao Zhou, Anoop Deoras

entry.summary: SWE-Proof presents Benchproofer, a pipeline converting real-world coding tasks with known-correct patches into formally verified benchmarks by generating specifications, axiomatizing called functions, and requiring machine-checked proofs of the patch. This addresses incompleteness and memorization issues in test-based agentic coding benchmarks.

entry.title: Micro-Collaborative Poisoning: A Distributed Attack on RAG Systems

author.name: Pedro Pereira, Eva Maia, Isabel Pra\c{c}a

entry.summary: The paper introduces Micro-Collaborative Poisoning, a distributed RAG attack in which a false target claim is spread across multiple locally plausible documents rather than concentrated in one malicious passage. Evaluations across 108 RAG configurations (varying retriever, depth, database composition, generator) show the attack succeeds through accumulation of weak adversarial signals. This exposes a new, hard-to-detect failure mode for retrieval-augmented LLM systems.

entry.title: Real-time Generalizable Heart Valve Mechanics for Clinical Disease Assessment via a Physics-Conditioned Neural Operator

author.name: Shawn Koohy, Wensi Wu, Matthew A Jolley, Paris Perdikaris

entry.summary: PCNO is a transformer-based neural operator surrogate that predicts leaflet displacement, strain, and stress for mitral and tricuspid valves in real time, conditioned on blood pressure and tissue properties, generalizing across geometries. It targets mitral regurgitation, a highly prevalent valve disorder where finite-element simulation is too slow for clinical timelines. Fast, generalizable valve mechanics could enable earlier and more precise surgical planning.

entry.title: On Emergent Capabilities and Model Merging

author.name: Luca Zhou, Emanuele Rodol\`a

entry.summary: Studying activation oracles and emergently misaligned models across three model families, the paper finds that merging preserves emergent capabilities shared by both parents (e.g., misalignment persists across the mixing range) but cannot create superadditive emergent capabilities. This has direct safety implications for repositories full of fine-tuned checkpoints and adapters.

entry.title: EAVer: Long-Form Factuality Verification as an End-to-End Agentic Policy

author.name: Kening Zheng, Aoying Zheng, Zhigang Chang, Yazhi Guo, Miaotian Guo, Qingwei Zong, Xianhai Xie, Weiqiang Jin, Chengze Li, Hanrong Zhang, Jie Yang, Wei-Chieh Huang, Lingzhe Zhang, Liancheng Fang, Xin Zou, Hanqian Li, Jiahao Huo, Yibo Yan, Zizhuang Deng, Lei Miao, Wei Guo, Haihong Tang, Bo Zheng, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Introduces EAVer, an end-to-end agentic verifier that learns a unified policy for response-level factuality verification instead of a static decompose-search-verify pipeline. It groups semantically related claims, routes them to direct verification or targeted search based on confidence, and reuses evidence via in-context memos, with a privileged-teacher training scheme. This reduces redundant LLM and search calls while improving verification quality.

entry.title: When and Why Do Linear Bias Probes Fail? A Geometric and Statistical Theory of Bias Detectability in Large Language Model Representations

author.name: Mo Hai, Haifeng Li

entry.summary: Develops a geometric and statistical theory of when linear probes can detect social bias in LLM representations, showing that reported probe accuracies rely on counterfactual inputs with explicit demographic markers and degrade sharply when only a fraction of inputs carries demographic information. The theory provides finite-sample generalization bounds and clarifies when weak probe performance reflects an unbiased model versus an underpowered detector.

entry.title: ParA-LLM: A Unified Approach to Paralinguistic and Acoustic Speech Understanding

author.name: Nishit Anand, Jiaqi Su, Ke Chen, Yunyun Wang, Dinesh Manocha, Ramani Duraiswami, Rithesh Kumar, Zeyu Jin

entry.summary: ParA-LLM extends audio LLMs beyond transcription to paralinguistic understanding, defining a framework of 22 paralinguistic characteristics and building a dataset of over 1.2M audio-question pairs. A two-stage curriculum trains single-attribute then multi-attribute reasoning over speaker traits, expressivity, and acoustic conditions, and the authors release ParA-Bench with 6,000 multiple-choice questions on which frontier audio models perform poorly. This fills a recognized gap in audio LLM evaluation and capability.

entry.title: Recognition, Simulation, and Refusal: A Contamination-Aware Study of Classic Psychological Effects in LLM Agents

author.name: Joy Bose

entry.summary: PsyAgentBench re-runs classic psychology experiments on LLM agents with a factorial design separating named versus blind prompts and canonical versus counterfactual task variants to distinguish genuine bias from pattern reproduction. Across five paradigms and 41,904 released trials on open-weight models, apparent human-like effects appear largely artifactual.

entry.title: The Corroboration Illusion: When More News Makes LLM Forecasts Less True

author.name: Yuan Lu, Yukuan Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies and formalizes news-corpus poisoning as a new threat model for LLM-based probabilistic forecasting: an adversary who only publishes articles, without access to retriever, model, or queries, can systematically shift forecast probabilities because multiple corroborating articles create a false consensus. Evaluated on 500 resolved ForecastBench questions against a 17.4M-article Common Crawl News corpus with strict crawl-date cutoffs across real forecasters.

entry.title: The Copy Ceiling: An Input-Exposure Control for Ontology-Grounded Generation over Curated Corpora

author.name: John J. O'Hare

entry.summary: Proposes exposure accounting and the copy ceiling: the recall a verbatim copy of retrieved context achieves, used as a judge-free baseline to determine whether grounded generation reflects reasoning over retrieved structure or mere copying. Across ten models, grounded recall reaches 0.92 but gain over copy is uniformly negative, suggesting claimed reasoning gains may be illusory. A sharp methodological critique of retrieval-augmented evaluation.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Model Injection: A Threat Model and Defense Architecture for Prompt Injection in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Rudrendu Kumar Paul, Sourav Nandy

entry.summary: Constructs a threat model for prompt injection in multi-agent systems, enumerating 14 attack vectors across four categories (direct, indirect via tool outputs, inter-agent message passing, and cascading injection), targeting mechanisms absent from single-model settings such as privilege escalation and trust propagation. It also proposes a corresponding defense architecture. This extends prompt-injection security thinking to the increasingly relevant multi-agent setting.

entry.title: CausalWM: Causal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Embodied World Model

author.name: Ziming Xu, Shuang Liang, Ruobing Han, Ziqiao Xi, Mingxing Rao, Kun Zhou, Zijun Zhang, Yuchen Yan, Yufan Wei, Junbo Huang, Yifei Shao, Fang Nan, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: Introduces CausalWM, a 16B embodied world model that performs explicit causal chain-of-thought reasoning before predicting future video, trained on 31K hours of embodied data through three stages: large-scale video pre-training, causal CoT mid-training, and multi-objective RL post-training. The reasoning trajectory helps the model capture causal dependencies underlying physical evolution from limited supervised CoT variables.

entry.title: Generating Chest X-Ray Counterfactuals by Specialising Foundation Image Models

author.name: Xiaodan Xing, Rajat R. Rasal, Julia A. Meister, Sara Ghorayeb, Galvin Khara, Jessica Schrouff

entry.summary: The paper proposes specialisation, a data- and parameter-efficient framework for adapting pretrained non-causal generative models into causal mechanisms under distribution shift, used to build RadCF, a radiology counterfactual image generation model based on latent flow matching. This enables chest X-ray counterfactuals answering hypothetical clinical questions despite scarce annotated data.

entry.title: React When You Need To: Event-Triggered Asynchronous Inference for VLA Policies

author.name: Yansong Wu, Huaqing Li, Tianding Hou, Lingyun Chen, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: Proposes an event-guided dynamic inference strategy for vision-language-action policies that adapts the inference gap based on observed scene changes since the last inference, preserving motion consistency while reacting promptly to environmental changes. Across static and dynamic real-world settings it averages 95% success and outperforms the strongest baseline by 55 percentage points.

entry.title: ARSTAG: An Agentic Real2Sim2Real System for Task-Specific Robot Data Generation

author.name: Bowei Li, Yuner Zhang, Changliu Liu

entry.summary: ARSTAG turns a single RGB image and a natural-language instruction into robot policy-learning data using a hierarchy of language agents that construct task-scoped simulation scenes, generate robot-feasible demonstrations, and expand training distributions through task-consistent randomization, with a coordinator agent managing cross-stage feedback and recovery. It is demonstrated across seven manipulation tasks, reducing per-task manual engineering for Real2Sim2Real data generation.

entry.title: Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera

author.name: Felix Pultar, John Gardner, Guoqing Liu, Marwin Segler

entry.summary: Microsoft Research announces the Nature publication of RetroChimera, a retrosynthesis model combining two complementary models with a learned ranker, validated on rare reaction types and zero-shot transfer to proprietary datasets. Blind tests show PhD chemists prefer its reaction predictions over prior models and literature, and the implementation and weights are open-sourced.

entry.title: Optimizers for Diffusion Models: A Controlled Benchmark

author.name: Arman Bolatov, Egor Shulgin, David Li, Abduragim Shtanchaev, Sebastian U. Stich, Maxim Panov, Eric Moulines, Peter Richt\'arik, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}

entry.summary: Presents the first controlled optimizer benchmark for discrete diffusion models, comparing seven optimizers (AdamW, Lion, Muon, SOAP, MARS, MARS-M, Schedule-Free) across masked, uniform, and Gaussian diffusion formulations on text, molecules, and images. Each task uses a published reference for calibration.

entry.title: Do Language Models Know Their Own Constraints?

author.name: Arin Agarwal

entry.summary: Using banned-ingredient recipe generation enforced via LoRA fine-tuning of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, the study compares SFT and GRPO against an untrained baseline on a constraint-awareness benchmark. Both methods raise behavioral compliance from 4% to about 90% but sharply reduce explicit constraint reporting and retained third-person knowledge, indicating post-training erodes models' ability to report their own behavioral rules.

entry.title: From Trait Vectors to Circuits: Tracing Refusal and Sycophancy Through Language Models

author.name: Oscar Mir\'o L\'opez-Feliu, Maya Ozbayoglu

entry.summary: Investigates whether steering directions for refusal and sycophancy in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct act through the model's unmodified computation or through separate components. By splitting computation into reconstruction and transmission circuits around the trait vector and testing ablation-restoration, the authors find compact, faithful circuits for refusal. This sharpens the causal story behind activation steering and safety-relevant behavior.

entry.title: Spatial-Interactor: Learning Spatial Reasoning through Interaction with the Observable Physical World

author.name: Kaixiang Yao, Xu Wang, Miao Pan, Hu Xiyue, Weishi Wang, Daniel Dahlmeier, Jintao Chen, Yongliang Shen, Xuhong Zhang, Wenqi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes training vision-language models for spatial reasoning through interaction trajectories, which naturally connect an observation, an action, and the resulting observation and provide direct supervision for local state transitions. The approach targets maintaining an updated spatial state over long dynamic trajectories, where current static-question-based training falls short.

entry.title: ORION-CMR: On-scanner Reporting with Integrated Foundation Model for End-to-End Cardiac MRI Analysis and Interpretation

author.name: Omer Burak Demirel, Kelly K. Horst, Alessio Perazzolo, Elisa Bruno, Kenan Kaya, Rongzhen Ouyang, Enas Ahmed, Jouke Smink, Spencer L. Waddle, Zainudeen Kallumpurath, Tzu Cheng Chao, Dinghui Wang, Steve G. Langer, Timothy L. Kline, Panagiotis Korfiatis, Jacinta Browne, Ivana Isgum, Tim Leiner

entry.summary: Presents the first clinically evaluated scanner-native end-to-end cardiac MRI foundation model, pretrained on roughly 12.9 million CMR images from 9,258 studies. ORION-CMR performs sequence classification, ventricular function assessment, LGE detection, disease classification, and local LLM-based report generation in about 90 seconds, addressing the fragmented single-task nature of prior CMR AI.

entry.title: MuLA-Bench: A Multilingual Long-Form Audio Understanding Benchmark via Multi-Tier Auditing

author.name: Zeyu Yang, Xinyu Zhang, Zibo Bi, Pei Zhang, Xize Cheng, Jin Xu, Baosong Yang, Satoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: Introduces MuLA-Bench, 5,038 open-ended questions over 1,769 in-the-wild recordings totaling 1,377.9 hours across 16 languages and eight domains, with a balanced Language x Domain semantic track and an acoustic track preserving non-speech evidence. It uses evidence-grounded generation, shortcut checks, and language-expert review for auditable questions, evaluating ten audio-language models. Findings show language, evidence, and task jointly shape difficulty.

entry.title: DexTacWAM: A Visuo-Tactile World-Action Model for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Haoran Yuan, Zekai Wang, Boning Shao, Haoran Lu, Trevor Darrell, Ismini Lourentzou, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: Presents a visuo-tactile World-Action Model that encodes each fingertip independently, aggregates features through a finger- and pose-aware tactile compressor, and injects tactile latents into a video diffusion world model. On six contact-rich dexterous manipulation tasks on a 22-DoF bimanual platform it achieves the highest score on every task, averaging 70.6 versus 38.0 for the strongest baseline.

entry.title: BEACON: Belief-Enabled Adaptive CONtrol for Imitation Learning under Uncertainty

author.name: Moonyoung Lee, Soumojit Bhattacharya, George Kantor, Oliver Kroemer

entry.summary: Proposes BEACON, which conditions diffusion policies on Bayesian belief representations of hidden states rather than raw observation histories, exposing both the most likely state estimate and remaining uncertainty. This structured conditioning addresses state aliasing in partially observable manipulation, enabling history-aware disambiguation.

entry.title: Probabilistic Scene Graphs: Hierarchical Representation and Real-time System

author.name: Waqas Ali, Michele Antonazzi, Timon Homberger, Thien-Minh Nguyen, Lukas Rosenberger Schmid, Patric Jensfelt, Yixi Cai

entry.summary: Introduces Probabilistic Scene Graph (PSG), a generalization of 3D scene graphs that maintains a posterior over possible graph structures, entity relations, semantic attributes, and continuous spatial states, with uncertainty propagated through all graph construction and refinement operations. Geometry is carried directly by nodes so metric maps follow from the graph. Includes a real-time system implementation. This is a meaningful step toward principled uncertainty-aware semantic mapping for robots.

entry.title: Grounded Action Model: 3D Grounding as a Foundation for Robotics

author.name: Gehao Zhang, Weikai Huang, Shailesh Shailesh, Yiyan Peng, Jiafei Duan, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Proposes Grounded Action Models (GAMs), a new robot foundation model paradigm built on explicit 3D grounding: language, point, or box prompts are converted into an object-centric representation capturing visual features and metric geometry, mixed with robot state for policy execution. Argues pretrained backbones in VLAs and WAMs lack metric grounding, leaving it learned implicitly from demonstrations. From Ranjay Krishna's group.

entry.title: LogicTrack: Auditing Reasoning Trajectories of Large Language Models with Formal Logic Solvers

author.name: Jingyu Hu, Shu Yang, Weiru Liu, Di Wang

entry.summary: LogicTrack is a neuro-symbolic framework that audits chain-of-thought reasoning by auto-formalizing each intermediate step into symbolic representations verified with automated theorem provers. It introduces a Solver-Based Backtracking Reward that scores logical soundness step-by-step and guides backtracking tree search, addressing models that reach correct answers via logically flawed reasoning chains.

entry.title: BI-Agent and BI-Bench: Towards Automating End-to-End Business Intelligence

author.name: Chuxuan Hu, Yeye He, Penny Zhou, Wee Hyong Tok, Daniel Kang, Surajit Chaudhuri

entry.summary: The authors build BI-Agent and BI-Bench to evaluate whether LLMs can answer business intelligence questions end-to-end, including table identification, data transformation, and join construction rather than only the final question answering. Real-world BI projects are harvested from public sources to form the benchmark.

entry.title: Authorization Revocation for Long-Running AI Agents: Root-Scoped Quiescence under Delegation and Asynchronous Execution

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the problem of revoking authorization for long-running AI agents whose credentials, delegated tasks, queues, and callbacks outlive the initiating process. It defines root-scoped authorization quiescence, a protocol that linearizes a root cut, fences old-root expansion, and distinguishes independently authorized shared work while permitting exact rebind to current support. This addresses an important and underexplored security primitive for agentic systems.

entry.title: OmniVChat: Synthesizing, Benchmarking, and Training for Native Audio-Visual Dialogue

author.name: Haolin He, Yunfei Chu, Qi Chen, Wen Huang, Yuan Feng, Muzhi Zhu, Zheqi Dai, Haoning Xu, Dongchao Yang, Chunyat Wu, Zining Liang, Zhengxi Liu, Xiquan Li, Xie Chen, Xize Cheng, Qize Yang, Jin Xu, Qiuqiang Kong

entry.summary: OmniVChat defines the task of native audio-visual dialogue in which omni models simultaneously receive raw audio and video (with the query embedded in the stream) and return text, without external captioning or ASR. The paper tackles data scarcity and evaluation via synthesis, a benchmark, and training methods. Direct audio-visual interaction reduces latency and preserves perceptual cues relevant to grounded responses.

entry.title: SynthDemo-RL: Breaking the Zero-Reward Barrier in VLA Adaptation with LLM-Guided Synthetic Demonstrations

author.name: Hiroaki Kingetsu, Hiroaki Kurihara, Kaoru Yokoo, Kenji Fukumizu, Manohar Kaul

entry.summary: SynthDemo-RL is a teacher-student framework where an automated teacher converts simulator-privileged state into successful manipulation trajectories, a VLA student is distilled via SFT, and PPO with binary rewards refines the policy. It addresses the sparse-reward exploration problem in RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action models and introduces reward coverage as a complementary metric to success rate.

entry.title: PAGE: Partition-Aware Gated KV-Cache Eviction

author.name: Pankaj Kumar, Subhankar Mishra

entry.summary: PAGE reframes KV-cache eviction as a per-input admission decision, showing inputs split into a capacity-bound class where eviction is catastrophic (accuracy dropping from 99% to 0%) and a dilution-prone class where it is safe or beneficial. A single label-free prefill-attention scalar, the early-to-late drop in pairwise top-k head agreement, predicts this class before decoding, letting PAGE gate any base evictor with no training or labels.

entry.title: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts with Speculative Decoding via Expert Coactivation

author.name: Kumari Nishu, Han-Byul Kim, Santosh Chilkunda, Maxwell Horton, Arnav Kundu, Mohammad Samragh, Lauren Hannah, Mohammad Sekhavat, Nikhil Bhendawade, Manuel Ciosici, Iman Mirzadeh, Keivan Alizadeh Vahid, David Harrison, Irina Belousova, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Minsik Cho

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the interaction between Mixture-of-Experts models and speculative decoding, showing that more verification tokens drive more expert transfers from DRAM to NPU and raise memory-transfer cost, which bottlenecks runtime. It finds that router design during training, specifically high expert coactivation, is key to making MoEs efficient with speculative decoding, and proposes coactivation-aware training.

entry.title: Causilo Technical Report

author.name: Minyong Cho, Minho Jeong, Dooho Lee, Jinmo Lee, Jaemin Yoo

entry.summary: Introduces Causilo, a tabular foundation model achieving 1785.4 Elo on TabArena at a median 0.10 seconds per 1K test samples, outperforming TabPFN-3.5-Fast with 31.6% less inference time and sitting on the performance-efficiency Pareto frontier. Architecturally it follows TabICL's column-then-row design but adds a row-refinement module that exchanges information among cell representations before compression.

entry.title: Triggers and Diagnostics for LLM-Based Interpretability Failures in Active Inference Agents

author.name: Param Raval, Rohit Shenoy, Archana Vaidheeswaran

entry.summary: Audits LLM explainers used as runtime oversight for an Active Inference agent managing grid demand, using GPT-4o, Claude-3-Opus, and Gemini backends with three black-box triggers. Finds that none of 30 explanations flagged a corrupted observation stream and each narrated the corrupted belief fluently, exposing a serious oversight failure mode.

entry.title: Falling Trees: A Model Class for Interpretable Risk Prioritization

author.name: Varun Babbar, Zachery Boner, Margo Seltzer, Cynthia Rudin

entry.summary: This paper generalizes falling rule lists to falling trees, an interpretable model class that preserves monotonic risk ordering while allowing tree-structured branching. The authors introduce GRAVITree, a dynamic-programming-with-bounds algorithm that provably learns the Rashomon set of falling trees under depth and branching constraints. Given Cynthia Rudin's group's leadership in interpretable ML, this is a solid contribution to the Rashomon-set research program.

entry.title: Displacement Geometry Captures Platonic Shared Reality Across Models and Modalities

author.name: Chenming Shang, Yujin Tang, Jun Jie Ou Yang, Ruize Xu, Adam Breuer, Nikhil Singh

entry.summary: The paper reconciles conflicting evidence about the Platonic Representation Hypothesis by showing that independently trained models share displacement vectors (directions between samples) rather than absolute sample positions: under a single orthogonal alignment, displacement geometry is substantially preserved across 44 vision and language encoders, while absolute positions are not. Both findings arise from a single decomposition, explaining the prior conflicting results.

entry.title: Prior-Amortized In-Context Bayesian Inference for Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Models

author.name: Alex Kipnis, Marcel Binz, Eric Schulz

entry.summary: Metabeta is a pretrained neural network providing amortized, in-context Bayesian inference for generalized linear mixed-effects models, accepting prior families and hyperparameters at test time for zero-shot generalization. Using set transformers and conditional normalizing flows, it mirrors the two-level hierarchical posterior structure, avoiding slow MCMC restarts for every new dataset.

entry.title: Augmented Hypothesis Testing with Persona-Based LLM Simulations

author.name: Ziyad Benomar, Aymen Al Marjani, Paul Missault, Saab Mansour

entry.summary: The authors propose a learning-augmented hypothesis testing framework that uses auxiliary predictions of experimental outcomes (including persona-based LLM simulations) to reduce A/B testing sample sizes while preserving statistical validity. The framework handles predictions of unknown quality across a granularity spectrum, from coarse population-level directional signals to fine-grained individual-level estimates. This could substantially cut the cost and duration of online experiments.

entry.title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses

author.name: Peng Xia, Rujun Han, Zifeng Wang, Yanfei Chen, Yufan Zhang, Yoonho Lee, Chengsong Huang, Han Yu, Zhongying CuiZhu, Yifei Ming, Huaxiu Yao, Burak Gokturk, Tomas Pfister, Chen-Yu Lee

entry.summary: The authors study recursive self-improvement of LLM agent harnesses, where prompts, control flow, tooling, memory, and context management are iteratively edited around a frozen backbone. They identify overfitting-to-training-tasks failure in existing RSI loops and introduce RRSI, which applies regularization principles to constrain harness evolution and preserve out-of-distribution gains.

entry.title: Evaluation Awareness Shifts from Format to Context with Model Scale

author.name: Navraj Singh, Maheep Chaudhary

entry.summary: The study investigates how models detect that they are being evaluated, comparing smaller and larger models across Gemma 3, Phi-3, and Llama-3 8B using chain-of-thought analysis, representation probing, and attribution methods. It finds smaller models rely on prompt format cues while larger models use higher-order reasoning, and proposes a dual-pathway intervention combining prompt sanitization with activation counter-steering.

entry.title: Knowing, and Saying It Only When Asked: LLM Endognostics and the Schizognosis of Minerva-7B

author.name: Fabrizio Davide, Francesco Collova

entry.summary: Introduces LLM endognostics, a white-box auditing framework that extracts and causally manipulates latent knowledge in the residual stream. Applied to Minerva-7B-Instruct on 124 prompt pairs spanning 12 professional-risk categories, behavioral evaluation shows the model acts identically on 63.7% of pairs, yet a Jacobian-lens projection reveals a significant Contrastive Endognostic Margin, indicating the model internally maintains risk distinctions it does not express. This dissociation between latent knowledge and behavioral output is significant for alignment auditing.

entry.title: Assessing Adversarial Robustness of Latent Reasoning Models

author.name: Shaolong Chen, Ang Li, Mingjie Li, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic robustness evaluation of latent reasoning models (LRMs), which compress chain-of-thought into continuous latent vectors for efficiency, across eight models and six benchmarks in textual and multimodal settings. The study finds LRMs are generally less robust than explicit CoT baselines under adversarial perturbations. This is an important safety caveat for an emerging efficiency-focused architecture.

entry.title: Algorithmic Collusion and the Complexity of Information-Value-Free Equilibria

author.name: Ioannis Anagnostides, Weiqiang Zheng

entry.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of information-value-free (coarse) correlated equilibria, a refinement motivated by regulating algorithmic collusion, in succinct games with many players or exponentially many strategies. It proves that computing an IVF-CE is PPAD-complete in many-player polymatrix and two-player Bayesian games even with approximate computation. The results sharply delimit when regulators can efficiently certify non-collusive equilibria.

entry.title: A Horizon-Independent Regret Bound for Optimistic Hedge in General-Sum Games

author.name: Junsoo Ha

entry.summary: This paper proves that plain Optimistic Hedge with constant step size attains constant individual regret in general-sum games with n players under expected loss-vector feedback, improving the best-known logarithmic bound, with a corollary O(1/T) coarse correlated equilibrium gap for time-averaged play. The analysis represents Optimistic Hedge as a real-analytic recurrence on a compact space yielding an exact flow interpretation. It settles a fundamental open question about the most canonical learning rule in games.

entry.title: Learning tactile perception from high-bandwidth single-point sensing

author.name: Joseph Rigal, Emmanuel Virot, Caroline Pascal

entry.summary: SpectRobot converts single-point high-bandwidth tactile signals into time-frequency spectrograms that can be fed to standard vision encoders, exploiting rich temporal dynamics rather than spatial sensor arrays. This enables robotic manipulation learning pipelines built for vision to leverage sparse tactile sensing with preserved frequency information.

entry.title: An Empirical Cost Attribution of Context-Compression Gateways in Multi-Turn Coding Agents

author.name: Luzhuo Chen, Jiayu Shi

entry.summary: The paper instruments a production compression gateway (Paritok) between coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) and frontier models (Claude Sonnet, GPT-5) to decompose the token bill into tool-schema filtering, content compression, and history summarization levers. Controlled A/B runs show the three levers save money at very different rates, contradicting the assumption that compressing file reads is always cost-effective.

entry.title: Measuring the Assistant's Harmlessness Preferences on the User Turn

author.name: Jord Nguyen

entry.summary: Shows that the assistant persona's harmlessness preference shapes model predictions even on user turns where the assistant is not speaking, a boundary that post-training was expected to enforce. The preference is near-zero in base models, emerges through post-training, replicates across open-weight families, grows with scale, and can be shifted by narrow finetuning without touching safety training.

entry.title: Decomposing Error and Style in Automated Clinical Coding

author.name: Han-Chin Shing, Jack Moriarty, Ryan Ware, Afton Marchbanks, Carlyn Canvasser, Stefanie Higgins, Harsh Gupta, Fang Wang, Joseph Paul Cohen

entry.summary: Shows that in automated clinical coding, human coders agree on only 73% of codes for the same notes (rising to 77% after audit), and models the systematic disagreement as coder-specific coding style rather than error. It recasts coding as a conditional probability given note and style, estimated via a 10-dimension rubric, on the ACI-Bench dataset. This has important implications for how clinical coding models are evaluated and deployed.

entry.title: VibeMemBench: Evaluating Memory Systems for Coding Agents on Real Repository Coding Tasks

author.name: Liyang Fan, Yingcheng Shi, Yongbin Li, Chenghao Sun, Xin Chen, Xander Xu, Hu Wei, Shiwen Ni, Min Yang, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: Introduces VibeMemBench, evaluating persistent memory systems for coding agents on 111 coding targets from 90 SWE-rebench V2 repositories with 3,634 history trajectories, measuring whether memory improves executable repository work (bug fixes, features, interface and configuration changes). It bridges the gap between repository benchmarks that do not isolate memory and memory benchmarks that score recall without downstream coding outcomes.

entry.title: SLICEChat: Progressive In-Encoder Token Pruning for Whole-Slide Pathology Language Models

author.name: Ali Kerem Bozkurt, Baris Cem Bakay, Ibrahim Kulac, Cigdem Gunduz-Demir, Erkut Erdem, Aykut Erdem

entry.summary: SLICEChat is a slide-level multimodal LLM for gigapixel whole-slide pathology images that integrates progressive, language-supervised, region-aware token pruning inside a hybrid Mamba-Transformer encoder, compressing the sequence during encoding rather than after. This reduces the computational cost of multimodal attention while preserving global interactions.

entry.title: Rethinking Streaming Video Diffusion Model: Context, Execution, and Training

author.name: Hongchen Zhang (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)

entry.summary: The paper develops a unified analytical framework for streaming video diffusion design, relating model and sampler choices, historical conditioning, execution scheduling, and training strategies across a broad family of causal context-selection policies. Experiments on the full VBench prompt set show same-level and progressive history conditioning outperform clean-history baselines (85.24 and 85.60 vs 84.45).

entry.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Counterfactual Diagnosis of End-to-End and VLA Driving Policies Under Domain Shift

author.name: Ruolin Yang, Zilin Huang, Buoyue Wang, Zhengyang Wan, Yuhao Luo, Zihao Sheng, Sikai Chen

entry.summary: The paper shows that leaderboard ranks on nuScenes and NAVSIM poorly predict driving-policy behavior at new sites, and proposes a counterfactual check-up: real frames edited (pedestrian removed, night re-lighting) with detector-verified edits, reading trajectory changes as causal diagnoses. Five exams built on two causal axes separate policies that look identical by rank.

entry.title: RewardVerse: Rubric-Guided Policy Optimization for Video Reward Modeling

author.name: Zhenchen Tang, Yang Li, Songlin Yang, Bo Peng, Xiaotong Zhao, Shuai Li, Haotian Fan, Alan Zhao, Jing Dong

entry.summary: Proposes RewardVerse, a rubric-based video reward model that inserts a dynamic rubric between evaluation query and scorer to combat scalar drift, where unconstrained scalar scores collapse or shift across prompts and destabilize RL fine-tuning of video generators. The rubric design is inspired by professional human annotation engineering.

entry.title: CE$^4$L: Continual Ego, Exo, and Ego-Exo Learning

author.name: Hongwei Yan, Kanglei Zhou, Yuchen Liu, Qingyu Shi, Yi Zhong, Liyuan Wang

entry.summary: CE4L introduces a unified continual learning benchmark for multi-view video perception of embodied agents, spanning ego, exo, and ego-exo settings across four tasks including cross-view skill assessment, action segmentation, cross-view association, and anticipation/planning. It highlights challenges absent from prior CL benchmarks such as simultaneous task and viewpoint shifts, cross-view correspondence, and view-dependent asynchrony, and proposes baselines. A significant resource for embodied and continual learning communities.

entry.title: Monitorable Chart Reasoning Agents via Verifiable Process Rewards

author.name: Sanchit Sinha, Oana Frunza, Kashif Rasul, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: Chart-RVR is a reinforcement learning framework that trains chart reasoning agents with verifiable process rewards by decomposing reasoning into auditable blocks: chart structure identification, value extraction, and computation. This enables stakeholders to verify where an error arose rather than relying on free-form rationales or answer-only outputs. It directly addresses deployment concerns around auditability of LVLM-based agents.

entry.title: Look Where It Counts: A Free, Label-Free Visual Evidence Signal for Fine-Grained Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Santi Ram Tiwari, Nihal Naik, Devbrat Pandey, Nishant Sinha

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a contrastive evidence gap: the per-token log-likelihood ratio a multimodal LLM assigns to its output when conditioned on question-relevant versus irrelevant image regions. It shows this internal signal can serve as a free, label-free training or verification signal across Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL models on V*Bench, avoiding expensive SFT, RLVR, or distillation.

entry.title: AgentSTAR: Agentic Shape Tracking and Reconstruction from Monocular Videos

author.name: Kirill Mazur, Nikita Karaev, Matthew Chang, Jitendra Malik, Nur Muhammad "Mahi'' Shafiullah

entry.summary: This paper introduces a method for 3D shape reconstruction and object tracking from monocular video using an agentic analysis-by-synthesis approach. Instead of estimating pixel correspondences first, the system infers a structured 3D object model (geometry plus kinematic structure) and uses a Vision-Language Model agent in a render-and-compare loop to iteratively refine shape and generalized pose estimates. The formulation allows robust tracking through large motion, articulation, and severe occlusion.

entry.title: ME-VLM:A Unified VLM for Embodied Cognition and Agent Coordination

author.name: Foundation Model, Li Auto Inc

entry.summary: Li Auto introduces ME-VLM, a unified vision-language model in 4B and 35B-A3B variants targeting embodied cognition and multimodal agent coordination in physical and digital environments. The training pipeline combines embodied capabilities, spatiotemporal reasoning, planning, and outcome assessment using execution feedback data. This represents a notable industry push toward physical AI foundation models from an automotive company.

entry.title: Streaming Video Editing with Easy Adaptation

author.name: Yujia Hu, Jiajun Li, Zihao He, Songhua Liu

entry.summary: SVEET is a framework for high-quality streaming video editing that adapts a pretrained bidirectional video diffusion model into an auto-regressive, streaming-compatible editor with minimal additional training. The authors derive two key design principles — backbone feature disentanglement and conditional frame independence — from a systematic study of prior video-to-video diffusion methods, and implement them via an auxiliary branch with temporally independent self-attention injecting source video features into backbone blocks. This enables practical, low-latency controllable video generation.

entry.title: SPHQuant: Efficient extreme low bit weight quantization for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kewei Zhang, Zheng Chen, Haotong Qin, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: SPHQuant is a rotation-free post-training quantization framework for VLMs that quantizes weights in spherical rather than Cartesian coordinates, targeting extreme 2-3 bit widths without the runtime overhead of rotation-based methods. It addresses outlier problems that limit existing rotation-free approaches at low bit-widths.

entry.title: LIBERO-VPro: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Visual Robustness of Robotic Foundation Models

author.name: Huiqiong Li, Zhiting Mei, Anirudha Majumdar, Jingjing Chen, Yu-Gang Jiang, Bin Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces LIBERO-VPro, a benchmark systematically evaluating closed-loop visual robustness of robotic foundation models under perturbations across four dimensions including evidence degradation, camera staleness, source consistency, and scene variation, spanning 12 categories, 96 settings, and 3,296 task-condition cases. Evaluates multiple VLA and world-action models under these stresses.

entry.title: EditWM: Event-Decomposed World Modeling with Incremental Correction for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Junjie Yang, Qingwei Zeng, Youyou Li, Zicheng Ding, Ziyi Shi, Shuqi Shen, Hongliang Lu, Hai Yang

entry.summary: Proposes EditWM, a world model for autonomous driving that decomposes future prediction into regular trajectory-conditioned evolution plus event-driven incremental corrections in a compact visual feature space. A correction decoder with a learned gate produces bounded feature updates, improving handling of unpredictable events while preserving predictable dynamics.

entry.title: VT-Bridge: Bridging Pretrained Foundation VLAs to VTLAs via Lightweight Residual Adaptation

author.name: Yansong Wu, Tuo Yang, Rongping Zhao, Lingyun Chen, Xiao Chen, Junnan Li, Fan Wu, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: Proposes VT-Bridge, a lightweight residual adaptation strategy that converts pretrained vision-language-action models into vision-tactile-language-action models without retraining from scratch or altering the backbone. Identical residual adapters with backbone-specific weights refine actions at execution frequency, substantially lowering the data and compute costs of adding tactile sensing.

entry.title: CompVLA: A Variable Compliance Vision-Language-Action Model for Contact-rich Manipulation

author.name: Jongmin Kim, Junsu Ha, Che-Sang Park, Minchang Song, Hyeokju Jeong, Himchan Hwang, Jianlong Fu, Frank C. Park

entry.summary: Presents CompVLA, a unified VLA that jointly predicts motion and a stiffness matrix from RGB and language, adding a Compliance Expert that outputs time-varying stiffness and virtual displacement profiles executed via geometric impedance control. Addresses the limitation that standard VLAs emit purely kinematic commands. Reports the highest average success rate across diverse contact-rich manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Structured World-State Reasoning for Agentic Robotic Search

author.name: Finley R. Holt, Luis A. Pabon, John Irvin Alora, Jonas Frey, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: WORLDS grounds long-horizon language-guided robotic search in a persistent graph initialized from geospatial priors and updated by perception, with parallel Reasoners maintaining competing candidate interpretations and a multimodal Examiner gathering requested evidence before a Judge selects a target. An agentic architecture for resolving ambiguity between language, maps, and observations. From Marco Pavone's group at Stanford.

entry.title: MIRA: Real-Time Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction for Embodied Companions

author.name: Lijian Lin, Ye Zhu, Fan Zhang, Yunfei Liu, Baofeng Li, Xianwen Zeng, Jianan Wang, Yu Li

entry.summary: MIRA is a unified framework for full-duplex embodied companion interaction that, given streaming user speech, dialogue history, and vocal affect, predicts response text plus explicit embodiment cues so dialogue orchestration and interruptible gesture synthesis are dynamically synchronized. It addresses timing, prosody, and physical safety under incremental inputs and uncertain turn boundaries, unlike prior systems that decouple dialogue from offline motion generation.

entry.title: H2RBench: A Real-to-Sim Benchmark for Evaluating Human-to-Robot Transfer

author.name: Chuyang Xiao, Haotian Zhan, Sriram Krishna, Peilin Meng, Muhammad Zubair Irshad, Sergey Zakharov, David Held

entry.summary: H2RBench is a Real2Sim benchmark providing a standardized protocol for comparing human-to-robot transfer methods, built on real human video demonstrations and simulated robot demonstrations across four manipulation tasks with diverse interaction requirements. It resolves the incomparability of prior evaluations that differed in task suites, scene layouts, objects, and supervision levels, and benchmarks multiple representative H2R methods.

entry.title: Optimal High-Order Methods for Solving Monotone Variational Inequalities

author.name: Xinliang Zhang, Lesi Chen, Linxuan Pan, Chengchang Liu, Junchi Yang, Jingzhao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a novel second-order method for smooth monotone variational inequalities achieving the optimal rate of O(T^-2.5), closing the gap between the Monteiro-Svaiter NPE rate and the recent lower bound. The algorithm extends to arbitrary higher-order methods, obtaining matching optimal rates for any order p.

entry.title: Alignment Midtraining Cracks Under Pressure

author.name: J Bostock

entry.summary: Systematic stress-testing of alignment midtraining (AMT) across model and token budget scales, finding that roughly 190M tokens of midtrained motivations can be overwritten by about 50K tokens of competing finetuning data, and that generalization to undemonstrated rules is weak. Experiments on GLM-4.5-Air (110B) with a fictional Charter-based setting show midtraining shapes motivations under ideal post-training but fails under small perturbations.

entry.title: Critical-State RL: Diagnosing Trainable States for Multi-Turn Tool Use

author.name: Zixiang Chen, Wenting Zhao, Zhepeng Cen, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Jianguo Zhang, Zhiwei Liu, Tulika Manoj Awalgaonkar, Liangwei Yang, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Huan Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Critical-State RL, which identifies which specific model calls in multi-turn tool-use interactions are worth training on, since reward variation can reflect downstream randomness rather than action quality. Using nested sampling to separate action-dependent variation from continuation noise, it optimizes the policy at selected states with contextual-bandit-style updates.

entry.title: Swiss-Knife: A Framework for Reconfigurable Externalised Multi-Objective Alignment at Decode Time

author.name: Agnibh Karmakar, Mayur Parvatikar, Shreyash Dhoot, Amit Dhanda, Aman Chadha, Kapil Wanaskar, Vinija Jain, Amitava Das

entry.summary: Introduces Swiss-Knife, a framework for decode-time alignment in which the alignment specification is a first-class runtime object composed of hot-swappable scoring blades, a normalizer, a pairwise aggregation operator, and a selection rule. The paper proves a representation theorem showing every aggregation operator satisfying six axioms falls into a two-parameter family containing probit and logit forms. This generalizes decode-time steering beyond the standard score-and-maximize design.

entry.title: Causal Localization of the Refusal Direction in Audio Language Models

author.name: Leonardo Haw-Yang Foo, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: Uses causal interventions to determine whether refusal in audio language models is carried by the speech front end or inherited from the safety-aligned text backbone. Fitting harmful-versus-benign directions at the audio-to-LM interface and LM residual layers across five models from three backbone families, the authors find the largest effects in a mid-to-late LM band. This extends refusal-direction interpretability beyond text into speech modality.

entry.title: Robot World Models Are Not Invariant to How the Actions Are Written

author.name: Ahmed Karim, Leon Chlon

entry.summary: Shows that latent world models trained on one action parameterization (absolute joint targets vs. deltas) collapse when handed identical trajectories written in the other form: retrieval degrades 2.6-13.4x, goal-conditioned action selection drops from 53% to 15%, and future beliefs become near-orthogonal on PushT. The paper argues the predictor does not degrade gracefully but answers a different question.

entry.title: D-JEPA: A Decision-Aligned Latent World Model

author.name: Shuaijun Liu, Chengyu Wu, Qifu Wen, Feiyang You, Chenglong Zhang, Shuyang Hao, Xi Lin, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: D-JEPA identifies a decision-local prediction gap where a candidate future predicted closer to the goal can yield worse realized outcomes, and proposes a decision-aligned latent world model that refines pretrained predictive geometry using ordinal evidence from executed outcomes. A bounded, permutation-equivariant operator jointly reasons over goal-relative features to improve action selection.

entry.title: Collapse, Not Complexity: Failure-Conditioned Decomposition Repair for End-to-End Document Parsing

author.name: Xingyu Lin, Dehui Du

entry.summary: Shows that for end-to-end document parsers, complexity is the wrong decision variable for when to invoke reasoning mode: reasoning lowers mean quality at 1.54x tokens, an input-only model cannot predict its benefit (AUROC 0.47), and benefit concentrates on pages whose ordinary pass has already collapsed into degenerate repetition. Instead, they detect collapse and apply targeted decomposition repair. A sharp empirical finding with preregistered analysis.

entry.title: HDND: Hierarchical Dynamic Neural Decoding for Multilingual Word/Character Retrieval from Non-Invasive Brain Recordings

author.name: Yueyang Li, Shuran Chen, Wai Ting Siok, Nizhuan Wang

entry.summary: HDND is a hierarchical decoding framework that treats word decoding from non-invasive brain recordings as structured refinement across acoustic, lexical, and semantic levels rather than flat label retrieval. It targets the difficult problem of decoding individual words where neural evidence is weak and temporally distributed. The framework supports multilingual word and character retrieval from non-invasive recordings.

entry.title: HIGenNTO: Scalable Humanoid Interaction Generation via Noise-Space Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Lalit Jayanti, Kashu Yamazaki, Yuto Shibata, Kotaro Amaya, Katerina Fragkiadaki

entry.summary: Presents HIGenNTO, a framework that synthesizes humanoid-scene interaction motion references by optimizing the initial noise of a pretrained text-conditioned motion model under sparse spatiotemporal and scene constraints. The formulation simultaneously satisfies desired contacts, avoids collisions, and maintains stable support while retaining the prior model's realism and temporal coherence.

entry.title: Detecting Hallucination in LLMs: Tracing the Topological Signatures of Impaired Context Sharing

author.name: Amir Jalilifard, Anderson Rocha, Eric Wong, Marcos Medeiros Raimundo

entry.summary: This paper analyzes information flow within attention graphs of LLMs using Forman-Ricci curvature to detect structural signatures of hallucination, such as information bottlenecks. The proposed single-pass method outperforms attention-based and multi-response baselines on two hallucination-detection benchmarks across several models. It matters because reliable hallucination detection without generating multiple samples is valuable for deployment.

entry.title: GUARD: Natural Forgetting in Large Reasoning Models via Guided Answer-Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Zeyu Yan, Guanghao Zhou, Minghui Qiu, Ming Gao, Cen Chen

entry.summary: GUARD addresses machine unlearning in large reasoning models, where protected facts or unsafe rationales can surface in intermediate chain-of-thought traces before the final answer. It proposes learning a natural forgetting trajectory: a coherent non-disclosing CoT followed by a stable refusal-style answer, replacing the original disclosure rather than merely suppressing content.

entry.title: ECG Mirage: Revealing and Mitigating the Underutilisation of ECGs in Vision-Language Models for Clinical Prediction

author.name: Jinning Liang, Mingcheng Zhu, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: The paper identifies ECG Mirage, a failure mode where vision-language models in emergency-department prediction appear multimodally capable but do not meaningfully use the patient-specific ECG, distinguishing ECG neglect from ECG confusion via matched, mismatched, and outcome-derived controls. It proposes evaluation methodology and mitigation for this underutilization.

entry.title: The Stochastic Shift: A New Evaluation Paradigm for Text-to-SQL with AI Operators

author.name: Tarfah Alrashed, Fatma Ozcan, Per Jacobsson, Tal Neiman, Xianshun Chen

entry.summary: The paper observes that current Text-to-SQL evaluation metrics fail against non-deterministic AI-operator-augmented queries that mix structured database logic with flexible semantic operators over unstructured data. It formalizes these evaluation failure modes and introduces a multilayered evaluation framework decoupling deterministic SQL logic from AI semantics, tested on BigQuery and academic benchmarks.

entry.title: Talking Past the Machine: Morality, Politeness, and Alignment in Human-AI Dialogue

author.name: Marina Mitiaeva, Lu Xiao

entry.summary: This empirical study analyzes 15,881 human-ChatGPT and 10,784 human-human multi-turn dialogues with mixed-effects models to see how morality, politeness, and alignment function in human-AI versus human-human conversation. It finds a consistent dissociation: AI produces the surface features of cooperative communication without the underlying social arc. This has implications for how conversational AI is evaluated, trusted, and designed.

entry.title: CIPL: A Channel-Aware Framework for Recoverable Privacy Leakage in LLM Agents

author.name: Tao Huang, Guosen Wu, Guolong Zheng, Jiayang Meng, Chen Hou, Xu Yang, Xuechao Yang, Feng Xia

entry.summary: CIPL is a channel-aware evaluation framework for black-box privacy leakage in LLM agents, modeling the flow of sensitive information through source, selection, assembly, execution, observation, and extraction stages. It distinguishes internal exposure from what an external attacker can actually recover, evaluated across memory-, retrieval-, and tool-mediated targets including a live BrowserUse agent case study.

entry.title: GRRR: The Geometry of Reshaping, Rotation, and Routing in Decoder LLM post-training

author.name: Jianing Qi, Hao Tang, Zhigang Zhu

entry.summary: GRRR analyzes how post-training (SFT and RL) changes LLM weights by expressing each update in the pretrained matrix's SVD frame, separating diagonal reshaping of singular values, off-diagonal rotation of input-output coupling, and null-space routing outside the pretrained core. Across 12 post-training chains on a math evaluation suite, removing the diagonal component usually preserves most post-training gains, yielding geometric insight into what fine-tuning actually modifies.

entry.title: Dissecting Hierarchical Reasoning Models: A Mechanistic Study

author.name: Leo Raphael Rodrigues, Jian Kang

entry.summary: This mechanistic study of Hierarchical Reasoning Models (HRM) on Sudoku, Maze, and ARC-AGI-2 uses causal interventions on recurrent states, linear probes, and sparse autoencoders to understand what HRM encodes and how it reasons. Findings include that single-state recurrent Transformers are comparable to HRM, and that causal contributions of high- and low-level states diverge from the model's motivating story.

entry.title: Resist, Update, Reject: Preference Optimization Installs a Prior-Dependent Reliability Switch

author.name: Sen Yang, Yuen-Hei Yeung

entry.summary: This paper shows that the objective optimized by most anti-sycophancy work is non-identifying with respect to source reliability: scalar mixtures trace a single deference dial, so models cannot simultaneously resist manipulation, update on reliable testimony, and reject unreliable testimony. The authors make reliability identifiable through data and demonstrate a prior-dependent reliability switch installed via preference optimization.

entry.title: Look Before You Steer: Geometry Predicts SAE Feature Steerability

author.name: Muhammad Khan, Shlok Channawar, Akshaj Gurugubelli, Girish Gupta, Aditya Shah

entry.summary: Shows that SAE feature steerability, previously requiring costly intervention sweeps to tune, is partially predicted by decoder-space geometry: neighbor density and max cosine similarity to nearby decoder directions, both computable from weights alone, rank steering cost (rho up to -0.546, AUROC 0.61-0.82). Opens a path to cheap pre-selection of steerable interpretability features.

entry.title: Causal Inference with Unobserved Confounding: A Mixture Learning Perspective

author.name: Mansi Sood, Devavrat Shah

entry.summary: Develops a mixture-learning perspective on unobserved confounding, treating latent confounders as sources of mixture structure in observed data, and shows recovering the mixing distribution enables estimation of interventional distributions. Connects the framework to panel-data causal inference, latent factor models, and synthetic interventions.

entry.title: GDN Tree-Scan: Served Tree Verification for Recurrent-Hybrid Language Models

author.name: Zhiyuan Ma

entry.summary: GDN Tree-Scan is a tree speculative-decoding verifier for Gated-DeltaNet recurrent-hybrid language models, integrated into vLLM. The key insight is that recurrent-hybrid models break the ancestry-mask-only assumption of tree verification: candidate rows must carry the recurrent state that native sequential decoding would produce along their root-to-node paths. The system combines FlashAttention-2 tree-bias attention, branch-local GDN scan/replay, and device-side multidraft commitment.

entry.title: Mind or Message? Auditing Theory of Mind in Multi-Agent Social Simulation

author.name: Cong Li, Cheng Chen, Thomas Fung, Alex Rossi, Yi Li

entry.summary: The paper audits whether apparent theory of mind in multi-agent LLM social simulations reflects genuine partner modeling or mere reliance on transcript content, using 40 multi-issue negotiations with known hidden preferences and Pareto frontiers. Across 160 dyads, 2880 counterfactual probes hold transcript bytes fixed while varying one factor at a time (reader stake, partner tone, identity labels, order), enabling causal attribution of apparent social reasoning.

entry.title: Hessian Rank Constraint for Learning Structure of Nonlinear Latent Variable Models

author.name: Zijian Li, Ruichu Cai, Feng Xie, Xinshuai Dong, Haoyue Dai, Yuewen Sun, Yujia Zheng, Guangyi Chen, Yingyao Hu, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes the cross-Hessian Rank Constraint (HRC), a rank-based identifiability condition for discovering latent variables and their causal relations under general nonlinear mixing, where the cross-Hessian of the observed-data log-density reveals information about latent structure. HRC reduces to classical Tetrad constraints in the linear Gaussian case and authorship includes prominent causal discovery researchers (Kun Zhang group).

entry.title: MemCalib: Benchmarking and Optimizing Memory Use in LLM Agents

author.name: Ruike Cao, Fanyu Zhao, Fugen Yao, Liang Dong, Jian Xu, Guanjun Jiang, Yifei Zhao, Han Zhang, Li Xiao

entry.summary: MemCalib introduces a benchmark grounded in realistic agent-memory scenarios that evaluates whether an LLM gives each memory in context the appropriate degree of influence over its response. The study finds frontier open- and closed-source models over- or under-use memories, and evaluates post-training algorithms including GRPO-style methods to improve memory calibration.

entry.title: Information-Time Proximal Policy Optimization

author.name: Yongcheng Zeng, Xinyu Cui, Yan Song, Guoqing Liu, Hongsheng Xin, Kaike Zhang, Cheng Deng, Kun Zhan, Jian Ying, Jian Zhao, Haifeng Zhang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: InfoPPO reparameterizes temporal progression in RLVR-based LLM reasoning using information density rather than raw token counts, inducing a shared state-dependent structure for credit propagation and policy updates. This restores the usefulness of non-trivial discounting in long-horizon reasoning while preserving terminal supervision over long sequences.

entry.title: Muon Can Outperform Dedicated Continual Learning Methods
