author.name: Sebastian George Sincari (Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Bucharest, Bucharest, Romania), Bogdan Alexandru Gheorghe (Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Bucharest, Bucharest, Romania), Antonio Barbalau (Bitdefender, Bucharest, Romania)

entry.summary: This paper shows that training incremental LoRA with the Muon optimizer, which orthogonalizes updates, matches or beats dedicated continual learning methods like O-LoRA and ELLA on the Standard CL Benchmark and TRACE. The key insight is that a generic optimizer-supplied constraint on update directions can substitute for task-aware penalties on weight overlap.

entry.title: LoRA-generating hypernetworks for efficient on-device LLM generative personalization

author.name: Sean Augenstein, Li Ding, Jihwan Lee, Keith Rush, Andrey Zhmoginov

entry.summary: The paper trains a hypernetwork that maps a user's context tokens to a LoRA adapter tailored to that user, enabling personalization of on-device LLMs on mobile hardware. Once common artifacts are deployed, each device generates its own adapter locally, avoiding heavy per-user server-side training given tight mobile compute budgets.

entry.title: Multilingual Safety Signals Are Multi-Layered: Filtering Safety-Degrading Data for Safer LLMs

author.name: Jiakun Li, Guowei Song, Sijia Li, Xingwei He, Hongzheng Chai, Yuan Yuan

entry.summary: The paper shows that in multilingual LLMs, safety-relevant representations are distributed across multiple layers rather than concentrated in a single safety-sensitive layer, since sensitive layers are only partially shared across languages. It builds on this to filter safety-degrading samples from fine-tuning data that would silently erode safety alignment.

entry.title: The Situated Identity Test: Distinguishing Persistent Cognitive Identity from Persona Imitation

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: Introduces the Situated Identity Test (SIT), an architecture-independent evaluation framework that tests whether an agent's behavior is attributable to a genuinely persistent identity rather than persona imitation conditioned on a public profile. It formalizes the attribution problem that identical profiles can mask different private histories, which an agent cannot resolve from the profile alone. This matters for agent identity, trust, and deployment accountability as LLM agents accumulate memories and autobiographies.

entry.title: Mask-Aware Execution for Efficient JEPA Training

author.name: Md Musfiqur Rahman Sanim, Zhihao Shu, Bahram Afsharmanesh, Amirali Mirian, Wei Niu, Gagan Agrawal

entry.summary: M-JEPA restructures JEPA training pipelines for efficiency without changing the learning objective, separating mask-independent computation from mask-dependent routing to enable shared context encoder execution, fused target-side work, and reduced memory-bound token routing. Since JEPAs are emerging as core representation-learning and world-model primitives, the reported efficiency gains grow in value with mask count and model scale.

entry.title: AVTR-1: Open Stack for Real-Time Interactive Avatars

author.name: Artem Kravtsov, Dmitrii Ziganshin, Vsevolod Poletaev, Gleb Balitskiy, Anastasia Tikhonova, Egor Burkov, Vadim Lebedev

entry.summary: Introduces AVTR-1, an open-source stack enabling real-time interactive avatar conversations, built around a compact 153M-parameter autoregressive flow-matching motion generator conditioned on both conversation participants' audio. The system handles synchronization with an external voice agent, video frame scheduling, and interruption handling, converting chunk-based generation into a continuous audio-video stream.

entry.title: Bayesian Filtering in Physical Systems via Test-time Trained Flow Matching

author.name: Ruiqi Feng, Chongyi Wang, Tao Zhang, Tailin Wu

entry.summary: Introduces the Belief Flow Filter (BFF), which encodes the evolving posterior distribution directly into flow matching model weights at test time rather than relying on particle-based posterior representations, aligning with the recursive structure of Bayesian filtering. Targets online state estimation for high-dimensional physical systems with complex posteriors.

entry.title: MobileCybench: Evaluating Agent Vulnerability Discovery via Executable Probes

author.name: Andy K. Zhang, Ava Huang, Joey Ji, Wai Han, Thomas Qin, Nardos Demilew, Michael Tian-Yue Liu, Brian Song, Riya Dulepet, Brian Wang, Kyleen Liao, Cuiyuanxiu Chen, Nishka Kacheria, Andrew Wu, Pratham Rangwala, Xinjie Wang, Laura Gomezjurado Gonzalez, Anita Ding, Benjamin Yi, Daniel E. Ho, Dan Boneh, Dawn Song, Ion Stoica, Percy Liang

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for evaluating AI agent vulnerability reports via probes: executable checks of security properties that replay reported exploits against applications, so a triggered probe confirms both exploit success and which security property was violated. Instantiates this as MobileCybench for mobile vulnerability discovery, addressing the overload of unverifiable agent-reported bugs.

entry.title: Poisson Exchange Beyond Submodularity: Effective Approximation Algorithms for Offline and Online Subset Selection over Matroids

author.name: Shi Fu, Youming Qiao, Dacheng Tao, Zongqi Wan, Qixin Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MGPE, an algorithm for maximizing weakly submodular functions over matroid constraints that performs maximum-gain local exchanges driven by a non-homogeneous Poisson clock, improving on the long-standing conservative approximation guarantee for this setting. It covers both offline and online variants.

entry.title: MiTHras: Task-specific Hierarchical Semi-supervised Contrastive Masked Autoencoder for Mitotic Figure Analysis

author.name: Trinh T. L. Vuong, Simon Graham, Quoc Dang Vu, Phat T. H. Ho, Jeewoo Lim, Mostafa Jahanifar, Nasir Rajpoot, Jin T. Kwak

entry.summary: MiTHras is a pretraining framework combining pseudo-label-guided contrastive learning with masked reconstruction for mitotic figure analysis in pathology, supported by a new corpus of 1.8 million cell-centered images from 14 TCGA cohorts. It achieves the best mean F1 on all evaluated MF classification and subtype benchmarks and outperforms general-purpose pathology models.

entry.title: Read-Best Is Not Steer-Best: A Probing--Steering Layer Dissociation in Omni-Modal Large Language Models

author.name: Yibo Wang, Jisheng Dang, Bimei Wang, Yitao Wu, Wencan Zhang, Hong Peng, Jizhao Liu, Bin Hu, Qi Tian, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: This arXiv paper presents the first causal test of the widely assumed practice of choosing activation-steering injection layers based on where linear probes read concepts most accurately. Across three independently developed omni-modal language models (integrating text, audio, and image into a shared residual stream), the authors show this assumption fails, identifying a probing-steering layer dissociation where reading and intervention rely on different layers. Using emotion as a controlled testbed, they measure layer-wise readability versus steerability across modalities, a finding that matters for anyone using activation steering in multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: The Role of AI in Online Reviews

author.name: Valeria Lerman, Oren Rigbi, Yaniv Dover

entry.summary: The paper introduces an empirical approach using discrete LLM supply shocks (abrupt price and capability changes) and verified versus non-verified review contrasts to identify AI-generated manipulation on platforms, applied to over 13 million Trustpilot reviews. It measures how generative AI supply improvements reshape platform activity where AI content is otherwise unobservable.

entry.title: Apollo Restore: A Foundation LLM for Historical Greek Optimized for Fill-in-the-Middle Restoration of Ancient Greek Texts

author.name: Hope McGovern, Anna Dolganov, Samuel Belkadi, Guillaume Kunsch, Dimitris Vlitas, David A. Smith

entry.summary: Presents Apollo Restore, a 24B-parameter model fine-tuned from Mistral Small with a fill-in-the-middle objective to restore lacunae in fragmentary Ancient Greek texts without oracle knowledge of gap length. Claimed as the first large-scale decoder model for historical Greek (and any ancient Mediterranean language), it exceeds the strongest published models by 1.6x-2.6x on documentary papyri, literary papyri, and stone inscriptions.

entry.title: Block-Sparse Attention with Semantic-Geometric Decoupled Routing

author.name: Xinwei Long, Weigao Sun, Weibo Gao, Pengkun Jiao, Biqing Qi, Feida Zhu, Yiran Zhong, Steven Hoi, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: Addresses training-free block-sparse attention for long-context LLMs by diagnosing why existing routers fail: pooling post-RoPE token representations entangles semantic aggregation with RoPE-induced geometry. The proposed Semantic-Geometric Decoupled Routing shifts semantic aggregation to pre-RoPE space, yielding more accurate query-to-key block routing and hardware-friendly efficiency gains.

entry.title: SoK: Formal Methods for Fact-Checking and Information Integrity

author.name: Nikolaos Kekatos, Theodoros Nestoridis, Charalampos Bratsas, Charalampos Dimoulas, Georgios Konstantinidis, Georgios Malogiannis, Michael Sirivianos, Andreas Veglis

entry.summary: A systematization-of-knowledge paper arguing that automated fact-checking systems lack auditable warrants: records of which evidence settled a verdict, what counterfactuals would change it, and robustness to rewording. It connects formal methods to regulatory demands from the Digital Services Act and AI Act for auditable system behavior.

entry.title: RPMem: Learning Long-Term Recurrent Parametric Memory Across Sessions for LLM Agents

author.name: Fanyu Zhao, Ruike Cao, Liang Dong, Fugen Yao, Jian Xu, Guanjun Jiang, Han Zhang, Yifei Zhao, Yinsheng Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces RPMem, a two-stage memory architecture for long-running LLM agents that compiles each session into a model-independent latent memory and integrates it with retained memory using a task-trained recurrent gating mechanism. Unlike text-based retrieval memory, parametric memory encodes experience directly into model computation, addressing the problem that long-horizon performance degrades as histories grow. It matters because persistent, reusable, backbone-independent memory is a key bottleneck for deploying agents over many sessions.

entry.title: You Can Tell Who's Asking: What the Web's Questions Are Made Of, and Where They Come From

author.name: Calvin Zhou, Vincent McCloskey, Krishna Srinivasan

entry.summary: This large-scale study extracts 13.4B question occurrences from 110 FineWeb snapshots (2013-2025) and tests whether web questions genuinely reflect human intent. It shows that provenance leaves a detectable signal in question form, with a logistic model separating genuine user questions from templated or manufactured ones at AUC 0.725, though performance is much weaker against commerce FAQ text. It also finds that question frequency does not measure demand, challenging a common assumption in QA data curation and benchmark construction.

entry.title: The Answer-Basin Representation Hypothesis: We Are Not Probing or Steering Concepts

author.name: Manjiang Yu, Hongji Li, Zihan Wang, Junwei Chen, Xue Li, Priyanka Singh, Yang Cao, Lijie Hu

entry.summary: Proposes the Answer-Basin Representation Hypothesis, arguing that concept-related linear structures in LLMs arise from the pushforward probability measure over answers: all continuations yielding the same answer form an answer basin whose mass defines this measure. This reframes the Linear Representation Hypothesis and challenges how interpretability research interprets probing and steering results.

entry.title: DolphinBench: Mapping the Pareto Frontier of Agent Memory

author.name: Soumil Rathi, Deshraj Yadav, Taranjeet Singh

entry.summary: DolphinBench is a benchmark that evaluates agent long-term memory through real task completion rather than conversational question-answering, using three knowledge-work personas with roughly 500k tokens of message history each. It also emphasizes the accuracy-cost tradeoff, mapping the Pareto frontier of memory systems instead of rewarding unbounded compute and latency for marginal accuracy gains. This is significant because memory is a critical bottleneck for long-running agents, and existing benchmarks leak retrieval cues and ignore efficiency.

entry.title: Performance vs Consistency: Evaluating a Foundation Model in Lung-RADS Screening

author.name: Benjamin Renoust, Pierre Baudot, Tiffany Foriel, Yousra Haddou, Charles Voyton, Pierre-Henri Siot, Ezequiel Geremia, Danny Francis, Jean-Christophe Brisset, Val\'erie Bourd\`es, Sylvain Bodard, Benoit Huet

entry.summary: This study evaluates MedGemma, a medical foundation model derived from Gemini, and its lung-cancer-fine-tuned variant against twelve radiologists performing Lung-RADS v2022 assessment on the NLST dataset in a multi-reader design. It emphasizes consistency alongside performance, quantifying inter-reader variability in a structured clinical interpretation setting.

entry.title: The Right Future for Action: Learning Action-Relevant Predictive States in World Action Models

author.name: Qiwen Gu, Jifan Li, Bingjie Gao, Rui Chen, Jing Tang, Xiangxiang Chu, Junqiao Zhao

entry.summary: This paper studies generation-free world action models (WAMs), which train with future-video prediction but act from internal video features, and diagnoses what those features must preserve for action decoding. The analysis shows predictable future changes do not necessarily make linear action decoding easier, motivating Action-Relevant Predictive States (ARPS), a compact horizon-conditioned interface between video and action experts. This is a useful conceptual contribution for robot learning and embodied world models, clarifying representation requirements for control.

entry.title: Pay More Attention To Text In High-Resolution MLLMs

author.name: Zhongkuan Mao, Wenzhuo Zhao, Xianjie Liu, Yidong Wang, Zhao Gao, Ronghao Xian, Yao Jiang, Yi Zhang, Liangjian Wen, Keren Fu

entry.summary: This paper argues that failures in high-resolution multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are often misattributed to visual processing, when the real bottleneck may lie in how question text fails to specify the visual evidence needed for localization. The authors introduce EviSpec, a training-free compiler that derives complementary evidence specifications from questions to guide visual search. This reframing of MLLM error sources challenges the prevailing focus on visual interventions like zooming and cropping.

entry.title: MotionJEPA: Preventing Temporal Feature Collapse by Capturing Visual Changes in Latent Space

author.name: Markus Karmann, Shile Li, Christian Intern\`o, Bruno Andreis, David Klindt, Randall Balestriero, Jindong Gu, Philip Torr, Qi Zhang, Peng-Tao Jiang, Hao Zhang, Bo Li, Onay Urfalioglu

entry.summary: MotionJEPA addresses slow-feature bias and latent collapse in JEPA training by introducing DISReg, a regularizer built on an inverse-dynamics-style module that predicts temporal difference-image embeddings without pixel reconstruction, encouraging balanced static and dynamic features. This advances label-free latent world-model learning for video.

entry.title: Benchmarking Off-the-Shelf Multimodal AI Models Against Dermatologists on Patient-Captured Skin Images

author.name: Rian Dolphin, Laura Knowles

entry.summary: The authors evaluate three recently released, low-to-mid-tier multimodal models on diagnosing dermatological conditions from patient-submitted images, comparing against a panel of three certified dermatologists who grade each image. They report four findings, including that these models represent a floor, not a ceiling, of current AI capability in this domain. The study offers practical evidence on whether consumer-accessible multimodal AI is ready for triage-level skin care use.

entry.title: HappyWorld-Bench

author.name: Zhiqi Bai, Junai Cai, Yixin Chen, Jingrun Du, Tao Feng, Wei Gong, Siyuan Huang, Xiao Lin, Jiaheng Liu, Jun Luo, Yongzhe Lyu, Liya Ma, Zenan Meng, Lin Qu, Wenbo Su, Jiaming Wang, Qinghe Wang, Shaofei Wang, Yanghai Wang, Zequn Wang, Ziming Wang, Hu Wei, Jiangtao Wu, Ruiqi Wu, Jiaxin Xie, Yuchi Xu, Ze Xu, Chengting Yu, Liangyu Yuan, Gang Zeng, Yawen Zeng, Xingyao Zhang, Zizheng Zhang, Bo Zheng, Jiancheng Zhu, Song-Chun Zhu

entry.summary: HappyWorld-Bench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating world models on consistency and responsiveness under exploration, interaction, and modification, organized around six hierarchical world capabilities across video, spatial, and embodied tracks. It comprises 1,138 video prompts, 300 spatial scenes, and 254 embodied test cases with an accompanying evaluation harness.

entry.title: PixelDiT2: Representation-Grounded Pixel Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Yongsheng Yu, Wei Xiong, Yichen Sheng, Shiqiu Liu, Jiebo Luo

entry.summary: PixelDiT2 is an end-to-end pixel-space diffusion transformer that decouples representation learning from pixel generation by grounding denoising in a frozen representation prior, avoiding an autoencoder or latent bottleneck. This addresses the slower convergence and lower final quality of pixel diffusion relative to latent diffusion.

entry.title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jiadi You, Qize Yu, Yue Chen, Minghong Cai, Zhide Zhong, Yuran Wang, Bowen Ping, Jiaqi Liang, Zhenhao Shen, Haodong Yan, Yinchuan Li, Ruihai Wu, Xiaojuan Qi, Yingcong Chen

entry.summary: AffordanceWAM is an affordance-aware generative World Action Model representing object-centric spatiotemporal affordances via Scalar Affordance and Affordance Heatmap within generated future worlds, grounding visual prediction in task-relevant interaction regions for action generation. It bridges egocentric human videos and robot action data for generalizable manipulation.

entry.title: Cognitive Action Reasoning for Proactive Robots from Human-Centered Multimodal Observations

author.name: Zhihao Gu, Kechao Zhu, Yuanfeng Wu, Mohan Liu, Ankit Kumar Shaw, ChenDong Hong, Xuanyu Chen, Dengchen Mei, Xu Tianyi, Lin Wang

entry.summary: Formulates Proactive Robot Action Reasoning (ProRobo), an upstream cognitive decision problem where robots infer which action to take from multimodal human and environmental cues without explicit instructions. Introduces the ProAction dataset to support research into proactive embodied assistance, a setting existing robot-learning datasets largely ignore.

entry.title: FRAMES: Failure Recovery And Monitoring of Embodied Skills for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Ajay Vikram Periasami, Xinyuan Luo, Haoyu Li, Xianyi Cheng

entry.summary: Presents FRAMES, a failure-aware supervisory framework for the Unitree G1 humanoid built above a whole-body controller. A planner agent selects parameterized mid-level skills while a vision-language-model-based monitor agent evaluates execution using temporal multi-view observations and structured contact evidence, detecting and recovering from failures during long-horizon loco-manipulation.

entry.title: Stable and Efficient Real-World Online VLA Post-Training via Asynchronous Replay-Anchored Policy Improvement

author.name: Jiarui Yang, Jiajin Zhang, Bin Zhu, Jingjing Chen, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: RAPolicy is a framework for online post-training of VLA models that runs rollout and learning concurrently, grounding critic and actor updates in replayed behavior. The critic learns chunk-level values from recorded actions without predicting next actions, and a one-step flow actor reuses rollout noise with advantage-weighted conditional likelihood for stable improvement.

entry.title: Search, Ground, Plan: Functional Sufficiency for Task and Motion Planning under Incomplete Scene Knowledge

author.name: Narendhiran Vijayakumar, Nav Singhal, Girish Varma, Antony Thomas

entry.summary: Introduces GRAB-TAMP, a foundation-model-based task and motion planning framework that incrementally searches for scene entities, grounds functional roles to valid physical objects, and plans only once a complete joint assignment establishes functional sufficiency. This addresses the gap between language-specified task requirements and the actual physical capability of partially observed scenes. It matters because incomplete scene knowledge is a central obstacle to deploying language-conditioned manipulation in real environments.

entry.title: Elevator-VIGS: Separating Elevator Motion from Robot Motion in Visual-Inertial Gaussian Splatting SLAM

author.name: Rui Zhou, Zihan Zhu, Wei Zhang, Zizhou Luo, Norbert Haala, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: Presents Elevator-VIGS, a visual-inertial 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system that keeps tracking and mapping through elevator rides by estimating the robot's pose in the elevator's coordinate frame and explicitly separating elevator motion from robot motion, resolving the camera-IMU conflict inside moving elevators. This targets a concrete, frequently encountered failure case that causes divergence in existing visual-inertial estimators. The insight of decoupling coordinate frames is clean and broadly applicable.

entry.title: EgoWild2Dex: Learning Dexterous Robotic Manipulation from In-the-Wild Human Experience

author.name: Kunyang Lin, Xutao Wen, Jingxi Lin, Lanyong Lin, Jiaming Liu, Tianshuo Yang, Xianchi Chen, Yue Han, Yiduo Li, Zhanpeng Zhang, Ping Luo

entry.summary: Collects in-the-wild egocentric demonstrations in real-world settings (homes, factories, pharmacies) with head-mounted cameras to supervise dexterous robot manipulation learning, capturing long-tailed objects and skills. Handles visually challenging data including heavy head-motion-induced viewpoint changes. Aligns robot learning supervision with genuine human workflow diversity.

entry.title: What Matters in Designing World Action Models: An Empirical Study

author.name: Chao Tang, Haoqing Wang, Zilang Cen, Weishi Mi, Wei Xia, Fangcheng Liu, Anda Cheng, Yeqing Shen, Xiaohui Cui, Xiaoyuan Zhang, Yehui Tang, Tingguang Li

entry.summary: This empirical study disentangles the bundled design choices in World Action Models (WAMs) for robot control, isolating the contributions of architecture and training strategy. It focuses on questions like what causal structure should govern world modeling versus action generation and in which latent space design decisions matter. Controlled ablation studies of this kind are valuable because the field is rapidly accumulating unified systems whose individual components are hard to compare.

entry.title: Bridge3D: Enabling Vision-Language-Action Models to See and Act in 3D

author.name: Haoxuan Li, Sixu Yan, Lianghui Zhu, Xuanlai Tang, Shikang Wang, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: Bridge3D augments pretrained 2D-centric vision-language-action models with both implicit and explicit 3D geometry guidance: implicit fusion enriches visual tokens with features from 3D foundation models, while an explicit strategy adds direct geometry supervision for action generation. This addresses the limited spatial precision of 2D observations in VLA manipulation.

entry.title: Touch2Robot: Robot Touch in the Human Demonstration Loop

author.name: Shengcheng Luo, Xiaoyang Cheng, Hong Ying, Xiaoying Zhou, Jiaming Jiang, Haoran Guo, Wanlin Li, Ziyuan Jiao, Chenxi Xiao

entry.summary: Touch2Robot lets humans collect demonstrations while observing how the target robot hand would contact the object, capturing human hand motion, tactile-glove measurements, and object motion. These recordings guide object-specific RL policies to reproduce demonstrated object motion while favoring robot-feasible contacts, with learned behaviors distilled to avoid the cost of collecting demonstrations directly on the robot.

entry.title: DualWAM: Dual-System World Action Models for Asynchronous Global Planning and Local Refinement

author.name: Yixin Zheng, Jiangran Lyu, Yuntian Deng, Kai Liu, Yizhou Zhou, Yizhou Wang, Xiaoguang Zhao, He Wang, Zhizheng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces DualWAM, a dual-system World Action Model architecture that decouples broad-horizon world-action generation from high-frequency local refinement. A slower system-2 process periodically establishes a global plan via bidirectional denoising over long world-action chunks, while a wrist-only system-1 produces short-horizon closed-loop actions, addressing the latency-responsiveness tradeoff in WAMs.

entry.title: GVPO++: Group Variance Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training and On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Kaichen Zhang, Yuzhong Hong, Junwei Bao, Hongfei Jiang, Yang Song, Dingqian Hong, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: GVPO is a post-training method for LLMs that integrates the analytical solution of KL-constrained reward maximization into gradient weighting, avoiding the training instability GRPO suffers from importance sampling. GVPO++ extends it to on-policy distillation, with an interpretation of gradients as mean squared error between implicit and actual reward central distances. This targets a key instability in the widely used GRPO family of RL methods.

entry.title: Fewer Steps, Better Actions: Rethinking Flow-Matching Inference for VLA Policies

author.name: Zhipeng Tang, Xinda Chen, Weining Rao, Xiao Li, Wenting Tan, Yuning Wang, Xiao Shi, Xiaofang Zhao

entry.summary: The paper proposes Coda, which reallocates flow-matching integration budget in vision-language-action policies to a single learned endpoint correction: a frozen few-step policy produces a candidate action and a lightweight transformer predicts a residual using observation-prefix caching, training only the corrector. Five-step Coda raises RoboTwin Easy success from 71.64% to 74.68% while reducing cost.

entry.title: Think Locally, Refine Globally for Memory-Efficient 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Jingke Zhou, Chenhang Ma, Zhizhou Zhong, Mingkai Liu, Zhuang Zhou, Yicheng ji, Binghua Su, Bo Cai, Xianliang Huang

entry.summary: LoG-VGGT is a memory-efficient framework for long-sequence 3D reconstruction that uses cross-window attention only at a small subset of transformer blocks, keeping memory bounded while propagating information across temporal windows. A global camera consistency refinement module lets camera tokens interact with compact register tokens to enforce scene-level constraints and mitigate long-horizon pose drift. This makes vision-foundation-model-based 3D reconstruction scalable to long sequences.

entry.title: ForceTwin: Physics-informed Digital Twins for Robotic Manipulation from Instrumented Human Interaction

author.name: Tim Engelbracht, Ren\'e Zurbr\"ugg, Mayank Mittal, Marco Hutter, Marc Pollefeys, Hermann Blum, Zuria Bauer

entry.summary: ForceTwin builds physics-informed digital twins of articulated objects by identifying state-dependent physical parameters such as inertia, friction, and mechanism dynamics from instrumented human interaction, rather than relying on visual or language priors. This yields physically plausible dynamics not captured in standard asset formats, supporting robotic manipulation simulation.

entry.title: Measuring the Checker: Mutation Analysis for GPU-Kernel Benchmark Oracles

author.name: Mingzhe Du, Anh Tuan Luu, Dong Huang, See-Kiong Ng

entry.summary: The paper introduces mutation analysis as an adequacy metric for GPU-kernel benchmark oracles, injecting 10,303 compilable faults into verified CUDA implementations of 188 KernelBench problems and scoring any test protocol by the fraction of faults it detects. The official check misses one in six kill witnesses, exposing weaknesses in correctness checkers that feed leaderboards and RL rewards.

entry.title: Common Cause, Not Cross-Attention: Blocking Visual Shortcuts in Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Jian Xu, Delu Zeng, John Paisley, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: This controlled causal study shows that joint audio-video generators learn a visual shortcut when audio reads video directly via cross-attention or shared latents: they predict sound from spurious appearance-event correlations and collapse when those correlations break at test time. The authors build an AV structural causal model where audio is by construction independent of video nuisance appearance and show architectures enforcing common-cause structure fix the failure.

entry.title: Prioritized Rollouts for Efficient World Model-based Vision-Language-Action Policy Optimization

author.name: Yifei Sheng, Haoxiang Ren, Zhilong Zhang, Haonan Wang, Runjie Xu, Yihao Sun, Nan Tang, Zhichao Wu, Lei Yuan, Haoxin Lin, Yang Yu

entry.summary: Proposes prioritizing world-model rollouts for RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action policies by using policy uncertainty to identify the small subset of states with the greatest potential for policy improvement, reducing the compute cost of model-based RL as VLAs and world models scale.

entry.title: Why Ghost Outputs Teach: A Kernel-Based Understanding of Subliminal Learning

author.name: Zhe Li, Bicheng Ying, Chaosheng Dong, Haibo Yang

entry.summary: Provides a mechanistic account of subliminal learning, where student models acquire task capabilities by matching seemingly unrelated auxiliary teacher outputs without seeing task data. Derives a chained cross-task kernel linking ghost-output supervision to task-prediction changes through shared backbone representations, yielding a unified analytical framework.

entry.title: Matched-Input Estimates Differ in Sign Across Architectures: Auditing EEG Foundation Models on Motor Imagery

author.name: Kevin Zhou, Sparsh Roy

entry.summary: This audit of EEG foundation models LaBraM and CBraMod on motor imagery uses a validation-locked protocol where all design choices are fixed on training-session data only. Surprisingly, every supervised comparator outperformed every foundation-model configuration, and sign flips in matched-input comparisons across architectures reveal that reported transfer results can depend on input-pipeline confounds rather than representation quality. It is a valuable caution about benchmarking practice for BCI foundation models.

entry.title: Context Poisoning as Extreme-Value Attention Interference in Long-Context Language Models

author.name: Meysam Ghaffari, Nina Fatehi, Bhaskar Sen, Nasim Sabetpour, Carlos Morato

entry.summary: The paper formalizes context poisoning, where long-context retrieval accuracy degrades as distractors accumulate, as extreme-value interference in attention. Under a softmax retrieval abstraction it derives a finite-sample bound showing the evidence margin must scale as Omega(sqrt(log N)) in the effective distractor count to hold a fixed accuracy target.

entry.title: Scout: Open-World Species Recognition on the Edge

author.name: Mohammad Mehdi Rastikerdar, Hui Guan, Deepak Ganesan

entry.summary: Scout is an autonomous system that brings VLM open-world recognition to camera traps on edge devices by invoking a cloud VLM intermittently to teach new species to a compact on-device model, operating under tight compute, energy, and bandwidth budgets. Given only deployment location and a seed list, it discovers and adapts to species unknown at deployment. This is a well-motivated systems contribution at the intersection of VLMs, continual learning, and edge computing.

entry.title: Measured Joules, Learned Routes: Learning to Route for Energy-Efficient LLM Serving

author.name: Muhammad Abdur Rab Siddiqui, Daniela Rojas, Chen Yang, Wenqi Cui, Yuanyuan Shi, Yize Chen

entry.summary: Investigates whether adaptive routing across a heterogeneous pool of LLMs can cut inference energy consumption without compromising task performance, profiling candidate models through offline energy measurement. A language-model-based router selects the answer model per query, targeting the growing energy burden of LLM and agentic inference.

entry.title: Latent Telepathy: Multi-Robot Communication with Self-Supervised Perceptual Latents

author.name: Howard Wang, Han Zheng, Cathy Wu

entry.summary: Proposes Latent Telepathy, where each robot in a decentralized team broadcasts the perceptual latent vector it already computes for its own use, produced by a frozen self-supervised joint-embedding encoder shared across the team. Teammates learn to act on these perceptual messages from task reward, conveying what a teammate perceives rather than only kinematic information.

entry.title: OSCAR: Order-aware Scoring and Calibration for AI Rankings

author.name: You Liu, Yue Liu, Quanchao Lu, Nick Shipilov

entry.summary: OSCAR introduces an order-aware framework for scoring and calibrating AI rankings, focusing on systematic presentation effects such as response order in pairwise LLM evaluations. Analyzing released judgments from 18 evaluators, the authors quantify substantial position-driven score differences (an overall difference of about 24 percentage points) and isolate how position sensitivity can distort aggregated rankings. This is significant because LLM-as-judge pipelines underpin many model benchmarks, and uncorrected order biases can materially misrank models.

entry.title: On the Information-Theoretic Limits of Latent-Space Watermarking Through Pretrained Generators

author.name: Jinwan Jeon, Minju Lee, Sung Hoon Lim

entry.summary: This work develops an information-theoretic theory of watermarking generated content by choosing latent inputs through a fixed latent-to-output renderer, deriving rate-key inner and outer bounds and characterizing capacity regions. It provides fundamental limits on how much message content can be embedded through a prescribed latent interface of a pretrained generator.

entry.title: PredActor: Predictive Action Diffusion for Steerable Onboard Humanoid Control

author.name: Lei Ye, Haibo Gao, Yitang Li, Peng Xu, Zetong Jing, Junhan Sun, Fanrong Dong, Ziqi Han, Xue Wang, Jianhua Sun, Cewu Lu, Hao Zhao, Liang Ding

entry.summary: PredActor is a predictive action diffusion policy for humanoid control that combines joint state-action diffusion with an explicit future-state trajectory enabling test-time motion steering, without depending on privileged full-body states. It targets feedback-responsive onboard control where reference motions may exceed tracker capabilities.

entry.title: PII-TRACE: A Benchmark for Context-Aware PII Detection in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations

author.name: Kaiyuan Zhang, Chuan Wang, Joey Zhong, Paul Fryzel, Kyle Polley, Jerry Ma, Ninghui Li

entry.summary: PII-TRACE is the first benchmark assessing PII detection across turns in multi-turn LLM conversations, with 13,148 synthetic dialogues in 13 languages, character-level spans, and coverage of every mention of recurring identifiers. It targets a real operational need, since providers mask PII in logged conversations but existing benchmarks target self-contained records.

entry.title: FLARE: A Full-Lifecycle Dense Supervision Paradigm for Long-Horizon Coding Agents via Generative Reward Model

author.name: Jingxuan Xu, Gang Wu, Yanan Wu, Yutao Mou, Songwei Yu, Tianzhuang He, Zhengshuo Gong, Zhao Liu, Zihang Xu, Wenqiang Zhu, Xinping Lei, Weihao Li, Yuhui Bai, Zhongqiu Wang, Yan Wu, Ariel Deng

entry.summary: Proposes FLARE, a dense supervision paradigm for long-horizon software-engineering agents using a lightweight Generative Reward Model, with an offline causal-diagnostic framework (RADAR) that distills hindsight-free supervision via causal-chain backtracking and online step-level guidance to address the credit-assignment crisis of sparse pass/fail rewards. Aims to salvage failed exploratory trajectories and provide actionable online guidance.

entry.title: LLMs as Linguistic Chameleons: Decoupling Semantics and Structure for Privacy-Preserving Communication

author.name: Yuzhu Mao, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes semantic decoupling for inference-time privacy: replacing original semantics with alternative content while preserving the structure needed for LLM reasoning, implemented in CROSS-MAP, a bidirectional framework that maps private inputs to a different semantic domain before API inference and recovers outputs afterward using locally trained models. This protects privacy-sensitive workflows that rely on remote LLM APIs.

entry.title: GameReplica: A Benchmark for Black-Box Visual Game Replication by Vision-Language Agents

author.name: Boyu Qiao, Zixin Tang, Xiaoshuai Hao, Wenbo Li

entry.summary: GameReplica is a closed-loop benchmark evaluating whether vision-language agents can induce a game's rules purely through visual observation and active interaction — without source code or documentation — and reproduce it as a verifiable executable system, covering perception, exploration, induction, reproduction, and verification. It extends coding-agent evaluation beyond text-specified targets.

entry.title: DriveReferee: Geometric Safety Verdicts Need Not Be Learned for Driving World-Action Models

author.name: Fengcheng Yu, Dhruv Parikh, Junjie Ye, Maulik Bhatt, Thang Vu, Igor Vasiljevic, Vitor Guizilini, Yue Wang

entry.summary: DriveReferee argues that geometric safety checks for generative world-action driving models do not require learned verifiers: the rules (collision, drivable-area) are explicit, and only the scene state is missing at deployment. It proposes recovering that state from the WAM's own generation to provide closed-loop geometric verdicts during training and deployment.

entry.title: An Eternal Irradiance Camera

author.name: Jeremy Klotz, Shree K. Nayar

entry.summary: From a Columbia-style computational imaging group (Klotz and Nayar), an omnidirectional irradiance camera that measures illumination incident on every point of a sphere; the irradiance function is bandlimited and approximated by the first seven spherical harmonic degrees, so a handful of measurements suffice instead of millions of pixels. This enables dramatic efficiency gains and new imaging capabilities.

entry.title: GeoBalance: Geometry-Aware Monitoring and Reconstruction with Asymmetric Optimization for Balanced Multimodal Learning

author.name: Zechang Xiong, Da Li, Rong Yin, Kexin Tang, Biao Yang, Pengyuan Li, Wenkang Kong, Yulan Hu, Shengyu Zhu, Hao Peng

entry.summary: GeoBalance reveals that persistent modality dominance in multimodal classifiers induces a representation-level collapse of the weak modality, termed manifold modality collapse (MMC), where weak-modality representations collapse onto fewer directions. The paper proposes geometry-aware monitoring and asymmetric optimization to detect and reverse this collapse, going beyond loss/gradient rebalancing. A conceptually fresh take on modality imbalance with diagnostic tools.

entry.title: PREM: Prefix-Steered Recurrent Memory for Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Siru Zhong, Qiongyan Wang, Xiaohui Lv, Yuzheng Zhuang, Shuai Tao, Wulong Liu, Haohuan Fu, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: PREM is a memory-token-free framework for frozen VLMs that separates video ingestion from question answering: a recurrent writer distills video streams into a compact 256 KiB associative state, and a question-conditioned readout injects memory-derived K/V steering into prompt prefixes during prefill. This enables write-once, query-many long-video inference under strict token budgets, evaluated across six benchmarks.

entry.title: Applications of Neural Cellular Automata: State of the Art, Challenges and Opportunities

author.name: Nick Lemke, Niklas Ihm, John Kalkhof, Mirko Konstantin, Henry J. Krumb, Daniel M. Lang, Ehsan Pajouheshagar, Ario Sadafi, Arjan Kuijper, Karim Lekadir, Marco Lorenzi, Carsten Marr, Julia A. Schnabel, Anirban Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of Neural Cellular Automata (NCAs), a class of extremely compact neural architectures capable of robust inference at very small model sizes. The review covers NCA fundamentals, applications in medical imaging, image generation, and simulation, and analyzes architectural modifications in terms of efficiency and accuracy. It positions NCAs as emerging low-resource alternatives to convolutional and attention-based models and outlines open challenges and research opportunities.

entry.title: Safety-Critical Control under Uncertainty via Adaptive Conformal Quantile Prediction Intervals

author.name: Hao Zhou, Yanze Zhang, Yiwei Lyu, Wenhao Luo

entry.summary: Develops a safe-control framework using adaptive conformal prediction to construct calibrated, state-dependent prediction intervals, yielding high-probability safety guarantees while avoiding overly conservative or misaligned constraints from symmetric, input-agnostic intervals. This bridges statistical uncertainty quantification with enforceable safety constraints in control synthesis. It is relevant to deploying learning-based controllers in safety-critical settings.

entry.title: BiRoAD: Learning Shared and Role-Adaptive Representations for Bimanual Manipulation

author.name: Yan Shen, Yuchen Liu, Feng Jiang, Hangtian Hu, Xiaoqi Li, Shu Chen, Ruihai Wu, Hao Dong

entry.summary: Introduces BiRoAD for bimanual manipulation, learning shared representations with role-adaptive structure so policies can coordinate two arms while exchanging functional roles across scene configurations, addressing uneven role distributions in demonstrations and the limits of fixed left/right action spaces. This tackles a genuine generalization problem in bimanual learning: how behaviors transform when arm roles swap. Bimanual coordination is a key frontier for general-purpose robot policies.

entry.title: AR-WAM: A Visual-Conditioned Agent-Ready World Action Model for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yicheng Jiang, Zesen Gan, Xiaobo Wang, Tianlun He, Chenxu Zhao, Minghui Wu, Xinyue Wang, Jiaxu Wang, Junhao He, Jianan Wang, Qiming Shao

entry.summary: Proposes AR-WAM, a world action model for manipulation that replaces natural-language instructions with visual grounding prompts (target bounding boxes) and learnable operation tokens, arguing language is an ill-suited interface for agent-driven control. This decouples intent from execution and offers spatially precise conditioning. A notable interface-level redesign for agent-to-robot control.

entry.title: Information-Gain Rewards over Diversity-Pruned Tests: GT-Anchored Verifier Co-Training for Reliable Code Generation

author.name: Ana Nunez, Peyman Najafirad

entry.summary: CoVer is a single-policy GRPO framework that co-trains a model as both coder and test author for code generation RL, addressing permissiveness collapse and concentration bias in self-play test generation. It scores self-generated tests via information gain against a graded ground-truth-anchored correctness signal. This extends RL for code generation beyond fixed test suites with more reliable reward signals.

entry.title: EnterpriseVal: Quantifying the Efficacy, Reliability and Value of Generative AI in the Enterprise

author.name: Abbas Raza Ali, Muhammad Ajmal Siddiqui, Moona Zahid

entry.summary: EnterpriseVal is a use-case-level evaluation system arguing that enterprise GenAI failures are substantially a measurement problem: public benchmarks ask what a model can do, while deployment requires assessing workflow fitness, reliability, and safety on the organization's own data and controls. It provides a formal specification of the use case and frozen socio-technical configuration to ground evaluation decisions.

entry.title: Physically Based Rendering in the Latent Space

author.name: Vuk Radovanovic, Vishesh Gupta, Adrien Gruson, Binh-Son Hua

entry.summary: The authors bridge classical physically based rendering with latent diffusion by performing light transport simulation directly in the VAE feature space, modifying the rendering equation and pairing it with a differentiable renderer to produce latent maps for physically guided image generation. This gives precise physical control over diffusion model outputs.

entry.title: AgentVidBench: A Multi-Hop Video Question Answering Benchmark for Evaluating MLLM Agents

author.name: Seoyeon An, Hyeonseo Jang, Minsu Kim, Chanho Lee, Younghan Park, Kangwook Lee

entry.summary: AgentVidBench is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal LLM agents on multi-hop video question answering that requires spatial, temporal, and cross-modal reasoning over long videos, moving beyond single-step scene-level queries. It targets agentic capabilities such as tool use and multi-step inference grounded in video content. This addresses a real gap in rigorous video-agent evaluation.

entry.title: When Steering Fails in Latent Reasoning: A Latent-to-Language Transition Gap

author.name: Gaoxiang Huang, Lei Qi

entry.summary: This paper shows that activation steering of continuous thoughts in latent chain-of-thought reasoning produces much weaker effects on final language generation than steering explicit CoT, despite comparable representational displacement. The authors propose a latent-to-language transition gap, supported by evidence that output distributions change abruptly at the latent-to-language boundary.

entry.title: A Shared Learning Rate Is Not a Neutral Control in Selective On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Chencheng Zhu

entry.summary: This methodological study shows that the common practice of comparing selective on-policy distillation selectors under a single shared learning rate is not neutral: dense supervision is statistically flat across an 8x learning-rate grid while selective methods move substantially (up to 17.7 pp swings), causing dense-versus-selective verdicts to differ by 2x depending on the chosen rate. Two of six pairwise significance conclusions flip across the grid.

entry.title: CHART: A Harness-Rotation Curriculum for Harness-Robust Search Agents

author.name: Xinlu Zhang, Ying-Chun Lin, Zhihan Zhang, Besnik Fetahu, Xi Chen

entry.summary: The paper documents a fragility of post-trained search agents: behaviors learned under a fixed harness (e.g., a system prompt) overfit to that harness and fail when it changes in production, causing fallback to inferior strategies like serial search. CHART proposes a harness-rotation curriculum that trains agents to retain parallel-search behavior across harness variations.

entry.title: Multi-Armed Bernoulli Bandits via Minimax Single-Arm Stopping

author.name: Huikang Liu, Zhengchao Wang, Daniel Kuhn, Wolfram Wiesemann

entry.summary: Derives an index policy for finite-horizon Bernoulli multi-armed bandits from minimax-optimal solutions to single-arm bandit stopping problems, formulated exactly as semi-infinite linear programs. Indices are built from cumulative continuation probabilities with monotone adjustment and reward-shortfall caps.

entry.title: Testing the Construct Validity of a Functional Valence Axis in LLM Agents

author.name: Weihan Li, Xinlei Chen, Yuhan Song, Xiaofeng Lin, Tianshi Zheng

entry.summary: Investigates whether a contrastive activation direction in LLM agents represents outcome valence or merely a correlated feature, using controlled maze interventions that separate realized outcome from informational history. Directions transfer across outcome encodings but fail to transfer between announced versus unannounced histories, revealing construct limits.

entry.title: Neural Spectral Capacity: Measuring and Designing Architectures from Network Specification Alone

author.name: Chenyu Zhu, Ruoyu Zhao, Zhichao Lu

entry.summary: Proposes Neural Spectral Capacity (NSC), a closed-form capacity scalar based on weight-matrix singular-value spectra that is computable from the architectural specification alone via the Marchenko-Pastur law, without instantiation, data, or gradients. Its additivity enables an exact dynamic-programming solver for architecture design and compression under budgets.

entry.title: RLVR$^{2}$: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rubric-based Ranking

author.name: Hao Li, Zhengkun Zhang, Gangqiang Hu, Zhen Zhang, Yude Gao, Dai Dai, Jing Liu

entry.summary: Identifies that aggregating multi-criterion rubric scores into a scalar reward for RLVR implicitly determines quality-dimension tradeoffs, and that standard normalize-plus-linear-combine assumptions are unreliable. Proposes rubric-based ranking as the reward signal, extending verifiable-reward RL from math/code toward multifaceted quality requirements.

entry.title: Circuit-Diff: Factual Edit-based Intervention Method for Localizing Knowledge in Attribution Graphs

author.name: Edward G. Friedman, Xiangchen Song

entry.summary: Circuit-Diff makes cross-layer-transcoder attribution graphs easier to interpret by intervening on the model with a low-rank factual edit and flagging features whose roles change under the edit as related to the edited knowledge. This automates the otherwise manual process of pruning and hand-labeling attribution-graph nodes during circuit discovery. It is a useful methodological addition to the growing mechanistic-interpretability toolkit built around CLTs.

entry.title: Luck Is Not Skill: When Do Paired Rollouts Help Group-Relative RL of LLM Agents?

author.name: Nazmus Sakib

entry.summary: This work analyzes paired rollouts in group-relative RL for LLM agents, where an event-keyed noise schedule is shared within each group to remove environment-noise variance from reward contrasts. The authors derive an exact condition for when pairing reduces gradient variance, give a counterexample where reward contrasts improve but gradient variance worsens, and validate with a preregistered controlled study on a 2B tool-use agent under tool faults and grader noise.

entry.title: The Undetected Damage of Quantization on Retrieval and How to Fix It

author.name: Luca Zhou, Alessandro Zirilli, Daniele Solombrino, Roberto Dess\`i, Emanuele Rodol\`a

entry.summary: The paper shows that quantized models retaining classification accuracy can still flip 14-46% of top-1 retrieval results, because retrieval lacks the score-gap protection that classification training creates. The authors derive a guarantee that top-1 results survive quantization only when the gap between the two highest scores exceeds twice the largest rounding error, and use the score gap to decide when quantized answers can be trusted and where to spend extra precision.

entry.title: $t_0$: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context

author.name: Lucas Meyer, Claudio Sole, Huikan Xiang, Nicolas Li, Lucas Franceschino, Arnau Quera-Bofarull, Maarten P. Scholl, Joachim Fainberg, Geoffrey N\'egiar

entry.summary: t0 is a family of open-weights time-series foundation models (102M and 256M parameters) that condition forecasts on target history, past covariates, and known-future covariates without task-specific retraining, alternating attention along time and across variates and producing probabilistic quantile forecasts. On GIFT-Eval, t0-beta achieves a CRPS of 0.4738, competitive with larger proprietary models.

entry.title: Correlation-Aware Structured Pruning for Large Language Models

author.name: Sicheng Xu, Hao Shi, Wei Zhang, Haoran Pang, Zhenyu Ming, Hao Wu, Zhongyi Huang, Xin Yao, Gong Zhang

entry.summary: This work proposes a structured pruning method that explicitly models cross-unit dependencies in reconstruction error, formulating pruning as a cardinality-constrained binary quadratic program rather than assuming pruning errors are additive. This addresses the invalidated independence assumption of methods that score channels or heads in isolation, aiming to preserve quality while cutting inference costs.

entry.title: SCoR: A Hierarchical Framework for Forecasting Relations Between Scientific Concepts

author.name: Jingze Wang, Fred Sun, Shangqi Guo

entry.summary: SCoR reframes research-direction discovery as hierarchical scientific-relation forecasting over three temporally aligned tasks: first co-occurrence, first scientific-relation formation, and relation type at formation, moving beyond mere concept co-occurrence. It builds SCoR-Graph from 187,848 cs.CV papers (2017-2026) with 270,687 concepts and 7.45M co-occurrence edges to predict how methods use, combine, replace, or contradict each other.

entry.title: Replicating the Geometry of Emotion Representations in a Base Open-Weights Model

author.name: Adam Hollowell

entry.summary: Replicates a prior study (Sofroniew et al.) that found emotion concepts in Claude Sonnet 4.5 are encoded as vectors mirroring human affect psychology, applying the disclosed methodology to the open-weights base model gemma-2-27b. Using 205,200 newly generated stories, the authors recover the affective circumplex and emotion family clustering with closely matching variance figures. The replication suggests emotion-representation geometry may be a general property of LLM representations rather than specific to one closed model.

entry.title: Do LLMs Choose Like Humans? Using Cognitive Theory to Evaluate LLM Decision-Making

author.name: Johnathan Sun, Andrei Shleifer, Yonatan Belinkov

entry.summary: Evaluates whether LLM context sensitivity aligns with a cognitive-economic theory of human decision-making based on problem categorization and attention allocation, using a novel 140,000-trial product choice benchmark across 12 open-source and commercial models. Context induces human-like shifts in choice and categorization but not in attention reweighting across features, and neither scale nor chain-of-thought reliably attenuates this. The findings suggest LLM decision-making mimics human behavior only superficially.

entry.title: Learning and Control Beyond Linearity: Towards a Non-asymptotic Theory for Bilinear Systems

author.name: Yahya Sattar, Yassir Jedra, Robin Str\"asser, Frank Allg\"ower, Maryam Fazel, Sarah Dean

entry.summary: A tutorial unifying the emerging area of bilinear learning and control, presenting finite-sample learning guarantees for fully and partially observed bilinear systems using tools like one-sided Bernstein inequalities and martingale concentration. It connects these results to nonlinear control, representation learning, and data-driven decision making.

entry.title: Do Student LLMs Inherit OOD Robustness? Invariance-Weighted Distillation for Reliable Knowledge Transfer

author.name: Dileesha Kannangara, Sanghamitra Dutta

entry.summary: The paper identifies two compounding causes of out-of-distribution degradation in distilled LLMs: spurious correlations in distillation data and uniform treatment of samples regardless of whether the teacher is using causal features or shortcuts. It proposes Invariance-Weighted Distillation (IWD), a theoretically grounded reweighting scheme, to make students inherit teacher robustness more reliably. This addresses an underexplored and practically important gap in knowledge distillation for LLMs.

entry.title: Anatomy of a Closed-Loop Collapse: A Causal Case Study of a Compressed VLA Policy

author.name: Fengze Jia (The Ohio State University)

entry.summary: Provides a causal case study of an 8-layer distillation of Octo-Base that passes all offline checks with high teacher ratios yet collapses completely in closed-loop execution (0/72 vs. 40/72 on a simulated pick-and-place task). The analysis shows the collapse is structured: early task stages degrade gradually while transport-to-target fails categorically across all training variants.

entry.title: Machine-Interpretable Information: Compiling Documents into Searchable and Readable Protocol States

author.name: Yifan Wang, Dejing Dou

entry.summary: Introduces Machine-Interpretable Information (MII), an agent-to-agent document-to-state protocol that compiles documents into a canonical fixed-bandwidth 56-token state via a dual-timescale state-space Writer, with a lightweight Translator mapping it into any frozen reader embedding space, reducing query-time cost from O(N^2) to O(K). Aims to close the index-payload schism in retrieval-augmented systems and create architecture-agnostic document states.

entry.title: Why Do Video Diffusion Models Violate Physics? Unveiling the Flaws in Attention Mechanisms

author.name: Yueyan Li, Haibo Wang, Caixia Yuan, Xiaojie Wang

entry.summary: Presents the first interpretability study of the motion planning process in text-to-video diffusion models, showing trajectories form in early denoising stages (first shape, then details) and identifying specific cross-attention heads driving motion planning plus self-attention mechanisms linked to physical violations. Aimed at explaining why SOTA video diffusion models generate physics-violating content internally rather than via external fixes.

entry.title: Exponential Family Synthetic Controls

author.name: Hector Rodriguez-Deniz, David M. Blei

entry.summary: Develops a distributional version of synthetic controls in which each panel cell is a dataset from an exponential family with natural parameters factorizing across units and time, estimated via black-box variational inference. Proposes causal estimands based on divergences between pre- and post-intervention distributions and distributional placebo tests.

entry.title: Not All Task Vectors Need Equal Rank: Energy-Proportional Allocation for Model Merging

author.name: Hyunjoong Cho, Jinhyeok Jang

entry.summary: The paper proposes SERA, a task-adaptive model merging method that allocates rank capacity across task vectors in proportion to their singular-value energy rather than uniformly. Assigning richer spectral capacity to spectrally complex tasks improves merging over uniform-rank spectral baselines.

entry.title: Conformalized Quantile Regression and Minimax Limits of Fixed-Score Calibration under Known Covariate Shift

author.name: Rustam Isaev, Anton Conrad, Denis Belomestny, Eric Moulines, Sergey Samsonov

entry.summary: The paper derives nonasymptotic L-p error bounds for interval length and conditional coverage in split conformalized quantile regression, instantiating them for sparse ReLU networks and extending to covariate shift. It establishes matching minimax upper and lower bounds for fixed-score calibration benchmarks under known covariate shift.

entry.title: TreeSpark: Calibrated, Load-Adaptive Draft Trees for Semi-Autoregressive Speculative Decoding

author.name: Huapeng Zhou, Huayu Wang, Xinyu Wang

entry.summary: TreeSpark improves speculative decoding for block drafters by reading a parent-conditioned distribution from the drafter to build draft trees, replacing per-position marginal ranking that mis-ranks candidates in semi-autoregressive settings, and adapting tree size to per-round and serving-load speculation capacity. This yields better verified acceptance under variable load.

entry.title: EvalMem: An Operation-Level Diagnostic Framework for Long-Term Memory Systems

author.name: Zeyu Liu, Jian Zhong, Rongduo Han, Ziyang Wu, Shunye Tang, Chenghao He, Yaxuan Yang, Yihang Qiu, Ailing Wang, Xiao Liang, Guohuan Xie, Xiaokang Xue, Gongchen Li, Haining Zhang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: EvalMem decomposes evaluation of LLM long-term memory systems into three parallel examiners testing encoding, retrieval, and generation separately, producing fine-grained multi-label defect codes instead of only end-to-end QA accuracy. It also adapts agentic RAG to improve store-level diagnosis. This matters because memory systems are central to long-horizon assistants, and prior evaluation cannot localize failures.

entry.title: LLaDA-PRM: A Bidirectional Step-Level Reasoning Evaluator

author.name: Yiming Feng, Naihao Deng, Yulong Chen, Rada Mihalcea

entry.summary: Shows that bidirectional diffusion-style attention improves step-level reasoning evaluation compared to causal autoregressive evaluators, since earlier steps can be judged in light of downstream consequences. Building on a controlled 54-run comparison, the authors introduce LLaDA-PRM, an 8B bidirectional process reward model achieving strong F1 on MR-MATH-invalid and out-of-distribution benchmarks.

entry.title: BabelArena: A Large-Scale Multilingual Benchmark for LLM Agents

author.name: Peng Kuang, Yuchun Fan, Jiangnan Li, Minghao Wu, Jialong Tang, Hao-Ran Wei, Weixuan Wang, Jianhong Tu, Baosong Yang, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces BabelFlow, a general pipeline that adapts existing agent benchmarks into new languages via runtime-dependency analysis, structure-preserving translation, and multi-layer verification with human review. It yields BabelArena with 16,146 instances from 702 canonical tasks spanning four benchmark families, 13 domains, and multiple languages, addressing the English-centricity of agent evaluation.

entry.title: Human-LLM Deliberation as Interactive Proof: Conditions for Verifiability Without Transparency

author.name: Baotong Zhang, Dean Foster, Jo\~ao Sedoc

entry.summary: Models human-LLM deliberation as an interactive proof between an LLM prover and a resource-bounded human verifier who checks supporting details without access to model internals. It proves anytime-valid soundness against adaptive provers under bounded false-pass and checking-error rates, with a finite-horizon completeness result. This gives formal guarantees for when a user can safely accept LLM claims.

entry.title: ConsistWorld: Evidence Routing for Consistent Multi-Agent World Models

author.name: Qianxun Xu, Xianfang Zeng, Xinyao Liao, Wei Cheng, Gang Yu, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: ConsistWorld extends autoregressive video world models to multiple agents, generating camera-controlled streams of a shared static scene with consistency across independently controlled views and temporal gaps. It routes evidence from committed multi-agent history and peer views via Pose Conditioned Memory Retrieval and Visibility-Gated Peer Sharing.

entry.title: MM-ContextFold: Context Folding for Multimodal Agentic Retrieval

author.name: Yang Tian, Fan Liu, Jingyuan Zhang, Zhenyang Li, Yupeng Hu, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Addresses context explosion in multimodal agentic retrieval, where ReAct-style agents accumulate raw images and interaction history in an ever-growing context. Based on an empirical study of ~10,000 trajectories showing raw images become redundant as cues are textualized, the authors propose a context-folding strategy for managing token-intensive visual content.

entry.title: Algebraic Consistency Alone Does Not Certify Temporal Structure in Latent Action Models

author.name: Di Wen, Ruodi Zhang, Kailun Yang, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: This critique paper shows that additive-composition and antisymmetric-reversal algebraic consistency metrics used to certify latent action models do not actually demonstrate temporal structure: reconstruction drives decoded transitions toward state-feature differences for which the identities hold trivially. Across five domains, an unconstrained trained model already achieves 83-97% of the reported error reductions. An important corrective for evaluation practice in this emerging area.

entry.title: VGGT-Prime: Compute-Adaptive Mixture-of-Heads for Efficient Visual Geometry Transformers

author.name: Abteen Arab, Guile Wu, Chengjie Huang, Dongfeng Bai

entry.summary: VGGT-Prime attacks the quadratic scaling of feed-forward visual geometry models like VGGT by targeting architectural rather than token redundancy: it identifies redundant multi-head attention modules in global-attention layers and replaces them with a compute-adaptive mixture-of-heads. This reduces latency for long multi-view sequences while maintaining reconstruction quality.

entry.title: Bridging Reconstruction and Generation: A Latent Distribution Perspective on Evaluation and Improvement

author.name: Xianghong Fang, Wenjie Shu, Tongda Xu, Wenlong Mou, Dehan Kong, Tim G. J. Rudner

entry.summary: The paper explains why reconstruction FID can correlate weakly or negatively with generation FID in latent generative models, attributing the gap to a latent distribution mismatch between encoder-induced and model-generated latents. It proposes generation-aware reconstruction (GAR), a trajectory that interpolates from standard reconstruction toward generation by perturbing encoder latents and denoising through the generative model. This reframes decoder evaluation and suggests diagnostics for latent generative model quality.

entry.title: Classifier-Free Guidance in Flow Matching: Non-Autonomous Potentials, Overshoot, and Posterior-Mean Control

author.name: Jishen Peng, Zheng Ma

entry.summary: The authors give a geometric account of classifier-free guidance in flow matching by viewing it as a time-varying gradient flow, explaining how strong guidance distorts distributions through mean displacement and trajectory concentration. They propose PMC-CFG, a training-free per-sample method that caps guidance via the model-implied terminal posterior mean without extra network evaluations.

entry.title: Do LiDAR Language Models Really Understand Spatio-temporal Relationships?

author.name: Runyi Yang, Murat Akkoyun, Di Wen, Ruiping Liu, Yufan Chen, Junwei Zheng, Xiaoye Wang, Kailun Yang, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: The paper shows that on existing 4D LiDAR language benchmarks, always selecting the same option nearly matches multiple-choice accuracy, indicating models may not truly understand spatio-temporal relations. It introduces LiDAR-Hallu, a geometry-referenced diagnostic benchmark with 10,000 questions across 150 nuScenes scenes covering object existence, ego-relative position, distance ordering, motion, and temporal localization with rigorous controls.

entry.title: When Wider Views Fail: Stress-Testing Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Daisy Li, Kyle Gao, Quanyun Wu, Hanna Chomko, John S. Zelek, Jonathan Li

entry.summary: This paper systematically stress-tests feed-forward 3D reconstruction models by varying the angular span of sparse input views while holding the input budget fixed, treating viewpoint variation as a controlled distribution shift. It finds substantial degradation with wide spans, producing incomplete surface coverage and geometry unsupported by observations.

entry.title: Simultaneous Forward and Inverse Human-in-the-Loop Optimization

author.name: Kyeongwon Park, Steven H. Collins

entry.summary: Proposes SFIHILO, a method that efficiently infers individual-specific reward functions from human preferences over outcomes while simultaneously identifying a control policy maximizing the learned reward. It is designed for assistive settings where experimental costs limit the number of queries and optimization iterations.

entry.title: Whole-Body UMI: Transferring UMI Manipulation Skills to Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation via Real-Time Motion Generation

author.name: Yuxuan Nai, Leixin Chang, Liangjing Yang, Shuo Yang, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: WB-UMI extends the scalable UMI data-collection paradigm to humanoid whole-body manipulation via an end-effector-conditioned real-time motion generator that decouples whole-body coordination learning from task semantics. A diffusion policy learns coordination from retargeted motion capture independently of the manipulation policy, requiring no body-specific demonstration collection.

entry.title: Fast and Robust Temporal Logic Planning via ADMM-based Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Lukas Pries, Joris Verhagen, Jon Arrizabalaga, Jana Tumova, Markus Ryll, Zachary Manchester

entry.summary: The authors present a fast numerical method for continuous-time motion planning under temporal logic specifications, encoding nonconvex safety and logic constraints as unions of convex sets in a joint feasibility graph. This allows projections and robustness maximization to be reformulated as shortest- and widest-path problems, enabling an ADMM-based splitting solver for smooth, collision-free, spec-satisfying trajectories.

entry.title: Verti-WM: A Physics-Aided Exteroceptive World Model for Off-Road Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chenhui Pan, Tong Xu, Xuesu Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes Verti-WM, a physics-aided world model for off-road robot navigation that recurrently fuses a frozen Transformer for rigid terrain with a neuro-symbolic terramechanics model for deformable terrain, conditioning transitions on exteroceptive data. It replaces costly high-fidelity simulator roll-outs during reinforcement learning policy optimization. This is significant because data collection for vehicle-terrain interaction is a well-known bottleneck in off-road autonomy.

entry.title: HEARTH: An Object-Centric RGB-Thermal-3D Dataset for Temperature-Aware Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yuning Su, Borui Li, Yonghao Shi, Bofei Liu, Xing-Dong Yang

entry.summary: Releases HEARTH, a dataset of 90 physical objects across 18 categories with RGB-thermal-3D captures (145 object states), mapping surface temperatures onto reconstructed meshes via calibration and pose transfer, plus 1,200 demonstrations on LIBERO-derived tasks for temperature-aware finetuning. Temperature is a physical property invisible to RGB that matters for manipulation. Filling the thermal-modality gap in manipulation datasets is a genuinely useful resource contribution.

entry.title: STRIDER: Stepping-Enabled Multi-Gait Hierarchical 3D Loco-Manipulation Framework for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Yuanzhuo Li, Wen Zhao, Zhe Yong, Xiang Meng, Gang Han, Hengle Ren, Xiaoyang Zheng, Zhen Wang, Yijie Guo

entry.summary: Introduces STRIDER, a hierarchical multi-gait humanoid loco-manipulation framework combining terrain-aware 3D stepping logic with foothold selection in the stance-foot frame, AMP-based natural walking, and Cartesian upper-body control, addressing the tension between continuous velocity commands and precise foothold regulation. It also improves imitation distillation to encourage shared representations of heterogeneous skills. Humanoid loco-manipulation with precise foothold control is an active industrial-relevance topic.

entry.title: HapticWAM: Distilling Imagined Touch into a World-Action Model without Inference-Time Tactile Sensing

author.name: Mikhail Sannikov, Ilya Mikhalchuk, Konstantin Gubernatorov, Petr Kovalev, Ogunwoye Faith Oluwatobi, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: HapticWAM is a world-action model whose teacher encodes gel images plus deformation, shear, distributed forces, and contact state into a frozen video backbone, then distills imagined touch into a student policy requiring no fingertip tactile sensing at deployment. Combines heterogeneous tactile encoding, structured contact prediction, and teacher-student distillation. Tackles contact-rich manipulation without tactile hardware costs.

entry.title: Opt2VLA: Force-Aware Vision-Language-Action for Contact-Rich Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation

author.name: Fukang Liu, Yipu Chen, Jaehwi Jang, Danfei Xu, Zsolt Kira, Ye Zhao

entry.summary: Opt2VLA brings explicit force awareness into humanoid whole-body VLA control, since existing humanoid systems use geometric motion goals with motion-tracking controllers and limited force reasoning. Targets contact-rich tasks where similar motions need different force regimes and vision becomes unreliable after contact. Part of an emerging wave of force-aware VLAs for humanoids.

entry.title: Zeva-Ego: Egocentric Mid-Training with In-Context Causal Learning for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Bingjia Huang, Xin Ding, Fu Chen, Kun Li, Wei Sun, Hao Wu, Yunxin Liu, Ting Cao

entry.summary: Zeva-Ego is a unified framework converting egocentric human video into action-centered supervision for VLA mid-training via an Action-Centric Encoder, plus parameter-free in-context adaptation from action-effect feedback at deployment. Scaling egocentric data to 10K hours improves RoboTwin success from 63.8% to 75.3%, matching 2K hours of robot demonstrations, implying an empirical egocentric-to-robot data ratio of roughly 4-5:1. This provides concrete evidence on how cheap human video substitutes for expensive robot data.

entry.title: TACIT: Tactile Contact Supervision for Spatial Attention in Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Yanhou Lai, Fucai Zhu, Ruiqiang Wang, Koichi Hashimoto

entry.summary: TACIT uses measured tactile contacts from teleoperated demonstrations to supervise spatial attention heads in visuomotor policies, removing the need for human point annotation or visual prior models. Gaussian targets over camera point clouds train an attention head whose pooled output conditions a visuotactile diffusion policy, showing improved object-position tracking with only ten demonstrations on real robots.

entry.title: HE-Guardrail: A Homomorphic Guardrail Against Jailbreak Attacks for Encrypted Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Byeongseo Min, Yongwoo Lee, Young-Sik Kim, Yongjune Kim

entry.summary: The paper identifies a security vulnerability in homomorphic-encryption-based LLM inference: confidentiality prevents servers from inspecting encrypted prompts, so malicious clients can submit jailbreak attacks undetected. It proposes HE-Guardrail, a guardrail mechanism that operates directly over encrypted data to detect adversarial prompts while preserving client privacy. This closes a genuine gap at the intersection of privacy-preserving ML and LLM safety.

entry.title: Are Coreset Selection Methods Worth Their Cost?

author.name: Yangze Liu, Zhongyi Han

entry.summary: Introduces an end-to-end benchmark that charges coreset selection and downstream training to the same auditable wall-clock budget across 4 datasets, 11 selectors, 5 fractions, and 3 seeds with over 1,500 released runs. Tests whether budget-aware evaluation favors simple random selection even when each selector gets its most favorable training recipe.

entry.title: Misaligned Clinical Risk Classification and Cost Asymmetry in Open-Weight Large Language Models

author.name: Star S. D. Liu, Xiyu Ding, Robert B. Barrett, Alberto Santamaria-Pang, Nic Dobbins, Harold P. Lehmann

entry.summary: Using a public diabetes dataset, the authors probe how four open-weight LLMs (Qwen-2.5-7B/32B and Llama-3.1-8B/70B) internally represent false-negative versus false-positive cost tradeoffs in clinical risk classification, varying 11 cost ratios across three phrasings. Patient risk is linearly recoverable with AUC around 0.83 and cost direction is recoverable in every model, yet representational shifts in cost direction fail to translate into correspondingly shifted behavioral decisions. This reveals a representational-behavioral misalignment with direct patient-safety implications for clinical LLM use.

entry.title: Fairness Beyond Anonymization? Demographic Leakage in German LLM-Generated Resumes

author.name: Charlotte Leininger, Helena Veit, Matthias A{\ss}enmacher, Andreas Bender

entry.summary: This two-stage audit examines whether LLM-generated German resumes encode recoverable demographic information, using GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, and Qwen 3 models (4B-14B) to generate resumes from real anonymized job-matching data. It addresses a gap under the EU AI Act, where hiring is high-risk, by showing fairness concerns extend beyond explicit decisions to the generated documents themselves.

entry.title: Detecting Agitation Before Behavioral Escalation in Autistic Youth Through Multimodal Wearable Sensing

author.name: Nibraas Khan, Abigale Plunk, John Staubitz, Ingrid Shragge, Jordan Brooks, Suzanne Wright, Alec Brewer, James Dieffenderfer, Alper Bozkurt, Amy Weitlauf, Nilanjan Sarkar

entry.summary: The study collects multimodal wearable data from 15 autistic youth across 30 clinician-annotated sessions, combining inertial, physiological, and vocal signals to predict agitation before behavioral escalation. Four pretrained foundation models, one per modality, are projected into a shared representation for early warning.

entry.title: PixelART: Image-to-Layer Decomposition without Latents or Text-to-Image Pretraining

author.name: Zelin Jia, Zhao Zhang, Zhicong Tang, Yuhui Yuan, Shixia Liu

entry.summary: PixelART is a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer trained from scratch for image-to-layer decomposition into editable RGBA layers, avoiding RGBA-VAEs, pretrained T2I backbones, and layer-specific decoders used by prior diffusion systems. The authors identify a key training property that makes this lighter-weight approach work.

entry.title: RopeFormer: Cross-Trial Adaptation from Interaction History for Dynamic Rope Manipulation

author.name: Menglin Wu, Kaixiang Yao, Shangbo Luan, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Yuxin Chen

entry.summary: Presents RopeFormer, a history-conditioned policy for dynamic rope manipulation that retains cross-trial action-response history as context while keeping weights frozen, requiring no explicit online rope-parameter estimation. In matched simulation across rotation, bimanual, and whipping tasks, retained context improves control versus resetting the same checkpoint, with benefits varying across rope dynamics. Implicit in-context adaptation from interaction history is an emerging and important robot-learning theme.

entry.title: Attention-Aware Routing: Coupling Routing and Attention in MoEs

author.name: Despoina Kosmopoulou, Anastasios Tsetsilas, Efthymios Georgiou, Giannis Karamanolakis, Swastik Roy, Alexandros Potamianos

entry.summary: The paper proposes Attention-Aware Routing (AAR), which augments Mixture-of-Experts routers with temporal and spectral features from attention-weight windows, training only routing parameters while freezing the base transformer. AAR improves GSM8K by 3.37 points over a routing-only SFT baseline on OLMoE and demonstrates that routing and attention form a coupled circuit whose changes propagate across layers.

entry.title: Implicit Rule Induction with Test-Time Task Embeddings in ARC-like Tasks

author.name: Adrien Deli\`ege, Claas Beger, Marc Van Droogenbroeck, Melanie Mitchell

entry.summary: The authors study test-time task embeddings in Vision ARC, introducing a two-step test-time training protocol that first finetunes only the task embedding and then the backbone. They evaluate on ARC-AGI-1, ConceptARC, and controlled datasets with known rules to determine whether success reflects genuine rule induction versus shortcuts. This addresses a fundamental question about abstract reasoning evaluation.

entry.title: PolyBridgeBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Physics-Grounded Bridge Design

author.name: Zicheng Zhao, Dongyin Chen, Rui Xu, Yinghui Xu

entry.summary: PolyBridgeBench is an executable benchmark requiring multimodal LLMs to design complete load-bearing bridge structures from visual scenes and engineering constraints, with deterministic legality checks gating execution in a dynamic physics simulation. It uniquely tests whether models can repair structures after simulator execution exposes failures, going beyond static validity checks.

entry.title: AutoRecLab: Describe the Experiment, Get the Code!

author.name: Moritz Baumgart, Philipp Meister, Justus Krell, Michael Schmidt, Bela Gipp, Joeran Beel

entry.summary: AutoRecLab is an autonomous recommender-systems lab that turns natural-language experiment descriptions into executable code, deriving requirements, building and validating prototypes, and expanding them into full experiments using RAG documentation lookup, static type verification, and execution-steered tree search. It demonstrates autonomous implementation of an explicit-to-implicit feedback conversion study with baseline comparisons.

entry.title: Making Latent Evolution Explicit: Operator-Structured Transitions for World Action Models

author.name: Xiaoxiao Lu, Yunlong Dong, Jiahao Shi, Ye Yuan
