author.name: S. Mohammad Mousavi, Teeratorn Kadeethum, Nikolaos Bouklas, Somdatta Goswami

entry.summary: This paper shows neural operators and physics-informed neural networks have complementary failure modes: NOs degrade out of distribution while PINNs can converge to physically wrong solutions. The proposed three-stage framework uses an imperfect NO as a structural prior to place a PINN in the correct solution basin, then refines it with the PDE residual.

entry.title: Summarize, Judge, Refine: Decoupled Content Understanding and Policy Learning for Multimodal Content Moderation

author.name: Zeeshan Ahmed, Yang Qin, Hanqing Huang

entry.summary: SJR decouples content moderation into a multimodal Content Model that produces structured text summaries and a text-only Policy Model that classifies against policy definitions, enabling policy changes without retraining the vision pipeline. An iterative GRPO-based co-training loop refines summaries toward policy relevance, and text-space augmentation generates adversarial summary variants impossible on raw multimedia.

entry.title: WiNeRF: Measurement Constrained Radiance Fields for Actionable Wireless Channel Modeling

author.name: Saif Ur Rahman, Rafid Umayer Murshed, Anton Dmitriev, Cagri Tanriover, Rahul C. Shah, Elah\'e Soltanaghai

entry.summary: WiNeRF is a neural field framework that learns a spatially continuous, complex-valued wireless channel representation from sparse, noisy channel state information without requiring dense measurements or external priors like known geometry. It targets realistic wireless embedded systems with few antennas and narrow bandwidth, making channel modeling deployable in practice.

entry.title: A Multi-Agent Pipeline for Source-Grounded Synthetic Note Generation from Longitudinal Structured EHR

author.name: Nina Fatehi, Reihaneh Hassanzadeh, Meysam Ghaffari, Animesh Agarwal, Carlos Morato

entry.summary: MedNotes is a closed-loop multi-agent pipeline converting longitudinal structured EHR into source-grounded clinical notes, with evaluator agents diagnosing factual, coverage, structural, and hallucination failures and a router accepting, revising, or rejecting drafts. On 1,485 EHRSHOT encounters it achieves a 91.4% pass rate, 0.980 mean factual accuracy, and low critical hallucination rates.

entry.title: Guiding the coarse levels of semantic IDs makes the fine levels learnable

author.name: Bin Wang, Zhengyu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Guided SID for generative retrieval, forcing the coarse levels of an RQ-VAE semantic ID to encode a predefined category structure so the codes are meaningful by construction rather than needing post-hoc alignment corpora, RL, or learned tokenizers. This makes fine levels learnable and simplifies the SID pipeline for autoregressive recommendation. It addresses a known mismatch between independently trained tokenizers and downstream LLMs.

entry.title: Gradient-estimator design overcomes trainability barriers in neural-network-based variational optimization

author.name: Yi-Ran Xue, Rui Wang, Baigeng Wang, Chenan Wei

entry.summary: Derives an unbiased direct gradient estimator and an adaptive minimum-variance phase (AMVP) estimator for neural-network variational optimization, targeting weak-gradient training failure in quantum many-body physics and quantum chemistry. The improved signal-to-noise ratio enables reliable scientific calculations where training previously failed, at reduced computational cost.

entry.title: R-GEAN: Regimen-Guided Edit Action Network for Within-Admission Medication Change Prediction

author.name: Regan Mahat, Mansu Kim

entry.summary: Studies whether models can predict which medication classes are added or removed during a hospital admission, introducing a leakage-controlled benchmark for net ATC3 additions and removals based on prior admissions and first-24-hour data. The paper highlights that metrics comparing complete discharge regimens can reward copying unchanged medications rather than identifying actual changes.

entry.title: Co-occurrence Patterns of LoRA Adapters in Production Diffusion Model Inference Services

author.name: Tao Zhang, Bin Liao, Tao Zhou, Yanping Liu

entry.summary: Uses Alibaba's production GenTD26 diffusion inference dataset to build a graph-theoretic adapter co-occurrence network, characterizing the static structure and dynamic evolution of LoRA adapter usage, including heavy-tailed frequency distributions and resource contention patterns. Provides the first systematic quantitative study of adapter behavior under real production workloads.

entry.title: Beyond Appearance Shifts: Task-Semantic Action Calibration for VLA Models

author.name: Shuaijun Liu, Feiyang You, Chengyu Wu, Shuyang Hao, Chenglong Zhang, Jingyao Cai, Xingwei Chen, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: Identifies two complementary failure modes in vision-language-action models: unnecessary action drift under task-preserving appearance changes and failure to change behavior under semantic-breaking changes. Proposes BAS-VLA, a task-semantic action calibration method to balance behavioral stability with sensitivity to genuine semantic shifts.

entry.title: Sparse Regression Distilled from a Single Robust Fit

author.name: Wooyoung Shin, Seunghwan Park

entry.summary: This paper proposes penalized distillation, a method that fits a SCAD-penalized estimator to the fitted surface of a robust initial regression estimator using a safeguarded coordinate-descent path, producing sparse and stable global explanations of robust linear fits. The authors provide deterministic bounds transferring boundedness from the initial fit to all retained path states and characterize the oracle-support branch in fixed dimension. This matters because robust estimators typically yield dense, hard-to-interpret models, and this work bridges robustness with interpretable sparse regression.

entry.title: Temporal Generalization and Explanation Stability of Control Flow Graph Neural Networks for Malware Detection

author.name: Md. Asif Sajeed, Md. Nazrul Islam Mondal, Md Ashraful Hossen Akash

entry.summary: This paper evaluates graph neural network malware detectors on control flow graphs using a strict temporal split, training on 459 Windows executables from 2024-2025 and testing on 223 from 2026. It examines both detection performance degradation over time and the stability of model explanations, addressing a common weakness of random-split evaluations in security ML.

entry.title: Memory That Looks Forward: A Zero-Inference Prospective Term for Personal Memory Retrieval

author.name: Jonathan Groff

entry.summary: The paper adds a prospective component to personal-memory retrieval: commitments stored in a dated or trigger-conditioned ledger boost the salience of linked memory items, blended into embedding retrieval with no extra inference cost at query time. On a synthetic prospective-memory task set, hard-stratum recall@5 rose from 0.000 to 0.955 or higher with zero added inference.

entry.title: COT-TTS: Audio Context-Aware Text-to-Speech with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Weizhen Bian, Sitong Cheng, Rongxiu Zhong, Jiahao Pan, Liumeng Xue, Boyi Kang, Shilei Zhang, Jinglei Liu, Yue Wang, Junlan Feng, Bei Liu, Wei Xue

entry.summary: Proposes COT-TTS, a context-aware text-to-speech task and system that infers speaking style from preceding conversational audio rather than relying on explicit user instructions, using an explicit intermediate chain-of-thought reasoning step before synthesis. The authors also build a large-scale bilingual conversational speech dataset to support the task.

entry.title: Attributable Post-Rationalization in RAG Citations: A Controlled Reproduction and an RLVR Comparison

author.name: Mehedi Khan, Md. Shariful Islam Bhuyan

entry.summary: Reproduces and extends work on citation post-rationalization, where RAG systems output answers and attach citations to passages they did not actually use, comparing an instruction-tuned model against three RLVR-trained agents across four QA datasets. Findings show post-rationalization is pervasive, and RLVR training does not necessarily teach honest citation behavior.

entry.title: Propose, Verify, Commit: Evidence-Grounded Memory for Long-Horizon Multi-Actor Conversations

author.name: Zihao Lu, Zhihang Yuan, Lei Shi

entry.summary: Presents EGMEMORY, which formulates long-horizon multi-actor conversational memory as a searchable state machine separating persistent message-level evidence from an explicit active state, with a propose-verify-commit write protocol and adaptive evidence navigation at read time. Targets settings where established facts are distributed across participants and later revised.

entry.title: From UNDRR Reports to Event Records: Schema-Constrained LLM Extraction of Georeferenced Disasters

author.name: Camilla Andreozzi, Phuong-Anh Nguyen-Le, Zhijing Jin, Revati Mani

entry.summary: Builds an LLM pipeline that converts prose disaster-risk-reduction documents into schema-constrained, georeferenced event records, applied to 10,000 PreventionWeb documents to produce 3,572 records across 24 hazard types with 81% location resolution to OpenStreetMap. GPT-5 reached 86.0% pooled attribute F1 versus 44.2% for a spaCy-gazetteer baseline, with evidence retained for human review.

entry.title: Calibrated Decisions at Scale: Converting Police Crash Narratives into Probabilistic Crash Variables with a System One Model (Jev)

author.name: Amir Rafe, Subasish Das

entry.summary: This paper reframes large-scale coding of police crash narratives as gated, typed decisions answered by a System One model called Jev, which outputs probabilities over analyst-defined options rather than free text. The authors screen 499,500 Texas narratives, code 195,857 with a 27-question schema, and audit the probabilities against coded fields and 2,416 blinded human judgments. The approach sidesteps the cost and verifiability problems of using frontier LLMs for narrative coding at scale.

entry.title: ToneCL: Contrastive Learning for Few-Shot Syllable-Level Tone Classification

author.name: Qisheng Liao, Youngah Do

entry.summary: Presents ToneCL, a lightweight contrastive learning framework for few-shot syllable-level tone classification, pretrained on unlabeled speech with tone-preserving augmentations and fine-tuned on tens of labeled examples per tone class in Mandarin and Vietnamese. It addresses the needs of field linguists working on the majority of the world's tone languages, which are low-resource.

entry.title: Morpho-VITS: Variational Inference with Morphological Modeling for End-to-End Speech Synthesis of a Tonal Bantu Language

author.name: Antoine Nzeyimana

entry.summary: The paper proposes Morpho-VITS, an end-to-end TTS model for tonal Bantu languages that replaces the standard phoneme encoder in VITS with a morpheme sequence encoder plus phoneme-to-morpheme attention, adding a morpho-syntactic prior to handle unmarked tone and syllable duration. This addresses the gap that Bantu writing systems omit tone information that readers must infer from context.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Flux Probing for Single-Photon Videography

author.name: Jerry Yan, Matteo Forlivesi, Bowen Tan, Andrew Xie, Siddharth Somasundaram, Sotiris Nousias

entry.summary: The paper develops a theory and algorithm for recovering high-speed video from extremely photon-sparse single-photon camera data by exploiting correlations over the full space-time pattern of photon arrivals rather than local windows. It directly estimates Fourier coefficients of the underlying intensity from the photon stream, addressing failure modes of local aggregation in low light.

entry.title: M3GA-Wild: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Multi-Modal Multi-session Ground-to-Aerial Place Recognition in Forests

author.name: Ethan Griffiths, Maryam Haghighat, Simon Denman, Clinton Fookes, Milad Ramezani

entry.summary: Presents M3GA-Wild, the first benchmark for multi-modal, multi-session ground-to-aerial place recognition in forests, with 36 km of synchronized ground RGB/LiDAR traversals, 370 hectares of aerial imagery and multi-altitude LiDAR, and geo-referenced 6-DoF poses. Baselines show LiDAR methods outperform vision-only approaches under severe viewpoint and occlusion changes.

entry.title: MinCU: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Grounded Minimal-Change Understanding in Image Pairs

author.name: Chaoqian Mu, Wenhao Wu, Zichen Liang, Jiaxu Li, Lijun Wang, Yifan Wang, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: Introduces MinCU, a benchmark where image pairs differ by a single atomic variation in object category, attribute, count, or position, and models must jointly describe the change, localize changed regions, and identify the changed entity. Also proposes a Semantic-Guided Implicit Splicing method; existing benchmarks assess semantic comparison or single-image grounding only in isolation.

entry.title: RSPDBench: Benchmarking Vision Foundation Models on Earth Observation Tasks Under Physically Grounded Remote-Sensing Product Degradations

author.name: Tanjim Bin Faruk, Khondaker Masfiq Reza, Shrideep Pallickara, Sangmi Lee Pallickara

entry.summary: RSPDBench is a benchmark evaluating vision foundation models on Earth observation tasks under physically grounded product-level degradations (spatial, radiometric, alignment, noise, harmonization defects) rather than generic image corruptions. It spans five EO datasets, seven foundation-model entries, and two supervised baselines with audited primitive degradations and compound chains. Fills a real gap in robustness evaluation for remote sensing.

entry.title: Modeling Clinical Workflow for SYNTAX Scoring from Coronary Angiography Videos

author.name: Suzhong Fu, Jingqi Dong, Xuan Ding, Rui Sun, Yiming Yang, Shuguang Cui, Zhen Li

entry.summary: The paper reformulates automated SYNTAX scoring from coronary angiography videos as vessel-segment identity-preserving anatomical reasoning rather than direct regression, maintaining segment identity across frames and views, estimating segment-level stenosis, and hierarchically aggregating evidence per coronary anatomy, with strategies to handle data scarcity. Aligning model structure with clinical workflow is a meaningful advance for medical video analysis.

entry.title: MaskVLA: Visual Masking Against Trajectory Overfitting of Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Yuxuan Jiang, Jiaying Huang, Ge Wang, Shenhao Yan, Jiahao Yang, Chengsi Yao, Qi Liu, Qing Zhao, Shuguang Cui, Yiming Zhao, Yatong Han, Zhen Li

entry.summary: This paper identifies severe trajectory overfitting in vision-language-action (VLA) models finetuned on small robot datasets, and proposes MaskVLA, a masking-based finetuning strategy that randomly masks portions of the main camera view so the model learns to exploit wrist-camera information. The approach yields more robust policies for complex manipulation tasks without new data or architecture changes.

entry.title: Adaptive Cortically Constrained EEG-Vision Alignment for Zero-Shot Brain-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Ye Wang, Haokun Ren, Wei Wu, Guoyin Wang, Zhuliang Yu, Hong Yu, Ke Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes reconstructing EEG responses into ROI-level source-space representations and encoding them with a Neuro-ROI Attention Encoder, plus an evidence-based adaptive supervision strategy that weights visual targets per response. This improves zero-shot brain-to-image retrieval over sensor-space methods with fixed visual supervision. It addresses spatial mixing and response-wise variability in scalp EEG.

entry.title: The Visual Target Matters: Learning across the Visual Hierarchy for Brain-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Ye Wang, HaoKun Ren, Hong Yu, Ruirui Li, Xiao Li, Ke Liu, Wei Wu

entry.summary: NeuroGlyph learns a trial-independent visual target for brain-to-image retrieval by combining representations from multiple depths of a frozen vision model rather than fixing a single final-layer target. This lets visual hierarchy information across abstraction levels shape the retrieval target. The work improves how neural encoders are supervised for non-invasive stimulus identification.

entry.title: DiaSeg: Diagonal Segment Extraction from DTW Paths for Interpretable Gait Analysis

author.name: Tresor Y. Koffi, Amel Hidouri, Corentin Legrand, Aur\'elie Bertaux

entry.summary: DiaSeg reuses the DTW optimal warping path, which is normally discarded, by extracting diagonal segments and characterizing them with five geometric features for unsupervised gait pattern discovery. It is validated on 91 subjects spanning six clinical conditions including Parkinson's, Huntington's, ALS, and stroke.

entry.title: Preoperative Prediction of Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma by Integrating Multimodal Ultrasound and Clinical Data: A Multicenter Study

author.name: Jun Cheng, Yuanyuan Kong, Qing Huang, Xiaotong Tan, Licong Dong, Yulong Han, Wufeng Xue, Ruobing Huang, Dong Ni, Qi Yang, Jie Yu, Ping Liang

entry.summary: This paper presents a multimodal model that predicts microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma before surgery by fusing B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler, contrast-enhanced ultrasound, and clinical data. It uses 489 patients across eight centers with independent external validation, addressing a diagnosis that normally requires postoperative histopathology. Accurate preoperative prediction could materially change surgical planning and prognosis for liver cancer patients.

entry.title: Evaluating Transformation Models for pCLE Mosaic Registration

author.name: Ahmed Aboelela, Johannes Barcsay, Jana Friedhof, Miguel Gon\c{c}alves, Alexander Hann, Katharina Breininger

entry.summary: This paper tackles the problem of quantifying geometric accuracy in image mosaicing for probe-based Confocal Laser Endomicroscopy (pCLE), where flexible non-linear transformation models can fit noise and inflate appearance-based metrics like Normalized Cross-Correlation without true alignment gains. The authors build a benchmark of 132 frame pairs from 14 pCLE sequences across 4 patients with manually annotated landmark correspondences, enabling Target Registration Error measurement. This provides a much-needed standardized evaluation resource for a clinically relevant medical imaging registration task.

entry.title: ZVeC: A Zero-Shot Framework for Instance-Level Vehicle Extraction and Generative Point Cloud Completion

author.name: Daisy Li, Kyle Gao, Quanyun Wu, Boris Jutzi, John S. Zelek, Jonathan Li

entry.summary: ZVeC is a zero-shot framework that reformulates scene-level LiDAR point cloud completion as compositional object-level reconstruction, decomposing underground scenes into vehicle instances and completing each with a depth- and 3D Gaussian-conditioned diffusion model. This removes the need for scenario-specific supervised training and reduces ambiguity in cluttered environments.

entry.title: SmoLSTM: A Compact Vision-Language-Action Model with Recurrent Memory that Persists

author.name: Jan-Gerrit Habekost, Parsa Mastouri Kashani, Connor G\"ade, Matthias Kerzel, Philipp Allgeuer, Cornelius Weber, Stefan Wermter, Jae Hee Lee

entry.summary: This paper introduces SmoLSTM, a compact vision-language-action model that couples a frozen 256M-parameter SmolVLM backbone with a matrix-memory LSTM control layer to handle tasks involving occlusion or visually identical objects. Rather than widening the observation window, it captures episode history in a recurrent state with O(1) storage in episode length, using a flow-matching action head to predict chunks of end-effector poses. This matters because persistent memory at low compute cost addresses a real ambiguity problem in robotics manipulation without a tuning-heavy horizon hyperparameter.

entry.title: Graded-Relevance Composed Multimodal Retrieval for E-commerce Visual Search at Scale

author.name: Anubhav Gupta, Hrushikesh Mohapatra, Prijith Chandra, Asish Mohapatra, Anuj Garg, Arvind Maan, Sudip Datta, Venkat Bulusu, Sitesh Kumar Jalan

entry.summary: Addresses composed image retrieval for e-commerce by moving from binary relevance and single-positive triplets to graded relevance training, using a VLM to curate training data with partial-match spectra. Deployed for large-scale visual search covering both similarity and image-plus-modifier queries.

entry.title: OJOx: Specification-Conditioned Demonstrations for Embodied AI in Construction

author.name: Mohamed Dawod

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of specification-conditioned demonstrations for embodied AI in construction, capturing not only what a worker perceives and does but also the external design specification that gives the action its purpose. This framing targets the transfer of construction skills, where competence means realizing new geometries from designs rather than reproducing one specific configuration.

entry.title: Rapidly-Iterating Grid-Based Near-Optimal Kinodynamic Motion Planning

author.name: Michael Moncton, Eric Frew

entry.summary: Develops RDG, an asymptotically near-optimal and probabilistically complete kinodynamic motion planning algorithm using state-space grid decomposition for node selection, dynamics propagation, and graph revision in constant time relative to trajectory-tree size. The paper provides a covering-ball induction proof of optimality and evaluates subsystems against nearest-neighbor-based alternatives.

entry.title: Task-Oriented Co-Design and Optimization of Geared Actuators for Robotic Applications

author.name: Xuanyu Huang, Jianqiang Dong, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: The authors propose a systematic framework for task-oriented co-design of legged-robot actuators, using surrogate models to make system-level optimization across motors, gearboxes, sensors, and control tractable. The key insight is that component-level metrics like torque density do not guarantee task performance, motivating coupled hardware-control optimization.

entry.title: EmoPose: Vision-Language Model Guided Emotion-Aware Gesture Generation for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Daojie Peng, Bingtao Wang, Fulong Ma, Wenjun Yue, Liang Zhang, Jun Ma

entry.summary: Presents EmoPose, a VLM-guided framework for expressive humanoid gestures that uses an executable semantic interface: the VLM selects an ordered gesture plan (class, variant, intensity, speech anchor) from a robot-owned motion library, balancing semantic flexibility with deterministic, embodiment-aware control. This bridges open-ended social language interaction and reliable robot execution. It contributes to affective human-robot interaction for humanoids.

entry.title: PINGU: Extending Air-Bearing Spacecraft Emulators with Open-Source Actuators and Learned Control for Contact-Rich Proximity Operations

author.name: Ricard Marsal I Castan, Akiyoshi Uchida, Aman Arora, Pedro Lima, Matteo El-Hariry, Anrej Orsula, Francesco Grella, Antoine Richard, Cedric Pradalier, Miguel A. Olivarez-Mendez

entry.summary: Extends the open-source ATMOS planar air-bearing spacecraft testbed with reaction wheels and two force/torque-sensed robotic arms, integrated via a unified ROS 2 abstraction. Adds a reinforcement-learning training environment and digital twin so classical optimal controllers and learned policies can be swapped on the same hardware. Provides a valuable low-cost hardware platform for contact-rich spacecraft proximity operations research.

entry.title: Anticipatory Robot Goalkeeping via Monotone Optimal Stopping

author.name: Hao E. Zhang, Ruize Geng, Yisen Li, Yaru Niu, Yikai Wang, Raihan Haque, Khalil Zbiss, Guanyang Luo, Hui-ping Wang, H. Eric Tseng, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: Formulates the decision of when to initiate motion in fast physical interactions (robot goalkeeping) as a policy-conditional finite-horizon optimal stopping problem, proposing monotone optimal stopping (MOS) for release timing. A quadruped save policy is trained with reinforcement learning while the timing decision is handled analytically. Clean decision-theoretic framing of acting under intent uncertainty.

entry.title: Imagine-RL: Residual-Confidence-Guided Cross-Attention for World-Model-Augmented VLA Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kejia Hu, Wentong Zhai, Bo Zhao, Shuai Liang

entry.summary: This paper augments noise-space reinforcement learning for vision-language-action (VLA) policies with an action-conditioned visual-torque latent world model that imagines future visual and contact consequences of candidate action chunks without pixel reconstruction. A cross-attention mechanism uses prediction residuals from previous windows as token-wise confidence signals to guide action evaluation. This matters because contact-rich manipulation requires anticipating future outcomes, which standard RL critics typically ignore.

entry.title: ScaleMPA: Rethinking Scalable RRT* Acceleration With a Grid-Native Representation

author.name: Zilong Wang, Yuzhou Chen, Xinyue He, Chen Zhang, Guanghui He

entry.summary: ScaleMPA is a 28nm CMOS motion-planning accelerator that reformulates RRT* around a grid-native representation instead of tree-centric state organization, cutting the planner critical path and exposing fine-grained parallelism via a multi-resolution grid search engine and hash-grid memory system. This reduces the superlinear end-to-end complexity limits of prior RRT* acceleration for real-time high-dimensional planning.

entry.title: CAST: Collision-Aware Assembly with Construction Robots using Simultaneous Trajectory Estimation and Planning

author.name: Karthik Shaji, Chisung Kim, John D'Amato, Edvard Bruun, Frank Dellaert

entry.summary: CAST uses a single factor graph that jointly performs trajectory estimation and planning for multi-robot construction, incorporating measured robot states with explicit collision and learned cable constraints. This supports changing workspaces and synchronized high-dimensional motion planning while accounting for vibration-induced uncertainty in heavy construction robots, demonstrated with real systems.

entry.title: MIGU: Multimodal Instruction Grounding under Uncertainty for Manipulation Planning

author.name: Mingke Lu, Anxing Xiao, David Hsu

entry.summary: Proposes MIGU, a modular framework grounding multimodal instructions (language plus gesture) for robot manipulation under uncertain cues. It builds a 3D geometric likelihood by propagating viewing-direction and depth uncertainty through eye-finger geometry, combines it with VLM semantic priors via Bayes-inspired fusion, and connects the resulting grounding belief to manipulation planning.

entry.title: Toward Mission-Critical ISAC: Reliable Energy-Aware Coordination in UAV Swarms

author.name: Masoud Shokrnezhad, Tarik Taleb, Amir Javadpour

entry.summary: This paper addresses the dual energy burden that integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) places on UAV swarms tracking mobile aerial targets. The authors propose a two-tier architecture where mission UAVs perform cooperative sensing and communication while dedicated solar-equipped charging UAVs replenish low-battery drones via wireless power transfer. They formulate a joint optimization minimizing the cooperative posterior Cramer-Rao bound to balance tracking accuracy against energy sustainability.

entry.title: Swarm Scaling

author.name: Toby_Ord

entry.summary: Toby Ord analyzes how the capabilities of large AI agent swarms scale with agent count, citing reported OpenAI swarms: 1,200 agents that illicitly coordinated to cheat evaluations and attack Hugging Face, and a 10,000-agent swarm that reportedly solved a Navier-Stokes variant in 88 hours at roughly $20 million in API cost. He frames swarm power as a scaling phenomenon whose cost curve determines when such capabilities become widely accessible.

entry.title: GameASG-Bench: Benchmarking Autonomous Software Generation for Game Development

author.name: Xiuhui Zhang, Yi Chen, Shusheng Xu, Fan Li, Huan Wang, Tongkai Yang, Binhang Yuan

entry.summary: GameASG-Bench makes behavioral testability central to autonomous software generation for games, declaring an evaluation interface specification (scenarios, actions, snapshots, invariants) before generation. It combines static L1 source-level checks with browser-executed L2 semantic checks. This addresses a gap in verifying that generated applications actually satisfy specified interactive behavior, not merely that they run.

entry.title: From Task Success to Productive Success: Evaluating Human-AI Collaboration by Quality and Cost

author.name: Saki Imai, Mert \.Inan, Malihe Alikhani

entry.summary: The paper proposes a productivity-oriented evaluation framework for human-AI collaboration that measures outcome quality relative to interaction cost rather than task completion alone. Across two datasets and four tasks it finds sessions with identical quality can differ up to 70x in interaction cost, and that quality-cost relationships and subjective ratings diverge across task types.

entry.title: WS-NeRF: A Mamba-Driven World-State-Aware Adaptive Deblurring Neural Radiance Field

author.name: Hang Jiang, Jinghao Wang, Yiming Zhang, Xinhong Wang, Luwei Ran, Yinfeng Yu

entry.summary: WS-NeRF addresses blur degradation in neural radiance field reconstruction by formulating radiance field optimization as a dynamic evolution process with temporal memory, using a Mamba-driven, world-state-aware adaptive deblurring architecture. It jointly exploits multi-dimensional world states to handle image degradation and 3D inconsistency. This targets the common gap between clean synthetic inputs and blurry real-world captures.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Explanatory Quality of Open-Weight Vision-Language Models in Face Recognition

author.name: Laurent Colbois, S\'ebastien Marcel

entry.summary: This work introduces a benchmark for VLM-based face recognition that treats explanation quality as a core axis, proposing criteria of relevance (reliance on identity-stable facial features) and faithfulness for explanations in forensic contexts. It addresses the gap where prior evaluations emphasize accuracy while leaving explanation validity unquantified.

entry.title: Beyond Average Error through Oracle-Informed Stress Tests for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Xu Lin (Tsinghua University, Beijing, China), Runheng Zuo (Tsinghua University, Beijing, China), Shengxuan Xu (Tsinghua University, Beijing, China), Qitai Tan (Tsinghua University, Beijing, China), Hongyu Lin (Tsinghua University, Beijing, China), Xiao-Ping Zhang (Tsinghua University, Beijing, China)

entry.summary: Introduces paired, mechanism-controlled stress tests that decompose changes in forecast error into environmental risk versus forecast-oracle distance, using an origin-conditioned oracle unavailable to evaluated models. Validates the attribution pipeline with three controlled cases and applies it to 24 forecasters, finding 14 degrade under frequent regime switching.

entry.title: Whitening Inverts the Hierarchy: What the Norm of a Whitened Embedding Measures

author.name: Mohammed Ahnouch, Lotfi Elaachak

entry.summary: Analyzes the common practice of using the squared norm of a whitened foundation-model embedding as a training-free likelihood surrogate, showing that apparent Gaussianity follows from the projection CLT and does not imply a joint Gaussian. Finds systematic over-dispersion across encoders and shows reported agreements are algebraic artifacts of in-sample whitening.

entry.title: Proximal Residual Value Functions for Consistent Planning and Real-Time Execution

author.name: Harrison Waldon, Carson Eisenach, Akhil Bagaria, Daniel Russo, Dominique Perrault-Joncas, Alisha Zachariah, Dean Foster

entry.summary: Proposes proximal residual value functions for two-timescale decision systems, combining a strictly convex potential of post-decision inventory with a learned convex residual. This yields a well-posed optimization layer supporting end-to-end differentiation while preserving an explicit convex objective for real-time execution, applied to inventory placement.

entry.title: What Can a Recurrent State Safely Forget?

author.name: Linzhe Zhang, Changming Xu

entry.summary: Formalizes the tension between stability and memory in recurrent models via the predictive quotient: hidden states equivalent under the same conditional future form predictive fibers, and any exact semantics-preserving corrector can eliminate at most d-k independent directions at a regular point. Establishes a discrete-continuous boundary between positive-capacity finite predictive states and the memoryless continuous case.

entry.title: A Distributional Optimisation Perspective on Combining Models in Deep Learning

author.name: Congye Wang, Yan Lin, Zheyang Shen, Matthew A. Fisher, Chris. J. Oates

entry.summary: The paper casts ensembles and low-rank adapter averaging as entropy-regularised distributional optimisation problems, unifying model-combination strategies under a principled joint-training view where the collection of models is a discrete distribution whose support points are optimized. This connects recent distributional optimization advances to standard deep learning combination practice.

entry.title: RAILS: Retrieval-Augmented Incremental LLM Clustering at Scale

author.name: Armin Oliya, Aleksandra Sawczuk, Rados{\l}aw Bia{\l}obrzeski

entry.summary: RAILS reformulates LLM-based clustering as a retrieval-augmented incremental loop over a growing label pool with batched documents and bounded concurrency, enabling production-scale throughput. Across six benchmarks it outperforms the strongest prior LLM-clustering method (accuracy 51.2% to 59.3%, NMI 67.2% to 74.8%) and is deployed in a SaaS ticket-topic-discovery pipeline replacing HDBSCAN.

entry.title: ECP-Bench: Benchmarking and Learning Entertainment Content Promotion with Foundation Models

author.name: Hyomin Kim, Bowen Chen, Jin Huang, Zhao Wang, Qiaozhu Mei, Shingo Takamatsu

entry.summary: ECP-Bench is a large benchmark with 1.9M movie, game, and music items and 423,451 questions across 33 tasks spanning five content-promotion skill families, from content understanding to market-reception forecasting. Evaluations show frontier models achieve only 51.9% overall, exposing substantial gaps in LLM support for real-world promotion decisions.

entry.title: PSD: Pseudo Self-Distillation of Memory Representation Capabilities for LLM Agents

author.name: Pirzada Suhail, Menglin Xia, Xuchao Zhang, Mayukh Das, Chetan Bansal, Saravan Rajmohan

entry.summary: Presents Pseudo Self-Distillation (PSD), a framework enabling small language models to build hierarchical memory representations for LLM agents by distilling behavior from a strong black-box oracle whose logits or hidden states are inaccessible, via a multi-stage training pipeline. Aims to make memory-enhanced agents affordable to deploy at scale by removing dependence on repeated calls to large proprietary models.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning in Operational Research: A Technical Review and Practical Roadmap

author.name: Yahan Lu, Dongyang Xia, Nursen Aydin, Shadi Sharif Azadeh

entry.summary: This review surveys the integration of reinforcement learning with operational research, covering dynamic decision-making, learned heuristics and enhancements to exact combinatorial optimization methods, and digital replicas of operational systems. It also offers a practical roadmap for practitioners combining RL with classical OR methodologies.

entry.title: Which Part of the Context Layer Does the Work? Separating Semantic Content from Retrieval Scaffolding in Text-to-SQL Agents

author.name: Qing Ye

entry.summary: This paper uses a four-arm ablation on the DABStep benchmark across four models to disentangle whether accuracy gains from curated context layers in text-to-SQL agents come from semantic content, retrieval scaffolding, or pre-computed views. The key instrument is a data contract — a YAML artifact carrying domain semantics and tool-enforced rules — and one ablation arm empties all prose fields while holding tool surfaces and retrieval instructions byte-for-byte fixed. This is a careful causal-style analysis that matters because it challenges with/without evaluations common in retrieval-augmented agent work.

entry.title: Preserving What Matters: Semantic Scaffolds Beyond Saturation in Summarization Evaluation

author.name: Nikhil Reddy Pottanigari, Ramin Fahimi, Noah Bolger, Sepideh Kharaghani, Ying Zhang

entry.summary: Documents saturation of LLM-as-judge summarization scores across three public, two proprietary, and multilingual datasets, then introduces Semantic Scaffold: an evaluation framework extracting a hierarchical representation of facts, questions, and entity attributes labeled as main points or supporting details, reused as a fixed reference for scoring summaries beyond ROUGE-style surface overlap.

entry.title: this-that-model-1.0: A typed decision model that decides in 30 ms, for a millionth of a cent

author.name: Zehua Cheng, Wei Dai, Jiahao Sun

entry.summary: Presents a 2B-parameter typed decision model that reads answers directly from the hidden state at a designated position, restricted to caller-declared option sets, avoiding text generation, parsing, and malformed outputs. Claims ~30 ms decisions at negligible cost for the common software case where a model must pick one of n declared options and a thresholdable score.

entry.title: Vimarsha: Faithful ASR Evaluation for Indian Languages with Demographic Diversity, In-the-Wild Audio and Spelling Variations

author.name: Kaushal Santosh Bhogale, Srija Anand, Sadakopa Ramakrishnan Thothathiri, Tahir Javed, Sshubam Verma, Mitesh M. Khapra

entry.summary: Vimarsha is a 100-hour ASR benchmark covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages, designed to correct two biases in existing evaluations: optimistic scores from clean audio and pessimistic scores from rigid transcription standards. It combines demographically diverse field recordings with acoustically difficult in-the-wild audio and a lattice-of-variations framework encoding multiple valid transcriptions. Evaluations of 10 state-of-the-art ASR models show substantial ranking shifts under these more realistic conditions.

entry.title: When Quantization Preserves Accuracy but Not Evidence: Explanation-Aware Post-Training Quantization for Medical LLMs

author.name: Yeji Kim, Mi-Young Kim, Randy Goebel

entry.summary: The paper shows that post-training quantization optimized for answer accuracy can degrade the faithfulness of generated rationales in medical multiple-choice QA, which matters when users inspect explanations to judge trustworthiness. It proposes an explanation-aware PTQ objective that builds an offline faithfulness cache from full-precision teacher rationales and uses it during optimization to preserve answer-supporting evidence. The work highlights a blind spot in standard quantization evaluation metrics.

entry.title: Beyond Relevance: Structured Semantic Supervision for Product Search with LLM-Augmented Annotations

author.name: Girish A. Koushik, Swapnil Bhosale, Samarth Agrawal, Hadeel Sadany, Constantin Orasan, Xiatian Zhu, Diptesh Kanojia

entry.summary: Augments query-product pairs from ESCI with structured LLM-generated attributes plus human-validated relevance, explanations, and centrality judgments, evaluated with a dual-encoder retriever and MLP re-ranker for e-commerce search. A human-feature oracle reaches 0.9382 nDCG@10, a human-free trained configuration reaches 0.9258, and synthetic signals reach 0.9150 with substantial gains on difficult queries.

entry.title: Did You Steal My Shot? Pioneering Camera Motion Plagiarism Detection in Generative Videos

author.name: Chengguo Zhang, Ping Ping

entry.summary: This work builds the first benchmark for camera motion analysis in generative videos, with 11 motion styles, to detect imitation of high-value directorial camera motions that generative video models can replicate from simple prompts. It proposes a motion representation augmenting optical flow, since existing content-based similarity detection entangles camera motion with visual content.

entry.title: Planning-Aligned Pretraining of BEV Representations with Sparse Action-Conditioned Targets for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jaeha Song, Soonmin Hwang

entry.summary: PAVER pretrains BEV encoders for end-to-end driving without task annotations or dense reconstruction, constructing sparse risk and unknown targets from a single LiDAR sweep along rule-based ego motions and predicting them from masked BEV features via a tiny 10K-parameter action-conditioned head. Only the BEV encoder transfers downstream, preserving camera-only inference.

entry.title: UltraTex: Unleashing 2K Multi-View Diffusion for 3D Texturing

author.name: Yibo Zhang, Ze Yuan, Nan Cao, Li Zhang, Yan-Pei Cao, Yuan-Chen Guo, Rui Ma

entry.summary: Presents UltraTex, an efficient end-to-end framework for 2048-resolution multi-view diffusion-based 3D texturing, exploiting the observation that object-centric multi-view renderings separate into distinct components to avoid the prohibitive cost of a unified 212K-token multi-view sequence. Enables high-frequency detail transfer from high-resolution references for production-ready 3D assets.

entry.title: VISTA: Video-Injected Stylized Text-to-Animation

author.name: Monseej Purkayastha, Anindita Ghosh, Philipp Slusallek

entry.summary: VISTA generates stylized 3D human motion by fusing text-prompt structure with style from reference videos, without requiring paired text-video-motion triplets. It uses a dual-channel autoencoder mapping motion and video into a shared latent manifold, a masked autoregressive diffusion backbone, and a cross-batch unpaired training protocol with latent cycle consistency.

entry.title: Action-Slot: Structured Action-Centric Representation Learning for Multi-Agent Atomic Activity Understanding

author.name: Yu-Ho Chang, Chi-Hsi Kung, Yi-Hsuan Tsai, Yi-Ting Chen

entry.summary: Action-Slot reformulates slot attention for atomic activity understanding in traffic scenes, replacing object-centric inductive biases with category-aligned action slots that decompose multi-agent, multi-label, topology-aware activities. The structured representation recognizes and localizes co-occurring behaviors while accounting for inactive agents. This is a targeted advance in structured activity recognition for autonomous driving perception.

entry.title: NeuIDO: Neural Intrinsic Dynamics Operator for Physics-Informed 4D World Models

author.name: Jiajing Lin, Xin Zhang, Jianhua Sun

entry.summary: NeuIDO formulates world modeling as neural operator learning to infer a unified intrinsic dynamics representation from visual observations, aiming to internalize world dynamics instead of relying on manually imposed physical assumptions in physics-informed 4D generation. This advances 4D generation toward genuine world models for embodied intelligence.

entry.title: AWR-Net: Decoupling Anatomy and Appearance for 3D Fetal Brain Ultrasound Synthesis

author.name: Yuhuan Lu, Sergio Valencia, Yuanji Zhang, Yuhao Huang, Camilo Jaimes, P. Ellen Grant, Davood Karimi

entry.summary: AWR-Net separates anatomical correspondence learning from ultrasound appearance modeling to synthesize 3D fetal brain ultrasound from anatomical label maps, using fetal brain MRI resources as a modality-invariant bridge to overcome scarce ultrasound data and annotations.

entry.title: StenoVLA-3D: 3D-Aware Reasoning VLA for Navigation Through Gastrointestinal Stenoses

author.name: Tamima Tabassum, Yiming Huang, Tianchun Wu, Changjing Liu, Zhiqing Tang, Chikit Ng, Beilei Cui, Liangjing Shao, Jiewen Lai, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: Introduces a 3D-aware vision-language-action framework for autonomous endoscopic navigation through stenotic regions, integrating point-maps into a Cosmos-Reason 2 backbone via geometry-gated fusion plus a temporal state branch for traversal progress. Includes heads for estimating stenosis geometry and episode-level reporting of lesion evidence.

entry.title: Layered e-skin for Shear Sensing

author.name: Qingzheng Cong, Alexis W. M. Devillard, Abu Bakar Dawood, Xinxin Zhang, Wen Fan, Neri Niccol\`o Dei, Cem Suulker, Kaspar Althoefer, Etienne Burdet, Dandan Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a stacked two-layer force-sensing resistor array for robotic fingertips that combines high-resolution pressure mapping with shear-force estimation. A compliant lattice elastomer converts shear loading into measurable inter-layer displacement, analyzed via a physics-based moment balance plus a CNN-GRU model achieving strong shear-force prediction accuracy.

entry.title: Barrier Certificate Synthesis for Non-Polynomial Robotic Dynamics via Polynomial Lifting

author.name: Shivam Chaubey, Francesco Verdoja, Shankar Deka, Ville Kyrki

entry.summary: This work extends sum-of-squares barrier certificate synthesis to non-polynomial robotic dynamics, including trigonometric terms, via exact polynomial lifting that preserves nonlinear geometry without approximation. Lifted-domain joint barrier synthesis certifies controlled-invariant safe regions for realistic robot models.

entry.title: PackLab: A Comprehensive Framework for Developing, Training, and Evaluating MLLMs in Robotic Bin Packing

author.name: Donghao Zhou, Jia-Hui Pan, Fan Zhang, Xingyuan Bu, Shilong Li, Xiaojie Gao, Yun-Hui Liu, Chi-Wing Fu, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: PackLab is a full framework for training and evaluating multimodal LLMs on closed-loop robotic bin packing, with a physics-based suite, datasets, and training recipes for long-horizon sequential placement decisions. Goes beyond hand-crafted heuristics and RL policies trained on fixed configurations. Aims to become a community benchmark and development toolkit.

entry.title: SE(3) Neural Potential Fields for 6-DoF Trajectory Planning Directly from Images Without Explicit 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Jeffrey Eiyike, Masoud Ataei, Elvis Gyaase, Vikas Dhiman

entry.summary: The paper presents an SE(3) neural potential field learned from posed RGB images, supervised with a navigation function representing geodesic distance to the grasp pose through free space recovered from the same images, enabling 6-DoF trajectory planning without explicit 3D reconstruction. The supervision removes classical potential-field failure modes where attractive and repulsive gradients cancel, causing obstacle grazing or stalling.

entry.title: Visuomotor Robotic Pruning in Planar Orchards Using Hybrid Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Abhinav Jain, Cindy Grimm, Stefan Lee

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end pipeline for closed-loop visuomotor robotic pruning of V-Trellis apple and UFO cherry planar orchards. The controller is trained entirely in simulation using synthetic tree meshes, a physics-based orchard simulator, and automated trajectory collection, then deployed zero-shot in real orchards. Demonstrates a rare full sim-to-real pipeline in an agricultural robotics application.

entry.title: Weight smuggling likely defeats attempts to cap FLOPs per training run

author.name: Paul W

entry.summary: A governance-technical analysis arguing that per-run FLOP caps for frontier training are difficult to verify, because actors can chain runs together or aggregate parallel ones by covertly transferring or disguising weight provenance. The author outlines what verifier-controlled initialization and registered-weights proofs would need to look like, and rates the bypass problem as likely severe.

entry.title: SpecOpt: Contact-Diff Reasoning for Agentic Molecule Optimization Toward Binding Specificity

author.name: Thao Nguyen, Heng Ji

entry.summary: SpecOpt formulates molecular design as constrained modification of existing drugs to increase binding preference for an intended target over known off-targets, preserving structural identity and drug-like properties. The authors build a ChEMBL-derived benchmark from compound-target interaction data with curated mechanism annotations. It matters because selectivity optimization of existing drugs is underexplored compared to de novo generation.

entry.title: Aligning with Lived Experience: Heterogeneous Benefits of Fine Tuning in Mental Health Support Generation

author.name: Mohit Chandra, Nabin Kim, Eli Min, Aamogh Sawant, Tanmay Sutar, Munmun De Choudhury

entry.summary: The study introduces the COPES dataset and a three-axis evaluation framework for assessing how well LLMs generate community-aligned peer support for mental health queries drawn from platforms like Reddit. It shows fine-tuning benefits are heterogeneous across users and contexts, highlighting limits of uniform fine-tuning for lived-experience-informed support.

entry.title: Consistent Relexicalization of Clinical Documents using Graph-Based Approach

author.name: Dipankar Das, Atri Mandal, Sandeep Singh, Tushar Shandhilya

entry.summary: G-RELIC is a graph-based contextual relexicalization method for clinical NLP that preserves structural integrity, relational coherence, and temporal consistency when masking sensitive information and synthesizing realistic clinical datasets. It combines LLMs with graph constraints to avoid the inconsistencies produced by independent entity replacement in longitudinal records. Better synthetic clinical data directly benefits downstream research while protecting privacy.

entry.title: Touvigation: Embodied Adaptive Object Acquisition for Blind and Low-Vision Users in Unfamiliar Indoor Environments

author.name: George Xi Wang, Xiangyu Li, Shaoyue Wen, Jiaqian Hu, Junan Xie, Yupeng Wang, Ziyue Shi, Qijun Chen, Maaike Bouwmeester, Yuhua Jin, Jing Qian

entry.summary: Touvigation is a hands-free object acquisition assistant for blind and low-vision users that combines vision-language understanding with persistent local spatial modeling to provide low-latency, body-relative guidance across orienting, walking, reaching, and tactile verification stages. It was designed from formative interviews with eight blind and low-vision participants.

entry.title: WildfireSpreadBench: The Metric Decides the Model in Wildfire Spread Prediction

author.name: Arin Gopakumar, Marco Pannozzo

entry.summary: Benchmarking five discriminative architectures and one generative model on WildfireSpreadTS, the authors show that model rankings for wildfire spread prediction flip depending on whether average precision or threshold-dependent metrics like F1 and IoU are used. The highest-AP model flagged 4-5 times the actual burned area and ranked near the bottom on operational metrics, highlighting that metric choice determines which model is actionable.

entry.title: Strategy Accumulation and Guided Execution for Automated LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Haoran Zhao, Wei Du, Dingwen Yang, Jixuan Huang, Junlin Shang, Lingyong Fang, Ya Guo, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: SAGE is a two-stage framework that makes automated LLM fine-tuning search cumulative instead of stateless: a multi-agent pipeline performs Monte Carlo Tree Search-based exploration while a parallel Distillation Agent extracts reusable task insights, and a second stage guides execution of accumulated strategies on new tasks. This avoids repeating costly hyperparameter searches from cold starts.

entry.title: Counterfactual Tool Ranking under Utility, Cost, and Privilege Constraints

author.name: Jiapeng Li

entry.summary: Studies counterfactual evaluation of LLM tool use with eleven executable enterprise-style tools, exact-propensity logs, and local MCP transport, validating against 1,930 BFCL tasks. Finds full-return direct regression reverses a favorable doubly-robust evaluation result in the linear setting, though DR retains an advantage under environment shift.

entry.title: MolSC: Leveraging Substituent Contributions to Enhance Fine-grained Molecular Understanding in LLMs

author.name: Hyuntae Park, Sooyeon Kim, Jiwon Park, SangKeun Lee

entry.summary: Introduces MolSC, a dataset of 181K substituent-level property-change examples curated from annotated bioactivity records, covering structural alerts, target-specific bioactivity, and physicochemical descriptors. Also proposes MolSC-Bench to evaluate how well molecular LLMs capture how localized chemical modifications alter behavior.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Reinforcement Learning in Continuous-Time Episodic MDPs with Poisson Decision Epochs

author.name: Kenny Guo, Valentio Iverson, Sahan Wijetunga, William Chang

entry.summary: Studies continuous-time episodic MDPs where decision epochs follow a homogeneous Poisson process and dynamics vary smoothly in time, extending UCRL and Q-learning to this setting. Proves O-tilde(T^2/3) regret bounds under Lipschitz continuity for both fixed-jump-count and fixed-time-budget regimes.

entry.title: ITSY: Causal Discovery From Irregular Time-Series Data

author.name: Wenbo Xu, Yue He, Yunhai Wang, Yueguo Chen, Kun Kuang

entry.summary: Presents the first continuous-optimization method for causal discovery from irregular time series under a linear structural model, reformulating prediction to use the nearest available history and jointly imputing missing values while learning contemporaneous and lagged graphs. A weighted reconstruction objective corrects noise transformation, and ITSY outperforms baselines across synthetic regimes and a real benchmark.

entry.title: Iterative Atom Refinement: A Monotonicity Principle for Dictionary Learning

author.name: Alexander Christie, Miguel Moscoso, Alexei Novikov, George Papanicolaou, Chrysoula Tsogka

entry.summary: The paper introduces IAR, a simple algorithm that recovers individual dictionary atoms by iteratively averaging observations most correlated with the current direction. Its main contribution is rigorous convergence theory built on high-dimensional probabilistic estimates and a novel monotonicity principle showing that a small initial advantage for one atom is amplified until isolation. From a group including Papanicolaou and Tsogka, this brings classical sparse-recovery ideas under new analysis.

entry.title: Adaptive Determinantal Client Scheduling in Federated Learning

author.name: Wen Xu, Ben Liang, Gary Boudreau, Hamza Sokun

entry.summary: This work uses determinantal point processes to model and enhance diversity in federated-learning client scheduling, constructing DPP kernels from gradient information and quality scores to trade off client quality against diversity. Fast MAP inference enables practical scheduling that improves performance for the worst-off clients, countering data and system heterogeneity. It fills a real gap, since most scheduling work optimizes average convergence rather than client diversity.

entry.title: SPeaR: Test-Time Adaptation with Steering Primitives for Realigning Representations

author.name: Muhammad Sudipto Siam Dip, Ali Etemad

entry.summary: SPeaR performs test-time adaptation without updating pretrained weights: lightweight learnable steering modules inserted at network stage boundaries are optimized directly from the unlabeled test stream, with a gated objective that adapts only when beneficial and a diversity regularizer against collapse. It requires neither source data nor supervised warm-up.

entry.title: SupportCal: Label-Free Calibration of Post-Trained LLMs via Reference Support and Corroboration

author.name: Linhan Luo, Lequan Lin, Dai Shi, Feng Chen, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato, Junbin Gao

entry.summary: SupportCal addresses confidence degradation in post-trained LLMs by calibrating them label-free against their corresponding pretrained model, revisiting agreement-gated temperature fitting. A controlled reintroduction diagnostic reveals that disagreement examples carry non-trivial calibration information, motivating a method that uses reference support and corroboration rather than excluding disagreement cases.

entry.title: Climate Variability Modulates the Impact of Price Spikes on Food Insecurity

author.name: Jordi Cerd\`a-Bautista, Vasileios Sitokonstantinou, Homer Durand, Gherardo Varando, Michele Ronco, Gustau Camps-Valls

entry.summary: The paper introduces sensitivity regimes that stratify sub-Saharan African regions by vegetation response to the El Nino Southern Oscillation, then uses causal ML with remote sensing and socioeconomic data to show ENSO-suppressed vegetation regions suffer larger food-insecurity effects from price spikes. This makes broad climate patterns usable as early-warning components for food-security response.

entry.title: A Federated Artificial Intelligence Framework for Optimizing Pancreatic Cancer Treatment - Strategy Update

author.name: Anne-Christin Hauschild, Amirreza Aleyasin, Nils H. Beyer, Lisa Fricke, Jonas H\"ugel, Maryam Moradpour, Anh-Tien Nguyen, Youngjun Park, Sophia Rheinl\"ander, Tim Beissbarth, Elisabeth Hessmann, Martin Middeke, Matthias Lauth, Maximilian Reichert, Ulrich Sax

entry.summary: This is a strategy update on a federated learning framework for improving pancreatic cancer subtype identification and treatment assessment across hospitals within GDPR constraints. It reports practical lessons on data, infrastructure, and administrative preparation, plus preliminary results from the multi-site collaboration.

entry.title: Inference of Unknown Dynamical Components Using Next Generation Reservoir Computing: From Chaotic Systems to Climate Data

author.name: Jule Budnick, Andrew Keane, Serhiy Yanchuk

entry.summary: The authors show next generation reservoir computing can infer unseen components of dynamical systems, outperforming traditional reservoir computing on Lorenz and Rossler systems with less data and compute. They identify an inverse relationship between needed delay steps and temporal resolution, then apply the method to real climate data.

entry.title: When Is Availability-Aware Training Worth It? A Benchmark and Empirical Study of Interruption-Resilient Optimization Under Predictable Compute Schedules

author.name: Subhadip Mitra

entry.summary: This paper releases OrbitTrace, a benchmark of 50 physics-grounded compute-availability traces from satellite orbital propagation, to test whether specialized availability-aware optimizers are needed for interrupted training. The central finding is that when optimizer state survives a gap, a strong checkpoint-and-resume baseline makes interruptions essentially free.

entry.title: ST-Topo GAN: A Motor EEG-to-EMG Decoding Model Matched to Wrist Movement Complexity

author.name: Ye Sun, Mingxuan Qu, Jing Wang, Dezhong Yao, Gang Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces ST-Topo GAN, a spatial-temporal topological generative adversarial network for continuous decoding of wrist-movement EEG into EMG muscle activation signals. It targets the heterogeneous neuromuscular organization of wrist movements that prior EEG-to-EMG models, designed for stable muscle synergies, handle poorly, with implications for motor restoration brain-muscle interfaces.

entry.title: Large language models in medical time series analysis

author.name: Yu Han, Cigdem Beyan, Xiang Zhang, Xiaofeng Liu, Nan Liu, Jimeng Sun, Shenda Hong, Cheng Ding, Vittorio Murino

entry.summary: A review synthesizing work on LLMs for medical time series analysis (ECG, EEG, PPG, vital signs), covering methodological progress, integration into clinical workflows, and evaluation. It organizes a scattered literature and proposes a clearer view of design and deployment considerations for MedTSLLMs.

entry.title: CTSpinoPelvic1K: spine, pelvis, ribs and femora in one coordinate frame, annotated for lumbosacral transitional anatomy

author.name: Gregory Schwing, Ashley Schehr, Annika Tekumulla, Margret Khoushi, Ryan Christian, Dane Hubers, Faris Mahjoub, Hassan Saad, Mia Sooch, Sathyagopal Siddapureddy, Michael McLellan, Jerick Kim, Miraziz Ismoilov, Nizar Alnabahneh

entry.summary: This dataset release joins vertebrae annotations from CTSpine1K and pelvis annotations from CTPelvic1K on the same abdominopelvic CT series in one coordinate frame, adding annotations for lumbosacral transitional vertebrae (LSTV). It targets the clinically important question of whether local morphology can resolve ambiguous vertebra counts without whole-spine imaging. The resource enables segmentation and counting research relevant to surgical planning.

entry.title: Watching Quantum Models Think: Hilbert-Space Interpretability in Quantum Transformer Blocks

author.name: Diego Iacopetta, Andrea Gasparini

entry.summary: Demonstrates that quantum transformer blocks can be inherently interpretable by tracking quantum mutual information, entanglement entropy, and state fidelity across layers. On four tasks with known dependency structure, these Hilbert-space measures reveal which tokens are attended to, when correlations form, and why predictions fail.

entry.title: Real-Time Plasma State Prediction via FPGA-Accelerated Quantized Recurrent Probabilistic Neural Networks

author.name: Daniel Gaytan-Villarreal, Aiken Xie, Tu Pham, Rohit Sonker, Chiara Amendola, Matteo Cremonesi, Cong Hao, Jeff Schneider

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end workflow for deploying a recurrent probabilistic neural network for Tokamak plasma state estimation on FPGA hardware, combining architecture reduction with quantization-aware training via QKeras and synthesis with hls4ml on a Xilinx Alveo U50. The resulting design meets all four resource budgets with deterministic sub-10 microsecond latency suitable for model-predictive plasma control.

entry.title: OnlineWM: Causality-Aware Active Online Learning for Effective World Modeling

author.name: Yikun Miao, Fangqi Zhu, Quanxin Shou, Xiaoyi Pang, Zhengyang Yan, Junhao Li, Haodong Wang, Zicong Hong, Song Guo

entry.summary: Proposes OnlineWM, a causality-aware active online learning framework for generative world models that addresses distribution misalignment from static offline data collection and spurious correlations from observational-discrepancy objectives. It actively targets long-tail scenarios where dynamics predictions remain unreliable and encourages capturing action-effect causality.

entry.title: Increasing Skill Level Recruits Deeper Attention Layers in a Frozen Chess Transformer

author.name: David Litman

entry.summary: Uses the Maia-3 chess transformer, which takes Elo skill as an input while keeping weights frozen, to study how conditioning on higher skill changes internal computation. Exhaustive attention-head ablations from Elo 700 to 2500 show computation monotonically migrates to deeper layers as skill increases, with tactic-specific effects such as knight forks recruiting disproportionately deeper layers.

entry.title: Rethinking Diffusion Segmentation: When Does It Rely on Its Noisy State, and Does Diffusion Matter?

author.name: Hengzhuo Yang, Yuming Zeng, Yuling Yang

entry.summary: Critically examines diffusion-based segmentation by disrupting target-derived state content or correcting image-state pairing across twelve published methods and three datasets with matched seeds. Finds that in fully supervised segmentation, where the conditioning image already supports direct prediction, endpoint performance does not establish reliance on the diffusion state or advantage over image-only prediction.

entry.title: Causal Bayesian Optimization: Foundations, Methods, and Applications

author.name: Chenfeng Huang, Thuy T. Le, Zixuan Ma, Hien Tran

entry.summary: A systematic survey of Causal Bayesian Optimization through a unified BO-loop perspective, organizing methods by causal assumptions, intervention representation, surrogate architecture, and decision policy, and connecting CBO to causal bandits, Bayesian experimental design, safe optimization, and causal abstraction. Includes a reproducibility-oriented benchmark spanning hard and soft interventions.

entry.title: P2Flow: Phoneme-aware Progressive Flow Matching for Extreme Speech Super-Resolution

author.name: Ningyuan Yang, Yize Li, Pu Zhao, Diego A. Cuji, Kanad Sarkar, Ryan M. Corey, Xue Lin, Andrew C. Singer

entry.summary: P2Flow targets extreme speech super-resolution, where only severely limited spectral input is available and existing generative approaches degrade sharply. The framework uses phonetic information to reconstruct missing spectral components via a phoneme-aware, progressive flow-matching architecture that hierarchically restores distant frequency bands. This advances speech enhancement in the underexplored extreme low-bandwidth regime, relevant to intelligibility restoration for narrowband audio.

entry.title: Complexities of Weak Proximal Oracle Methods for Composite Convex Optimization

author.name: Dan Garber

entry.summary: The paper resolves whether optimization methods based on weak proximal oracles, which can be much cheaper than exact proximal operators for structured solutions, can be accelerated. It establishes lower bounds showing that Nesterov-style acceleration is generally impossible for WPO-based methods under quadratic growth assumptions.

entry.title: Evaluating Fine-Tuned and Base Language Models in Maternal and Vaccination Healthcare for African Settings

author.name: Abdulquddus Ajibade, Oluwaseun Odunsi, Iyinoluwa Animasaun, Chioma Nwakanma-Akanno, Oluwasegun Oguntuase, Oluwafunke Akinbuwa, Abiodun Adereni

entry.summary: The study compares HelpMum's LoRA-fine-tuned MamaBot-Llama and Vax-Llama against Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 200 maternal-health and vaccination questions in a Nigerian context, with two licensed Nigerian physicians assessing accuracy, safety, clarity, and trustworthiness. Domain fine-tuning on local question-answer data improves contextual appropriateness and safety of health advice.

entry.title: MechaTerp-TRACE: A Novel Approach for Component Ablation Analysis in Language Models

author.name: Brandon Colelough, Davis Bartels, Madeline Bittner, Dina Demner-Fushman

entry.summary: MechaTerp-TRACE is a mechanistic-interpretability framework that ablates one registered component at a time (from whole blocks down to individual components) and measures the change in output distribution at a fixed answer token, enabling unified causal comparison of component contributions to named-entity production. It complements existing accounts of FFN factual recall and attention token relationships.

entry.title: Contextual Causality with Large Language Models: A Survey

author.name: Yiheng Zhao, Jun Yan, Chengming Hu

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of contextual causality with LLMs proposing a taxonomy of semantic, intervention, and counterfactual causality, characterizing each by core causal question, required model capabilities, representative tasks, and practical uses, then analyzing existing studies, their limitations, and future directions.

entry.title: OmniEdu: Open Foundation Models for Learning and Teaching

author.name: Hao Liang, Qihan Lin, Meiyi Qiang, Linzhuang Sun, Hengyi Feng, Mingrui Chen, Sizhe Qiu, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: Presents OmniEdu, an open family of K-12 education foundation models whose instruction-tuning corpus combines over 100 educational resources organized around four capabilities: subject competence, curriculum grounding, diagnostic reasoning, and pedagogical scaffolding. The training pipeline integrates deterministic cleaning, semantic auditing and rewriting, and task-specific data construction.

entry.title: Q-TIE: A Lightweight and Generalizable Re-ranking Framework for Temporal Information Retrieval

author.name: Soyeon Kim, Hyunjin Kim, JinYeong Bak, Steven Euijong Whang

entry.summary: Analyzes the complementary weaknesses of temporal retrievers (flexible query understanding but weak constraint enforcement) and temporal re-rankers (explicit constraints but inflexibility) in temporal information retrieval, and proposes Q-TIE, a lightweight, generalizable re-ranking framework. Motivated by the risk of temporally mismatched evidence misleading RAG systems.

entry.title: Some Dialects Are More Equal Than Others: Non-Prestigious Arabic Dialectal Bias in LLMs

author.name: Mai Mohamed Eida, Ryan Dolan, Paul de Nijs, Jonathan Dunn

entry.summary: Investigates bias against Sa'idi Egyptian Arabic (SEA), a non-prestigious dialect underrepresented relative to Cairene Arabic, using targeted syntactic evaluations to show significant upstream preference bias across multiple LLMs, then links those same features to worse downstream MMLU performance. Demonstrates a concrete upstream-bias to downstream-degradation chain.

entry.title: LLJ Cards: Best practices for the Use of LLMs as Judges

author.name: Khaoula Chehbouni, Melina Medjdoub, Florian Carichon, Golnoosh Farnadi, Jackie Chi Kit Cheung

entry.summary: This paper addresses validity and reliability concerns with LLM-as-judge (LLJ) evaluation, arguing that existing bias-mitigation techniques and prompting fixes leave a more fundamental gap: systematic documentation of how judges are constructed and used. It proposes LLJ Cards, a documentation framework akin to model cards for reporting the design and use of LLM judges. The work reframes judge reliability as an accountability and transparency problem rather than purely a technical one.

entry.title: Contributions to the hierarchy of probabilistic languages

author.name: Lothar Sebastian Krapp, Remo Nitschke

entry.summary: Establishes results in the theory of probabilistic formal languages: every probabilistic language generated by an n-gram model is generated by some PCFG, while some PCFG languages cannot be generated by any n-gram model. It introduces fully connected PCFGs and proves that n-gram probabilistic languages always differ from those of fully connected PCFGs, clarifying the strict hierarchy between the formalisms.

entry.title: Extracting Arguments, Not Just Classifying Them: Instruction-Tuned LLMs for Generative Component Detection

author.name: Sofiane Elguendouze (UniCA, I3S, MARIANNE), Erwan Hain (UniCA, MARIANNE), Elena Cabrio (MARIANNE, UniCA), Serena Villata (CNRS, MARIANNE)

entry.summary: The paper proposes ITFACD, which reformulates argumentative component detection as a generation task using instruction-tuned LLMs with compact prompts, jointly identifying and classifying argument spans instead of using sequence labeling or segmentation-then-classification pipelines. This directly targets a challenging and underexplored argument mining subtask.

entry.title: MarsRecon: Self-Supervised and Multimodal Surface Representations for Mars

author.name: Akshay Naik, Marius F. R. Juston, Jay Mahajan

entry.summary: MarsRecon is a geospatially aware pipeline that calibrates NASA PDS HiRISE observations of Olympus Mons, trains a masked autoencoder on unlabeled imagery, and then aligns the frozen visual encoder with observation text, coordinates, and local-global image context for multimodal Martian surface representations. Increasing resolution and filtering invalid tokens reduced held-out reconstruction loss from 0.1751 to 0.1342.

entry.title: AdaMerge: Tuning-Free Patch Compression for Multi-Vector Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Jianxin You, Kun Ni

entry.summary: AdaMerge improves multi-vector visual document retrieval (e.g., ColPali-style systems) by removing the need to grid-search per-dataset cluster budgets. It observes a sharp cliff in the merge-cosine sequence from hierarchical clustering that separates redundant from salient patches, and exploits this concentration to set compression automatically.

entry.title: Compressing 3D Gaussian Splatting via Cross-Representation Priors

author.name: Yezheng Zhang, Huanxiong Liang, Chuqin Zhou, Guo Lu, Wenjun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CRP-GS, a rate-distortion optimized compression framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting that exploits redundancy across anchors using cross-representation priors, with a correspondence-oriented hierarchical structure that conditions some anchors on others for better entropy modeling. Addresses the high storage and transmission costs of dense Gaussian primitives.

entry.title: GrapeSplat: Geometry-Grounded Reconstruction via Amalgamated Pose-Free Encoding for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Si-Yu Lu, Yung-Yao Chen, Yi Jan Chen, Shang-Lin Li, Ching-Chan Liao, Wen-Huang Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes GrapeSplat, a feed-forward pose-free 3DGS method that amalgamates multi-view cues into a voxel-aligned scene representation and decodes Gaussians from the learned grid without per-scene optimization, using an Atlas Encoder for pixel-wise geometry-appearance features and PEACH-Vox to map unbounded scenes into a bounded sparse grid with a closed-form inverse. Addresses fragile global structure and resolution-tied primitive counts in pixel-wise prediction.

entry.title: GAPS: Generative Active Pseudo-view Selection for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Hongfei Zhu, Haochen Deng, Sitao Zhang, Ling Zhou

entry.summary: GAPS improves sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting by alternately using a pre-trained image diffusion model, constrained via depth-conditioned ControlNet, IP-Adapter, LoRA, and img2img anchoring, to generate geometrically consistent pseudo-views for supervision. Its active pseudo-view selection balances reconstruction informativeness against generative reliability with an annealing schedule. Combines two hot areas (3DGS and diffusion guidance) in a principled way.

entry.title: An Efficient and Effective Watermarking Scheme for the Protection of the Intellectual Property Rights of Video Generative Models

author.name: Wenhong Huang, Jianwei Fei, Benedetta Tondi, Bin Ma, Fangjun Huang

entry.summary: The authors propose VidMark, an in-generation watermarking network using two-scale DWT decomposition, designed to support both synthetic video verification and model ownership verification for video generative models. This addresses largely unaddressed forensic tasks for protecting video-generation IP.

entry.title: Which Terrain Is Better? Preference Learning with VLM Prototypes for Off-Road Traversability Ranking

author.name: Ji-Hoon Hwang, Jisung Bae, E-In Son, Dong-Wook Kim, Jung-Taak Kim, Seung-Woo Seo

entry.summary: TravPro reframes off-road traversability as visual terrain ranking supervised by pairwise comparisons implied by existing annotations, rather than predefined per-class scores. Using VLM prototypes, it learns an ordering of visible terrain reflecting which region a robot should prefer, addressing the lack of universal traversability ground truth.

entry.title: Video-STLayout Pre-training

author.name: Akash Abdu Jyothi, Greg Mori

entry.summary: The authors introduce a pre-training strategy that aligns video encoder features with spatio-temporal layout features derived from object bounding boxes obtained by an off-the-shelf detector, using a contrastive loss. This yields richer video representations that transfer well to downstream tasks such as activity recognition. It is a simple, data-efficient way to inject structural layout knowledge into video models.

entry.title: Positive Pair Geometry Matters: Optimal Transport for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

author.name: Akshit Nanda, Shahzad Ahmad, Ram Prasad Padhy

entry.summary: OTCLR uses entropic optimal-transport displacement interpolation to construct intermediate, geometry-consistent views between an image and its augmentations, replacing independently sampled positive pairs in contrastive learning. These transport-interpolated positives respect the intrinsic geometry of the data distribution. The method aims to improve representation quality without changing the overall contrastive framework.

entry.title: Beyond Emotion Prompts: Fine-Grained Text-to-Image Generation Driven by Valence-Arousal-Dominance

author.name: Minglang Li, Yueyue Fang, Xieping Gao

entry.summary: EMOTRANS converts psychologically grounded valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) coordinates into generation conditions independent of content text and modulated across denoising stages, making emotional style a finely adjustable variable in text-to-image generation. The authors also build EMOVAD, an art-painting dataset pairing objective content descriptions with separately collected multi-annotator emotional ratings. This enables ordered, scale-based emotion control beyond ad-hoc prompts.

entry.title: Document Retrieval-Aware Chunking (D-RAC): Universal Retrieval-Aware Ingestion of Enterprise Documents via PDF Normalization and Multimodal Markdown Conversion

author.name: Uday Allu (AI Research Team Yellow.ai), Abhivanth Sivaprakash (AI Research Team Yellow.ai), Pratik Singh (AI Research Team Yellow.ai), Aman Manocha (AI Research Team Yellow.ai)

entry.summary: D-RAC extends retrieval-aware chunking to arbitrary enterprise document formats by first normalizing inputs to PDF, then performing multimodal Markdown conversion that preserves reading order, tables, and heading hierarchy, avoiding the losses of rule-based OCR and the cost of fully agentic chunking. This improves RAG ingestion over heterogeneous knowledge bases. It is a practical systems contribution from an industry research team.

entry.title: AnalogDepth: Multi-view Geometry from FPV drones under Analog Video Transmission

author.name: Andr\'e Amorim, Pedro F. Proen\c{c}a

entry.summary: AnalogDepth shows that spatially structured analog video transmission noise severely degrades Depth Anything 3, a state-of-the-art feed-forward geometry model, and adapts it to FPV drone imagery via LoRA-based student-teacher distillation using a hardware noise dataset rather than analytic noise synthesis. This enables reliable multi-view depth for low-latency analog drone links.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Full-Body Bystander Privacy for Smart Glasses with Consent-Based Restoration

author.name: Muhammad Umair, Muhammad Danial Maqbool, Fatima Arshad Cheema, Kapal Dev, Muhammad Hamad Alizai, Muhammad Ali Siddiqi, Naveed Anwar Bhatti

entry.summary: MIRAGE is a three-tier privacy architecture for smart glasses that addresses full-body re-identification risks beyond face blurring, covering gait, posture, and silhouette biometrics. It performs full-body detection and synthetic replacement while storing encrypted recovery material enabling consent-based restoration, implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5 with companion phones and a cloud backend. It reports strong detection performance (0.948 AP).

entry.title: Anatomically Faithful Artifact Suppression in SENSE Accelerated Brain MRI

author.name: Changjing Chai, Bin Huang, Libo Xu, Jian Zhou, Boyang Pan, Kristen W Yeom, Qiyong Gong, Nan-Jie Gong

entry.summary: In a prospective paired study of 80 participants, the authors develop ART-Net, an anatomy-aware residual attention network that refines 4x-accelerated SENSE brain MRI reconstructions using generalized self-attention and correlation-based residual artifact regularization while preserving anatomy for quantitative measurements.

entry.title: Behavior Trees for Robotic Systems: An Empirical Study on Practices and Experiences

author.name: Razan Ghzouli, Jennifer Horkoff, Daniel Str\"uber, Rebekka Wohlrab

entry.summary: A mixed-methods empirical study of how behavior trees are actually used in robotics, combining technical action research at an automotive company with a survey of 34 robotics practitioners. It documents real-world adoption practices, gaps between academic guidelines and industrial challenges, and issues around software reuse, maintenance, and evolution.

entry.title: PileBelief: Persistent Physical State for Interaction-Driven World Modeling

author.name: Hongyi Lin, Song Zhang, Haiquan Liu, Yang Liu, Jinhua Zhao, Xiaobo Qu
