author.name: Boyuan Zhao, Sifan Zhang, Luping Chen

entry.summary: Bio-MF generates fNIRS signals from EEG for hybrid motor-imagery brain-computer interfaces, using a one-step generative model to avoid slow iterative refinement while preserving physiological fidelity. It enables hybrid BCI operation when paired EEG-fNIRS acquisition is unavailable, with low latency suitable for real-time use.

entry.title: Neural Cellular Automata Learn General Features in their Hidden Channels

author.name: Etienne Guichard, Stefano Nichele

entry.summary: This paper investigates the internal hidden channels of neural cellular automata and introduces a transfer-learning mechanism that injects a pretrained teacher NCA's hidden states into a student to guide early optimization. On few-shot and scale-variant MNIST, NCAs outperform comparable recurrent and feed-forward architectures, suggesting hidden channels encode general features.

entry.title: Joint Domain-Class Modeling for Federated Learning Under Feature Skew

author.name: Sina Najafi, Mostafa Tavassolipour, Seyed Pooya Shariatpanahi

entry.summary: Proposes JDFL, a lightweight optimizer-agnostic federated learning extension for feature skew, inferring client-specific pseudo-domains from local update signals and expanding the classifier head to joint domain-class logits while keeping a shared backbone. Allows representation of domain-conditioned appearance without sharing raw data.

entry.title: Optimal No-Regret Learning for Repeated Prophet Inequality

author.name: Kun Wang

entry.summary: Studies repeated prophet inequalities under prefix feedback with unknown box distributions, giving an efficient algorithm achieving O-tilde(sqrt(T)) regret against the best policy that knows the distributions, matching the lower bound up to log factors. The algorithm combines empirical backward induction with box-specific reach bonuses and a relative-drop aggregation rule.

entry.title: Global Ranks Survive, Selected Heads Shift: BOS-Sink Topology under 4-bit Weight-Only Quantization

author.name: Kuanlin Chen, Chen-Wei Kuo, Cheng-En Ou

entry.summary: Tests whether sink-head maps identified before quantization can be safely reused after 4-bit NF4 PTQ, introducing Sink Topology Consistency metrics that separate global rank preservation, top-k overlap, and layerwise sink-mass shift. Across Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B and Llama-3.2-1B, global ranks survive (Spearman >= 0.980) but top-k overlap drops to 0.619-0.793 with terminal-layer shifts of 6.2-7.9x.

entry.title: Q-DEQ: Discrete Solving and Quantization for Deep Equilibrium Models in Time Series Forecasting under Edge Deployment Coding Constraints

author.name: Ruotong Yang, Hongdong Zhu, Qi Gao, Yin Ma, Hai Wei, Kai Wen

entry.summary: Q-DEQ reformulates the local updates in deep equilibrium model forward solving as discrete optimization, constructing candidate directions from the current state and iteration history and encoding coefficient choices as a QUBO problem solvable with low-bit representations. This targets edge deployment where compact parameter storage and low-bit representations are required. It connects DEQ implicit depth with quantization constraints in a novel way.

entry.title: SCoP: Structured Constraint Parsing for Evidence-Space Control in Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Xiaokun Guo, Zhen Xu, Dongdong Huo, Yanqiu Zhang, Dongjin Yu, Yu Wang

entry.summary: SCoP formulates temporal KGQA as evidence-space control, externalizing anchor-event binding, temporal admissibility, and ordinal selection decisions before answer inference instead of accepting retrieved facts by default. A constraint-centric parsing framework separates answer-seeking event patterns from temporal anchors to exclude locally relevant but invalid facts.

entry.title: To Consolidate or not to Consolidate? Evaluating the Impact of Consolidation in Multi-Reference Training using Peer Reviews

author.name: Maitreya Prafulla Chitale, Ketaki Mangesh Shetye, Yash More, Harshit Gupta, Manav Chaudhary, Manish Shrivastava, Vasudeva Varma

entry.summary: Studies peer-review generation as an intermediate-entropy NLG task where a single input admits multiple valid outputs, showing that single- and multi-reference training paradigms are suboptimal for such tasks. The authors release MERC-36K, a corpus of over 36,000 papers paired with original and consolidated peer reviews, and show that consolidating references into a unified training signal improves results.

entry.title: Open-Jev Judgments on CallScreenBench: Calibrated One-Pass Scam Screening with a Small Language Model

author.name: Simiao Ren, Kidus Zewde, Xingyu Shen, Yuchen Zhou, Dennis Ng, Ankit Raj, Tommy Duong, Yuxin Zhang, Neo Tiangratanakul

entry.summary: Tests JevLite, an open implementation of typed one-pass probability readout, for per-turn scam-call screening: LoRA-tuned Qwen3-4B outputs P(scam) from label-logit softmax, reaching AUROC .974 with calibration error .052 on CallScreenBench, non-inferior to an LLM judge (MiniMax-M3) with no false alarms on legitimate calls and earlier decisions.

entry.title: Event-Frame Fusion for Inter-Frame Segmentation via Event-Guided Motion

author.name: Dalia Hareb, Jean Martinet, Benoit Miramond, Elisabetta Chicca

entry.summary: This work proposes a hybrid architecture combining frame-based and event cameras for semantic segmentation in autonomous navigation, using event-guided motion to recover information lost between standard 20-30 FPS frames. It targets the accuracy gap of event-only methods while gaining the high temporal resolution and dynamic range of event sensing.

entry.title: SPACE: Semantic Projection and Alignment of CLIP Embeddings for Domain Adaptation

author.name: Jo\~ao Renato Ribeiro Manesco, Danilo Samuel Jodas, Douglas Rodrigues, Leandro Aparecido Passos, Jo\~ao Paulo Papa

entry.summary: Proposes SPACE, an unsupervised domain adaptation method that leverages the semantic structure of CLIP's vision-language space, using text descriptions as semantic anchors to align cross-domain samples of the same class even when visual similarity is weak, such as photographs versus sketches. Targets domain shift where existing distribution-alignment methods ignore class-level semantic relationships.

entry.title: AniPrO: Interpretable Anime Image Provenance Detection via Multi-Dimensional Semantic Reasoning

author.name: Yan Liu, Baoxiang Huang, Zi'an Wang, Wenbo Xie

entry.summary: Proposes AniPrO, an interpretable framework distinguishing human-drawn, AI-inpainted, and text-to-image anime images, built on a 15,000-sample balanced set from AnimeDL-2M with structured five-dimensional descriptions, addressing the gap where existing AI-image detectors target photographs and miss anime-specific cues. Relevant to copyright attribution and content governance.

entry.title: ProxyBuild: Text-Guided Structured 3D Building Generation with Mesh-Anchored Procedural Proxies

author.name: Xiang Tang, Ruotong Li, Xiaopeng Fan

entry.summary: ProxyBuild is a hybrid framework for text-guided 3D building generation that introduces Mesh-Anchored Procedural Proxies (MAPP), an intermediate representation anchoring building components onto geometric shells to decouple generation from rule authoring. It aims to combine the editability of procedural modeling with the flexibility of generative models, avoiding non-interactive single-mesh outputs. Relevant to architecture, games, and digital twins.

entry.title: SewFusion: Tailored Generation of Topology and Panel-Level Geometry for Sewing Patterns

author.name: Jiaxin Lin, Xiao Pan, Hangjie Yuan, Luyan Liang, Wan Li, Daquan Feng

entry.summary: SewFusion generates sewing patterns from images and text with a unified autoregressive framework that uses distinct generation mechanisms for discrete pattern topology (next-token prediction) and continuous panel-level geometry, overcoming limitations of diffusion-only and autoregressive-only paradigms. Bridging symbolic structure and continuous geometry is valuable for garment design and 3D cloth simulation.

entry.title: Training-Free Spectral Transductive Refinement for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Classification

author.name: Fahim Rahman, S. M. Tanjeeb Meheran Rohan, Md. Taimum Ibne Sayed, Asaduzzaman Herok, Md. Bakhtiar Hasan

entry.summary: STR is a training-free transductive inference rule for cross-domain few-shot classification that builds a joint k-NN graph over frozen support-query embeddings, maps the episode into normalized-Laplacian spectral coordinates, and iteratively refines class representatives with pseudo-labelled queries. It reduces fragility under domain shift and one-shot supervision purely at test time.

entry.title: TReViS: Temporal Repetition Structure Aware Video Synthesis for Self-supervised Repetitive Action Counting

author.name: Fanqi Yu, Shengming Ma, Stefano Fiorini, Vito Paolo Pastore, Xuan Qi, Vittorio Murino, Cigdem Beyan

entry.summary: TReViS enables self-supervised repetitive action counting by estimating temporal repetition structure from unlabeled video via a Temporal Self-Similarity Matrix and synthesizing new training sequences with realistic repetition patterns and controlled variability. Paired with pseudo-labels, these videos train RAC architectures from scratch without dense temporal annotations.

entry.title: MIGA:Shared-Geometry Gaussian Representation with Implicit Amplitude Modeling for Accelerated 3D Multi-Echo MRI

author.name: Jingran Xu, Yuanyuan Liu, Yanjie Zhu

entry.summary: MIGA reconstructs undersampled 3D multi-echo MRI using shared anisotropic Gaussian geometry across echoes, a coordinate-conditioned multi-output amplitude network, and explicit echo-specific phase variables. This exploits shared anatomy while preserving echo-dependent signal variation under heavy computational and memory constraints.

entry.title: GraphSVR: q-Space--Aware Graph-Based Slice-to-Volume Registration for Diffusion MRI

author.name: Noga Kertes, Daphna Link Sourani, Alex M. Bronstein, Moti Freiman

entry.summary: GraphSVR introduces a q-space-aware graph-based framework for 4D slice-to-volume registration in diffusion MRI, representing slice groups in a way that accounts for diffusion-direction-dependent contrast. Existing sequential or pairwise approaches degrade under sparse gradient sampling or severe motion, which this method targets. It addresses motion corruption in motion-prone populations and time-efficient DWI protocols.

entry.title: INTCORT: Training-Free Spatial Reasoning Enhancement for Vision-Language Models via Input Transformations and Confidence Routing

author.name: Haoran Sun, Jingqi Xu, Yanhui Li, Enci Liu, Kaidi Xu, Yanwei Liu

entry.summary: INTCORT is a training-free framework that improves spatial reasoning in vision-language models by exploiting two findings: geometric image transformations and query reversal can recover incorrect spatial predictions, and correct predictions exhibit higher relation-token confidence. It constructs multiple transformed predictions and routes based on relation-token confidence, avoiding catastrophic forgetting of training-based methods. This offers a cheap enhancement path for existing VLMs.

entry.title: Active Spatial Inspection for Effective and Efficient Embodied Exploration

author.name: Wenbin Wang, Xiang Bai, Yizhao Wang, Hang Sun, Dong Ren, Jie Qin, Qingquan Li, Bing Wang

entry.summary: The ACE framework rethinks embodied exploration with a spatially resolved decision paradigm, coupling evidence-grounded perception with exposure-informed movement so agents can judge whether cues are sufficient or further inspection is needed. This counters early termination or excessive continuation in coarse cue-guided exploration.

entry.title: FinsSim: A Reality-Aligned Integrated Simulation Platform for Underwater Robot Learning

author.name: Yu Zhang, Yuanmingqing Song, Xiangyun Rao, Pangkit Fong, Kunhao Zhang, Chongrong Fang, Jianping He

entry.summary: FinsSim is a simulation platform for underwater robot learning with selectable high-fidelity hydrodynamics backends, standard control baselines, unified learning workflows, multi-sensor fusion localization, and calibrated thruster-hydrodynamics models for sim-to-real transfer. Fills a gap in credible underwater RL simulation. Infrastructure contribution for a underserved domain.

entry.title: BayesianGS-SLAM: Uncertainty-Aware Neural Rendering SLAM via Probabilistic Formulation

author.name: Kyeongsu Kang, Seongbo Ha, Sibaek Lee, Hyeonwoo Yu

entry.summary: BayesianGS-SLAM is an uncertainty-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM framework that estimates predictive color and depth uncertainty during mapping and reuses it across tracking and map optimization, weighting unreliable RGB-D residuals and avoiding redundant updates for well-explained frames. It combines a tractable probabilistic formulation of sensor noise and coverage limits. Uncertainty weighting addresses a known weakness of rendering-based SLAM systems.

entry.title: Distributional Balancing with Machine Learning for Clinical Trial Augmentation Using Real-World Data

author.name: Zern Ke, Mingshi Cui, Gemma Moran, Javier Cabrera

entry.summary: Proposes DBML, a method to augment clinical trial control arms with real-world data patients by matching the covariate distribution of the treatment group against the potential external control pool, rather than unit-level matching. Includes anomaly detection for database units, ML-based distributional balancing, and estimator construction for causal effects.

entry.title: Reducing Barriers to Academic Support: Evaluating a Course-Specific RAG System for Addressing Help-Seeking Disparities in Higher Education

author.name: Andy Gray, Jake Hobbs

entry.summary: The study presents and evaluates Beacon, a course-specific RAG system offering private, immediate, module-aligned academic support in computing education, aimed at students who hesitate to seek help due to anxiety or low confidence. It measures how such a system addresses help-seeking disparities compared to general-purpose generative AI tools.

entry.title: Learning Cardiac Features: ECG Biometrics Across Time and~Exercise

author.name: Luca Thiebaud (AMU, AMU SCI, DIAPRO, LIS), Paul Chauchat (AMU SCI, AMU, LIS, DIAPRO), Mustapha Ouladsine (AMU SCI, AMU, LIS, DIAPRO), St\'ephane Delliaux (AMU, APHM, C2VN)

entry.summary: The paper evaluates ECG biometrics under realistic conditions of exercise-induced stress and cross-session variability, training a Siamese ResNet with late multi-lead fusion on a large dataset extracted from cardiopulmonary exercise tests. It positions biometric discrimination both as an authentication mechanism and as a potential pretext task for self-supervised learning.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning for post-coronagraphic wavefront control

author.name: Manuela Casta\~neda-Medina (LIRA), Yann Gutierrez (LIRA), Johan Mazoyer (LIRA, CNRS), Baptiste Abeloos, Laurent Mugnier, Olivier Herscovici-Schiller

entry.summary: A fully data-driven deep reinforcement learning method controls a deformable mirror for post-coronagraphic aberration correction in simulated high-contrast imaging testbeds, targeting the subnanometric wavefront precision needed for exoplanet direct imaging. It offers an adaptive alternative to traditional focal-plane wavefront control.

entry.title: Federated Deep Clustering Networks for High-Dimensional and Heterogeneous Data

author.name: Morris Stallmann, Charalampos S. Kouzinopoulos, Marcin Pietrasik, Anna Wilbik

entry.summary: This work generalizes deep clustering to federated learning, targeting high-dimensional, non-IID distributed data where existing federated deep clustering methods fail to reliably perform. The proposed federated deep clustering networks aim to learn clustering-friendly representations across private client data.

entry.title: Gricea: An Open Science Platform for Conversational AI Research

author.name: Nikhil Sharma, Yunlin Gong, Xinyang Cheng, Ziang Xiao

entry.summary: Gricea is an open-science platform representing conversational AI studies as configurable, deployable research artifacts that can be run, inspected, shared, and reused. In a replication study it replicated configurations from 93% of eligible CUI 2026 papers while flagging missing information in 96% of papers that hinders faithful replication.

entry.title: Toward Fairness in Machine Learning Models for Predicting Treatment Retention and Premature Discontinuation in Medication for Opioid Use Disorder

author.name: Tongnian Wang, Carolina Vivas-Valencia, Cici Bauer, Yanmin Gong, Kim-Kwang Raymond Choo, Yuanxiong Guo

entry.summary: The study systematically audits algorithmic fairness in ML models predicting retention and premature discontinuation in medications for opioid use disorder, using the U.S. TEDS-D dataset (2015 onward) and testing bias mitigation techniques across patient subpopulations. It addresses an underexplored fairness question in clinically deployed treatment decision support.

entry.title: StationPDE: Station-Oriented Surface PDE Learning for Multi-Station Multivariate Weather Forecasting

author.name: Xiao Wang, Changjian Chen, Rongwen Li, Hongwu Liu, Kun Fang, Zhuo Tang

entry.summary: StationPDE bridges statistical station-level weather forecasting and physics-based PDE models by constructing terrain-aware continuous surface fields from discrete station observations and decomposing evolution into surface wind transport and upper-air inference. This yields interpretable physical dynamics for multi-station multivariate forecasting where traditional PDE weather models are inapplicable.

entry.title: EvoRank: LLM-Guided Evolution of Multi-Objective Learning-to-Rank Pipelines

author.name: Rayhan Patel, Shabaz Patel

entry.summary: EvoRank is an LLM-guided evolutionary loop that autonomously discovers complete learning-to-rank pipelines for multi-objective e-commerce search, beating an Optuna-tuned LambdaMART on held-out queries at low cost (about ten dollars per run) and placing in the top 6 percent of a prior competition. The paper also reports a campaign design lesson about selection-fold overfitting when evolving only training objectives.

entry.title: Task-Aware Hybrid QUBO Optimization for Structured Neural Network Pruning

author.name: Osama Orabi, Artur Zagitov, Hadi Salloum, Viktor A. Lobachev, Yaroslav Kholodov

entry.summary: This work frames structured filter pruning as a QUBO combinatorial optimization problem that combines first-order Taylor and Weight-Fisher sensitivity terms with quadratic interactions capturing filter co-dependence, plus activation-similarity information. A binary encoding controls target pruning cardinality without an explicit quadratic penalty.

entry.title: Complex-valued Phase-Coherent Transformers

author.name: Leona Hioki

entry.summary: The paper shows that complex-valued transformers inheriting softmax attention over raw complex inner products perform near chance, and that the fix is L2-normalizing queries and keys so attention reads cosine similarity at order-one scale. This yields phase-coherent transformers that train successfully on diagnostic tasks like ListOps and Needle, whereas unnormalized or mis-scaled variants fail.

entry.title: Concurrency-Aware Process Model Forecasting with Causal Nets

author.name: Yongbo Yu, Jari Peeperkorn, Johannes De Smedt, Jochen De Weerdt

entry.summary: Extends process model forecasting from directly-follows graphs to causal nets by forecasting time series of relation and binding counts and reconstructing future models with AND/XOR concurrency semantics. Introduces a conformance-checking protocol for partial traces and shows forecasted models approach the conformance of re-mined models on four event logs.

entry.title: LPINNs: First-Layer Gated Localization for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Lakshay Chawla, Hardik Jain

entry.summary: Proposes a minimal architectural change to PINNs: gating the first hidden layer with input-dependent localization functions to give units local receptive fields without domain partitioning. Screens 13 localization families across several PDE benchmarks with paired seeds, finding large improvements on long-domain and high-order problems.

entry.title: CSC: Calibrated Simplicity for Conflict-Aware Social Bot Detection in the LLM Era

author.name: Yipeng Qian, Pengjie Zhao, Chaoxi Niu

entry.summary: Argues that LLM-generated semantic camouflage makes text-only bot detection unreliable and that modality conflict (human-like text with suspicious graph structure) is the key signal. Proposes CSC, which uses calibrated simplicity instead of added graph-side complexity, showing that complexity alone is not the most reliable path to robust detection.

entry.title: Preserving Geometric Integrity in Graph Prompting via Measure-Constrained Optimal Transport

author.name: Xiangyu Wang, Shuo Wang, Ruiyi Fang, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: Introduces MINT, an entropically regularized optimal transport framework for graph prompt learning that formulates node-to-prompt adaptation as a globally coupled allocation problem. A prescribed prompt-side marginal prevents node-adaptive routing from concentrating assignment mass on a few prompts, balancing local geometric compatibility with graph-wide utilization.

entry.title: Actionable Insights from Observational Data: The Case of Advanced Classes in K-12 Education

author.name: Nabit Bajwa, Seth B. Hunter, Sanmay Das

entry.summary: The paper studies the causal effect of enrolling in advanced middle-school classes using a novel district-wide dataset capturing enrollment decisions, academic histories, and outcomes around an open-enrollment policy change. Because enrollment is self-selected, the authors confront the standard observational-data challenge of confounding by student characteristics. It is a careful applied causal-inference contribution to education policy with unusually rich data.

entry.title: ShapeLex: Decoupling Local Shape Symbolization and Global Scale Modeling for Text-Controlled Time Series Generation

author.name: Subo Wei, Jianqi Gao, Mingyan Fan, Shaorong Xie, Xinzhi Wang, Yongpeng Dong

entry.summary: ShapeLex decouples text-controlled time series generation into discrete symbolization of local shapes (rises, spikes, sharp drops) and continuous modeling of global attributes, preserving local structures that single-latent-space paradigms tend to smooth or misplace. It induces a reusable vocabulary of discrete shape units and models global continuous attributes separately. This improves faithfulness of language-conditioned synthetic time series to real distributions.

entry.title: PAC-Bayesian Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Identification of Linear Dynamical Systems

author.name: Chenfeng Huang, George Michailidis

entry.summary: PBML-LTI is a PAC-Bayesian meta-learning framework for few-shot identification of linear time-invariant systems, learning a transferable, data-dependent prior over transition matrices from related systems and performing Bayesian adaptation for new systems with limited data. This exploits shared structure across tasks where classical system identification treats each system independently.

entry.title: Pharmacokinetic State Space Models for Unbiased Prediction of Haemodynamic Collapse

author.name: Rithin Nagaraj, Sudiksha Chindula, Bhaskarjyoti Das

entry.summary: The paper builds state space models that incorporate propofol and remifentanil effect-site concentrations to predict intraoperative hypotension, achieving AUROC 0.7360 and a 2.73-fold lift over the random-guessing AUPRC baseline, with drug concentrations contributing a 13.9% AUPRC improvement. This brings pharmacological infusion history into predictive models for a clinically consequential perioperative event.

entry.title: NAVIR: Neuromorphic Audio-Visual Speech Recognition for Robust Human-Robot Interaction on Edge Hardware

author.name: Leonidas Delimpasis, Panagiota Moraiti, Antonis Porichis, Panos Chatzakos, Michail Karamousadakis

entry.summary: NAVIR is an end-to-end audio-visual speech recognition system designed for the BrainChip Akida neuromorphic processor, which only supports sequential 2D convolutional inference. It factorizes spatial and temporal encoding into separate AkidaNet-based modules to bring robust, noise-tolerant speech recognition to industrial robots on strict edge compute budgets.

entry.title: Universal Multi-Modal Traceformer: Integrating Heterogeneous Context for Process Event Prediction

author.name: Fabian Spaeh, Jingxing Fang, Shandian Zhe, Bin Shen

entry.summary: UMT is a Transformer-based framework for next-event prediction over process event logs that incorporates heterogeneous context (numerical, categorical, textual, and metadata features) via a universal feature encoder mapping diverse types into a shared space. This extends beyond temporal point process models that consider only activities and timestamps.

entry.title: Guaranteed Low-Rank Tensor Recovery from Modewise Measurements via Normalized Block-Weighted Riemannian Gradient Descent

author.name: Yushi Zhou, Feng Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose an adaptive block-weighted modewise Riemannian gradient descent method for recovering low-multilinear-rank tensors from linear measurements. They prove local linear convergence under tensor restricted isometry conditions and derive sampling guarantees for sub-Gaussian and SORS measurements, with improved convergence at no extra memory cost.

entry.title: Leakage-Safe Empirical Benchmarking of EEG-Based Machine Learning Pipelines for Dementia Classification

author.name: Haitian Wang, Chamara Madarasingha, Redowan Mahmud, Aneesh Krishna, Ryu Takechi

entry.summary: The paper builds a leakage-safe empirical benchmark for resting-state EEG dementia classification on the public OpenNeuro ds004504 dataset, systematically comparing preprocessing, segmentation, augmentation, features, and validation protocols. It identifies a practical best-practice pipeline for reproducible, data-leakage-free evaluation.

entry.title: Token Signatures of Code: Comparing Coding Behaviors Across Large Language Models

author.name: Junpeng Wang, Yuzhong Chen, Menghai Pan, Uday Singh Saini, Yiwei Cai

entry.summary: The paper proposes CLIC, a visual analytics approach that characterizes how LLMs differ in coding behavior via token-frequency features and interpretable decision trees that separate model code outputs. It introduces new behavioral metrics beyond pass@k as performance ceilings reduce the discriminative power of benchmark scores.

entry.title: DiFA: Dual Evidence Fusion and Aggregation for Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yanyu Qian, Pengcheng Weng, Yue Tan, Enguang Zuo, Yu Zheng, Yixin Liu

entry.summary: DiFA fuses complementary anomaly cues to detect anomalous words or fragments within documents, moving beyond document-level text anomaly detection and single-cue representation-distance methods. Token-level localization of harmful or anomalous content supports targeted prevention in language-driven applications.

entry.title: Beyond the Stitching Assumption: A Unified Framework for Multimodal Synthetic Data Evaluation via Semantic Quantization

author.name: Yefeng Yuan, Zhan Shi, Liang Cheng, Yuhong Liu

entry.summary: The paper presents a projection-based evaluator for tabular-text synthetic data that jointly assesses structured attributes and text, using semantic quantization and contingency-table comparisons via JSD, NMI, and conditional JSD. It demonstrates that separate-modality metrics can stay high even when tabular-text pairings are disrupted, motivating unified cross-modal evaluation.

entry.title: A Channel-Boosted Multi-Agent System with Iterative Consultation for Document Sensitivity Classification

author.name: Aleesha Zainab, Asifullah Khan, Muhammad Ahmed Khalid, Faheem Ullah Khan

entry.summary: Presents CB-MAS/IC-MAS, a multi-agent system with iterative consultation that classifies sensitive documents in critical-infrastructure contexts, avoiding long-context costs by consulting over document channels rather than truncating input. Built on a prior benchmark where BERT reached 89.14% accuracy on the Strategic 16K corpus, it addresses the structural weakness that sensitive evidence often lies beyond a fixed truncation window.

entry.title: ALPINE: Adaptive Localization for Parameter- and Sample-Efficient Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Neeraj Yadav

entry.summary: Presents an ultra-lightweight (under 35k-parameter) spatial-relational architecture for few-shot image classification combining Gabor edge-energy guidance with a content-adaptive patch locator. Under a strictly matched iso-episode-budget protocol, it beats Prototypical Networks, Relation Networks, and MAML on CIFAR benchmarks across five seeds. The paper emphasizes parameter and sample efficiency, which accuracy-only evaluation typically ignores.

entry.title: Locally Private Inference for Riemannian Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Xiaotian Chang, Yangdi Jiang, Qirui Hu

entry.summary: The paper develops statistical inference for manifold-valued population minimizers under local differential privacy, where each participant releases only randomized tangent gradients. Conditional centering of released gradients preserves the first-order estimation equation, and symmetric-pair regression estimates asymptotic variance from the same private messages. The authors prove a central limit theorem and construct confidence procedures.

entry.title: Counting and Covering in Nearest-Neighbour Representations of Boolean Functions

author.name: Martin Anthony

entry.summary: Studies the number of prototypes needed to represent Boolean functions via nearest-neighbour classification, in settings where prototypes are arbitrary Euclidean points or restricted to the Boolean cube. It strengthens lower bounds for almost all Boolean functions, derives sharp VC-dimension bounds for bounded-prototype classes, and analyzes Boolean prototype constructions.

entry.title: Stochastic Reconfiguration as Statistical Filtering for Overparameterized Neural Quantum States

author.name: Tak Hur

entry.summary: Analyzes stochastic reconfiguration, the standard optimizer for neural quantum states, in the overparameterized regime, showing the diagonal shift acts as a statistical filter balancing useful update shrinkage against overfitting to finite Monte Carlo samples. Frames SR as ridge regression from tangent features to local energy with the residual as an expressivity gap.

entry.title: Financial Language Models as Applied Artificial Intelligence Systems for News-Based Trading under Market Frictions

author.name: Kemal Kirtac

entry.summary: Proposes an integrated deployment framework for financial language models that jointly tests news-derived trading signals under event-time observability, probability calibration, execution timing, transaction costs, liquidity constraints, capacity limits, and statistical inference. Bridges computer science methods for text and forecasting with rigorous financial decision-system evaluation.

entry.title: On Generalized Naive Bayes with Continuous Features

author.name: \'Abrah\'am Papp, Botond Szil\'agyi, Edith Alice Kov\'acs

entry.summary: Extends the Generalized Naive Bayes framework from discrete variables to continuous explanatory variables, showing that GNB structure learning depends only on bivariate marginal pair copulas. The authors prove GNB structures form a matroid basis, enabling greedy algorithms that minimize Kullback-Leibler divergence for optimal structure discovery.

entry.title: Data Agents: Agentic Data Systems

author.name: Guoliang Li, Peiyao Zhou, Xuanhe Zhou, Ji Sun, Yuyu Luo, Ju Fan

entry.summary: Proposes the Data Agent paradigm for autonomous data management, processing, and analysis with minimal human intervention, built on six components including semantic data organization, semantic operators, and agentic pipeline orchestration. Argues traditional data systems must shift from manual, literal, reactive processing to autonomous, semantic, proactive operation.

entry.title: MCP-GRANITE Benchmark: GRANularity Interface TEsting for MCP-Based LLM Agents

author.name: Demetris Paschalides, Moysis Symeonides, George Pallis, Marios D. Dikaiakos

entry.summary: Introduces MCP-GRANITE, an open-source benchmark treating tool-interface granularity as a controlled variable for MCP-based LLM agents, with 81 multi-step scenarios across 9 domains instantiated at 4 granularity levels, evaluated under edge and IoT constraints. It studies how functionality decomposition affects tool selection and argument construction.

entry.title: A principled approach for energy-efficient training via phase-aware GPU frequency tuning

author.name: Miguel Braga, J\'ulio Pinto, Rahma Nouaji, Olivier Michaud, Bettina Kemme, Oana Balmau, Cl\'audia Brito, Ricardo Macedo

entry.summary: Presents PAFT, a system that dynamically tunes GPU clock frequencies based on training phase and pipeline bottlenecks, exploiting stalls as energy-saving opportunities rather than pure performance problems. Reduces training energy consumption with minimal performance overhead, relevant given AI training's growing datacenter energy footprint.

entry.title: Fathom-Vaidya: Advancing Medical Reasoning with Rubric-Based Rewards

author.name: Kalash Shah, Kunal Singh, Snehan J, Shreyas Singh

entry.summary: The paper presents a sequential training framework for medical LLMs that targets both diagnostic reasoning and multi-turn clinical dialogue reasoning, using synthetic data and rubric-based rewards. It addresses weaknesses exposed by benchmarks such as HealthBench and MedXpertQA.

entry.title: Mobile Imaging Solutions for Medical Diagnosis: Trends and Applications

author.name: Syed Muhammad Ibne Zulfiker, Tanzima Hashem, Fariha Tabassum Islam, Md Sultanul Arifin, Khandker Aftarul Islam, Nishat Anjum Bristy, Faria Huq, Priyeta Saha, Syeda Nahida Akter, Arpita Saha

entry.summary: This survey examines smartphone and webcam-based medical diagnosis across eye, ENT, skin, oral, cardiac, and nutritional conditions, comparatively analyzing state-of-the-art solutions. It emphasizes the potential of low-cost mobile imaging to expand accessible healthcare.

entry.title: Privacy Personalization Trade offs in LLMs: The Impact of Stylometric Signal Reduction on User-Specific Text Generation

author.name: Muhammed Nazmul Arefin, Omar Jamal Hammad

entry.summary: Using a controlled framework on the LaMP-7 Twitter benchmark with 250 sampled users, the paper compares LLM personalization conditioned on original versus anonymized profiles to test whether reducing stylometric and demographic markers degrades personalization quality. It quantifies the trade-off between stylometric re-identification risk and user-specific text fidelity.

entry.title: Checkpoints Are Not Enough: Trust Calibration in CoSLR, a Human-AI System for Systematic Literature Reviews

author.name: MD Aidul Islam, Malik Abdul Sami, Muhammad Waseem, Zeeshan Rasheed, Kai-kristian Kemell, Zheying Zhang, Pekka Abrahamsson

entry.summary: Presents CoSLR, a human-AI collaborative multi-agent system for systematic literature reviews with a modular three-phase LLM and RAG pipeline, focusing on trust calibration so researchers can distinguish verified synthesis from merely authoritative-looking AI text. It warns that unverified AI synthesis entering the scholarly record carries unwarranted credibility.

entry.title: Toward Personalized Sleep Guidance from Wearable Data Using Language Models

author.name: Yusheng Tan, Running Zhao, Sofia Angel, Ninghui Hao, Ash Arian, Nikita N. Dulin, Jay Lin, Ou Zhu, Faiza Shaik, Xinxing Yang, Bonnie W. Leung, Katie Roster, Arlene Ruiz de Luzuriaga, Kenneth Lee, Alejandra Lastra, Habibul Ahsan, Guihong Wan

entry.summary: A two-stage framework for personalized sleep guidance from wearable data: Stage 1 uses a multi-agent LLM pipeline to generate structured guidance from unannotated wearable records for scalable dataset construction, and Stage 2 distills reasoning trajectories into small language models via supervised fine-tuning plus a training-free component for lightweight local deployment addressing privacy.

entry.title: AlexandriaX 2026: The First Shared Task on Dialectal Arabic Machine Translation

author.name: Abdellah El Mekki, AbdelRahim A. Elmadany, Samar M. Magdy, Saad Ezzini, Mo El-Haj, Mustafa Jarrar, Zaid Alyafeai, Bernard Ghanem, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed

entry.summary: Presents the AlexandriaX 2026 shared task on dialectal Arabic machine translation, with three subtasks covering context-aware English-to-dialect dialogue translation across 13 Arabic varieties, cross-dialect financial-domain translation, and sociolinguistically aware evaluation. The task highlights that conventional MT metrics give limited insight into dialectal and sociolinguistic errors.

entry.title: Knowing When to Trust Images: Reliability-Aware Multi-modal Entity Alignment

author.name: Chenxiao Li, Yunhe Feng, Dongfang Liu, Dong Nie, Yan Huang, Heng Fan

entry.summary: Introduces RA-MMEA, a multi-modal entity alignment framework that predicts visual reliability and adaptively repairs unreliable image representations via dependency-aware reliability prediction and stability-regularized embedding generation. This addresses noisy image-entity misalignment that naive fusion overlooks.

entry.title: GRACE: Grounded Adversarial Reasoning over Canadian Law

author.name: Jiakang Xu, Wantong Huo, Udom Silparcha, Jonathan H. Chan

entry.summary: Introduces GRACE, a dataset of 1,915 question-reasoning-answer instances grounded in Canadian federal legislation covering adversarial advocacy, uncertainty, and applied reasoning modes, built via a pipeline that partitions statutes and generates filtered scenario-based questions. It targets underexplored abilities such as defending legal positions and synthesizing multiple statutory provisions in the underrepresented Canadian law domain.

entry.title: From Content Generation to Learning Support: Pedagogy-Guided Generative Video Tutors for STEM Learning

author.name: Xinchen Ma, Shuimu Wang, Gaole He, Yanbin Zhang, Chunyang Wang, Yunshi Lan, Weining Qian

entry.summary: PIVOT is a generative video tutoring framework for STEM that embeds pedagogical principles into the entire generation pipeline, from storyboard construction to verified multimodal content and learner-assessment mechanisms. It shifts the goal from visually coherent video production toward measurable learning support, including addressing misconceptions. This targets a known gap where generative educational media lacks instructional structure and quality control.

entry.title: Structure Before Sampling: Community-Aware Core-Set Selection for Data-Efficient Text-to-Speech

author.name: Mizbaul Haque Maruf, Muhammad Nur Yanhaona

entry.summary: The authors model TTS corpora as phonotactic graphs linking phonemically similar utterances, first demonstrating strong structure (clustering 199x and 56x random baselines for Bangla and English). They propose Community Representative, a core-set selector that samples across graph communities starting from utterances rich in rare phonemes, selecting a small training subset under a fixed audio-duration budget. This reduces costly recording requirements for data-efficient TTS training.

entry.title: Linguistic Features for Interpretable Textual Entailment

author.name: David Torres-Moreno, Jorge Hermosillo-Valadez, Asela Reig-Alamillo

entry.summary: Introduces SLITE, an explainable hybrid model for Recognizing Textual Entailment combining a structural-relational layer (entity-level semantic compatibility) with a distributional-informational layer over embeddings, using 17 interpretable linguistic features. It aims to expose the linguistic phenomena behind entailment decisions rather than relying on black-box neural models.

entry.title: Complementary rPPG-Derived and Lip-Region Frequency Cues for Talking-Face Deepfake Detection

author.name: Othmane Harraq, Tamer Aldwairi

entry.summary: The paper studies two lightweight visual-only cues for talking-face deepfake detection — rPPG waveforms from RhythmFormer and lip-region DCT coefficients — across seven generators of Celeb-DF++ under subject-independent and leave-one-generator-out protocols. Concat fusion reaches AUC 0.891 in-domain, but transfer across generators varies, with some cues falling to near chance for IP-LAP.

entry.title: Style as Cover: Deep Image Steganography via Stylized Transmission

author.name: Qi Li, Jidong Yang, Huaike Yu, Chunpeng Wang, Suo Gao, Herbert Ho-Ching Iu, Yuantian Miao, Bin Ma, Xiao Chen

entry.summary: StyleStegaNet rethinks image steganography by abandoning cover-preserving transmission in favor of style-concealment: stego images are generated in a stylized form conditioned on public style references, making hiding rely on behavior-level camouflage rather than matching a specific cover. This shift complicates reliable secret recovery but improves robustness when the original cover is exposed or approximable.

entry.title: General Collaborative Intelligence: Architecting Cognition for Resilient Multi-Agent Ecosystems

author.name: Lei Zhang, Chun Ye, Le Yang, Zhaozhong Wang, Deng-Ping Fan, Hang Dai, Binglu Wang

entry.summary: A survey synthesizing collaborative intelligence for multi-agent unmanned systems using a five-dimensional taxonomy (collaboration stage, communication paradigm, fusion architecture, learning strategy, application domain) plus complementary analytical lenses that expose dependencies prior surveys treated in isolation. Useful as a roadmap for distributed sensing beyond ego-centric perception.

entry.title: VDGS: Visibility-Driven Large-Scale 3D Gaussian Splatting for Aerial Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Haolin Yu, Jiadong Tang, YiXian Wang, Yu Gao, Shi He, Zhilin Lai, Yi Yang, Mengyin Fu

entry.summary: Proposes VDGS, a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for large-scale aerial reconstruction that incorporates camera distribution into scene modeling via visibility-driven statistics quantifying supervision coverage of scene anchors. Targets memory excess and uneven viewpoint coverage typical of UAV acquisition for mapping and autonomous driving.

entry.title: LiteTex-GS: Fast and Lightweight Texturing for Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zhiwei Li, Yijia Guo, Yishi Lu, Liwen Hu, Hong Rao, Shengbo Chen, Lei Ma

entry.summary: LiteTex-GS tackles the memory and optimization cost of attaching texture maps to Gaussian primitives for high-frequency detail in Gaussian Splatting, proposing a fast lightweight texturing approach that simplifies the parameterization bridging discrete Gaussians and continuous 2D grids. It targets preserving real-time rendering efficiency while adding detailed appearance. Useful for graphics and 3D content pipelines.

entry.title: HOIBlender: Blending Lightweight Detection with Vision-Language Priors for Efficient Human-Object Interaction Detection

author.name: Junwen Chen, Keiji Yanai

entry.summary: HOIBlender is an efficient human-object interaction detector that blends detector-grounded visual tokens, spatial subject-object reasoning, and BLIP-2 semantic priors in one lightweight decoding pipeline built on an RF-DETR/LW-DETR-style foundation with a DINOv2 backbone. It avoids heavy transformer stacks and complex denoising schedules used by prior work, targeting long-tail HOI supervision. A solid systems-efficiency contribution in a well-established task.

entry.title: Transferring Visual Explanations: How Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation Affects Model Interpretability

author.name: Aleks Czufarow, Ihor Babin

entry.summary: This empirical study examines whether knowledge distillation transfers a ResNet-152 teacher's spatial feature attributions to a compact ResNet-34 student on ImageNet-1K across five KD configurations, evaluating accuracy alongside interpretability metrics (Relevance Mass Accuracy, Relevance Rank Accuracy). It addresses whether efficient deployed models can retain interpretability, important for safety-critical domains. A useful, well-scoped empirical contribution.

entry.title: PETR: Prompt Ensembling with Training-free Routing for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weihan Cai, Hao Tan, Xinping Gao, Shibiao Xu, Jun Wan

entry.summary: PETR tackles the seen-class vs unseen-class tradeoff in prompt learning for VLMs by learning two complementary prompts with different objectives on a frozen CLIP backbone, then routing test samples between them based on similarity to seen data at inference time. This training-free routing improves generalization without sacrificing seen-class performance.

entry.title: PRISM-RAG: Multimodal Hypergraph Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Tobacco Product and Legislative Policy Reasoning

author.name: Manuel Serna-Aguilera, Raegan Anderes, Page Dobbs, Khoa Luu

entry.summary: PRISM-RAG addresses inter-context conflict in RAG, where semantically similar statutes across jurisdictions mislead generative models, using multimodal hypergraph retrieval-augmented generation applied to US tobacco and nicotine regulation. The system determines which jurisdiction's law governs a product, a key issue for emerging products like nicotine pouches.

entry.title: WebMRIQC: A Web-Based Implementation of MRIQC for Accessible MRI Image Quality Assessment in Resource-Constrained Settings

author.name: Philip Nkwam, Ifeoluwa Oladeji, Sekinat Zurakat-Aderibigbe, Jasmine Cakmak, Harrison Aduluwa, Confidence Raymond, Cliff Mokua, Abdulrazaq Zubair, Daniel Champanda, Tolulope Olusuyi, Maruf Adewole, Udunna Anazodo

entry.summary: WebMRIQC wraps the validated MRIQC quality-control engine behind a zero-installation browser interface that automates DICOM-to-BIDS conversion and runs containerized MRIQC on shared compute, targeting resource-constrained settings without local HPC or imaging expertise. It lowers the barrier to standardized MRI quality assessment globally.

entry.title: U-PEN Mamba: Progressive Expansion with Selective State-Space Modeling for Efficient Retinal Vessel Segmentation

author.name: Abel A. Reyes-Angulo, Sidike Paheding, Vijayan K. Asari, Mohammad Alam, Jeevan Devagiri

entry.summary: This paper presents a U-shaped segmentation architecture combining progressive nonlinear feature expansion with a Mamba-based Global Context block that models long-range dependencies with linear sequence complexity. Attention-based decoder fusion helps recover thin vessel boundaries on medical fundus images. It targets efficiency and accuracy on retinal vessel benchmarks like CHASE DB1 and DRIVE.

entry.title: A paired synthetic construction-site image dataset for robust computer vision under adverse conditions

author.name: Viet Huy Duong, Ruoxin Xiong, Md Abdullah Al Forhad, Weishi Shi

entry.summary: ConSynth-X is a paired synthetic dataset of 34,199 construction-site images derived from 3,109 real scenes, spanning 11 adverse-condition subsets such as fog, rain, and nighttime. Each synthetic image is linked to its source scene, enabling controlled cross-condition comparisons for robustness research. It addresses underrepresentation of adverse conditions in construction monitoring data.

entry.title: SRPR-Net: Semantic and Relational Prompt Refinement for Automated SAM-based Instance Segmentation

author.name: Lufei Liu, Guojie Li, Suncheng Xiang, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: SRPR-Net introduces a sequential prompt refinement mechanism for automated SAM-based instance segmentation, first enriching detector geometry with vision-language semantics and then modeling same-image instance dependencies before segmentation. Experiments on standard benchmarks show improved context-aware box prompting.

entry.title: DeCo: Efficient Decouple-to-Couple Learning for Multi-Task Visual Grounding

author.name: Xiaoqiang Lu, Licheng Jiao, Long Sun, Yuting Yang, Xu Liu, Lingling Li, Wenping Ma, Fang Liu

entry.summary: DeCo is a two-stage framework for adapting multimodal LLMs to multiple visual grounding objectives: task-specific representation decoupling followed by complementary prior coupling. It argues that shared-representation task cooperation overlooks intrinsic conflicts between task-oriented feature interests.

entry.title: STA-TFM: Spatio-Temporal Aggregation Across Views TransForMer for Pose Estimation

author.name: Mena Kamel, Natalie Won, Amrut Sarangi, Sven Jager, Albert Pla Planas

entry.summary: STA-TFM is a transformer architecture for multi-view 3D human pose estimation that combines DSTformer monocular features per view with a fusion transformer aggregating across views and time. To address data scarcity, it uses a pipeline converting any 3D pose dataset into multi-view setups with controlled camera geometry.

entry.title: Ev-YOLO: Uncertainty-Aware Object Detection via a Unified Evidential Formulation

author.name: Simon Barbarit-Gaboriau (LITIS - STI, INSA Rouen Normandie), Hind Laghmara (LITIS - STI), R\'emi Boutteau (LITIS - STI), Samia Ainouz (LITIS, LITIS - STI)

entry.summary: Ev-YOLO reformulates YOLOv8 so that both classification and bounding-box regression are expressed within a single evidential deep learning framework, exploiting distribution-based bounding-box representations. Existing evidential detectors typically mix evidential classification with regression uncertainty models lacking a shared theoretical foundation. The unified formulation improves principled uncertainty estimation for object detection in autonomous systems.

entry.title: Ananke: Contractive Torus Attractor Networks

author.name: Zhongping Ji

entry.summary: Ananke introduces a representation-learning framework that structures latent spaces as a product-torus prior, factoring high-dimensional latents into orthogonal two-dimensional phase planes. Its flagship visual backbone, CTAN, coordinates feature updates via a decoupled dual-phase continuous flow combining skew-symmetric Hamiltonian transport with signed gradient dissipation toward invariant manifolds. The paper proposes a mathematically grounded, dynamical-systems-inspired alternative to standard latent-space design for vision models.

entry.title: Visual Graph Reasoning via Knowledge Compilation

author.name: Rongzheng Wang, Zhe Wang, Ke Qin, Rongwei Wang, Muquan Li, Yizhuo Ma, Yihong Huang, Jielei Wang, Shuang Liang

entry.summary: VGCompiler proposes a compilation-centric paradigm for visual graph reasoning, organizing inference around two compilers that recover an explicit graph representation preserving topology and state from graph images, rather than prioritizing final-answer supervision. This targets VLMs' failure on simple visual graph problems.

entry.title: SomaNet: Weakly Supervised Learning for Instance Soma Segmentation in 3D Electron Microscopy with Partial Annotations

author.name: Mohammad Khateri, Morteza Ghahremani, Jussi Tohka, Alejandra Sierra

entry.summary: SomaNet is a weakly supervised framework for segmenting individual cell somas in 3D electron microscopy data when only partial manual annotations are available. It uses a teacher-student paradigm where a teacher trained on partially labeled data generates pseudo-labels to train the student, reducing the need for prohibitively costly dense instance-level annotation. This matters for scalability of connectomics and cellular analysis, where annotation bottlenecks limit fully supervised approaches.

entry.title: OpenFlyScan: A Quality-Guided Aerial Reconstruction System for Consumer Drones

author.name: Zhongrui You, Zhen Li, Junli Liu, Zhigang Wang, Bin Zhao

entry.summary: Presents a quality-guided aerial reconstruction system for consumer drones targeting 3D Gaussian Splatting scene capture, with a model that predicts regional reconstruction quality from GS rendering errors and a planner that generates complementary reacquisition flight strips via a mobile app. Reduces the need for return visits and reprocessing after discovering defects.

entry.title: Tracker-Free Robotic Ultrasound Calibration with a Spherical-Marker Phantom and Threshold-Free Center Localization

author.name: Kyoungmo Koo, Guangshen Ma, Xueding Wang, Mark Draelos

entry.summary: Develops a tracker-free calibration framework for robotic ultrasound using a spherical-marker phantom and automated perception for sphere-center localization. A threshold-free image-processing method adapts to each image's intensity distribution, removing hand-tuned thresholds and improving robustness across imaging settings.

entry.title: Physical-Touch Observability from Wrist Wrench in Granular Scooping

author.name: Hongyi Lin, Song Zhang, Xubo Liu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This empirical study tests whether a scoop's six-axis wrist force/torque signal contains information about final collected volume in granular scooping for mining and earthmoving, defining the concept of physical-touch observability. It shows wrench sensing reveals interaction properties like resistance and load transfer that pre-contact RGB-D sensing cannot.

entry.title: On the Control of Mobile Ad-Hoc Agent Deployments in Partially Observed Space

author.name: Edwin Meriaux, Louis-Roy Langevin, Shuo Wen, Ndiam\'e Ndiaye, Gregory Dudek, Antonio Lor\'ia

entry.summary: The paper formalizes online deployment of mobile ad hoc agent networks in unknown orthogonal environments as a Partially Observable Cooperative Guard Art Gallery Problem and proves that CADENCE algorithms achieve full coverage with a connected visibility graph using at most n/2 + h - 2 agents. It also evaluates deployment-order heuristics that reduce agent count and deployment time in practice.

entry.title: Safety Control of a Hyper-redundant Robot via Adaptive Weighted Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Zijian Cai, Kiwan Wong, Wenci Xin, Wei Xiao, Daniela Rus, Cecilia Laschi

entry.summary: This paper proposes a weighted control barrier function (W-CBF) framework for safe control of hyper-redundant robots in cluttered confined spaces, where weights adapt to reduce tracking errors caused by uneven load distribution along the slender robot body. It reports up to 59.6% RMS tracking error reduction in simulation and 87% in hardware compared to non-weighted CBFs on path-following tasks. The work matters for deploying soft or snake-like robots safely in real environments.

entry.title: vla.simd: Efficient CPU Inference for Language-Conditioned Manipulation

author.name: Khanh D. Nguyen, Hoang M. Truong, An T. Le

entry.summary: vla.simd is a CPU inference engine for language-conditioned manipulation policies combining shared SIMD micro-kernels, computation reuse, and target-specific optimization, achieving about 1.4x median speedup over compiled PyTorch across six policies and four CPUs while preserving fp32 fidelity. It also analyzes the relationship between query latency, execution horizon, and action availability under lagged versus time-aligned execution, and introduces IMPACT, an ACT-based policy with cached text representations. This matters for deploying robot policies without dedicated GPUs.

entry.title: Robotic Valve Turning: Axial Misalignment Correction Using Reaction Torque Feedback

author.name: Amit Kumar, Sri Harsha Turlapati, Gautami Golani, Yang Lin, Ravi N. Banavar, Domenico Campolo

entry.summary: This paper proposes a haptic control law that uses reaction torques from gripper-valve contact to correct axial misalignment during valve turning, avoiding the calibration, occlusion, and contact-geometry issues of vision-based estimation. The controller exploits a geometric relationship between the error vector and torque measurements and is proven uniformly asymptotically stable, with simulation verification and experiments on a Kinova Gen3 arm.

entry.title: A Switched Adaptive Control Framework for Aerial Manipulators Under Dynamic Transitions

author.name: Rishabh Dev Yadav, Saksham Gupta, Amitabh Sharma, Sarthak Mishra, Wei Pan, Spandan Roy, Simone Baldi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a switched adaptive control framework for aerial manipulators that handles abrupt dynamic transitions during task execution, tight vehicle-manipulator couplings, and state-dependent uncertainties that existing aerial manipulation methods do not address. The switched-system formulation provides stability across discontinuous regime changes.

entry.title: Partial-Scan-and-Move Source Seeking for Mobile Robots

author.name: Bo Wang, Ishvar Sitaldin

entry.summary: The paper introduces a partial-scan-and-move strategy enabling a mobile robot with an offset scalar sensor to seek a signal source without completing a full rotational scan before each move. It develops a gradient estimation method for partial scans paired with a confidence set that accounts for measurement noise and local field variation, letting the robot decide when it has enough information to move in a descent direction. The authors provide theoretical guarantees that, under suitable conditions, the strategy converges toward the source.

entry.title: Subspace Learning with Interval-Censored Likelihoods for Dequantizing Percept PC LFP Snapshots

author.name: Shreesh Karjagi, Elif Ceren Fitoz, Maryam Khalid, Tanya Nauvel, Parisa Sarikhani, Helen S. Mayberg, Christopher J. Rozell, Sankaraleengam Alagapan

entry.summary: Identifies a quantization artifact in Medtronic Percept PC DBS devices, where spectral amplitudes stored at ~0.1 uV resolution cause FOOOF to fit spurious oscillatory peaks to plateaus, corrupting clinical biomarkers. Proposes a subspace learning method with interval-censored likelihoods to dequantize local field potential snapshots, feeding cleaner spectra to clinical models.

entry.title: Selective Inference for CART with Binary Outcomes

author.name: Tomoshige Nakamura

entry.summary: Develops finite-sample conditional selective inference tests for binary classification trees, testing homogeneity of success probabilities within a parent node selected by deterministic Gini CART. Conditions on the selected split and ancestor path, and constructs exact or super-uniform p-values via a reversible parallel Monte Carlo scheme.

entry.title: Mech Interp is a Verifiable Task

author.name: Logan Riggs

entry.summary: The author proposes framing mechanistic interpretability as an RLVR (reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards) environment, defining ideal decomposition via a Pareto frontier trading reconstruction loss against simplicity, with criteria such as out-of-distribution predictive power and extractable minimal circuits.

entry.title: Do Personality-Tuned LLMs Make Better Social Agents?

author.name: Tim Krabbe, Xiaodan Shi

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune two small open-weight LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Ministral-8B-Instruct) on personality-labelled social media posts and dialogues to test whether personality-aware fine-tuning improves consistency and controllability of personality-conditioned dialogue versus instruction prompting. The work targets reduced alienness of LLM-based social agents in simulation.

entry.title: The Price of Self-Calibration: Exact Evidence Budgets and Manufactured Blind Sets in Adaptive Monitoring

author.name: Abdou-Raouf Atarmla

entry.summary: Analyzes self-calibrating monitors that adapt thresholds online to guarantee long-run false-alarm rates, computing the exact cost of that guarantee via evidence identities: step drifts yield excess alarm mass of delta/eta and ramps yield stationary excess rate c/eta. Shows the guarantee is an accounting identity insensitive to what the monitor detects.

entry.title: Physics-residual machine learning predicts oxygen-evolution catalyst activity beyond the training range from sparse polarization measurements

author.name: Yong-Woon Kim, Jihyeok Lee, Sungtae Park, Sooseok Choi, Yung-Cheol Byun

entry.summary: Combines the Tafel equation for physical extrapolation with a learned distance-attenuated residual and an applicability-domain score to predict oxygen-evolution catalyst activity beyond the measured potential window. On a separately fabricated 322-candidate library with 282 candidates above the training maximum, two measurements per candidate achieved 0.203 mA cm-2 mean absolute error.

entry.title: Taking a Second Look: Correcting Sea Ice Forecasts with Sparse Observations

author.name: Tianshuo Zhang, Xianglei Xing, Aowen Yang, Jia Gao, Wenzhe Zhai, ShanShan Liu

entry.summary: ECHO corrects issued sea ice forecasts using sparse new observations, with ECHO-Scale adapting propagation distance in a state-dependent way (concentrating corrections near high-gradient ice edges) and ECHO-Delta learning a bounded residual. It improves forecasts across 96 evaluation settings spanning diverse priors, sparsity levels, and noise conditions.

entry.title: Machine Learning for Invisible Dark Boson Searches at the Electron-Ion Collider

author.name: Rojae Mighty, Ankush Reddy Kanuganti

entry.summary: The authors test whether adding the four-momentum transfer variable t lets boosted decision trees outperform optimized rectangular cuts for selecting invisible dark boson signals at the Electron-Ion Collider. Using electron-only information the BDT shows no consistent advantage across 11 masses per boson type, but adding t yields a slight improvement. The paper is a sober negative-to-marginal result that informs detector analysis design at a future collider.

entry.title: A Bayesian Vertical Federated Learning Framework for Multivariate Reduced-Rank High-Dimensional Regression

author.name: Brigham Halverson, Sharmistha Guha, Jessica Bernard, Rajarshi Guhaniyogi

entry.summary: This paper advances Bayesian multivariate reduced-rank regression to vertical federated learning, where sites share observations across distinct feature sets under strict privacy constraints. It addresses challenges that local per-site regressions miss, such as inter-variable correlations. The work extends the comparatively underexplored VFL setting with principled Bayesian machinery.

entry.title: ARID: A Deployable Edge AI System for Structured Information Extraction from Industrial Maintenance Work Orders

author.name: Kuanlin Chen, Chen-Wei Kuo

entry.summary: Presents ARID, an edge-deployable system that extracts components, failure modes, symptoms, and actions from maintenance work orders into fixed-schema JSON on an 8 GB Jetson Orin NX, combining dual-teacher filtering, noise-aware synthesis, 4-bit inference, and grammar-constrained decoding. Achieves 84.8% token-F1 on human-labeled records with strong deployed-stack performance.

entry.title: BizSage: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework for Business Research with Efficient Knowledge Retrieval

author.name: Yuhe Wu, Guangyu Wang, Jiaxin Liu, Guang Zhang

entry.summary: BizSage is a multi-agent framework for economics and business research that addresses paper-level retrieval granularity mismatch with section-level evidence retrieval and adds mechanisms for learning from evaluation feedback (self-evolution). It targets the empirical rigor demands of business research that general academic-research agents do not meet.

entry.title: Rethinking Pivot Programming Languages in Code Language Models

author.name: Andor Diera, Lukas Galke Poech, Matthias Tichy

entry.summary: Revisits whether any programming language occupies a privileged pivot position in multilingual code models, controlling for representational anisotropy and length variation that confound prior cosine-based analyses. Across three code models and three analysis views (geometry, PL-English alignment, pivoted retrieval), results are relation-dependent with no consistent privileged pivot.

entry.title: Federated Multilingual Speech-LLMs: Architecture and Aggregation Strategy Benchmarking

author.name: Jordi Luque, Aleix Sant, Fernando L\'opez

entry.summary: A comprehensive federated-learning benchmark for multilingual ASR comparing four Speech-LLM architectures on Multilingual LibriSpeech, evaluating FedAvg versus FedProx across frozen and unfrozen encoders. Key findings: independently tuned per-component learning rates matter most, and FedProx advantages are architecture-dependent.

entry.title: SatOV: Restoring Spatial Priors for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation in Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Changhao Zhao, Linglin Zeng, Hai Liu

entry.summary: SatOV is a training-free framework for open-vocabulary segmentation of remote sensing imagery that restores spatial priors lost by vision-language foundation models' image-level classification design, addressing degraded structural relations and downsampled fine details at two stages of the representation.

entry.title: Reassessing Global Gradient-Norm Imbalance in BLIP Fine-Tuning Across Physical Domains

author.name: Kiran Naseer, Samreen Azhar, Dwarikanath Mahapatra

entry.summary: This empirical study challenges the assumption that visual-language gradient-norm imbalance in BLIP fine-tuning is a defect needing correction, measuring imbalance across nine conditions, three seeds, and three domain-shifted captioning datasets (underwater, aerial, radiological). It finds imbalance varies unpredictably across domains and that simple learning-rate reduction substantially reduces it.

entry.title: Estimating Accurate Hand Pose in Camera Space with Vision Transformer

author.name: Kaiwen Ren, Yiran Jiang, Yongjing Ye, Shihong Xia

entry.summary: This work tackles global monocular hand pose estimation in camera space, addressing depth ambiguity and the coupling between local hand poses, wrist position, and camera intrinsics in perspective projection. It introduces transformer-based components to disentangle these factors for accurate camera-frame hand pose.

entry.title: 0.5\%>100\%: Bidirectional Reciprocal Learning for Referring Image Segmentation

author.name: Xiaoqiang Lu, Licheng Jiao, Lingling Li, Yuting Yang, Long Sun, Wenping Ma, Xu Liu, Fang Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes bidirectional reciprocal learning for adapting vision foundation models to referring image segmentation, moving beyond unidirectional language-to-vision PEFT guidance by incorporating progressive cross-modal interaction and visual feedback for textual refinement, avoiding full fine-tuning costs and catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Doubly robust target inference for generalized linear regression with completely missing covariates

author.name: Huali Zhao (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Huazhong University of Science and Technology), Ke Deng (Department of Statistics and Data Science, Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: Develops a doubly robust transfer learning framework for target-population inference in generalized linear regression when key covariates are entirely absent from the target data but observed in a related source population. Allows sub-population shifts between the outcome/covariate distribution while requiring only a conditional-distribution assumption for missing covariates.

entry.title: RS-Claw-Evolution: Environment-Feedback-Driven Evolution for Lightweight Remote Sensing Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Kai Ouyang, Dongyang Hou, Liangtian Liu, Zeyuan Wang, Ziyu Li, Chengfu Liu, Zichao Tang, Xuezhi Cui, Shengwu Ouyang, Wentao Yang, Hanwen Yu, Haifeng Li

entry.summary: RS-Claw-Evolution improves lightweight LLM-based remote sensing agents across three stages: interaction evolution using executable code to control observations and maintain state, experience evolution with failure-aware trajectory generation and error-turn masking, and progressive optimization to overcome sparse signals in long-horizon multi-step tasks.

entry.title: SAGE: Optimal-Stopping Peer Selection for Decentralised Federated Learning

author.name: Ke Xiao, Qiyuan Wang, Christos Anagnostopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes SAGE, an optimal-stopping peer selector for decentralised federated learning under a one-model-bearing-exchange budget, where a receiver scores candidate neighbors on receiver-owned anchor evidence and selects once an advantage is certified, otherwise falling back to random gossip. Provides theoretical guarantees that the stopping problem admits a finite-stage optimal rule and order-optimal anchor scheduling.

entry.title: The Bairong System for MLC-SLM 2026: Dynamic Question-Aware Evidence Routing for Multilingual Conversational Speech Understanding

author.name: Shangkun Huang, Junchao Hu, Huan Shen, Guoji Wang, Yingao Wang, Shaosai Li, Wei Zou, Yunzhang Chen

entry.summary: The Bairong system for the MLC-SLM 2026 challenge couples a diarization-ASR front-end with a dynamic evidence router that infers the required evidence type and context scope from each question, selecting among full transcript context, local audio-text fusion, speaker-linked evidence, and compact global acoustic samples. The transcript-backbone design preserves discourse context while exploiting sparse acoustic cues.

entry.title: Bridging Static and Agentic RAG for Taiwanese Historical Question Answering

author.name: Kai-Hsin Chen, Wei-Yu Chen, Xuanjun Chen, Jyh-Shing Roger Jang

entry.summary: Conducts a controlled comparison of agentic versus static RAG for Taiwanese historical QA under a shared generator and hybrid retrieval backend, finding similar aggregate performance despite the two pipelines differing on 70.83% of questions. An oracle selecting the better response per question substantially outperforms either pipeline, revealing headroom for question-level routing.

entry.title: When Evidence Conflicts: Reliability-aware Meta-review Generation

author.name: Xinzhe Wang, Fei Tao, Jiang Xie, Hong Yu, Ye Wang

entry.summary: Frames meta-review generation as reliability-aware evidence aggregation: extracting aspect-level opinions from peer reviews, identifying conflicts, estimating opinion support and review quality, and weighting evidence accordingly. Addresses the weakness of uniform aggregation in standard multi-document summarization approaches.

entry.title: Dual-Interest Sequential Product Recommendation With Multi-Granular SSM

author.name: Shuiying Liao, P. Y. Mok

entry.summary: DSRec is a dual-interest cross-SSM model for sequential recommendation that disentangles item roles (polysemy) depending on user context and captures dynamic behavior across multiple temporal granularities. It leverages state space models for efficient long-range modeling where transformer-based recommenders are cost-prohibitive.

entry.title: Trustworthy FinAInce: Unpacking How AI-Mediated Financial Advice is Judged

author.name: Aryan Ramchandra Kapadia, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: A randomized vignette experiment with 285 US adults varies advice source labels (AI, expert, online community) across eight financial decisions while holding recommendations constant, measuring how source style and decision context shape trust, safety, and quality judgments. Appraisals explain a large fraction of downstream judgment variance.

entry.title: From Code Archival to Knowledge Graph: Bridging Software Heritage, COAR Notify and Wikidata

author.name: Camillo Carlo Pellizzari di San Girolamo, Francesco Tosoni

entry.summary: This paper presents a pipeline linking scholarly publications to their archived source code by harvesting editorially verified paper-repository pairs from software-focused venues (JOSS, SoftwareX, IPOL, SIGMOD ARI), yielding 4,397 curated DOI-repository pairs. It models these links in the Linked Open Data cloud via Software Heritage, COAR Notify, and Wikidata.

entry.title: ZoAQ: Adaptive Zeroth-Order Querying via Query-Reuse Coupling

author.name: Yangyang Feng, Yao Shu

entry.summary: ZoAQ is an adaptive zeroth-order optimization method that reuses past function evaluations both for the next gradient update and for deciding whether more queries are needed, avoiding the extra validation queries typical adaptive controllers require. The paper provides analysis of when evaluation agreement indicates a descent-supporting update and shows gains on synthetic objectives and further tasks.

entry.title: Helix-FNO: Spectral-Domain Operator Learning Coupled with a High-Fidelity Mechanistic Model for Fast Surrogate Simulation

author.name: Jiabao Zhao, Chuwei Wang, Jinxi Yang

entry.summary: Helix-FNO is a teacher-student surrogate architecture pairing a thirty-two-state mechanistic water-treatment simulation model with a Fourier neural operator student, enabling fast forward evaluations at a 5-minute decision cadence while generalizing across influent profiles, control settings, and plant layouts. The mechanistic teacher supplies high-fidelity training data mapping input fields to solution trajectories.

entry.title: From Latent Biomarkers to Clinical Rules: Embedding-Guided Rule Mining and Attribution-Based Translation for Interpretable Tabular Learning

author.name: Majid Lotfian Delouee, Hamed Ayoobi, Sjors G. J. G. In 't Veld, Martijn C. Schut

entry.summary: The paper presents a four-step pipeline that mines interpretable decision rules in the latent space of an FT-Transformer and translates them back into measurable clinical features, treating consistently separating embedding dimensions as latent biomarkers. Rules are extracted with small decision trees and translated using gradient-input saliency and CLS attention attribution, evaluated on six public clinical datasets.

entry.title: Role-Aware Morgan Fingerprints for Reaction Yield Prediction

author.name: Chinmay Mirji, Prashant Shekhar, Foram Madiyar, Hao Peng

entry.summary: This paper proposes MFP, a reaction yield prediction method based on role-aware Morgan fingerprints, computing count-based circular fingerprints per reaction component and aggregating them by chemical role (reactant, reagent, product) with transformation-sensitive difference features. It aims to avoid the heavy preprocessing and formatting fragility of graph neural network and Transformer approaches, speeding condition screening in synthetic chemistry.

entry.title: CALM: A Calibrated LLM Choice Network Framework for Activity-Based Traveler Simulation

author.name: Yezhou Cheng

entry.summary: CALM is a hybrid framework combining an optional LLM activity planner with calibrated stochastic choice models, network feedback, memory/habit mechanisms, feasibility checks, and deterministic replay for traveler-day simulation. Evaluated on the 2024 NYC Citywide Mobility Survey, training-only alternative-specific constant calibration cuts holdout mode Jensen-Shannon divergence from 0.156 to 0.004.

entry.title: The Role of Coordinates in Pareto Regret for Adversarial Multi-Objective Bandits

author.name: Changkun Guan, Mengfan Xu

entry.summary: Studies adversarial multi-objective bandits where reward is a multidimensional vector and performance is measured by Pareto regret. Shows a negative result: when the learner does not know which coordinate is easier, smaller cumulative loss on a coordinate does not improve worst-case Pareto regret order.

entry.title: Neural Residual Modeling for Scientific Data Compression under Guaranteed Error Bounds

author.name: Surya Majumder, Liangji Zhu, Sanjay Ranka, Anand Rangarajan

entry.summary: Proposes a post-processing pipeline that augments RVQ-based scientific data compressors with a U-Net trained to predict and correct pixel-space residuals, exploiting the finding that such residuals are spatially structured. The approach targets error-bounded lossy compression of simulation data.

entry.title: A Patient World Model for Early Forecasting of Digital Health Campaign Outcomes: Capabilities and Limits

author.name: Yunlong Wang

entry.summary: Reframes in-flight forecasting of DTC health campaign outcomes as a dynamic-system problem with a compact patient world model that maintains per-patient latent states and learns exposure-conditioned dynamics with a weekly conversion hazard. On a 147k-patient US campaign dataset it forecasts remaining new-to-brand prescription volume through week 52 with 2.9% relative error, while honestly documenting limits.

entry.title: Tail-Weight Control and Localized Generalization in Nearly Low-Rank Adversarial Classification

author.name: Kunyu Wang, Dehan Wang, Wenjun Chen

entry.summary: Proves that in a Gaussian linear classification model with a low-dimensional informative subspace and independent noise tail, a principal-space witness with risk below one half forces every near-optimal predictor to have small tail weight under Euclidean adversarial perturbations. Boundary normalization removes attack-penalty terms, yielding localized finite-sample generalization guarantees governed by principal dimension and tail energy.

entry.title: Collaborative Streaming Anomaly Detection with Interactive Explanations and Ensemble Consensus

author.name: Diogo Risca, Afonso Louren\c{c}o, Ricardo Martins, Goreti Marreiros

entry.summary: The paper presents a streaming anomaly detection system that integrates human analysts into the decision loop, combining heterogeneous detectors via a normalization-based weighted consensus with surrogate models exposing human-readable conditions behind anomaly scores. Analysts can review episodes, adjust consensus behavior, and refine surrogate rules, producing a human-adjusted ensemble. It emphasizes the often-neglected human-in-the-loop and interpretability dimensions of operational anomaly detection.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Online Change Point Detection with Adaptive Thresholding and Interpretability

author.name: Sven Jacob, Bardh Prenkaj, Weijia Shao, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: The paper introduces a change point detection framework that uses the Sliced Wasserstein distance to compress multivariate sequential data into one-dimensional scores compatible with existing CPD methods, improving scalability in high-dimensional settings with adaptive thresholding and interpretability of detected changes. Applications span activity recognition, finance, cybersecurity, manufacturing, and autonomous systems.

entry.title: MUSE: Dependency-Aware Adaptation of a Frozen Vision Backbone for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xinying Cai, Junkai Lu, Yuhan Zhu, Xiaoyun Yu, Xiangfei Qiu, Jilin Hu

entry.summary: MUSE adapts a fully frozen pretrained masked-autoencoder vision model for multivariate time-series forecasting, with a Variable Context Refinement Module that models cross-variable dependencies while preserving independent visual representation spaces. It addresses the mismatch between natural-image priors and temporal semantics of time-series images.

entry.title: Intelligent Degradation Monitoring in Lithium-ion Batteries via Discharge Incremental Capacity Feature Estimation

author.name: Amir Madmolilvand, Farzaneh Abdollahi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a neural network framework that predicts discharge incremental capacity features directly from charging signals, removing the need for slow low-current discharge cycling in battery degradation monitoring. Trained on 53 cells under diverse fast-charging protocols, the model generalizes across conditions. It is a practical advance for real-time battery management in EVs and storage systems.

entry.title: Reconstructed holograms and explanation-aware evaluation for low-cost computational pollen analysis in veterinary cytology

author.name: Swarn Warshaneyan, Joial Danyal, Bla\v{z} Cugmas, Mindaugas Tamo\v{s}i\=unas, Edgars Kviesis-Kipge, Kirishanth Manivannan, Roberts Kadi\c{k}is
